This Sanskrit classic was extensively referenced by His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in writing his purports for the Fifth Canto of the Srimad-Bhagavatam. Now the entire compendium of commentaries \[which includes those of Srila Sridhara Svami, Sri Viraraghavacarya, Srimad Vijayadhvaja Tirtha, Srila Jiva Gosvami and Srimad Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura\] is available for first time in English. The translation was done by erudite Vasnava scholars and edited by His Holiness Danavir Goswami. (850 pages, 8 color pages of illustrations, hardbound stitched binding, Sanksrit devanagari, English translations and glossaries.)

# Fifth Canto Commentaries

The cosmology portion of *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*’s Fifth Canto translated and commented upon by His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda is, in our opinion, totally fulfilling and comprehensive. It was directly inspired by Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa to succinctly explain *bhāgavata* cosmology to the world. Nevertheless, before his departure, Śrīla Prabhupada also expressed a strong desire to construct a Temple of Vedic Planetarium using specific insights from *authoritative commentaries by important ācāryas* on the Fifth Canto. A recently discovered letter sheds more light on this:

*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\**

*Krishna Balarama Mandir, Chattikara Road, Vrindaban, U.P.,*  
*November 14 1976*  
*Mr. S. L. Dhani, Deputy Secretary*

*Subject: The Times of India Article of November 7th 1976 concerning your paper on the Puranic theory of evolution.*

*Dear sir,*

*The above mentioned International Society for Krishna Consciousness has published within the last ten years English translations of the Bhagavad Gita, Srimad Bhagavatam (Maha-purana), Caitanya Caritamrta, Isopanisad and many other volumes of India's most ancient Vedic cultural heritage, which are now translated into French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Italian, Chinese, etc. and which are being purchased by the millions all over the world.*

*Now, here in India, we are planning construction of a very large "Vedic Planetarium" or "Temple of Understanding". Within the planetarium we will construct a huge, detailed model of the universe as desdcribed in the text of the fifth canto of the Srimad Bhagavatam. Within the planetarium the model will be studied by onlookers from different levels by use of escalators. Detailed information will be given on open verandas at the different levels by means of dioramas, charts, films, etc.*

*The planetarium is planned to be approximately 400 feet high and will have floor space of approximately 90,000 sq. ft. The model will depict: (from bottom to top)*

*1) The lower planetary system (pataladi-saptaloka)*

*2) The earthly system (bhu-mandala with Sumeru in center, seven islands (saptadvipa), seven oceans (sapta-samudra), Manosattara Parvata, Lokaloka Parvata, Alokavarsa.*

*3) The Bhuvarloka (Siddha-caranadi-loka)*

*4) The upper planetary system (Svarga loka) beginning from the Sun, showing with electrial apparatus both its horizontal and vertical rotations, Rahu, the Moon, the Naksatras, the other seven planets ending with Saturn (Saniscara), the Saptarsis, and Dhruvaloka with Ksirodakasayi Visnu on the Ksirodaka ocean.*

*5) Maharloka*

*6) Janaloka*

*7) Tapoloka*

*8) Satyaloka*

*9) Garbhodakasayi Visnu lying on Sesanaga on the Garbhodaka ocean*

*10) The seven coverings of the universe*

*11) Sivaloka*

*12) Karanarnavasayi visnu lying on the Karana-samudra*

*13) Impersonal brahmajyoti*

*14) Vaikunthaloka with the various Visnumurtis*

*15) Goloka Vrndavana*

*This model (approximately 200 feet high and 100 feet wide) will be engineered to suspend from the structure of the dome and rotate according to the real movement of the planets. The plans for this very large project are being taken soley from the references found in fifth canto Srimad Bhagavatam and its authoritative commentaries by important acaryas, along with other Puranas and Samhitas like Brahma-samhita etc.*

*As you can appreciate, the work involved in this project will be gigantic and the advice of many experts from all fields will be needed to make it come out successful. It will be a glorious exhibition of India's Vedic culture that will attract visitors from all the world. I am inquisitive to know how you can help us with this project, as I know you are an expert in the field of Puranic astronomy. Hoping to hear from you in the near future.*

*Faithfully yours,*  
*A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami*  
*ACBS/jda*

*Hare Krishna Land, Gandhi Gram Rd., Juhu, Bombay, 400 ̮̮4*

*Fifth Canto Commentaries* (*Cosmology Chapters*) is likely the first English translation of the eleven-chapter cosmological section (chapters 16-26) of the Sanskrit book primarily used as a reference by Śrīla Prabhupāda for his own *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* purports. The famous scholar Krsna Sankara Sastri published the book entitled *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam Mahā-Purāṇam* in 1935. Śrīla Prabhupada had this to say about the book:

“*Perhaps you know that there is an edition of the Srimad-Bhagavatam by Krsna Sankara Sastri "abhinavah sukah'' Vedantacarya, Sahitya-tirtha, sribhagavatasudhanidhi, from Ahmedabad. In his book he has given almost all the important commentaries on the Bhagavatam, as follows: 1. Sridhara Svami 2. Sri Vamsidhara 3. Sri Gangasahaya 4. Srimad Viraraghavacarya 5. Srimad Vijayadhvaja Tirtha 6. Srimad Jiva Gosvami 7. Srimad Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura 8. Srimad Sukadeva 9. Gosvami Sri-giridharalal (Vallabhacarya Sampradaya) 10. Sri Bhagavat-prasadacarya, etc.*” (Letter to Sumati Morarjee, 7, August, 1976)

The actual names of the commentaries are *Bhāvārthadīpikā* by Śrīdharasvāmi, *Vīrarāghavīya* by Vīrarāghava, *Padaratnāvalī* by Vijayadhvaja, *Krama-sandarbha* by Jīva Gosvāmī, *Sārārthadarṣinī* by Viṣvanātha Cakravarti, *Bhāvārthadīpikāprakāśa* by Śrīvaṁśīdhara, *Siddhānta Pradīpa* by Śukadeva, *Tīrtha Bāla Prabodhinī* by Śrī Giridhara Lāla, and *Bhaktamanorañjanī* by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya. However, in this book we have simply given the names of the commentators above each comment. In addition to the above-mentioned nine commentators, we have also included the translation (chapters 18-26) of the Sanskrit commentary by Yadavarya, a highly respected scholar in the line of Śrīpād Madhvācārya.

Together, these ten commentaries provide a most significant symphony of conclusions harmonizing views from Vaiṣṇava *sampradāyas*. Repetition appears in this volume, yet instead of becoming monotonous, the wise will hear a beautiful crescendo of voices singing in authoritative unison.

Variances of opinions amongst the commentators, indicates realization seen from different angles of vision, or, as mentioned in this book by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī:

*“Different viewpoints described in the commentaries are to be taken as in different creations.”*

Here “different creations” refers to diverse manifestations of universal cosmography found in separate universes and/or the dissimilar aspects found within our universe in the thousands of *kalpas* or days of Brahmā.

It is interesting to note, however, that none of commentators has whimsically introduced any new concepts. Rather, they have all followed in the footsteps of the original speaker of *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*, namely Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī, and its first commentator Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally had this to say about Śrīdhara Svāmī:

*śrīdhara-svāmi-prasāde ‘bhāgavata’ jāni*  
*jagad-guru śrīdhara-svāmī ‘guru’ kari’ māni*

***“Śrīdhara Svāmī is the spiritual master of the entire world because by his mercy we can understand Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. I therefore accept him as a spiritual master.*****” \[Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 7.133\]**

The level of agreement between the commentaries is nothing less than astounding. This proves that consistency is one of the most profound characteristics of Vaiṣṇava literature. Śrīla Prabhupada explains:

*Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam has many ṭīkās, or commentaries, following the paramparā system, but Śrīdhara Svāmī’s is first. The commentaries of all the other ācāryas follow his. The paramparā system does not allow one to deviate from the commentaries of the previous ācāryas. By depending upon the previous ācāryas, one can write beautiful commentaries. However, one cannot defy the previous ācāryas. The false pride that makes one think that he can write better than the previous ācāryas will make one’s comments faulty. At the present moment it has become fashionable for everyone to write in his own way, but such writing is never accepted by serious devotees. Because of false pride, every scholar and philosopher wants to exhibit his learning by interpreting the śāstras, especially the Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, in his own way. This system of commenting in one’s own way is fully condemned by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Therefore He says, ‘artha-vyasta’ likhana sei. Commentaries written according to one’s own philosophical way are never accepted; no one will appreciate such commentaries on the revealed scriptures.* \[Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 7.134 Purport\]

Within the opus of Vedic literature, the topmost position of authority is reserved exclusively for the *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*.

*nigama-kalpa-taror galitaṁ phalaṁ*  
*śuka-mukhād amṛta-drava-saṁyutam*  
*pibata bhāgavataṁ rasam ālayaṁ*  
*muhur aho rasikā bhuvi bhāvukāḥ*

***O expert and thoughtful men, relish Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the mature fruit of the desire tree of Vedic literatures. It emanated from the lips of Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī. Therefore this fruit has become even more tasteful, although its nectarean juice was already relishable for all, including liberated souls.***

Śrīpād Madhvācārya said: “Everything should be interpreted without contradiction to *Bhāgavata*.” In approaching scientific subject matters, Śrīla Prabhupāda gives the following advice:

*“In the creation of the Lord there are many wonderful things we can see with our own eyes every day and night, but we are unable to reach them equipped by modern materialistic science. We should not, therefore, depend on the fragmentary authority of materialistic science for knowing things beyond the range of scientific purview. For a common man, both modern science and Vedic wisdom are simply to be accepted because none of the statements either of modern science or of Vedic literature can be verified by him. The alternative for a common man is to believe either of them or both of them. The Vedic way of understanding, however, is more authentic because it has been accepted by the ācāryas, who are not only faithful and learned men, but are also liberated souls without any of the flaws of conditioned souls. The modern scientists, however, are conditioned souls liable to so many errors and mistakes; therefore the safe side is to accept the authentic version of Vedic literatures, like Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which is accepted unanimously by the great ācāryas.” (2.2.26)*

The “Śukadeva” listed as a commentator is a different person from Śrīla Vyāsadeva’s son*—*Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the original speaker of *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*.

Within the translations, brackets found with information inside are mine. Also, there are occasional notes from the translators in brackets marked as such.

The English transliteration of Sanskrit incorporates several styles—including the standard diacritical system known as Harvard Kyoto as well as more regional usages presented by our translators.

Since this volume is largely a reference work, we have purposely avoided much editing to keep the essential message of the commentators unencumbered.

In conclusion, this book offers essential answers to cosmological questions, provides a blueprint for future scholars and an immense opportunity for scientific preaching by all sincere devotees. Those with implicit faith in *guru*, *śāstra* and *sādhu* cannot help but be incredibly inspired from reading these commentaries. Naturally then, they will want to explain it to others.

## Chapter 16 - A Description of Jambūdvīpa

### Text 1

*राजोवाच*  
*उक्तस्त्वया भूमण्डलायामविशेषो यावदादित्यस्तपति यत्र चासौ ज्योतिषां*  
*गणैश्चन्द्रमा वा सह दृश्यते ॥१॥*

*rājovāca*  
*uktas tvayā bhū-maṇḍalāyāma-viśeṣo yāvad ādityas tapati yatra cāsau jyotiṣāṁ gaṇaiś candramā vā saha dṛśyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*rājā uvāca*—Mahārāja Parīkṣit said; *uktaḥ*—already been said; *tvayā*—by you; *bhū-maṇḍala*—of the planetary systems known as Bhū-maṇḍala; *āyāma-viśeṣaḥ*—the specific length of the radius; *yāvat*—as far as; *ādityaḥ*—the sun; *tapati*—heats; *yatra*—wherever; *ca*—also; *asau*—that; *jyotiṣām*—of the luminaries; *gaṇaiḥ*—with hordes; *candramā*—the moon; *vā*—either; *saha*—with; *dṛśyate*—is seen.

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said to Śukadeva Gosvāmī: O brāhmaṇa, you have already informed me that the radius of Bhū-maṇḍala extends as far as the sun spreads its light and heat and as far as the moon and all the stars can be seen.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The five chapters henceforth (i.e, chapters 16 to 20) are begun for clearly explaining the previously mentioned islands, oceans etc. by their extent, definitions and essential characteristics. \[1\]

In the sixteenth chapter, the configuration of Mount Meru, what lies to its bottom, top and surroundings and the pericarp of the earth-lotus are explained. \[2\]

In the previous chapter, while narrating the story of King Priyavrata, mention was made of the division of the globe into islands. To know about it in greater detail, at the end of that story, the king (Parīkṣit) inquires further. \[3\]

(ukta:)—“To what extent was told,” is specified as up to where the sun reigns, where also the moon in the bright and dark fortnights is seen along with the stellar clusters (constellations).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The knowledge of the world-globe and its particulars is illustrative of Śrī Nārāyana's greatness and hence is essential for liberation. Therefore, the description of the globe is elaborated in the next five chapters. Therefore, Parīkṣit inquires from the sage Śuka about details by summarizing what is indicated earlier briefly in the part “ukta iti”—thus, “You have said that the extent of the world is up to the region where the sun glows or where the moon along with stellar constellations is visible.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the Sixteenth (chapter), the extents of the continents of Jambūdvīpa, the intervening mountains and Sumeru are being described.  
The king inquires about the mention of the islands, seas, etc. and their extents made during the episode of Priyavrata at the end of the episode (context) as “uktah.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s first verse: The term “etc.” after “islands,” indicates continents, etc.

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s second verse: Surroundings indicates “from all around.” The situation of Mount Meru is described as analogical to earth in the form of a lotus that has Meru as the pollen-case amid its pericarp. Here the particle “ca” is used as quarter-filler (for metrical requirement).

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s third verse: Previously, after the episode of King Priyavrata was told, King Parīkṣit was desirous of knowing the specific details and distinctions of the islands, etc.

The particulars of length (extent) of the world (globe) etc. “Glows” = illuminates. Until “that much”, i.e, the region/place.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Having briefly heard of the islands, etc. in the narration of the Priyavrata episode, the king asks further to know its elaboration as “ukta iti.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s first verse: In the fifteen previous chapters, the essential nature is described. In the remaining eleven chapters, the location is being described.

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s second verse: As earth is the most important among the five elements, it is being described in five chapters. This is because it is the cause of the four-fold attainments. \[the four-fold attainments are: (1) *dharma*—occupational duties; (2) artha—economic development; (3) kāma—fulfillment of desires; (4) mokṣā—ultimate salvation\]

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s third verse: In the four chapters beginning from Chapter 16 Jambūdvīpa is described. Its extent, etc. are described in the Sixteenth Chapter.

Having covered the essential characteristics in fifteen chapters, now the locational details of the earth (the most important among the five elements) are being described in five chapters. Although there are other islands and worlds which are like heavenly stations for enjoyment, their attainment depends on actions performed in Jambūdvīpa and the Bhārata continent. Devotion to the Supreme Lord is most likely there.

Mount Meru and other continents are the places for deities and the Lord's incarnations and thus they support the four-fold attainments of man. This is described in four chapters. In this Sixteenth Chapter, the nature, extent, etc. of Jambūdvīpa and Mount Meru are described.

Having heard about the islands, continents, etc. during the Priyavrata episode, and wanting to know more about them, the king says “ukta iti.” “Until where the sun glows/illuminates and where, along with stellar groups, the moon is seen, that much is the extent of earth's spread as indicated by you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s first verse: Islands, seas, etc. mentioned earlier, are now being clearly explained by size, characteristics and essential nature in the following five chapters.

Comment on Śrīdhara Svāmi’s second verse: The periphery, the top, the bottom and the configuration of the earth globe and Meru, the central part of the earth as a lotus, are explained in the Sixteenth Chapter.

Thus, having heard the story of Priyavrata and his progeny, the king, desirous of knowing, asks about the details regarding the division of the world into islands. These were mentioned briefly in the story of Priyavrata, at the end of the episode, by summarizing what was said earlier as “uktah.” “‘O sage!, you mentioned the expanse of the world, i.e, the length, and extent unto where the sun illuminates and the moon (in bright and dark fortnights) and the stars are seen. So much was told.”

*prathame dhyāye “yāvad avabhāsayati suragirim anuparikraman bhagavān ādityo*  
*vasudhā-talam arddhrena pratapatyarddhenācchādayati” anenādityaḥ suragires*  
*tamisrā timirā saṁvalita prakāśenaikasmin ardhe divā karoti.*  
*Asyopalakṣaṇatvāt tad aprakāśavantam suragirer bhāgam timira saṁvalita*  
*jyotsnā puñjena candramāḥ nakṣatraiḥ saha prakāśayan rajanīṁ karoti ityapi*  
*muninā sucitatvāt tad api smṛti pathamānīyān nānuvādenābhihitam*

The purport is this: In the first chapter it was said,

*yāvad avabhāsayati suragirim anuparikraman bhagavān ādityo*  
*vasudhā-talam arddhrena pratapatyarddhenācchādayati*

***“As much as the sun in going around Meru illuminates it, it light ups half the surface of the earth and covers half.”***

By this it is understood that the sun makes day in one half of Meru by illumination not endowed with darkness of night. The moon, along with the stars illuminating the portion of Meru not illuminated (by the sun) with quantities of moonlight surrounded with darkness makes night. Because this is the intention of the sages, followed by the *smṛtis*, it is not repeated.

### Text 2

*तत्रापि प्रियव्रतरथचरणपरिखातैः सप्तभिः सप्त सिन्धव उपकॢप्ता यत*  
*एतस्याः सप्तद्वीपविशेषविकल्पस्त्वया भगवन् खलु सूचित एतदेवाखिलमहं*  
*मानतो लक्षणतश्च सर्वं विजिज्ञासामि ॥२॥*

*tatrāpi priyavrata-ratha-caraṇa-parikhātaiḥ saptabhiḥ sapta sindhava upakḷptā yata etasyāḥ sapta-dvīpa-viśeṣa-vikalpas tvayā bhagavan khalu sūcita etad evākhilam ahaṁ mānato lakṣaṇataś ca sarvaṁ vi-jijñāsāmi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra api—in that Bhū-maṇḍala; priyavrata-ratha-caraṇa-parikhātaiḥ—by the ditches made by the wheels of the chariot used by Priyavrata Mahārāja while circumambulating Sumeru behind the sun; saptabhiḥ—by the seven; sapta—seven; sindhavaḥ—oceans; upakḷptāḥ—created; yataḥ—because of which; etasyāḥ—of this Bhū-maṇḍala; sapta-dvīpa—of the seven islands; viśeṣa-vikalpaḥ—the mode of the construction; tvayā—by you; bhagavan—O great saint; khalu—indeed; sūcitaḥ—described; etat—this; eva—certainly; akhilam—whole subject; aham—I; mānataḥ—from the point of view of measurement; lakṣaṇataḥ—and from symptoms; ca—also; sarvam—everything; vijijñāsāmi—wish to know.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, the rolling wheels of Mahārāja Priyavrata's chariot created seven ditches, in which the seven oceans came into existence. Because of these seven oceans, Bhū-maṇḍala is divided into seven islands. You have given a very general description of their measurement, names and characteristics. Now I wish to know of them in detail. Kindly fulfill my desire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Yataḥ”— from the seas. “Etasyaḥ”—earth. “Indicated”—briefly shown.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The words “yata etat” recall the divisions created by Priyavrata in the earth-circle. The purport is: the seven seas were formed by the mud scooped (dug) out by the sharp wheels of Priyavrata's chariot. The mud which was scooped out settled solidly as boundaries and became the seven islands (land-fills).

Only their names were indicated while details were not mentioned earlier. I wish to know the particulars in fuller detail and in such a way, that nothing remains to be known. The emphasis by the word “eva” denotes that even intermediary details are fully relevant and not extraneous.

*Māna* means extent; *lakṣaṇa* is a circular, square shape, etc. Not only this, but even about the golden mountain, the regions beyond the seven seas, and the things thenceforth are all covered by the word “sarva” used later. *Jijñāsaṁ* indicates only desire to know and not to discuss. The *parasmaipada* (middle voice) is used. The first person (I) denotes that although others might also benefit, it is most beneficial to me. Otherwise, the generic word *jijñāsyaṁ* would not have been used.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“From where”—the seas. This earth's seven islands, their particulars, divisions and sub-divisions. *Etat*—sea, island, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“There also”—i.e. in the middle of the world also. “By the depression of the chariot's wheels on earth”—i.e. due to the sharpness of the wheels’ periphery, the earth gets excavated/upturned, \[i.e, pits are formed like craters and repeatedly they become large troughs and eventually seas\].

“The details of seven islands” = differences, i.e. their sub-divisions into continents. “Indicated” denotes that the specifics are not given. “Glorious one” denotes the knowledge of the states of the great and small things alike, and hence, “it is not surprising that you know these things.” Thus, “I wish to know elaborately about the oceans, islands etc. so as not to miss out on this opportunity.”

*Māna* is extent, measure. *Lakṣaṇam* means “characteristics.” *Sarvam* means not only the islands and oceans but even beyond that, namely the golden land—without omitting anything. *Jijñāsāmi* denotes a desire to know and not merely to contemplate. The use of *parasmaipada* (active voice instead of middle voice) is sagely (epic) usage. The additional use of the word *aham* (“I”—although the verb in first person alone is sufficient) indicates that, “although this knowledge (from your answer) will be useful to many people, I intend to be the most benefited.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Yataḥ”—from which seas.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“There also you said that, Priyavrata was circumambulating Mount Meru behind the sun and his chariot's wheels dug up all around the earth (mud), forming the seven seas. From those seven seas, the earth's general division into seven islands was also indicated by you.” In order to know the specific details, the king praises the sage as having the knowledge of past, present and future, and as being omniscient by addressing him as “Bhagavān.” “I wish to know comprehensively the complete details including extent and unique characteristics.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

“There” = on earth also; the seven seas are formed by the seven big craters caused by the wheels of Priyavrata's chariot excavating mud. This earth's seven islands, Jambū and so on, along with their divisions and sub-divisions were indicated by you, O learned one! This was briefly stated as, “The seven seas were created by the wheels of his chariot upturning earth which formed the seven islands of earth,” was is not? I am desirous of knowing this earth's description entirely by magnitude, characteristics and by name.

### Text 3

*भगवतो गुणमये स्थूलरूप आवेशितं मनो ह्यगुणेऽपि सूक्ष्मतम आत्मज्योतिषि परे*  
*ब्रह्मणि भगवति वासुदेवाख्ये क्षममावेशितुं तदु हैतद् गुरोऽर्हस्यनुवर्णयितु*  
*मिति ॥३॥*

*bhagavato guṇamaye sthūla-rūpa āveśitaṁ mano hy aguṇe 'pi sūkṣmatama ātma-jyotiṣi pare brahmaṇi bhagavati vāsudevākhye kṣamam āveśituṁ tad u haitad guro 'rhasy anuvarṇayitum iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; guṇa-maye—into the external features, consisting of the three modes of material nature; sthūla-rūpe—the gross form; āveśitam—entered; manaḥ—the mind; hi—indeed; aguṇe—transcendental; api—although; sūkṣmatame—in His smaller form as Paramātmā within the heart; ātma-jyotiṣi—who is full of Brahman effulgence; pare—the supreme; brahmaṇi—spiritual entity; bhagavati—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vāsudeva-ākhye—known as Bhagavān Vāsudeva; kṣamam—suitable; āveśitum—to absorb; tat—that; u ha—indeed; etat—this; guro—O my dear spiritual master; arhasi anuvarṇayitum—please describe factually; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**When the mind is fixed upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His external feature made of the material modes of nature—the gross universal form—it is brought to the platform of pure goodness. In that transcendental position, one can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, who in His subtler form is self-effulgent and beyond the modes of nature. O my lord, please describe vividly how that form, which covers the entire universe, is perceived.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The result of the desire to know is directly entering (meditating upon) the glories of the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Thus having heard the episode of Priyavrata and his progeny, King Parīkṣit asks about the particulars of the division of islands etc. which were only briefly mentioned. Earth's length (extent) of the world (globe) etc. “Up to what extent was told” is replied as, “up to the point where the sun glows and the moon with bright and dark fortnights and stars is visible. Up to which point these two are is replied as where in the world's expanse the seven islands beginning with Jambū etc. of earth are. Their details such as name, measure, identifications etc. and their differences were briefly indicated by you, the glorious one. I wish to know comprehensively the details of the earth circle by extent, characteristics and names. By “and” is meant by names also.

The results of this knowledge are explained in this verse, starting “bhagavata.”

Only the mind firmly placed in the gross form of the Lord in the manifestations comprising of the result of the qualities sattva etc. is capable of dwelling on even things devoid of qualities of sattva, etc. i.e, supernatural, very subtle, of the size of a thumb, a form made of pure sattva, the self-luminous, essential nature of Paramātman, Brahman, denoted by words Bhagavān, Vāsudeva etc. So I wish to know the particulars. As I am desirous, O master! Kindly enlighten me on the extent, characteristics etc. of the earth's circle, elaborately.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is that utmost benefit is explained by the terms “bhagavata iti” etc. Hitherto my mind well-placed in the gross form of the Lord, comprised of qualities of sattva etc., having non-sentient parts like Pātāla etc., and trained and capable of remembering the details, becomes capable of contemplating on the subtle forms. It can contemplate forms devoid of the effects of qualities like sattva etc., i.e. the form of the immutable, sentient, blissful being which cannot be seen without its grace.

Is it darkness then?

No. It is self-luminous.

What is its name? Para-brahman. *Bhagavān*—full of auspicious qualities like sovereignty, etc.

Is there a colloquial name besides the Vedic name?

Vāsudeva. By this is indicated that even legends have authority. *Kṣamaṁ*—capable of being placed. The article “ha” indicates that the maxim “one should not instruct anyone unless asked,” is not applicable here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The benefit of the desire to know is mentioned as “bhagavataḥ.” Here as the agentive word “by me” is absent, the text is rendered as follows: “Those with devotion and meditation present here have desired me to ask this for contemplation, and hence, I am complying. For me however, drinking (through my ears) the nectar of the narration of the Lord's auspicious qualities emanating from your lotus mouth is the only means of attaining the Lord.”

The apparently contradictory terms, “in the Lord's gross form comprising attributes” and “in the Lord devoid of attributes” establish that the Lord is beyond worldly qualities. The vocative use of “guro” denotes that, “As you are the preceptor of all sages, you should certainly tell me about this.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

What is the benefit? “Hitherto my mind was trained to meditate on things comprised of attributes in gross form encompassing non-sentient objects like Pātāla, etc. After sufficient practice, it has acquired the special capability to dwell on things more subtle—where actions due to the modes of material nature are absent—i.e, the eternal, knowing, blissful Supreme Being, Who is not knowable without His grace.” But is it sloth, dark, inert or empty? No. It is self-luminous and illumining. What is its name? Para-brahman, bhagavān, with all splendor and glory. Apart from the Vedic title is there a personal name? Vāsudeva. This indicates the authority.

*Kṣamaṁ*—capable. Here, the absence of an agentive word for self means that, “I am asking to know this in tune with those who perform devotional *yoga* and who place firmly in their minds such form, but do not intend to pursue that path. For me, however, it is enough to enjoy through my ears the nectar of the Lord's conduct and stories flowing out of your lotus-like mouth. This is the means to salvation, i.e, attainment to the Lord.” Also, here the difference denoting, “gross form of the Lord with attributes” is used in the genitive case and “Lord in a subtle form devoid of action arising from qualities” in common relationship connotes that the Lord's qualities are beyond sattva, \[goodness\] etc.

“Guro” as a vocative implies, “As you are the teacher of even the sages, you should certainly enlighten me on this.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The benefit of desire to know is said as “bhagavata iti.” The mind being firmly placed in the resplendent, gross form comprising attributes of sattva etc. will be capable of contemplating the supernatural form devoid of the material modes of nature such as sattva *guṇa*, etc. It is also self-illuminating and personal.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“But for a great devotee like you, what is the need to know these details of islands, seas etc.” is answered by the terms beginning with “bhagavatah.” Since the mind placed firmly in the gross, resplendent form of the Lord becomes capable of meditating on His very subtle, unperceivable form, in that way, I wish to know of this gross universe-form of the Lord. Hence kindly enlighten me as you are competent to do so.” This implies that, “I am not after pleasing my senses by wanting to know the details of the external, worldly things, but only to know the Lord's manifestations, to meditate on Him.”

Grossness is due to having the forms with attributes of sattva, etc. Supreme subtleness is due to their absence. To rule out formlessness, it is said to have the name Vāsudeva. To avoid suggesting limitedness, it is called “infinite,” Brahman. To denote that He is the ultimate, He is called Supreme. To distinguish it from an insentient entity, it is called self-illuminating. The address “guro” is per the dictum, “Just try to learn the truth by approaching a spiritual master. Inquire from him submissively and render service unto him. The self-realized souls can impart knowledge unto you because they have seen the truth.” Thus, he inquires humbly, falling at his master’s feet pleading for a merciful explanation of the details.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Why does he have this desire to know? “Bhagavataḥ” etc. with attributes—the result of meditating on the form of the Lord with attributes will be that the mind will then become capable of meditating on the supernatural, self-luminous form of the Lord. “Very subtle” indicates the size of thumb, as mentioned in the scriptures as “thumb-sized person dwelling in the hearts of living beings.”

*Brahman*—infinitely big. *Bhagavān*—possessing the six great qualities of sovereignty etc. “Named as Vāsudeva”—being perceived by a pure mind and denoted by the word Vāsudeva, the supreme ruler. Hence, “I wish to know,” is to be added for semantic connection. “As I am desirous, O master, explain to me lucidly the names, qualities and so forth of this earth's globe.”

### Text 4

*ऋषिरुवाच*  
*न वै महाराज भगवतो मायागुणविभूतेः काष्ठां मनसा वचसा*  
*वाधिगन्तुमलं विबुधायुषापि पुरुषस्तस्मात्प्राधान्येनैव भूगोलकविशेषं नाम*  
*रूप मानलक्षणतो व्याख्यास्यामः ॥४॥*

*ṛṣir uvāca*  
*na vai mahārāja bhagavato māyā-guṇa-vibhūteḥ kāṣṭhāṁ manasā vacasā vādhigantum alaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi puruṣas tasmāt prādhān-yenaiva bhū-golaka-viśeṣaṁ nāma-rūpa-māna-lakṣaṇato vyākhyāsyāmaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ṛṣiḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued to speak; na—not; vai—indeed; mahā-rāja—O great King; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; māyā-guṇa-vibhūteḥ—of the transformation of the qualities of the material energy; kāṣṭhām—the end; manasā—by the mind; vacasā—by words; vā—either; adhigantum—to understand fully; alam—capable; vibudha-āyuṣā—with a duration of life like that of Brahmā; api—even; puruṣaḥ—a person; tasmāt—therefore; prādhānyena—by a general description of the chief places; eva—certainly; bhū-golaka-viśeṣam—the particular description of Bhūloka; nāma-rūpa—names and forms; māna—measurements; lakṣaṇataḥ—according to symptoms; vyākhyāsyāmaḥ—I shall try to explain.

**Перевод:**

**The great ṛṣi Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, there is no limit to the expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead's material energy. This material world is a transformation of the material qualities \[sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa and tamo-guṇa\], yet no one could possibly explain it perfectly, even in a lifetime as long as that of Brahmā No one in the material world is perfect, and an imperfect person could not describe this material universe accurately, even after continued speculation. O King, I shall nevertheless try to explain to you the principal regions, such as Bhū-goloka \[Bhūloka\], with their names, forms, measurements and various symptoms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Treasure of wonderful attributes, its limit” = end. *Form*= structure. *Definition*= mark.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

After having been questioned, the sage-son of Bādarāyaṇa replies that, “as the forms of the Lord are infinite, it is impossible to deal with them exhaustively by mind or words. Still, I promise to explain in more detail the earth globe. O great King! Bhagavān's treasure of amazing attributes manifesting into myriad, infinite globes for his sporting are countless and cannot be ascertained even through the entire life-span of any human. Hence, instead of attempting the impossible, I shall dwell on the prominent details of the earth-globe, its divisions, including the names, extents and nature etc. to answer your query.”

The phrase; “maya *guṇa* vibhuteh kastam” means, “the end of the powers made of the *guṇas* of *māyā*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The Lord is a treasure of amazing attributes. To stimulate the qualities of nature (*prakṛti*), becoming various (manifesting into many forms) is the greatness of the Lord. Its end or limit cannot be fathomed in the lifespan of deities amounting to two parārdhas.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Use of the terms “Bhagavān's form comprising qualities, etc.” establishes that the quality of Bhagavān is beyond material qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Limit*—end; *form*—manifestation; *characteristics*—signs.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“The sage said,”—here the word *sage* is used to mean one who knows past, present and future. His treasure of amazing attributes is manifesting into myriad forms to make nature's qualities active. The life-span of the devatas is defined as two parārdhas. Prādhānyenaiva—primarily alone.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

A treasure of amazing attributes in the form of the world (globe), its specific locations and their limit (end).

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Thus passionately implored, the sage Śuka replied beginning with “na”: “O King! It is befitting your majesty that you are devoted to the Lord. The amazing powers of the Lord displayed through His attributes of nature like sattva (goodness) etc. are so vast that their limit cannot be fathomed by man’s thoughts or words even in the lifetime of the demigods. Hence, only the prominent aspects of the globe will be elaborated.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The son of Bādarāyaṇa replied by the terms starting with “na vai,”—thus, “As the manifestations of the Lord are infinite and, exhaustively describing them is beyond mind and speech. O great King! Bhagavān's wealth in the form of amazing attributes and their expansions covering the sport of creation of the universe, made of nature's qualities like sattva, etc. is infinite. Describing them by name and form etc., up to their end/limit is beyond mind and speech, i.e, unthinkable and inexplicable. Even to know or reach their end by mind or words is impossible. This is so even if one is given the life-span of the demigods. This is due to the countlessness of the locations, etc. So, we opt to elaborate the prominent particulars regarding the earth's configuration with divisions by name, dimension, form and structural features.”

### Text 5

*यो वायं द्वीपः कुवलयकमलकोशाभ्यन्तरकोशो नियुतयोजन विशालः समवर्तुलो*  
*यथा पुष्करपत्रम् ॥५॥*

*yo vāyaṁ dvīpaḥ kuvalaya-kamala-kośābhyantara-kośo niyuta-yojana-viśālaḥ samavartulo yathā puṣkara-patram.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yaḥ—which; vā—either; ayam—this; dvīpaḥ—island; kuvalaya—the Bhūloka; kamala-kośa—of the whorl of a lotus flower; abhyantara—inner; kośaḥ—whorl; niyuta-yojana-viśālaḥ—one million yojanas (eight million miles) wide; samavartulaḥ—equally round, or having a length and breadth of the same measurement; yathā—like; puṣkara-patram—a lotus leaf.

**Перевод:**

**The planetary system known as Bhū-maṇḍala resembles a lotus flower, and its seven islands resemble the whorl of that flower. The length and breadth of the island known as Jambūdvīpa, which is situated in the middle of the whorl, are one million yojanas \[eight million miles\]. Jambūdvīpa is round like the leaf of a lotus flower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Kuvalayam* means Bhū-maṇḍala which is itself a lotus. Its sheaths are seven islands, among them, the first inner sheath is Jambūdvīpa, one *lakh yojana* (100,000 *yojanas* or 800,000 miles) wide (extant = area).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The island named Jambūdvīpa means one which drinks water of the seas from east and west or north and south sides (*dvīpa*—drinks from two sides). Without it drinking, the heat of the sun's rays would cause the earth to lose its solidity. Due to such atomic disintegration, inhabitants of the island would be submerged (as the substrate would be lost). The elongation (ṅ) is proper due to special enumeration. This is one *lakh yojanas* \[100,000 *yojanas* or 800,000 miles\] in extent. As the extent is the aggregate of eleven places, they amount to one 100,000. “Niyuta” denotes one *lakh* (100,000). In precise terms, the earth with its configuration is figuratively explained as “the earth (globe) which is itself a lotus.” Its sheaths are the other islands. The inner sheath is this island, Jambūdvīpa. Its form is described as uniformly circular. It is illustrated with the example of a lotus-leaf. Since the lotus petals, pericarp and sheaths have gaps in between, it (flower) would not truly depict the earth's shape and so, this example is mentioned (as the lotus-leaf is one and continuous). This detail regarding the extent etc. is not described anywhere else.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though the word “niyuta” literally means one million, somehow it denotes one *lakh* (100,000), being proximate to that.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vai*—definitely. *Kuvalaya*—earth's field, that itself is a lotus; its sheaths are as its regions. The inner sheath of the seven islands, the visible Jambūdvīpa is one *lakh yojana* (100,000 *yojanas*) \[800,000 miles\] wide, i.e, in area.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The word “dvīpa” is derived from “that which drinks (sea water) by two sides,” i.e, from the east and west or from the north and south. The elongation of vowel(s) is due to grammatical status as a “nipāta” particle. In the absence of such “drinking,” there would be deluges as sea-water would submerge all life-forms on the island. In the lexicon *amara* however, it is mentioned as “dvīpo'striyāmantarīpaṁ yadantarvāriṇastaṭam” (1.9.8). In that case, “dvīpa” means where water has entered twice or inside and is a compound ending by the grammar rule, *ṛkpūrabdhūḥ pathāmānakṣe* (5.4.74). The elongation of the vowel *ī* is according to dnyantarupasargṛbhy’opa īt (6.3.97).

Although the word “niyuta” denotes a million, here it means a *lakh* (100,000). “Lotus-leaf” here is not that which is related to the flower but that which is used for eating. *Rupa* means “appearance or form.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

This well-known Jambūdvīpa; *kuvalaya*—earth's field; that itself is a lotus; among its seven sheaths as the seven islands, it is the inner sheath; it is 100,000 *yojanas* wide \[800,000 miles\], i.e, in area.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Thus promising to elaborate important details, the sage begins with “yo vai.” *Kuvalaya* is the world as a lotus; the seven islands are as its sheaths; their inner sheath is this first island Jambūdvīpa; it is one *lakh yojanas* (100,000 *yojanas*)\[800,000 miles\] across, uniformly round compared to a lotus-leaf.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

This well-known Jambūdvīpa earth-world is like a lotus, its layers are the seven islands. Their interior layer is one *lakh yojana* (100,000 *yojanas* wide) \[800,000 miles\]. The Ratna Dictionary lists thus: “*Śata, sahasra, ayuta, niyuta, prayuta, koṭi* \[in feminine gender\] and *arbuda*—hundred, thousand, ten thousands, 100,000 (one *lakh*), 1,000,000, one *crore* (10,000,000) and ten *crores* (100,000,000) each ten times the earlier.”

It is like the lotus-leaf that is uniformly circular, as the circularity means no edges it has the same dimension everywhere.

### Text 6

*यस्मिन्नव वर्षाणि नवयोजनसहस्रायामान्यष्टभिर्मर्यादागिरिभिः सुविभक्तानि*  
*भवन्ति ॥६॥*

*yasmin nava varṣāṇi nava-yojanasahasrāyāmāny aṣṭabhir maryādā-giribhiḥ suvibhaktāni bhavanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasmin—in that Jambūdvīpa; nava—nine; varṣāṇi—divisions of land; nava-yojanasahasra—72,000 miles in length; āyāmāni—measuring; aṣṭabhiḥ—by eight; maryādā—indicating the boundaries; giribhiḥ—by mountains; suvibhaktāni—nicely divided from one another; bhavanti—are.

**Перевод:**

**In Jambūdvīpa there are nine divisions of land, each with a length of 9,000 yojanas \[72,000 miles\]. There are eight mountains that mark the boundaries of these divisions and separate them nicely.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The āyāma is nine thousand *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\], i.e. length. Length here is area. Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla are also said to be 31,000 *yojanas* \[248,000 miles\] long. Some explain that the width of Niṣadha and Nīla is reduced at the tips because those parts are submerged in the sea. Some reconcile the 9,000 *yojana* \[72,000 mile\] length by the ends of Nīla and Niṣadha being submerged into the sea, and becoming reduced. The configuration is described in *Vāyu Purāna* as: “Two of the *varṣas* (continents) are to be known as being in the shape of a bow formation to the south and north. Four are linear (longish) among them and Ilāvṛta is square in shape.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Yasmin”—in which island.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nine thousand *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] is the length of them. Length here is expanse. The configuration of eight mountains, Himālaya, etc.— their structure is said by Vāyu as: “Two of the *varṣas* (continents) is to be known as being in the shape of a bow formation to the south and north. Four are linear (longish) among them and Ilāvṛta is square in shape.” North-south are the continents Bhārata and northern Kuru; the four (linear continents) are: Kimpuruṣa, Harivarṣa, Ramyaka and Hiraṇmaya; taking Nīla and Niṣadha as being transverse and having entered the seas as contiguous. These along with Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla make the shape of a bow. Hence, their lengths only are reduced in the middle to make it 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long. But for Ilāvṛta, from Meru, in all four directions, 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] is possible a length. Actually, Ilāvṛta, Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla continents are 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\] long.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

By eight mountains, i.e, Himalaya etc. “North-south” = to the north of India in Kuru-varṣa, there are four *varṣas*, i.e, Kimpuruṣa-Harivarṣa-Ramyaka-Hiraṇmayas. Taking Nīla and Niṣadha as having entered the sea and also Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla taken together, present a bow-like shape. Hence, due to their contraction in length in the middle, they are 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long. From Mount Meru, it is plausible for Ilāvṛta to be 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long in all four directions. In fact, Ilāvṛta, Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla are each 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\] long. *Akhilam* means everything about the islands and oceans and nothing should be excluded.

The following verses are given in the *Śiva Purāṇa* to explain the origin of the names of these continents: A) Ila was a beautiful, divine damsel (dancer-nymph), in the prime of her youth and was wooed by Mahendra here and hence the name Ilāvṛta, for this continent. B) In the days of yore, during the battle between demigods and demons, a shower of comets (*ketumala*) appeared and thus the place is called Ketumāla. C) The divine horse Uccaiḥśravā, emerging from the churning of the nectar-ocean wanders here always and hence this continent is named Bhadrāśva. D) Kuru: the place where Upamanyu after coming there, was told by Hara “do that austerity (kuru), and drink that milk.” E) Where everything is golden and even people resemble gold, that continent, due to the abundance of gold is called Hiraṇmaya. F) Where the pleasing, divine dancer-nymph Urvaśī was seen by the moon, addressed as Ramya and fulfilled their desires, is the continent named Ramya. G) Where Lord Viṣṇu Himself is worshipped by the serpent Ananta, and Viṣṇu was pleased to grant boons, is this continent called Harivarṣa. H) Where the pleasing divine magician lady (Vidyādharī) is let off from the hands. Vidyādhara is the continent called Kimpuruṣa, meaning rhetorically, “is he a man that is let off by her?” I) Where Bhārata bore sorrow due to his sons going in devious ways, is named Bhārata continent by wise men.

It is also said there (in the *Śiva Purāṇa*) that: “Six atoms make a tryaṇuka. Eight of them make a vālāgra. Eight of them make a likṣā. Eight of them yūka; Eight of them yava; Tāla should be same amount (eight) of angulis. Double that is a hasta; four of them a daṇḍa; 2,000 of these is called a krośa by the learned. Four of them are a *yojana*. Vyāsa is saying this.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In Jambūdvīpa there are nine continents, each is 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long. Here *length* denotes area. This is to be taken for six only by the maxim of *chhatri*: i.e. “under the umbrella”; when many persons are said to be under the same umbrella, although only one or a few hold the umbrella, others beneath it (not holding it) are also referred to as “under the umbrella.” The other three islands among them having a 34,000-*yojana* \[272,000 mile\] length and the six islands with their boundary mountains amount to 66,000 *yojanas* \[528,000 miles\], totaling one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. “Two of the *varṣas* (continents) are to be known as being in the shape of a bow formation to the south and north. Four are linear (longish) among them and Ilāvṛta is square in shape.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“In which” means Jambūdvīpa; nine continents (regions) are well-demarcated by eight mountains serving as their boundaries. Among them, Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya, Kuru, Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa, Bhārata continents are 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] extent each. This area includes the boundary mountains from north to south. These extend from east to west unto the salty sea on either side and are longer. Ilāvṛta is from east to west 82,000 *yojanas* \[656,000 miles\] wide and from north to south, 46,000 *yojanas* \[368,000 miles\] wide. Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla are each from east to west 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] wide. From north to south, they extend till Niṣadha and Nīla mountains.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*In which* means Jambūdvīpa; Ilāvṛta, Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya, Kuru, Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa, Bhārata, Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva are the nine *varṣas* (continents), each 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long. The Viṣṇu-Purāṇa also corroborates this. The length here is the extent to be taken for the middle line going from north to south. This excludes Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla as they are 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\] long. Their configuration is said in the *Vāyu Purāṇa* as follows:

“Two of the varṣas (continents) are to be known as being in the shape of a bow formation to the south and north. Four are linear (longish) among them and Ilāvṛta is square in shape.”

Ilāvṛta's square shape is illustrative of the square shape of Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla also. Some, in order to comply with the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* description, interpret their lengths also as 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] by taking their contiguous ends as having entered into the sea between the Nīla and Niṣadha mountains, demarcated well by the eight mountains Nīla, Śveta, Śṛṅgavat, Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa, Himālaya, Mālyavad and Gandhamādana.

### Text 7

*एषां मध्ये इलावृतं नामाभ्यन्तरवर्षं यस्य नाभ्यामवस्थितः सर्वतः सौवर्णःकुलगिरिराजो*  
*मेरुर्द्वीपायामसमुन्नाहः कर्णिकाभूतः कुवलयकमलस्य मूर्धनि द्वात्रिंशत्सहस्र*  
*योजनविततो मूले षोडशसहस्रं तावतान्तर्भूम्यां प्रविष्टः ॥७॥*

*eṣāṁ madhye ilāvṛtaṁ nāmābhyantara-varṣaṁ yasya nābhyām avasthitaḥ sarvataḥ sauvarṇaḥ kula-giri-rājo merur dvīpāyāma-samunnāhaḥ karṇikā-bhūtaḥ kuvalaya-kamalasya mūrdhani dvā-triṁśat sahasra-yojana-vitato mūle ṣoḍaśa-sahasraṁ tāvat āntar-bhūmyāṁ praviṣṭaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṣām—all these divisions of Jambūdvīpa; madhye—among; ilāvṛtam nāma—named Ilāvṛta-varṣa; abhyantara-varṣam—the inner division; yasya—of which; nābhyām—in the navel; avasthitaḥ—situated; sarvataḥ—entirely; sauvarṇaḥ—made of gold; kula-giri-rājaḥ—the most famous among famous mountains; meruḥ—Mount Meru; dvīpa-āyāma-samunnāhaḥ—whose height is the same measurement as the width of Jambūdvīpa; karṇikā-bhūtaḥ—existing as the pericarp; kuvalaya—of this planetary system; kamalasya—like a lotus flower; mūrdhani—on the top; dvā-triṁśat—thirty-two; sahasra—thousand; yojana—yojanas (eight miles each; vitataḥ—expanded; mūle—at the base; ṣoḍaśa-sahasram—sixteen thousand yojanas; tāvat—so much; āntaḥ-bhūmyām—within the earth; praviṣṭaḥ—entered.

**Перевод:**

**Amidst these divisions, or varṣas, is the varṣa named Ilāvṛta, which is situated in the middle of the whorl of the lotus. Within Ilāvṛta-varṣa is Sumeru Mountain, which is made of gold. Sumeru Mountain is like the pericarp of the lotuslike Bhū-maṇḍala planetary system. The mountain's height is the same as the width of Jambūdvīpa—or, in other words, 100,000 yojanas \[800,000 miles\]. Of that, 16,000 yojanas \[128,000 miles\] are within the earth, and therefore the mountain's height above the earth is 84,000 yojanas \[672,000 miles\]. The mountain's width is 32,000 yojanas \[256,000 miles\] at its summit and 16,000 yojanas at its base.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In the navel (center/middle), the length of the island is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. That much is the height of Mount Meru. It is 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] wide at the base. By that much, 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] underground and 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] above the surface, the total height is one *lakh yojanas* \[100,000 *yojanas* or 800,000 miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The same is said beginning with *yo vai* etc. This island Jambūdvīpa is well-known. *Kuvalaya* means the periphery of the earth. That is the lotus. Its sheaths are the seven islands. Their innermost sheath is Jambūdvīpa. It is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] in area. It is uniform and circular, i.e, has no corners or sides and hence is of the same size everywhere, just as the leaf of lotus, being round, has same dimensions all around. In the Jambūdvīpa, there are nine continents each 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] long. Length here denotes area. This quantity is for all but Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla, as their configuration is described elsewhere as "Two of the *varṣas* (continents) are to be known as being in the shape of a bow formation to the south and north. Four are linear (longish) among them and Ilāvṛta is square in shape." These are well-demarcated by eight mountains, viz. Nīla, Śveta, Śṛṅgavān, Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa, Himālaya, Mālyavān and Gandhamādana. Of these nine continents, Ilāvṛta continent is the inner one. In the nave of the island, Jambūdvīpa, or on the continent Ilāvṛta, is located the golden Mount Meru, the king of great mountains. It has the same height as the length (area) of the island Jambūdvīpa, i.e one *lakh yojanas*. It is like the pericarp of the lotus of earth (globe) with a 32,000-yojana \[256,000 miles\] expanse at the top (Meru) and at the root is 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] (Sumeru). Items in brackets are the qualifications. If the reading has *yojanam* as neutral gender, then it means a collection of 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\], i.e, the extent is that much. The absence of the feminine suffix is due to the stem of word being an element of the *pātra*, etc. (Śrīmad Bhāgavatam 2.1.48). By the same amount, i.e, 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\], it \[Sumeru\] is hidden beneath the earth's surface. Thus the conclusion is Sumeru is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Eṣāṁ*—of the continents. “In the nave of Ilāvṛta” means in the middle. The height of it (Meru) is equal to the length (extent) of the island Jambūdvīpa, i.e., one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high. After telling the extent, the configuration is said as to be in the form of a pericarp of the lotus (earth-globe). But how can the description that one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] is the extent of the island and the same is the height of Meru be clear in the light of the statement of Parāśara that Meru is 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] tall? The reply is, “That cannot be known as “it is thus,” since it cannot be described in words, nor inferred or debated. Even highly learned people, although seeing it, do not know the nature and form of Meru.” This sums up the difficulty and also it is plausible that Parāśara could have been mistaken. The mention that Indra saw it as circular while Bṛhaspati saw it as pentagonal also means that deities like Indra etc. also could be mistaken.

It may well be questioned that, “Is it not preposterous to suppose that sages who see past, present and future can mistake things? How could Parāśara having attained divine knowledge by the grace of the Lord, say untrue things?” But since it is established in the light of other authorities, the fact that anyone other than the Lord can theoretically have occasional mistaken notions is admissible. But instead of rejecting one view for another, would it not be great if both views could be reconciled? Alas! Then listen. It is also said that it has entered 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] below. But, if it is said that its height is as much as the length of the earth and has entered into the earth by that much, that would make its height more than one *lakh yojanas*. It is to be countered that including the hidden part, the total height is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]; that makes it 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] above the surface, by proper connection of words in the text (sentence). Also, to mean 84,000, instead of using the normal word “caturaśīti,” the word “caturāśīti” has been used with an additional vowel *“ā,”* also suggests some special significance which is what is mentioned in *Bhāgavata*. The words of Vyāsa, an ocean of infinite wisdom, cannot be doubted, and, according to him, “details regarding the world (earth's sheaths) should be taken as per *Bhāgavata*. Any other text, in case of contradiction, should be reconciled as required.” The completion of *maṇḍoda*, the difference with regard to the milk ocean, twice the quantity of the *maṇḍalas* of Rāhu, Soma and Ravi, are all to be handled so by reconciliation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the nave = middle. The length of the island is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. By that much = an amount of 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\]. Hence, 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] is visible above the earth's surface.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Between these continents are the great mountains beginning with Mahendra etc. and that is said in *Mahābhārata*: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, Īkṣavān, Vindhya and Pāriyātra are the seven great mountain ranges (kula girayaḥ).

The king of these mountains is Meru. The compound word *kulagirirāja* is ending in the vowel *“a”* as described by the grammatical aphorism rājā'hassa khibhyaṣṭac." “Ṭac” is a compound ending affix although *rājan* is a consonant ending in *“n.” Vitata* means extant. *Antarbhūmyāṁ* means in the center of the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In the nave (middle) of Ilāvṛta, Meru is situated. The length of the island Jambūdvīpa is one *lakh yojanas*; that much height is Meru. By that much = an amount of 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Among these continents, the interior region Ilāvṛta is square in shape. In the middle of Ilāvṛta is Mount Meru, which is golden throughout and, being the best among great mountains, is as high as the island's extent; Jambūdvīpa's extent is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. Meru is situated as the pericarp of the lotus of the globe.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Among these nine continents, Ilāvṛta is the innermost. In the middle of Ilāvṛta, or Jambūdvīpa, is located the Mount Meru. Meru is golden all around, i.e. no part of it is not golden. It is the king of great mountains, i.e, great like a king. The *kulagiris* (great mountains) are enumerated in the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* as follows: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, Ṛkṣa, Vindhya and Pāriyātra are the seven. Meru is as tall as the extent of the island Jambūdvīpa, i.e, one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. The earth's shell is like a lotus; Meru is like its cap or pericarp. The definitions of *anekārtha saṁgraha* are “earring and pollen-case of a lotus” for the word “karṇikā.” Hence, Meru is in the middle region of the earth-shell in the nave of Jambūdvīpa, analogous to the central location of the pollen-case of a lotus.

### Text 8

*उत्तरोत्तरेणेलावृतं नीलः श्वेतः शृङ्गवानिति त्रयो रम्यकहिरण्मयकुरूणां वर्षाणां*  
*मर्यादागिरयः प्रागायता उभयतः क्षारोदावधयो द्विसहस्रपृथव एकैकशः*  
*पूर्वस्मात्पूर्वस्मादुत्तर उत्तरो दशांशाधिकांशेन दैर्घ्य एव ह्रसन्ति ॥८॥*

*uttarottareṇelāvṛtaṁ nīlaḥ śvetaḥ śṛṅgavān iti trayo ramyaka-hiraṇmaya-kurūṇāṁ varṣāṇāṁ maryādā-girayaḥ prāg-āyatā ubhayataḥ kṣārodāvadhayo dvi-sahasra-pṛthava ekaikaśaḥ pūrvasmāt pūrvasmād uttara uttaro daśāṁśādhikāṁśena dairghya eva hrasanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

uttara-uttareṇa ilāvṛtam—further and further north of Ilāvṛta-varṣa; nīlaḥ—Nīla; śvetaḥ—Śveta; śṛṅgavān—Śṛṅgavān; iti—thus; trayaḥ—three mountains; ramyaka—Ramyaka; hiraṇmaya—Hiraṇmaya; kurūṇām—of the Kuru division; varṣāṇām—of the varṣas; maryādā-girayaḥ—the mountains marking the borders; prāk-āyatāḥ—extended on the eastern side; ubhayataḥ—to the east and the west; kṣāroda—the ocean of salt water; avadhayaḥ—extending to; dvi-sahasra-pṛthavaḥ—which are two thousand yojanas wide; eka-ekaśaḥ—one after another; pūrvasmāt—than the former; pūrvasmāt—than the former; uttaraḥ—further north; uttaraḥ—further north; daśa-aṁśa-adhika-aṁśena—by one tenth of the former; dairghyaḥ—in length; eva—indeed; hrasanti—become shorter.

**Перевод:**

**Just north of Ilāvṛta-varṣa—and going further northward, one after another—are three mountains named Nīla, Śveta and Śṛṅgavān. These mark the borders of the three varṣas named Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru and separate them from one another. The width of these mountains is 2,000 yojanas \[16,000 miles\]. Lengthwise, they extend east and west to the beaches of the ocean of salt water. Going from south to north, the length of each mountain is one tenth that of the previous mountain, but the height of them all is the same.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Towards the north of Ilāvṛta successively are the three boundary mountains named Nīla, Śveta, and Śṛṅgavān respectively. They are wide in the front and long on the eastern side. They have as their limit, the salt water sea. They are each 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and reduce by a little more than 10% in length only and not in height or girth. As told in the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*:

*“Two in the middle measure one lakh (100,000) yojanas and the others reduce by a tenth.”*

This is to be taken in a gross perspective only, as they are not actually the middle ones and hence are not of one *lakh* (100,000) measure.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

To the north of Ilāvṛta-varṣa, one after another respectively are Nīla, Śveta, Śṛṅgavān mountains being the boundary markers of the three continents Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru. They are long on the eastern side. Extending to the salt sea on both east and west, they are 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide, reduced by more than 10% in length only, i.e, not in girth or height. Since the island is circular, in the latter mountains like Nīla, Śveta, Śṛṅgavān, compared to the earlier ones, are lesser in length by more than 10%.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

From Ilāvṛta continent further northwards—by peaks on the eastern side, in curved shape, long on the east, 2,000 wide, 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] high and reduce in length only, not width and height.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Northwards of Ilāvṛta = to the north of Ilāvṛta, on both sides, i.e., east-west directions. *Thick* = wide. *From each* (preceding) = in length. Nīla is a little less than one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. From there Śveta, and thence, Śṛṅgavān by an amount a little more than 10% each.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Ubhayata*: Nīla and Niṣadha ranges (on the north and south of Ilavrta) both extend from east to west. This is also a sentence in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Northwards of Ilāvṛta = towards the north of Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Explaining the dimensions of Meru, its being in the (center-top) as pericarp is justified thus: It is 32,000 *yojanas* \[256,000 miles\]wide at the top and 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] wide at the base; by the same amount it is hidden inside the earth. Thus 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] is visible above the earth. Thus it is to be known that it is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] tall.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

At the summit, Meru is 32,000 *yojanas* \[256,000 miles\] wide. Like a golden tree which is wider at the top, it is 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] at the root. By that much (16,000 *yojanas*) \[128,000 miles\] it is hidden inside the earth. 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] are visible outside. Thus, Meru is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high. To the northwards of Ilāvṛta, are the mountains Nīla, Śveta and Śṛṅgavān respectively. (The word “uttareṇa” is derived with the “enap” suffix in the locative (seventh) case sense and should not be mistaken as instrumental (third) case-ending). These three mountains are the boundary-hills of the three continents Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru *varṣas*. These are longish eastwards and extend unto the salty sea on either sides (east and west). Since they are said to extend unto the salty sea on either sides, the description that they are longish eastwards becomes redundant. Hence, we should take their shape to be in the form of cow-tail, which is wide at the base and narrow at the tip. Thus, they are wider at the eastern side and relatively narrower at the western side. They are each 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] in girth. The height is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] as will be described. Each of these (three) reduce in length only, by more than 10% than the previous one's length. But this reduction is not in height or thickness, because the island is circular in shape. As is said the in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “Two are in the middle with a one-*lakh* (100,000) magnitude and others are a tenth less.” In the *Vārāha Purāṇa*, it is said: “Niṣadha is described with the dimension of Jambūdvīpa. A tenth less than that is Hemakūṭa.” This is to be taken as generally stated, since they also are not actually at the middle and hence do not extend one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\].

### Text 9

*एवं दक्षिणेनेलावृतं निषधो हेमकूटो हिमालय इति प्रागायता यथा नीलादयो*  
*ऽयुतयोजनोत्सेधा हरिवर्षकिम्पुरुषभारतानां यथासङ्ख्यम् ॥९॥*

*evaṁ dakṣiṇenelāvṛtaṁ niṣadho hemakūṭo himālaya iti prāg-āyatā yathā nīlādayo 'yuta-yojanotsedhā hari-varṣa-kimpuruṣa-bhāratānāṁ yathā-saṅkhyam*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; dakṣiṇena—by degrees to the southern side; ilāvṛtam—of Ilāvṛta-varṣa; niṣadhaḥ hema-kūṭaḥ himālayaḥ—three mountains named Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa and Himālaya; iti—thus; prāk-āyatāḥ—extended to the east; yathā—just as; nīla-ādayaḥ—the mountains headed by Nīla; ayuta-yojana-utsedhāḥ—ten thousand yojanas high; hari-varṣa—the division named Hari-varṣa; kimpuruṣa—the division named Kimpuruṣa; bhāratānām—the division named Bhārata-varṣa; yathā-saṅkhyam—according to number.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, south of Ilāvṛta-varṣa and extending from east to west are three great mountains named (from north to south) Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa and Himālaya. Each of them is 10,000 yojanas \[80,000 miles\] high. They mark the boundaries of the three varṣas named Hari-varṣa, Kimpuruṣa-varṣa and Bhārata-varṣa \[India\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

10,000 *yojanas* is the height of these. This height is also for Nīla etc. The girth of Nīla etc. is also to be taken for these. Respectively “these are boundary-hills” is to be added.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Thus to the south of Ilāvṛta varṣa, the three mountains Niṣadha etc., respectively, of the same size as Nīla etc., (10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high and wide) are the boundary-markers of the three *varṣas* Harivarṣa, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Thus to the south of Ilāvṛta, the three mountains Niṣadha etc., like Nīla etc., reduce in length (successively from the previous ones). The difference is Nīla and Niṣadha are one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] long and the rest are shorter by 10%. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: "Two in the middle are one *lakh* (100,000) in size while the rest are 10% less." In the Vārāha Purāṇa, it is said: "Niṣadha is equal to Jambūdvīpa in magnitude. Hemakūṭa is perceived to be 10% less than that." In this way, the boundary-markers are described.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

10,000 *yojana* \[80,000 miles\] high = this height is to be taken for Nīla etc. also. The width of Nīla etc. is also to be taken for these.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The girth of Nīla etc. = 2,000 *yojanas* in extent.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Thus Nīla, Niṣadha etc. are also 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide each and are, respectively, the boundary mountains of Harivarṣa etc. 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high = this height is to be taken for Nīla etc. also.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Tells about the division of continents by mentioning the boundary—north of Ilāvṛta. To the north of Ilāvṛta are the three; Nīla, Śveta and Śṛṇgavān, as demarcations of boundaries of the *varṣas* Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru respectively. Being longish from east to west and touching the salty sea as the limit on either side, they are each 2,000 (*yojanas*) \[16,000 miles\] thick. *Height* is to be taken as 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\]. From the previous (northern) ones, successively, the ones situated southwards are lesser in length by a little over 10%. As these islands are circular, the height and width are the same for all. Only in length there is a reduction.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The suffix “ena” on the stem dakṣiṇa, is to be understood in the locative sense. Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa and Himālaya are three mountains. These are also longish on the eastern side and of the same size as Nīla etc. Being 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high, \[this has to be taken for the height and width of Nīla etc.\] these mark the boundaries for the three *varṣas* Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa and Bhārata, respectively.

### Text 10

*तथैवेलावृतमपरेण पूर्वेण च माल्यवद्गन्धमादनावानीलनिषधायतौ द्विसहस्रं*  
*पप्रथतुः केतुमालभद्राश्वयोः सीमानं विदधाते ॥१०॥*

*tathaivelāvṛtam apareṇa pūrveṇa ca mālyavad-gandhamādanāv ānīla-niṣadhāyatau dvi-sahasraṁ paprathatuḥ ketumāla-bhadrāśvayoḥ sīmānaṁ vidadhāte*

**Пословный перевод:**

tathā eva—exactly like that; ilāvṛtam apareṇa—on the western side of Ilāvṛta-varṣa; pūrveṇa ca—and on the eastern side; mālyavad-gandha-mādanau—the demarcation mountains of Mālyavān on the west and Gandhamādana on the east; ā-nīla-niṣadha-āyatau—on the northern side up to the mountain known as Nīla and on the southern side up to the mountain known as Niṣadha; dvi-sahasram—two thousand yojanas; paprathatuḥ—they extend; ketumāla-bhadrāśvayoḥ—of the two varṣas named Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva; sīmānam—the border; vidadhāte—establish.

**Перевод:**

**In the same way, west and east of Ilāvṛta-varṣa are two great mountains named Mālyavān and Gandhamādana respectively. These two mountains, which are 2,000 yojanas \[16,000 miles\] high, extend as far as Nīla Mountain in the north and Niṣadha in the south. They indicate the borders of Ilāvṛta-varṣa and also the varṣas known as Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Extending to Nīla and Niṣadha = till Nīla in the north and Niṣadha in the south.

Wide = extent. How can Jambūdvīpa be all around one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] in magnitude? It is thus: Meru is 16,000 all around, Ilāvṛta 18,000, the other six *varṣas* 54,000, six mountains account for 12,000 and hence the total is one *lakh* (100,000) on the south-north axis. On the east-west axis also, Meru and Ilāvṛta account for 34,000, mountains 4,000, and the remaining 62,000 for two *varṣas* on the east and west, flowing unto the salty sea and hence, there is no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, to the west and east of Ilāvṛta, are Mālyavān and Gandhamādana respectively. They extend to Nīla in the north and Niṣadha in the south. They are two thousand *yojanas* wide forming the boundaries of Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva *varṣas*. But, if this be so, then, on the east-west axis, with Meru surrounded by Ilāvṛta in the middle, and the two east-west mountains and two *varṣas*,—nothing else would exist. However, on the south-north axis Meru is surrounded by Ilāvṛta in the middle, then on both sides, there are three *varṣas* and three mountains—in all six; how then can Jambūdvīpa be one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] in circumference? It is like this: Meru is 16,000 around \[128,000 miles\], Ilāvṛta 18,000 \[144,000 miles\], the other six *varṣas* 54,000 \[432,000 miles\], six mountains account for 12,000 and hence the total is one *lakh* (100,000) on the north-south axis. On the east-west axis also, Meru and Ilāvṛta account for 34,000, for mountains 4,000, and the remaining 62,000 for two *varṣas* on the east and west, unto the salty sea. Hence, there is no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Similarly = like Nīla and Niṣadha in the north and south, likewise, to the west and east of Ilāvṛta, are Mālyavān and Gandhamādana respectively. They extend unto Nīla in the north and Niṣadha in the south, touching them. They form the boundaries.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

To the west and east directions; extending until Nīla in the north and Niṣadha in the south; i.e, 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\] long; thus, on the south-north axis—the three continents Bhārata, Kiṁpuruṣa and Harivarṣa are 27,000 *yojanas* \[216,000 miles\]; Himālaya, Hemakūṭa and Niṣadha are 6,000 *yojanas* \[48,000 miles\], Sumeru and Ilāvṛta are 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\], Gandhamādana and Mālyavān are 4,000 *yojanas* \[32,000 miles\], Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru are 27,000 *yojanas*, and mountains Nīla, Śveta and Śṛṅgavān are 6,000 *yojanas* \[48,000 miles\], totaling one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] as the dimension. It is taught, that on the east-west axis Bhadrāṣva is 31,000 *yojanas* \[248,000 miles\], Sumeru and Ilāvṛta are 34,000 *yojanas* \[272,000 miles\], Ketumāla is 31,000 *yojanas* \[248,000 miles\] and Gandhamādana and Mālyavān are 4,000 *yojanas* \[32,000 miles\], totaling one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] as the dimension of Jambūdvīpa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Apareṇa* = to the west; *pūrveṇa* = to the eastern direction. Objects to this as “nanu.”

“Atah” = by such reasoning. No fault = no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*2,000 yojanas wide* = extent; *vidadhāte* = create.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

To the south of Ilāvṛta are the three; Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa and Himālaya mountains which demarcate the boundaries of the *varṣas* Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa and Bhārata, respectively. Being longish from east to west, and touching the salty sea as the limit on either side, they are 2,000 (*yojanas*) wide. The height is to be taken as 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\]. From the previous (northern) mountain ranges, successively, the ones situated southwards are lesser in length only by a little over 10%. The height and width are the same for all.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The same occurs to the west and east of Ilāvṛta. Here also, the suffix “enap” on the stems “apara” and “pūrva,” is to be understood in the locative sense. Being indeclinables, the case-suffixes have been omitted. Mālyavān and Gandhamādana, extending unto Nīla in the north and Niṣadha in the south, are 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide. The height is to be taken as that for Nīla, etc.

### Text 11

*मन्दरो मेरुमन्दरः सुपार्श्वः कुमुद इत्ययुतयोजनविस्तारोन्नाहा मेरो*  
*श्चतुर्दिशमवष्टम्भगिरय उपकॢप्ताः ॥११॥*

*mandaro merumandaraḥ supārśvaḥ kumuda ity ayuta-yojana-vistāronnāhā meroś catur-diśam avaṣṭambha-giraya upakḷptāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

mandaraḥ—the mountain named Mandara; meru-mandaraḥ—the mountain named Merumandara; supārśvaḥ—the mountain named Supārśva; kumudaḥ—the mountain named Kumuda; iti—thus; ayuta-yojana-vistāra-unnāhāḥ—which measure ten thousand yojanas high and wide; meroḥ—of Sumeru; catuḥ-diśam—the four sides; avaṣṭambha-girayaḥ—mountains that are like the belts of Sumeru; upakḷptāḥ—situated.

**Перевод:**

**On the four sides of the great mountain known as Sumeru are four mountains-Mandara, Merumandara, Supārśva and Kumuda—which are like its belts. The length and height of these mountains are calculated to be 10,000 yojanas \[80,000 miles\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] extent and tall each. Wide-topped Meru's support means the eastern and western mountains are from north to south wide and northern and southern mountains are from east to west wide. If the circumference of 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] area is taken, then Ilāvṛta will be excluded and to the east of Ilāvṛta will become submerged. There will be contradictions.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Supporting mountains* = forming like seats or bases.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

10,000 *yojana* \[80,000 miles\] long and tall each; wide-topped Meru's support means eastern and western mountains are wide from north to south, and northern and southern mountains are wide from east to west. If all-round, a 10,000 *yojana* \[80,000 miles\] area is taken, Ilāvṛta will be missed and to the east of Ilāvṛta would become submerged etc. This would be contradictory.

Caturdiṣam—(covering) in all four directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Area* here is length. *Caturdiśam* = (covering) in all four directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Also, Mandara etc. are four mountains respectively from east on the four sides of Meru, made as propping mountains, 10,000 *yojana* \[80,000 miles\] long and tall each; Of these, Mandara is on the east and extends from north to south. Similarly, the others are also to be taken. Thus, Ilāvṛta will not be missed.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Similarly, to the west and east of Ilāvṛta are, Mālyavān and Gandhamādana extending lengthwise unto Nīla in the north, and Niṣadha in the south, which demark the boundaries of the *varṣas* Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva, respectively. Each are 2,000 (*yojanas*) wide. The height is to be taken as 10,000 *yojanas*.
