Thus, to the north of Ilāvṛta, along with the boundary-hills of the *varṣas*, Ramyaka, Hiraṇmaya and Kuru are 27,000 *yojanas* and situated to their south are the *varṣas* Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa and Bhārata. Along with their boundary-hills, they are 27,000 *yojanas*; Ilāvṛta and Meru together are 46,000 *yojanas*; hence, from north to south, Jambūdvīpa is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas*. On the east-west axis, Jambūdvīpa's extent is one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas*, i.e. west of Ilāvṛta (Ketumāla—9,000 *yojanas*) east of Ilāvṛta (Bhadrāśva—9,000 *yojanas*), and between them, Ilāvṛta and Meru together are 82,000 *yojanas*.

Note: But, Śrīdhara Svāmi has taken the six *varṣas* Ramyaka etc. as 54,000 *yojanas*, Meru and Ilāvṛta as 34,000 *yojanas* and the six boundary hills Nīla etc. as 12,000 *yojanas*. Thus on north-south axis, it is one *lakh yojanas* (100,000 *yojanas*); and on the east-west axis, Meru and Ilāvṛta are 34,000 *yojanas*. The boundary hills Mālyavān and Gandhamādana are 4,000 *yojanas*, Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva *varṣas* account for the remaining 62,000 *yojanas* and thus the east-west axis is one *lakh yojanas* (100,000 *yojanas*). In that case, assuming Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva to be 31,000 *yojanas* each, is clearly contradictory to the text mentioning the length as 9,000 *yojanas* for all. But then it cannot be argued that as per the text, Ilāvṛta also should be taken as 9,000 *yojanas*, since the distance of a 16,000 *yojana* width at the base of Meru cannot be accommodated. Also, with Ilāvṛta being 34,000 *yojanas*, at its root, Meru having a 16,000 *yojana* base and with four propping hills of 10,000 *yojanas* on four sides cannot be accommodated; and also due to the fear that, as per the ensuing Gaṇgā's descent submerging to the east of Ilāvṛta, becoming contradictory, positing that the eastern and western hills are north-southwise 10,000 *yojanas* long and northern and southern hills are east-westwise 10,000 *yojanas* long is avoided in our interpretation. Ilāvṛta having been taken as 46,000 *yojanas* can allow the propping hills to be 10,000 *yojanas* all around as per text.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

These form the boundaries of Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva varṣa respectively. But, if this be so, then, on the east-west axis, where Meru is surrounded by Ilāvṛta in the middle and these two *varṣas* and two mountains are on either side, there would be no room for anything else. Similarly, on the south-north axis, Meru is surrounded by Ilāvṛta in the middle, and on both sides three *varṣas* and three mountains (in all six). How then can Jambūdvīpa be one *lakh* (100,000) *yojanas* in magnitude? We reply: Meru being 16,000 in circumference and having south-north and east-west axes in its middle, becomes 8,000 on either side. Thus, Ilāvṛta, without Meru, on south-north and east-west axes, remains 9,000 on either side. Then, 18,000 for Ilāvṛta, 16,000 for Meru, 54,000 for the other six *varṣas*, six mountains account for 12,000 and hence the total is one *lakh* (100,000) on the south-north axis.

On the east-west axis however, Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla are 34,000 each, along with 4,000 for two mountains amounts to 106,000 *yojanas*. How to reconcile this? It is thus: Meru and Ilāvṛta account for 34,000, 4,000 for mountains and the remaining 62,000 is to be divided as 31,000 each for the two *varṣas* Ketumāla and Bhadrāśva on east and west since they are said to be extending unto the salt water ocean. Their length mentioned as 34,000 is to be taken on the south-north axis and thus, there is no contradiction.

### Text 12

*चतुर्ष्वे तेषु चूतजम्बूकदम्बन्यग्रोधाश्चत्वारः पादप प्रवराः पर्वतकेतव इवाधि*  
*सहस्रयोजनोन्नाहास्तावद् विटपविततयः शतयोजनपरिणाहाः ॥१२॥*

*caturṣv eteṣu cūta-jambū-kadamba-nyagrodhāś catvāraḥ pādapa-pravarāḥ parvata-ketava ivādhi-sahasra-yojanonnāhās tāvad viṭapa-vitatayaḥ śata-yojana-pariṇāhāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

caturṣu—on the four; eteṣu—on these mountains, beginning with Mandara; cūta-jambū-kadamba—of trees such as the mango, rose apple and kadamba; nyagrodhāḥ—and the banyan tree; catvāraḥ—four kinds; pādapa-pravarāḥ—the best of trees; parvata-ketavaḥ—the flagstaffs on the mountains; iva—like; adhi—over; sahasra-yojana-unnāhāḥ—one thousand yojanas high; tāvat—so much also; viṭapa-vitatayaḥ—the length of the branches; śata-yojana—one hundred yojanas; pariṇāhāḥ—wide.

**Перевод:**

**Standing like flagstaffs on the summits of these four mountains are a mango tree, a rose apple tree, a kadamba tree and a banyan tree. Those trees are calculated to have a width of 100 yojanas \[800 miles\] and a height of 1,100 yojanas \[8,800 miles\]. Their branches also spread to a radius of 1,100 yojanas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

One thousand one hundred *yojanas* in height.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The covering of branches (of trees) is as much as the height in *yojanas*. “*Surrounding thickness” is denoted by “pariṇāha”* = circumference. “The trees, as mountain-posts (flags), are 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] long,” as known from other *Purāṇas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The four mountains in four directions from east such as Mandara, etc., are meant for support of Meru, like a belt. Each of these is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] extent and tall. On these four mountains, are the four great trees, mango, jambū, kadamba and banyan, respectively. They are like the flags on the mountains, in groups of branches, one thousand one hundred *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] high and one hundred *yojanas* \[800 miles\] in periphery.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] across and 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] height are the dimensions of the avenue of branched trees.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] long and tall; the four mountains in the four directions from Meru, namely Mandara, etc. are meant for support and are created by the Supreme Lord. They are all golden, in the shape of a churning staff and are known from the reference in the 8th Skandha \[canto of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*\] as: “The golden hill which crushed the demigods and demons by its weight.” They were using Mandara for churning the milk-ocean.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Mandara, Merumandara, Supārṣva and Kumuda, the four mountains, are each 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] tall and wide. Being the props for Meru which is wider at the top, the eastern and western mountains run south-northwise wide while the southern and northern mountains run east-west wise in width. If a 10,000-*yojana* \[80,000 miles\] width is taken all around, in all four directions being less by 9,000 than Meru, Ilāvṛta would become eliminated. However, submerging Ilāvṛta on the east would create a contradiction. In the four directions from the east of Meru, means they are designed for support.

### Text 13-14

*ह्रदाश्चत्वारः पयोमध्विक्षुरसमृष्टजला यदुपस्पर्शिन उपदेवगणा योगैश्वर्याणि*  
*स्वाभाविकानि भरतर्षभ धारयन्ति ॥१३॥ देवो द्यानानि च भवन्ति*  
*चत्वारि नन्दनं चैत्ररथं वैभ्राजकं सर्वतोभद्रमिति ॥१४॥*

*hradāś catvāraḥ payo-madhv-ikṣurasa-mṛṣṭa-jalā yad-upasparśina upadeva-gaṇā yogaiśvaryāṇi svābhāvikāni bharatarṣabha dhārayanti; devodyānāni ca bhavanti catvāri nandanaṁ caitrarathaṁ vaibhrājakaṁ sarvatobhadram iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

hradāḥ—lakes; catvāraḥ—four; payaḥ—milk; madhu—honey; ikṣu-rasa—sugarcane juice; mṛṣṭa-jalāḥ—filled with pure water; yat—of which; upasparśinaḥ—those who use the liquids; upadeva-gaṇāḥ—the demigods; yoga-aiśvaryāṇi—all the perfections of mystic yoga; svābhāvikāni—without being tried for; bharata-ṛṣabha—O best of the Bharata dynasty; dhārayanti—possess; deva-udyānāni—celestial gardens; ca—also; bhavanti—there are; catvāri—four; nandanam—of the Nandana garden; caitra-ratham—Caitraratha garden; vaibhrājakam—Vaibhrājaka garden; sarvataḥ-bhadram—Sarvatobhadra garden; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, best of the Bharata dynasty, between these four mountains are four huge lakes. The water of the first tastes just like milk; the water of the second, like honey; and that of the third, like sugarcane juice. The fourth lake is filled with pure water. The celestial beings such as the Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Gandharvas, who are also known as demigods, enjoy the facilities of those four lakes. Consequently they have the natural perfections of mystic yoga, such as the power to become smaller than the smallest or greater than the greatest. There are also four celestial gardens named Nandana, Caitraratha, Vaibhrājaka and Sarvatobhadra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Four deep lakes of milk, honey, sugarcane juice and pure water—O great one among Bharatas, groups of Siddhas bathe there and attain the eight great powers.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

On these four mountains, Mandara, etc. trees of 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] tall are like the flags. It is said: “The trees as mountain-posts (flags) are 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] long.” Here, *by length* is meant *height*. The coverage of branches (of the trees) is as much as the height in *yojanas*, 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] high and 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] in periphery.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The coverage of branches (of trees) is the same as the height in *yojanas*; groups of branches are 1,100 *yojanas* high and 100 *yojanas* in periphery.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Mṛṣṭa* = pure (water); *milk, madhu* = honey made from sugarcane juice and pure water. The suffix here is “ac” in the sense of “it is there in it” (*Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 5.2.127 and 5.2.94). “Bharatarṣabha” etc. = you also naturally possess such power, being the descendant of the great king Bharata. Hence, you don't aspire for such places.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The words “are made” are to be supplied after *deep lakes*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

On top of these four mountains, Mandara etc, stand four great trees, mango etc., appearing like flags 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] high and 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] in periphery.  
By bathing in these four deep lakes (one in each mountain), the Siddhas and others attain eight mystic powers such as that of becoming atomic in size etc. The address, “O great among Bharatas!” denotes wonderment.

### Text 15

*येष्वमर परिवृढाः सह सुरललनाललामयूथपतय उपदेवगणैरुपगीयमानमहिमानः*  
*किल विहरन्ति ॥१५॥*

*yeṣv amara-parivṛḍhāḥ saha sura-lalanā-lalāma-yūtha-pataya upadeva-gaṇair upagīyamāna-mahimānaḥ kila viharanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

yeṣu—in which; amara-parivṛḍhāḥ—the best of the demigods; saha—with; sura-lalanā—of the wives of all the demigods and semi-demigods; lalāma—of those women who are like ornaments; yūtha-patayaḥ—the husbands; upadeva-gaṇaiḥ—by the semi-demigods (the Gandharvas); upagīyamāna—being chanted; mahimānaḥ—whose glories; kila—indeed; viharanti—they enjoy sports.

**Перевод:**

**The best of the demigods, along with their wives, who are like ornaments of heavenly beauty, meet together and enjoy within those gardens, while their glories are sung by lesser demigods known as Gandharvas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Lalāma* = ornament; *those who are like adornments for divine damsels* = the best of ladies. Where demigods make merry.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Nandana and other divine gardens serve as sporting arenas for the demigods and their damsels while the Gandharvas sing their praise.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Parivṛḍhāḥ* = best; *lalāma* = ornament.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Masters of deities. *Prabhau parivṛḍhāḥ* (*Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 7.2.21) denotes *lord, master*. Wherein = (in which) gardens; *deputy-deities* = Gandharvas etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Beginning with Nandana, four divine gardens adorn the four mountains.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Divine gardens named Nandana, Caitraratha, Vaibhrājaka and Sarvatobhadra exist also in these mountains.

### Text 16

*मन्दरोत्सङ्ग एकादशशतयोजनोत्तुङ्गदेवचूतशिरसो गिरिशिखरस्थूलानि*  
*फलान्यमृतकल्पानि पतन्ति ॥१६॥*

*mandarotsaṅga ekādaśa-śata-yojanottuṅga-devacūta-śiraso giri-śikhara-sthūlāni phalāny amṛta-kalpāni patanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

mandara-utsaṅge—on the lower slopes of Mandara Mountain; ekādaśa-śata-yojana-uttuṅga—1,100 yojanas high; devacūta-śirasaḥ—from the top of a mango tree named Devacūta; giri-śikhara-sthūlāni—which are as fat as mountain peaks; phalāni—fruit; amṛta-kalpāni—as sweet as nectar; patanti—fall down.

**Перевод:**

**On the lower slopes of Mandara Mountain is a mango tree named Devacūta. It is 1,100 yojanas high. Mangoes as big as mountain peaks and as sweet as nectar fall from the top of this tree for the enjoyment of the denizens of heaven.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The *Vāyu Purāṇa* describes: “From that divine mango tree (1,100 *yojanas* tall) sages have told, come fruits the size of 861 *aratnis* (an *aratni* is the distance of a man’s elbow to his finger-tip).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The *Vāyu Purāṇa* describes: “Below the summit of Mandara, from that divine mango tree (1,100 *yojanas* tall) sages have told, come fruits the size of 861 *aratnis* (an *aratni* is the distance of a man’s elbow to his finger-tip).”

Nectar-like ripened fruit is like saying the “goer goes” (or e.g., “the cook cooks”). The primary derivative suffix qualifies the action hence the verbal root meaning is not intended. The intended meaning is that the fruits ripen and remain so due to lack of consumers. \[Note: this comment is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*In the lap of Mandara* = slope; *from the top of* = tip region. Fit for consumption of deities and so on is a divine mango tree.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The size of the fruit is said in the *Vāyu Purāṇa* as, "Sages who directly and truly perceive entities said the fruits are 861 *aratnis* (elbow to fist) in size."

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Divine mango. As per the *Amara Dictionary*, *aratni* denotes the “closed fist” (i.e, the distance from one’s elbow to his fist).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Those who are like adornments for divine damsels, the best of deities, enjoy.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The best of the devas, the singing Gandharvas and other attractive celestials enjoy in the divine gardens according to their rank.

*Kila*—meaning *indeed*, is to clear doubt.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Wherein* indicates “in which divine gardens” great demigods, along with the best of divine damsels, enjoy themselves while their praises are sung by groups of subordinates.

### Text 17

*तेषां विशीर्यमाणानामतिमधुरसुरभिसुगन्धि बहुलारुणरसोदेनारुणोदा नाम नदी*  
*मन्दरगिरिशिखरान्निपतन्ती पूर्वेणेलावृतमुपप्लावयति ॥१७॥*

*teṣāṁ viśīryamāṇānām ati-madhura-surabhi-sugandhi-bahulāruṇa-rasodenāruṇodā nāma nadī mandara-giri-śikharān nipatantī pūr-veṇelāvṛtam upaplāvayati*

**Пословный перевод:**

teṣām—of all the mangoes; viśīryamāṇānām—being broken because of falling from the top; ati-madhura—very sweet; surabhi—fragrant; sugandhi—scented with other aromas; bahula—large quantities; aruṇa-rasa-udena—by reddish juice; aruṇodā—Aruṇodā; nāma—named; nadī—the river; mandara-giri-śikharāt—from the top of Mandara Mountain; nipatantī—falling down; pūrveṇa—on the eastern side; ilāvṛtam—through Ilāvṛta-varṣa; upaplāvayati—flows.

**Перевод:**

**When all those solid fruits fall from such a height, they break, and the sweet, fragrant juice within them flows out and becomes increasingly more fragrant as it mixes with other scents. That juice cascades from the mountain in waterfalls and becomes a river called Aruṇodā, which flows pleasantly through the eastern side of Ilāvṛta.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Very sweet, pleasantly fragrant, indicates, “not scented by other aromas.” Variegated and reddish (taste) means, “that itself is the water.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Those exploding mango fruits submerge the eastern side of Ilāvṛta, i.e, “deluging it.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The variegated, reddish juice oozing out of the sweet, naturally fragrant (not scented by others) falling fruits explode to form the famous river named Aruṇodā. It descends from the summit of Mandara and flows down to the eastern part of Ilāvṛta continent. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The juice of the sweet, fragrant fruit forms the river flowing down the eastern side of the Ilāvṛta continent. Some take the meaning of the verbal root *dhāvu*, to cleanse, which then means that, “the region gets cleaned with the flow of this river.”

### Text 18

*यदुपजोषणाद्भवान्या अनुचरीणां पुण्यजनवधूनामवयवस्पर्शसुगन्धवातो*  
*दशयोजनं समन्तादनुवासयति ॥१८॥*

*yad-upajoṣaṇād bhavānyā anucarīṇāṁ puṇya-jana-vadhūnām avayava-sparśa-sugandha-vāto daśa-yojanaṁ samantād anuvāsayati*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—of which; upajoṣaṇāt—because of using the fragrant water; bhavānyāḥ—of Bhavānī, the wife of Lord Śiva; anucarīṇām—of attendant maidservants; puṇya-jana-vadhūnām—who are wives of the most pious Yakṣas; avayava—of the bodily limbs; sparśa—from contact; sugandha-vātaḥ—the wind, which becomes fragrant; daśa-yojanam—up to ten yojanas (about eighty miles); samantāt—all around; anuvāsayati—makes fragrant.

**Перевод:**

**The pious wives of the Yakṣas act as personal maidservants to assist Bhavānī, the wife of Lord Śiva. Because they drink the water of the River Aruṇodā, their bodies become fragrant, and as the air carries away that fragrance, it perfumes the entire atmosphere for eighty miles around.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By consuming whose “essence” means “taste.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Describes the river Aruṇodā—by consuming whose juice, the wives of Pārvatī's attendants emit fragrance from their body (limbs). The wind carries this fragrance up to ten *yojanas* \[80 miles\] all around.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Upajoṣa*—consuming. *Anucarī*—servant maid. *Anuvāsana*—making fragrant.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Naturally fragrant and scented by others too.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Puṇyajana ladies*—Yakṣa ladies. *Anuvāsana*— making fragrant.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By consuming whose juice.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The falling fruits produce the very sweet, fragrant, scented, variegated, reddish juice which forms the liquid of the river *Aruṇodā*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

By the falling down and breaking of the fruits, very sweet, fragrant, solidified, red colored juice forms the liquid of a famous river called *Aruṇodā*. Descending from the peak of Mandara mountain, it flows down and sprinkles the eastern side of Ilāvṛta continent. Some (commentators) take *upadhāvati* as a verb meaning “to cleanse,” thus, the meaning is “the river cleans them by its flow.” The root of *upadhāvati* is *dhāvu gati-ṣuddhyoḥ.*

### Text 19

*एवं जम्बूफलानामत्युच्चनिपातविशीर्णानामनस्थिप्रायाणामिभकायनिभानां रसेन*  
*जम्बू नाम नदी मेरुमन्दरशिखरादयुतयोजनादवनितले निपतन्ती दक्षिणेना*  
*त्मानं यावदिलावृतमुपस्यन्दयति ॥१९॥*

*evaṁ jambū-phalānām atyucca-nipāta-viśīrṇānām anasthi-prāyāṇām ibha-kāya-nibhānāṁ rasena jambū nāma nadī meru-mandara-śikharād ayuta-yojanād avani-tale nipatantī dakṣiṇenātmānaṁ yāvad ilāvṛtam upasyandayati*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—similarly; jambū-phalānām—of the fruits called jambū (the rose apple); ati-ucca-nipāta—because of falling from a great height; viśīrṇānām—which are broken to pieces; anasthi-prāyāṇām—having very small seeds; ibha-kāya-nibhānām—and which are as large as the bodies of elephants; rasena—by the juice; jambū nāma nadī—a river named Jambū-nadī; meru-mandara-śikharāt—from the top of Merumandara Mountain; ayuta-yojanāt—ten thousand yojanas high; avani-tale—on the ground; nipatantī—falling; dakṣiṇena—on the southern side; ātmānam—itself; yāvat—the whole; ilāvṛtam—Ilāvṛta-varṣa; upasyandayati—flows through.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, the fruits of the jambū tree, which are full of pulp and have very small seeds, fall from a great height and break to pieces. Those fruits are the size of elephants, and the juice gliding from them becomes a river named Jambū-nadī. This river falls a distance of 10,000 yojanas, from the summit of Merumandara to the southern side of Ilāvṛta, and floods the entire land of Ilāvṛta with juice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Not with many pits,” indicates “with very small seeds.” “From where it falls” indicates “flows towards south, covering Ilāvṛta completely.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Thus, the fruit of Jambū, of the size of an elephant and having small seeds fall from the great height of the plateau of Meru and Mandara. Upon falling, juice comes out forming the famous river Jambūnadī which descends to earth, from the 10,000 *yojana* \[80,000 miles\] high Merumandara. From there it flows to the south of Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Not boney” means *with very small seeds*. On the south of Ilāvṛta, extends till its end = *flowing for 9,000 yojanas* \[72,000 miles\] is the meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

From where it falls, to the south of it, fully submerges Ilāvṛta. But Cakravartī \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\] explains as, “On the southern side, up to where Ilāvṛta is, up to there it grows (expands) emerging up to 9,000 *yojanas* \[72,000 miles\].”

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*“Not boney”*—small seeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

By consuming (drinking) whose juice.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Aruṇodā River is described further—by consuming or drinking whose juice—just by the contact of bodies of Pārvatī's maids, the wives of demons, the wind becomes very fragrant for up to 10 *yojanas* \[80 miles\]. \[i.e. their bodies are so fragrant\]

### Text 20-21

*तावदुभयोरपि रोधसोर्या मृत्तिका तद्रसेनानुविध्यमाना वाय्वर्कसंयोगविपाकेन*  
*सदामरलोकाभरणं जाम्बूनदं नाम सुवर्णं भवति ॥२०॥ यदु ह वाव विबुधा*  
*दयः सह युवतिभिर्मुकुटकटककटिसूत्राद्याभरणरूपेण खलु धारयन्ति ॥२१॥*

*tāvad ubhayor api rodhasor yā mṛttikā tad-rasenānuvidhyamānā vāyv-arka-saṁyoga-vipākena sadāmara-lokābharaṇaṁ jāmbū-nadaṁ nāma suvarṇaṁ bhavati; yad u ha vāva vibudhādayaḥ saha yuvatibhir mukuṭa-kaṭaka-kaṭi-sūtrādy-ābharaṇa-rūpeṇa khalu dhārayanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāvat—entirely; ubhayoḥ api—of both; rodhasoḥ—of the banks; yā—which; mṛttikā—the mud; tat-rasena—with the juice of the jambū fruits that flows in the river; anuvidhyamānā—being saturated; vāyu-arka-saṁyoga-vipākena—because of a chemical reaction with the air and sunshine; sadā—always; amara-loka-ābharaṇam—which is used for the ornaments of the demigods, the denizens of the heavenly planets; jāmbū-nadam nāma—named Jāmbū-nada; suvarṇam—gold; bhavati—becomes; yat—which; u ha vāva—indeed; vibudha-ādayaḥ—the great demigods; saha—with; yuvatibhiḥ—their everlastingly youthful wives; mukuṭa—crowns; kaṭaka—bangles; kaṭi-sūtra—belts; ādi—and so on; ābharaṇa—of all kinds of ornaments; rūpeṇa—in the form; khalu—indeed; dhārayanti—they possess.

**Перевод:**

**The mud on both banks of the River Jambū-nadī, being moistened by the flowing juice and then dried by the air and the sunshine, produces huge quantities of gold called Jāmbū-nada. The denizens of heaven use this gold for various kinds of ornaments. Therefore all the inhabitants of the heavenly planets and their youthful wives are fully decorated with golden helmets, bangles and belts, and thus they enjoy life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Filling the banks of the rivers all around.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Unto where it flows over Ilāvṛta, the mud on both banks of it, being mixed with the juice becomes the gold named *Jāmbūnada*, due to the contact of wind and sun. This gold is always used for making the ornaments for divinities. This gold is worn in the form of crowns etc. by demigods along with their divine damsels.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

"The size of an elephant" is meant to perceive the fullness and not actual dimension. The actual size is mentioned in *Vāyu Purāṇa* as: "Sages who directly and truly perceive entities have told the fruit to be 861 *aratnis* (distance from elbow to finger-tip) in size."

From the summit 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high is to be known as the total height of the mountain from the ground level. In the region where it flows to the south of Ilāvṛta, the soil on either bank, becomes the gold called *Jāmbūnada* due to the impact of the Jambū juice by contact with wind and sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Only the portion of the two banks which hits the juice becomes gold.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Up to there only, the mud which makes contact becomes *jāmbūnada* gold. This is because of the wind, sun etc.

*Which*—the “jāmbūnada” gold. By “etc.” is meant Gandharvas, etc. Again “etc.” refers to earrings and various ornaments.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The river Jambū is formed by the fruit containing very fine seeds and flows to the south covering the entire Ilāvṛta continent. On both her banks—the soil, being wet with juice, gets converted by contact with the wind and sun into *Jāmbūnada* gold. This gold is made into the jewelry of heaven. This is illustrative of humans, Gandharvas, etc.

Deities, along with their consorts, wear this gold in the form of ornaments like crowns, etc. The two indeclinable particles *u ha* and *vāva* denote the amazing greatness of the juice. The indeclinable *khalu* is used to denote certainty.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Likewise, due to the fall from the very tall Merumandara summit, the elephant-sized Jambū fruits with small seeds, grown in the lap of Merumandara, shatter causing their juice to form a renowned river named *Jambū*. They fall 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] from Merumandara's peak to the ground to the south of Ilāvṛta, and flow to its end. Unto where it flows in Ilāvṛta, up to that; the soil on both banks, mixed with the juice of the river, becomes the famed gold called as *Jāmbūnada*, due to the effect of wind and sun, which is always used for making the ornaments of demigods.

*U, ha, vā, va*—well-known as “invaluable.” *Which*—Jāmbūnada, used by demigods, etc. with their wives, make into jewelry like crowns, etc. and wear, indeed.

### Text 22

*यस्तु महाकदम्बः सुपार्श्वनिरूढो यास्तस्य कोटरेभ्यो विनिःसृताः पञ्चाया*  
*मपरिणाहाः पञ्च मधुधाराः सुपार्श्वशिखरात्पतन्त्योऽपरेणात्मानमिलावृतमनुमोद*  
*यन्ति ॥२२॥*

*yas tu mahā-kadambaḥ supārśva-nirūḍho yās tasya koṭarebhyo viniḥsṛtāḥ pañcāyāma-pariṇāhāḥ pañca madhu-dhārāḥ supārśva-śikharāt patantyo 'pareṇātmānam ilāvṛtam anumodayanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

yaḥ—which; tu—but; mahā-kadambaḥ—the tree named Mahākadamba; supārśva-nirūḍhaḥ—which stands on the side of the mountain known as Supārśva; yāḥ—which; tasya—of that; koṭarebhyaḥ—from the hollows; viniḥsṛtāḥ—flowing; pañca—five; āyāma—vyāma, a unit of measurement of about eight feet; pariṇāhāḥ—whose measurement; pañca—five; madhu-dhārāḥ—flows of honey; supārśva-śikharāt—from the top of Supārśva Mountain; patantyaḥ—flowing down; apareṇa—on the western side of Sumeru Mountain; ātmānam—the whole of; ilāvṛtam—Ilāvṛta-varṣa; anumodayanti—make fragrant.

**Перевод:**

**On the side of Supārśva Mountain stands a big tree called Mahākadamba, which is very celebrated. From the hollows of this tree flow five rivers of honey, each about five vyāmas wide. This flowing honey falls incessantly from the top of Supārśva Mountain and flows all around Ilāvṛta-varṣa, beginning from the western side. Thus the whole land is saturated with the pleasing fragrance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“In Supārṣva,” means the western prop mountain of Meru. *Nirūḍha*—situated. *Koṭara*—holes in the large trunks. *Pañcavyāma* is a bahuvrīhi compound. *Anumodana* means pleasing.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Koṭara*—tree holes. *Vyāma*—distance of outstretched hands. *Apareṇa*—to the west.

### Text 23

*या ह्युपयुञ्जानानां मुखनिर्वासितो वायुः समन्ताच्छतयोजनमनुवासयति ॥२३॥*

*yā hy upayuñjānānāṁ mukha-nirvāsito vāyuḥ samantāc chata-yojanam anuvāsayati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāḥ—which (those flows of honey); hi—indeed; upayuñjānānām—of those who drink; mukha-nirvāsitaḥ vāyuḥ—the air emanating from the mouths; samantāt—all around; śata-yojanam—up to one hundred yojanas (eight hundred miles); anuvāsayati—makes sweetly flavored.

**Перевод:**

**The air carrying the scent from the mouths of those who drink that honey perfumes the land for a hundred yojanas around.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*“Vyāma”* indicates the distance between a man’s outstretched arms. Five times that is the thickness of those (honeyfalls).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

There are five honey-falls, emerging from the holes in the trunk of the great Kadamba tree grown on the western propping mountain of Meru, i.e, Supārṣva. Honey falls from its summit, each in streams five times the distance between a person's extended arms across. It flows towards the western side of Ilāvṛta making the region fragrant. The falls are described as such: “The extremely fragrant aroma is carried by the breeze for a distance of 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] all around.”

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Mukha-nirvāsita*—coming out of the mouth.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vyāma*—distance between outstretched hands. Five vyāma is the width of these falls. Some take this as the circumference. *Anumodana*—pleased by the people praising them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Which”—honeyfalls. *Upayuñjāna*—consumers, eaters.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Until where*—circumference.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Then there is the great Kadamba tree grown on Supārṣva, from whose trunks emerge five honey-falls, each five times the distance between a person's extended arms across. These falls flow from the summit towards the western side of Ilāvṛta, making the region lustrous; or make the living beings there happy. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The mouths of those who consume the honey-falls become fragrant. The wind also carrying it becomes very fragrant and makes the region fragrant for 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] all around.

### Text 24

*एवं कुमुदनिरूढो यः शतवल्शो नाम वटस्तस्य स्कन्धेभ्यो*  
*नीचीनाः पयोदधिमधुघृतगुडान्नाद्यम्बरशय्यासनाभरणादयः सर्व एव*  
*कामदुघा नदाः कुमुदाग्रात्पतन्तस्तमुत्तरेणेलावृतमुपयोजयन्ति ॥२४॥*

*evaṁ kumuda-nirūḍho yaḥ śatavalśo nāma vaṭas tasya skandhebhyo nīcīnāḥ payo-dadhi-madhu-ghṛta-guḍānnādy-ambara-śayyāsanābharaṇādayaḥ sarva eva kāma-dughā nadāḥ kumudāgrāt patantas tam uttareṇelāvṛtam upayojayanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; kumuda-nirūḍhaḥ—having grown on Kumuda Mountain; yaḥ—that; śata-valśaḥ nāma—the tree named Śatavalśa (because of having hundreds of trunks); vaṭaḥ—a banyan tree; tasya—of it; skandhebhyaḥ—from the thick branches; nīcīnāḥ—flowing down; payaḥ—milk; dadhi—yogurt; madhu—honey; ghṛta—clarified butter; guḍa—molasses; anna—food grains; ādi—and so on; ambara—clothing; śayyā—bedding; āsana—sitting places; ābharaṇa-ādayaḥ—carrying ornaments and so on; sarve—everything; eva—certainly; kāma-dughāḥ—fulfilling all desires; nadāḥ—big rivers; kumuda-agrāt—from the top of Kumuda Mountain; patantaḥ—flowing; tam—to that; uttareṇa—on the northern side; ilāvṛtam—the land known as Ilāvṛta-varṣa; upayojayanti—give happiness.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, on Kumuda Mountain there is a great banyan tree, which is called Śatavalśa because it has a hundred main branches. From those branches come many roots, from which many rivers are flowing. These rivers flow down from the top of the mountain to the northern side of Ilāvṛta-varṣa for the benefit of those who live there. Because of these flowing rivers, all the people have ample supplies of milk, yogurt, honey, clarified butter \[ghee\], molasses, food grains, clothes, bedding, sitting places and ornaments. All the objects they desire are sufficiently supplied for their prosperity, and therefore they are very happy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Kumuda*—propping. *Upayoyanti*—eating.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Please (feed) the people of Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Emerging from the trunks*—falling downward; *kāma*—being desired, i.e, objects of desire; *granting all things wished for*—which are they? Milk, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

For the living beings.

### Text 25

*यानुपजुषाणानां न कदाचिदपि प्रजानां वलीपलितक्लमस्वेददौर्गन्ध्यजरामय*  
*मृत्युशीतोष्णवैवर्ण्योपसर्गादयस्तापविशेषा भवन्ति यावज्जीवं सुखं निरतिशयमेव*  
*॥२५॥*

*yān upajuṣāṇānāṁ na kadācid api prajānāṁ valī-palita-klama-sveda-daurgandhya-jarāmaya-mṛtyu-śītoṣṇa-vaivarṇyopasargādayas tāpa-viśeṣā bhavanti yāvaj jīvaṁ sukhaṁ niratiśayam eva*

**Пословный перевод:**

yān—which (all the products produced because of the flowing rivers mentioned above); upajuṣāṇānām—of persons who are fully utilizing; na—not; kadācit—at any time; api—certainly; prajānām—of the citizens; valī—wrinkles; palita—grey hair; klama—fatigue; sveda—perspiration; daurgandhya—bad odors because of unclean perspiration; jarā—old age; āmaya—disease; mṛtyu—untimely death; śīta—severe cold; uṣṇa—scorching heat; vaivarṇya—fading of the luster of the body; upasarga—troubles; ādayaḥ—and so on; tāpa—of sufferings; viśeṣāḥ—varieties; bhavanti—are; yāvat—as long as; jīvam—life; sukham—happiness; niratiśayam—unlimited; eva—only.

**Перевод:**

**The residents of the material world who enjoy the products of these flowing rivers have no wrinkles on their bodies and no grey hair. They never feel fatigue, and perspiration does not give their bodies a bad odor. They are not afflicted by old age, disease or untimely death, they do not suffer from chilly cold or scorching heat, nor do their bodies lose their luster. They all live very happily, without anxieties, until death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Which* = nadas; *upasarga* = disease due to elements, etc. By *etc.* those due to daiva influence.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, the banyan tree named Śatavalṣa, grown on Kumuda mountain, has, emerging from its trunks, milk, curd, honey, ghee, brown sugar, food items, clothes, beds, seats, and jewels. These rivers (nadīs), are falling from the summit of Kumuda, to the north of Ilāvṛta, making the residents of that region healthy and happy. This is elaborated as such: “Consuming the offerings of these nadīs, people don't undergo any diseases such as skin diseases, graying of hair, tiredness, infirmities, and mental states like light-headedness, sorrow, desire, hatred, fear, haughtiness, mistake, lunacy, grief, ignorance, greed, pride, avarice, envy. The consumers remain fit life-long.”

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Upasarga* = trouble caused by elements, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Downward flowing, streaming with milk etc., all these rivers (nadas), granting all the wishes, descend from the peak of Kumuda mountain, to the north of Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Thus, emerging downwards from the branches of the great Banyan tree, grown on the Kumuda mountain, known as Śatavalśa, are boon-granting rivers (nadas) descend from the peak of Kumuda, streaming milk, curd, honey, ghee, jaggery, rice, etc. and various types of clothes, beds, seats, jewels etc. flow to the north of Ilāvṛta. Upayojayanti = feed these people residing there. If the reading is “upajoṣayanti,” then it denotes make people inhabiting the northern region of Ilāvṛta happy.

Savouring which (nadas = rivers), the people never undergo skin deformation, hair deformation, fatigue, difficulty, sweat, bad odor, old age, disease, death, cold, heat, discoloring, afflictions like happiness, sorrow, desire, hatred, fear, pride, mistake, lunacy, despair, ignorance, greed, haughtiness, avarice, jealousy etc., and other such fevers etc. They remain happy life-long.

### Text 26

*कुरङ्गकुररकुसुम्भवैकङ्कत्रिकूटशिशिरपतङ्गरुचकनिषधशिनीवासकपिलशङ्ख*  
*वैदूर्यजारुधिहंसऋषभनागकालञ्जरनारदादयो विंशतिगिरयो मेरोः कर्णिकाया*  
*इव केसरभूता मूलदेशे परित उपकॢप्ताः ॥२६॥*

*kuraṅga-kurara-kusumbha-vaikaṅka-trikūṭa-śiśira-pataṅga-rucaka-niṣadha-śinīvāsa-kapila-śaṅkha-vaidūrya-jārudhi-haṁsa-ṛṣabha-nāga-kālañjara-nāradādayo viṁśati-girayo meroḥ karṇikāyā iva kesara-bhūtā mūla-deśe parita upakḷptāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuraṅga—Kuraṅga; kurara—Kurara; kusumbha-vaikaṅka-trikūṭa-śiśira-pataṅga-rucaka-niṣadha-śinīvāsa-kapila-śaṅkha-vaidūrya-jārudhi-haṁsa-ṛṣabha-nāga-kālañjara-nārada—the names of mountains; ādayaḥ—and so on; viṁśati-girayaḥ—twenty mountains; meroḥ—of Sumeru Mountain; karṇikāyāḥ—of the whorl of the lotus; iva—like; kesara-bhūtāḥ—as filaments; mūla-deśe—at the base; paritaḥ—all around; upakḷptāḥ—arranged by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**There are other mountains beautifully arranged around the foot of Mount Meru like the filaments around the whorl of a lotus flower. Their names are Kuraṅga, Kurara, Kusumbha, Vaikaṅka, Trikūṭa, Śiśira, Pataṅga, Rucaka, Niṣadha, Sinīvāsa, Kapila, Śaṅkha, Vaidūrya, Jārudhi, Haṁsa, Ṛṣabha, Nāga, Kālañjara and Nārada.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Kuraṅga etc. are the mountains, like the filaments of a flower, at the root of Meru as the pericarp of world lotus, created by Brahmā.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Kuraṅga, Kurara etc. are the mountains, the root of Meru, standing all around like the filaments of a flower, of Meru as the pericarp of a lotus flower.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Vali* = contraction of skin; *palita* = whitening (greying) of hair; *klama* = tiredness from working (fatigue); *upasarga* = the afflictions due to vali etc. *From the middle* = in the middle.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Those consuming the things related with these nadas, i.e, milk etc., are never afflicted by the effects of body-skin contraction, body fatigue, sweating, untimely death and diseases caused by them. Instead, they enjoy ultimate happiness throughout life. The afflictions are enumerated in the text itself and explained therein.

### Text 27

*जठरदेवकूटौ मेरुं पूर्वेणाष्टादशयोजनसहस्रमुदगायतौ द्विसहस्रं पृथुतुङ्गौ*  
*भवतः । एवमपरेण पवनपारियात्रौ दक्षिणेन कैलासकरवीरौ प्रागाय*  
*तावेवमुत्तरतस्त्रिशृङ्गमकरावष्टभिरेतैः परिसृतोऽग्निरिव परितश्चकास्तिकाञ्चन*  
*गिरिः ॥२७॥*

*jaṭhara-devakūṭau meruṁ pūrveṇāṣṭādaśa-yojanasahasram udagāyatau dvi-sahasraṁ pṛthu-tuṅgau bhavataḥ; evam apareṇa pavana-pāriyātrau dakṣiṇena kailāsa-karavīrau prāg-āyatāv evam uttaratas triśṛṅga-makarāv aṣṭabhir etaiḥ parisṛto 'gnir iva paritaś cakāsti kāñcana-giriḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

jaṭhara-devakūṭau—two mountains named Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa; merum—Sumeru Mountain; pūrveṇa—on the eastern side; aṣṭādaśa-yojanasahasram—eighteen thousand yojanas; udagāyatau—stretching from north to south; dvi-sahasram—two thousand yojanas; pṛthu-tuṅgau—in width and height; bhavataḥ—there are; evam—similarly; apareṇa—on the western side; pavana-pāriyātrau—two mountains named Pavana and Pāriyātra; dakṣiṇena—on the southern side; kailāsa-karavīrau—two mountains named Kailāsa and Karavīra; prāk-āyatau—expanding east and west; evam—similarly; uttarataḥ—on the northern side; triśṛṅga-makarau—two mountains named Triśṛṅga and Makara; aṣṭabhiḥ etaiḥ—by these eight mountains; parisṛtaḥ—surrounded; agniḥ iva—like fire; paritaḥ—all over; cakāsti—brilliantly shines; kāñcana-giriḥ—the golden mountain named Sumeru, or Meru.

**Перевод:**

**On the eastern side of Sumeru Mountain are two mountains named Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa, which extend to the north and south for 18,000 yojanas \[144,000 miles\]. Similarly, on the western side of Sumeru are two mountains named Pavana and Pāriyātra, which also extend north and south for the same distance. On the southern side of Sumeru are two mountains named Kailāsa and Karavīra, which extend east and west for 18,000 yojanas, and on the northern side of Sumeru, extending for the same distance east and west, are two mountains named Triśṛṅga and Makara. The width and height of all these mountains is 2,000 yojanas \[16,000 miles\]. Sumeru, a mountain of solid gold shining as brilliantly as fire, is surrounded by these eight mountains.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Śitivāsa” also is an occasional reading—some mountain with the name “ādi” also is to be known, elsewise 20 names would not be there. ; are created for Meru as the pericarp; Paridhis are surounding fire kept in pot etc. and their construction has to be known from Vedic texts. Thus, location of transverse Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa mountains, longish northwards, is to be known after (to the outside of) Mandara Mountain. Similarly, on the west, after Supārśva, location of Pavana and Pāriyātra, longish northwards, 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\]; likewise, on the south, after Merumandara, location of Kailāsa and Karavīra; and after Kumuda, the propping mountain, on the north, Triśṛṅga and Makara's location is to be known. Width and height of all the eight is the same. Similarly is the length. Like sacred fire being covered by darbha grass on the four sides.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, to the east of Meru, leaving 1,000 *yojanas* \[8,000 miles\] from its root, are situated Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa mountains, of 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] length and 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall. Similarly, on the west, are located Pavana and Pāriyātra, with the dimensions of Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa. Likewise, on the south, are located Kailāsa and Karavīra longish eastwise; and on the north are located Triśṛṅga and Makara. Like sacred fire being covered by darbha grass on the four sides, the golden mountain Meru reigns bright all around, surrounded by these eight mountains.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] away, to the east of Mandara mountain, are located the northwise longish Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa mountains; at 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] between Meru and Ilāvṛta. Similarly, on the west, after Supārśva, at 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] between Meru and Ilāvṛta, are located the northwise longish mountains Pavana and Pāriyātra; likewise, on the south, outside of Merumandara, are located the east-westwise long mountains Kailāsa and Karavīra; and outside of Kumuda, on the north, the east-westwise long mountains Triśṛṅga and Makara's location is to be known. 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] is to be added. The width and height of all the eight is the same. Like sacred fire being covered by darbha grass on the four sides, the golden mountain Meru reigns bright all around, surrounded by these eight mountains. Thus the length eastwards etc. and 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] width and height are to be known as the dimensions.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Surrounded by these = glows like fire.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The twenty hills, viz. Kuraṅga, Kurara, Kusumbha, Vaikaṅka, Trikūṭa, Śiśira, Pataṅga, Rucaka, Niṣadha, Śitivāsas, Kapila, Śaṅkha, Vaidūrya, Jārudhi, Hamsa, Ṛṣabha, Nāga, Kālañjara, Nārada and Ṇdi, are created all around the root of Meru like the filament hills at the middle of the pericarp of Jambūdvīpa or Ilāvṛta.

“By the creator” is to be supplied. In the names of the twenty hills, Kuraṅga etc., some people have taken “Kapiśa” as an additional name (taking “ādi” in the end to mean *etc.*) for accounting for twenty names, while some others have taken Nīra as an additional one. We say that the twentieth hill is named “Ādi” itself, since while listing twenty names there is no need for a word meaning “etc.”

In *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*, are mentioned five “kesara” (filament) mountains in each of the four directions, as: The chief filament-like mountains, to the east of Meru are, Śītānta, Cakramuñja, Kurara, Mālyavān and Vaikaṅka etc.; those to the south of Meru are, Trikūṭa, Śiśira, Pataṅga, Rucaka and Niṣadha etc.; those to the west of Meru are, Śikhivāsas, Pravaidūrya, Kapila, Gandha-mādana, Yārudhi etc.; those to the north are, Śaṅkhakūṭa, Ṛṣabha, Hamsa, Nāga and Kālañjara etc.; The difference in names are to be taken as in different cycles of creation.

To the east of Meru, leaving 1,000 *yojanas* \[8,000 miles\] from the root of Meru, the two mountains Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa are located, They are 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall. Likewise, on the west of Meru, Pavana and Pāriyātra are located. They are also 18,000 *yojanas* long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* wide and tall. Similarly, on the south of Meru, Kailāsa and Karavīra, 18,000 *yojanas* long, east-westwise, 2,000 *yojanas* wide and tall, are located. To the north of Meru, the mountains Triśṛṅga and Makara, 18,000 *yojanas* long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* wide and tall, are located. Surrounded by these eight mountains, the golden mount Meru, glows like a sacred fire surrounded by darbha grass on four sides. The meaning is: “To the east of Meru, between Meru and Ilāvṛta, and similarly to the west of Meru between Meru and Ilāvṛta, leaving 1,000 *yojanas* from the root of Meru, to the east are Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa; to the west are Pavana and Pāriyātra; These are supporting the earth and extend transversely northwards being 18,000 *yojanas* long and 2,000 *yojanas* wide and tall. Similarly, to the south of Meru, between Meru and Ilāvṛta, and similarly to the north of Meru between Meru and Ilāvṛta, leaving 1,000 *yojanas* from the root of Meru, to the south are Kailāsa and Karavīra; to the north are Triśṛṅga and Makara; These are supporting the earth and extend transversely eastwards being 18,000 *yojanas* long and 2,000 *yojanas* wide and tall. Thus, in these eight mountains, being longish on north or east etc. and 2,000 *yojana* width and height are to be known. The variation in the dimensions of these in Purāṇa-s like Vaiṣṇava etc. are to be taken as in different cycles of creation.

### Text 28

*मेरोर्मूर्धनि भगवत आत्मयोनेर्मध्यत उपकॢप्तां पुरीमयुतयोजनसाहस्रीं*  
*समचतुरस्रां शातकौम्भीं वदन्ति ॥२८॥*

*meror mūrdhani bhagavata ātma-yoner madhyata upakḷptāṁ purīm ayuta-yojanasāhasrīṁ sama-caturasrāṁ śātakaumbhīṁ vadanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

meroḥ—of Sumeru Mountain; mūrdhani—on the head; bhagavataḥ—of the most powerful being; ātma-yoneḥ—of Lord Brahmā; madhyataḥ—in the middle; upakḷptām—situated; purīm—the great township; ayuta-yojana—ten thousand yojanas; sāhasrīm—one thousand; sama-caturasrām—of the same length on all sides; śāta-kaumbhīm—made entirely of gold; vadanti—the great learned sages say.

**Перевод:**

**In the middle of the summit of Meru is the township of Lord Brahmā. Each of its four sides is calculated to extend for ten million yojanas \[eighty million miles\]. It is made entirely of gold, and therefore learned scholars and sages call it Śātakaumbhī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In the four directions, leaving 1,000 *yojanas* \[8,000 miles\] from the root of Meru, like the paridhi (square perimeter) around a sacred fire, Jaṭhara, Devakūṭa etc. are situated and hence the size of 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] is mentioned. The different description with regard to dimensions in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* etc. are to be taken as being in different *kalpas* (creation cycles). 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall also.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

On the top of Meru, which is 32,000 *yojanas* \[256,000 miles\] wide, at the center, the city of Brahmā, called “śatakoṭi,” which is golden, is said to exist.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Śatavalṣa*—with a hundred branches; *nīcīna*— downward.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

At the head, 32,000 *yojana* \[256,000 miles\] wide. *Caturasra* = all four sides are equal (square). Śātakaumbhī = golden. The name is Manovatī from other Purāṇa text.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

To the east of Meru, the two mountains Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa are located, 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall. Likewise, on the west of Meru, Pavana and Pārijāta are located. They are also 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall. Similarly, on the south of Meru, Kailāsa and Karavīra, 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] wide and tall, are located. To the north of Meru, the mountains Triśṛṅga and Makara, 18,000 *yojanas* \[144,000 miles\] long, north-southwise, 2,000 *yojanas*\[16,000 miles\] wide and tall, are located. These mountains Jaṭhara etc. are to be known as silverish as Kailāsa is known to be so and these are analogous to it.

### Text 29

*तामनुपरितो लोकपालानामष्टानां यथादिशं यथारूपं तुरीयमानेन पुरोऽष्टा*  
*वुपकॢप्ताः ॥२९॥*

*tām anuparito loka-pālānām aṣṭānāṁ yathā-diśaṁ yathā-rūpaṁ turīya-mānena puro 'ṣṭāv upakḷptāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

tām—that great township named Brahmapurī; anuparitaḥ—surrounding; loka-pālānām—of the governors of the planets; aṣṭānām—eight; yathā-diśam—according to the directions; yathā-rūpam—in exact conformity with the township of Brahmapurī; turīya-mānena—by measurement only one fourth; puraḥ—townships; aṣṭau—eight; upakḷptāḥ—situated.

**Перевод:**

**Surrounding Brahmapurī in all directions are the residences of the eight principal governors of the planetary systems, beginning with King Indra. These abodes are similar to Brahmapurī but are one fourth the size.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

From east onwards and forms with colors of Indra etc. *Turīya* = 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\]. Names are to be known from other *Purānas*. As is said: “There are nine cities in Meru, viz. Manovatī, Amarāvatī, Tejovatī, Saṁyamanī, Kṛṣṇāṅganā, Śraddhāvatī, Gandhavatī, Mahodayā and Yaśovatī, of Brahmā, Indra, Agni etc. respectively.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

After Brahmā's city. All around = in each direction, respectively.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“One-fourth of Brahmā's city dimension,” i.e, 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\], is the dimension of (the eight) cities. Following it (Brahmā's city) is elucidated as respectively in the directions starting with east etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Different viewpoints described in the commentaries are to be taken as in different creations.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*In proper directions* = east onwards (respectively). *Of proper forms* = not exceeding (differing from) the colors of Indra etc. *Turīyamāna* = one fourth extent, i.e, 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\]. The names are to be known from other Purāṇas. As is said: There are nine cities in Meru, viz. Manovatī, Amarāvatī, Tejovatī, Saṁyamanī, Kṛṣṇāṅganā, Śraddhāvatī, Gandhavatī, Mahodayā and Yaśovatī are of Brahmā, Indra, Agni etc. respectively. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The golden city is named Manovatī and is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] in extent. Around that city of Brahmā, the cities of other eight world-protectors, from east onwards, respectively, befitting their forms, one-fourth the size of Brahmā's city, i.e, 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\] extent, are constructed. These are: in the east, Amaravatī for Indra; in south-east, Tejovatī for Agni; in the south, Samyamanī for Yama; in south-west, Kṛṣṇāṅganā for Nirṛti; in the west, Śraddhāvatī for Varuṇa; in the north-west, Gandhavatī for Vāyu; in the north, Mahodayā for Dhanada; and in the north-east, Yaśovatī for Īśāna. As it is said: There are nine cities in Meru, viz. Manovatī, Amarāvatī, Tejovatī, Saṁyamanī, Kṛṣṇāṅganā, Śraddhāvatī, Gandha-vatī, Mahodayā and Yaśovatī are of Brahmā, Indra, Agni etc. respectively. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Sixteenth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “A Description of Jambūdvīpa.”

## Chapter 17 - The Descent of the River Ganges

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*तत्र भगवतः साक्षाद्यज्ञलिङ्गस्य विष्णोर्विक्रमतो वामपादाङ्गुष्ठनखनिर्भिन्नो*  
*र्ध्वाण्डकटाहविवरेणान्तःप्रविष्टा या बाह्यजलधारा तच्चरणपङ्कजावनेजना*  
*रुणकिञ्जल्कोपरञ्जिताखिलजगदघमलापहोपस्पर्शनामला साक्षाद्भगवत्पदीत्य*  
*नुपलक्षितवचोऽभिधीयमानातिमहता कालेन युगसहस्रोपलक्षणेन दिवो*  
*मूर्धन्यवततार यत्तद्विष्णुपदमाहुः ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*tatra bhagavataḥ sākṣād yajña-liṅgasya viṣṇor vikramato vāma-pādāṅguṣṭha-nakha-nirbhinnordhvāṇḍa-kaṭāha-vivareṇāntaḥ-praviṣṭā yā bāhya-jala-dhārā tac-caraṇa-paṅkajāvanejanāruṇa-kiñjalkoparañjitākhila-jagad-agha-malāpahopasparśanāmalā sākṣād bhagavat-padīty anupalakṣita-vaco 'bhidhīyamānāti-mahatā kālena yuga-sahasropalakṣaṇena divo mūrdhany avatatāra yat tad viṣṇu-padam āhuḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; tatra—at that time; bhagavataḥ—of the incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; sākṣāt—directly; yajña-liṅgasya—the enjoyer of the results of all sacrifices; viṣṇoḥ—of Lord Viṣṇu; vikramataḥ—while taking His second step; vāma-pāda—of His left leg; aṅguṣṭha—of the big toe; nakha—by the nail; nirbhinna—pierced; ūrdhva—upper; aṇḍa-kaṭāha—the covering of the universe (consisting of seven layers-earth, water, fire, etc.); vivareṇa—through the bole; antaḥ-praviṣṭā—having entered the universe; yā—which; bāhya-jala-dhārā—the flow of water from the Causal Ocean outside the universe; tat—of Him; caraṇa-paṅkaja—of the lotus feet; avanejana—by the washing; aruṇa-kiñjalka—by reddish powder; uparañjitā—being colored; akhila-jagat—of the whole world; agha-mala—the sinful activities; apahā—destroys; upasparśana—the touching of which; amalā—completely pure; sākṣāt—directly; bhagavat-padī—emanating from the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; iti—thus; anupalakṣita—described; vacaḥ—by the name; abhidhīyamānā—being called; ati-mahatā kālena—after a long time; yuga-sahasra-upalakṣaṇena—consisting of one thousand millenniums; divaḥ—of the sky; mūrdhani—on the head (Dhruvaloka); avatatāra—descended; yat—which; tat—that; viṣṇu-padam—the lotus feet of Lord Viṣṇu; āhuḥ—they call.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, Lord Viṣṇu, the enjoyer of all sacrifices, appeared as Vāmanadeva in the sacrificial arena of Bali Mahārāja. Then He extended His left foot to the end of the universe and pierced a hole in its covering with the nail of His big toe. Through the hole, the pure water of the Causal Ocean entered this universe as the Ganges River. Having washed the lotus feet of the Lord, which are covered with reddish powder, the water of the Ganges acquired a very beautiful pink color. Every living being can immediately purify his mind of material contamination by touching the transcendental water of the Ganges, yet its waters remain ever pure. Because the Ganges directly touches the lotus feet of the Lord before descending within this universe, she is known as Viṣṇupadī. Later she received other names like Jāhnavī and Bhāgīrathī. After one thousand millenniums, the water of the Ganges descended on Dhruvaloka, the topmost planet in this universe. Therefore all learned sages and scholars proclaim Dhruvaloka to be Viṣṇupada \[“situated on Lord Viṣṇu's lotus feet”\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Then the seventeenth chapter describes the coming forth of Ganges in its four directions within Ilāvṛta and its dragging and consumption by Rudra. “In the yajña (sacrifice) of Bali, the form of Trivikrama was taken by whom” = *yajñaliṅga*, i.e, Viṣṇu.

Viṣṇu (the striding one) stamped the ground with His right foot and extended His left foot above—the toenail of which ruptured the upper part of the cosmic shell. Through that hole the external water stream enters inside the universe and descends to the head (top) of heaven. The water which washes His lotus-feet turns saffron reddish and inundates the whole world. Those who bathe in this river become purified of their sins, although the river remains devoid of blemishes (pure). The river is originally called “Bhagavatpadi”, i.e, “from the Lord's feet,” prior to other references such as Jāhnavī, Bhāgīrathī etc., which came about later. Which is the heaven's head? The answer is “Viṣṇupada.” \[Note: this paragraph is also included by Vīrarāghava, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Thus having elucidated the mountains, continents, their extents etc. of Jambūdvīpa, now, in the next three chapters beginning from the seventeenth, the advent of the sacred river Gaṅgā, and worshipping of the forms Saṅkarṣaṇa, etc. of the Lord through meditation by Rudra etc. will be described. The configuration of the sub-islands in the continents of Ilāvṛta will also be described. *Yajñaliṅga* = the revered form of Viṣṇu, the Lord of the sacrifices who took the form of Vāmana (lit. a dwarf).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

In this chapter, the descent of Bhāgīrathī is described—even by involuntarily drinking its water, a person gets his mind purified and develops unsurpassed devotion to Lord Hari. The descent begins from outside the cosmic shell as a continuous stream of water to the place called Viṣṇupada or the abode of Lord Hari in His Śiśumāra (porpoise) form. This is the heavenly place of Dhruva. Though naturally pure white, the water becomes blossom reddish by washing the red lotus-like feet of Lord Hari, combined with the saffron dust of His lotus-feet. The red color may cause desire in the devotees' minds. Would this not instigate them to commit sins? No. Since the river eradicates the sins of the entire world even by its mere touch, or by sipping, then, what to say of the effect of bathing in it etc.? Sākṣāt = directly; *at once* indicates that even by singing the glory of or the names of the river one’s sins are removed, then what to mention of the effect of touching. *Not referred to by any other words* means the names found in scriptures and epics. This water comes directly from His lotus-feet distinguishing it from even the equivalent hallowed water used to bathe the divine “sālagrāma” stone.

During different *kalpas* the feet differ. It is said that in the Varāha-kalpa, Lord Trivikrama lifted up His left foot and in other *kalpas*, He lifted the right foot.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The names of Gaṅgā, its descent to earth, the joys of earthly gold, the service by Rudra to Saṅkarṣaṇa are told in the Seventeenth Chapter.

*There* = during His incarnation as Vāmana. While taking strides, covering the earth by his right foot, He lifted up his left foot and “in three steps, shaking the very abode,” as mentioned in *Brāhma Purāṇa*, extended his presence to the outer shells of the universe. “*Water stream of pure consciousness, from outside of the eight outer shells of earth etc.*” relates to the Causal Ocean which descended onto the head of heaven, i.e, Dhruva's place.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Then* = after describing Sumeru; *on its four directions* = the four directions of Sumeru.

Thus having described the beauty of the perimeter, filaments etc. of Meru, (the sage) now begins to describe the most grand origin of the river Gaṅgā, lustrous like a diamond in a crown, with her very long branches. \[this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

*There* = pronouns “tyad” etc.; *being denoters of intended things* = during His incarnation as Vāmana; *taking strides* = “in three steps, shaking the very abode”; *by mention of* Brahmā = his area being up to the outer shells of the universe; *from outside of the eight outer shells of earth, etc.* = related to the ocean of origin; *descended onto the head of heaven* = *Dhruva's place*. *Thence* = the water used for washing the lotus-feet of the Lord only; *unlike the water sprinkled to bathe śālagrāma* \[the divine stone incarnation of the Lord used in worshipping\] = equivalent to Gaṅgā, directly from His feet alone. Or we can take this as connected to the next prose sentence as “descended from that renowned Viṣṇupada as told by learned seers.” *Yuga* here denotes the technical term used in astronomy, consisting of five years, as, according to Śrīpati: “a *yuga* comprises five years.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

In the Seventeenth (chapter), the supremacy of Gaṅgā is elucidated by narrating its descent to earth and explaining natural greatness and transcendental qualities.

While defeating the demons, the incarnation as Vāmana took place.

How long was the period it took for the river to reach Dhruva’s place? A thousand four-yuga cycles equal the duration of one “night” of Brahmā. “On top of heaven” indicates that being beyond the three worlds, it is not destroyed by the “praḷaya” (deluge). Taken literally, one thousand yugas are well within the daytime of Brahmā and thus the descent of Gaṅgā in Dhruva's place is plausible.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Then in the seventeenth (chapter), the arrival of Gaṅgā from four directions and the service performed by Rudra to Saṅkarṣaṇa in Ilāvṛta are recollected.

That it took such a long time for the river to descend on heaven also suggests its other name “Mandākinī” (lit. slow-moving).

### Text 2

*यत्र ह वाव वीरव्रत औत्तानपादिः परमभागवतोऽस्मत्कुलदेवताचरणारविन्दो*  
*दकमिति यामनुसवनमुत्कृष्यमाणभगवद्भक्तियोगेन दृढं क्लिद्यमानान्तर्हृदय*  
*औत्कण्ठ्यविवशामीलितलोचनयुगलकुड्मलविगलितामलबाष्पकलयाभिव्यज्य*  
*मानरोमपुलककुलकोऽधुनापि परमादरेण शिरसा बिभर्ति ॥२॥*

*yatra ha vāva vīra-vrata auttānapādiḥ parama-bhāgavato 'smat-kula-devatā-caraṇāravindodakam iti yām anusavanam utkṛṣyamāṇa-bhagavad-bhakti-yogena dṛḍhaṁ klidyamānāntar-hṛdaya autkaṇṭhya-vivaśāmīlita-locana-yugala-kuḍmala-vigalitāmala-bāṣpa-kalayābhivyajyamāna-roma-pulaka-kulako 'dhunāpi paramādareṇa śirasā bibharti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatra ha vāva—in Dhruvaloka; vīra-vrataḥ—firmly determined; auttānapādiḥ—the famous son of Mahārāja Uttānapāda; parama-bhāgavataḥ—the most exalted devotee; asmat—our; kula-devatā—of the family Deity; caraṇa-aravinda—of the lotus feet; udakam—in the water; iti—thus; yām—which; anusavanam—constantly; utkṛṣyamāṇa—being increased; bhagavat-bhakti-yogena—by devotional service unto the Lord; dṛḍham—greatly; klidyamāna-antaḥ-hṛdayaḥ—being softened within the core of his heart; autkaṇṭhya—by great anxiety; vivaśa—spontaneously; amīlita—slightly open; locana—of eyes; yugala—pair; kuḍmala—from the flowerlike; vigalita—emanating; amala—uncontaminated; bāṣpa-kalayā—with tears; abhivyajyamāna—being manifested; roma-pulaka-kulakaḥ—whose symptoms of ecstasy on the body; adhunā api—even now; parama-ādareṇa—with great reverence; śirasā—by the head; bibharti—he bears.

**Перевод:**

**Dhruva Mahārāja, the famous son of Mahārāja Uttānapāda, is known as the most exalted devotee of the Supreme Lord because of his firm determination in executing devotional service. Knowing that the sacred Ganges water washes the lotus feet of Lord Viṣṇu, Dhruva Mahārāja, situated on his own planet, to this very day accepts that water on his head with great devotion. Because he constantly thinks of Kṛṣṇa very devoutly within the core of his heart, he is overcome with ecstatic anxiety. Tears flow from his half-open eyes, and eruptions appear on his entire body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Viṣṇupada* is explained that Dhruva holds the water from the lotus feet of the original deity Lord Hari on his head. *He is qualified* = with an adoration to the Lord, which grows stronger and deeper every moment, the hairs on his body become erect out of ecstasy, his heart softens, he closes his budlike eyes and pure tears roll down. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Which is that “Viṣṇupada”* is explained as Dhruva's abode. *Where* = at the head of heaven, Dhruva, the greatest devotee and son of Uttānapāda. Dhruva knows that this is the stream from the lotus feet of the ancestral deity, Lord Hari and thus he holds the river water on head at the three times of the day, even now. Or “anusavanam” may mean *always, i.e, every moment*. Or the devotion growing every moment which strongly satisfies his heart and hence, and being moved by adoration, he involuntarily closes his eyes, resembling flower buds, and pure tear drops roll down in ecstasy from them. He experienced horripilation in abundance out of the thrill of His meditation. Such was his state.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Where* = in the world of Dhruva.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In the term thousands of yugas, *yuga* is to be known as the astronomically defined five-year duration.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Where* = in Viṣṇupada.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Where* = in Viṣṇupada. *Auttānapādi* = Dhruva (lit. son of Uttānapāda). *Thence only* = being wet (moved) inside the heart. *Erect hair* = horripilation. *Kula* = group.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Where* = in Viṣṇupada; *vīra* = one with Garuḍa as vehicle (Lord Viṣṇu) \[literally from vi = bird and īra = commander\]; *vrata* = penances; *one whose object of pleasing through penances is Lord Viṣṇu* means Dhruva; It may be noted that other commentators have explained the term “vīravrata” as (one with) firm resolution etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Which is that head (top) of heaven? That which is well-known, etc. The particle “ha” denotes renowned and “vāva” denotes certainty.

Thus, due to intense devotion, Dhruva achieved strict penances with firm resolution during his childhood. This is indicated by the adjective “vīravrata.”

There is a statement, “the residue of water used for cleaning or to wash feet as well as the remnant of water which has been drunk are all to be treated as equivalent to liquor.” Thus water used to wash feet, being impure, is unfit for use in rituals. By this logic Gaṅgā also, being the water used to wash Lord's feet, becomes unfit for His worship. It is also stated that “the sky is His head, the directions are His ears and the earth is His feet.” One may question whether the earth is inferior due to its being His feet, and Gaṅgā’s purity is also questionable. In answer to this it should be understood that the Lord’s feet do not make anything impure by their contact and use of Gaṅgā water for His worship is not wrong. Gaṅgā’s purity is confirmed in scripture and by sadhus whereas ordinary people’s bathing water is impure.

If due to the contact with His feet, something becomes unfit for His worship, then, even earth, being described as His feet, should, with all its derivatives, also become unfit for His worship/service. However earth’s purity is asserted in scriptures, “The most auspicious place is where a worthy person is available. Great souls who know of the qualities of worthy things, O king, assert the all-pervading Lord Hari alone to be the most worthy thing. Thus, wherever worship of Lord Hari takes place, that place begets all prosperity. The famous rivers such as Gaṅgā are mentioned in Vedic epics.” The excellence of the nine continents is indicated due to their being places of the Lord's worship. In all the nine *varṣas*, Lord Nārāyaṇa, full of the six great auspicious qualities of supremacy lies on Śeṣa, the primary cause of the all things and the greatest person, in order to bless the devotees worshipping Him. Even today He remains present in His transcendental vyūha forms as Saṅkarṣaṇa, etc.

### Text 3

*ततः सप्त ऋषयस्तत्प्रभावाभिज्ञा यां ननु तपसआत्य*  
*न्तिकी सिद्धिरेतावती भगवति सर्वात्मनि वासुदेवेऽनुपरतभ क्ति*  
*योगलाभेनैवोपेक्षितान्यार्थात्मगतयो मुक्ति मिवागतां मुमुक्षव इव*  
*सबहुमानमद्यापि जटाजूटैरुद्वहन्ति ॥३॥*

*tataḥ sapta ṛṣayas tat prabhāvābhijñā yāṁ nanu tapasa ātyantikī siddhir etāvatī bhagavati sarvātmani vāsudeve 'nuparata-bhakti-yoga-lābhenaivopekṣitānyārthātma-gatayo muktim ivāgatāṁ mumukṣava iva sabahu-mānam adyāpi jaṭā-jūṭair udvahanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—thereafter; sapta ṛṣayaḥ—the seven great sages (beginning with Marīci); tat prabhāva-abhijñāḥ—who knew very well the influence of the Ganges River; yām—this Ganges water; nanu—indeed; tapasaḥ—of our austerities; ātyantikī—the ultimate; siddhiḥ—perfection; etāvatī—this much; bhagavati—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; sarva-ātmani—in the all-pervading; vāsudeve—Kṛṣṇa; anuparata—continuous; bhakti-yoga—of the mystic process of devotional service; lābhena—simply by achieving this platform; eva—certainly; upekṣita—neglected; anya—other; artha-ātma-gatayaḥ—all other means of perfection (namely religion, economic development, sense gratification and liberation); muktim—liberation from material bondage; iva—like; āgatām—obtained; mumukṣavaḥ—persons desiring liberation; iva—like; sa-bahu-mānam—with great honor; adya api—even now; jaṭā-jūṭaiḥ—with matted locks of hair; udvahanti—they carry.

**Перевод:**

**The seven great sages \[Marīci, Vasiṣṭha, Atri and so on\] reside on planets beneath Dhruvaloka. Well aware of the influence of the water of the Ganges, to this day they keep Ganges water on the tufts of hair on their heads. They have concluded that this is the ultimate wealth, the perfection of all austerities, and the best means of prosecuting transcendental life. Having obtained uninterrupted devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, they neglect all other beneficial processes like religion, economic development, sense gratification and even merging into the Supreme. Just as jñānīs think that merging into the existence of the Lord is the highest truth, these seven exalted personalities accept devotional service as the perfection of life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Then, the seven sages, aware of the greatness of that river, Gaṅgā, hold its water on their matted hair, thinking that this much alone is the ultimate objective (summum bonum) namely renunciation, divine meditation and ultimate liberation. \[Note: this paragraph is also repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Afterwards, the seven sages, knowing the greatness of Gaṅgā, determined that the fruition of penance personified is this river Viṣṇupadī, and nothing more than this. Even now, they reverentially hold its water on the matted hair on their heads. This is analogous to seeking deliverance directly getting final emancipation. This can be attained by 1) renunciation of all other objects of desire such as material wealth, sensual pleasures etc., and 2) incessant contemplation with devotion upon the soul of all things, Lord Vāsudeva.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Thence* = from Dhruva's world. By those who have discarded the pursuit of soul's other objects of desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*So much* = there is achievement greater than this by those saintly persons who have neglected other objects of desire and spiritual knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Then* = after Dhruva. *Upekṣita* = renounced. *Other desires* = like moral/ethical virtues, material wealth and sensual pleasures.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

After that, (the seven sages) exclaim in amazement that, “The ultimate achievement of performing penances is this (river) Viṣṇupadī. Is it not?” Thus knowing her glories, even now they reverentially hold her on their twisted, matted hair. *They are qualified* = by incessant devotional attachment in the Lord, neglecting all other objects of desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Below that, the seven sages bear the Gaṅgā with reverence on their twisted, matted hair. This is because they know the auspicious glories of Gaṅgā. The particle “nanu” denotes certainty. The ultimate achievement of penance is this much, i.e, getting the sacred water of the Lord's lotus feet, and nothing more. The reason for this knowledge is the incessant devotional attachment to Lord Vāsudeva, the soul and immanent ruler of all and the possessor of six auspicious attributes (strength, fame, wealth, knowledge, beauty and renunciation). Such a person becomes fully content and renounces other objects of desire like moral rectitude, material wealth, sensual pleasures and even spiritual knowledge. The knowledge of the greatness of things related to the Lord accrues only to the devotees of the Lord and not to others hostile towards Him. The acceptance (of Gaṅgā's water) with reverence is elucidated with the analogy of people seeking deliverance, rejoice reverentially on the direct perception of the final emancipation.

### Text 4

*ततोऽनेकसहस्रकोटिविमानानीकसङ्कुलदेवयानेनावतरन्तीन्दुमण्डलमावार्य ब्रह्म*  
*सदने निपतति ॥४॥*

*tato 'neka-sahasra-koṭi-vimānānīka-saṅkula-deva-yānenāvatar-antīndu maṇḍalam āvārya brahma-sadane nipatati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—after purifying the seven planets of the seven great sages; aneka—many; sahasra—thousands; koṭi—of millions; vimāna-anīka—with contingents of airplanes; saṅkula—congested; deva-yānena—by the spaceways of the demigods; avatarantī—descending; indu-maṇḍalam—the moon planet; āvārya—inundated; brahma-sadane—to the abode of Lord Brahmā atop Sumeru-parvata; nipatati—falls down.

**Перевод:**

**After purifying the seven planets near Dhruvaloka \[the polestar\], the Ganges water is carried through the spaceways of the demigods in billions of celestial airplanes. Then it inundates the moon \[Candraloka\] and finally reaches Lord Brahmā's abode atop Mount Meru.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Then descending through the heavenly (aerial) route, bustling with the traffic of many hundreds and thousands of aircraft, drenching the moon's disc, the river falls onto the abode of Brahmā atop Mount Meru. The traffic of planes (denoting the path of performers of rituals) is below the station of the seven sages as indicated by describing the bustle after them. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*After that*= after the circle of the seven sages.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Then, descending aerially, by the bustling route of groups of hundreds of thousands of aircraft, downwards, covering and drenching the disc of the moon, the river falls on to the Brahmā's abode, located on the top of Meru.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

From the world of seven sages, the river flows through the divine path, touching the cities of Indra, etc., to the city Śatakoṭi of Brahmā, situated in the middle of Meru's crest.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The traffic jam of planes of those performing rituals and reaching their destination is below those of the seven sages. This is supported by the statement, “that (goal) is not attained by performance of rituals which is attainable by those of learning, penance, meditation or deep contemplation.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Probably, the destination of the sacrificial ritual performers is below that of the seven sages, as the traffic of aircraft of such people is mentioned after the sages' abode.

### Text 5

*तत्र चतुर्धा भिद्यमाना चतुर्भिर्नामभिश्चतुर्दिशमभिस्पन्दन्ती*  
*नदनदीपतिमेवाभिनिविशति सीतालकनन्दा चक्षुर्भद्रेति ॥५॥*

*tatra caturdhā bhidyamānā caturbhir nāmabhiś catur-diśam abhispandantī nada-nadī-patim evābhiniviśati sītālakanandā cakṣur bhadreti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—there (on top of Mount Meru); caturdhā—into four branches; bhidyamānā—being divided; caturbhiḥ—with four; nāmabhiḥ—names; catuḥ-diśam—the four directions (east, west, north and south); abhispandantī—profusely flowing; nada-nadī-patim—the reservoir of all great rivers (the ocean); eva—certainly; abhiniviśati—enters; sītā-alakanandā—Sītā and Alakanandā; cakṣuḥ—Cakṣu; bhadrā—Bhadrā; iti—known by these names.

**Перевод:**

**On top of Mount Meru, the Ganges divides into four branches, each of which gushes in a different direction \[east, west, north and south\]. These branches, known by the names Sītā, Alakanandā, Cakṣu and Bhadrā, flow down to the ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Abhispandantī* = flowing in front.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

There, getting split into four directions, with names such as Sītā, etc., four streams each reach the ocean, the husband of rivers. The substrate of action here is the destination, denoted by preverbs “abhi” and “ni” added before the verbal root “viś”—to enter, as per the aphorism “abhiniviśaśca” (see *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* 1.4.47). The names are listed as Sītā, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*There* = in the court hall of Brahmā's abode. *Nada-nadī-pati* = ocean.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

By aerial route; probably the place of enjoyment for performers of rituals is below the abode of the seven sages, as the bustle in the path is mentioned only below theirs. *Covering* = drenching; the top of Mount Meru, i.e. in Brahmā's place.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*There* = in the court of Brahmā's dwelling place. *Nada-nadī-pati* = ocean (lit. husband of rivers flowing westward \[male\] and eastward).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Covering the ring of sky* = drenching; *in Brahmā's abode* = on the top of Meru.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

*Abhispandantī* = going around.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

There, in Brahmā's place, splitting into four streams with four names, flowing in four directions, she enters the ocean itself. By the aphorism “abhiniviśaśca” (see Śrīmad Bhāgavatam 1.4.47), using the accusative case for locus is due to its being designated as the destination (object).

### Text 6

*सीता तु ब्रह्मसदनात्केसराचलादिगिरिशिखरेभ्यो ऽधोऽधः प्रस्रवन्ती*  
*गन्धमादनमूर्धसु पतित्वान्तरेण भद्राश्ववर्षं प्राच्यां दिशि क्षारसमुद्रम*  
*भिप्रविशति ॥६॥*

*sītā tu brahma-sadanāt kesarācalādi-giri-śikharebhyo 'dho 'dhaḥ prasravantī gandhamādana-mūrdhasu patitvāntareṇa bhadrāśva-varṣaṁ prācyāṁ diśi kṣāra-samudram abhipraviśati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sītā—the branch known as Sītā; tu—certainly; brahma-sadanāt—from Brahmapurī; kesarācala-ādi—of Kesarācala and of other great mountains; giri—hills; śikharebhyaḥ—from the tops; adhaḥ adhaḥ—downward; prasravantī—flowing; gandhamādana—of Gandhamādana Mountain; mūrdhasu—on the top; patitvā—falling down; antareṇa—within; bhadrāśva-varṣam—the province known as Bhadrāśva; prācyām—in the western; diśi—direction; kṣāra-samudram—the ocean of salt water; abhipraviśati—enters.

**Перевод:**
