**The branch of the Ganges known as the Sītā flows through Brahmapurī atop Mount Meru, and from there it runs down to the nearby peaks of the Kesarācala Mountains, which stand almost as high as Mount Meru itself. These mountains are like a bunch of filaments around Mount Meru. From the Kesarācala Mountains, the Ganges falls to the peak of Gandhamādana Mountain and then flows into the land of Bhadrāśva-varṣa. Finally it reaches the ocean of salt water in the west.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The filament mountains are of the same height as Meru and hence (she) first falls on their main peaks and then progressively flows downwards.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

There, among the four streams, Sītā, the eastern stream, first falls onto the main peaks of the Kesara (filament) mountains from Brahmā's dwelling, as they are of the same height as the Meru, and then flowing downwards, falls on top of Gandhamādana. Flowing through the middle of Bhadrāśva varṣa, she enters the salt-ocean in the eastern direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

First she falls on the main peaks of the Kesara (filament) mountains being of the same height as Meru, and from there flowing downwards into the middle of Bhadrāśva varṣa, crossing Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In the middle of Bhadrāśva varṣa (continent). *Having fallen* = overshooting Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Filament-like mountains, i.e, Kuraṅga etc. are of the same height as that of Meru; also other mountains like Mandara etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Her names are listed as Sītā etc. In four directions entering the ocean is shown then. Since the Kesara (filament) mountains etc. are taller than the boundary-hills Gandhamādana etc. and closer the fall is first on them. The river branch known as Sītā first falls on their main peaks from Brahmā's abode. Flowing downwards, she falls on the summits of Gandhamādana through the middle of the Bhadrāśva continent and then she reaches the salty ocean in the eastern direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The names are: Sītā, Alakanandā, Cakṣus and Bhadrā. “*There, among the four streams,*” should be added. Sītā, the eastern stream, first falls from Brahmā's abode onto the main peaks of Kesara (filament) mountains etc. as they are of the same height as Meru. From them, flowing downwards, falling on the summits of Gandhamādana, through the middle of Bhadrāśva continent, she reaches the salty ocean in the eastern direction.

### Text 7

*एवं माल्यवच्छिखरान्निष्पतन्ती ततो ऽनुपरतवेगा केतुमालमभि चक्षुः*  
*प्रतीच्यां दिशि सरित्पतिं प्रविशति ॥७॥*

*evaṁ mālyavac-chikharān niṣpatantī tato 'nuparata-vegā ketumālam abhi cakṣuḥ pratīcyāṁ diśi sarit-patiṁ praviśati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this way; mālyavat-śikharāt—from the top of Mālyavān Mountain; niṣpatantī—falling down; tataḥ—thereafter; anuparata-vegā—whose force is uninterrupted; ketumālam abhi—into the land known as Ketumāla-varṣa; cakṣuḥ—the branch known as Cakṣu; pratīcyām—in the West; diśi—direction; sarit-patim—the ocean; praviśati—enters into.

**Перевод:**

**The branch of the Ganges known as Cakṣu falls onto the summit of Mālyavān Mountain and from there cascades onto the land of Ketumāla-varṣa. The Ganges flows incessantly through Ketumāla-varṣa and in this way also reaches the ocean of salt water in the West.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The stream named 'Cakṣus’, falls towards Ketumāla from the peak of Mālyavān.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, Cakṣus, the western stream, falling on the summit of Mālyavān, flowing downwards with unabated velocity, courses through the middle of Ketumāla varṣa and enters the salt-ocean in the western direction. The accusative case here is used with a desire to denote substrate as destination. *Similarly =* further also. The case of two specific preverbs “abhi” and “ni” is covered by the aphorism cited earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The different paths of the four-fold division of Gaṅgā is stated as starting with Sītā, etc. *Ocean with pungent taste* = salty ocean.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

From Kesara mountain, it falls in Ketumāla.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Even after falling the velocity is not reduced, i.e, with full speed (force).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Thus, gradually flowing down from Brahmā's abode, the stream named “Cakṣus,” approaches Ketumāla from the summit of Mālyavān and enters the ocean on the western direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Similarly, Cakṣus, from Brahmā's abode, first falls on the main peaks of the filament mountains and falling on the summit of Mālyavān, flowing downwards with unabated velocity, courses through the middle of Ketumāla varṣa and finally enters the ocean, the husband of rivers, in the western direction. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

### Text 8

*भद्रा चोत्तरतो मेरुशिरसो निपतिता गिरिशिखराद्गिरिशिखरमतिहाय शृङ्गवतः*  
*शृङ्गादवस्यन्दमाना उत्तरांस्तु कुरूनभित उदीच्यां दिशि जलधिमभिप्रविशति*  
*॥८॥*

*bhadrā cottarato meru-śiraso nipatitā giri-śikharād giri-śikharam atihāya śṛṅgavataḥ śṛṅgād avasyandamānā uttarāṁs tu kurūn abhita udīcyāṁ diśi jaladhim abhipraviśati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhadrā—the branch known as Bhadrā; ca—also; uttarataḥ—to the northern side; meru-śirasaḥ—from the top of Mount Meru; nipatitā—having fallen; giri-śikharāt—from the peak of Kumuda Mountain; giri-śikharam—to the peak of Nīla Mountain; atihāya—passing over as if not touching; śṛṅgavataḥ—of the mountain known as Śṛṅgavān; śṛṅgāt—from the peak; avasyandamānā—flowing; uttarān—the northern; tu—but; kurūn—the land known as Kuru; abhitaḥ—on all sides; udīcyām—in the northern; diśi—direction; jaladhim—the ocean of salt water; abhipraviśati—enters into.

**Перевод:**

**The branch of the Ganges known as Bhadrā flows from the northern side of Mount Meru. Its waters fall onto the peaks of Kumuda Mountain, Mount Nīla, Śveta Mountain and Śṛṅgavān Mountain in succession. Then it runs down into the province of Kuru and, after crossing through that land, flows into the saltwater ocean in the north.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*From hill-peak, etc.* = from the peak of Kumuda, she jumps to the summit of Nīla and from there to that of Śveta and crossing that flows down the peak of Śṛṅgavān.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, the stream Bhadrā, falling from the peaks of Meru to the north, jumping upwards from the peaks of Kumuda, jumps over the peak of Nīla without touching it, and falls on the peak of the mountain Śṛṅgavān and then flows down through the Kuru-varṣa, enters the salt-ocean in the northern direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

From the head of Meru, aerially falling on the summit of Nīla mountain; from the peak of Nīla mountain, she flows aerially to the summit of Śveta mountain; again hopping to the summit of the mountain Śṛṅgavān and from there, continues to flow through north Kuru region. The river then hops many peaks of the Niṣadha mountain and falls between the mountains Hemakūṭa and Himācala.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*From hill-peak* = from the peak of the Kesara (filament) mountain, she jumps up to the summit of Nīla and from there to that of Śveta and crossing that flows down the peak of Śṛṅgavān. She crosses the three continents Ilāvṛta, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Flows down towards* = crossing the three *varṣas* starting with Ilāvṛta.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The stream Bhadrā also jumps up from the peak of the mountain to the summit of the mountain Śveta, and hopping that also, descending from the peak of Śṛṅgavān, flows down through the north Kuru continent, drenching it on all sides and enters the salty ocean in the northern direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The stream Bhadrā also, falling from the peaks of Meru to the north, on the peaks of filament mountains and jumping upwards from them, falls over the peak of Nīla and from there, falls over the peak of Śveta and leaving it, reaches the peak of the mountain Śṛṅgavān and then flows down through the northern Kuru -varṣa, and finally enters the ocean in the northern direction. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

### Text 9

*तथैवालकनन्दा दक्षिणेन ब्रह्मसदनाद्बहूनि गिरिकूटान्यतिक्रम्य*  
*हेमकूटाद्धैमकूटान्यतिरभसतररंहसा लुठयन्ती भारतमभिवर्षं दक्षिणस्यां*  
*दिशि जलधिमभिप्रविशति यस्यां स्नानार्थं चागच्छतः पुंसः पदे पदेऽश्वमेधराज*  
*सूयादीनां फलं न दुर्लभमिति ॥९॥*

*tathaivālakanandā dakṣiṇena brahma-sadanād bahūni giri-kūṭāny atikramya hemakūṭād dhaimakūṭāny ati-rabhasatara-raṁhasā luṭhayantī bhāratam abhivarṣaṁ dakṣiṇasyāṁ diśi jaladhim abhipraviśati yasyāṁ snānārthaṁ cāgacchataḥ puṁsaḥ pade pade 'śvamedha-rājasūyādīnāṁ phalaṁ na durlabham iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tathā eva—similarly; alakanandā—the branch known as Alakanandā; dakṣiṇena—by the southern side; brahma-sadanāt—from the city known as Brahmapurī; bahūni—many; giri-kūṭāni—the tops of mountains; atikramya—crossing over; hemakūṭāt—from Hemakūṭa Mountain; haimakūṭāni—and Himakūṭa; ati-rabhasatara—more fiercely; raṁhasā—with great force; luṭhayantī—plundering; bhāratam abhivarṣam—on all sides of Bhārata-varṣa; dakṣiṇasyām—in the southern; diśi—direction; jaladhim—the ocean of salt water; abhipraviśati—enters into; yasyām—in which; snāna-artham—for bathing; ca—and; āgacchataḥ—of one who is coming; puṁsaḥ—a person; pade pade—at every step; aśvamedha-rājasūya-ādīnām—of great sacrifices like the Aśvamedha yajñaand Rājasūya yajña; phalam—the result; na—not; durlabham—very difficult to obtain; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, the branch of the Ganges known as Alakanandā flows from the southern side of Brahmapurī \[Brahma-sadana\]. Passing over the tops of mountains in various lands, it falls down with fierce force upon the peaks of the mountains Hemakūṭa and Himakūṭa. After inundating the tops of those mountains, the Ganges falls down onto the tract of land known as Bhārata-varṣa, which she also inundates. Then the Ganges flows into the ocean of salt water in the south. Persons who come to bathe in this river are fortunate. It is not very difficult for them to achieve with every step the results of performing great sacrifices like the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha yajñas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Atirabhasatararaṁhasā* = with an uninterrupted, very high velocity.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Similarly, the stream Alakanandā also, falling from the south of Brahmā's place, crossing many hill peaks of filament mountains, Kailāsa, Niṣadha, etc., reaching the hill Hemakūṭa, with an undiminished, high velocity, breaking many icy peaks related to Himālaya, covers the Bhārata-varṣa and enters the ocean in the southern direction. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

The descent of Gaṅgā in Kailāsa is to be necessarily mentioned, as is told in the fourth skandha, during the description of mount Kailāsa as: “Nandā and Alakanandā are the two rivers from outside, in front of Kailāsa; they are very sacred due to the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord which purifies everything.”

### Text 10

*अन्ये च नदा नद्यश्च वर्षे वर्षे सन्ति बहुशो मेर्वादिगिरिदुहितरः शतशः*  
*॥१०॥*

*anye ca nadā nadyaś ca varṣe varṣe santi bahuśo merv-ādi-giri-duhitaraḥ śataśaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

anye—many others; ca—also; nadāḥ—rivers; nadyaḥ—small rivers; ca—and; varṣe varṣe—in each tract of land; santi—are; bahuśaḥ—of many varieties; meru-ādi-giri-duhitaraḥ—daughters of the mountains beginning with Meru; śataśaḥ—in the hundreds.

**Перевод:**

**Many other rivers, both big and small, flow from the top of Mount Meru. These rivers are like daughters of the mountain, and they flow to the various tracts of land in hundreds of branches.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Bahuśaḥ* = of many types; *daughters of mountains Meru etc.* = born (emerging) from them.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Similarly, crossing the three continents, falling from peak to peak towards Bhārata, then hopping over the middle of the islands, the river flows in the continents closer to the ocean in the four directions of east. Descending from great mountains, falling to the ground, before reaching her husband (the ocean), she seems bent down out of shyness, having left her haughtiness. She falls to earth after meandering along the peaks between Hemakūṭa and Himālaya in the sky.  
*Wherein* = in Alakanandā. Regarding the phrase, “for bathing and drinking”: though in many books, the part of text from “yasyām” until “na durlabham” is not present, and even in some readings the phrase, “for drinking” is not there, still, in a book written over 500 years ago, this verse is seen with these phrases. Hence *sarvamedha etc.* is used. “Can be easily gotten” is the purport, since, an even greater fruit of liberation is attainable, as described in the scriptures. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Similarly, the southern stream Alakanandā, flowing from Brahmā's place on Meru, crossing many mountain peaks, without touching those in the middle, meanders through the peaks of Hemakūṭa and Himālaya, with very great velocity, covering the Bhārata-varṣa, and finally enters the ocean in the southern direction.

*Anye* = other; *male and female rivers, daughters of the mountains like Meru etc.* = originating from them, are in hundreds. “Anye” here is a residual (ekaśeṣa tatpuruṣa) compound meaning “anye ca anyāśca,” as per the aphorism “pumān striyā.” (See Śrīmad Bhāgavatam 1.2.67) \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

(Flowing) very fast = in a highly agitated state causing to the river’s water roll against the top and bottom rocks and then turn erratically.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By unimpeded, very high speed = breaking rocks.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The greatness of Gaṅgā due to the contact of the Lord's lotus feet is indicated here as: “If for anyone who even bathes in her waters, all sins are removed, then can there be any doubt that one who worships her with great conviction and determination will attaining release from worldly bondage and reach the Lord? The first canto of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam also confirms this: “by consuming the holy water of the heavenly river.”

### Text 11

*तत्रापि भारतमेव वर्षं कर्मक्षेत्रमन्यान्यष्ट वर्षाणि स्वर्गिणां*  
*पुण्यशेषोपभोगस्थानानि भौमानि स्वर्गपदानि व्यपदिशन्ति ॥११॥*

*tatrāpi bhāratam eva varṣaṁ karma-kṣetram anyāny aṣṭa varṣāṇi svargiṇāṁ puṇya-śeṣopabhoga-sthānāni bhaumāni svarga-padāni vyapadiśanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra api—out of all of them; bhāratam—known as Bhārata-varṣa; eva—certainly; varṣam—the tract of land; karma-kṣetram—the field of activities; anyāni—the others; aṣṭa varṣāṇi—eight tracts of land; svargiṇām—of the living entities elevated to the heavenly planets by extraordinary pious activities; puṇya—of the results of pious activities; śeṣa—of the remainder; upabhoga-sthānāni—the places for material enjoyment; bhaumāni svarga-padāni—as the heavenly places on earth; vyapadiśanti—they designate.

**Перевод:**

**Among the nine varṣas, the tract of land known as Bhārata-varṣa is understood to be the field of fruitive activities. Learned scholars and saintly persons declare the other eight varṣas to be meant for very highly elevated pious persons. After returning from the heavenly planets, they enjoy the remaining results of their pious activities in these eight earthly varṣas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Heaven is said to be of three types; as celestial, earthly and underground.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*There also* = in Jambūdvīpa also. Only in Bhārata-varṣa scriptural rituals can be performed, causing virtue and vice, yielding happiness and sorrow. This connects to “say so” in the end of the sentence. The other eight *varṣas* are for virtuous people who have already gone to celestial heaven and still possess some pious credits to enjoy. That is why they are said to be earthly heavens, but they are not for creating *karma* either virtuous or vicious. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

In the scriptures it is described how persons reach the moon (where they enjoy happiness in paradise) through the path of the manes (forefathers), by departing during the period of the smoke and after spending the fruit of their accrued virtues gained through sacrifices and giving in charity, once again return to earth. This is stated, “stay there until the deed lasts and then return by this same path again.” “Sampāta” here denotes deeds (*karma*) by the derivation, “reach heaven by this.” Another scriptural text states: “Whatever one does here, reaching there, (enjoys) it (the fruit) and on nearing that deed's end, comes back from that world, to this world, for karmic activity again.” Then, how can virtue be left over? How can the eight *varṣas* become the place for their enjoyment? We reply: it should be conceded that the residue of virtues minus those spent by enjoying the fruit in celestial heaven plus those vices which are not atoned, exist still, since, otherwise, there would be no reason for taking another birth on earth.

A scriptural text state, “those doing auspicious deeds attain auspicious births as a *brāhmaṇa*, *kṣatriya* or *vaiśya*.” The *smṛtis* also state: “those in the *varṇas* (castes) and *āśramas* (spiritual orders) following the stipulated duties, enjoy the fruit of their deeds after death and then return with their remaining *karma* to take birth in distinctive families and enjoy beauty, long life, learning, wealth, happiness, intelligence, etc.” Thus, birth in those continents is for enjoying the special fruits of residual virtues is plausible.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The speciality of Bhārata-varṣa among the nine *varṣas* is stated starting with “atrāpi.” The “field of action” = a place for performing deeds leading to virtues and sins. The other eight *varṣas* are the places of the virtuous, for enjoying the remaining virtues after attaining heaven by good deeds and experiencing happiness there. These are called earthly paradises, where pleasure is mixed with earthly pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

There are three types of heaven as divine, earthly and in caves.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*There also* = in Jambūdvīpa, glowing with nine *varṣas* (continents). The term *tatrāpi* is read by some as *atrāpi*, but both mean the same. *There* = in the three types.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Field of action* = place for performing the means for enjoying worldly pleasures or getting liberated. Heaven is of three types, viz. divine, earthly and subterranean. Among them, (the other eight *varṣas*) are mentioned as the places of earthly heaven. “Padam vyavasitatrāṇasth- ānalakṣmāṅghrivastuṣu” (*Amarakośa* 3.3.93) is the lexicon text supporting this meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

There are hundreds of daughters (rivers), of various types, originating from mountains such as Meru and there are also other male and female rivers in the continent.

### Text 12

*एषु पुरुषाणामयुतपुरुषायुर्वर्षाणां देवकल्पानां नागायुतप्राणानां*  
*वज्रसंहननबलवयोमोदप्रमुदितमहासौरतमिथुनव्यवायापवर्गवर्षधृतैकगर्भ कल*  
*त्राणां तत्र तु त्रेतायुगसमः कालो वर्तते ॥१२॥*

*eṣu puruṣāṇām ayuta-puruṣāyur-varṣāṇāṁ deva-kalpānāṁ nāgāyuta-prāṇānāṁ vajra-saṁhanana-bala-vayo-moda-pramudita-mahā-saurata-mithuna-vyavāyāpavarga-varṣa-dhṛtaika-garbha-kalatrāṇāṁ tatra tu tretā-yuga-samaḥ kālo vartate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṣu—in these (eight) varṣas, or tracts of land; puruṣāṇām—of all the men; ayuta—ten thousand; puruṣa—by the measure of men; āyuḥ-varṣāṇām—of those whose years of life; deva-kalpānām—who are like the demigods; nāga-ayuta-prāṇānām—having the strength of ten thousand elephants; vajra-saṁhanana—by bodies as solid as thunderbolts; bala—by bodily strength; vayaḥ—by youth; moda—by abundant sense enjoyment; pramudita—being excited; mahā-saurata—a great deal of sexual; mithuna—combinations of man and woman; vyavāya-apavarga—at the end of their period of sexual enjoyment; varṣa—in the last year; dhṛta-eka-garbha—who conceive one child; kalatrāṇām—of those who have wives; tatra—there; tu—but; tretā-yuga-samaḥ—exactly like the Tretā-yuga (when there is no tribulation); kālaḥ—time; vartate—exists.

**Перевод:**

**In these eight varṣas, or tracts of land, human beings live ten thousand years according to earthly calculations. All the inhabitants are almost like demigods. They have the bodily strength of ten thousand elephants. Indeed, their bodies are as sturdy as thunderbolts. The youthful duration of their lives is very pleasing, and both men and women enjoy sexual union with great pleasure for a long time. After years of sensual pleasure—when a balance of one year of life remains—the wife conceives a child. Thus the standard of pleasure for the residents of these heavenly regions is exactly like that of the human beings who lived during Tretā-yuga.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By human measure = 10,000 year life-span of men. *Vajrasaṁhanana* = body is hard like diamond. *In that* = couples happy by strength and age indulge freely in copulation and near the end of their lives when one year remains in their life-span life, their wives conceive a child but once. *Equal to the Tretā-yuga* = due to superior sensual pleasure. In Kṛta-yuga, all are inclined to meditation. In Dvāpara, etc. are mixed with more misery. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī and Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Puruṣamānena* = by human measure. *Mithunas* = man and woman (husband-wife), pairs. In many versions of this text there are the words, “tatra tu,” but that is only recent and is useless anyway as it is unrelated.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He then narrates, in two prose sentences, those eight continents, starting “yeṣu” and “yatra ha”: wherein, those eight *varṣas*, people live as though in the Tretā age with great happiness. Tretā is mentioned because in the Kṛta Age people are deeply involved in meditation and in Dvāpara, etc. miseries are more. How are they? They are similar to demigods, strong as 10,000 elephants, they have 10,000 year life-spans (by human count) and their bodies are hard like diamonds. The couples have extensive intercourse, with vigor, age and delight, and their wives conceive a baby when one year is left of their lives. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

For those living in those varṣas, the time is like the Tretā Age. The wives of the couples bear a single child after sexual union, like in the harem of kings in palaces, towards the end of their life. The men have hard bodies like diamonds, strength, age, ordinary and special delights. They indulge in copulation continuously with their consorts who conceive but once. There is a rumor that if they conceive many times, their bodies would loosen, thus the wives would lose their youthful appearance and for fear of interrupting their intercourse, they prefer to bear only one child in progeny.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

As heaven is of three types as divine, earthly and underground, the other eight *varṣas* are said to be earthly heaven. The reason for this is, those who go to celestial heaven by great virtues, spend their virtues there by enjoying and the remainder is to be enjoyed in these earthly heavens.

### Text 13

*यत्र ह देवपतयः स्वैः स्वैर्गणनायकैर्विहितमहार्हणाः सर्वर्तुकुसुम*  
*स्तबकफलकिसलयश्रियानम्यमानविटपलता विटपिभिरुपशुम्भमानरुचिर*  
*काननाश्रमायतनवर्षगिरिद्रोणीषु तथा चामलजलाशयेषु विकचविविधनववन*  
*रुहामोदमुदितराजहंसजलकुक्कुटकारण्डवसारसचक्रवाकादिभिर्मधुकरनिकराकृति*  
*भिरुपकूजितेषु जलक्रीडादिभिर्विचित्रविनोदैः सुललितसुरसुन्दरीणां*  
*कामकलिलविलासहासलीलावलोकाकृष्टमनोदृष्टयः स्वैरं विहरन्ति ॥१३॥*

*yatra ha deva-patayaḥ svaiḥ svair gaṇa-nāyakair vihita-mahārhaṇāḥ sarvartu-kusuma-stabaka-phala-kisalaya-śriyānamyamāna-viṭapa-latā-viṭapibhir upaśumbhamāna-rucira-kānanāśramāyatana-varṣa-giri-droṇīṣu tathā cāmala-jalāśayeṣu vikaca-vividha-nava-vanaruhāmoda-mudita-rāja-haṁsa-jala-kukkuṭa-kāraṇḍava-sārasa-cakravākādibhir madhukara-nikarākṛtibhir upakūjiteṣu jala-krīḍādibhir vicitra-vinodaiḥ sulalita-sura-sundarīṇāṁ kāma-kalila-vilāsa-hāsa-līlāvalokākṛṣṭa-mano-dṛṣṭayaḥ svairaṁ viharanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatra ha—in those eight tracts of land; deva-patayaḥ—the lords of the demigods, such as Lord Indra; svaiḥ svaiḥ—by their own respective; gaṇa-nāyakaiḥ—leaders of the servants; vihita—furnished with; mahā-arhaṇāḥ—valuable gifts, such as sandalwood pulp and garlands; sarva-ṛtu—in all seasons; kusuma-stabaka—of bunches of flowers; phala—of fruits; kisalaya-śriyā—by the opulences of shoots; ānamyamāna—being bent down; viṭapa—whose branches; latā—and creepers; viṭapibhiḥ—by many trees; upaśumbhamāna—being fully decorated; rucira—beautiful; kānana—gardens; āśrama-āyatana—and many hermitages; varṣa-giri-droṇīṣu—the valleys between the mountains designating the borders of the tracts of land; tathā—as well as; ca—also; amala-jala-āśayeṣu—in lakes with clear water; vikaca—just fructified; vividha—varieties; nava-vanaruha-āmoda—by the fragrance of lotus flowers; mudita—enthused; rāja-haṁsa—great swans; jala-kukkuṭa—water fowl; kāraṇḍava—aquatic birds called kāraṇḍavas; sārasa—cranes; cakravāka-ādibhiḥ—by birds known as cakravākas and so on; madhukara-nikara-ākṛtibhiḥ—by the bumblebees; upakūjiteṣu—which were made to resound; jala-krīḍā-ādibhiḥ—such as water sports; vicitra—various; vinodaiḥ—by pastimes; su-lalita—attractive; sura-sundarīṇām—of the women of the demigods; kāma—from lust; kalila—born; vilāsa—pastimes; hāsa—smiling; līlā-avaloka—by playful glances; ākṛṣṭa-manaḥ—whose minds are attracted; dṛṣṭayaḥ—and whose vision is attracted; svairam—very freely; viharanti—engage in sportive enjoyment.

**Перевод:**

**In each of those tracts of land, there are many gardens filled with flowers and fruits according to the season, and there are beautifully decorated hermitages as well. Between the great mountains demarcating the borders of those lands lie enormous lakes of clear water filled with newly grown lotus flowers. Aquatic birds such as swans, ducks, water chickens, and cranes become greatly excited by the fragrance of lotus flowers, and the charming sound of bumblebees fills the air. The inhabitants of those lands are important leaders among the demigods. Always attended by their respective servants, they enjoy life in gardens alongside the lakes. In this pleasing situation, the wives of the demigods smile playfully at their husbands and look upon them with lusty desires. All the demigods and their wives are constantly supplied with sandalwood pulp and flower garlands by their servants. In this way, all the residents of the eight heavenly varṣas enjoy, attracted by the activities of the opposite sex.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Yatra ha* = in which *varṣas*; *leading deities along with their main groups of servants* = being served well, enjoy at will. In which places? In all continents amid breathtaking valleys, forests and gardens with dwellings beautified by flowers, trees and creepers. There, stimulating romance, pure water lakes various types of lotus flowers blossom and spread their fragrance, royal swans swim, honeybees hum and divine damsels cavort and attract the mind. \[Note this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Śukadeva, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The masters of the demigods, being served well by the leaders of groups of their respective servants, enjoy at will in this *varṣa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Where =* in which *varṣas*, lords of demigods sport at will. In which places? Where trees have bent-down branches and creepers due to a wealth of flowers, fruits, sprouts, etc. born in all seasons. These trees are very distinct from those in Bhārata-khaṇḍa and make lustrous, beautiful hermitage dwellings, rain-causing hill-valleys, (both sides being tall and the middle being low). In pure water sources like ponds, with fragrant, blossomed, various forest lotuses, pleasing royal swans, delightful humming black bees (this is adjective of pond), their minds and eyes are attracted by the amorous dalliances of sensuous, divine nymphs.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Even now* = after the descent, at all times.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Wherein masters of demigods enjoy at will. In all seasons, due to the abundance of flowers etc. trees bend very much. By their branches and creepers, the forests become lustrous. There, rain-indicating hills (in their water-bodies), provide cooing royal swans and large black bees of distinct species. Here, the use of the locative case is denoted by past passive suffix. The lack of possessive case is sagely usage.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Rain-hills are those that portend rains in their valleys. In “upakūjiteṣu,” the past passive suffix niṣṭhā (“kta”) is in the sense of locus. The lack of using the genitive case is sagely usage.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Where even demigods take great delight, what is the surprise that humans should wish to delight there? The maxim of “how much more” (an argument “a fortiori”) proves their earthly heaven-ness. There on eight continents, even the masters among the demigods such as Indra are served well by garlands, sandal paste and servants while they enjoy water-sporting with beautiful damsels.

### Text 14

*नवस्वपि वर्षेषु भगवान्नारायणो महापुरुषः पुरुषाणां तदनुग्रहायात्मतत्त्व*  
*व्यूहेनात्मनाद्यापि सन्निधीयते ॥१४॥*

*navasv api varṣeṣu bhagavān nārāyaṇo mahā-puruṣaḥ puruṣāṇāṁ tad-anugrahāyātma-tattva-vyūhenātmanādyāpi sannidhīyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

navasu—in the nine; api—certainly; varṣeṣu—tracts of land known as varṣas; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nārāyaṇaḥ—Lord Viṣṇu; mahā-puruṣaḥ—the Supreme Person; puruṣāṇām—unto His various devotees; tat-anugrahāya—to show His mercy; ātma-tattva-vyūhena—by expansions of Himself in the quadruple forms Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha; ātmanā—personally; adya api—until now; sannidhīyate—is near the devotees for accepting their services.

**Перевод:**

**To show mercy to His devotees in each of these nine tracts of land, the Supreme Personality of Godhead known as Nārāyaṇa expands Himself in His quadruple principles of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. In this way He remains near His devotees to accept their service.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

For blessing the persons in all the nine continents, He remains always near, dividing Himself appropriately.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In all the nine *varṣas* starting with Ilāvṛta, Lord Nārāyaṇa, is served by the great person in-charge of that continent. In order to bless the persons in those continents, even today, He remains present in His transcendental forms that are beyond imagination. Those forms are absolutely unlike all known things and contain unsurpassed, innumerable, auspicious qualities. These forms are not expansions like His *vyūha* forms of Saṅkarṣaṇa, etc., since, in Harivarṣa the forms for contemplation are the *vibhava* form of Narahari (man-lion). It cannot be the *vyūha* forms because that would contradict the common form in all nine *varṣas* being described. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The time is not spent in only conjugal bliss in the nine *varṣas*, but also in worship of Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The internal form of the Lord (not external) is invoked, installed and worshipped in all nine *varṣas* \[by the men\]. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

For the sake of blessing the persons with His grace, Lord Nārāyaṇa remains present with His expansions. Here, probably the object of worship is the Lord's *arcā* deity forms only, since, later, Prahlāda also pleads Him to manifest.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

For the sake of blessing those worshipping Him in all the nine continents, He remains present by His grace with His expansion forms like Saṅkarṣaṇa, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The characteristics of *vibhava* forms, etc. are to be known from *Tattva-traya, Laghu Bhāgavatāmṛta*, etc.

### Text 15

*इलावृते तु भगवान् भव एक एव पुमान्न ह्यन्यस्तत्रापरो निर्विशति*  
*भवान्याः शापनिमित्तज्ञो यत्प्रवेक्ष्यतः स्त्रीभावस्तत्पश्चाद्वक्ष्यामि ॥१५॥*

*ilāvṛte tu bhagavān bhava eka eva pumān na hy anyas tatrāparo nirviśati bhavānyāḥ śāpa-nimitta-jño yat-pravekṣyataḥ strī-bhāvas tat paścād vakṣyāmi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilāvṛte—in the tract of land known as Ilāvṛta-varṣa; tu—but; bhagavān—the most powerful; bhavaḥ—Lord Śiva; eka—only; eva—certainly; pumān—male person; na—not; hi—certainly; anyaḥ—any other; tatra—there; aparaḥ—besides; nirviśati—enters; bhavānyāḥ śāpa-nimitta-jñaḥ—who knows the cause of the curse by Bhavānī, the wife of Lord Śiva; yat-pravekṣyataḥ—of one who forcibly enters that tract of land; strī-bhāvaḥ—transformation into a female; tat—that; paścāt—later; vakṣyāmi—I shall explain.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: In the tract of land known as Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the only male person is Lord Śiva, the most powerful demigod. Goddess Durgā, the wife of Lord Śiva, does not like any man to enter that land. If any foolish man dares to do so, she immediately turns him into a woman. I shall explain this later \[in the Ninth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Apara* = later, more recent; *later* = in the Ninth Canto of the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The divine forms for contemplation and the seekers in the *varṣas* beginning with Ilāvṛta are now mentioned. In Ilāvṛta continent, Lord Rudra is the only male person living (no other male member lives) there. This is because Bhavānī, his wife, cursed that any man entering there, even unknowingly, would become transformed into a woman. The episode is explained later (in the Ninth Canto of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

In Ilāvṛta, the forms of the Lord and Their seekers are mentioned.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The eternal revelation of self manifest, original incarnations of Pradyumna are shown sporting in all nine *varṣas* is narrated. These are not arca deity forms made of stone or metal. The fact that these incarnations are present even now indicates that They are eternal.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Later* = in the Ninth Canto.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In the nine *varṣas* the Lord is always present in His full features. These are not arca forms but rather as in the manifestation of Pradyumna, whose movements, gestures, pastimes etc. will be narrated. *Even now* = from the time of the incarnation until now also; always. Here, according to the commentator Viśvanātha, in the continents, the objects of meditation are to be known as the forms of the Lord only, since in a later skandha, as Prahlāda pleads “kindly manifest, manifest.” But to me, it appears that, by contemplating on the form of the incarnations there, immediately the Lord manifests, therefore he is said to become present.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The Supreme Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is worshipped by Lord Rudra, the only male person in Ilāvṛta continent. No other man enters who knows about the curse of Pārvatī. *Later* = in the Ninth Canto. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This curse is only effective in the place between Kailāsa and Karavīra mountains in Ilāvṛta continent. Otherwise, if the entire Ilāvṛta continent were taken as cursed, the existence of demigods in Meru, earthly heavens and the Lord’s pastimes of visiting to the places of Indra and other demigods for recoveries, etc. which are mentioned in the Tenth Canto of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*, would all be contradicted.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

There, the forms for contemplation and the seekers in the *varṣas* Ilāvṛta, etc. are now mentioned.

### Text 16

*भवानीनाथैः स्त्रीगणार्बुदसहस्रै रवरुध्यमानो भगवतश्चतुर्मूर्तेर्महापुरुषस्य*  
*तुरीयां तामसीं मूर्तिं प्रकृतिमात्मनः सङ्कर्षणसंज्ञामात्मसमाधिरूपेण*  
*सन्निधाप्यैतदभिगृणन् भव उपधावति ॥१६॥*

*bhavānī-nāthaiḥ strī-gaṇārbuda-sahasrair avarudhyamāno bhagavataś catur-mūrter mahā-puruṣasya turīyāṁ tāmasīṁ mūrtiṁ prakṛtim ātmanaḥ saṅkarṣaṇa-saṁjñām ātma-samādhi-rūpeṇa sannidhāpyaitad abhigṛṇan bhava upadhāvati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhavānī-nāthaiḥ—by the company of Bhavānī; strī-gaṇa—of females; arbuda-sahasraiḥ—by ten billion; avarudhyamānaḥ—always being served; bhagavataḥ catuḥ-mūrteḥ—the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is expanded in four; mahā-puruṣasya—of the Supreme Person; turīyām—the fourth expansion; tāmasīm—related to the mode of ignorance; mūrtim—the form; prakṛtim—as the source; ātmanaḥ—of himself (Lord Śiva); saṅkarṣaṇa-saṁjñām—known as Saṅkarṣaṇa; ātma-samādhi-rūpeṇa—by meditating upon Him in trance; sannidhāpya—bringing Him near; etat—this; abhigṛṇan—clearly chanting; bhavaḥ—Lord Śiva; upadhāvati—worships.

**Перевод:**

**In Ilāvṛta-varṣa, Lord Śiva is always encircled by ten billion maidservants of goddess Durgā, who minister to him. The quadruple expansion of the Supreme Lord is composed of Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Saṅkarṣaṇa. Saṅkarṣaṇa, the fourth expansion, is certainly transcendental, but because his activities of destruction in the material world are in the mode of ignorance, He is known as tāmasī, the Lord's form in the mode of ignorance. Lord Śiva knows that Saṅkarṣaṇa is the original cause of his own existence, and thus he always meditates upon Him in trance by chanting the following mantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Bhavānīnātha* = of whom Bhavānī, i.e, Pārvatī, is the mistress; *surrounded by thousands of females* = served by thousands of females; *prakṛti* = cause of himself; *in the form of self* = meditation; *reciting the hymn etc.* = that will be told.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

There, Lord Bhava (Rudra) and the mistress for tens of thousands of females, namely his wife Bhavānī, are served. Bhavānīnātha may be a separate adjective for Bhava, which might indicate the presence of Bhavānī. The fourth form of the four forms = Vāsudeva; *great person, the Lord, called Saṅkarṣaṇa,* = Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Saṅkarṣaṇa; the fourth order = with disregard to order; *tāmasī* = the presiding deity of “tamas”; “tamas” here refers to nature (pradhāna), as it is used in such sense in the texts, “tamas” existed and by “tamas” the known was hidden. The avyakta (primary germ of nature) dissolves in “akṣara,” the “akṣara” dissolves in “tamas,” which covers knowledge. The controller of “tamas” is the meaning. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

Placing the form firmly in the mind *is the process* (should be added). Reciting the following hymn, Bhava worships Saṅkarṣaṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Rudra, surrounded by those (females) with Bhavānī as their mistress, worships with deep meditation, the fourth part of the Lord Vāsudeva (tāmasī) the source of himself and the activator of the quality of “tamas” which causes destruction. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī and Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Tāmasī* = causing “tamas,” as it is the cause of dissolution (deluge).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Actually, *turīyā* = fourth, i.e, beyond sattva, rajas and tamas, i.e. of pure consciousness; due to *“one who has no māyā”* and “bereft of the three (qualities)” will be described further. *Cause of the living entities* = as it is shared by him; *by deep meditation* = concentration of the mind on the form. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Reciting the hymns* = shall be described further.

### Text 17

*श्रीभगवानुवाच*  
*ॐ नमो भगवते महापुरुषाय सर्वगुणसङ्ख्यानायानन्तायाव्यक्ताय*  
*नम इति ॥१७॥*

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*oṁ namo bhagavate mahā-puruṣāya sarva-guṇa-saṅkhyānāyānantāyāvyaktāya nama iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the most powerful Lord Śiva says; oṁ namo bhagavate—O Supreme Personality of Godhead, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You; mahā-puruṣāya—who are the Supreme person; sarva-guṇa-saṅkhyānāya—the reservoir of all transcendental qualities; anantāya—the unlimited; avyaktāya—not manifested within the material world; namaḥ—my respectful obeisances; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**The most powerful Lord Śiva says: O Supreme Personality of Godhead, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You in Your expansion as Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa. You are the reservoir of all transcendental qualities. Although You are unlimited, You remain unmanifest to the nondevotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Although He is the illumination of all attributes, He himself is indistinct, immeasurable and not properly understood.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hymn for reciting is, “Oṁ namaḥ.” Oṁ denotes Brahman as it is stated, “‘oṁ, tat, sat’ are the three forms denoting Brahman.” (*Bhagavad-gītā* 17.23). The meaning of *oṁ* is all sentient and non-sentient things in this world. The eternal world is subservient to Him and is fully under his direction. *Bhagavate* denotes the six main qualities and *great person* denotes creation, maintenance and destruction as His pastimes. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

The word “mahāpuruṣa” reminds us of the scriptural text in the Puruṣa Sūkta; “I know this great person” indicates “from Him was born Virāṭ”which denotes the principal cause of the entire world. The words, “adbhyaḥ sambhūtaḥ” again specifies the great person. This paragraph along with the eight verses, “hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre” is instructed as a single context (in *Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad*), denoting the (four-faced) Brahmā (Hiraṇyagarbha), born from waters, and hence all such scriptural texts following these in stating Brahmā as the origin of the creation of the world denote the great person. He possesses all the auspicious qualities required for being the (material and efficient) cause of the world, those required for His being approachable by devotees and those needed for granting the wishes of the devotees. Further the scriptures sing of His omniscience, omnipotence, compassion, friendliness, accessibility, knowledge and power. This corresponds to the scriptural statement, “whose abode all the Vedas proclaim.”

The Vedas denote His qualities by the word by the word “anantāya”—infinite.This also indicates His being the worthy object of worship and attainment. The means to attain Him is nothing but seeking His feet alone as also stated in *Puruṣa Sūkta*: “knowing Him thus, the seeker reaches immortality here; there exists no other path (for reaching).” This rejects any other means literally as “avyaktāya” which means he is not accessible or comprehended by the senses (avyakta). Texts like “(that) is not grasped by eyes (sight) or speech (words)” reiterate this. For such a person, we bow down. “Obeisances” here is illustrative of meditation upon. The meaning is, “That alone is the means for my protection.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Renowned with all qualities like knowledge and well-known in scriptures etc. indicate “Brahman is of knowledge and bliss.” “Anantāya” suggests that Lord Viṣṇu, inherent in Ananta and with that name, is being worshipped by Śiva along with him (Ananta). It is said: “Lord Viṣṇu, being Ananta, and being within Ananta, is worshipped by Giriśa, along with him in Ilāvṛta (continent).” But, if Ananta also is worshipped along with Lord Viṣṇu, then, the doubt might arise as to how Ananta can be the giver of liberation. This is to be cleared by the maxim, “when Lord Viṣṇu is praised along with others, then such praises are to be known as mixed.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This womanhood is due to meditating with a servant's devotion. The Lord said Saṅkarṣaṇa being the first person, is praised *oṁ namaḥ*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The illumination of all attributes comes from Him but He himself is not perceivable.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Cause of self* = as it is said, “between the crooked eye-brows of whom, Rudra, the part of Saṅkarṣaṇa arose.”

It should be known that the multitude of females was manifested simultaneously by the Lord for serving Pārvatī and they all have recreation, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The hymn to be recited is, *oṁ*. By scriptural texts like, “who is omniscient...” His attributes are declared.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Bhavānī is the mistress for thousands of women. Bhava worships with the praise the great person, the Lord, with four forms as Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Saṅkarṣaṇa. The fourth of them, named Saṅkarṣaṇa, presides over “tamas,” is the cause of self, is known as “tāmasa,” and is brought near by meditation.

### Text 18

*भजे भजन्यारणपादपङ्कजं*  
*भगस्य कृत्स्नस्य परं परायणम् ।*  
*भक्तेष्वलं भावितभूतभावनं*  
*भवापहं त्वा भवभावमीश्वरम् ॥१८॥*

*bhaje bhajanyāraṇa-pāda-paṅkajaṁ*  
*bhagasya kṛtsnasya paraṁ parāyaṇam*  
*bhakteṣv alaṁ bhāvita-bhūta-bhāvanaṁ*  
*bhavāpahaṁ tvā bhava-bhāvam īśvaram*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhaje—I worship; bhajanya—O worshipable Lord; araṇa-pāda-paṅkajam—whose lotus feet protect His devotees from all fearful situations; bhagasya—of opulences; kṛtsnasya—of all different varieties (wealth, fame, strength, knowledge, beauty and renunciation); param—the best; parāyaṇam—the ultimate shelter; bhakteṣu—to the devotees; alam—beyond value; bhāvita-bhūta-bhāvanam—who manifests His different forms for the satisfaction of His devotees; bhava-apaham—who stops the devotees' repetition of birth and death; tvā—unto You; bhava-bhāvam—who is the origin of the material creation; īśvaram—the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, You are the only worshipable person, for You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the reservoir of all opulences. Your secure lotus feet are the only source of protection for all Your devotees, whom You satisfy by manifesting Yourself in various forms. O my Lord, You deliver Your devotees from the clutches of material existence. Nondevotees, however, remain entangled in material existence by Your will. Kindly accept me as Your eternal servant.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

O! (one) worthy of worship! I worship you, the supreme power! Your lotus feet are the refuge. You are the supreme repository for all the six chief qualities of power, etc.” He reveals Himself to and removes the bondage for His devotees whereas non-devotees remain in bondage. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Gives verses echoing these sentiments further: “I worship you, the Lord.” The qualifications of that Lord are: one whose lotus-feet are worthy of serving and attaining. In the word “bhajanya,” the vowel “ī” of the suffix “anīyar” is omitted due to sagely usage, or “bhajanya” is a separate word in the vocative case. Or those who do worship are “bhajanas,” which becomes “bhajanam” in the instrumental mode. When the “ṭi” is omitted to mean “does that” gets the suffix “kvip” in a genitive sense (bhajana); one who goes to them (yāti), comes near “bhajanya.” The word “bhajana” ending in the consonant “n,” gets the *kṛt* affix “ka” introduced after the verbal stem ending in the vowel “ā” when not co-occurring with a pre-verb, but co-occurring with a nominal word functioning as the direct object by the aphorism “ātonupasarge kaḥ” (aṣṭā. 3.2.3). “Ṭi” is not omitted.

“Parāyaṇam” = the only shelter of all qualities like power or revealed very well among devotees or the principal cause of all things is the essential form. Or “bhūtabhāvanam” means the cause of prosperity of beings or the destroyer of bondage for devotees. Mukti or liberation depends on His will. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Brahmā was created by or meditated on whom; such a person (you) is the object of devotion (bhāva) for devotees (bhava) like me.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Bhajanīya* = worthy of worship; the purport is that it is improper to worship anyone but one's own cause. Or, if the reading is taken as “*bhaje bhaje* araṇa-pāda-paṅkajam,” one whose lotus-feet are truly refuge, I serve him, I serve him.” The repetition here is out of delight. *Bhūtabhāvana* means “present as an embellishment in things of creation or created by mind or simply *meditated*. In other words, “you are the target of my devotion.” Revered Svāmi \[Śrīdhara Svāmi \]has taken *bhava* as world and *bhāvayitā* as one who creates it. Or else, *bhajanya*, one who is worth serving, and has red, lotus-feet. O! (one) meditated on intensely by devotees! or (one) satisfied with or charmed. Or else *bhavāpaha* is he who renounces the world, the liberated one, and hence, the Lord is the one who destroys bondage. *Bhava* refers to auspicious virtue and its origin is from Him.

*Bhaga =* like earlier. *Īśvara* = the all-powerful, Lord. By the aphorism, “stheśabhāsapisakaso varac” (aṣṭā. 3.2.175), the suffix “varac” is in the sense of habitual disposition. By this, the praise of Hari as non-different from the servant is suggested. Or else, *one who has a bow (iṣu)* to his devotee (*bhakte*), *me* (Sanskrit), meaning Cupid. *Alambha* indicates negation or anger. Brahmā says: “by the sight of anger, fortunate ones indeed burn lust (Cupid).” *Avitā* = the savior. So the Lord is “bhakteṣvalambhāvita,” meaning “O, protector from anger!” During the sacrifice of Dakṣa, though very much disregarded, Rudra did not lose temper and this address refers to him.

You serve (bhaja) the inner ruler, the Lord. How is He? Ī refers to Lakṣmī and one who has reddish, lotus-feet, worthy of her service, and is the basis for success and auspiciousness. This means He is the shelter for auspiciousness of all sentient beings from Brahmā onwards. *Bhūtabhāvana* is one who creates the past, present and future worlds. *Bhava* means the *world as it is created* and its annihilator into himself is *bhavāpaha*. The form “ha” in “apaha” is from the verbal root “o hāṅ” in the sense of going, with “a” as suffix, or from the verbal root “hṛ,” with the omission of “ṭi” the portion starting from the last vowel. The learned consider “i” as Cupid, “ī” as Lakṣmī and “u” as Bhava,” is from the monosyllabic definition. \[Note: these two paragraphs are repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The hymn is mentioned as, *oṁ namaḥ*. To the Lord, one replete with the six major qualities of Lordship, etc. *Great person* = best among persons. But, how can *tāmasa* be the Lord (with six major qualities)? The effects of all the qualities are coming from Him. Then, how is the reference as tāmasa (inert, dark) to the illuminator of all? Although for the sake of effects, tamas (darkness) is admitted, He is essentially infinite in terms of space, time and things, as denoted by the word “anantāya.” But then, why is He not perceived so? He is subtle and unperceivable by senses and is beyond words and the imagination of the mind.

The word “namaḥ” used in the beginning and end is to indicate that it applies to all the words of the sentence in dative case. “Iti” signals the end of the hymn.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Praising the Lord with “bhaje”— “O one worthy of worship!” In the word “bhajanya,” the vowel “ī” is omitted due to sagely usage. Him, whose lotus-feet is the “araṇa,” protector, refuge. Or another version is “bhajanīya” is worthy of worship and “araṇa” the lotus feet is worthy of attaining.

### Text 19

*न यस्य मायागुणचित्तवृत्तिभि*  
*र्निरीक्षतो ह्यण्वपि दृष्टिरज्यते ।*  
*ईशे यथा नोऽजितमन्युरंहसां*  
*कस्तं न मन्येत जिगीषुरात्मनः ॥१९॥*

*na yasya māyā-guṇa-citta-vṛttibhir*  
*nirīkṣato hy aṇv api dṛṣṭir ajyate*  
*īśe yathā no 'jita-manyu-raṁhasāṁ*  
*kas taṁ na manyeta jigīṣur ātmanaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—never; yasya—whose; māyā—of the illusory energy; guṇa—in the qualities; citta—of the heart; vṛttibhiḥ—by the activities (thinking. feeling and willing); nirīkṣataḥ—of Him who is glancing; hi—certainly; aṇu—slightly; api—even; dṛṣṭiḥ—vision; ajyate—is affected; īśe—for the purpose of regulating; yathā—as; naḥ—of us; ajita—who have not conquered; manyu—of anger; raṁhasām—the force; kaḥ—who; tam—unto Him (the Supreme Lord); na—not; manyeta—would worship; jigīṣuḥ—aspiring to conquer; ātmanaḥ—the senses.

**Перевод:**

**We cannot control the force of our anger. Therefore when we look at material things, we cannot avoid feeling attraction or repulsion for them. But the Supreme Lord is never affected in this way. Although He glances over the material world for the purpose of creating, maintaining and destroying it, He is not affected, even to the slightest degree. Therefore, one who desires to conquer the force of the senses must take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord. Then he will be victorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The term “na yasya” meaning whose sight, even while seeing things, for ruling, controlling, is not blurred even atomically by the qualities of *māyā*, objects, sensory inclination etc explains why His Lordship is not disqualified by the term *tāmasa* (inert). *Īṭ* denotes controlling, in the sense of “state,” derived with the suffix “kvip,” being a member of the “sampadādi” list. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

A counter example is: unlike us whose sight is blurred due to not conquering the force of anger. Hence, who, desirous of conquering one's senses, could disregard this? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava and Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In the aphorism “sampadādi...,” although, due to the presence of the pre-verb “sam,” the suffix “kvip” can be added only for words with pre-verb, still, here, taking shelter under sagely usage only it can be reconciled. Otherwise, the aphorism would have been “padādi...” itself.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

But how can Lord Hari who exists in the world be “*bhaga*,” (the possessor of six major qualities) since He also would become helpless due to the contact with *māyā*, like us? The answer is: “Your sight is not even slightly subdued by the contact of nature’s qualities.” “Iha” denotes emphasis. The reason is, “You are the Lord.” The word-form “*īṭ*” is possible from the verbal stem “*īśa-aiśvarye*,” with the suffix “*kvip*,” even without a subordinate word. Hence, *īśaḥ* is genitive. The meaning is: He is praiseworthy and excellently capable of removing any trace of defect.

*Ātmanaḥ* is accusative by the saying “*kṛdyoge ṣaṣṭhī.*” The essential form of self may also be indicated by “ātmā.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

For the sake of devotees, He intensely performs the creation and protection of all beings.

### Text 20

*असद्दृशो यः प्रतिभाति मायया*  
*क्षीबेव मध्वासवताम्रलोचनः ।*  
*न नागवध्वोऽर्हण ईशिरे ह्रिया*  
*यत्पादयोः स्पर्शनधर्षितेन्द्रियाः ॥२०॥*

*asad-dṛśo yaḥ pratibhāti māyayā*  
*kṣībeva madhv-āsava-tāmra-locanaḥ*  
*na nāga-vadhvo 'rhaṇa īśire hriyā*  
*yat-pādayoḥ sparśana-dharṣitendriyāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

asat-dṛśaḥ—for a person with polluted vision; yaḥ—who; pratibhāti—appears; māyayā—the influence of māyā; kṣībaḥ—one who is inebriated or angry; iva—like; madhu—by honey; āsava—and liquor; tāmra-locanaḥ—having eyes reddish like copper; na—not; nāga-vadhvaḥ—the wives of the serpent demon; arhaṇe—in worshiping; īśire—were unable to proceed; hriyā—because of bashfulness; yat-pādayoḥ—of whose lotus feet; sparśana—by the touching; dharṣita—agitated; indriyāḥ—whose senses.

**Перевод:**

**For persons with impure vision, the Supreme Lord's eyes appear like those of someone who indiscriminately drinks intoxicating beverages. Thus bewildered, such unintelligent persons become angry at the Supreme Lord, and due to their angry mood the Lord Himself appears angry and very fearful. However, this is an illusion. When the wives of the serpent demon were agitated by the touch of the Lord's lotus feet, due to shyness they could proceed no further in their worship of Him. Yet the Lord remained unagitated by their touch, for He is equipoised in all circumstances. Therefore who will not worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

For one drunk by self-delusion the Lord appears dangerously mad like one whose eyes are reddened by drinking liquors of honey or distilled spirits. By the worship of the Lord’s feet, the wives of the serpent’s senses became seduced and they could not move their shoulders, etc. due to shyness. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī and Śukadeva\]

Who would disregard such a person? This sentence is connected to the previous verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

How could desire and so on not arise in someone perceived as tāmasa? The answer is in given “asad-dṛśaḥ.” “To one who identifies himself with the body (“asat”), whose eyes are reddish because of intoxicating liquor, You appear as drunk.” In “kṣībeva,” the *sandhi* (euphonic combination) is sagely (for “kṣība iva”). “In fact, Your form is of pure sattva, supernatural, causeless and is liberating for meditators. Hence, the wives of the snakes, their minds going out of control due to the touch of your lotus feet, were unable to worship them without apprehension. Because they thought, ‘how can we touch His holy feet, being influenced by amorous desires?’ Who would not regard such a Person” This sentence is connected to the previous verse. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Proper knowledge of the essential nature of Lord Hari, who is very close due to being the immanent ruler, is possible through good means only. This is indicated by the word “asaṁdṛśaḥ.” “Those who are bereft of proper knowledge due to the shrouding power of material nature (*māyā*), like those who drink toxic liquor either generated from tree-cavity, honey or distilled from flowers of coconuts etc., lose their discrimination by hearing bad scriptures and with reddish eyes, see You also as drunk.” Here case endings are to be altered to get coherence. For a person having drunk honey or distilled liquor, affected by red eyes and faulty eyesight, the Lord appears as drunk just as for a person with defective senses, a pole looks like a person. The usage as “kṣībā” is to be understood as either due to the fear of breaking the meter of the verse or as scriptural. Scriptures say, “His form is not revealed before defective senses.” Now, in the pretext of telling the reason, mentions a mixed praise as “Na nāga” indicates the wives could not worship as their senses were overwhelmed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The wives of the serpents realized that He, being omniscient, knew their internal tumult and thus, how could they continue to worship Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Kṣībā is from 'kṣībṛ* = made, the verbal root in the yavādi group with the uṇādi suffix “kan” and is in nominative singular. “As one gets red-eyed and loses discrimination on consuming liquor and distilled wine, You are not like that. Rather You are full of eternal bliss and discrimination.” This is the intended meaning denoted by the word “iva” and “surā,” etc. Pulastya states: “there are eleven kinds of liquor including that made from bread-fruit, grapes, honey, dates, palmyra, sugarcane, sweet spirits, maireya (from mirā) and coconut. But, surā (wine) is the twelfth liquor which is the worst of all. *Surā* is the “mala” (filth) of food and sin is also “mala.” Surā is to be known as of three types, viz. from jaggery, honey and flour.” Their characteristics are omitted for fear of getting voluminous. A general definition of liquor is, “that liquid substance which having been mechanically extracted causes intoxication.” This definition carefully avoids juice, hemp, plants such as Anethum \[dill\] Sowa, Arka from being categorized as liquor. Otherwise by over-generalization of the definition even water can also be called liquor. So, all aspects of the definition are needed. Because of tempting the serpent maidens the appearance appeared like one drunk. *Could not etc.* = omniscient. He knows our inner tumult and how we can serve/worship Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

How can one who is inert (dark) be the Lord worthy of worship? The reply is a quality accepted for a certain purpose by one’s own volition, does not contradict Lordship. Thus detachment in sensual joys is a symptom of the Lord whereas attachment to sensual pleasures symptomizes the *jīvas*.

That the Lord is worthy of worship confirmed appropriate by the term “na” for his vision, mind and senses are never affected in the least by the qualities of material nature. He is unlike us who are overwhelmed by anger and lust. So, which person, wishing to conquer over his senses, mind and vital airs would not serve that Lord? Why does He oversee? For controlling. *īṭ, īśana* = controlling.

### Text 21

*यमाहुरस्य स्थितिजन्मसंयमं*  
*त्रिभिर्विहीनं यमनन्तमृषयः ।*  
*न वेद सिद्धार्थमिव क्वचित्स्थितं*  
*भूमण्डलं मूर्धसहस्रधामसु ॥२१॥*

*yam āhur asya sthiti-janma-saṁyamaṁ*  
*tribhir vihīnaṁ yam anantam ṝṣayaḥ*  
*na veda siddhārtham iva kvacit sthitaṁ*  
*bhū-maṇḍalaṁ mūrdha-sahasra-dhāmasu*

**Пословный перевод:**

yam—whom; āhuḥ—they said; asya—of the material world; sthiti—the maintenance; janma—creation; saṁyamam—annihilation; tribhiḥ—these three; vihīnam—without; yam—which; anantam—unlimited; *ṝ*ṣayaḥ—all the great sages; na—not; veda—feels; siddha-artham—a mustard seed; iva—like; kvacit—where; sthitam—situated; bhū-maṇḍalam—the universe; mūrdha-sahasra-dhāmasu—on the hundreds and thousands of hoods of the Lord.

**Перевод:**

**Lord Śiva continued: All the great sages accept the Lord as the source of creation, maintenance and destruction, although He actually has nothing to do with these activities. Therefore the Lord is called unlimited. Although the Lord in His incarnation as Śeṣa holds all the universes on His hoods, each universe feels no heavier than a mustard seed to Him. Therefore, what person desiring perfection will not worship the Lord?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Who is the cause of stability, origin and regulation of this world? Who is not touched by the three qualities of material nature? Who is infinite? Ananta—Heis without end for His transcendental form and attributes are not limited in space and time. He is infiniteness personified. He does not consider the weight of a universe situated upon one of His thousands of hoods any more than the weight of one mustard seed. *Sages* = hymns. For metrical purposes when the reading has elongation (of vowel “ṝ”), then vowel “ṛ” denotes the mother of the demigods, Lakṣmī; so she and the sages are indicated. Salutation to Him. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*By that only* = due to being the cause of everything. Although, the terrestrial globe of 34 *lakh* (340,000) less than 50 *crore yojanas* \[500 million billion *yojanas*\] is resting atop one of His heads it appears as a mustard seed to Him. This fact is not illusory and it is another wonder which is part of His infiniteness. \[This paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Yamāhuḥ* may also refer to the states of wakefulness. In all three times, infinite greatness is understood by the word “anantam.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Saṅkarṣaṇa is located in the lower world (nether region). “Asad” = actually the drunkenness is not due to wine or liquor. The Lord did not appear in a terrifying way to the wives of the serpents, rather He appeared in an attentive, teasing, blush-causing way. *Na nāgavadhvaḥ* indicates their swooning out of love and devotion.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By the word “asya” the Lord is known as the supersoul of all and cause of everything.

### Text 22-23

*यस्याद्य आसीद् गुणविग्रहो महान्*  
*विज्ञानधिष्ण्यो भगवानजः किल ।*  
*यत्सम्भवोऽहं त्रिवृता स्वतेजसा*  
*वैकारिकं तामसमैन्द्रियं सृजे ॥२२॥*  
*एते वयं यस्य वशे महात्मनः*  
*स्थिताः शकुन्ता इव सूत्रयन्त्रिताः ।*  
*महानहं वैकृततामसेन्द्रियाः*  
*सृजाम सर्वे यदनुग्रहादिदम् ॥२३॥*

*yasyādya āsīd guṇa-vigraho mahān*  
*vijñāna-dhiṣṇyo bhagavān ajaḥ kila*  
*yat-sambhavo 'haṁ tri-vṛtā sva-tejasā*  
*vaikārikaṁ tāmasam aindriyaṁ sṛje*  
*ete vayaṁ yasya vaśe mahātmanaḥ*  
*sthitāḥ śakuntā iva sūtra-yantritāḥ*  
*mahān ahaṁ vaikṛta-tāmasendriyāḥ*  
*sṛjāma sarve yad-anugrahād idam*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—from whom; ādyaḥ—the beginning; āsīt—there was; guṇa-vigrahaḥ—the incarnation of the material qualities; mahān—the total material energy; vijñāna—of full knowledge; dhiṣṇyaḥ—the reservoir; bhagavān—the most powerful; ajaḥ—Lord Brahmā; kila—certainly; yat—from whom; sambhavaḥ—born; aham—I; tri-vṛtā—having three varieties according to the three modes of nature; sva-tejasā—by my material strength; vaikārikam—all the demigods; tāmasam—material elements; aindriyam—the senses; sṛje—I create; ete—all of these; vayam—we; yasya—of whom; vaśe—under the control; mahā-ātmanaḥ—great personalities; sthitāḥ—situated; śakuntāḥ—vultures; iva—like; sūtra-yantritāḥ—bound by rope; mahān—the mahat-tattva; aham—I; vaikṛta—the demigods; tāmasa—the five material elements; indriyāḥ—senses; sṛjāmaḥ—we create; sarve—all of us; yat—of whom; anugrahāt—by the mercy; idam—this material world.

**Перевод:**

**From that Supreme Personality of Godhead appears Lord Brahmā, whose body is made from the total material energy, the reservoir of intelligence predominated by the passionate mode of material nature. From Lord Brahmā, I myself am born as a representation of false ego known as Rudra. By my own power I create all the other demigods, the five elements and the senses. Therefore, I worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is greater than any of us and under whose control are situated all the demigods, material elements and senses, and even Lord Brahmā and I myself, like birds bound by a rope. Only by the Lord's grace can we create, maintain and annihilate the material world. Therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Being.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The cause of creation is explained through the word “mahat.” Whose form became “mahān,” due to quality. The abode of intellect, *sattva*, became Lord “Aja” (Brahmā). \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Jīva Gosvāmi\]

From Brahmā I am born as Rudra. “By the three qualities, through my own power, egotism, I create the demigods (vaikārika), elements (tāmasa) and sense-organs (aindriya). We create this cosmic egg by whose grace? How? Under His control, bound like a bird tied to a rope. Who are we? Mahān, ahaṅkāra and the vaikārika, as before mentioned. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*I create* = I attain the state of utility for creation. As “the fire itself cooks the rice,” it is with me as the agent. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Jīva Gosvāmi\]

*Tells another* = I am also; *great soul* = Lord of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The order of creation aforesaid is told in 'yasya' etc.: From you has come Aja (Brahmā), the first among created things. Among created things in nature, the entity mahat is the first, and Brahmā being its presiding deity, his being first is proper. His body is constructed with the quality of *rajas*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

The word “vijñāna” indicates that although he has a body, he does not have loss of knowledge like other embodied souls. *Seat of knowledge =* repository; *dhiṣṇya* = one whose form is essentially comprised of knowledge.

Our creation is also not independent but due to the grace of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is indicated by the word *yataḥ*. These = us = mahān, Brahmā, etc. Birds tied with ropes are Vaikṛtas, i.e, deities of Vaikārika, Tāmasas, (deities of the five elements), Aindriyas, (presiding deities of the senses and their objects such as sound, etc.). \[This paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In the three verses starting with “yasya,” praise continues for the principal cause of the world revealing that Brahmā, and others are generated by the Lord and under His control. This is indicated by the reverential salute from “His māyā.” The genitive case-ending in “yasya” is in the ablative sense.

“Is being known well by this” denotes the verbal testimony, i.e, the scriptures \[Brahman in the sound form\]. He is the asylum of that.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The word “yam” establishes the Lord as the cause of creation, etc.

How is Saṅkarṣaṇa said to be the cause of birth, nature etc.? Although, there is difference for the sake of effects, actually Vāsudeva and Brahmā are identical as presiding deities. This is explained in the two verses starting with “yasya” that the Lord is the cause of the creation of the world through “mahat.” The first body called “mahān” was due to the sattva quality permeated by knowledge as a substrate of consciousness.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Apādāna*, the point of separation, has a genitive case in “yasya.” From whom? *Mahān*, presiding deity of mahat entity, locus of knowledge required for building the world etc., His body is chiefly made of the quality “rajas.” He is the first born, even earlier than Rudra. Thus Lord Aja, (Brahmā) who has powers like the Lord in the matter of creation of the world emerged.

### Text 24

*यन्निर्मितां कर्ह्यपि कर्मपर्वणीं*  
*मायां जनोऽयं गुणसर्गमोहितः ।*  
*न वेद निस्तारणयोगमञ्जसा*  
*तस्मै नमस्ते विलयोदयात्मने ॥२४॥*

*yan-nirmitāṁ karhy api karma-parvaṇīṁ*  
*māyāṁ jano 'yaṁ guṇa-sarga-mohitaḥ*  
*na veda nistāraṇa-yogam añjasā*  
*tasmai namas te vilayodayātmane*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—by whom; nirmitām—created; karhi api—at any time; karma-parvaṇīm—which ties the knots of fruitive activity; māyām—the illusory energy; janaḥ—a person; ayam—this; guṇa-sarga-mohitaḥ—bewildered by the three modes of material nature; na—not; veda—knows; nistāraṇa-yogam—the process of getting out of material entanglement; añjasā—soon; tasmai—unto Him (the Supreme); namaḥ—respectful obeisances; te—unto You; vilaya-udaya-ātmane—in whom everything is annihilated and from whom everything is again manifested.

**Перевод:**

**The illusory energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead binds all of us conditioned souls to this material world. Therefore, without being favored by Him, persons like us cannot understand how to get out of that illusory energy. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Lord, who is the cause of creation and annihilation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Praise for the cause of maintenance and dissolution. People verily know only *māyā* (illusion) created by Him and not the means to cross over *māyā*. The cause of dissolution is said to be “vilaya” denoting the receptacle and “udaya,” the origin. Salutations to both of His features. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The illusion created by You is not known by people, so where is the question of knowing You? *Those shrouded by illusion are in the world and those who reached its end cross beyond worldly life* characterizes Him as the cause of maintenance. The means of crossing over the material ocean is meditation of Him with devotion. The Supreme Soul dissolves the illusion His devotees. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Cakravartī \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\] has taken *tadvilaya* (its dissolution) as the reading, while it appears that revered Svāmi \[Śrīdhara Svāmi\] has taken *namaste* as the reading.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*māyā* (material nature), along with its rules and regulations bewilder people and disallow them from ever knowing the means to get free from *māyā*. This is because, confusion caused by the objects of material sound, touch, smell and so on result in contrary knowledge. This suggests that knowledge of the creator, and specifically His essential form is the easy, accessible means to liberation for all. That this alone is the means to please the Lord is concluded by the word “tasmai.” Surrendering to the transcendental form of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is the remover of illusion.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The words *ete vayam* indicate that *we*, beginning with *mahat* \[the material energy\], create this world only by the grace of the actual controller.

But, even so, could somebody, somehow, get released from bondage like a bird and become free? Mentioning that without His grace, none is capable of releasing one's self, is indicated by the address “yad”.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He is praised as the cause of bondage is addressed as “yannirmitām.” The embodied soul, bewildered by the material nature (*māyā*) does not know the means of crossing over that *māyā* as per the scriptural text, “people see only His (delightful) garden, but none sees Him.” Salutations to You, the cause of the creation, maintenance and destruction of the world.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Seventeenth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The Descent of the River Ganges.”

## Chapter 18 - The Prayers Offered to the Lord by the Residents of Jambūdvīpa

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*तथा च भद्रश्रवा नाम धर्मसुतस्तत्कुलपतयः पुरुषा भद्राश्ववर्षे*  
*साक्षाद्भगवतो वासुदेवस्य प्रियांतनुं धर्ममयीं हयशीर्षाभिधानां परमेण*  
*समाधिना सन्निधाप्येदमभिगृणन्त उपधावन्ति ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*tathā ca bhadraśravā nāma dharma-sutas tat-kula-patayaḥ puruṣā bhadrāśva-varṣe sākṣād bhagavato vāsudevasya priyāṁ tanuṁ dharmamayīṁ hayaśīrṣābhidhānāṁ parameṇa samādhinā sannidhāpyedam abhigṛṇanta upadhāvanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—*Śukadeva Gosvāmī said*; tathā ca—*similarly (just as Lord Śiva worships Saṅkarṣaṇa in Ilāvṛta-varṣa); *bhadra-śravā—*Bhadraśravā; *nāma—*known as; *dharma-sutaḥ—*the son of Dharmarāja; *tat—*of him; *kula-patayaḥ—*the chiefs of the dynasty; *puruṣāḥ—*all the residents; *bhadrāśva-varṣe—*in the land known as Bhadrāśva-varṣa; *sākṣāt—*directly; *bhagavataḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *vāsudevasya—*of Lord Vāsudeva; *priyām tanum—*very dear form; *dharma-mayīm—*the director of all religious principles; *hayaśīrṣa-abhidhānām—*the Lord's incarnation named Hayaśīrṣa (also called Hayagrīva); *parameṇa samādhinā—*with the highest form of trance; *sannidhāpya—*coming near; *idam—*this; *abhigṛṇantaḥ—*chanting; *upadhāvanti—*they worship.

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Bhadraśravā, the son of Dharmarāja, rules the tract of land known as Bhadrāśva-varṣa. Just as Lord Śiva worships Saṅkarṣaṇa in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, Bhadraśravā, accompanied by his intimate servants and all the residents of the land, worships the plenary expansion of Vāsudeva known as Hayaśīrṣa. Lord Hayaśīrṣa is very dear to the devotees and He is the director of all religious principles. Fixed in the topmost trance, Bhadraśravā and his associates offer their respectful obeisances to the Lord and chant the following prayers with careful pronunciation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Bhadraśravā is the ruler of the *varṣa*. Kulapatayaḥ means the best among his servants.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having narrated the upāsanā and the upāsakas in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the same is described in regards to Bhadrāśva and other *varṣas* in this and the next chapter.

Bhadraśravā is the son of Dharma and the ruler of Bhadrāśva-varṣa. The plural denotes his servants and other upāsakas there, to the east of Meru. The word “sākṣāt” implies that the word “Bhagavān” and “Brahma” should not be taken in the secondary sense. The word “priyā” means dear. It does not mean that Hayaśīrṣa is dearer to Vāsudeva than Rāma and Kṛṣṇa. Dharmamayī means abounding in Vedas which teach *dharma*. This sort of Dharmamaya nature is there in Rāma, Kṛṣṇa and others also. But the special thing about Hayagrīva is that in this form only he brought back the frightened Vedas and taught them. When devotees place Lord Hayagrīva in their hearts, chant *mantras* and offer this prayer, they attain the stage of samādhi. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The worship in the remaining *varṣas* is described in the next chapter. To start with, the Hayagrīvopasana in Bhadrāśva-varṣa is stated. The chiefs of his family also do the same worship. Dharmamayī means which is responsible for the sustenance of the world by teaching the real philosophy. “*Haya*” is derived from the root “*haya*” which means “to know.” So *haya* means those who know everything. They are Brahmā, Vāyu and others. *Śīrṣa* means important, superior. Hayaśīrṣa means superior to Brahmā, Vāyu and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhadraśravā is the ruler of the *varṣa*. *Kulapathayaḥ* means the leaders among his progeny.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tataḥ* = after the description of Ilāvṛta-varṣa, very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa as this form is responsible for the manifestation of the Vedas. Haya is derived from the root “haya” = to know. *Haya* means people who know all. *Śīrṣa* = the foremost among them. So Hayaśīrṣa means the best among the omniscient. *Sannidhāpya* = visualizing. The following *mantra* is chanted.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In this chapter the forms of God present in Bhadrāśva and other six *varṣas*, as also the worshippers are described. *Bhadraśravāsah* = Bhadraśrava's sons and servants. They chant this *mantra* in the presence of this form.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**
