In the previous chapter it was said that tamasa Rudra performs the worship of tāmasa Saṅkarṣaṇa. That the worshipper and worshipped should be of the same nature is stated in the 1stskandha \[first canto of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam\]. Otherwise worship and blessings will not be possible. The particular attributes of the different forms of Gods are to be known from the *mantra* and the stotra (prayer). The two types of defects, latent and manifest are to be overcome through chanting the *mantra* and prayer respectively. Because God has taken a form appearing as though made of material quality on His own record, He is not affected by the modes of material nature and there is no defect in him.

In Bhadrāśva there is Hayagrīva. His form has predominant tamas mixed with rajas. The people who live there are also of the same constitution, hence they worship Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Having stated the particulars of God’s seva \[service\] in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the same is stated for Bhadrāśva and other *varṣas* in these two chapters. Dharmasuta means the son of Dharma Prajāpati and the son’s name is Bhadraśrava.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Having described the worshipped form of God and the worshippers in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the same is narrated in other *varṣas* starting from the east. Just as in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the worshipped form and the worshippers are here also, in Bhadrāśva-varṣa. The chieftains of Bhadraśrava’s also join him in the worship of the form dear to Lakṣmī and others. *Dharmamayī* means the promulgator of Dharma.

### Text 2

*भद्रश्रवस ऊचुः*  
*ॐ नमो भगवते धर्मायात्मविशोधनाय नम इति ॥२॥*

*bhadraśravasa ūcuḥ*  
*oṁ namo bhagavate dharmāyātma-viśodhanāya nama iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhadraśravasaḥ ūcuḥ—*the ruler Bhadraśravā and his intimate associates said; *om—*O Lord; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *dharmāya—*the source of all religious principles; *ātma-viśodhanāya—*who purifies us of material contamination; *namaḥ—*our obeisances; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**The ruler Bhadraśravā and his intimate associates utter the following prayer: We offer our respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the reservoir of all religious principles, who cleanses the heart of the conditioned soul in this material world. Again and again we offer our respectful obeisances unto Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The plural number in Bhadraśravāsaḥ is due to the plurality in the sentences spoken, i.e. like a transferred epithet.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Oṁkāra and the word Bhagavān have been explained earlier. *Dharmaya* means this: the Vedas are divided into two parts, the first and second. The pūrva bhāga (first part) is intended to describe the nature of the worshipped. But actually God is the purport of even the first part. Because it is said “those who know the Vedas say Kṛṣṇa himself is *dharma*.” *Dharma* is what is elaborated in the first part. That Kṛṣṇa only is the purport of the latter part is obvious. So Dharmaya means to Him, who is the purport of both parts of the Vedas. There is the word *ātma-viśodhanāya*. Ātma means either the mind (antaḥkaraṇa) or *jīva* \[the soul\]. He cleanses both. He causes the mind to shed the rajas and tamas aspects and makes him attain mokṣa \[liberation\] through absorption in His worship. “Dharmaya” implies that He is the means of attainment. The word “*ātma-viśodhanā*” expresses His attainability. The word “bhagavān” justifies both. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Dharmaya* = to Him who is of the nature of *dharma* such as creation and so on. It is said “God is *dharma* as He bears/sustains everything.” *Dharma* is derived from the root *dhṛ* which means “to bear.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhadraśravā means the group containing Bhadraśrava.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The word Bhadraśravas signifies the group of people living there, thus the plural is justified. *Tadyogad* means “because of the word Bhadraśravas.” *Guni* = people related to Bhadraśravas.

To purify the *jīvas* by removing impurity caused by ignorance.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The sons and servants of Bhadraśravās are also called by the same name, as they belong to him, and have identical qualities. So the plural number is justified.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The *mantra* is stated. “*Ātma-viśodhanā*” means he removes the desires and other defects of the mind. The word *namaḥ* is repeated as a gesture of affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The plural in “Bhadraśravāsaḥ” is to be understood as shown in the Pūrva-mīmāṁsā śāstra. The principle is, “unimportant ones associated with an important one are also denoted as important ones.” So Bhadraśravā is the important person. His servants and other chieftains are important but they are associated with Bhadraśravā in the worship. So they are also called Bhadraśravās and hence the plural number.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Dharmaya means, “You are of the nature of attributes like the creativity of the universe and so on. Or it may also be taken to mean the supporter, being derived form the root *dhṛ* = to support. Ātmā is *jīva*. He purifies the *jīva* by giving him knowledge. That is why he is called ātmaśodhana. Obeisances to Him.

### Text 3

*अहो विचित्रं भगवद्विचेष्टितं*  
*घ्नन्तं जनोऽयं हि मिषन्न पश्यति ।*  
*ध्यायन्नसद्यर्हि विकर्म सेवितुं*  
*निर्हृत्य पुत्रं पितरं जिजीविषति ॥३॥*

*aho vicitraṁ bhagavad-viceṣṭitaṁ*  
*ghnantaṁ jano 'yaṁ hi miṣan na paśyati*  
*dhyāyann asad yarhi vikarma sevituṁ*  
*nirhṛtya putraṁ pitaraṁ jijīviṣati*

**Пословный перевод:**

*aho—*alas; *vicitram—*wonderful; *bhagavat-viceṣṭitam—*the pastimes of the Lord; *ghnantam—*death; *janaḥ—*a person; *ayam—*this; *hi—*certainly; *miṣan—*although seeing; *na paśyati—*does not see; *dhyāyan—*thinking about; *asat—*material happiness; *yarhi—*because; *vikarma—*forbidden activities; *sevitum—*to enjoy; *nirhṛtya—*burning; *putram—*sons; *pitaram—*the father; *jijīviṣati—*desires a long life.

**Перевод:**

**Alas! How wonderful it is that the foolish materialist does not heed the great danger of impending death! He knows that death will surely come, yet he is nevertheless callous and neglectful. If his father dies, he wants to enjoy his father's property, and if his son dies, he wants to enjoy his son's possessions as well. In either case, he heedlessly tries to enjoy material happiness with the acquired money.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

People do not think about death in spite of seeing it daily. This is one of the astonishing līlās \[pastimes\] of the Lord. The reason for not thinking about death is this: they perform the funeral of both their father and son and wish to live comfortably with their money.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Bāla* = son. *Vṛddha* = father. The extremely foolish person fails to realize that death will not elude him. Even a life span of five to six years, in the service of God, is laudable. But here the case is different and there is no such intention. It is true that in the sacred Bhadrāśva and other *varṣas* a person does not see the death of both his father and son. But nevertheless, the people of Bhārata-varṣa are providing these teachings meant for places where such things are possible. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Verses in the form of praise are told. They utter those verses wondering at Bhagavānmaya which is very difficult to overcome. Seeing death killing his father, he does not think about his own death. He performs the funeral of his father and son and tries to live on their money, doing bad deeds, having a craze for enjoyment. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Just as a person performs the funeral of his father, but yet does not think about his own death, even so others see death around them but yet do not contemplate about their own deaths. This is an astonishing power of God.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He does not see death. He performs the funeral of his father and son and desires to live on their money and enjoy creature comforts. He contemplates on various activities to achieve this. This is astonishing.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The person performs the funeral of his father and son and desires to live not for worshipping God, but to enjoy life. The enjoyments lead only to hell and so it is not proper to have such desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Although one sees death taking away his father and son and he performs the funeral for them still he tries to live comfortably on their wealth. He still has interest in bad acts to derive pleasure. This is what is astonishing.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

If there is impurity in the *jīvas*, then the purification holds good, but how are they impure? The reply is, they are impure by God’s will only. This is what is stated here. A person does not think about his own death even though he infers it will come. Why? Because he is contemplating in his mind the objects of the senses which give him pleasure and thus he enjoys them in such a way that he earns sinful reactions. So he does not see his death. The knowledge that he gains becomes obscured by the sin earned in enjoying the forbidden things. This is the idea. So the ways of the Lord are wonderful and astonishing. What was said that he does not see for himself the death which kills all, is demonstrated by an example.

### Text 4

*वदन्ति विश्वं कवयः स्म नश्वरं*  
*पश्यन्ति चाध्यात्मविदो विपश्चितः ।*  
*तथापि मुह्यन्ति तवाज मायया*  
*सुविस्मितं कृत्यमजं नतोऽस्मि तम् ॥४॥*

*vadanti viśvaṁ kavayaḥ sma naśvaraṁ*  
*paśyanti cādhyātmavido vipaścitaḥ*  
*tathāpi muhyanti tavāja māyayā*  
*suvismitaṁ kṛtyam ajaṁ nato 'smi tam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*vadanti—*they say authoritatively; *viśvam—*the entire material creation; *kavayaḥ—*great learned sages; *sma—*certainly; *naśvaram—*perishable; *paśyanti—*they see in trance; *ca—*also; *adhyātma-vidaḥ—*who have realized spiritual knowledge; *vipaścitaḥ—*very learned scholars; *tathā api—*still; *muhyanti—*become illusioned; *tava—*your; *aja—*O unborn one; *māyayā—*by the illusory energy; *su-vismitam—*most wonderful; *kṛtyam—*activity; *ajam—*unto the supreme unborn one; *nataḥ asmi—*I offer my obeisances; *tam—*unto Him.

**Перевод:**

**O unborn one, learned Vedic scholars who are advanced in spiritual knowledge certainly know that this material world is perishable, as do other logicians and philosophers. In trance they realize the factual position of this world, and they preach the truth as well. Yet even they are sometimes bewildered by Your illusory energy. This is Your own wonderful pastime. Therefore, I can understand that Your illusory energy is very wonderful, and I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

An ignorant person does not think about death. What is astonishing about it? A scholar says that life is transient. The enlightened see in their meditation that life is transient, yet they are also subject to illusion. So Your ways are astonishing. So I would like to leave the study of śāstras aside and take refuge in Your feet.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It is not that only ordinary and ignorant people behave like this. Even those who have studied Vedanta and have performed a certain amount of worship also fall into this confusion. It is so because they pine at the loss of their children and so on. So to overcome this *māyā* of Yours we take refuge in You. That is the only solution. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Even for the learned the greatness of Hari will be confusing without His grace. The learned know from the scriptures, they see it in their meditation, yet without Your grace they are subject to confusion regarding the correct philosophy. It is most astonishing. They do not know their duty. Only You are the person who knows everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is not that only the ignorant do not see impending death, even the learned do not see it. It is very astonishing. “So I discard everything and offer my obeisances to You. Those who worship You are the only learned.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

An objection is raised. It means only those who worship You are learned.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Even the learned, who know adhyātma, who know the past and other things and say that the world is transient; still they become absorbed in it. They do not try to have love for You, who is full of eternal bliss. This is most astonishing.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

It is not that only the ignorant do not see their death. Even those who know the *Upaniṣads* and the scriptures are also subjected to illusion. They say that life is short-lived but still they become interested in it. Because *māyā* is Yours it is so very strong and causes illusion. It is strong because it is the power of You, who are bereft of births and deaths. Those who take refuge in You cross this *māyā* even though they are not equipped with other purifying practices (sadhanas). Those who do not take refuge in Your lotus feet will not cross *māyā* even though they perform many purifying practices.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

What is astonishing here? An ignorant person naturally does not see his death. No. A scholar teaches others saying that the world is transient. He sees this in his meditation (samādhi) also. Yet still he also falters under the influence of *māyā*. This is astonishing. So I offer my obeisances to You, who are naturally the opponent of births and deaths.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

It is not that only the ignorant who have this illusion. Even the learned are subject to illusion by God’s will. They see their death while they meditate. Still they are subject to illusion by Your will. Dear Aja, this act of Yours is extremely astonishing. We offer our obeisances to You to get rid of this illusion.

### Text 5

*विश्वोद्भवस्थाननिरोधकर्म ते*  
*ह्यकर्तुरङ्गीकृतमप्यपावृतः ।*  
*युक्तं न चित्रं त्वयि कार्यकारणे*  
*सर्वात्मनि व्यतिरिक्ते च वस्तुतः ॥५॥*

*viśvodbhava-sthāna-nirodha-karma te*  
*hy akartur aṅgīkṛtam apy apāvṛtaḥ*  
*yuktaṁ na citraṁ tvayi kārya-kāraṇe*  
*sarvātmani vyatirikte ca vastutaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*viśva—*of the whole universe; *udbhava—*of the creation; *sthāna—*of the maintenance; *nirodha—*of the annihilation; *karma—*these activities; *te—*of You (O dear Lord); *hi—*indeed; *akartuḥ—*aloof; *aṅgīkṛtam—*still accepted by the Vedic literature; *api—*although; *apāvṛtaḥ—*untouched by all these activities; *yuktam—*befitting; *na—*not; *citram—*wonderful; *tvayi—*in You; *kārya-kāraṇe—*the original cause of all effects; *sarva-ātmani—*in all respects; *vyatirikte—*set apart; *ca—*also; *vastutaḥ—*the original substance.

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, although You are completely detached from the creation, maintenance and annihilation of this material world and are not directly affected by these activities, they are all attributed to You. We do not wonder at this, for Your inconceivable energies perfectly qualify You to be the cause of all causes. You are the active principle in everything, although You are separate from everything. Thus we can realize that everything is happening because of Your inconceivable energy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“This is another thing which is not astonishing in You, though it could be astonishing elsewhere. The Vedas ascribe to You the creation of the world, although You are a non-doer, because Your creation is justified by *māyā* because You create the effects in the causes. But in reality, Your absolute form is neither entrapped by *māyā*, nor do You exhibit creative power.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Another astonishing thing about You is that although You are akartā (non-doer), You create the world. This is what they think: “Although He creates everything, the diversity to be found in all *jīvas* \[living entities\] is due to their own *karma*. He does not do it. So he is akartā.” You have accepted the creation, sustenance and destruction of the world. It is proper, for it is not binding to You as it is for the living entities. You are not bound because Your knowledge does not diminish by either good or bad deeds. So far as the *jīvas* are concerned, they are covered with ignorance, thus their knowledge is shrouded. They perform many deeds in ignorance and the earlier one leads to the later. So they are bound by their *karma*s. If there was ignorance in You it would have led to partiality and mercilessness as is found in the living entities. But this is not the case. Actions do not stain You because You are the cause and effect.

The causality is not like that of clay and the clay pot but rather it is like the relation of the body and soul. The soul is not affected by the defects of the body and so also You remain unaffected. Mere actions do not bind, for, if that were the case then the liberated soul also should be bound because of deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is most astonishing elsewhere is not astonishing in Hari. For example, the Vedas have ascribed to you the creation, sustenance and destruction of this world though you are an akartā (non-doer). The Vedas say He is niṣkriya, literally devoid of action. Then, how can He create? The reply is: it is proper. You are called niṣkriya because you do everything effortlessly.

His akartṛtva (non-doing) is explained by the scriptures themselves as the absence of tiresome action. How can a single person do various wonderful things invisibly? The reply is: it is not astonishing for the Lord (Hari). It is astonishing for those whose knowledge is weak. It is not astonishing in case of Hari, who has infinite wonderful, inconceivable powers as is stated in the Vedas. *Kārya-kāraṇa* means it is He who is the cause of every effect. *Sarva-ātma* means the inner controller of all. *Vyatirikita* means different from all. *Vasta* means eternal and unharmed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“If even the learned are confused, then the fault lies with Me (God).” If this be the suspicion lurking in one’s mind, it is cleared here. “Even though *māyā* is Yours, You are different from it. You are not the agent because the *guṇas* \[modes of nature\] are the agents. It has been accepted in the Vedas. You do not have the sense of agency (*kartṛtva*) because You are not conditioned by the material modes of nature, unlike the living entities. This is only proper for You and is not astonishing. *Māyā* is Your power. Everything springs from *māyā*, but You are different from that. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Having stated the defects of the living entities which are due to their beginningless inclination towards the objects of senses and aversion to God. The virtues of God are stated here. “You create the world without depending on anything else. This is a virtue. There is no creator for You.” By this, His eternity and uniqueness are described. “You create the world just by Your desire.” By this the truthfulness and infallibility of His resolve is described. “You are not covered by any material qualities.” By this, His infiniteness is described. “That You create the world for the sake of the living entities and for their liberation is accepted by the Vedas.” This describes His kindness. “This is only proper in You, but not astonishing.” This indicates that these qualities are not to be found elsewhere and form a small part of His qualities. “You are the antaryāmī \[supersoul\]of all, but different from them.” This indicates that he is free from all defects.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Now God is praised as endowed with contradictory attributes. “The creativity which lies in You, is accepted by the Vedas although You are a non-doer. You are not the doer because You are not in association with *māyā*.” Then how is action possible? The reply is: “Although You are different from everything, You are also non-different because You are the cause of all effects. The relationship between cause and effect is one of identity. Both these aspects are possible because of the unthinkable wonderful powers You have.” The word *“kārya-kāraṇe”* denotes He is the efficient cause. The word *“sarva-ātmani”* denotes that He is the material cause also.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Why do you say that controlling the illusory *māyā* is astonishing? My creation*—*the creation of a non-doer is also astonishing.” For this query the devotees reply: “The Vedas have accepted Your creativity, so it is not astonishing. You are the creator of even the cause. Thus, Your creativity must be accepted even though You are a non-doer, bereft of all attachment. Because You create only through *prakṛti* \[nature\] and puruṣa \[living entities\], You are said to be a non-doer (akartā). Because You are the cause of both *prakṛti* and puruṣa (or a motivator of both), Your creativity also must be accepted. Therefore, it is not astonishing in You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In the earlier verse it was said He is *dharma*, the creator of the world. But the Vedas say that He is niṣkriya, devoid of action. Then how can He create the world? This objection is answered in this verse. The acts of creation, sustenance and destruction of the world and the agency of God regarding these are true. It is justified that Hari is the agent of these acts in spite of His being proclaimed niṣkriya in the Vedas as established by trustworthy people. The Vedas say that He is niṣkriya not because of the absence of any action, but because of the effortlessness with which he performs actions. All actions are seen to be tiresome in our experience. God’s actions are not like that. He does not tire. So he is said to be niṣkriya, devoid of tiresome action. The creation of this universe by a single person is also not astonishing in His case. Because He is “*kārya-kāraṇa”* = He has all the powers of causality of all causes. He is *“sarva-ātma”*. That means even the existence of the prime cause *prakṛti* \[material nature\] depends on Him. He is also “*vyatrikta”*, different from any person whom we see in this world. For a person like You, singularly creating the wonderful universe is not at all astonishing.

### Text 6

*वेदान् युगान्ते तमसा तिरस्कृतान्*  
*रसातलाद्यो नृतुरङ्गविग्रहः ।*  
*प्रत्याददे वै कवयेऽभियाचते*  
*तस्मै नमस्तेऽवितथेहिताय इति ॥६॥*

*vedān yugānte tamasā tiraskṛtān*  
*rasātalād yo nṛ-turaṅga-vigrahaḥ*  
*pratyādade vai kavaye 'bhiyācate*  
*tasmai namas te 'vitathehitāya iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*vedān—*the four Vedas; *yuga-ante—*at the end of the millennium; *tamasā—*by the demon of ignorance personified; *tiraskṛtān—*stolen away; *rasātalāt—*from the lowest planetary system (Rasātala); *yaḥ—*who (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); *nṛ-turaṅga-vigrahaḥ—*assuming the form of half-horse, half-man; *pratyādade—*returned; *vai—*indeed; *kavaye—*to the supreme poet (Lord Brahmā); *abhiyā-cate—*when he asked for them; *tasmai—*unto Him (the form of Hayagrīva); *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *te—*to You; *avitatha-īhitāya—*whose resolution never fails; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**At the end of the millennium, ignorance personified assumed the form of a demon, stole all the Vedas and took them down to the planet of Rasātala. The Supreme Lord, however, in His form of Hayagrīva retrieved the Vedas and returned them to Lord Brahmā when he begged for them. I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, whose determination never fails.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Having praised the Supreme God, the story of the present incarnation is now narrated. You have the form of both a human being and a horse. *Kavaye* means “to Brahmā.” The Vedas had been stolen away by a demon called Tamas. *Avitathehitā* means “whose wishes are never unfulfilled.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having praised Him, endowed with many wonderful powers, they now narrate the purpose for the present incarnation. “When the Vedas were stolen by a demon Tamas during the pralaya \[devastation which takes place after each day of Brahmā\] You took the form of a man-horse and retrieved the Vedas, returning them to Brahmā. Obeisances to You.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Yugante* means at the end of *pralaya*, in the first creation. *Tamasa* means the demon Madhu who is of *tamas* nature. “Obeisances to You having taken the Hayagrīva form, for having brought back the Vedas stolen by Madhu and handed them over to Brahmā.” *Avitathehitā* means all his actions are true. This refutes the philosophy which says His actions are figments of *māyā* and so false. It is said in *Tantra Bhāgavatas*: “Persons with weak knowledge regard the creation as imaginary. How can there be a false thing in He who is always devoid of falsehood. Those who are not competent to create actual things, indulge in magic. Why should Hari, endowed with infinite splendid powers, indulge in false magic?”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The story of the present incarnation is stated here. The Vedas are stolen by Tamas, a demon. “You brought them back for the sake of Brahmā bearing a combined human-horse form. *Avitathehitā* means one of truthful resolves.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Daitya* \[demon\] refers here to Madhu by name.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

You brought the Vedas back and handed them over to Brahmā. “Obeisances to You for these truthful actions.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The story of the present incarnation is described. How is it that You could do what was not possible to do by even Brahmā? The answer is given by the word “*avitathehitāya*” which means Your resolves and actions are always truthful and thus never go away. It is not the same for Brahmā and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Bhadraśravās praises Him by narrating the story of this incarnation and offers his obeisances. *Yugante* means at the end of *pralaya*, during the first creation of the *kalpa*. “The *tamasa* demon, Madhu by name, stole the Vedas. You took a form which resembles both a human and a horse, killed the demon and took back the Vedas and returned them to Brahmā.” *Avitathehitā* means whose acts are true. This refutes the opinion that his actions are false. The same word can also be interpreted as one whose wishes always come true.

### Text 7

*हरिवर्षे चापि भगवान्नरहरिरूपेणास्ते । तद्रूपग्रहणनिमित्तमुत्तरत्राभिधास्ये*  
*। तद्दयितं रूपं महापुरुषगुणभाजनो महाभागवतो दैत्यदानवकुलतीर्थी*  
*करणशीलाचरितः प्रह्लादोऽव्यवधानानन्यभक्तियोगेन सह तद्वर्षपुरुषैरुपास्ते*  
*इदं चोदाहरति ॥७॥*

*hari-varṣe cāpi bhagavān nara-hari-rūpeṇāste; tad-rūpa-grahaṇa-nimittam uttaratrābhidhāsye; tad dayitaṁ rūpaṁ mahā-puruṣa-guṇa-bhājano mahā- bhāgavato daitya-dānava-kula-tīrthīkaraṇa-śīlā-caritaḥ prahlādo 'vyavadhānānanya-bhakti-yogena saha tad-varṣa-puruṣair upāste idaṁ codāharati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*hari-varṣe—*in the tract of land known as Harivarṣa; *ca—*also; *api—*indeed; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *nara-hari-rūpeṇa—*His form of Nṛsiṁhadeva; *āste—*is situated; *tat-rūpa-grahaṇa-nimittam—*the reason why Lord Kṛṣṇa (Keśava) assumed the form of Nṛsiṁha; *uttaratra—*in later chapters; *abhidhāsye—*I shall describe; *tat—*that; *dayitam—*most pleasing; *rūpam—*form of the Lord; *mahā-puruṣa-guṇa-bhājanaḥ—*Prahlāda Mahārāja, who is the abode of all the good qualities of great personalities; *mahā-bhāgavataḥ—*the topmost devotee; *daitya-dānava-kula-tīrthī-karaṇa-śīlā-caritaḥ—*whose activities and character were so exalted that he delivered all the Daityas (demons) born in his family; *prahlādaḥ—*Mahārāja Prahlāda; *avyavadhāna-ananya-bhakti-yogena—*by uninterrupted and unflinching devotional service; *saha—*with; *tat-varṣa-puruṣaiḥ—*the inhabitants of Hari-varṣa; *upāste—*offers obeisances to and worships; *idam—*this; *ca—*and; *udāharati—*chants.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: My dear King, Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva resides in the tract of land known as Hari-varṣa. In the Seventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, I shall describe to you how Prahlāda Mahārāja caused the Lord to assume the form of Nṛsiṁhadeva. Prahlāda Mahārāja, the topmost devotee of the Lord, is a reservoir of all the good qualities of great personalities. His character and activities have delivered all the fallen members of his demoniac family. Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is very dear to this exalted personality. Thus Prahlāda Mahārāja, along with his servants and all the denizens of Hari-varṣa, worships Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva by chanting the following mantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Described below* means in the story of Prahlāda. He is a receptacle of the virtues of noble men, whose behavior is a model for all Daityas and Dānavas. Prahlāda serves God with a devotion which is continuous and not accompanied by any desire for reward. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The details of worship in Hari-varṣa, lying south of Meru, is stated here. He is there in the form of Nṛsiṁha. The reason for taking this form will be stated later in the Seventh Canto. Prahlāda, along with the people there, offers his worship with an unswerving, uninterrupted and artless devotion. Prahlāda’s greatness is described: he is endowed with virtues similar to those of God, the Mahāpuruṣa; he is a great devotee; the clans of Daityas and Dānavas are sanctified by his behavior and actions; he chants the following *mantra*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Ananya bhakti-yoga* means a devotion which is not directed towards any one except Hari.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Uttaratra* means in the Seventh Canto. Prahlāda’s behavior and actions sanctify others. *bhakti-yoga* is direct as it is not mixed with *jñāna* or *karma*. It is *ananya* (unique), as it is not coupled with the worship of other demigods.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Narahari* = Nṛsiṁha. Prahlāda’s story will be narrated in the Seventh Skandha \[Canto\]. Valor, heroism, knowledge and devotion are virtues of noble people. The word *Prahlāda* means who is endowed with great virtues like contentment and bliss.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Mahā-puruṣa-guṇa-bhājanaḥ* = virtuous. Prahlāda’s character and actions sanctify the clans of Daityas and Dānavas. *Avyavadhāna* = constant. *Ananya* = unswerving. “He worships You with such *bhakti-yoga*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The worship in Hari-varṣa-khaṇḍa is stated here. How is it that Prahlāda had so much of devotion in spite of being born in the Daitya family? The answer is that he was endowed with the virtues of great men and birth is of no consequence. He has been practicing this devotion from various previous births. Otherwise how can there be such virtues?

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Avyavadhāna* = without the defective desire to enjoy the rewards of worship. *Ananya* = having no other desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Narahari* means *Nṛsiṁha*. *Uttonatra* means in the Seventh Canto. *Priya* means dear to his devotees. Brahmā and others are *Mahāpuruṣas—*great persons. Hari-bhakti and others are their *guṇas* \[qualities\]. One who is endowed with (bhajana), the virtue of great persons is *mahā-puruṣa-guṇa-bhājanaḥ*. Prahlāda is one such. His character and actions sanctify the families of Daityas and Dānavas. *Avyavadhāna* = not obscured by the desire for reward. *Ananya* means this devotion is not directed towards any one else except God. Prahlāda worships Nṛsiṁha along with others who live there, with such a *bhakti-yoga*.

### Text 8

*ॐ नमो भगवते नरसिंहाय नमस्तेजस्तेजसे आविराविर्भव वज्रनख*  
*वज्रदंष्ट्र कर्माशयान् रन्धय रन्धय तमो ग्रस ग्रस ॐ स्वाहा । अभयमभयमात्मनि*  
*भूयिष्ठा ॐ क्ष्रौम् ॥८॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate narasiṁhāya namas tejas-tejase āvir-āvirbhava vajra-nakha vajra-daṁṣṭra karmāśayān randhaya randhaya tamo grasa grasa oṁ svāhā; abhayam abhayam ātmani bhūyiṣṭhā oṁ kṣraum.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O Lord; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *nara-siṁhāya—*known as Lord Nṛsiṁha; *namaḥ—*obeisances; *tejaḥ-tejase—*the power of all power; *āviḥ-āvirbhava—*please be fully manifest; *vajra-nakha—*O You who possess nails like thunderbolts; *vajra-daṁṣṭra—*O You who possess teeth like thunderbolts; *karma-āśayān—*demoniac desires to be happy by material activities; *randhaya randhaya—*kindly vanquish; *tamaḥ—*ignorance in the material world; *grasa—*kindly drive away; *grasa—*kindly drive away; *om—*O my Lord; *svāhā—*respectful oblations; *abhayam—*fearlessness; *abhayam—*fearlessness; *ātmani—*in my mind; *bhūyiṣṭhāḥ—*may You appear; *om—*O Lord; *kṣraum—*the bīja, or seed, of mantras offering prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁha.

**Перевод:**

**I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, the source of all power. O my Lord who possesses nails and teeth just like thunderbolts, kindly vanquish our demonlike desires for fruitive activity in this material world. Please appear in our hearts and drive away our ignorance so that by Your mercy we may become fearless in the struggle for existence in this material world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“You are the most effulgent of all luminaries. Be manifest. Burn up our desires.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He is the most shining of all luminaries. He is not illumined by any other light. “Be manifest to us. Your nails and teeth are as sharp and strong as the diamond. Burn up our *karma-āśayāns* (material desires). Be kind to us so that we will get rid of our fears.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Tejastejase* = who is more refulgent than Sūrya and other luminaries. *Tamograsa* = dispel our ignorance. *Karmāshaya* = desires. Be kind towards us so that we will be fearless.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

You are the effulgence of the effulgence. “*Karmāshaya*” means the remnants of *karma*. If the reading is *karmāshrayan* then it means desires and other such things. *Randhaya* means burn them down. Be present in my mind so that I will have no fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Ātmani* = in my mind. The chanting of this *mantra* gives quick results in the case of deadly diseases.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Vajranakha*, *vajra-daṁṣṭra* = whose nails and canine teeth are sharp like diamonds. *Tamas* = ignorance.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The *mantra* is stated: How will I be competent to destroy the ignorance? The answer is given by the word “*tejasam tejase.”* You give the illuminating power to all the luminaries. So you are able to do that.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

(The commentary is the same of others). *Vajranakha*, *vajra-daṁṣṭra* = you have got diamond like nails and teeth for the sake of frightening the Asuras. You are to be worshipped (upāsya) by the Bījākṣaras. Always stay in our fearless minds.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Tejas tejase* = whose brightness exceeds the brightness of the sun and other shining bodies. *Aviravih* = become more and more manifest or become manifest everyday. *Karma* is sin and merit. *Asaya* is mind. “Burn them down. *Tamo grasa*. Dispel our ignorance.”

### Text 9

*स्वस्त्यस्तु विश्वस्य खलः प्रसीदतां*  
*ध्यायन्तु भूतानि शिवं मिथो धिया ।*  
*मनश्च भद्रं भजतादधोक्षजे*  
*आवेश्यतां नो मतिरप्यहैतुकी ॥९॥*

*svasty astu viśvasya khalaḥ prasīdatāṁ*  
*dhyāyantu bhūtāni śivaṁ mitho dhiyā*  
*manaś ca bhadraṁ bhajatād adhokṣaje*  
*āveśyatāṁ no matir apy ahaitukī*

**Пословный перевод:**

*svasti—*auspiciousness; *astu—*let there be; *viśvasya—*of the entire universe; *khalaḥ—*the envious (almost everyone); *prasīdatām—*let them be pacified; *dhyāyantu—*let them consider; *bhūtāni—*all the living entities; *śivam—*auspiciousness; *mithaḥ—*mutual; *dhiyā—*by their intelligence; *manaḥ—*the mind; *ca—*and; *bhadram—*calmness; *bhajatāt—*let it experience; *adhokṣaje—*in the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is beyond the perception of mind. intelligence and senses; *āveśyatām—*let it be absorbed; *naḥ—*our; *matiḥ—*intelligence; *api—*indeed; *ahaitukī—*without any motive.

**Перевод:**

**May there be good fortune throughout the universe, and may all envious persons be pacified. May all living entities become calm by practicing bhakti-yoga, for by accepting devotional service they will think of each other's welfare. Therefore let us all engage in the service of the supreme transcendence, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and always remain absorbed in thought of Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

If the welfare of the world is prayed for, the welfare of the wicked is also as good as prayed for. And that does not happen without harming the good. So it is said, “let even the wicked become propitious. Let them shed their cruelty and let all animals wish good only for others. Let their minds become tranquil. Let our minds and the minds of all other humans and creatures be devoid of desire.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Let the wicked abandon their bad thoughts and anger and become endowed with good thoughts. Let all beings think of the welfare of others only. Let our minds be free from desires for the fruit of our actions. Let our minds be fixed in Adhokṣaja. This will achieve everything. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

May Nṛsiṁha be pleased indeed. *Śiva* is Nṛsiṁha only. The scriptures say that which is devoid of grief and has only bliss is called Śiva. *Ahaitukī* means without the desire of a reward; let the mind meditate on Nṛsiṁha.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

That the Bhadraśravās perform the worship with great devotion is stated here. In their samādhi \[transcendental absorption\], they concentrate their minds on the only thing, God, and try to see Him. Nothing is astonishing because of His wonderful powers which are beyond our grasp. It is said that Prahlāda performs the worship with bhakti, which is of the nature of *vīra, karuṇa* and *śānta rasas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having chanted the *mantra*, the prayer is offered. The welfare of the world includes the welfare of the wicked also. The welfare of the wicked implies harming the good. So it is prayed: “Let the wicked also shed their cruelty. There cannot be any welfare if there is enmity between persons. So it is prayed, let all creatures think about their personal pleasures. So it is prayed, let the mind become detached from the world and attached to God. God will grant whatever Prahlāda asks for in due course of time. If everyone gets *mokṣa* \[liberation\], there is no fear of the world coming to an end. As the *jīvaśakti* and *mayaśakti* are eternal, many, many *jīvas* come to the world at the same moment. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Prahlāda chants the *mantra* and prays. The well being of wicked people results only in harming the good. “Let there not be any inauspicious thing. Let everything be auspicious. Let the mind shed its attachment to various objects. This will not happen without devotion. So let Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself be kind enough to place our minds only in Him.

God will bestow on Prahlāda whatever he has asked for, in the course of time, because there is no word like “today” or “now” in the prayer. This is what Viśvanātha \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\] says.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Let even the wicked discard their wickedness. Let all animals contemplate the welfare of others. Let our minds have artless devotion and be absorbed in You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The welfare of the wicked person cannot happen without harming the good. Then how is that welfare prayed for? True, the *jīvas* cannot bring about this welfare. But God can. It is not necessary that the welfare of one is based on the harm of another. The good never think of harming others. “Let the wicked also shed their cruelty and think about the welfare of others, then the welfare of all is achieved.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Let there be welfare for the world. *Khala* means Nṛsiṁha who is like a *khala* to the wicked. Let Him be auspicious to the world. Dear people, meditate on Nṛsiṁha who is *śiva—*blissful, knowledgeable (*manaḥ*) and auspicious (*bhadra*). For that purpose let our minds also become auspicious, let our minds become absorbed on Adhokṣaja, without desiring reward for any act done in His service.”

### Text 10

*मागारदारात्मजवित्तबन्धुषु*  
*सङ्गो यदि स्याद्भगवत्प्रियेषु नः ।*  
*यः प्राणवृत्त्या परितुष्ट आत्मवान्*  
*सिद्ध्यत्यदूरान्न तथेन्द्रियप्रियः ॥१०॥*

*māgāra-dārātmaja-vitta-bandhuṣu*  
*saṅgo yadi syād bhagavat-priyeṣu naḥ*  
*yaḥ prāṇa-vṛttyā parituṣṭa ātmavān*  
*siddhyaty adūrān na tathendriya-priyaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*mā—*not; *agāra—*house; *dāra—*wife; *ātma-ja—*children; *vitta—*bank balance; *bandhuṣu—*among friends and relatives; *saṅgaḥ—*association or attachment; *yadi—*if; *syāt—*there must be; *bhagavat-priyeṣu—*among persons to whom the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very dear; *naḥ—*of us; *yaḥ—*anyone who; *prāṇa-vṛttyā—*by the bare necessities of life; *parituṣṭaḥ—*satisfied; *ātma-vān—*who has controlled his mind and realized his self; *siddhyati—*becomes successful; *adūrāt—*very soon; *na—*not; *tathā—*so much; *indriya-priyaḥ—*a person attached to sense gratification.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, we pray that we may never feel attraction for the prison of family life, consisting of home, wife, children, friends, bank balance, relatives and so on. If we do have some attachment, let it be for devotees, whose only dear friend is Kṛṣṇa. A person who is actually self-realized and who has controlled his mind is perfectly satisfied with the bare necessities of life. He does not try to gratify his senses. Such a person quickly advances in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, whereas others, who are too attached to material things, find advancement very difficult.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Let us not be attached to anything. If there is going to be attachment, let it be for the devotees of the Lord and not for home and other things. For attachment to home and other things is dangerous.” *Indriya-priya* means a person interested in his household affairs only.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Let us have no attachment. If there is going to be attachment let it not be with the home and other things. Let it be with those who are dear to God. The association with good people will pave the way for liberation. One who is attached to one’s personal comforts does not achieve anything. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is stated here: “To achieve concentration of mind, renunciation (vairāgya) is required and for renunciation, the company of good people is the cause. Let us not be attached to wife and children. Let us be attached to good people only. The attachment to good people purifies the mind, enables one to study the śāstras, meditate, be subject to Hari’s grace and get liberated. Attachment for wife and children drags him again and again into saṁsāra which is an ocean of miseries.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

A person who is attached to his senses does not attain the accomplishment which a non attached person attains. There is the gradation there. In spite of it, if there is to be attachment for us, let it be with those who are dear to God and let it not be with those who have all sorts of attachments. *Prāṇa-vṛttyā* means contented with what little quenches one’s thirst and hunger. *Ātma-vān* means a person who is not attached.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The attachment for good people is stronger than the attachment for wicked people. So it removes the latter. If we have attachment for those who are dear to God, then attachment to the home and other things gradually vanishes. Even if there is no house, one can live on alms and continue to serve Him. Detachment is ineffective without attachment to good people for in that case non-attachment will be considered superior to the attachment, which is against the basic principle of *bhakti siddhanta*. Such thinking is even contradictory to many statements in the Bhāgavata.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“The company of good people is conducive to Adhokṣaja bhakti and the company of bad people is opposed to it. But the company of good people gradually destroys the company of bad people,” is what is stated here. If we are attached to those who are dear to God, the attachment to family and home gradually disappears. Even if one has no home, he will be satisfied through receiving alms because the mind becomes courageous by God consciousness. He will accomplish his desire very soon, whereas for a person attached to his family, it takes a very long time. Or it may be explained like this: “If there is going to be attachment with those who are dear to God, let there be no attachment to any worldly objects, for a simultaneous attachment to both is detrimental to devotion.” So detachment which generates “knowledge” will also go in vain. So detachment to other things, coupled with attachment to good people, is what should be prayed for. Attachment to good people is always superior to non-attachment to worldly objects. Otherwise the main tenet of *bhakti siddhanta* will be at stake. Such a devotee will be content with minimum food for keeping his body functioning.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Prāṇa-vṛttyā* = what is obtained without effort.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The attachment to children and wife bring us happiness. What will the attachment to those who are dear to God achieve, it cannot achieve any happiness? The reply is: “It is the contrary which is true. The attachment to great devotees brings eternal happiness and the attachment to wife and children bring never-ending misery.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

“Let us not have any attachment. If there is to be attachment let it not be with home, wife, and so on. Let it be with those who are dear to God. The devotee will be contented with minimum things to lead his life and persons attached to him become accomplished souls very soon. Attachment to wife and others intent on sense gratification pave the way for the miseries of hell. One who is dear to God will lead the way to god. So let us be attached to those who are dear to God.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

It is stated here: “It is *vairāgya* (renunciation) which is responsible for directing the mind and other senses towards Hari, and renunciation is achieved only in the company of good people. If we become attached to those who are dear to God, then the attachment for home and family will vanish.” *“Ma bhut”* should not be interpreted as “let there not be.” It should be interpreted as “there will not be.” It is not the imperative form of the verb. It is the *aorist* form. Then the mind will think of auspicious things only. For that reason, let there be attachment to those who are dear to God. This is the central idea.

To the questions of how can one live without getting attached to the home and family, the reply is given stating the defects of such an attachment. He who is contented with minimum food and comforts that enable him to live will have his mind under his control and gets to see God (apanoksha mana) very soon. But one who is intent on pleasing his senses by consuming more than required will never accomplish this.

### Text 11

*यत्सङ्गलब्धं निजवीर्यवैभवं*  
*तीर्थं मुहुः संस्पृशतां हि मानसम् ।*  
*हरत्यजोऽन्तः श्रुतिभिर्गतोऽङ्गजं*  
*को वै न सेवेत मुकुन्दविक्रमम् ॥११॥*

*yat-saṅga-labdhaṁ nija-vīrya-vaibhavaṁ*  
*tīrthaṁ muhuḥ saṁspṛśatāṁ hi mānasam*  
*haraty ajo 'ntaḥ śrutibhir gato 'ṅgajaṁ*  
*ko vai na seveta mukunda-vikramam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yat—*of whom (the devotees); *saṅga-labdham—*achieved by the association; *nija-vīrya-vaibhavam—*whose influence is uncommon; *tīrtham—*holy places like the Ganges; *muhuḥ—*repeatedly; *saṁspṛśatām—*of those touching; *hi—*certainly; *mānasam—*the dirty things in the mind; *harati—*vanquishes; *ajaḥ—*the supreme unborn one; *antaḥ—*in the core of the heart; *śrutibhiḥ—*by the ears; *gataḥ—*entered; *aṅga-jam—*dirty things or infections of the body; *kaḥ—*who; *vai—*indeed; *na—*not; *seveta—*would serve; *mukunda-vikramam—*the glorious activities of Mukunda, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**By associating with persons for whom the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Mukunda, is the all in all, one can hear of His powerful activities and soon come to understand them. The activities of Mukunda are so potent that simply by hearing of them one immediately associates with the Lord. For a person who constantly and very eagerly hears narrations of the Lord's powerful activities, the Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead in the form of sound vibrations, enters within his heart and cleanses it of all contamination. On the other hand, although bathing in the Ganges diminishes bodily contaminations and infections, this process and the process of visiting holy places can cleanse the heart only after a long time. Therefore who is the sane man who will not associate with devotees to quickly perfect his life?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The advantage of being attached to the devotees of the Lord is stated here. The Lord removes all the dirt in the minds of those who become attached to noble men and listen to the greatness of the Lord from them. The Lord’s greatness and valor are unique. For those who worship and bathe in the Gaṅgā repeatedly, only the dirt on their skin is washed off, not the desires of the heart. Which person will not listen to the greatness of the Lord? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The greatness of attachment to good people is stated here. Śrī Kṛṣṇa removes the dirt of desires from the mind of those who listen to his *līlā* \[pastimes\] in the company of good people. Going within, through the ears, He attracts the mind also. Who will not be interested in Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, which can only be heard in the company of good people? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Again the way by which association with good people achieves everything is elaborated: “My mind achieved the ability to meditate upon God only because of association with good people.” *Nija-vīrya-vaibhavam* means my ability to concentrate on God. For those who listen to His pastimes, He enters through the ear and becomes seated in the mind and cleanses it. Then the mind becomes competent to meditate upon Him. “So who will not listen to Mukunda’s valor?” Or the verse can be interpreted in another way: Now *nija* means *Bhagavān*. *Nija-vīrya-vaibhavam* means the splendor of Hari *līlā*. This is perceived only because of the contact with good people. For those who listen to this He enters within and purifies the mind. An example is cited here. Just as the Gaṅgā removes the external dirt of those who bathe in her waters, Mukunda enters within and removes the internal dirt of the mind. Listening to his *vikrama*, purification of the mind, competence to meditate upon Him, worship and the final accomplishment*—*this is the process shown here.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Stated here is the process of obtaining vairāgya in the company of good people. By serving great people, one comes to know about the greatness of Hari by listening to their advice. Then, Hari enters one’s mind and purifies it by removing the desire for external objects. Then *vairāgya* \[renunciation\] arises. Who will not listen to the great pastimes of Mukunda?

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

For those who meditate well on the pastimes of God, which are known only in the company of good people, Mukunda enters the heart through the ear and cleanses the heart. He attracts the mind, rousing sincere devotion. He also destroys the desires (*aṅga-jam*) there.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

For those who listen to the pastimes, which are capable of revealing the object of meditation in the company of good people, and also serve Him through glorification and other things, Mukunda enters the heart and cleanses it. Gaṅgā and others remove only the external dirt for those who bathe in their waters. Who will not listen to Mukunda *līlā*?

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

How is the association with great devotees going to bring any accomplishment? The reply is through hearing (*śravaṇa*), thinking (manana) and meditating (dhyana). Hearing God's pastimes is the most important. He enters the mind, purifies it, and sanctifies by His presence.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The necessity of the association with good people is stated here by illustrating the manner in which the company of good people brings about *vairāgya*. The glory of Mukunda’s valor and virtues will be known through the scriptures only in the company of devotees. For those who repeatedly listen to them and those who repeatedly bathe and drink Gaṅgā waters, the Lord will enter their heart and remove the desire for wordly things. Who will not listen to the glory of Mukunda?

### Text 12

*यस्यास्ति भक्तिर्भगवत्यकिञ्चना*  
*सर्वैर्गुणैस्तत्र समासते सुराः ।*  
*हरावभक्तस्य कुतो महद्गुणा*  
*मनोरथेनासति धावतो बहिः ॥१२॥*

*yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā*  
*sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ*  
*harāv abhaktasya kuto mahad-guṇā*  
*manorathenāsati dhāvato bahiḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yasya—*of whom; *asti—*there is; *bhaktiḥ—*devotional service; *bhagavati—*to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *akiñcanā—*without any motive; *sarvaiḥ—*with all; *guṇaiḥ—*good qualities; *tatra—*there (in that person); *samāsate—*reside; *surāḥ—*all the demigods; *harau—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *abhaktasya—*of a person who is not devoted; *kutaḥ—*where; *mahat-guṇāḥ—*good qualities; *manorathena—*by mental speculation; *asati—*in the temporary material world; *dhāvataḥ—*who is running; *bahiḥ—*outside.

**Перевод:**

**All the demigods and their exalted qualities, such as religion, knowledge and renunciation, become manifest in the body of one who has developed unalloyed devotion for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva. On the other hand, a person devoid of devotional service and engaged in material activities has no good qualities. Even if he is adept at the practice of mystic yoga or the honest endeavor of maintaining his family and relatives, he must be driven by his own mental speculations and must engage in the service of the Lord's external energy. How can there be any good qualities in such a man?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The result of the purification of one’s mind is narrated here. *Akiñcana* means bereft of desires. By the association with great people, devotion is kindled, whereupon the demigods, with all their virtues, come and reside. For a person interested in his family, where are the virtues of knowledge and renunciation? His mind always moves out in search of creature comforts. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Here devotion is extolled. *Akiñcana* means those who do not depend upon any comfort in this world and the next. That means they have no desire for anything except God. For a person who has such devotion, Indra and other demigods come and reside in him with all their virtues like control of senses, knowledge and so on. Having stated the position of a devotee, the position of a person who does not have devotion is stated. How can such a person obtain the virtues obtained by a devotee when his mind is always running towards external objects in search of pleasure?

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

When one has devotion for Hari, Hari will be pleased. When Hari is pleased, all other gods are pleased, is what is stated here.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The gods, Hari included, come of their own accord, and stay there.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhakti is of the nature of dwelling the mind on God’s pastimes. It is possible only in the company of good people. For this reason, the *bhakta* is extolled in this verse. *Akiñcana* means bereft of desires. They dwell on God exclusively with all their knowledge and renunciation. God is the receptacle of all other deities and so service to God is service to all other deities. The lords of the senses, Rudra and others reside in Him with their virtues only, and not vices. So the *bhakta* is not subjected to pride and prejudice. For a person who does not have devotion, where can one find the virtues which are to be found in a devotee? Even if he is learned in the Vedic scriptures he will have envy and other vices as his mind will be running towards external accomplishments and prestige. The gods reside happily in a devotee. In others the demigods are present but always fear that they may be destroyed along with that wicked person. In a devotee, they feel they will become stronger, with the juice of Harilīlā, on which the devotee always meditates.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The greatness of the devotee who is intent on listening to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa is stated here. He will be a residing place for all demigods because Kṛṣṇa seva \[service\] amounts to the service of all gods. The supervisors of the senses, Rudra and others, reside in Him only with all their virtues and with no blemishes. So his mind will be rid of conceit and false ego. How can there be great virtues for a non-devotee? Even if there is the study of śāstras \[scriptures\], it will be coupled with envy and the like. His mind will only be running towards the external objects which good people try to keep away from. The demigods who reside in a wicked person are always afraid that the wicked person will cause harm even to them. So they are not placed well there. But a devotee who enjoys the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa *līlā*, is very happy and comfortable. They would like to bestow immortality upon such a person.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The gods reside in him who has no other desire except serving God. The gods reside there with all their virtues. Demigods never approach a person whose mind repeatedly runs towards the external objects. They do not reside there.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

It is well known that those who are blessed by God and have *dharma*, mana and vairāgya will attain liberation. Without these, how can there be liberation? The reply is: “The concept is wrong. Devotion is the root cause of every achievement—only it will bring divine grace and *dharma*, etc. This is because the demigods, endowed with all these virtues, reside in the heart of a devotee.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Stated here is: “Extolling devotion to God results in the purification of the mind.” The demigods come and reside in a devotee who has no desire for pleasure in this world and the next. For a person without devotion, how will he obtain the virtues of good people, such as knowledge, renunciation and so on? His desires will drag his mind to external material things again and again.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The person who obtains *vairāgya* and directs his mind only towards God gets but one advantage*—*Hari’s \[God’s\] grace*—*however, he will not obtain other virtues and the grace of demigods. This objection is answered in this verse.

The accepted reading is the plural *akiñcanah* rather than the singular *akiñcana*. It is an adjective to the noun *bhakti*. In the plural it is an adjective to the noun “*suras*.” The gods who are devoid of the worldly desires happily reside in that person with all the virtues. The idea is demigods will be pleased and the person will have all the virtues. The same thing is established by citing the situation to the contrary. For a person whose mind always runs towards the external inauspicious (*asate*) things, whence virtues and whence gods?

### Text 13

*हरिर्हि साक्षाद्भगवान् शरीरिणा*  
*मात्मा झषाणामिव तोयमीप्सितम् ।*  
*हित्वा महांस्तं यदि सज्जते गृहे*  
*तदा महत्त्वं वयसा दम्पतीनाम् ॥१३॥*

*harir hi sākṣād bhagavān śarīriṇām*  
*ātmā jhaṣāṇām iva toyam īpsitam*  
*hitvā mahāṁs taṁ yadi sajjate gṛhe*  
*tadā mahattvaṁ vayasā dampatīnām*

**Пословный перевод:**

*hariḥ—*the Lord; *hi—*certainly; *sākṣāt—*directly; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *śarīriṇām—*of all living entities who have accepted material bodies; *ātmā—*the life and soul; *jhaṣāṇām—*of the aquatics; *iva—*like; *toyam—*the vast water; *īpsitam—*is desired; *hitvā—*giving up; *mahān—*a great personality; *tam—*Him; *yadi—*if; *sajjate—*becomes attached; *gṛhe—*to household life; *tadā—*at that time; *mahattvam—*greatness; *vayasā—*by age; *dam-patīnām—*of the husband and wife.

**Перевод:**

**Just as aquatics always desire to remain in the vast mass of water, all conditioned living entities naturally desire to remain in the vast existence of the Supreme Lord. Therefore if someone very great by material calculations fails to take shelter of the Supreme Soul but instead becomes attached to material household life, his greatness is like that of a young, low-class couple. One who is too attached to material life loses all good spiritual qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Greatness is seen even in those who are not devotees of Hari. But that greatness is ridiculed here in this verse. For the fish, water is God. Similarly, even if a person considered to be very great is attached only to his home, then that greatness is not praiseworthy. It is to be found even in *śūdras* who are bereft of knowledge. The respect given then to such a person is due only to age, just as in a couple, the husband is honored and in a relationship between a boy and an old man, the old man is honored.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Ātma* means one who bears. It is the water that bears the fish, for without water they will die. Similarly, it is Hari who bears all the *jīvas*. Without Him the *jīvas* will die. Vālmīki said, “Dear Rāghava , without Sītā , I will not live for a single moment*—*like fish out of water.” For those who leave God and become attached to one’s house, there is no other greatness for them other than that due to age. What is implied is that the couple will enjoy the comforts of age, the young age and nothing beyond it. The comforts of the home are sweet at the beginning, but will beget endless misery in the end. They will never get unexcelled bliss through knowledge of God and oneself. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Even without Hari bhakti, an aged couple is honored in this world. Then how is it said from where come virtues to one who is devoid of devotion? The reply is they are honored for their age by ignorant people only. Without devotion one does not become great on any other score. Just as the fish move out of water to get some temporary happiness (of food or something else) and ultimately die, even so ordinary people in search of some temporary comforts forsake Hari, who is responsible for their life as is water to the fish. They ultimately land in the miseries of hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Just as a fish leaves the tank and moves outside in search of pleasure and dies, even does a person who is averse to God dies. He will never become great. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Age is not what commands respect. It is knowledge which commands respect. This is what Viśvanātha \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\] says.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

If one, absorbed in his family, discards Hari, who is like water for the fish, then his greatness, if there is any, is due to age only, and not to wisdom. Just like it is among śūdras, who are bereft of wisdom and knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Hari is the *ātmā* of all *jīvas*. Here *ātmā* means responsible for the life and not soul, as others interpret. Just as fish under illusion move out of the water to get some pleasure, even so does a man who is subjected to an illusion discard God, and meets his end.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

If devotion to Hari is the only thing to be achieved and is the only thing which commands respect, then how is it that an old couple is respected and honored in this world? How can it be said wherefrom is greatness to a person who has no devotion, as greatness is to be found in the aged couple? This question is answered here. *Ātmā* means one who gives what is desired, one who nourishes. So He is desirable like water is to fish. One should necessarily be devoted to Him. He is the most helpful. The respect shown to the old couple is only for their age even among śūdras who have no knowledge or devotion. So age is not what commands respect.

### Text 14

*तस्माद्रजोरागविषादमन्यु*  
*मानस्पृहाभयदैन्याधिमूलम् ।*  
*हित्वा गृहं संसृतिचक्रवालं*  
*नृसिंहपादं भजताकुतोभयमिति ॥१४॥*

*tasmād rajo-rāga-viṣāda-manyu-*  
*māna-spṛhā-bhayadainyādhimūlam*  
*hitvā gṛhaṁ saṁsṛti-cakravālaṁ*  
*nṛsiṁha-pādaṁ bhajatākutobhayam iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tasmāt—*therefore; *rajaḥ—*of passion or material desires; *rāga—*attachment for material things; *viṣāda—*then disappointment; *manyu—*anger; *māna-spṛhā—*the desire to be respectable in society; *bhaya—*fear; *dainya—*of poverty; *adhimūlam—*the root cause; *hitvā—*giving up; *gṛham—*household life; *saṁsṛti-cakravālam—*the cycle of repeated birth and death; *nṛsiṁha-pādam—*the lotus feet of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva; *bhajata—*worship; *akutaḥ-bhayam—*the shelter of fearlessness; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O demons, give up the so-called happiness of family life and simply take shelter of the lotus feet of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, which are the actual shelter of fearlessness. Entanglement in family life is the root cause of material attachment, indefatigable desires, moroseness, anger, despair, fear and the desire for false prestige, all of which result in the repetition of birth and death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Because of this reason, the *asuras* are told to shun their homes and dedicate themselves to the worship of the feet of Nṛsiṁha, which gives protection from all fears. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Devotion to God is the cause of infinite bliss, and attachment to home is the cause of endless misery. Thus, one should abandon the home which is the center of saṁsāra and hence the root cause of all desires, anger and so on. Instead, one should worship Nṛsiṁha’s feet, which give protection from all fears. *Rajaḥ* = desire of objects. *Rāga* = anger, which erupts when enjoyment is hampered. *Viṣāda* = the grief which ensues when enjoyment is stopped. *Māna* = ego, which is responsible for insulting worthy people. *Manya* = rage, an offshoot of ego, another form of anger. *Spṛhā* = desire to grab other’s wives and wealth. *Dainya* = the depression of the mind. *Aadhi* = the oppression of the mind due to the above depression. \[Note: Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Saṁsṛti-cakravālam* means the non-disruption of the chain of births and deaths.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If one were to leave God and become attached to one’s home, then even if he were known as great, his greatness would be because of his age only, and nothing else. It could be old age or young age. A young couple is honored by another young couple, only because of youth and nothing else.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Rajas* is desire. *Rāga* is vehement attachment. The center of saṁsāra is the home only. So worship God. This is teaching asuras.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

There is no greatness in one’s family, around which the saṁsāra cycle rotates. Therefore, one should leave it.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He preaches to the asuras. “Leave the home, which is the cause of many defects, and worship Nṛsiṁha's feet, which remove all sorts of fears.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This is Prahlāda's wonderful nature that he wishes the welfare of all and urges others to worship God. From the context it should be noted that both Prahlāda and Nṛsiṁha have a predominant tamas mixed with sattva *guṇa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Because bhakti is the cause for everlasting bliss, and attachment to external things is the cause of endless misery, one should leave the home and worship Nṛsiṁha’s feet which ensure fearlessness. This is the main explanation.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The topic is concluded again stressing that *vairāgya* should necessarily be earned. *Rajas* = desire, the affection towards son and others who are *rajasas*. *Mānah* = ego. *Spṛha* = the desire of so many things. *Saṁsāra* is a circle (*cakra*vāla) of births and deaths. One should get liberated from that.

### Text 15

*केतुमालेऽपि भगवान् कामदेवस्वरूपेण लक्ष्म्याः प्रियचिकीर्षया*  
*प्रजापतेर्दुहित्णां पुत्राणां तद्वर्षपतीनां पुरुषायुषाहोरात्रपरिसङ्ख्यानानां यासां*  
*गर्भा महापुरुषमहास्त्रतेजसोद्वेजितमनसां विध्वस्ता व्यसवः संवत्सरान्ते*  
*विनिपतन्ति ॥१५॥*

*ketumāle 'pi bhagavān kāmadeva-svarūpeṇa lakṣmyāḥ priya-cikīrṣayā prajāpater duhitṝṇāṁ putrāṇāṁ tad-varṣa-patīnāṁ puruṣāyuṣāho-rātra-parisaṅkhyānānāṁ yāsāṁ garbhā mahā-puruṣa-mahāstra-tejasodvejita-manasāṁ vidhvastā vyasavaḥ saṁvatsarānte vinipatanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ketumāle—*in the tract of land known as Ketumāla-varṣa; *api—*also; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Viṣṇu; *kāmadeva-svarūpeṇa—*in the form of Kāmadeva (Cupid or Pradyumna); *lakṣmyāḥ—*of the goddess of fortune; *priya-cikīrṣayā—*with a desire to bring about the satisfaction; *prajāpateḥ—*of Prajāpati; *duhitṝṇām—*of the daughters; *putrāṇām—*of the sons; *tat-varṣa-patīnām—*the ruler of that land; *puruṣa-āyuṣā—*in a human lifetime (about one hundred years); *ahaḥ-rātra—*the days and nights; *parisaṅkhyānānām—*which equal in number; *yāsām—*of whom (the daughters); *garbhāḥ—*fetuses; *mahā-puruṣa—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *mahā-astra—*of the great weapon (the disc); *tejasā—*by the effulgence; *udvejita-manasām—*whose minds are agitated; *vidhvastāḥ—*ruined; *vyasavaḥ—*dead; *saṁvatsara-ante—*at the end of the year; *vinipatanti—*fall down.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: In the tract of land called Ketumāla-varṣa, Lord Viṣṇu lives in the form of Kāmadeva, only for the satisfaction of His devotees. These include Lakṣmījī \[the goddess of fortune\], the Prajāpati Saṁvatsara and all of Saṁvatsara's sons and daughters. The daughters of Prajāpati are considered the controlling deities of the nights, and his sons are considered the controllers of the days. The Prajāpati's offspring number 36,000, one for each day and each night in the lifetime of a human being. At the end of each year, the Prajāpati's daughters become very agitated upon seeing the extremely effulgent disc of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and thus they all suffer miscarriages.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Lord resides in the form of Kāmadeva in Ketumāla-varṣa. The next part of the sentence states why he resides there. Prajāpati means saṁvatsara, a year-god. His daughters rule over the nights, and his sons over the days, of a year to look to their welfare. This figure matches with the number of days and nights in a human life. By the power of Sudarśana the fetuses of the daughters miscarry. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The details of worship in Ketumāla-varṣa is stated herein. God resides there in the form of Kāmadeva i.e. Pradyumna, with a view to give happiness to Lakṣmī. Prajāpati is saṁvatsara. His daughters are the supervisors of the nights of a year and his sons, of the days. There, the life span is 36,000 years. Pradyumna gives happiness to them also here. These women are frightened by the Sudarśana *chakra* of the Lord and their fetuses fall dead one year after the conception. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Hari is there as Pradyumna, the form in which he is present in Kāmadeva (Manmatha). Lakṣmī is there in the form in which she is present in Rati, Manmathas’s wife. Hari is present there in order to give pleasure to Ramā and also to give happiness to Manmatha and Rati. This fact is clarified in the *Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa*, “Lakṣmī stationed in Rati worships Pradyumna stationed in Manmatha.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He resides there in the form of Kāmadeva for the sake of blessing Lakṣmī. He is also desirous of blessing the sons and daughters of Prajāpati. They are the supervisors of the days and nights of a year.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Here Viṣṇu is in the form of Pradyumna, the form in which he is present in Kāmadeva (Manmatha, the god of love). Here also Kāmadeva is there. Pradyumna is here to give happiness to Lakṣmī who is present in Rati, the wife of Manmatha, who is also present here. Prajāpati is saṁvatsara which is another name of Śrī Brahmā, who pleases his daughters who are the goddesses supervising the nights. Their number is counted by the number of days and nights of year, i.e. they are thirty six thousand in number. Viṣṇu is the Mahāpuruṣa. Sudarśana is his great weapon. *Vyasavaḥ* means “fall dead.”

### Text 16

*अतीव सुललितगतिविलासविलसितरुचिरहासलेशावलोकलीलया*  
*किञ्चिदुत्तम्भितसुन्दरभ्रूमण्डलसुभगवदनारविन्दश्रिया रमां*  
*रमयन्निन्द्रियाणि रमयते ॥१६॥*

*atīva sulalita-gati-vilāsa-vilasita-rucira-hāsa-leśāvaloka-līlayā kiñcid-uttambhita-sundara-bhrū-maṇḍala-subhaga-vadanāravinda-śriyā ramāṁ ramayann indriyāṇi ramayate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*atīva—*very much; *su-lalita—*beautiful; *gati—*with movements; *vilāsa—*by pastimes; *vilasita—*manifested; *rucira—*pleasing; *hāsa-leśa—*mild smiling; *avaloka-līlayā—*by playful glancing; *kiñcit-uttambhita—*slightly raised; *sundara—*beautiful; *bhrū-maṇḍala—*by the eyebrows; *subhaga—*auspicious; *vadana-aravinda-śriyā—*with His beautiful lotuslike face; *ramām—*the goddess of fortune; *ramayan—*pleasing; *indriyāṇi—*all the senses; *ramayate—*He pleases*.*

**Перевод:**

**In Ketumāla-varṣa, Lord Kāmadeva \[Pradyumna\] moves very graciously. His mild smile is very beautiful, and when He increases the beauty of His face by slightly raising His eyebrows and glancing playfully, He pleases the goddess of fortune. Thus He enjoys His transcendental senses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Causing delight to Lakṣmī, He causes delight to His own senses. How does He cause delight? By the beauty of His slightly lifted face, decorated with a smile and kind gaze, and also by His graceful gait. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Indriyāṇi ramayate* means He causes delight to the eyes and other senses of those who see Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is stated here that Lakṣmī praises the Lord in Ketumāla-varṣa always with a pure devotion. The word *puruṣa-āyuṣā* refers to the life span of humans.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lakṣmī prays with devotion coupled with a sense of servitude. Prajāpati is the god who rules over the year. His sons and daughters are the rulers of day and night. The fetuses referred to are the smaller divisions of the day and night in the form of hours, minutes and seconds. The passing of these particular divisions of time are used up enjoying the good or bad results of one’s previous actions. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara and Śukadeva\] He gives pleasure to Ramā with His gentle gait, smiles, affectionate glances and slightly lifted handsome face. On his part He enjoys the glances, smiles and beautiful face of Ramā.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

These demigods reside in the material world only, perform their *seva*, ascend to Vaikuṇṭha and then become immersed in the sweet nectar of affection towards God. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He brings delight to Lakṣmī by His grace, etc. and in the process pleases His senses also.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Ramayate is explained as "plays with His senses" and not as "derives pleasure from."

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

What is the function of Praydyumna who is present in Manmatha there? This question is answered here. He pleases Lakṣmī with His pastimes. His handsome face with slightly raised brows, His affectionate looks, smiles, the dalliance of His graceful gait—all these cause delight to the eyes of those who see.

### Text 17

*तद्भगवतो मायामयं रूपं परमसमाधियोगेन रमा देवी संवत्सरस्य रात्रिषु*  
*प्रजापतेर्दुहितृभिरुपेताहःसु च तद्भर्तृभिरुपास्ते इदं चोदाहरति ॥१७॥*

*tad bhagavato māyāmayaṁ rūpaṁ parama-samādhi-yogena ramā devī saṁvatsarasya rātriṣu prajāpater duhitṛbhir upetāhaḥsu ca tad-bhartṛbhir upāste idaṁ codāharati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tat—*that; *bhagavataḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *māyā-mayam—*full of affection for the devotees; *rūpam—*form; *parama—*highest; *samādhi-yogena—*by absorption of the mind in the service of the Lord; *ramā—*the goddess of fortune; *devī—*divine woman; *saṁvatsarasya—*known as Saṁvatsara; *rātriṣu—*during the nights; *prajāpateḥ—*of Prajāpati; *duhitṛbhiḥ—*with the daughters; *upeta—*combined; *ahaḥsu—*during the days; *ca—*also; *tat-bhartṛbhiḥ—*with the husbands; *upāste—*worships; *idam—*this; *ca—*also; *udāharati—*chants.

**Перевод:**

**Accompanied during the daytime by the sons of the Prajāpati \[the predominating deities of the days\] and accompanied at night by his daughters \[the deities of the nights\], Lakṣmīdevī worships the Lord during the period known as the Saṁvatsara in His most merciful form as Kāmadeva. Fully absorbed in devotional service, she chants the following mantras.**
