**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Tat-bhartṛbhiḥ* means along with the rulers of the day.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

There, He pleases Lakṣmī while at the same time enjoying Himself. His smiles and looks embellished by His graceful gait and dalliance please her as also His handsome face with slightly raised brows. Ramā performs her worship during the nights, along with the daughters of Prajāpati and during daytime with his sons. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Lakṣmī present in Rati performs the worship of Pradyumna present in Kāmadeva. *Māyā-mayam* means of the nature of knowledge. *Māyā* is a synonym of *jñāna* as quoted earlier. Rati performs the worship of Manmatha also.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Māyā-mayam* means abounding in kindness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Māyā-mayam* means of the nature of kindness or the dispeller of ignorance in the living entities. Prajāpati's daughters are the supervisors of the nights and his sons are the supervisors of the day. Ramā performs her worship along with them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Māyā-mayam* means abounding in kindness. Or *māya* means the *avidyā* \[ignorance\] of the living entity (*jīva*). *Āmaya* means disease, destruction. *Māyā-mayam* means the destroyer of the ignorance of the living entities.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Māyā* means *vayuha*, which is of the nature of a wish. The world is manifested by His mere wish.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Lakṣmī worships this Kāmadeva (Pradyumna) form which is *rajasa* in nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Māyā-mayam* = abounding in *māyā* = taken by His own free will.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In addition to the above, it should also be taken that Manmatha pleases Rati by all his grace. *Māyā-mayam* in the case of Pradyumna means “of the nature of knowledge and desire.” In the case of Manmatha it means “an expansion of *prakṛti*.” The deity in which Ramā shines here is Rati, it should be noted. Both Rati and Ramā chant (the following *mantra*):

### Text 18

*ॐ ह्रां ह्रीं ह्रूँ ॐ नमो भगवते हृषीकेशाय सर्वगुणविशेषैर्विलक्षितात्मने*  
*आकूतीनां चित्तीनां चेतसां विशेषाणां चाधिपतये*  
*षोडशकलायच्छन्दोमयायान्नमयायामृतमयाय सर्वमयाय सहसे ओजसे*  
*बलाय कान्ताय कामाय नमस्ते उभयत्र भूयात् ॥१८॥*

*oṁ hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ oṁ namo bhagavate hṛṣīkeśāya sarva-guṇa-viśeṣair vilakṣitātmane ākūtīnāṁ cittīnāṁ cetasāṁ viśeṣāṇāṁ cādhipataye ṣoḍaśa-kalāya cchando-mayāyānna-mayāyāmṛta-mayāya sarva-mayāya sahase ojase balāya kāntāya kāmāya namas te ubhayatra bhūyāt.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O Lord; *hrām hrīm hrūm—*the seeds of the mantra, chanted for a successful result; *om—*O Lord; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *hṛṣīkeśāya—*unto Hṛṣīkeśa, the Lord of the senses; *sarva-guṇa—*with all transcendental qualities; *viśeṣaiḥ—*with all varieties; *vilakṣita—*particularly observed; *ātmane—*unto the soul of all living entities; *ākūtīnām—*of all kinds of activity; *cittīnām—*of all kinds of knowledge; *cetasām—*of the functions of the mind, such as determination and mental effort; *viśeṣāṇām—*of their respective objects; *ca—*and; *adhipataye—*unto the master; *ṣoḍaśa-kalāya—*whose parts are the sixteen original ingredients of creation (namely the five objects of the senses and the eleven senses, including the mind); *chandaḥ-mayāya—*unto the enjoyer of all ritualistic ceremonies; *anna-mayāya—*who maintains all living entities by supplying the necessities of life; *amṛta-mayāya—*who awards eternal life; *sarva-mayāya—*who is all-pervading; *sahase—*the powerful; *ojase—*who supplies strength to the senses; *balāya—*who supplies strength to the body; *kāntāya—*the supreme husband or master of all living entities; *kāmāya—*who supplies all necessities for the devotees; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *te—*unto You; *ubhayatra—*always (during both day and night, or both in this life and the next); *bhūyāt—*may there be all good fortune.

**Перевод:**

**Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, the controller of all my senses and the origin of everything. As the supreme master of all bodily, mental and intellectual activities, He is the only enjoyer of their results. The five sense objects and eleven senses, including the mind, are His partial manifestations. He supplies all the necessities of life, which are His energy and thus nondifferent from Him, and He is the cause of everyone's bodily and mental prowess, which is also nondifferent from Him. Indeed, He is the husband and provider of necessities for all living entities. The purpose of all the Vedas is to worship Him. Therefore let us all offer Him our respectful obeisances. May He always be favorable toward us in this life and the next.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Whose self is embellished by all the virtues and good things. *Ākūti* = actions. *Cetasām* = wish and resolve. *Viśeṣaiḥ* = pertaining to various things. The “sixteen parts” are the eleven sense organs and the five elements. *Chandaḥ-mayāya* = attainable by Vedic rites. *Anna-mayāya* because rejuvenated by food. *Amṛta-mayāya* because of the nature of supreme bliss. *Sarva-mayāya* because of his association with everything. He is the cause of the power of resistance, valor and strength.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Lakṣmī chants the *mantra* describing the kindness of the Lord and suggests that any other person who chants the *mantra* should think of God in the same way. “Obeisances to my Lord Kāma,” is the main explanation. The word “kāma” is used in place of “Kāmadeva” for a wife should not pronounce the name of her husband in full. Hṛṣīkeśa means, *one who attracts my mind, eyes and other senses by His handsomeness and other virtues*. Or, *one who enjoys the sweetness of my eyes and other senses*. The reason for this is, “My senses and body are different from the ordinary type as they are *aprakṛta* (not produced of matter) and this is due to His kindness only.” *Ākūti* is the motor-organs, *cittīnām* = the sensory organs, the mind, ego and intellect, *vritti* = the objects of the sensory organs, the mind, ego and intellect. “You are the Lord of all those things.” In the case of Lakṣmī, Kṛṣṇa is the enjoyer of all these things. In the case of others, Kṛṣṇa is present in all these things. This is how it should be viewed. The other gods cannot make Lakṣmī’s body and senses *aprakṛta*. *Chandaḥ-mayāya* means one who teaches devotion through the Vedas. He is *anna-mayāya* because he protects the devotee in the form of food. *Amṛta-mayāya* means all His pastimes are sweet like nectar or He is of the nature of liberation (immortality). *Sarva-mayāya* means having the form of every object. “*Mahase”* and the other two adjectives mean, “One who gives strength to my mind, intellect and body so that I am in Your service.” *Ubhayatra* means “in this world and the next” or “from inside and outside.” The *bījākṣara* of shyness (*hṛa*) and *praṇava* signify the attainment of the four *puruṣartas*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

She chants this *mantra* along with the others who also perform the same worship. *Hṛṣīkeśa* means the controller of senses (hṛṣīka). “You are endowed with the virtues of truthfulness and knowledge, which are not to be found in *prakṛti* and *puruṣa*. You are glorified as endowed with such attributes by the Vedas. “Obeisances to one such You” is to be appended at every part of the sentence, after every adjective. “You are the controller of actions (*ākūti*), perceptions (*jñāna*) wishes and resolves (*cetas*), in short, all the operations of the motor organs, sensory organs and mind. You are the controller of nature and other great elements. This control is not like that of a king over his servants. It is like the control of the soul over the body, though the controller and the controlled are different in both the examples. The sixteen parts (*kalās*) are the five elements and the eleven organs (motor, sensory and mind). You are the controller of all these just as the soul controls the body. You are *Chandaḥ-mayāya*, abounding in the Vedas, because the Vedas come out of You.”

Having stated that these principles collectively are in the position of His body, here it is stated that these principles form His body individually also. *Anna-mayāya* means the bodies of the living entities. *Amṛta* means living entities. *Amṛta-mayāya* means whose body is *jīva* himself. The word *sarva-mayāya* signifies that everything mentioned or not mentioned, forms His body only. “The various kinds of strengths are also under your control.” *Sahase* is the strength of the mind. *Ojase* is the strength of the senses, *bala* is physical strength. The identity that appears in the sentence is because He is the cause of all these strengths. *Kānta* means very dear. *Kāmāya* means one who shows dearness to His devotees. “Obeisances to you both from the front and from behind.” \[Note: the two paragraphs above are repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Ākuti* = opinions (thoughts), *citta* = the modes of mind responsible for memory, *cetas* = modes of the intellect. “Obeisances to the lord of all these.” *Ṣoḍaśa-kalāya* = whose inner controlling forms are present in the demigods who rule over the eleven senses and five elements. Or the living entity is said to be the sixteenth *kalā*. *Ṣoḍaśa-kalāya* in this sense means the motivator of the living entity. *Anna-mayāya* = the important enjoyer of food and other things. *Amṛta-mayāya* means the controller of the demigods. *Sarva-mayāya* means the *sarvottama*, Supreme. *Kānta* = husband. *Kāmāya* = present in *kāma* or one who is most desired. *Ubhayatra* = inside and out, “for the sake of protection” should be appended.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“To Him who is stationed in the sixteen powers: the Vedas, the eatables (enjoyables) which give earthly and divine strength.” What is meant by such enumeration? He is stationed in all powers. That is why He is stationed in strength, resistance, and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The Vedas wish to describe Him as endowed with all the qualities like *sarveśvaratva*. He is of the lord of *ākūti* = the operation of sensory organs, *cetas* = of mental thought processes, *viśeṣa* = of their objects. He is *ṣoḍaśa-kalāya* because of His presence in the subtle body, *chandomaya*, because He is of the nature of the Vedas , *amṛta-mayāya* because He has the forms of eternal things.  *Sahas* is mental strength. *Ojas* is the strength of the sensory organs. *Bala* is physical strength. He is *sarva-ātma*, because He is everything. *Kānta* = dear obeisances to You.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The main explanation is: “She chants this *mantra*: Obeisances to You who are my husband and dear to me.” What will happen by this salutation? The reply is, “Since You are non-different from all other things, by offering my respects to You, I will have honored all others.”

The lordship of senses is ascribed to Sūrya and other demigods. How is it that Pradyumna is called the lord of senses? The reply is Pradyumna is not different from Sūrya—thus, his lordship is justified. *Annamaya* means He is non-different from the food the humans consume. *Amrtamaya* means He is non-different from the food the demigods consume. *Chandaḥ-mayāya* means He is not different from the Vedas. “I offer my obeisances both inside (by the mind) and outside (by my body).”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The three *bījākṣaras* are called “Kāmabija.” That means they are capable of giving the desired object to those who chant them.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Brahmā and others are those who know all *kṣetras*. Their abode is the deity form Viṣṇu. He is the lord of *ākūti* = ideas, *citta* = the thought processes, *cetas* = inner sense and *viśeṣa* = mind, intellect and ego which are the modes of the *antaḥ-karaṇa* (inner-sense). He is the motivator of the sixteen *kalās* comprising eleven senses and five elements. *Chandaḥ-mayāya* means the main purport of Vedas. *Annamaya* means the great enjoyer on whom everything depends. *Amrtamaya* means the chief of all *muktas* \[liberated souls\], *sarvamaya* means supreme, *kāma* means desired, *ubhayatra* means inside and out.

### Text 19

*स्त्रियो व्रतैस्त्वा हृषीकेश्वरं स्वतो*  
*ह्याराध्य लोके पतिमाशासतेऽन्यम् ।*  
*तासां न ते वै परिपान्त्यपत्यं*  
*प्रियं धनायूंषि यतोऽस्वतन्त्राः ॥१९॥*

*striyo vratais tvā hṛṣīkeśvaraṁ svato*  
*hy ārādhya loke patim āśāsate 'nyam*  
*tāsāṁ na te vai paripānty apatyaṁ*  
*priyaṁ dhanāyūṁṣi yato 'sva-tantrāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*striyaḥ—*all women; *vrataiḥ—*by observing fasting and other vows; *tvā—*you; *hṛṣīkeśvaram—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead, master of the senses; *svataḥ—*of your own accord; *hi—*certainly; *ārādhya—*worshiping; *loke—in the world; patim—a husband; āśāsate—ask for; anyam—*another; *tāsām—*of all those women; *na—*not; *te—*the husbands; *vai—*indeed; *paripānti—*able to protect; *apatyam—*the children; *priyam—*very dear; *dhana—*the wealth; *āyūṁṣi—*or the duration of life; *yataḥ—*because; *asva-tantrāḥ—*dependent.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, You are certainly the fully independent master of all the senses. Therefore all women who worship You by strictly observing vows because they wish to acquire a husband to satisfy their senses are surely under illusion. They do not know that such a husband cannot actually give protection to them or their children. Nor can he protect their wealth or duration of life, for he himself is dependent on time, fruitive results and the modes of nature, which are all subordinate to You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“I am blessed because I am Your servant at Your behest. Those who worship You with other desires are not complete people. You are the Lord of all the senses. The women worship You and ask for something else. The worship of Kāma (Manmatha) is famous in the Vedas for the women who desire a husband. Those husbands are not competent to look after the offspring they produce.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Chanting the above *mantra*, Lakṣmī says, “You are the only one worthy to be called “*pati.”*  Women worship You by performing so many austerities desiring to get a husband other than You. Those husbands are not competent to protect their wives, children or belongings because they are not independent. They are under the control of others. Therefore, they do not deserve to be called “*pati*” (protector).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Women worship You and get another husband. Pleased by their austerities You protect their children and husbands. The husbands themselves cannot protect anyone. A person who is bitten by a serpent himself cannot rescue another. The word “*pati*” is used just out of courtesy to denote a husband, which he is really not.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Herself bereft of any desire, she pities other women whose devotion is mingled with desires. “They worship You, the Lord of all the senses and ask for something else.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Herself desireless, she offers her prayer with pity for those who are afflicted with desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“They worship You, the Lord of all senses and wish for another husband. They are not husbands (*pati*), as they are unable to protect their wives.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Then why do women worship me and pray for another husband? The reply is because they are foolish. This idea is explained in the next five verses.

The husbands are not capable of protecting their wives. “Only You are capable of protecting everything. In fact they should choose You only and not any other person. Since You are the inner dweller and the Lord of the senses, You are capable of giving everything. Since You are fearless, as You control even time, You are able to give protection to the frightened.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Chanting this *mantra*, Lakṣmī says, “I am contented and feel myself blessed with Your service only. I have only one desire*—*the desire for You. The other women who worship You with other desire will not fulfill their desires.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Lakṣmī states here: “I am blessed because I worship You with no other desire. The women who worship You with other desires are not blessed, You are the supreme Lord of all the senses. You are not under the control of any one. Women worship You and pray for another husband.” That women who want a husband should worship Viṣṇu present in Manmatha is enjoined by the Vedas. This is suggested by the indeclinable “*hi*” here. Those husbands gotten as a result of their worship are actually not their *patis*. Why? “Because they are not able to protect their children.” And that is because they are not independent.

### Text 20

*स वै पतिः स्यादकुतोभयः स्वयं*  
*समन्ततः पाति भयातुरं जनम् ।*  
*स एक एवेतरथा मिथो भयं*  
*नैवात्मलाभादधि मन्यते परम् ॥२०॥*

*sa vai patiḥ syād akutobhayaḥ svayaṁ*  
*samantataḥ pāti bhayāturaṁ janam*  
*sa eka evetarathā mitho bhayaṁ*  
*naivātmalābhād adhi manyate param*

**Пословный перевод:**

*saḥ—*he; *vai—*indeed; *patiḥ—*a husband; *syāt—*would be; *akutaḥ-bhayaḥ—*who is not fearful of anyone; *svayam—*self-sufficient; *samantataḥ—*entirely; *pāti—*maintains; *bhaya-āturam—*who is very afraid; *janam—*a person; *saḥ—*therefore he; *ekaḥ—*one; *eva—*only; *itarathā—*otherwise; *mithaḥ—*from one another; *bhayam—*fear; *na—*not; *eva—*indeed; *ātma-lābhāt—*than the attainment of You; *adhi—*greater; *manyate—*is accepted; *param—*other thing.

**Перевод:**

**He alone who is never afraid but who, on the contrary, gives complete shelter to all fearful persons can actually become a husband and protector. Therefore, my Lord, you are the only husband, and no one else can claim this position. If you were not the only husband, You would be afraid of others. Therefore persons learned in all Vedic literature accept only Your Lordship as everyone's master, and they think no one else a better husband and protector than You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

So they are not the masters (*pati* means a master who protects). “The best husband and master is Yourself as You are self-satisfied with Your bliss and look for nothing else. Otherwise if Your bliss also depended on something else, You would not have been the independent entity You are. If there is a multiplicity of independent masters, it only leads to chaos.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Lakṣmī says here: “But the word *pati* is not secondary in You because You are the independent protector. You, who are endowed with all the qualities stated in the *mantra*, are the real *pati*. And You are the only *pati*. It is because You have no fear of any kind. That is, You are not subordinate to *karma*. Not merely that, You protect the people who are afflicted by fear. You are the only *pati*, there is nothing superior to You and You do not regard anything superior. It cannot be otherwise. If there were to be a multiplicity of *patis* then it would lead to opposition, like in the case of the multiplicity of feudal kings.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Then who is the real *pati*? He is one who has no fear of time or other things and rescues others from all such fears. Such is Yourself since you are *svatantrā*, independent of anything else. It is because You do not regard anything superior to You or anything able to give You pleasure except Your own self. There cannot be a multiplicity of *patis* in this world, for it will lead to confrontation as in the case of feudal kings, and only chaos would ensue.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because he attains God Himself, one does not consider any other attainment of value. Prahlāda has said, “He who desires other things from You is not your servant. He is a trader.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She says that they do not know even the meaning of the word *pati*. One who protects is *pati*. How can those who cannot protect themselves, protect others? They cannot be called *patis*. He should be free from fear in the first place. Such a person is Yourself only. Though small kings protect their subjects, they are afraid of other kings. So their protection is not protection at all. Thus the learned do not regard anything superior to You. No other attainment is greater than attaining You. So you are the only *pati*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Because they are not competent to protect their subjects, they are also subject to fear like their subjects. So there is no protection. This is what Viśvanātha \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\] says here.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Then who is a *pati*? A *pati* is one who is contented in himself and does not regard anything superior to him. That *pati* is Yourself. There cannot be a multiplicity of *patis* in the world, for then there would be disorder.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“*Itarathā mitho bhayaṁ*” is differently interpreted here. *Itarathā* means by getting attached to external objects without the knowledge of self and God. “*Mitho bhayaṁ*” means there will be mutually fear from each other. “The husbands are also bound by time and they fear it. You are not bound by time. So You have no fear. Therefore only You should be chosen and no one else.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

“The word *pati* is justified in You only and to none else. Endowed with the qualities stated in the *mantra*, You are the real *pati*. The *Vedas* and *Brahma Sutras* bear testimony to this. You are free from fear as You are not ruled by *karma*. Thus You are the real protector (*pati*). That is why You protect Your devotees who are afflicted with fear. You are the only *pati*. Otherwise the multiplicity of protectors would lead to the disorder of the world.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Showing the etymology of the word *pati*, it is established in this verse that the others are not *patis*. Who is that *pati*? You are the only one, because You are independent. *Itarathā* means otherwise, if it were to the contrary. In the event of many independent *patis*, there would be mutual fear, thus, You are the only independent *pati*. You are independent because You do not depend on anything else. You do not regard anything other than Yourself to be of any use to You*—*which might have caused You to depend upon that. But that is not the case.”

### Text 21

*या तस्य ते पादसरोरुहार्हणं*  
*निकामयेत्साखिलकामलम्पटा ।*  
*तदेव रासीप्सितमीप्सितोऽर्चितो*  
*यद्भग्नयाच्ञा भगवन् प्रतप्यते ॥२१॥*

*yā tasya te pāda-saroruhārhaṇaṁ*  
*nikāmayet sākhila-kāma-lampaṭā*  
*tad eva rāsīpsitam īpsito 'rcito*  
*yad-bhagna-yācñā bhagavan pratapyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yā—*a woman who; *tasya—*of Him; *te—*of You; *pāda-saroruha—*of the lotus feet; *arhaṇam—*the worship; *nikāmayet—*fully desires; *sā—*such a woman; *akhila-kāma-lampaṭā—*although maintaining all kinds of material desire; *tat—*that; *eva—*only; *rāsi—*You award; *īpsitam—*some other desired benediction; *īpsitaḥ—*being looked to for; *arcitaḥ—*worshiped; *yat—*from which; *bhagna-yācñā—*one who desires objects other than Your lotus feet and who thus becomes broken; *bhagavan—*O my Lord; *pratapyate—*is pained.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, You automatically fulfill all the desires of a woman who worships Your lotus feet in pure love. However, if a woman worships Your lotus feet for a particular purpose, You also quickly fulfill her desires, but in the end she becomes broken-hearted and laments. Therefore one need not worship Your lotus feet for some material benefit.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is stated here: “Those who worship You with no other desire get everything. But those who worship You with specific desires get only the particular things. The woman who worships desiring nothing other than Your lotus feet gets everything. The other woman, however, gets only the particular desired thing. After the enjoyment of that particular thing, she again pines. You give her only the transient thing, and not that which is permanent.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

For a woman who has all sorts of desires except the one for Your lotus feet, You give the paltry desired objects, being supplicated by her. They are not goals of life but an apology for it. You do not give her Yourself, who is the essence of all goals of life. She gets the desired objects, enjoys for a while and when it comes to an end, she again falls into grief.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is stated here: “*Niṣkāma bhajan* \[selfless devotion\] alone pleases You and not *sakāma bhajan* \[devotion mixed with furtive desire\]. A person who does the former bhajan will be competent to achieve everything. The second type achieves only the desired object and laments after its loss.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Your feet are those capable of fulfilling whatever one desires. This is what the word *akhila-kāma-lampaṭā* means.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is stated here: “In *niṣkāma bhajan*, all things come without asking for them. In *sakāma bhajan*, only the desired object is acquired and that too is transitory. A woman who desires only Your feet will be able to receive all objects and still she is called a *niṣkāma bhakta*. But for a *sakāma bhakta*, You supply what she asks for and after the enjoyment of the object, she again laments. Lakṣmī suggests by her censure that she does not belong to the second type. But in fact even *sakāma bhajan* is extolled later.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Here it is said that *niṣkāma seva* is superior to the one coupled with desires. The word *bhagavān* signifies that He is competent to give anything asked for. The person with desires laments after the fulfillment of his desires. This is only when compared to Lakṣmī. Otherwise, even a *sakāma-seva* is lauded in *Bhagvad-gītā* where it is said that devotees are of four kinds of which the *sakāma-sevakas* are one.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

One who wishes only your feet will get everything that one needs. On the other hand, a woman who worships you and asks for husband and children, gets them, but pines later.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

In *niṣkāma bhajan*, the devotee gets everything. In *sakāma bhajan*, the devotee gets the desired object and that too will be temporary. This is the idea expressed here.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

It is stated here. “You are pleased when one worships You without any personal desire. You are not pleased with a worship coupled with desires. The person who abandons all his desires and desires the worship of Your lotus feet only, will be competent to achieve all the *puruṣarthas* \[religion, wealth, sense gratification and liberation\], not one who worships with desires. It is because if there are any strong impediments, the second type of worship does not bear any fruits and the person will become sad on that score.

### Text 22

*मत्प्राप्तयेऽजेशसुरासुरादय*  
*स्तप्यन्त उग्रं तप ऐन्द्रियेधियः ।*  
*ऋते भवत्पादपरायणान्न मां*  
*विन्दन्त्यहं त्वद्धृदया यतोऽजित ॥२२॥*

*mat-prāptaye 'jeśa-surāsurādayas*  
*tapyanta ugraṁ tapa aindriye dhiyaḥ*  
*ṛte bhavat-pāda-parāyaṇān na māṁ*  
*vindanty ahaṁ tvad-dhṛdayā yato 'jita*

**Пословный перевод:**

*mat-prāptaye—*to obtain my mercy; *aja—*Lord Brahmā; *īśa—*Lord Śiva; *sura—*the other demigods, headed by King Indra, Candra and Varuṇa; *asura-ādayaḥ—*as well as the demons; *tapyante—*undergo; *ugram—*severe; *tapaḥ—*austerity; *aindriye dhiyaḥ—*whose minds are absorbed in thoughts of superior sense gratification; *ṛte—*unless; *bhavat-pāda-parāyaṇāt—*one who is wholly and solely engaged in the service of the Supreme Lord's lotus feet; *na—*not; *mām—*me; *vindanti—*obtain; *aham—*I; *tvat—*in You; *hṛdayāḥ—*whose hearts; *yataḥ—*therefore; *ajita—*O unconquerable one.

**Перевод:**

**O supreme unconquerable Lord, when they become absorbed in thoughts of material enjoyment, Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, as well as other demigods and demons, undergo severe penances and austerities to receive my benedictions. But I do not favor anyone, however great he may be; unless he is always engaged in the service of Your lotus feet. Because I always keep You within my heart, I cannot favor anyone but a devotee.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is stated here: “Everyone worships Lakṣmī only for the fulfillment of their desires. The demigods Brahmā and others worship me (Lakṣmī) for the sake of obtaining my grace. Even then they do not get it without devotion to Hari. As my heart is with You, I only cast my glance at those at whom You cast Your graceful glance.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Lakṣmī says: “Brahmā, Indra, *asuras* and others perform severe penance to obtain me. They do it without taking refuge in Your lotus feet. But they do not get me because I am in your heart. They cannot get me without You. Our relation is *aprthaksiddhi* (one not existing without the other) or I have You always in my heart so they cannot get me without You. I bless only those to whom You are dear.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is stated here: “The worship of Hari without any other desire brings the achievement of everything. The worship of other demigods with many desires will not lead to this.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“If Brahmā and others worship me for the sake of material wealth, let them have it. If anyone of them is intent on Your lotus feet, then he will certainly get me.” Lakṣmī says, “You are always in my heart.” This is to shun any sense of pride.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Some people leave You and worship me only. They only get dust and no real stuff.” This is what Lakṣmī says as she censures such worshippers. “Brahmā and others perform various penances to please me, but I do not cast my kind glance at any one who is averse to You. Wealth and prosperity are seen in demigods and *asuras* who are not Your devotees. However, that is not permanent. It is attained by the grace of Durgā, the *māyā-śakti*. Only Prahlāda, Dhruva and others get permanent wealth bestowed by me. It is not *māyā*, as I am not *māyā*. I am Yours, my mind always set in You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Lakṣmī says here: “Those who worship me only and not You, endowed as they are with many desires, get only dust. Only people like Dhruva and Prahlāda, who are always intent on serving You, get everything. Prosperity is seen even in people who are not Your bhaktas, but that is not given by me. It is given by Durgā, the wielder of the power of *māyā* and such gifts are temporal. What is given by me will be conducive to Your *seva* and devotion, because I am not *māyā*. I have conquered everyone including the demigods Brahmā and others. But it is You who has conquered me.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The central idea here is: “Your devotees who are content with the nectar of Your meditation do not wish for riches which disturb the meditation. But they want to attain You, who is stationed in my heart. They worship me with great devotion as their mother par excellence. I am very kind to my children. So I never leave them and thus they get me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This is the idea. Without devotion even Brahmā will not get his splendor. Then what about the other souls? Without the blessings of Lakṣmī, they cannot bestow wealth on their devotees. So Hari-bhakti is the root cause of everything. If devotees of other demigods get splendor, it should be inferred that they also have Hari-bhakti.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Lakṣmī says: “Everyone who desires something worships You only, and not me, for they are afraid that I will destroy them. Brahmā, Rudra and Indra are also interested in their own sensory pleasures.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

According to the *kaimutya nyaya* (*kaimutya nyaya* is that in which if one is said the other is accepted without saying): “Only *niṣkāma* \[desireless\] worship of Viṣṇu brings religion, wealth, sense gratification and liberation whereas worship of demigods does not.” (If I have ten fruits, that I have fruits goes without saying. This is the kaimutya analogy). Lakṣmī says, “Even the demigods perform penance to get wealth which is under my control.” This implies that Viṣṇu is superior to all other gods and others who worship Lakṣmī. They perform penance with an eye on comforts. “But they do not get me, i.e., they do not get the wealth controlled by me. I will not give them trouble-free wealth. But there is an exception. I do give wealth for those who worship Your lotus feet, abandoning all other desires. This is because I am Your devotee, my heart is always placed in You. Though worshipped by all gods and others, I am afraid of Your displeasure and thus I do not give wealth to those who are averse to You. When I cannot give it, it goes without saying that the demigods who are inferior to me, cannot give it.

### Text 23

*स त्वं ममाप्यच्युत शीर्ष्णि वन्दितं*  
*कराम्बुजं यत्त्वदधायि सात्वताम् ।*  
*बिभर्षि मां लक्ष्म वरेण्य मायया*  
*क ईश्वरस्येहितमूहितुं विभुरिति ॥२३॥*

*sa tvaṁ mamāpy acyuta śīrṣṇi vanditaṁ*  
*karāmbujaṁ yat tvad-adhāyi sātvatām*  
*bibharṣi māṁ lakṣma vareṇya māyayā*  
*ka īśvarasyehitam ūhituṁ vibhur iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*saḥ—*that; *tvam—*You; *mama—*of me; *api—*also; *acyuta—*O infallible one; *śīrṣṇi—*on the head; *vanditam—*worshiped; *kara-ambujam—*Your lotus hand; *yat—*which; *tvat—*by You; *adhāyi—*placed; *sātvatām—*on the head of the devotees; *bibharṣi—*You maintain; *mām—*me; *lakṣma—*as an insignia on Your chest; *vareṇya—*O worshipable one; *māyayā—*with deceit; *kaḥ—*who; *īśvarasya—*of the supremely powerful controller; *īhitam—*the desires; *ūhitum—*to understand by reason and argument; *vibhuḥ—*is able; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**O infallible one, Your lotus palm is the source of all benediction. Therefore Your pure devotees worship it, and You very mercifully place Your hand on their heads. I wish that You may also place Your hand on My head, for although You already bear my insignia of golden streaks on Your chest, I regard this honor as merely a kind of false prestige for me. You show Your real mercy to Your devotees, not to me. Of course, You are the supreme absolute controller, and no one can understand Your motives.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

You bear me on your chest only out of kindness. You are Acyuta, infallible. So you have no desire for a woman. Only those who are fallible have a desire for a woman. You have placed your hand upon my head, the hand you placed on the heads of sattvatas \[devotees\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now Lakṣmī prays for His kindness. Your hand is celebrated in the scriptures as capable of giving all benedictions. Place on my head that same hand which You placed on the heads of devotees. Don’t say, ‘Why do you ask for this as you are always very dear to me and always subjected to my grace.’ You bear me on your chest in the form of *srivatsa*. As the *srivatsa* is just a speck on Your body, I am also a speck. So I am praying for Your kindness. Because You have said, ‘a *jnani* (a learned person) is My own self,’ I am praying for this. No one can know the reason for Your saying this because no one is able to guess or speak about your ways.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Though Hari has always placed his hand on Lakṣmī’s head, Lakṣmī prays for the Lord to instruct other devotees as to what is to be prayed for. “Place Your hand on my head also*—*the hand You have placed on the heads of devotees; Brahmā, Rādhā and others and which has been acclaimed by the scriptures and devotees as capable of giving all benedictions. Lakṣmī is enthralled with the novelty of every action and every form of the Lord. That is why she prays for this. She acknowledges His affection which is superior to the affection He has for anyone else by saying, “You bear me on your chest as a speck by Your own free will. How can anyone imagine Your ways? None can.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“I feel myself blessed as You bear me on your chest, but show me some more kindness. Place Your hand on my head, the hand which You placed on the heads of the devotees and which has been described as giving infinite bliss by the learned. Who is able to know your ways?”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Lakṣmī prays for His kindness since she is also a devotee. If the Lord were to think thus: “Why do you pray for placing My hand on your head? I have shown you My regard by bearing you on my chest.” Lakṣmī’s reply is this: “You always place Your hand on the head of Your devotees. Fearing that I will envy them You have borne me on your chest. This is just a farce. So recognize me also as Your devotee by placing Your hand on my head.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Now Lakṣmī prays for His kindness. “Place Your celebrated hand on my head also—the same hand you placed on other devotees’ heads.” “Why do you ask for this? Don’t I have regard for you?” Lakṣmī replies: “Not that You have no regard for me. You bear me in the form of a sign on Your chest as You bear *śrīvatsa* on one side. You have only regard for me but kindness to other devotees. Your astonishing ways cannot be imagined. So I am praying for Your kindness.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now she prays for His placing His hand on her head, which is indicative of extreme kindness. “You, whose worship gives all benedictions, place Your hand, which You placed on the heads of the devotees, on my head also.” This prayer is for His extraordinary kindness. “Actually You are always kind to me, willfully bearing me on Your chest. Why should You bear at all? No one will be able to answer this question since Your ways cannot be understood.”

### Text 24

*रम्यके च भगवतः प्रियतमं मात्स्यमवताररूपं तद्वर्षपुरुषस्य मनोः*  
*प्राक्प्रदर्शितं स इदानीमपि महता भक्तियोगेनाराधयतीदं*  
*चोदाहरति ॥२४॥*

*ramyake ca bhagavataḥ priyatamaṁ mātsyam avatāra-rūpaṁ tad-varṣa-puruṣasya manoḥ prāk-pradarśitaṁ sa idānīm api mahatā bhakti-yogenārādhayatīdaṁ codāharati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ramyake ca—*also in Ramyaka-varṣa; *bhagavataḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *priya-tamam—*the foremost; *mātsyam—*fish; *avatāra-rūpam—*the form of the incarnation; *tat-varṣa-puruṣasya—*of the ruler of that land; *manoḥ—*Manu; *prāk—*previously (at the end of the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara); *pradarśitam—*exhibited; *saḥ—*that Manu; *idānīm api—*even until now; *mahatā bhakti-yogena—*by dint of advanced devotional service; *ārādhayati—*worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *idam—*this; *ca—*and; *udāharati—*chants.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: In Ramyaka-varṣa, where Vaivasvata Manu rules, the Supreme Personality of Godhead appeared as Lord Matsya at the end of the last era \[the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara\]. Vaivasvata Manu now worships Lord Matsya in pure devotional service and chants the following mantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Now His kindness is prayed for: “Kindly place your hand on my head, the hand You placed on the devotees’ heads.” What kind of hand? A hand capable of giving whatever the suppliants ask for, as the learned say. “You are not indifferent towards me as You bear me on Your chest. It is astonishing that You have only affection for me and kindness to all other devotees. Your ways are bewildering.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the situation in Ketumala-varṣa, now the situation in Ramyaka is described. In Ramyaka, Hari \[the Supreme Lord\] resides in the form of Matsya \[the divine fish incarnation\] which he showed to Manu, the ruler of that *varṣa* \[land\], at the end of the previous *kalpa* \[day of Brahmā\]. There Manu worships Matsya with an uninterrupted love and devotion.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The Manu referred to here is named Vaivasvata, the son of Vivasvan.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“You placed your hand, which You placed on the heads of the devotees, on my head also. This is a humble approach. You bear me on your chest in the form of *śrīvatsa*. This is astonishing (as I am only your servant). It is out of kindness only. So who can know Your ways?

The incarnation of fish is God, and thus is very dear to all the devotees and to God Himself.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Though worshipped by Brahmā and others, and though I am Your wife, I am not as fortunate as a *niṣkāma bhakta* \[pure devotee\]. It is my fate. So place Your hand on my head, the hand which You placed on the heads of the devotees. That You bear me on Your chest is your kindness only. Who is competent to know Your ways? *Prak* means at the end of Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, during the time of deluge. The pronoun “sa”(he) refers to Vaivasvata Manu.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The worship in Ramyaka-varṣa is stated here.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Having described the worship in Ketumala, the worship in Ramyaka is described here. Even now Manu worships the Matsya form which he saw at the end of the previous *manvantara*, with great devotion, and chants this *mantra*:

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The Manu \[director of mankind\] referred to here is known by the name Vaivasvata \[the son of the sun-god\].

### Text 25

*ॐ नमो भगवते मुख्यतमाय नमः सत्त्वाय प्राणायौजसे सहसे बलाय*  
*महामत्स्याय नम इति ॥२५॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate mukhyatamāya namaḥ sattvāya prāṇāyaujase sahase balāya mahā-matsyāya nama iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O my Lord; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *mukhya-tamāya—*the first incarnation to appear; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *sattvāya—*unto the pure transcendence; *prāṇāya—*the origin of life; *ojase—*the source of the potency of the senses; *sahase—*the origin of all mental power; *balāya—*the origin of bodily strength; *mahā-matsyāya—*unto the gigantic fish incarnation; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is pure transcendence. He is the origin of all life, bodily strength, mental power and sensory ability. Known as Matsyāvatāra, the gigantic fish incarnation, He appears first among all the incarnations. Again I offer my obeisances unto Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Sattvaya* = whose quality of pure transcendence predominates. *Mukhyatama prana* means *sutra* (a form of Vāyu \[the wind god\])

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The *mantra* is stated: *Sattvaya* = to You who are pure transcendence. *Mukhya* means the first incarnation. *Pranaya* means one who enlivens. *Ojase* means present in the strength of the senses. *Balaya* = present in physical strength. The unique virtues of the particular *avatāras* are stated, for *mahate* means You are dissimilar to the fish found in the world. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Mukhyatamaya sattvaya* means to You whose form is present in pure Godness. He is called Prana*, etc.* as He is the controller of *prana*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Prak* = formerly i.e. during the deluge at the end of Cākṣuṣa Manu’s reign. Even the form of fish is a blemishless form of Himself. *Tadvarsapuruṣa* = the leaders of those who live in Ramyaka- varṣa. Manu referred to here is Vaivasvata.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Mukhyatama* means the superior.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The *mantra* is stated. The word “namah” at the beginning, middle and end suggests that it should be appended to every other word denoting the virtues.

*Sattvaya* = to the incarnation of Viṣṇu who is of pure transcendence in nature. *Pranaya* = to *sutra* (name of Vāyu). *Prana* is predominant *rajas* mixed with *tamas*. The *nirbandha* also says, “Matsya is *tamas* mixed with *rajas*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The *mantra* is stated: “One who is in the front (*mukha*) is Mukhya.” That means the first. “Obeisances to You, the first incarnation. *Mahamatsya* means, “You are different from the other fish we see.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Sattva* means who is of the nature of auspicious virtues. *Prana* means the supreme motivator who causes action in the living beings.

### Text 26

*अन्तर्बहिश्चाखिललोकपालकै*  
*रदृष्टरूपो विचरस्युरुस्वनः ।*  
*स ईश्वरस्त्वं य इदं वशेऽनय*  
*न्नाम्ना यथा दारुमयीं नरः स्त्रियम् ॥२६॥*

*antar bahiś cākhila-loka-pālakair*  
*adṛṣṭa-rūpo vicarasy uru-svanaḥ*  
*sa īśvaras tvaṁ ya idaṁ vaśe 'nayan*  
*nāmnā yathā dārumayīṁ naraḥ striyam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*antaḥ—*within; *bahiḥ—*without; *ca—*also; *akhila-loka-pālakaiḥ—*by the leaders of the different planets, societies, kingdoms and so on; *adṛṣṭa-rūpaḥ—*not seen; *vicarasi—*You wander; *uru—*very great; *svanaḥ—*whose sounds (Vedic *mantras*); *saḥ—*He; *īśvaraḥ—*the supreme controller; *tvam—*You; *yaḥ—*who; *idam—*this; *vaśe—*under control; *anayat—*has brought; *nāmnā—*by different names like brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra; *yathā—*exactly like; *dārumayīm—*made of wood; *naraḥ—*a man; *striyam—*a doll.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, just as a puppeteer controls his dancing dolls and a husband controls his wife, Your Lordship controls all the living entities in the universe, such as the brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras. Although You are in everyone's heart as the supreme witness and commander and are outside everyone as well, the so-called leaders of societies, communities and countries cannot realize You. Only those who hear the vibration of the Vedic mantras can appreciate You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Urusvana* means the Vedas. This is a *bahuvrihi* compound. “You are the master who controls this universe*—*the universe in which human beings bearing the names *brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya* and *śūdra* are obliged to follow the do’s and dont’s enjoined in the Vedas.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“You move everywhere inside and outside. You are not known even to the Loka-pāla*s* \[masters of the planets\], let alone others. It is not that You do not exist, for the Vedas testify of Your existence. You can also be inferred as the independent principle because the universe is not without supervision.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

They praise Him as endowed with the gross and subtle forms of the universe and as having the ability to protect all. “The Loka-pāla*s* have also not seen Your form inside or outside. You are endowed with the great voice of the Vedas.” Who is this Īśvara? It is He, who controls all beings, who have different labels such as *brāhmaṇa* and others, as is enjoined in the Vedas. The controlling is only for the sake of protection, just as a man controls and makes a doll dance. By stating this controlling nature it is implied that He is the cause also. The controlling power is denoted by the word *sarvabhutantaratma*. That He is the cause is suggested by the word “eka.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

God is present in the living entities’ bodies and gives knowledge in the form of the puruṣa. The form which is outside the body is called *īśvara*. He gives the rewards of knowledge by that form.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *mukhyatama* is to be explained as shown earlier. He is called *sattva*, because He is the support of all such things.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“You move inside the body as *antaryāmī* and outside in the form of various incarnations. Yet Your form is not determined.” *Urusvana* = by whom the Vedas are pronounced.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The prayer is stated in three verses. The protection offered by Him in the form of *prana* is described in the first two*—“antah”* and “*bahis”* mean that He moves inside the body in the form of *prana* and outside the body in the form of *Vāyu* \[air\]. “You control the actions of the living entitles through the Vedas and make them move in hell and heaven as the magnet makes the iron filings move.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Urusvana* = Vedas. “Just as a person has a doll under his control, even so, You have the whole world under Your control. You are the Īśvara.”

### Text 27

*यं लोकपालाः किल मत्सरज्वरा*  
*हित्वा यतन्तोऽपि पृथक समेत्य च ।*  
*पातुं न शेकुर्द्विपदश्चतुष्पदः*  
*सरीसृपं स्थाणु यदत्र दृश्यते ॥२७॥*

*yaṁ loka-pālāḥ kila matsara-jvarā*  
*hitvā yatanto 'pi pṛthak sametya ca*  
*pātuṁ na śekur dvi-padaś catuṣ-padaḥ*  
*sarīsṛpaṁ sthāṇu yad atra dṛśyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yam—*whom (You); *loka-pālāḥ—*the great leaders of the universe, beginning with Lord Brahmā; *kila—*what to speak of others; *matsara-jvarāḥ—*who are suffering from the fever of envy; *hitvā—*leaving aside; *yatantaḥ—*endeavoring; *api—*although; *pṛthak—*separately; *sametya—*combined; *ca—*also; *pātum—*to protect; *na—*not; *śekuḥ—*able; *dvi-padaḥ—*two-legged; *catuḥ-padaḥ—*four-legged; *sarīsṛpam—*reptiles; *sthāṇu—*not moving; *yat—*whatever; *atra—*within this material world; *dṛśyate—*is visible.

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, from the great leaders of the universe, such as Lord Brahmā and other demigods, down to the political leaders of this world, all are envious of Your authority. Without Your help, however, they could neither separately nor concertedly maintain the innumerable living entities within the universe. You are actually the only maintainer of all human beings, of animals like cows and asses, and of plants, reptiles, birds, mountains and whatever else is visible within this material world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Lord might ask: “The *lokapalas* Indra and others control the universe, why do you praise Me?” This question is answered here: “These gods Indra and others are envious of one another. Without You they are not capable of protecting the universe consisting of moving and non-moving creatures. So You are the master.” They are envious of one another is stated in the *Upaniṣads* also.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Here it is said that this protection is unique and not found anywhere else. “The so-called Loka-pālas are envious of each other and unable to protect the world collectively or individually without You.” The world consists of moving and non-moving beings. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The Loka-pālas are regarded as *īśvaras*. How is it that in the previous verse it was said Hari is the only *īśvara*? The reply, Hari is the independent *īśvara* and the Loka-pālas are subordinated *īśvaras.* The Loka-pālas are unable to protect the two-legged and four-legged creatures collectively or individually, without You. They are envious of each other also. Here it should be noted that they exhibit this envy only to mislead the wicked people. As they are all *brahmajnanis* \[knowers of the spiritual truth\] and they do everything according to the dictates of Hari, they are not endowed with a natural envy. Only occasionally, when their minds are also soiled by demons, they compete with each other. But this is a rare phenomenon. By nature they do not envy each other.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śrīdhara has said the demigods have jealousy. The word “mutually” should be supplemented there.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Indra and others are competent to protect the world because they are Loka-pālas. Why should You approach me?” To this question of God it is replied that Indra and others are called Loka-pālas in name only, since they are unable to protect the world collectively or individually. Moreover they are envious of each other as is well-known in the *Upaniṣads*. So only You are to be approached.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“The Loka-pālas (guardians of the planets) are Loka-pālas in name only, for without You they cannot do anything collectively or individually.” They are envious of each other also as is stated in the *Upaniṣads*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“You are not known even by the gods, because they are envious of each other. Leaving You, they are not able to protect even the bipeds and quadrupeds here.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“Even if I move inside and outside, what is the benefit?” The reply: “The demigods are regarded to be protectors of the planets and rulers of the senses? Without *prana*, Brahmā and others are unable to protect anything collectively or individually. That *prana* is Yourself. You are the protector in the form of *prana*. So protection is Your excellence only. The other gods cannot protect as they are envious of one another.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The Loka-pālas Indra and others are said to be the guardians of the world under whose control it is. Then how is it said that Viṣṇu has the world under his control? This question is answered here that they are guardians not independently, but as per Viṣṇu's dictates. So Viṣṇu only is the *īśvara*. “The demigods are envious” means sometimes they appear to be envious of each other. They have no envy against Viṣṇu. They are great devotees of Viṣṇu. Sometimes, when their minds are soiled by the advent of *asuras* \[demons\], there they confront Viṣṇu for a short time and that too very rarely.”

“Without You, the Loka-pālas are unable to protect whatever is there in this world, the bipeds, quadrupeds and so on, individually or collectively. This is because they are not independent.”

### Text 28

*भवान् युगान्तार्णव ऊर्मिमालिनि*  
*क्षोणीमिमामोषधिवीरुधां निधिम् ।*  
*मया सहोरु क्रमतेऽज ओजसा*  
*तस्मै जगत्प्राणगणात्मने नम इति ॥२८॥*

*bhavān yugāntārṇava ūrmi-mālini*  
*kṣoṇīm imām oṣadhi-vīrudhāṁ nidhim*  
*mayā sahoru kramate 'ja ojasā*  
*tasmai jagat-prāṇa-gaṇātmane nama iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhavān—*Your Lordship; *yuga-anta-arṇave—*in the water of devastation at the end of the millennium; *ūrmi-mālini—*possessing rows of big waves; *kṣoṇīm—*the planet earth; *imām—*this; *oṣadhi-vīrudhām—*of all kinds of herbs and drugs; *nidhim—*the storehouse; *mayā—*me; *saha—*with; *uru—*great; *kramate—*You roamed; *aja—*O unborn one; *ojasā—*with speed; *tasmai—*unto Him; *jagat—*of the entire universe; *prāṇa-gaṇa-ātmane—*the ultimate source of life; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**O almighty Lord, at the end of the millennium this planet earth, which is the source of all kinds of herbs, drugs and trees, was inundated by water and drowned beneath the devastating waves. At that time, You protected me along with the earth and roamed the sea with great speed. O unborn one, You are the actual maintainer of the entire universal creation, and therefore You are the cause of all living entities. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The pastime of this *avatāra* \[incarnation\] is described. “You move in the ocean of deluge along with the earth and myself (Manu) by your own might. You are intent on protecting the earth, which is a receptacle of herbs, creepers and other plants. Obeisances to You who control the living beings.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“During a daily devastation of deluge, You bear myself and the earth (the cradle of all herbs and plants) and You move in the waters with enormous strength. Without depending upon anything else, You mightily do this only for protecting the earth. Obeisances to You, the soul of all living entities.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“You rescued me along with the earth in the ocean of devastation. You are the motivator of the entire world.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“You who are seen by devotion are visualized directly also. I myself, a mere imitation devotee, stand witness to this quality of Yours. You revel in the waters of deluge, bearing this earth and myself. You are the controller of all living beings in the world. Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“You are perceived by Your devotees—I, but an apology of a devotee, stand testimony to this fact. In the ocean of deluge, You saved me and the earth.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“To protect the earth along with me, You move with great strength. You are the receptacle of all living beings.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The story of the incarnation is narrated here. *Pranaganatmane* means *sutratmane* = to *sutra* (our obeisances are due is to be appended).

Here Manu’s *tamas* \[ignorance\] aspect should be noted by his abusing the Loka-pālas. Since he is a king, he is affected by *rajasa* \[passion\] also.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Jagatah* = of the living beings. *Niyanta* = Controller.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now he prays narrating the story of this incarnation. “During the previous deluge (the pralaya which takes place after each day of Brahmā), You bore me while I was in a boat. You rescued me along with the earth, the plants, etc. Your nature is to enliven the beings in this world.”

### Text 29

*हिरण्मयेऽपि भगवान्निवसति कूर्मतनुं बिभ्राणस्तस्य तत्प्रियतमां*  
*तनुमर्यमा सह वर्षपुरुषैः पितृगणाधिपतिरुपधावति मन्त्रमिमं चानुजपति*  
*॥२९॥*

*hiraṇmaye 'pi bhagavān nivasati kūrma-tanuṁ bibhrāṇas tasya tat*  
*priyatamāṁ tanum aryamā saha varṣa-puruṣaiḥ pitṛ-gaṇādhipatir*  
*upadhāvati mantram imaṁ cānujapati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*hiraṇmaye—*in Hiraṇmaya-varṣa; *api—*indeed; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *nivasati—*resides; *kūrma-tanum—*the body of a tortoise; *bibhrāṇaḥ—*manifesting; *tasya—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *tat—*that; *priya-tamām—*dearmost; *tanum—*body; *aryamā—*Aryamā, the chief resident of Hiraṇmaya-varṣa; *saha—*with; *varṣa-puruṣaiḥ—*the people of that tract of land; *pitṛ-gaṇa-adhipatiḥ—*who is the chief of the pitās; *upadhāvati—*worships in devotional service; *mantram—*hymn; *imam—*this; *ca—*also; *anujapati—*chants.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: In Hiraṇmaya-varṣa, the Supreme Lord, Viṣṇu, lives in the form of a tortoise \[kūrma-śarīra\]. This most dear and beautiful form is always worshiped there in devotional service by Aryamā, the chief resident of Hiraṇmaya-varṣa, along with the other inhabitants of that land. They chant the following hymns.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Tatpriyatama* means that dearest form.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tatpriyatama* is a *karmadharaya* compound. It means that dearest. *Varṣapuruṣa* means the denizens of Hiranyamaya-khaṇḍa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now the details of worship in Hiranmaya-varṣa are stated. Hari is there in the Kurma form. Aryama, the head of the groups of Pitrs performs the worship of Kurma along with others who live there. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Yuganta* means the end of a Manvantara. *Ksoni* means earth. She \[the earth personified\] has only taken the form of a boat as is said in the Eighth Canto.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

That dear form of His.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The worship in Hiranmaya-varṣa is stated here. “Kurma is predominant goodness mixed with passion (*rajas*).”

### Text 30

*ॐ नमो भगवते अकूपाराय सर्वसत्त्वगुणविशेषणायानुपलक्षितस्थानाय नमो*  
*वर्ष्मणे नमो भूम्ने नमो नमोऽवस्थानाय नमस्ते ॥३०॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate akūpārāya sarva-sattva-guṇa-viśeṣaṇāyānu-palakṣita-sthānāya namo varṣmaṇe namo bhūmne namo namo 'vasthānāya namas te.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O my Lord; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *akūpārāya—*in the form of a tortoise; *sarva-sattva-guṇa-viśeṣaṇāya—*whose form consists of śuddha-sattva, transcendental goodness; *anupalakṣita-sthānāya—*unto You, whose position is not discernible; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *varṣmaṇe—*unto You who, although the oldest, are unaffected by time; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *bhūmne—*to the great one who can go everywhere; *namaḥ namaḥ—*repeated obeisances; *avasthānāya—*the shelter of everything; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *te—*unto You.

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who have assumed the form of a tortoise. You are the reservoir of all transcendental qualities, and being entirely untinged by matter, You are perfectly situated in pure goodness. You move here and there in the water, but no one can discern Your position. Therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto You. Because of Your transcendental position, You are not limited by past, present and future. You are present everywhere as the shelter of all things, and therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto You again and again.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Akupara* = tortoise. He is replete with abundant transcendental qualities. His place is not fixed, as He is always moving. “Varsma” means He who showers His blessings. He is timeless. *Bhuman* means all-pervasive; *avasthana* means He is the substratum of everything. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Akupara* means Kurma. It literally means one who does not accept a small quantity of water as his abode. “All the qualities of living beings are directly or indirectly related to You. You are a reservoir of pure goodness. Your place in the ocean is not known to anyone because you live at the foot of Mandara.” *Avarshmane* = to you, devoid of a physical \[mundane\] frame. If it is read as *Varsmane* then it means “the best.” *Gariyase* means not bound by time. *Bhumne* means “to you endowed with greatness.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Akupara* etymologically means “one who does not go to a well.” That implies Kurma lives only in that great ocean. *Sattva* means valor. *Sarva sattva guṇa vishesanaya* means “to you endowed with the virtue of complete valor.” *Varsmane* means, “to you who showers your devotees with their desired objects.” *Pramanaya* means, “to you who explains the sacred scriptures.” *Avasthanaya* = to you who is the supporter of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“This, Your form of Kurma, You have shown to Your devotees, only out of kindness. *Ayathopalambhanat* means it is not possible to know You fully, because You are beyond the grasp of the mind and speech. “Obeisances to Him, who has forms which cannot be known and which have no number.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Akupara* = a tortoise. *Sarva* = entire. *Visesana* = form. The entire sattva \[pure goodness\] is His form. *Bhumne* = pervasive. *Avasthana* = support.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Akupara* literally means one who does not live in a well. Endowed with all virtues like knowledge and bliss. His place Vaikuṇṭha is not seen by all. This is what *anuplakshitasthanaya* means. Varsmane = to You having a very big size.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Sarva* = the entire *sattva guṇa* is under whose control. This adjective sets Him apart from all other beings. *Varsiyase* = to You, not bound by time.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

*Akuparaya* = to you who is of the nature of Kurma. *Varsiyase* = to you not bound by time. The repetition of the word “namah” is to show affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Bhagavate* = endowed with six virtues in spite of the tortoise form.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Akupana* means one who does not get into a well*—*because Kurma lives in the vast ocean. He leads the qualities of all living beings. That is why he is called s*arva-sattva-guṇa-visesana*. It may also mean, “endowed with all auspicious qualities and valor.” His place is not defined as He keeps on moving in the waters. *Avansmane* is the split*—*it means devoid of a material body. *Bhuyase* means having infinite forms. *Avasthana* means the support.

### Text 31

*यद्रूपमेतन्निजमाययार्पित*  
*मर्थस्वरूपं बहुरूपरूपितम् ।*  
*सङ्ख्या न यस्यास्त्ययथोपलम्भनात्*  
*तस्मै नमस्तेऽव्यपदेशरूपिणे ॥३१॥*

*yad-rūpam etan nija-māyayārpitam*  
*artha-svarūpaṁ bahu-rūpa-rūpitam*  
*saṅkhyā na yasyāsty ayathopalambhanāt*  
*tasmai namas te 'vyapadeśa-rūpiṇe*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yat—*of whom; *rūpam—*the form; *etat—*this; *nija-māyayā arpitam—*manifested by Your personal potency; *artha-svarūpam—*this entire visible cosmic manifestation; *bahu-rūpa-rūpitam—*manifested in various forms; *saṅkhyā—*the measurement; *na—*not; *yasya—*of which; *asti—*there is; *ayathā—*falsely; *upalambhanāt—*from perceiving; *tasmai—*unto Him (the Supreme Lord); *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *te—*unto You; *avyapadeśa—*cannot be ascertained by mental speculation; *rūpiṇe—*whose real form.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, this visible cosmic manifestation is a demonstration of Your own creative energy. Since the countless varieties of forms within this cosmic manifestation are simply a display of Your external energy, this virāṭ-rūpa \[universal body\] is not Your real form. Except for a devotee in transcendental consciousness, no one can perceive Your actual form. Therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“The earth with its numberless forms, which is perceivable by Your māyā \[illusion\] is not different from You.” It is because their perception is an illusion. No one can count the particles of water in a mirage. *Avyapadesheyarupine* means, “To Him who has the form of the world.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He is praised as having the universal form \[Visvarupa\] and the everlasting attributes. “Obeisances to You, whose body is this world.” *Vyavasayarupine* means the promulgator of knowledge or one who is of the nature of knowledge. Some read it as *vyapadesharupine* which means that this world, consisting of demigods and humans, is also His body. If it is read as *avyapadesharupine*, it means that His form cannot be fully explained. The world is described as composed of *prakṛti*, possessing many names and forms which have no number. It is perceived as different from Brahman. If the world appears in a way that is different from its nature, as stated above, it is only an illusion. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The supporting nature of Hari \[the Lord\] mentioned in the above verse is explained. This world which is real and which Hari has placed in Himself of His own accord is a great *pratima* (deity form) of Hari. The world is described as consisting of four types of living beings. It goes on changing every moment because of the evolution of *prakṛti* \[material nature\]. So the world is not the same the next moment. It goes on changing every moment because of the evolution of *prakṛti*. So the world is not the same the next moment. It has another form which is different from what was seen earlier. This is what “*ayatholambhana*” means and not that the perception of the world is an illusion. *Avyapadesharupine* means His forms cannot be fully explained. “Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The objects are only figments of *māyā* and do not exist in reality. It has the form of humans, birds, animals and so on. But there is no number. It is not possible to comprehend the various modes in which these various things exist. Even the human bodies are very different from each other and even inside the body there are so many peculiarities which are unique to each body. When this is the case with external objects what should be said about You? You cannot also be visualized as You are. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

“This universe is Your form designed by *māyā*. It is not Your own self.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The *viśvarūpa* of the Lord is described, so that one sheds one's envy and becomes devoted to the Lord’s service (*bhajana*). “The entire world consisting of *prithvi* \[mother earth\] and others is Your form. You have established this world by *māyā* which is controlled by You. There is no number for the things which are perceived in the world. And these things are Your forms. Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The prayer is stated: “Obeisances to You who has the forms of Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Nṛsiṁha and so on. How is it that Matsya and others are forms of God since they appear very much like us? The reply is that God has accepted the qualities to perform the various deeds and manifest those forms to us. Yet although His *saccidananda* \[consisting of eternity, knowledge and bliss\] virtues appear to be eclipsed by these qualities, His forms are supreme*—*they are not like us. Then why do they appear like us? The reply is, ‘it is God’s will.’ He does not want the unworthy to know His supreme nature. If He does not show this human nature/animal nature but shows His real self, then the Daityas will not be subjected to any illusion and there will be no pastime of confrontation and war. But in fact the characteristics of an ordinary living entity which appear in Him are false only. Just because His forms are seen it should not be decided that they are physical (products of *bhutas*, the elements). We see many forms in our dreams. But they are not physical (*bhautika*). It is just like that. So God takes many forms of His own free will and shows them according to the eligibility of the perceiver. That He takes *sattva* \[goodness\] and other *guṇas* in His forms and at the same time He is of the form of *sacchidananda* is borne out by Bhāgavata and other scriptures.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

His supporting nature is being described along with praise. By His own will He has placed the whole world within Himself. The world is described. It consists of the four kinds of living beings and matter. Even the living beings are infinite in number. It is said infinite living entities are there in an atomic space. The world does not stay the same always*—*it is always evolving. So it is different from what was seen earlier. It is not false but real and always changing. “Obeisances to You who bears such a world and who cannot be fully described by words.”

### Text 32

*जरायुजं स्वेदजमण्डजोद्भिदं*  
*चराचरं देवर्षिपितृभूतमैन्द्रियम् ।*  
*द्यौः खं क्षितिः शैलसरित्समुद्र*  
*द्वीपग्रहर्क्षेत्यभिधेय एकः ॥३२॥*

*jarāyujaṁ svedajam aṇḍajodbhidaṁ*  
*carācaraṁ devarṣi-pitṛ-bhūtam aindriyam*  
*dyauḥ khaṁ kṣitiḥ śaila-sarit-samudra-*  
*dvīpa-graharkṣety abhidheya ekaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*jarāyu-jam—*one born from a womb; *sveda-jam—*one born from perspiration; *aṇḍa-ja—*one born from an egg; *udbhidam—*one born of the earth; *cara-acaram—*the moving and the stationary; *deva—*the demigods; *ṛṣi—*the great sages; *pitṛ—*the inhabitants of Pitṛloka; *bhūtam—*the material elements air, fire, water and earth; *aindriyam—*all the senses; *dyauḥ—*the higher planetary systems; *kham—*the sky; *kṣitiḥ—*the earthly planets; *śaila—*the hills and mountains; *sarit—*the rivers; *samudra—*the oceans; *dvīpa—*the islands; *graha-ṛkṣa—*the stars and planets; *iti—*thus; *abhidheyaḥ—*to be variously named; *ekaḥ—*one.

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, You manifest Your different energies in countless forms: as living entities born from wombs, from eggs and from perspiration; as plants and trees that grow out of the earth; as all living entities, both moving and standing, including the demigods, the learned sages and the pitās; as outer space, as the higher planetary system containing the heavenly planets, and as the planet earth with its hills, rivers, seas, oceans and islands. Indeed, all the stars and planets are simply manifestations of Your different energies, but originally You are one without a second. Therefore there is nothing beyond You. This entire cosmic manifestation is, therefore, not false but is simply a temporary manifestation of Your inconceivable energy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here the non-difference of the various forms is stated. “The animals born in various manners, the islands, the mountains and rivers*—*everything is Yourself only. Nothing is different from You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Since You display the universal form (*viśvarūpa*) and You are infinite, You are denoted by whatever words there are in the world. Words such as ‘sky, heaven, ocean and so on’ denote You only. Dear God, this world is two fold as moving and non-moving. The non-moving is also four-fold (as stated earlier). This is Your excellent form. So You are denoted by all the words like ‘sky and so on.’ The name and form of everything ultimately end up in God as He is the soul of everything, having different names and forms. The words which signify the body ultimately signify the inner soul only. This is what is found in the usage of words like ‘cow, white and so on.’” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Hari \[the Supreme Lord\] is the inner dweller of everything. It should be always borne in mind that He is the main purport of all the words, because He possesses the attributes the words express in full. *Jarayuja* = human beings and other animals born with placentas. *Svedaja* = insects which are born out of perspiration. *Andaja* = birds born out of eggs. *Udbinda* = plants born of seeds. The words *deva*, *pitr*, *Indra* and so on, all mean Hari only in their primary sense*—*they convey others only in the secondary sense.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The universe is made of infinite different things. But since you are the cause of the universe, it is of one kind also, is what is stated here. It is supported by the sruti “This everything is *brahma*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

This universe with its infinite differences springs from You alone. So, in a sense, it is unique also. The Vedas have proclaimed the identity of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

All kinds of animals and all mountains and rivers are Yourself only. You have all names and all forms. The Vedas say, “All this is *brahma* only.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Here it is said that God is identical with everything in the world because the Vedas say, “everything is indeed Brahman.” “You are the one indicated by all the words because the forms they denote are identical with You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In the previous verse, the word “yadrupa” is interpreted as Viṣṇu, i.e. that Viṣṇu is the *antaryāmī* \[Lord in the heart\] of everything. It should be understood as postulating the identity of Brahman with the world. Sentient beings and insentient matter can never be identical. Here, it is stated that the words which signify the objects in the world and the human beings and demigods and so on, actually signify Him only in the primary sense. Because *dharma* or “aspect”, based on which a word signifies an object independently and abundantly, exist in Viṣṇu only.

### Text 33

*यस्मिन्नसङ्ख्येयविशेषनाम*  
*रूपाकृतौ कविभिः कल्पितेयम् ।*  
*सङ्ख्या यया तत्त्वदृशापनीयते*  
*तस्मै नमः साङ्ख्यनिदर्शनाय ते इति ॥३३॥*

*yasminn asaṅkhyeya-viśeṣa-nāma-*  
*rūpākṛtau kavibhiḥ kalpiteyam*  
*saṅkhyā yayā tattva-dṛśāpanīyate*  
*tasmai namaḥ sāṅkhya-nidarśanāya te iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yasmin—*in You (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); *asaṅkhyeya—*innumerable; *viśeṣa—*particular; *nāma—*names; *rūpa—*forms; *ākṛtau—*possessing bodily features; *kavibhiḥ—*by great learned persons; *kalpitā—*imagined; *iyam—*this; *saṅkhyā—*number; *yayā—*by whom; *tattva—*of the truth; *dṛśā—*by knowledge; *apanīyate—*is extracted; *tasmai—*unto Him; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *sāṅkhya-nidarśanāya—*who is the revealer of this numerical knowledge; *te—*unto You; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, Your name, form and bodily features are expanded in countless forms. No one can determine exactly how many forms exist, yet You Yourself, in Your incarnation as the learned scholar Kapiladeva, have analyzed the cosmic manifestation as containing twenty-four elements. Therefore if one is interested in Sāṅkhya philosophy, by which one can enumerate the different truths, he must hear it from You. Unfortunately, nondevotees simply count the different elements and remain ignorant of Your actual form. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Having narrated the existence of the world, here obeisances are offered to God negating the world. The number “twenty-four,” etc. which are ascribed by Kapila and sages, to the different principles, seem to be present in You. These are negated by the knowledge of Yourself, who is of the nature of pure knowledge. Obeisances to you, who is of the nature of the Sāṅkhya philosophy.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is stated here that the learned feel that the world is only temporal and so one should not be attached to it.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

All things in the world are His own energies (*vibhutis*). The earth and other principles are said to be twenty-four in number. Then how can there not be a number in the Lord’s energies? This objection is answered in this verse. *prakṛti* \[material nature\] and its derivatives are twenty-four in and twenty-five in number. But things that are seen here are not those pure principles, but the by-products of these principles. There is no counting the effects for they are infinite. Similarly, the living entities are also infinite. Both the living entity (*jīva*) and *jada* (matter) are the energies of God. So God’s energies’ forms have no number.
