The number “twenty-four” or “twenty-five” is put forward by Kapila and other sages for the easy understanding of the universe. It is not the final word. This concept of number recedes when *tattvajñāna* arises.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The innumerable attributes, names, forms and configurations of Hari have been mentioned in the Vedas. The number of “ten” as in the “ten *avatāras* \[incarnations\]” has been proved to be real by the seers. The ten incarnations are taken by Hari for the protection of the world. This number “ten” is not false*—*for *tattvajnanis* carefully teach their students about this number and the students on their part transfer the same knowledge to their students. *Viniyate* does not mean “is dispelled.” It is *vi* + *niyate*. *Vi* stands for “assiduously.” *Niyate* means “is transferred.” The word *vinaya* nowhere means “removal.” It should not be confused with “apanaya” which is used in that sense. In this construction, “tattvadrsha” means by the seers. This can be interpreted in another way taking “tattvadrsha” to mean “by correct knowledge.” The number “ten” and others are interpreted as “infinite” based on correct knowledge. “This is the only number ten. Ten tens make a hundred and ten hundreds make a thousand. Ten is the base number. It means ‘infinite.”’ The *Upaniṣads* say that God has this knowledge as He is intrinsically of the nature of knowledge. The word *sankhyanidarsanaya* is there. Sāṅkhya means correct knowledge of the living entity as well as his servant-master relationship with God. *Nidarsana* means one who manifests that. God takes many forms and clearly shows by His various acts that He is the master and the living entities are His servants. The correct knowledge of Brahman always shines. The correct knowledge of the living entities is eclipsed and shines only when there is Hari’s grace. Obeisances to You.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

How can various things be one? The reply is, as effects, they are many. Viewed from the point of view of the cause, they are one. There is a natural difference and non-difference between Brahman and the world. This is what is stated here. *Brahma* is the *ātmā*  of all. The multiplicity perceivable in Him is dispelled by the sight of oneness which is supported by the sight of oneness, which is supported by the Vedas. “All the world is just an imagination (*kalpita*) and that is why it has many names and forms. All these withdraw when the correct knowledge arises. You are of the nature of such knowledge. Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“If even the material world is Myself, then why does it not appear like that?” The reply is that without taking refuge in You, *māyā* does not recede and that is why it appears differently. For those who have taken refuge in You, and for that reason become blessed by You, the material energy appears identical with You. This is what is stated here. The numbers given by Kapila and others are offshoots of *māyā*. They appear as long as the living entities are shrouded by *māyā*. Once the covering of *māyā* is gone, the offshoots of *māyā* will also be gone and these numbers also disappear. The difference is but a product of *māyā*. As long as *māyā* is there, the world appears to be in duality. After the dissolution of *māyā*, however, the world appears as *brahma* \[spirit\] only.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

If His body is comprised of twenty-four principles of matter, then it would be finite. But the Vedas say He is infinite. How is this possible? The reply is given here. “There are innumerable forms and names of Yours, but Kapila and other sages have stated the aforesaid number. The numbers are only given for the less-intelligent people. They are not true, as Your powers are infinite. This number recedes when one gets the correct knowledge regarding Your relationship with nature and the living entity. Obeisances to one such as You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Previously by the word *bhuyase* it was stated that He has infinite forms. But the finite numbers like the ten incarnations, etc. are famous. Then how to justify His infinite forms? This objection is answered in this verse. The *jñānīs* have established as real the numbers “four, five, ten, one thousand,” etc. when describing Your forms. These numbers, which are also stated in the Vedas, will be properly understood only with the correct knowledge of the scriptures. For example, the number “ten” devotes infinity. This is clear in the *Upaniṣads*. So there is contradiction between the statements regarding the number of His forms. He is the propounder of *sankhya śāstra*, thus the *sankhya śāstra* is based on His knowledge. The knowledge of modern people could be based on *sankhya śāstra* propounded by a Kapila other than Viṣṇu.

### Text 34

*उत्तरेषु च कुरुषु भगवान् यज्ञपुरुषः कृतवराहरूप आस्ते तं तु देवी*  
*हैषा भूः सह कुरुभिरस्खलितभक्तियोगेनोपधावति इमां च परमामुपनिषद*  
*मावर्तयति ॥३४॥*

*uttareṣu ca kuruṣu bhagavān yajña-puruṣaḥ kṛta-varāha-rūpa āste taṁ tu devī haiṣā bhūḥ saha kurubhir askhalita-bhakti-yogenopadhāvati imāṁ ca paramām upaniṣadam āvartayati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*uttareṣu—*on the northern side; *ca—*also; *kuruṣu—*in the tract of land known as Kuru; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *yajña-puruṣaḥ—*who accepts all results of sacrifices; *kṛta-varāha-rūpaḥ—*having accepted the form of a boar; *āste—*exists eternally; *tam—*Him; *tu—*certainly; *devī—*the goddess; *ha—*certainly; *eṣā—*this; *bhūḥ—*planet earth; *saha—*along with; *kurubhiḥ—*the inhabitants of the land known as Kuru; *askhalita—*unfailing; *bhakti-yogena—*by devotional service; *upadhāvati—*worship; *imām—*this; *ca—*also; *paramām upaniṣadam—*the supreme Upaniṣad (the process by which one can approach the Lord); *āvartayati—*chants again and again for the purpose of practice.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Dear King, the Supreme Lord in His boar incarnation, who accepts all sacrificial offerings, lives in the northern part of Jambūdvīpa. There, in the tract of land known as Uttarakuru-varṣa, mother earth and all the other inhabitants worship Him with unfailing devotional service by repeatedly chanting the following Upaniṣad mantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The main explanation is, “This earth praises You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Here the worship and other things in Uttarakuru-varṣa are described. God is there in the Varaha \[boar\] form. *Yajña* is His body. He is worshipped through *yajñas* (sacrifices) and He is the one who gives the fruit of *yajña*. Bhudevi \[goddess of the earth\] worships Him here along with other people who reside there. She chants this *mantra* also. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is stated here that because the universe is transient, the learned are not attached to it. There are infinite names and forms here. The number is only a figment of *māyā*. It recedes by knowing You. Obeisances to You who is of the nature of knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

She chants this *mantra*. A *mantra* is one which should not fall on six ears.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

For these, Bhumi \[the goddess of the earth\] is the supervising deity, stationed there.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

A description of worship in Kuru-varṣa, in the extreme north is given here. Residing there is Lord Varaha who is of predominant *sattva* \[goodness\] mixed with *tamas* \[ignorance\].

### Text 35

*ॐ नमो भगवते मन्त्रतत्त्वलिङ्गाय यज्ञक्रतवे महाध्वरावयवाय महापुरुषाय*  
*नमः कर्मशुक्लाय त्रियुगाय नमस्ते ॥३५॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate mantra-tattva-liṅgāya yajña-kratave mahā-dhvarāvayavāya mahā-puruṣāya namaḥ karma-śuklāya tri-yugāya namas te.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O Lord; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *mantra-tattva-liṅgāya—*who is understood in truth by different mantras; *yajña—*in the form of animal sacrifices; *kratave—*and animal sacrifice; *mahā-dhvara—*great sacrifices; *avayavāya—*whose limbs and bodily parts; *mahā-puruṣāya—*unto the Supreme Person; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *karma-śuklāya—*who purifies the fruitive activities of the living entities; *tri-yugāya—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full with six opulences and who appears in three yugas (remaining concealed in the fourth yuga); *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *te—*unto You.

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, we offer our respectful obeisances unto You as the gigantic person. Simply by chanting mantras, we shall be able to understand You fully. You are yajña \[sacrifice\], and You are the kratu \[ritual\]. Therefore all the ritualistic ceremonies of sacrifice are part of Your transcendental body, and You are the only enjoyer of all sacrifices. Your form is composed of transcendental goodness. You are known as tri-yuga because in Kali-yuga You appeared as a concealed incarnation and because You always fully possess the three pairs of opulences.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Mantralinga* means known correctly by means of the *mantras*. *Yajña* is one where there is no sacrificial post. *Kratu* is one where there is a sacrificial post. Both are sacrifices only. All the great sacrifices are his limbs. *Sukla* means he is pure by his actions. He only performs the sacrifices. He is Triyuga because there are no sacrifices in the Kṛta-yuga. Or He is Triyuga because he is latent in the Kali-yuga.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Mantralinga* means what is told by the *mantras* is itself the body of God or Indra and others who are extolled in the *mantras* as the body of God. Sacrifices without *soma* juice are *yagas*. Sacrifices with *soma* juice are *kratus*. The identity which appears is because He is the inner-dweller of the sacrifices, worshipped through the sacrifices and the bestower of the results of the sacrifices. His limbs form the *yajña*. This means that the instruments used in the sacrifices are produced by His limbs. *Mahapurushaya* means one endowed with all the virtues enumerated in the *Puruṣa* Sukta. *Karmashuklaya* means His actions are pure*—*they are not the actions of living entities which draw them into *saṁsāra* repeatedly. The word  *niṣkriya* means that He is devoid of any *karma* which binds Him and not that He is absolutely devoid of all actions. *Triyugaya* means containing the three pairs of virtues. This is said to differentiate Him from the individual, tiny living entities. *Arunaya* means having crimson color. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

His form is known properly through Gāyatrī and other *mantras*. He is the propagator of yajñas without sacrificial post and *kratas* (with sacrificial post). *Karmasukla* means He sanctifies by His valor. *Triyuga* means He takes incarnations in the first three *yugas* \[ages\] only.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *mantras* are the forms of whom? There was no *yajña* in Kṛta-yuga, as the *Vedas* became classified into the three only in the Tretā-yuga. But the *Vedas* say that Hiraṇyagarbha performed a sacrifice in Kṛta-yuga, so the word “Triyuga” is interpreted in a different way. God is visible only in the first three yugas and not in Kali-yuga. That is why he is called Triyuga. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Triyuga* means three pairs, that is the six qualities of *aisvarya* \[wealth\] and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Tattvalinga* = that which shows his nature. “*Mantras* themselves reveal the true nature of Yours. You are of the form of *yajñas* and *kratas*. *Yajña* does not have a sacrificial post, but the *krata* has one. *Sukla* = shining. “You were perceived while lifting the earth from below. Even the living entities will get the six opulences by Your worship. The six qualities are what *bhaga* means. Obeisances to You.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

*Karma sukla* is a *bahuvrihi* compound meaning he who gives happiness as a reward of *karma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The *mantra* is stated. *Mantralinga* means it is the *mantra* which reveals the correct nature of Yourself. *Yajñas* have no sacrificial post and have no *soma* juice. *Kratas* have the sacrificial post and have *soma* Juice.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

He is called *yajña-puruṣa* because the accessories of *yajña* have come out of His limbs. He is the promulgator of *yajñas* and *krtas*, the former without a sacrificial post and the latter having one. He is the promulgator of and other auspicious actions. He chooses only the first three *yugas* for His incarnation.

### Text 36

*यस्य स्वरूपं कवयो विपश्चितो*  
*गुणेषु दारुष्विव जातवेदसम् ।*  
*मथ्नन्ति मथ्ना मनसा दिदृक्षवो*  
*गूढं क्रियार्थैर्नम ईरितात्मने ॥३६॥*

*yasya svarūpaṁ kavayo vipaścito*  
*guṇeṣu dāruṣv iva jāta-vedasam*  
*mathnanti mathnā manasā didṛkṣavo*  
*gūḍhaṁ kriyārthair nama īritātmane*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yasya—*whose; *sva-rūpam—*form; *kavayaḥ—*the greatly learned sages; *vipaścitaḥ—*expert in ascertaining the Absolute Truth; *guṇeṣu—*in the material manifestation, consisting of the three modes of nature; *dāruṣu—*in wood; *iva—*like; *jāta—*manifested; *vedasam—*fire; *mathnanti—*stir; *mathnā—*with a piece of wood used for producing fire; *manasā—*by the mind; *didṛkṣavaḥ—*who are inquisitive; *gūḍham—*hidden; *kriyā-arthaiḥ—*by fruitive activities and their results; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances; *īrita-ātmane—*unto the Lord, who is manifested.

**Перевод:**

**By manipulating a fire-generating stick, great saints and sages can bring forth the fire lying dormant within wood. In the same way, O Lord, those expert in understanding the Absolute Truth try to see You in everything—even in their own bodies. Yet you remain concealed. You are not to be understood by indirect processes involving mental or physical activities. Because You are self-manifested, only when You see that a person is wholeheartedly engaged in searching for You do You reveal Yourself. Therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The intelligent, learned people search for You in the body and senses. *Mathna* means by the mind which is the instrument in getting correct knowledge. They want to see You, hidden as You are in the various rites and their results. Your form becomes manifest when only they churn like this.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The learned perceive His form by turning their minds toward His names and forms again and again. This is what is known as churning, just as the fire in the wood manifests itself by churning, so does God manifest Himself by repeatedly placing one’s mind in Him. He is hidden in the Vedic rites and their results. He is visible only by devotion and *niṣkarma*. The *śravaṇa* (hearing) and *manana* (thinking) should be done with an attentive mind. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Bhudevi praises Him as the inner principle of everything and the worship done by aspirant devotees to Him as the *upasya* (object of worship). “You are the omniscient person who is concealed in everything perceivable. Thus, the living entities do not know You. The learned think about You with their discerning minds and find You different from the twenty-five principles, residing everywhere like fire in wood.” The analogy of fire suggests that He is the inner-most principle of everything. The words *didrksavah* and *kavayah* imply that worshipping Him is performed by those who aspire for salvation (*mumukshaupasyatva*). “Obeisances to You who is the controller of all living entities.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Mathna* = by the mind which is the instrument to thought and understanding. *Mathnanti* = churn. The churning here means the proper examination of the Vedic passages by considering their beginning, end, the logic contained there in, and so on.

Just as people desirous of fire find it concealed in the wood by churning the wood, even so the *jñānīs* examine the Vedic passages and find the real nature of *brahma* concealed in the living entities.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This number of the *jarayajas* and all is imaginary. It is stated for the sake of initial worship indicating that they are Your forms or Yourself. You are of the form of the philosophy of *sankhyas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Your real self is concealed in various actions and their fruits, so it does not shine in the heart of the living entities. It is concealed in the twenty-four forms of *prakṛti* and also in *jīva* \[living entity\]. The other twenty-eight principles are there and You are the twenty-ninth. They search for You there and find you as fire is found in the wood, by churning. You are also perceivable by the mind’s churning according to Vedic knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The worship of God is by three methods; *karma, jñāna* and *bhakti*. Bhumi offers her obeisances in the next three stanzas by using all three of them. *Yoga* is also included in the *karma* category. The method of *yoga* is described: “With a controlled mind they search for You, hidden in the body and ultimately they find You by Your grace. God does not appear to those with a disturbed mind. But for those who control their mind and concentrate on God only, he reveals Himself. Why do all people not take resort to mental contemplation? It is because they do not know how to do it, for they do not have that wisdom and because they are interested in external objects only.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Obeisances are offered remembering His *sarvantaratmatva* (the characteristic of dwelling in the hearts of all) and *mumukshaupasyatva* (characteristic of being worshipped by those who aspire for liberation). *Kavayah* = those who have the correct knowledge. *Gunesu* means in the elements associated with the bodies of demigods which are the products of material qualities. You are concealed by the actions and their reactions. You are not perceived by the living entities even though You are present with them. The learned regard You as different from the twenty-five principles.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The *jñānīs* examine the *Vedas* and find You concealed in their own hearts. They study the *Vedas* properly with an efficient mind, get knowledge, meditate and then find You within themselves. Just as fire hidden in the wood is manifested by churning. Here it is the mind that does the churning. Obeisances to You who is denoted by the words Indra, Agni and so on, which are useful in the performance of a sacrifice.

### Text 37

*द्रव्यक्रियाहेत्वयनेशकर्तृभि*  
*र्मायागुणैर्वस्तुनिरीक्षितात्मने ।*  
*अन्वीक्षयाङ्गातिशयात्मबुद्धिभि*  
*र्निरस्तमायाकृतये नमो नमः ॥३७॥*

*dravya-kriyā-hetv-ayaneśa-kartṛbhir*  
*māyā-guṇair vastu-nirīkṣitātmane*  
*anvīkṣayāṅgātiśayātma-buddhibhir*  
*nirasta-māyākṛtaye namo namaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*dravya—*by the objects of sense enjoyment; *kriyā—*the activities of the senses; *hetu—*the predominating deities of sensory activities; *ayana—*the body; *īśa—*the predominating time; *kartṛbhiḥ—*by false egotism; *māyā-guṇaiḥ—*by the modes of material nature; *vastu—*as a fact; *nirīkṣita—*being observed; *ātmane—*unto the Supreme Soul; *anvīkṣayā—*by careful consideration; *aṅga—*by the limbs of yogic practice; *atiśaya-ātma-buddhibhiḥ—*by those whose intelligence has become fixed; *nirasta—*completely freed from; *māyā—*the illusory energy; *ākṛtaye—*whose form; *namaḥ—*all respectful obeisances; *namaḥ—*respectful obeisances.

**Перевод:**

**The objects of material enjoyment \[sound, form, taste, touch and smell\], the activities of the senses, the controllers of sensory activities \[the demigods\], the body, eternal time and egotism are all creations of Your material energy. Those whose intelligence has become fixed by perfect execution of mystic yoga can see that all these elements result from the actions of Your external energy. They can also see Your transcendental form as Supersoul in the background of everything. Therefore I repeatedly offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Bhudevi praises Varaha showing the manner of churning referred to above. *Dravya* = objects. *Kriya* = the operation of the senses. *Heta* = the ruling God. *Ayana* = the body. *Isa* = time. *Karta* = the ego. These are by-products of *māyā*, which cause God to be taken as just another object. Obeisances to You. *Anviksiki* = thinking. *Anga* means the limbs like *yama*, *niyama* and so on. Those who think about You with sharpened intellect know that Your form is not endowed with any derivative of *māyā*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

She offers her obeisances again explaining the principles stated in the previous verse. “Obeisances to You, who are beyond the influence of *māyā* and who are very well understood by those with excellent minds. You are perceived in this body only, which is a configuration of the five elements, the five motor organs, the five sensory organs and the mind. So it is clear that the word “*guṇa*” in the previous verse does not denote only the body, but it also denotes demigods where God is perceived by the *jñānīs*.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Many seers have seen God in their hearts. They have seen the form of God whose reflection they are. It is stated here that one must go forward in this direction, without any hesitation. The word “Isa” is to be constructed separately with all the preceding words. *Dravyesa* is Śiva. *Krisyesa* is Garuḍa. *Hetvisa* is Brahmā. *Ayanesa* is Vāyu. *Ayana* means support. These are the agents of all the activities of the world. “All these people consider You as real and endowed with all virtues. They are also not independent in acquiring this knowledge.” It is only by His grace that they know this. *Māyā* means desire. *Māyā guṇa* means when they are in accordance with God’s desire, they know*—*otherwise they do not. They have excellent intellect which is capable of receiving His knowledge as no one else can. Their knowledge is also very special, uncommon. They perceive Him directly as endowed with a non-material divine form and free from all defects perpetually. So the analogy of fire should not be taken in the sense that God is also materialistic like Agni. It should only be taken in the sense that what is concealed earlier becomes manifest later by proper effort.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The pure *jīva* principle is to be known through the *upalaksanas* (features that do not form a part of the particular thing), Dhruva and others. You are perceivable in the living entity. *Māyā* has been repelled by *anviksa* (real knowledge) by Yourself.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The churning is possible if only the subtle and gross bodies which are products of *māyā* are there. And God becomes visible only after this churning, is what is stated here. *Kriya* = the operation of the senses. *Hetu* = the deity. *Ayana* = body. *Isa* = time. *Karta* = *ahamkara* \[false ego\]. You are perceived by constantly dwelling on Your pastimes with the help of all the above mentioned principles. Obeisances to such a one.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He is visible only after the above-mentioned churning done by those endowed with subtle and gross bodies. Such bodies are products of *māyā*. His form is visualized as the truth after hearing and meditating with an attentive mind. Even the form which is visualized is of the nature of bliss. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The above verse is explained: “Those who are endowed with good intellect coupled with austerities churn the twenty-five principles (including the *jīva*) and the three modes of nature and find You, the twenty-ninth. Obeisances to You. *Dravya* is the five elements. *Kriya* = the five motor organs; *hetu* = *prakṛti* \[material nature\]*, mahattattva* \[total material substance\]*, ahamkara* \[false ego\] and the five objects of sensory organs (eight in all). *Ayana* = the sensory organs. *Isa* = mind. *Kanta* = living entity (*jīva*). *Māyā-guṇa* = *sattva, rajas, tamas*. But you are *aprakrta* = different from *prakṛti* and it's offshoots.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The worship in *jñāna marga* is visualizing that Brahman is devoid of any contact with *māyā*. Stating this she offers her obeisances. *Nirastamayakrtaye* means the forms which are products of *māyā* have been cast away by Him. “To You, my obeisances are due. *Anviksa* is *vicara* (discussing and justifying in one’s own mind); *anga* means *yama, nigama*, and so on. The intellect will be sharpened by these two and will be competent to imbibe wisdom there.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The mode of contemplation is stated as she offers her obeisances. *Anga* is the mode of address for a dear one. “Those endowed with good intellect and thinking power regard You as very different from this body which is a mixture of five elements along with the sensory and motor organs. Being different, You are above all the effects of material nature (*prakṛti*). Obeisances to You.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Those who are endowed with extraordinary intellect see you as You are and that is also by Your grace only. Who are these intelligent persons? They are Śiva, the lord of matter, Garuḍa, the lord of actions, Brahmā, the master of causes and Vāyu the master of supports. The word “*Isa*” is to be construed separately with each of the preceding words. “Obeisances to You who has no *prakṛti* (material form).” The repetition of the word “*namah*” is to show regard and affection. It is said in *Brahma Tarka,* "Sankara is the ruler of matter. Garuḍa is the ruler of all actions, Brahmā is the ruler of all causes and Vāyu is the ruler of all supports."

### Text 38

*करोति विश्वस्थितिसंयमोदयं*  
*यस्येप्सितं नेप्सितमीक्षितुर्गुणैः ।*  
*माया यथायो भ्रमते तदाश्रयं*  
*ग्राव्णो नमस्ते गुणकर्मसाक्षिणे ॥३८॥*

*karoti viśva-sthiti-saṁyamodayaṁ*  
*yasyepsitaṁ nepsitam īkṣitur guṇaiḥ*  
*māyā yathāyo bhramate tad-āśrayaṁ*  
*grāvṇo namas te guṇa-karma-sākṣiṇe*

**Пословный перевод:**

*karoti—*performing; *viśva—*of the universe; *sthiti—*the maintenance; *saṁyama—*winding up; *udayam—*creation; *yasya—*of whom; *īpsitam—*desired; *na—*not; *īpsitam—*desired; *īkṣituḥ—*of the one glancing over; *guṇaiḥ—*with the modes of material nature; *māyā—*the material energy; *yathā—*as much as; *ayaḥ—*iron; *bhramate—*moves; *tat-āśrayam—*placed near that; *grāvṇaḥ—*a magnetic stone; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *te—*unto You; *guṇa-karma-sākṣiṇe—*the witness of the actions and reactions of material nature.

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, You do not desire the creation, maintenance or annihilation of this material world, but You perform these activities for the conditioned souls by Your creative energy. Exactly as a piece of iron moves under the influence of a lodestone, inert matter moves when You glance over the total material energy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In the previous verse obeisances were offered to the attributeless Brahman. Here He is praised as the qualified God. All His actions are meant for the welfare of the living entities and not for Himself. *Māyā* itself executes the creation, sustenance and destruction of the universe. Although it is non-sentient matter, it is capable of doing the above operations because of the presence of God in it*—*just as iron filings move under the influence of a magnet. This is the example cited to justify the activity of *prakṛti* (or *māyā*). “Obeisances to You who is the perceiver of all *guṇas, kriyas, jīvas* and their *adrstas.*

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In the previous verse it was said that God has dispelled all the effects of *māyā* from Himself. To justify that, Bhudevi praises Him saying that *māyā* is under His control. “You perform the creation and so on of the world for the sake of the *jīvas* \[living entities\] and not for Your own self. You give them the body, sense and mind so that they are able to achieve all the four goals of life. Thus, the creation and so on is desired by You for this reason, out of kindness for the *jīvas*. You make *māyā* act as you desire just as a magnet makes iron filings move. As the body moves as per the dictates of the soul, so *māyā*, as Your body, acts under Your order. You install Your power in her so that she can create and so on.” Creation is God’s feature. How can it be ascribed to *māyā*? The reply is Brahmā does the creation, to be more precise, the Lord present in *Brahmā* does the creation. While doing so, he uses *rajoguṇa* \[the mode of passion\] which is a constituent of *māyā*. This is why it is said māyā creates. This statement however, only applies in a secondary sense. It was stated that the creation is not for His personal happiness but only to bless the living entities. Since it is only due to creation that the living entities are subjected to misery, how can such a statement be made? The reply is that He is the perceiver of all the qualities (*guṇas*) of nature (*prakṛti*) and all the actions (*karma*) of the living entities (*jīvas*). He gives pain or pleasure to the *jīvas* according to their previous *karma*. So He is not to be blamed as prejudiced. God creates the universe and provides every *jīva* with a body and mind. Externally, He gives the *Vedas* revealing His own nature, the nature of the universe and the duties of the *jīvas*. Then the *jīvas* act according to their previous *karma* and perform good or bad deeds. Demigods give only the commensurate fruit of the *karma* performed by the living entities (*jīvas*). So He is not biased.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Let Brahmā and His followers act according to Hari’s wish. But Lakṣmī is the creator. Let her create on her own. To this question the reply given is that even Lakṣmī is not independent. She acts by the grace of Hari only. This is what is stated here. Lakṣmī carries out the act of creation, etc. of the universe only by Hari’s grace. Hari desires this universe to be created for the benefit of the living entities (*jīvas*) and not for the benefit of Himself. Just as iron filings move under the influence of a magnet, Lakṣmī also acts stirred by Hari’s graceful glance at her. “Obeisances to You, the perceiver of all the attributes and actions of the living entities.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

For the establishment of the universe, He deploys His natural power, which controls *māyā*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Stated here is: “The universe is not Your form, rather it is the form of *māyā*. The universe is desired by You for the sake of the *jīvas* and not for Yourself. You create the universe with the modes of material nature (*māyā guṇas*). Even though it is insentient, it is capable of action because of Your presence, just as iron filings move under the influence of a magnet. Obeisances to You, the perceiver of the modes of nature (*guṇas*) and *karma* (actions) of the living entities (*jīvas*).

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

She offers her obeisances to the Lord stating that the universe is a product of *māyā*. *Ayaskanta* means a magnet.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Thus three entities are discussed: matter, living entities (*jīvas*) and *brahma*. According to the Sāṅkhyas, mother material nature (*prakṛti*) is different from *brahma* and she is the creator. This concept is refuted here and *brahma* is established as the creator. *Māyā* is only a *śakti* \[energy\] of the creator *brahma*, who perceives (iksita). Matter cannot perceive. In fact, there is no sentient or non-sentient entity apart from *brahma*. “You create the world for those that want it and for the liberation for those who aspire for it. You do not create for Your own sake. You are the perceiver of the qualities and actions of all *jīvas*. Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Matter, *jīvas* and Brahman have been enumerated. The theistic Sāṅkhyas say that *prakṛti* is different from *brahma* and *prakṛti* \[material nature\] itself is the creator. This notion is refuted here and instead *brahma* is established as the creator of the universe. The creator has a desire which *māyā* does not have*—*this is stated in the *Vedas*, i.e. *māyā* is only *brahma’s* power and not an entity is different from Brahman. There is nothing in this world which is not Brahman. This *māyā’s* existence and operation are controlled by *brahma*, like the movement of iron pieces are controlled by a magnet. This world is desired by God for the sake of *jīvas* and not for His own sake. For those who want to enjoy, the Lord creates the world to give them the opportunity to do so while those aspiring for liberation, can be liberated. He is the perceiver of every aspect of *jīva* and jada (matter). “Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

It was said that he has shed all the ill-effects of *māyā*. To justify this, here it is stated that *māyā* is under His control. “*Māyā* operates under Your control. Just as iron filings move under the influence of a magnet, so does material energy (*prakṛti*) act under your influence, in Your favor. You are only the observer of *jīvas*, their actions (*karma*), *māyā* and its by-products. So You are not affected by them. Obeisances to You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Let Brahmā and others act under Hari’s control*—*however Lakṣmī is the creator. Let her create independently. If this proposition is taken, the reply is: “Even Lakṣmī is not independent. She acts under Hari’s control only.” This is what is stated in this verse.

Lakṣmī brings about the creation, sustenance and destruction of this universe. But yet she does not see Him as she wants to see. Even from the point of view of Lakṣmī there is much desired to be known in Hari. What is to be known still remains. This is because she is not omniscient like Viṣṇu. The verse explains this as justification for her taking support in Viṣṇu.

She also acts under His control and support like iron filings under the influence of a magnet. I offer my obeisances to You, who is like an unshakable solid rock supporting everything. Hari knows His own virtues in full although Lakṣmī does not. He is the perceiver of Himself and of the modes of nature (*guṇas*), the actions of the goddess of fortune (Ramā) and others. He is the *saksin* \[witness\]. This justifies his supreme position over all others.

### Text 39

*प्रमथ्य दैत्यं प्रतिवारणं मृधे*  
*यो मां रसाया जगदादिसूकरः ।*  
*कृत्वाग्रदंष्ट्रे निरगादुदन्वतः*  
*क्रीडन्निवेभः प्रणतास्मि तं विभुमिति ॥३९॥*

*pramathya daityaṁ prativāraṇaṁ mṛdhe*  
*yo māṁ rasāyā jagad-ādi-sūkaraḥ*  
*kṛtvāgra-daṁṣṭre niragād udanvataḥ*  
*krīḍann ivebhaḥ praṇatāsmi taṁ vibhum iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*pramathya—*after killing; *daityam—*the demon; *prativāraṇam—*most formidable opponent; *mṛdhe—*in the fight; *yaḥ—*He who; *mām—*me (the earth); *rasāyāḥ—*fallen to the bottom of the universe; *jagat—*in this material world; *ādi-sūkaraḥ—*the original form of a boar; *kṛtvā—*keeping it; *agra-daṁṣṭre—*on the end of the tusk; *niragāt—*came out of the water; *udanvataḥ—*from the Garbhodaka Ocean; *krīḍan—*playing; *iva—*like; *ibhaḥ—*elephant; *praṇatā asmi—*I bow down; *tam—*to Him; *vibhum—*the Supreme Lord; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, as the original boar within this universe, You fought and killed the great demon Hiraṇyakṣa. Then You lifted me \[the earth\] from the Garbhodaka Ocean on the end of Your tusk, exactly as a sporting elephant plucks a lotus flower from the water. I bow down before You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The story of the incarnation is narrated here. You placed me on your tusk and came up from the bottom of the ocean of deluge, like an elephant from a pond. I offer my obeisances to You who killed the demon as he attacked like an elephant.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

She states the story of this incarnation and offers her obeisances to Him. “You brought me up from Rasātala, placing me on Your tusk. While doing so, You killed the demon who confronted You like an opposing elephant. You killed him (Hiraṇyākṣa) effortlessly. My obeisances to You.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“He placed me on His tusk and brought me up from Rasātala and killed Hiraṇyākṣa who opposed Him like a warring elephant in the battle that ensued. He is the Varaha who is the cause of the universe. I offer my obeisances to Him.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

She prays for His kindness as she narrates the story of this incarnation. *Prativarana* = like an opposing elephant. *Rasayah* = from Garbhodaka. *Jagadadih* = the cause of the world. *Udanvatah* = in the waters of deluge.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

She narrates the story of the incarnation mentioning his extraordinary kindness shown to her. The word *sūkara* etymologically means one who expertly lifts the earth, etc. The prefix *su* has become *sū* because of what is technically called “nipatana” meaning “he utters the sound *shūm* as he roars”, and that is why He is called *Sūkara*. “From Rasātala” means from the fetal waters of the *brahmāṇḍa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“I offer my obeisances to You, who brought me up from Rasātala, placing me on your canine teeth and killing the demon who opposed You like an elephant.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“I offer my obeisances to You who lifted me up from the Rasātala and while in the process killed Hiraṇyākṣa, who confronted You like a warring elephant.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

She offers her obeisances, narrating the story of the present incarnation. “You placed me on Your tusk and came up from Rasātala in the ocean. Being confronted by Hiraṇyākṣa, You killed him with ease like a wild elephant. I offer my obeisances to You, endowed with extraordinary powers.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now she offers her obeisances stating the story of this particular incarnation. “You are the cause of this universe and You took the form of a boar. You placed me on Your tusk and came up from Rasātala in the waters. You killed Hiraṇyākṣa who confronted you like another elephant. It was only your pastime, an effortless act of Yours. You are endowed with such extraordinary power. I offer my obeisances unto You.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas’* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Eighteenth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The prayers Offered to the Lord by the Residents of Jambūdvīpa.”

## Chapter 19 - A Description of the island of Jambūdvīpa

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*किम्पुरुषे वर्षे भगवन्तमादिपुरुषं लक्ष्मणाग्रजं सीताभिरामं रामं तच्चरण*  
*सन्निकर्षाभिरतः परमभागवतो हनुमान् सह किम्पुरुषैरविरतभक्तिरुपास्ते ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kimpuruṣe varṣe bhagavantam ādi-puruṣaṁ lakṣmaṇāgrajaṁ sītābhirāmaṁ rāmaṁ tac-caraṇa-sannikarṣābhirataḥ parama-bhāgavato hanumān saha kimpuruṣair avirata-bhaktir upāste.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—*Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued to speak; *kimpuruṣe varṣe—*the tract of land known as Kimpuruṣa; *bhagavantam—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *ādi-puruṣam—*the original cause of all causes; *lakṣmaṇa-agra-jam—*the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa; *sītā-abhirāmam—*who is very pleasing to mother Sītā, or who is the husband of Sītādevī; *rāmam—*Lord Rāmacandra; *tat-caraṇa-sannikarṣa-abhirataḥ—*one always engaged in service at the lotus feet of Lord Rāmacandra; *parama-bhāgavataḥ—*the great devotee celebrated throughout the universe; *hanumān—*His Grace Hanumānjī; *saha—*with; *kimpuruṣaiḥ—*the inhabitants of the tract of land known as Kimpuruṣa; *avirata—*continuous; *bhaktiḥ—*who possesses devotional service; *upāste—*worships.

**Перевод:**

**Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, in Kimpuruṣa-varṣa the great devotee Hanumān is always engaged with the inhabitants of that land in devotional service to Lord Rāmacandra, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa and dear husband of Sītādevī.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

By saying, “of God, his master,” it is suggested that Hanumān is not interested in the stories of other incarnations as is Nārada and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Abhirama = handsome.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the position in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, the important aspects like worship and other things in Kimpuruṣa and Bhārata-varṣa are described in this chapter. Also the greatness of Bhārata-varṣa is described.

First, the form of God and the *mantra* used for worship and meditation in Kimpuruṣa are stated. Rāma, Dasaratha’s son, the creator of the universe, Laksmana’s elder brother and the worthy husband of Sītā , is worshipped. The etymology of the word Rāma is stated, “Because the yogis rejoice in His lotus feet, He is called Rāma.” The word *Rāma* is derived from the root *ram* which means to enjoy. The great *bhāgavata* Hanumān is engrossed in the meditation of Rāma’s lotus feet. *Sannikarsa* means proximity, which is of the nature of bhajan. Along with those who live in Kimpuruṣa, Hanumān worships Rāma with uninterrupted devotion.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Sītā-abhirāmam* means, “He gives joy to Sītā .”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In this Nineteenth Chapter, the position of the worshipped and the worshippers in Kimpuruṣa and Bhārata are narrated.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Worship of God in Kimpuruṣa-varṣa is described. Along with those who live in Kimpuruṣa, Hanumān worships Rāma with uninterrupted devotion. The worshipped is Adipuruṣa, the cause of all causes. He is Lakṣmaṇa’s brother and Sītā ’s husband. Hanumān worships only for the sake of service of God. He has no other intentions because he is a *parama-bhāgavata*. He has devotion which is never hampered.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The nature of worship, the form of God worshipped, the worshiper (upasaka), the *mantra* and the prayer (stotra) are described here. Along with those who live in Kimpuruṣa, Hanumān worships Rāma with uninterrupted devotion. Rāma is the creator of the Universe, Lakṣmaṇa’s brother, Dasaratha’s son and a fitting husband of Sītā . Hanumān is a great devotee whose devotion is never hampered.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Sītā-abhirāmam* means, “He gives happiness to Sītā.” It is not that He derives happiness from Sītā.

The mode of his worship is described. He listens to the story of his master Rāma along with Arshtishena, a chief of the Gandharvas. He also chants the following *mantra***:**

Arshtishana is a famous person living in Kimpuruṣa. Some say he is a sage—others say he is a Gandharva. Along with other people in Kimpuruṣa, he worships Rāma.

He is the master and God. His story.

### Text 3

*ॐ नमो भगवते उत्तमश्लोकाय नम आर्यलक्षणशीलव्रताय नम*  
*उपशिक्षितात्मन उपासितलोकाय नमः साधुवादनिकषणाय नमो ब्रह्मण्य*  
*देवाय महापुरुषाय महाराजाय नम इति ॥३॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate uttamaślokāya nama ārya-lakṣaṇa-śīla-vratāya nama upaśikṣitātmana upāsita-lokāya namaḥ sādhu-vāda-nikaṣaṇāya namo brahmaṇya-devāya mahā-puruṣāya mahā-rājāya nama iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O my Lord; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *uttama-ślokāya—*who is always worshiped with selected verses; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *ārya-lakṣaṇa-śīla-vratāya—*who possesses all the good qualities of advanced personalities; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *upaśikṣita-ātmane—*unto You whose senses are under control; *upāsita-lokāya—*who is always remembered and worshiped by all the different classes of living entities; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *sādhu-vāda-nikaṣaṇāya—*to the Lord, who is like a stone for examining all the good qualities of a sādhu; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *brahmaṇya-devāya—*who is worshiped by the most qualified *brāhmaṇas*; *mahā-puruṣāya—*unto the Supreme Lord, who is worshiped by the puruṣa-sūkta because of being the cause of this material creation; *mahā-rājāya—*unto the supreme king, or the king of all kings; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Let me please Your Lordship by chanting the bīja-mantra oṁkāra. I wish to offer my respectful obeisances unto the Personality of Godhead, who is the best among the most highly elevated personalities. Your Lordship is the reservoir of all the good qualities of Āryans, people who are advanced. Your character and behavior are always consistent, and You always control Your senses and mind. Acting just like an ordinary human being, You exhibit exemplary character to teach others how to behave. There is a touchstone that can be used to examine the quality of gold, but You are like a touchstone that can verify all good qualities. You are worshiped by brāhmaṇas who are the foremost of all devotees. You, the Supreme Person, are the King of kings, and therefore I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He who is endowed with noble signs, character and vows: *upashikshitatmane* = to him whose mind is controlled. He has followed the etiquette of the world. *Sadhuvada* means, fame as a noble person. He is the touchstone \[a stone which transforms objects it touches\] which determines another’s fame as a noble person. Actually, He is the ultimate limit of goodness.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The meaning of omkara (praṇava) is as narrated earlier. *Uttamshloka* means, “one who is praised by the great Brahmā and others.” Or, it can also mean, “A person whose form has no limit.” He has the noble signs and character of great people. His mind is controlled. He respects the world. He is a touchstone of all nobleness. He is always favorable to *brāhmaṇas*. He has said, “Dear Sītā, I will discard My life, I may even discard you, but I will never go back on the words given to *brāhmaṇas*.” “He shines by His own brightness” or, “His knowledge is produced only by the *Vedas*.” He is the emperor extolled in the *Puruṣa-sūkta* \[Vedic prayers from the Ṛg *mantra*\] Our obeisances to Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

He is endowed with the features and actions of Arya Hari. He creates the universe. His feature and nature are free of blemish. *Upashritama* means, “He has been the support of all living entities,” or it can also mean “for whose sake the living entities perform worship.” He puts an end to disputes between good people. \[Note from the translator: While all others have taken the reading as nikasha to mean “touchstone,” Vijayadhvaja’s reading is *nikarshana* meaning, “decider or a person who puts an end to something and hence the different interpretation.”\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *bhagavate* indicates His lordship (i.e., control of everything). The word *uttamshloka* signifies His sweetness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Whose signs of the *dvaja* \[flag\] and *vajra* \[thunderbolt\] on the soles of the feet are respected by everyone. *Features* means long arms and other such things. *Sila* means the courageous disposition of a hero. *Vrata* means observing *dharma*. Although worshipped by Brahmā and other demigods, He was of the opinion that even a *dhobi* \[washerman\] should be pleased by Him. This is his display of “current practice” (*lokachara*). He is the touchstone of good conduct.

*Sadhuvada nikashana* means virtues like truthfulness and kindness were embellished by Him. Just as shining gold shines even better after rubbing against a touchstone, so the virtues of others themselves become embellished by coming in contact with Rāma.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Aryani* = respectable by everyone. *Lakshana* means the signs of the *dvaja* \[flag\] and *vajra* \[thunderbolt\] on the soles of the feet, etc. *Sila* means noble character. *Vrata* means, “*his addiction to dharma*.” Rāma has all these. *Upashikshitatma* means, “He has been instructed by *brāhmaṇa* and teachers. Although worshipped by Brahmā and other demigods, He was of the opinion that even a *dhobi* \[washerman\] should be pleased by Him. This is his display of “current practice” (*lokachara*). He is the touchstone of good conduct. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

His signs, character and vows are all noble. *Upashikshitama* means, “He is to be worshipped by well educated souls.” *Upasitaloka* means, “for the sake of teaching *dharma*, He followed the ways of the world.” *Sadhuvadanikashana* means, “He is the crest jewel among dharmic people \[those who abide by Vedic principles\].”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“Obeisances to God, the emperor,” is the construction of the sentence. His being God as well as an emperor are justified by the epithets used here. *Uttamshloka* means who is glorified by excellent prayers. It may also mean whose fame removes ignorance. *Aryalakshanasheelavrata* means, “He who is endowed with the signs, character and vows, etc. of noble persons.” *Upashikshitatma* means one whose mind is withdrawn from the objects of senses or one who is emulated by others. A second meaning is, “His grief and lamentation are present because He followed the ways of the world.” A third meaning of the same word is, “His grief and lamentations are not actual.”

*Sadhuvadanikashana* means He is the touchstone \[a stone which transforms objects it touches\] which determines another’s fame as a noble person. Virtues come to Him and are embellished themselves. *Brahmanyadeva* means, “He is fond of *brāhmaṇa* and is dear to them” or *brahmanya* means, “established in Brahman i.e., free from the material modes of nature.” *Deva* means *līlā* \[pastime\], which is His nature. The word Mahapuruṣa indicates all these qualities.

He is the Purushottama. By displaying grief and lamentation, Rāma appears to be composed of *rajo guṇa* \[the mode of passion\] mixed with *sattva guṇa* \[the mode of goodness\], however an incarnation of God enters into the modes of nature as fire into an iron ball. Although He appears to be affected by material nature, His bliss, pastimes and Godhood are unaffected.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The repetition of the word “namah” is intended to offer obeisances for every virtue present in Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Ārya-lakṣaṇa-śīla-vratāya* means “He who is endowed with the signs, character and vows, etc. of noble persons.” *Upashritaloka* means the *loka* \[world\] has taken refuge in Him. *Upasitaloka* means the world (*loka*) performs worship for His sake. He is the touchstone of sadhuvada*—*the very limit of noble behavior.

### Text 4

*यत्तद्विशुद्धानुभवमात्रमेकं*  
*स्वतेजसा ध्वस्तगुणव्यवस्थम् ।*  
*प्रत्यक् प्रशान्तं सुधियोपलम्भनं*  
*ह्यनामरूपं निरहं प्रपद्ये ॥४॥*

*yat tad viśuddhānubhava-mātram ekaṁ*  
*sva-tejasā dhvasta-guṇa-vyavastham*  
*pratyak praśāntaṁ sudhiyopalambhanaṁ*  
*hy anāma-rūpaṁ nirahaṁ prapadye*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yat—*which; *tat—*to that supreme truth; *viśuddha—*transcendentally pure, without contamination by material nature; *anubhava—*experience; *mātram—*that sac-cid-ānanda transcendental body; *ekam—*the one; *sva-tejasā—*by His own spiritual potency; *dhvasta—*vanquished; *guṇa-vyavastham—*the influence of the modes of material nature; *pratyak—*transcendental, not to be seen with material eyes; *praśāntam—*undisturbed by material agitation; *sudhiyā—*by Kṛṣṇa consciousness, or purified consciousness, uncontaminated by material desires, fruitive activities and speculative philosophy; *upalambhanam—*who can be achieved; *hi—*indeed; *anāma-rūpam—*without a material name and form; *niraham—*without a material ego; *prapadye—*let me offer my respectful obeisances.

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, whose pure form \[sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha\] is uncontaminated by the modes of material nature, can be perceived by pure consciousness. In the Vedānta He is described as being one without a second. Because of His spiritual potency, He is untouched by the contamination of material nature, and because He is not subjected to material vision, He is known as transcendental. He has no material activities, nor has He a material form or name. Only in pure consciousness, Kṛṣṇa consciousness, can one perceive the transcendental form of the Lord. Let us be firmly fixed at the lotus feet of Lord Rāmacandra, and let us offer our respectful obeisances unto those transcendental lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Rāma is saluted in His absolute form. “I take refuge in the single principle propounded in the *Vedas*.” How is He? He is of the nature of pure knowledge. The reason for His purity is the tranquility. The reason for that is that He has vanquished the various states of *guṇas* \[qualities\] like wakefulness, dreaming and sleep. He is only knowledge because He is beyond that which is known because He is devoid of any mundane name or form. Actually He is the *jīva* \[individual soul\] Himself, but He is different from the *jīvas* because He has no *ahamkara* \[false ego\].

If it be objected that Śrī Rāma does not appear to have the nature stated, the reply is, only wise men know him correctly, not all.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Stating that He is different from *prakṛti* (matter) and *puruṣa* (the enjoyer, i.e. the living entity), he offers his obeisances to this Rāma form of the Lord. Rāma is free from desires. He is of the nature of knowledge. He is not mixed with matter. By His *dharmabhutajñāna* \[a technical term of Rāmanuja philosophy*—Note from the translator*\] which is non-different from Him, He is free of desires, hatred and origin, etc. By this epithet, it is implied that He is different from the *jīva* \[living entity\], who is bound by *prakṛti* \[material nature\] and its attendants. The *jīva* is not free from the material qualities (*guṇas*)*—*for he is subjected to hunger and thirst. Rāma is different from the liberated souls also because they were once bound by *prakṛti* \[matter\], but He was never bound. The word *visuddha* implies that although He is of the nature of knowledge, that knowledge is not received by the senses. He is the cause of the universe and because he has no material name or form, He does not become transformed like clay. Although He is identified by names and forms of those that reside in Him, He, Himself has no name or form. Such is the nature of Parabrahma Narahari who is praised in the Upanishads. The word *prashantha* signifies difference from liberated souls. But the word Nrhari is used to signify the difference from those who are always liberated. There is another reading for Nrhari. It is Niraham which means He is different from the *jīva* \[living entity\], who is stuck in ahamkara, a product of the material energy (*prakṛti*). *ātmā* is also called aham \[the conception of I-ness\] but here it is not *ātmā* . It is God who is devoid of the transformations of *prakṛti* and *puruṣa* and that is why he is Niraham. It should be interpreted in this way. I take refuge in Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The main point of the sentence is “I take refuge in You.” “You are the nature of pure knowledge.” This means that He is endowed with sensory organs which are also of the nature of knowledge and which are not mixed with *prakṛti* or its products. By Your own might You have vanquished the three *guṇas—sattva* and others, or the three states of waking, dream and sleep. Pratyak stationed facing the *jīva*. Prashanta means full of joy. Sudhiyopalambhana means he is cognized by a good intellect. He is different from all other objects in the world and so he is Anamarupa. That is why he has no ego.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Some people do not believe that Rāma is Parabrahma as he does not bear the *śaṅkha* and *chakra* and does not have Garuḍa as his vehicle. Let them have their doubts*—*but I for one, regard Him as *parabrahma*. He says, “I take refuge in Him who is free from the influence of *māyā*.” The objection may be raised that the living entity (*jīva*) is also like this in his pure form, so why take refuge in Rāma only?” The objection is answered: “By his own power, Rāma has repelled the power of *māyā*. That is why He is imperceptible, but for those endowed with good intellect, He appears as described above.” It may also be interpreted as, “I take refuge in Him, shedding my false ego.”.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Let those who doubt Rāma is not Parabrahma because He does not wield the *śaṅkha* and *Chakra*, continue to have their doubt. But I for one, worship Rāma as *parabrahma*, as I perceive Him like that. Devoid of any relation with *māyā*, He is of the nature of knowledge. This is because He is Anamarupa bereft of popular name and form. He cannot be perceived without the purity of mind.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Śrī Rāma is saluted in His absolute form. “I take refuge in the single principle propounded in the *Vedas*.” *Eka* means having no equal or superior. He is endowed with name and form, which give pure knowledge to the suppliants. He is free from desire and other such blemishes by His own power. He gives peace to the *jīvas* and is perceived by people with noble intellect. He is devoid of physical form and name. *Niraham* means not becoming proud due to possessing extraordinary qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The prayer is given in five verses. Rāma is saluted in His absolute form. “I take refuge in the single principle propounded in the *Vedas*.” He is of the nature of pure knowledge.

The word vishuddha differentiates this knowledge from the one rising from the senses. Prashanta means free from lust and other desires. The reason is that He has driven away the *guṇas* by His own power. This means that a person who experiences the three states of wakefulness, dream and sleep (which are an outcome of the modes of material nature) is subjected to desires. Where there are no material qualities, there can be no desire. Why does He not have the waking state? The answer is given by the word niraham*—*He is unaffected by ahamkara, which causes the three states. This is explained by the word *pratyag—*He is the inner-dweller. He perceives the hearts of the living entities (antaḥ-karaṇa) but does not impose Himself upon them. But if it be objected that Śrī Rāma does not appear like this, the word *sudhiyopalamtham* gives the reply: “He may not be known like this to ordinary people*—*rather only to those with good intellect.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Rāma is different from *prakṛti* and *puruṣa*. Having stated this by the words of the above *mantra*, he offers his obeisances to Rāma. *Vishuddhanubhavamatram* means endowed with senses, which are not produced by material nature (*prakṛti*); He has driven away the three material modes of nature and the three states of wakefulness, dream and sleep by His own power. *Pratyak* means stationed facing the *jīva*. He is Anamarupa, devoid of *prakṛti*k color and name (or form and name). Niraham means free from ego. Eva means unparalleled. I take refuge in Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In the *mantra* it is said that Rāma is known by the word “bhagavate.” That is clarified here. “I take refuge in Parabrahma which is one i.e., devoid of duality. “How is he? He is of the nature of pure knowledge. Kevala means His form is without any blemish. By His own power, He is transcendental to the three *guṇas* and the three states of sleep, etc. Pratyak means He is the inner -dweller of living entity prashanta means he is full of happiness. He is Anamarupa, because words cannot describe him in full and he has no material color. He is Niraham, has no false ego.

### Text 5

*मर्त्यावतारस्त्विह मर्त्यशिक्षणं*  
*रक्षोवधायैव न केवलं विभोः ।*  
*कुतोऽन्यथा स्याद्रमतः स्व आत्मनः*  
*सीताकृतानि व्यसनानीश्वरस्य ॥५॥*

*martyāvatāras tv iha martya-śikṣaṇaṁ*  
*rakṣo-vadhāyaiva na kevalaṁ vibhoḥ*  
*kuto 'nyathā syād ramataḥ sva ātmanaḥ*  
*sītā-kṛtāni vyasanānīśvarasya*

**Пословный перевод:**

*martya—*as a human being; *avatāraḥ—*whose incarnation; *tu—*however; *iha—*in the material world; *martya-śikṣaṇam—*for teaching all the living entities, especially human beings; *rakṣaḥ-vadhāya—*to kill the demon Rāvaṇa; *eva—*certainly; *na—*not; *kevalam—*only; *vibhoḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *kutaḥ—*from where; *anyathā—*otherwise; *syāt—*there would be; *ramataḥ—*of one enjoying; *sve—*in Himself; *ātmanaḥ—*the spiritual identity of the universe; *sītā—*of the wife of Lord Rāmacandra; *kṛtāni—*appearing due to the separation; *vyasanāni—*all the miseries; *īśvarasya—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**It was ordained that Rāvaṇa, chief of the Rākṣasas, could not be killed by anyone but a man, and for this reason Lord Rāmacandra, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, appeared in the form of a human being. Lord Rāmacandra's mission, however, was not only to kill Rāvaṇa but also to teach mortal beings that material happiness centered around sex life or centered around one's wife is the cause of many miseries. He is the self-sufficient Supreme Personality of Godhead, and nothing is lamentable for Him. Therefore why else could He be subjected to tribulations by the kidnapping of mother Sītā?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Then why was he born as Dasaratha's son? It is because Rāvaṇa could not be killed by any one other than a human being. Not merely that*—*He wanted to teach to the world that attachment to a woman brings only grief. Otherwise how can there be grief due to separation from Sītā for He who is immersed in His own bliss? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Jīva Gosvāmī and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

How can Rāma be Anamarupa when He is endowed with the name and form of a human being? If a question be asked like this, the reply is given here: “Rāma is the incarnation of Nārāyaṇa in this world. Incarnation means taking another form without losing any aspect of His nature. So it is a form of His supreme blissful nature resembling a human being. The purpose of an incarnation is to instruct people, protect *dharma* \[religious occupational duties\] and deliverance of the pious. Why should we not say that the purpose is to kill Rāvaṇa? The reply is that the killing of Rāvaṇa is not the main purpose. It is said in Gītā, “Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bhārata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself.” Teaching the people is illustrated in this incarnation also. If we do not accept this purpose, and hold that He came only for killing Rāvaṇa, it is incorrect because He is the *antaryāmī* \[supersoul dwelling in the hearts of everyone\] of even Rāvaṇa. How then could He allow Rāvaṇa to abduct His wife? This proves two things: first, that He does not have any grief because of separation from Sītā or anything else. He always enjoys His own bliss. If separation would hamper His bliss, He would not have allowed Rāvaṇa to do this act. The second thing is that the grief that he displayed when separated from Sītā is not genuine*—*it is just a show intended to teach the people that over-attachment to women invariably brings grief. The *Vedas* propound that He is not attached to anything lest His blissful nature would be at stake.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

How can Śrī Rāma be of the nature of pure knowledge and bliss when He is subjected to grief by separation of Sītā and thus goes in search of her? This doubt is cleared here: “It is not for the sake of killing Rāvaṇa only that this incarnation was taken*—*teaching human beings values such as obeying elders, not forsaking the loyal followers and those in distress. This he did by obeying Dasaratha, going to the forest, giving Vibhishana the kingdom of Lanka, and so on. How can there be grief due to separation from Sītā for He who is immersed in His own bliss?

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Śrī Rāma’s form is the hue of tender grass. He has His Svarupa Shakti \[Sītā \] which is different from māyā. By His Swarupa Shakti He has driven away the *māyā* Shakti consisting of three *guṇas* \[modes of material nature\]. Prashanta means free from all troubles. The reason for His being described as mere consciousness is that He is different from what is perceived or that He is imperceptible. This is because He has no material name and form as do other objects. In the Śruti \[*Vedas*\], *ātmā Shabda* denotes His his own parts (the living entities or *jīva* Shakti). “He has entered the world in the *ātmā* form,” means that in this form, He is attached to the three elements by which He brings out the name and form of all objects. Living entities have this misconception, but the supersoul (antaryāmī), although stationed within the *jīva*, is free from this misconception. The supersoul has no form or name unlike His *jīva* part. If there is no false ego, then He cannot create the world and cannot say, “I will create the names and forms.” But if it be objected that Śrī Rāma’s form is not visualized like this by all, the reply is that He is known properly by people with good intellect and not all.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Then how does He reveal Himself in this world? It is not merely for the killing of Rāvaṇa that He manifested Himself in the world. Instructing human beings is also His intention. Human beings are of two kinds, the pious and the devoted. It is to instruct them the true nature of *dharma* and love by his own example, that He manifested himself in this world. Otherwise how could there be grief for Him by the separation from Sītā as He is always enjoying His own bliss? It is only to instruct that a devoted wife should not be neglected and the grief that comes in the process of looking after her should be borne. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Then why did He manifest in the world, if He is of the nature as described above? The reply is, that although there is another purpose, the main purpose is to show His leelamadhurya (sweet pastimes) to His devotees.

Humans are of two kinds, those endowed with *dharma* and those endowed with bhakti and thus the Lord manifested to instruct them in *dharma* and bhakti. Otherwise what is His incarnation for? He also wanted to teach the world that a devoted wife should not be forsaken and any misery which comes along with her should be borne bravely. That is why He displayed grief not actually present in Him. Sītā is His own shakti and so his *ātmā* rāma (self-satisfied) nature is not hampered even if he enjoys the company of Sītā. If Sītā is his own Shakti, how could there be separation from her? The reply is, the supreme entity has two modes: cit power and vrtti. The first form is of the nature of bliss and excellence or even of the nature of only bliss. It is called Parameswara. The second is called Bhakti and it has four modes Dashyabhava (servitude), Sakhibhava (friendship), Pitradi Bhava (parenthood) and Preyas bhava (conjugal love) These modes come out of the Supreme and reenter. Other than this, there is no separation from Sītā. Those who do not know this, are unable to explain the grief of the Rāma and Kṛṣṇa incarnations, for in reality grief is also an expression of bliss. Others say that he showed the grief to instruct the living entities.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

His incarnation among mortals is not only for the sake of killing Rāvaṇa, but it is for teaching noble behavior to the human beings also. Otherwise how can there be any grief for Him who is always immersed in his infinite bliss?

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

If Rāma were God, then He could have killed Rāvaṇa by just His wish. Where was the necessity to take a human form to do such a trivial task? It is trivial for one who creates infinite *crores* of Brahmāṇḍas \[universes\] and destroys them. If an objection be raised like this the reply is: “Rāma did not take this incarnation for just killing Rāvaṇa. Instructing the people by His own example was also His intention which could not have been otherwise. A devoted wife should not be abandoned. The grief on her score should be borne. A devoted person should not be let down. The order of elders is necessarily to be carried out. These were what He wanted to teach by His own example. If it was not for that, how can there be grief to Him who is always enjoying bliss?

### Text 6

*न वै स आत्मात्मवतां सुहृत्तमः*  
*सक्तस्त्रिलोक्यां भगवान् वासुदेवः ।*  
*न स्त्रीकृतं कश्मलमश्नुवीत*  
*न लक्ष्मणं चापि विहातुमर्हति ॥६॥*

*na vai sa ātmātmavatāṁ suhṛttamaḥ*  
*saktas tri-lokyāṁ bhagavān vāsudevaḥ*  
*na strī-kṛtaṁ kaśmalam aśnuvīta*  
*na lakṣmaṇaṁ cāpi vihātum arhati*

**Пословный перевод:**

*na—*not; *vai—*indeed; *saḥ—*He; *ātmā—*the Supreme Soul; *ātmavatām—*of the self-realized souls; *suhṛt-tamaḥ—*the best friend; *saktaḥ—*attached; *tri-lokyām—*to anything within the three worlds; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *vāsudevaḥ—*the all-pervading Lord; *na—*not; *strī-kṛtam—*obtained because of His wife; *kaśmalam—*sufferings of separation; *aśnuvīta—*would obtain; *na—*not; *lakṣmaṇam—*His younger brother Lakṣmaṇa; *ca—*also; *api—*certainly; *vihātum—*to give up; *arhati—*be able.

**Перевод:**

**Since Lord Śrī Rāmacandra is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, He is not attached to anything in this material world. He is the most beloved Supersoul of all self-realized souls, and He is their very intimate friend. He is full of all opulences. Therefore He could not possibly have suffered because of separation from His wife, nor could He have given up His wife and Lakṣmaṇa, His younger brother. To give up either would have been absolutely impossible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is argued that since He has no attachment to any object He is not eligible to be subjected to grief. He is not attached to anything in the three worlds because He is the dearest of the courageous. He cannot get grief on account of a woman. Had He any attachment, He would not have abandoned Lakṣmaṇa. He was about to kill Lakṣmaṇa, when he violated His order in the end, but as per Vasista’s wish, He left him. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is stated here that all this is possible because of His virtues such as truthfulness, attachment to His devotees, etc. He is not attached to anything as He is the infinite Vāsudeva Himself and the support of everything. He is very dear to those who always think about Him as their Lord. So He does not lament like others on account of Sītā, nor does He discard Lakṣmaṇa. Ultimately, it is only to instruct the ways of the world that He gave some punishment as it were. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Vaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The same thing is argued in this verse. Rāma, the incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, is supremely dear to Sanaka and others, of purest mind and renunciation of all worldly activities. He is stationed in those who love Him so much and He also shows love and affection towards them. He is Bhagavān, which means endowed with the knowledge, power, strength, supremacy and so on. He is Vāsudeva who is everywhere but unaffected by the imperfections of this world. He has accepted everything as an appendage to Him \[this is a technical term used in Rāmanuja philosophy*—*Note from the translator\]. He cannot grieve over separation from a woman if it were not to instruct people. He would not have attained grief, blissful as He is, and He would not have abandoned Lakṣmaṇa. Lakṣmaṇa is an incarnation of Śesa and served Rāma without caring for food and sleep all through his life. This is evident from the verses in the Rāmayana. Lakṣmaṇa is as dear to Him as is Sītā , who is Lakṣmī herself. His vow is that He will never forsake anyone who approaches Him with affection. That being the case, how can He abandon Laksman who served him extraordinaly? That is why it should be said that the purpose of incarnation is to teach people. Rāvaṇa’s killing is not the main purpose because the killing could have been done otherwise. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He was eagerly waiting for His union with Lakṣmaṇa in heaven. His form is still present in Kimpuruṣa-varṣa, the place from which He and Sītā, departed to His abode.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The same thing is explained again. He is not attached to anything in the three worlds. He is Vāsudeva himself. He does not get any grief from Shurpanaka’s act which ultimately separated Sītā from Him, nor does He forsake Lakṣmaṇa. When He was about to kill Lakṣmaṇa for violating his order, at the behest of Vasista, he withdrew and forsook Him. This story is famous in Rāmayana. All this is only imitation.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He is not attached to anything and therefore His grief is only an offshoot of attachment*—*He cannot have any grief. Only for the sake of instructing people he imitated the ways of the grief-stricken *jīvas*. He is not attached to anything in the three worlds, because he is Bhagavān replete with all the things He desires. He cannot be sad on account of a woman. He is Vāsudeva which means He pervades all things and is all things. He will not abandon Lakṣmaṇa at anytime. The Lakṣmaṇa episode is narrated by all the commentators. Because He is God and not answerable to anyone and as the well-wisher of all the creatures, He does all this to instruct people. He does not derive any benefit from such actions.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He is most dear to Sanaka and other sages who have shuned all activities of the cycle of birth and death (*saṁsāra*). He is always purna, full with whatever is needed. There is no dearth of anything in Him. He is not attached to anything in the three worlds and thus not subjected to grief on account of the separation from Sītā . He does not abandon either Sītā or Lakṣmaṇa.

### Text 7

*न जन्म नूनं महतो न सौभगं*  
*न वाङ् न बुद्धिर्नाकृतिस्तोषहेतुः ।*  
*तैर्यद्विसृष्टानपि नो वनौकस*  
*श्चकार सख्ये बत लक्ष्मणाग्रजः ॥७॥*

*na janma nūnaṁ mahato na saubhagaṁ*  
*na vāṅ na buddhir nākṛtis toṣa-hetuḥ*  
*tair yad visṛṣṭān api no vanaukasaś*  
*cakāra sakhye bata lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*na—*not; *janma—*birth in a very polished, aristocratic family; *nūnam—*indeed; *mahataḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *na—*nor; *saubhagam—*great fortune; *na—*nor; *vāk—*an elegant manner of speaking; *na—*nor; *buddhiḥ—*sharpness of intelligence; *na—*not; *ākṛtiḥ—*features of the body; *toṣa-hetuḥ—*the cause of pleasure to the Lord; *taiḥ—*by all those above-mentioned qualities; *yat—*because; *visṛṣṭān—*rejected; *api—*although; *naḥ—*us; *vana-okasaḥ—*the inhabitants of the forest; *cakāra—*accepted; *sakhye—*in friendship; *bata—*alas; *lakṣmaṇa-agra-jaḥ—*Lord Śrī Rāmacandra, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa.

**Перевод:**

**One cannot establish a friendship with the Supreme Lord Rāmacandra on the basis of material qualities such as one's birth in an aristocratic family, one's personal beauty, one's eloquence, one's sharp intelligence or one's superior race or nation. None of these qualifications is actually a prerequisite for friendship with Lord Śrī Rāmacandra. Otherwise how is it possible that although we uncivilized inhabitants of the forest have not taken noble births, although we have no physical beauty and although we cannot speak like gentlemen, Lord Rāmacandra has nevertheless accepted us as friends?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Śrī Rāma should be worshipped by all. He is not pleased by one’s noble birth, etc.*—*rather He is only pleased by devotion. Thus, He blessed us, although we are forest dwellers and not born in a great family.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Rāma is inclined to shower His grace upon low caste, sinful persons. Birth in a *brāhmaṇa* family does not please Him nor do bodily beauty, education or high intellect, for He has blessed even the animals. We are animals \[these are the words of the monkeys*—*Note from the translator\] bereft of any noble birth or education or anything. We live in forests. It is astonishing that Rāma who always enjoys the company of such a blessed and accomplished soul as Laksman accepted us as His friends (and not as his servants). Not caring for birth and other things, He blessed us just because we took shelter in Him. Such is the greatness of Rāma. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

He is Ishwara and the master of all great souls. He has no grief. The *Vedas* says He is always free from anxiety and other defects. Out of compassion towards His devotees only did He take the incarnation of Rāma. Nothing is contradictory in His nature. Devotion and pure knowledge are the only things that please Him and not birth in a noble family and such things. “Dear Arshtisena, this is proved by the fact that He has treated us as his friends even though we are born as animals (forest-dwelling monkeys).” This is indicated by the word “api.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

His kindness is causeless. He made Lakṣmaṇa His servant, although he is endowed with all excellences like noble birth and other things, yet He treated us as His friends, although we are devoid of any noble birth or handsomeness, etc. This is kindness and nothing else.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Rāma is very kind. It is astonishing that Rāma, who always enjoys the company of such a blessed and accomplished soul as Laksman, accepted us as his friends (and not as his servants). Where else do we find this kindness?

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Saubhaga* = handsomeness; *Akrti* = caste, *Viershta* = bereft of.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Sincere devotion only makes one eligible to worship Him, the ocean of causeless compassion. It is not that only highly placed and noble persons should worship Rāma. It is astonishing that Rāma, the elder brother, always enjoys the company of such a blessed and accomplished soul as Laksman as a servant, accepted us as His friends (and not as his servants). It is not that He befriended us to help search for Sītā . The master of infinite *brahmāṇḍa* \[universes\] does not require the help of anyone else for anything.
