Out of compassion only He gave us an opportunity to serve Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Having is an animal such as yourself eligible to receive His mercy? For this question, Hanumān replies: “Noble birth and all are not what Rāma is pleased with. *Anga* is an address meaning, “Dear Arshtisena.” *Visrshtan* means, “Created by Him in various manners as monkeys, bears and so on.” So when Rāma Himself has shown His grace, noble birth and other things are of no consequence.

### Text 8

*सुरोऽसुरो वाप्यथ वानरो नरः*  
*सर्वात्मना यः सुकृतज्ञमुत्तमम् ।*  
*भजेत रामं मनुजाकृतिं हरिं*  
*य उत्तराननयत्कोसलान्दिवमिति ॥८॥*

*suro 'suro vāpy atha vānaro naraḥ*  
*sarvātmanā yaḥ sukṛtajñam uttamam*  
*bhajeta rāmaṁ manujākṛtiṁ hariṁ*  
*ya uttarān anayat kosalān divam iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*suraḥ—*demigod; *asuraḥ—*demon; *vā api—*or; *atha—*therefore; *vā—*or; *anaraḥ—*other than a human being (bird, beast, animal and so on); *naraḥ—*a human being; *sarva-ātmanā—*wholeheartedly; *yaḥ—*who; *su-kṛtajñam—*easily made grateful; *uttamam—*most highly elevated; *bhajeta—*should worship; *rāmam—*Lord Rāmacandra; *manuja-ākṛtim—*appearing as a human being; *harim—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *yaḥ—*who; *uttarān—*of northern India; *anayat—*brought back; *kosalān—*the inhabitants of Kosala-deśa, Ayodhyā; *divam—*to the spiritual world, Vaikuṇṭha; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, whether one is a demigod or a demon, a man or a creature other than man, such as a beast or bird, everyone should worship Lord Rāmacandra, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who appears on this earth just like a human being. There is no need of great austerities or penances to worship the Lord, for He accepts even a small service offered by His devotee. Thus He is satisfied, and as soon as He is satisfied, the devotee is successful. Indeed, Lord Śrī Rāmacandra brought all the devotees of Ayodhyā back home, back to Godhead \[Vaikuṇṭha\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Therefore, whether Rāma is a God or not, all should praise and worship Him in every possible way. Rāma rewards even the lowest devotee. *Uttaran Kosalan* = the denizens of Ayodhya.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Therefore, among incarnations, the very kind Rāma should be worshipped and praised by all, including the demigods.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Therefore, anyone who devotes Himself to Śrī Rāma fully will be accepted and blessed by Him. An instance is quoted to prove this. He took not merely the human beings of Uttara Kosala (i.e., Ayodhya) with Him when He went to His permanent abode, but He also took the creepers, trees and animals also with Him. He does not bless considering one’s knowledge and piety, etc. rather He simply uses some pretext to bestow blessings upon His devotees. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Therefore, whether he be a demigod (sura) or a demon (Asura) or a human being or a monkey, one should worship Śrī Rāma with devotion and knowledge. Not all demons are bad. There are asuras like Prahlāda and Bali, who are great devotees of Viṣṇu. The ill fate of Asuras mentioned in the Śāstras is related to those who have no devotion to Viṣṇu and hate him. Those Asuras who are devoted to Viṣṇu are surely blessed by Him. It is not that only the original form in Vaikuṇṭha is capable of giving *mokṣa*, even the incarnation form is also capable of doing that. This was demonstrated by Rāma when He took all the human beings and creatures of Ayodhya with him back to His permanent abode. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

To justify what has been stated earlier, His supreme compassion is described in the next two verses. Though we are devoid of noble birth, beauty and high caste, Rāma was pleased with us for our attempting to search for Sītā . It is astonishing that Rāma, who always enjoys the company of such a blessed and accomplished soul as His brother Lakṣmaṇa, accepted us as His friends (and not as his servants). How astonishing. Therefore, whether he be a demigod (sura) or a demon (Asura) or a human being or a monkey, one should worship Śrī Rāma with devotion and knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Therefore, whether Rāma is God or not, everyone should worship Him only. *Uttara Kosalam* means the denizens of Ayodhya.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He will not forsake those who serve Him.

### Text 9

*भारतेऽपि वर्षे भगवान्नरनारायणाख्य आकल्पान्तमुपचितधर्मज्ञानवैराग्यै*  
*श्वर्योपशमोपरमात्मोपलम्भनमनुग्रहायात्मवतामनुकम्पया तपोऽव्यक्तगतिश्चरति*  
*॥९॥*

*bhārate 'pi varṣe bhagavān nara-nārāyaṇākhya ākalpāntam upacita-dharma-jñāna-vairāgyaiśvaryopaśamoparamātmopalambhanam anugrahāyātmavatām anukampayā tapo 'vyakta-gatiś carati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhārate—*in Bhārata; *api—*also; *varṣe—*the tract of land; *bhagavān—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *nara-nārāyaṇa-ākhyaḥ—*known as Nara-Nārāyaṇa; *ā-kalpa-antam—*up to the end of the millennium; *upacita—*increasing; *dharma—*religion; *jñāna—*knowledge; *vairāgya—*renunciation or nonattachment; *aiśvarya—*mystic opulences; *upaśama—*control of the senses; *uparama—*freedom from false ego; *ātma-upalambhanam—*self-realization; *anugrahāya—*to show favor; *ātma-vatām—*unto persons interested in self-realization; *anukampayā—*by causeless mercy; *tapaḥ—*austerities; *avyakta-gatiḥ—*whose glories are inconceivable; *carati—*executes.

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] The glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are inconceivable. He has appeared in the form of Nara-Nārāyaṇa in the land of Bhārata-varṣa, at the place known as Badarikāśrama, to favor His devotees by teaching them religion, knowledge, renunciation, spiritual power, sense control and freedom from false ego. He is advanced in the opulence of spiritual assets, and He engages in executing austerity until the end of this millennium. This is the process of self-realization.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He performs that penance which enhances *dharma* and leads to the perception of *ātmā*. *Upashama* is control over senses. *Uparama* means absence of false ego. It is not for His sake because He is God. It is only to bless the devoted.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The form worshipped in Bhārata, the nature of the worshipper, and the *mantra* that is chanted are stated here. In Bhārata, Nārāyaṇa performs penance in Badari till the end of the *kalpa*. His ways are not known to others. \[Note this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

The penance is described as that which increases *dharma*, i.e., *karma-yoga*, Jñāna ie., Jñāna *yoga*, Vairāgya, which means control over one's mind, Aishwarya which means the Animadi Siddhis, *yoga* which means conquering the breath and Uparama which means conquering the external senses. Why does He perform penance like an ordinary person? It is to bless the aspirants by showing the way the penance should be done so that they will also emulate Him. He blesses people who have a precocious mind because of his compassion only. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Upashama* is loyalty to God. *Uparama* is control over mind and other senses. These activities are not necessary for Him to perform*—*He wanted to show that these are necessary for others who perform penance. Because all his senses are under his control, He always has perception of His own self.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The identity between Nara and Nārāyaṇa is shown by the compound word Nara-nārāyaṇa. out of compassion, He performs penance for the welfare of those who regard Him as their master. Then why do not people know Him like that? It is because he is *Avyaktagati*, one whose ways are not known to others except Himself.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He performs a penance by means of which the “thou-element” is perceived as endowed with *dharma* and other attributes. Upashama is control of senses. Uparama is the absence of ego. His penance is also intended to instruct the way penance should be performed. This instruction is for the enlightened.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The identity of Nara and Nārāyaṇa is stated by the word Nara-nārāyaṇa. For the welfare of those who regard Him as their Lord, He performs penance*—*Oh, the degree of kindness. *Upachita* = increased. *ātmā* = the principle called “tvam” \[you\]. *Upalabhyate* = is known.

Why do ordinary people not know Him like that? The reply is given by the word *avyaktagati* which means His ways are unknowable.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The incarnation of God even in Bhārata-varṣa is stated here. He has taken two forms Nara and Nārāyaṇa and is engaged in penance in Badarikashram. He does not appear like God because His ways are unknown to others. His penance has no limit and it extends to the end of the *kalpa*. What is the outcome of this penance? It is God perception for others. How can it be a fruit for Him, who always has perception of His own self. It is to show to the other aspirants that *dharma* will increase by penance and it will lead to the perception of God. What is the benefit He derives from guiding the people? Nothing. The other persons are the beneficiaries. He acts only out of compassion.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Atmopalambhana* means He will be visible by the strength of *dharma* that accrues from penance. Such a penance He performs. *Upashama* is loyalty to God. *Uparama* is control over the mind and other senses. His penance is to teach others so that those who perform penance should do like this.

### Text 10

*तं भगवान्नारदो वर्णाश्रमवतीभिर्भारतीभिः प्रजाभिर्भगवत्प्रोक्ताभ्यां*  
*साङ्ख्ययोगाभ्यां भगवदनुभावोपवर्णनं सावर्णेरुपदेक्ष्यमाणः परम*  
*भक्तिभावेनोपसरति इदं चाभिगृणाति ॥१०॥*

*taṁ bhagavān nārado varṇāśramavatībhir bhāratībhiḥ prajābhir bhagavat-proktābhyāṁ sāṅkhya-yogābhyāṁ bhagavad-anubhāvopavarṇanaṁ sāvarṇer upadekṣyamāṇaḥ parama-bhakti-bhāvenopasarati idaṁ cābhigṛṇāti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tam—*Him (Nara-Nārāyaṇa); *bhagavān*—the most powerful saintly person; *nāradaḥ—*the great sage Nārada; *varṇa-āśrama-vatībhiḥ—*by followers of the institution of the four varṇas and four āśramas; *bhāratībhiḥ—*of the land known as Bhārata-varṣa (India); *prajābhiḥ—*who are the inhabitants; *bhagavat-proktābhyām—*which was stated by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *sāṅkhya—*by the sāṅkhya-yoga system (the analytical study of material conditions); *yogābhyām—*by practice of the yoga system; *bhagavat-anubhāva-upavarṇanam—*which describes the process of God realization; *sāvarṇeḥ—*unto Sāvarṇi Manu; *upadekṣyamāṇaḥ—*instructing; *parama-bhakti-bhāvena—*in greatly ecstatic loving service to the Lord; *upasarati—*serves the Lord; *idam—*this; *ca—*and; *abhigṛṇāti—*chants.

**Перевод:**

**In his own book, known as Nārada Pañcarātra, Bhagavān Nārada has very vividly described how to work to achieve the ultimate goal of life—devotion—through knowledge and through execution of the mystic yoga system. He has also described the glories of the Lord, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The great sage Nārada instructed the tenets of this transcendental literature to Sāvarṇi Manu in order to teach those inhabitants of Bhārata-varṣa who strictly follow the principles of varṇāśrama-dharma how to achieve the devotional service of the Lord. Thus Nārada Muni, along with the other inhabitants of Bhārata-varṣa, always engages in the service of Nara-Nārāyaṇa, and he chants as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Pancharatra* elucidates what Bhāgavatam has said. *Sarvani* is a manu. *Upasarati* means, “Is in the service of.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Nārada worships Nārāyaṇa along with other people who live in Bhārata, and follow the *varṇas* and *āśramas*. Sāṅkhya means Jñāna *yoga*, the Jñāna relating to the correct nature of the *ātmā*. *yoga* is *karma-yoga*, such as fire sacrifices prescribed for householders. These two are described in the *Bhagavad-gītā* by God himself. Nārada follows the Lord with utmost devotion. In what manner? Teaching *Pancharatra* to Savarni Manu. *Pancharatragama* deals with the nature of Brahman. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Sāṅkhya means correct knowledge and *yoga* is the means to correct knowledge. *Pancharatra* contains the description of Hari’s greatness and Nārada teaches that to Savarni Manu. *Upasarati* means performs *upāsanā* \[worship\]. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

To Savarni he teaches *Pancharatra* wherein the greatness of the Lord is extolled with Sāṅkhya and *yoga*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The other *prajas* (subjects) are also sages. He teaches Sāṅkhya and *yoga* propounded by God Nara-nārāyaṇa to Savarni. Sāṅkhya means the awareness of the distinction between the important and the unimportant. *Yoga* means one’s attachment to God. Tirtha has interpreted Sāṅkhya as knowledge and *yoga* as its means.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Yoga* is *niṣkāmakarma*.

### Text 11

*ॐ नमो भगवते उपशमशीलायोपरतानात्म्याय नमोऽकिञ्चनवित्ताय*  
*ऋषिऋषभाय नरनारायणाय परमहंसपरमगुरवे आत्मारामाधिपतये नमो*  
*नम इति ॥११॥*

*oṁ namo bhagavate upaśama-śīlāyoparatānātmyāya namo 'kiñcana-vittāya ṛṣi-ṛṣabhāya nara-nārāyaṇāya paramahaṁsa-parama-gurave ātmārāmādhipataye namo nama iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*om—*O Supreme Lord; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *bhagavate—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *upaśama-śīlāya—*who has mastered the senses; *uparata-anātmyāya—*having no attachment for this material world; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *akiñcana-vittāya—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the only asset of persons who have no material possessions; *ṛṣi-ṛṣabhāya—*the most exalted of saintly persons; *nara-nārāyaṇāya—*Nara-Nārāyaṇa; *paramahaṁsa-parama-gurave—*the most exalted spiritual master of all paramahaṁsas, liberated persons; *ātmārāma-adhipataye—*the best of self-realized persons; *namaḥ namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances again and again; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Nara-Nārāyaṇa, the best of all saintly persons, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is the most self-controlled and self-realized, He is free from false prestige, and He is the asset of persons who have no material possessions. He is the spiritual master of all paramahaṁsas, who are the most exalted human beings, and He is the master of the self-realized. Let me offer my repeated obeisances at His lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Uparata-anatmyaya* means, “One who is devoid of ego.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Uparata-anatmyaya* means, “For one who has no attachment even to his own body.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The *mantra* is described. The words “praṇava” and “Bhagavān” have been explained earlier. “Paramasheela” means one who has unexcelled character traits such as “sausheelya.” “Sausheelya” means that a great person mixes with ordinary people without any inhibition. This gives a lot of comfort to those who are under His protection. The other virtues of kindness, easy accessibility and lordship should also be included here.

Anatma means, “which is not *ātmā*  (i.e., the body and sensory organs).” *Anatmya* means their nature like hunger, thirst and so on. This is a Bahuvrihi compound. Uparata means destroyed or discarded. He by whom the nature of the body, hunger, thirst and so on are destroyed is Uparata-anatmya. The dative case is used here. \[Note: this paragraph was also written by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

Akinchana means those who do not own anything. They are the mumukshas aspiring for salvation. For them He is Vitta, a treasure. \[Note: these paragraphs are repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

“To Him, the *paramahaṁsa*,” means that He is always higher and different from the *jīvas*. Or “parama” means infinite auspicious attributes. *Hamsa* means a person who is devoid of all blemishes. *Ātmārāma* is one who has unexcelled bliss. Obeisances to such a person (God).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Uparata-anatmyaya means one who surpassed the dictations of bodily hunger and aging, etc. He is the Lord of *ātmārāmas*. To Him our obeisances are due.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Those who reside there are also like sages, although not all. To Savarni Manu he teaches *Pancharatra* wherein the greatness of the Lord is extolled with Sāṅkhya and *yoga*. Sāṅkhya is discerning between the good and bad or useful and useless. *Yoga* means loyalty to God.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

To the ultimate teacher of *paramahaṁsas*. *Uparata-anatmya* means one who has no ego.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The *mantra* is recited: “Obeisances to Bhagavān Nara-nārāyaṇa. He is Bhagavān because He is Adhipati, the protector of everything. He is the Guru of Paramahamsas, who discern between the good and bad. He protects them from the fear of Saṁsāra \[repeated birth and death\]. Why is His lordship over *paramahaṁsas* particularly mentioned when he is the Lord of everything? It is because they are very dear to Him. He is the treasure for those *paramahaṁsas* who do not own anything. Also they are protected by Him like a treasure. Although all activities in the world are guided by some purpose, the actions of God are not done to achieve any purpose for Himself*—*rather it is his *līlā* \[pastime\]. The actions of those who are under the control of their mind and senses may be guided by desires, but God is not under any other's control and his actions are therefore not guided by any mundane desire. Even the actions of sages is not under the influence of material desire.

He is Rishi Rshabha, the best among sages. For others money may be a dear thing, but for the wise, God and His devotees are dear. His wisdom is stated by the word Uparata-anatmya and He has no false ego as do ignorant people. The reason is that He is Upashamasheela. Controlling the mind and senses is His nature because He is Atmarama, i.e. He enjoys in Himself the nature of bliss. He is not interested in any happiness from outside, for if He were, He would be under the influence of His mind and senses.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Haṁsa is interpreted in a different way. He is Haṁsa because he destroys all the blemishes. The word “namah” is construed with each attribute and hence the repetition.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Uparata-anatmya* means, “One who is free from the grief attendant on being associated with the body.”

### Text 12

*गायति चेदम्*  
*कर्तास्य सर्गादिषु यो न बध्यते*  
*न हन्यते देहगतोऽपि दैहिकैः ।*  
*द्रष्टुर्न दृग्यस्य गुणैर्विदूष्यते*  
*तस्मै नमोऽसक्तविविक्तसाक्षिणे ॥१२॥*

*gāyati cedam—*  
*kartāsya sargādiṣu yo na badhyate*  
*na hanyate deha-gato 'pi daihikaiḥ*  
*draṣṭur na dṛg yasya guṇair vidūṣyate*  
*tasmai namo 'sakta-vivikta-sākṣiṇe*

**Пословный перевод:**

*gāyati—*he sings; *ca—*and; *idam—*this; *kartā—*the executor; *asya—*of this cosmic manifestation; *sarga-ādiṣu—*of the creation, maintenance and destruction; *yaḥ—*one who; *na badhyate—*is not attached as the creator, master or proprietor; *na—*not; *hanyate—*is victimized; *deha-gataḥ api—*although appearing as a human being; *daihikaiḥ—*by bodily tribulations such as hunger, thirst and fatigue; *draṣṭuḥ—*of Him who is the seer of everything; *na—*not; *dṛk—*the power of vision; *yasya—*of whom; *guṇaiḥ—*by the material qualities; *vidūṣyate—*is polluted; *tasmai—*unto Him; *namaḥ—*my respectful obeisances; *asakta—*unto the Supreme person, who is unattached; *vivikta—*without affection; *sākṣiṇe—*the witness of everything.

**Перевод:**

**Nārada, the most powerful saintly sage, also worships Nara-Nārāyaṇa by chanting the following mantra: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the master of the creation, maintenance and annihilation of this visible cosmic manifestation, yet He is completely free from false prestige. Although to the foolish He appears to have accepted a material body like us, He is unaffected by bodily tribulations like hunger, thirst and fatigue. Although He is the witness who sees everything, His senses are unpolluted by the objects He sees. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto that unattached, pure witness of the world, the Supreme Soul, the Personality of Godhead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Obeisances to the Sākṣī \[witness\], the perceiver who is aloof. He is unattached because having created the world, He does not feel that He is the creator. He is aloof because in spite of apparently residing in the body He is unaffected by hunger and thirst. He is the Sākṣī because His perception is unaffected by the modes of material nature (*guṇas*). \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He sings the ensuing four verses. In the first place he (Nārada) offers obeisances to Nārāyaṇa, Who in spite of being the creator of the universe, does not regard Himself as the creator. This is because He is not attached to anything in the world. It is said in Gītā, “Dear Arjuna, And although I am the creator of this system, you should know that I am yet the nondoer, being unchangeable.” In another sense it means that there is diversity, inequality and gradation in this universe for which the individual living entities (*jīvas*) and their *karma* \[actions\] are responsible. God is not responsible, thus He does not regard Himself responsible for the inequality in the world, for it is due to the *jīvas* themselves. Although He is present in the physical bodies of demigods and other beings, He is unaffected by the hunger, thirst, and other sufferings obtained by the individuals. He is the Drashta, the perceiver. His *guṇa* \[quality\] is knowledge, unaffected by *prakṛti* \[material nature\], sattva \[mundane goodness\], etc. Or His stature is unalloyed by the qualities of the sentient and nonsentient. Thus, He is Asakta (unattached), Vivikta (different from every other thing), and Sākṣi, the observer. He is different from the living entity (*jīva*) because He is endowed with infinite auspicious virtues without even a trace of faults. “Obeisances to Him.

The *Brahmasutras* establish this truth also. The living entity is also an observer, but his observation is limited by the modes of nature under which he is conducted. The *jīva*, then, only perceives part of a thing, whereas God’s perception is correct and complete, being the controller of nature and unaffected by it.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is established that He is the guru \[instructor\] and Paramātmā \[supersoul\] within the bodies of all as *antaryāmī* and thus He sees everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is stated here that He is the crest jewel of *ātmārāmas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is stated here that He is the best among the *ātmārāmas* \[the self-satisfied\].

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He is praised in four slokas.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He also sings his praise in the next four verses. *Eka* means there is nothing equal to or superior to Him. \[Note from the translator: this differs from the view of the Advaitins which defines the term as, “the absence of a second principle in the world.”\] Obeisances to him.

### Text 13

*इदं हि योगेश्वर योगनैपुणं*  
*हिरण्यगर्भो भगवाञ्जगाद यत् ।*  
*यदन्तकाले त्वयि निर्गुणे मनो*  
*भक्त्या दधीतोज्झितदुष्कलेवरः ॥१३॥*

*idaṁ hi yogeśvara yoga-naipuṇaṁ*  
*hiraṇyagarbho bhagavāñ jagāda yat*  
*yad anta-kāle tvayi nirguṇe mano*  
*bhaktyā dadhītojjhita-duṣkalevaraḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*idam—*this; *hi—*certainly; *yoga-īśvara—*O my Lord, master of all mystic power; *yoga-naipuṇam—*the expert process of executing yogic principles; *hiraṇya-garbhaḥ—*Lord Brahmā; *bhagavān—*the most powerful; *jagāda—*spoke; *yat—*which; *yat—*which; *anta-kāle—*at the time of death; *tvayi—*in You; *nirguṇe—*the transcendence; *manaḥ—*the mind; *bhaktyā—*with a devotional attitude; *dadhīta—*one should place; *ujjhita-duṣkalevaraḥ—*having given up his identification with the material body.

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, master of all mystic yoga, this is the explanation of the yogic process spoken of by Lord Brahmā \[Hiraṇyagarbha\], who is self-realized. At the time of death, all yogīs give up the material body with full detachment simply by placing their minds at Your lotus feet. That is the perfection of yoga.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Nārada explains the perfection of *yoga* practice in the next three stanzas: “O my Lord, master of all mystic *yoga*, the yogic excellence extolled by Hiranyagarba is described here as a person remembering You all through his life and keeping his mind on You at the time of death. How? By having discarding the attachment to his bad body. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Nārada explains what Brahmā has taught him, namely that the *jīva* is prone to faults whereas God is not. For the living entity to overcome his faults the only way is to shun all material attachments and devote himself to the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The result of *dharma* earned in many births is the excellence of *yoga* practice taught by Hiraṇyagarbha that one should devoutly place his mind in You at the time of death.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

That non-attachment should be cultivated goes without saying. To establish this *yoga*, which is to be known in detail, is broadly taught here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A secret is revealed here for those who practice *yoga*. The word *yat* is a present participle meaning “wavering.” If the wavering mind is fixed in God at the time of death, one achieves the perfection of *yoga*. The word “*ujjhita*” is a present participle*—*not a past participle as it appears. Thus the meaning is, “abandoning” and not “abandoned.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

A secret is divulged here for those who practice *yoga*. It is that one should place the otherwise fickle mind at the lotus feet of the Lord at the time of death.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Stability of mind and detachment are the products of knowledge, otherwise it is just a tiresome effort. So in this and the next two verses Nārada prays, “O Yogeswara, kindly give us jñāna *yoga* by which we will set our minds on You. The highest *yoga* taught by Hiraṇyagarbha is this only*—* that a man should discard attachments and place his mind in You at the time of death.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

What Hiraṇyagarbha has said is correct. A person who does not place his mind in God earlier cannot do it in the end, so this should be practiced right from childhood.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The word *upashamasheela* suggests that Nārāyaṇa performs penance for teaching others. “The excellence of *dhyana* \[meditation\] is stated by Brahmā that one should fix his mind in You while leaving this body. To do that one should practice it from the beginning of life.”

### Text 14

*यथैहिकामुष्मिककामलम्पटः*  
*सुतेषु दारेषु धनेषु चिन्तयन् ।*  
*शङ्केत विद्वान् कुकलेवरात्ययाद्*  
*यस्तस्य यत्नः श्रम एव केवलम् ॥१४॥*

*yathaihikāmuṣmika-kāma-lampaṭaḥ*  
*suteṣu dāreṣu dhaneṣu cintayan*  
*śaṅketa vidvān kukalevarātyayād*  
*yas tasya yatnaḥ śrama eva kevalam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yathā—*as; *aihika—*in the present life; *amuṣmika—*in the expected future life; *kāma-lampaṭaḥ—*a person who is very attached to lusty desires for bodily enjoyment; *suteṣu—*children; *dāreṣu—*wife; *dhaneṣu—*wealth; *cintayan—*thinking about; *śaṅketa—*is afraid; *vidvān—*a person advanced in spiritual knowledge; *ku-kalevara—*of this body, which is full of stool and urine; *atyayāt—*because of loss; *yaḥ—*anyone; *tasya—*his; *yatnaḥ—*endeavors; *śramaḥ—*a waste of time and energy; *eva—*certainly; *kevalam—*only.

**Перевод:**

**Materialists are generally very attached to their present bodily comforts and to the bodily comforts they expect in the future. Therefore they are always absorbed in thoughts of their wives, children and wealth and are afraid of giving up their bodies, which are full of stool and urine. If a person engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, however, is also afraid of giving up his body, what is the use of his having labored to study the śāstras? It was simply a waste of time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

If the “so-called yogi” thinks about how his sons are going to live after his death, then whatever he has studied is in vain. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Vaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

For a person who has no devotion to God, the study of *śāstras* and other things are in vain. In spite of studying the *śāstras*, if a scholar is attached to his children, heavenly comforts hereafter and is afraid of death due to over-attachment to his body, then all that he has studied is in vain. The study of *śāstras* is of no avail for one who is afraid of death. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Because everything is transient here, a learned man should not be afraid of death like an ordinary person. If a learned man were to think, as ignorant persons do, that his sons may perish after his death, then whatever he has studied is in vain. One should not think like that.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

If one wants to be eligible to get that knowledge of *yoga*, one should be able to discern between good and bad.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Otherwise his meditation and other things are in vain is what is stated here.

### Text 15

*तन्नः प्रभो त्वं कुकलेवरार्पितां*  
*त्वन्माययाहंममतामधोक्षज ।*  
*भिन्द्याम येनाशु वयं सुदुर्भिदां*  
*विधेहि योगं त्वयि नः स्वभावमिति ॥१५॥*

*tan naḥ prabho tvaṁ kukalevarārpitāṁ*  
*tvan-māyayāhaṁ-mamatām adhokṣaja*  
*bhindyāma yenāśu vayaṁ sudurbhidāṁ*  
*vidhehi yogaṁ tvayi naḥ svabhāvam iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tat—*therefore; *naḥ—*our; *prabho—*O my Lord; *tvam—*You; *ku-kalevara-arpitām—*invested in this bad body full of stool and urine; *tvat-māyayā—*by Your illusory energy; *aham-mamatām—*the conception of "I and my"; *adhokṣaja—*O Transcendence; *bhindyāma—*may give up; *yena—*by which; *āśu—*very soon; *vayam—*we; *sudurbhidām—*which is very difficult to give up; *vidhehi—*please give; *yogam—*the mystic process; *tvayi—*unto You; *naḥ—*our; *svabhāvam—*which is symptomized by a steady mind; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Lord, O Transcendence, kindly help us by giving us the power to execute bhakti-yoga so that we can control our restless minds and fix them upon You. We are all infected by Your illusory energy; therefore we are very attached to the body, which is full of stool and urine, and to anything related with the body. Except for devotional service, there is no way to give up this attachment. Therefore kindly bestow upon us this benediction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Otherwise his study of scriptures and all are in vain. If a learned man were also to think in the same way a layman does, getting attached to his children and fearing death, all that he has studied will be in vain.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Dear Lord, please give us Your devotional service because even a scholar’s plight is described here. “We want *bhakti* which is unattainable by those with material desires and which is capable of rooting out the bodily conceptions of “I” and “my” \[I am this body and things related to the body are mine\]. Since it is not possible to have *bhakti-yoga* by any other means other than Your grace, be kind enough to bestow this upon us.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and also written by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is stated here that, “Only Your blessings can prove fruitful in *yoga*.” *Yoga* is a means like meditation, etc. *Yogīs* pray for the destruction of the “I and my” misconceptions because they are harmful to liberation (*mokṣa*).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

They express their desire. “In this bad body,” is said with respect to their superiors.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

So destroy attachments and make our minds firm.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

This is said with respect to people who are born in Kaliyuga. You are the only person competent to fulfill our desires. The word Adhokshaja implies that without His grace God cannot be known. “Since the mind naturally flows out towards the objects of senses, let it flow towards You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Having praised the power of *yoga*, now *yoga* \[divine connection\] is prayed for. “Dear Lord, You are the one capable of uplifting Your devotees. Kindly give us devotion to You so that we can shed attachment to our cursed materialistic, sweating, foul smelling and transient bodies. Without this, we are incompetent to cross the ocean of Saṁsāra.” Although Nārada’s body is not made of the five elements \[earth, water, fire, air and ether\] since it is of the nature of pure Sattva (as stated in the first canto), still he uses the plural “we” and consequently it refers to others.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now Nārada prays for that same excellence, “Kindly give us the excellence of *yoga* by which we will fix our minds in You and cut off the attachment to the body and other things, which are very, very difficult to do.”

### Text 16

*भारतेऽप्यस्मिन् वर्षे सरिच्छैलाः सन्ति बहवो मलयो मङ्गलप्रस्थो*  
*मैनाकस्त्रिकूट ऋषभः कूटकः कोल्लकः सह्यो देवगिरिरृष्यमूकः श्रीशैलो*  
*वेङ्कटो महेन्द्रो वारिधारो विन्ध्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षगिरिः पारियात्रो*  
*द्रोणश्चित्रकूटो गोवर्धनो रैवतकः ककुभो नीलो गोकामुख इन्द्रकीलः*  
*कामगिरिरिति चान्ये च शतसहस्रशः शैलास्तेषां नितम्बप्रभवा नदा*  
*नद्यश्च सन्त्यसङ्ख्याताः ॥१६॥*

*bhārate 'py asmin varṣe saric-chailāḥ santi bahavo malayo maṅgala-prastho mainākas trikūṭa ṛṣabhaḥ kūṭakaḥ kollakaḥ sahyo devagirir ṛṣyamūkaḥ śrī-śailo veṅkaṭo mahendro vāridhāro vindhyaḥ śuktimān ṛkṣagiriḥ pāriyātro droṇaś citrakūṭo govardhano raivatakaḥ kakubho nīlo gokāmukha indrakīlaḥ kāmagirir iti cānye ca śata-sahasraśaḥ śailās teṣāṁ nitamba-prabhavā nadā nadyaś ca santy asaṅkhyātāḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhārate—*in the land of Bhārata-varṣa; *api—*also; *asmin—*in this; *varṣe—*tract of land; *sarit—*rivers; *śailāḥ—*mountains; *santi—*there are; *bahavaḥ—*many; *malayaḥ—*Malaya; *maṅgala-prasthaḥ—*Maṅgala-prastha; *mainākaḥ—*Maināka; *tri-kūṭaḥ—*Trikūṭa; *ṛṣabhaḥ—*Ṛṣabha; *kūṭakaḥ—*Kūṭaka; *kollakaḥ—*Kollaka; *sahyaḥ—*Sahya; *devagiriḥ—*Devagiri; *ṛṣya-mūkaḥ—*Ṛṣyamūka; *śrī-śailaḥ—*Śrī-śaila; *veṅkaṭaḥ—*Veṅkaṭa; *mahendraḥ—*Mahendra; *vāri-dhāraḥ—*Vāridhāra; *vindhyaḥ—*Vindhya; *śuktimān—*Śuktimān; *ṛkṣa-giriḥ—*Ṛkṣagiri; *pāriyātraḥ—*Pāriyātra; *droṇaḥ—*Droṇa; *citra-kūṭaḥ—*Citrakūṭa; *govardhanaḥ—*Govardhana; *raivatakaḥ—*Raivataka; *kakubhaḥ—*Kakubha; *nīlaḥ—*Nīla; *gokāmukhaḥ—*Gokāmukha; *indrakīlaḥ—*Indrakīla; *kāma-giriḥ—*Kāmagiri; *iti—*thus; *ca—*and; *anye—*others; *ca—*also; *śata-sahasraśaḥ—*many hundreds and thousands; *śailāḥ—*mountains; *teṣām—*of them; *nitamba-prabhavāḥ—*born of the slopes; *nadāḥ—*big rivers; *nadyaḥ—*small rivers; *ca—*and; *santi—*there are; *asaṅkhyātāḥ—*innumerable.

**Перевод:**

**In the tract of land known as Bhārata-varṣa, as in Ilāvṛta-varṣa, there are many mountains and rivers. Some of the mountains are known as Malaya, Maṅgala-prastha, Maināka, Trikūṭa, Ṛṣabha, Kūṭaka, Kollaka, Sahya, Devagiri, Ṛṣyamūka, Śrī-śaila, Veṅkaṭa, Mahendra, Vāridhāra, Vindhya, Śuktimān, Ṛkṣagiri, Pāriyātra, Droṇa, Citrakūṭa, Govardhana, Raivataka, Kakubha, Nīla, Gokāmukha, Indrakīla and Kāmagiri. Besides these, there are many other hills, with many large and small rivers flowing from their slopes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Dear Adhokshaja, please give us Your devotional service because even a scholar’s plight is described here. “We want Bhakti which is unattainable by those with material desires and which is capable of rooting out the bodily conceptions of “I” and “my” \[I am this body and things related to the body are mine\]. Since it is not possible to have *bhakti-yoga* by any other means other than Your grace, be kind enough to bestow this upon us.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the form of God worshipped in Bhārata and things related to it, now the mountains and rivers there are delineated. It is implied that there are mountains and rivers like these in other varshas also, although not mentioned thoroughly. The list of mountains is from Malaya to Kāmagiri. The rivers born from the peaks of these mountains, numbering in the hundreds, mostly flow westward and not eastward. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Now Bhārata’s important mountains and the rivers originating from them are described.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Api* means as in Ilavarta, here also.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Govardhana mountain is famous in the Śāstras and also in the world as the playground of Kṛṣṇa. It is in Vrindavan. It appears very small as it is sinking into earth year after year. Raivata mountain is also mentioned here. Chitrakuta is mentioned first because it relates to Rāmavatara which is prior to Kṛṣṇavatara.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Having described the excellence of the earth, now the excellence of Bhārata because of its holy water is described*—*beginning with Ilavrta *Varṣa*, there are many mountains and rivers in Bhārata *Varṣa* also. The rivers originate from the slopes of the mountains. The mountains are Malaya and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Both male and female rivers are there in the thousands.

### Text 17-18

*एतासामपो भारत्यः प्रजा नामभिरेव पुनन्तीनामात्मना चोपस्पृशन्ति*  
*॥१७॥ चन्द्रवसा ताम्रपर्णी अवटोदा कृतमाला वैहायसी कावेरी वेणी*  
*पयस्विनी शर्करावर्ता तुङ्गभद्रा कृष्णा वेण्या भीमरथी गोदावरी निर्विन्ध्या*  
*पयोष्णी तापी रेवा सुरसा नर्मदा चर्मण्वती सिन्धुरन्धः शोणश्च नदौ*  
*महानदी वेदस्मृतिरृषिकुल्या त्रिसामा कौशिकी मन्दाकिनी यमुना सरस्वती*  
*दृषद्वती गोमती सरयू रोधस्वती सप्तवती सुषोमा शतद्रूश्चन्द्रभागा मरुद्वृधा*  
*वितस्ता असिक्नी विश्वेति महानद्यः ॥१८॥*

*etāsām apo bhāratyaḥ prajā nāmabhir eva punantīnām ātmanā copaspṛśanti; candravasā tāmraparṇī avaṭodā kṛtamālā vaihāyasī kāverī veṇī payasvinī śarkarāvartā tuṅgabhadrā kṛṣṇāveṇyā bhīmarathī godāvarī nirvindhyā payoṣṇī tāpī revā surasā narmadā carmaṇvatī sindhur andhaḥ śoṇaś ca nadau mahānadī vedasmṛtir ṛṣikulyā trisāmā kauśikī mandākinī yamunā sarasvatī dṛṣadvatī gomatī sarayū rodhasvatī saptavatī suṣomā śatadrūś candrabhāgā marudvṛdhā vitastā asiknī viśveti mahā-nadyaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*etāsām—*of all these; *apaḥ—*water; *bhāratyaḥ—*of Bhārata-varṣa (India); *prajāḥ—*the residents; *nāmabhiḥ—*by the names; *eva—*only; *punantīnām—*are purifying; *ātmanā—*by the mind; *ca—*also; *upaspṛśanti—*touch; *candra-vasā—*Candravasā; *tāmra-parṇī—*Tāmraparṇī; *avaṭodā—*Avaṭodā; *kṛta-mālā—*Kṛtamālā; *vaihāyasī—*Vaihāyasī; *kāverī—*Kāverī; *veṇī—*Veṇī; *payasvinī—*Payasvinī; *śarkarāvartā—*Śarkarāvartā; *tuṅga-bhadrā—*Tuṅgabhadrā; *kṛṣṇā-veṇyā—*Kṛṣṇāveṇyā; *bhīma-rathī—*Bhīmarathī; *godāvarī—*Godāvarī; *nirvindhyā—*Nirvindhyā; *payoṣṇī—*Payoṣṇī; *tāpī—*Tāpī; *revā—*Revā; *surasā—*Surasā; *narmadā—*Narmadā; *carmaṇvatī—*Carmaṇvatī; *sindhuḥ—*Sindhu; *andhaḥ—*Andha; *śoṇaḥ—*Śoṇa; *ca—*and; *nadau—*two rivers; *mahā-nadī—*Mahānadī; *veda-smṛtiḥ—*Vedasmṛti; *ṛṣi-kulyā—*Ṛṣikulyā; *tri-sāmā—*Trisāmā; *kauśikī—*Kauśikī; *mandākinī—*Mandākinī; *yamunā—*Yamunā; *sarasvatī—*Sarasvatī; *dṛṣadvatī—*Dṛṣadvatī; *gomatī—*Gomatī; *sarayū—*Sarayū; *rodhasvatī—*Rodhasvatī; *saptavatī—*Saptavatī; *suṣomā—*Suṣomā; *śata-drūḥ—*Śatadrū; *candrabhāgā—*Candrabhāgā; *marudvṛdhā—*Marudvṛdhā; *vitastā—*Vitastā; *asiknī—*Asiknī; *viśvā—*Viśvā; *iti—*thus; *mahā-nadyaḥ—*big rivers.

**Перевод:**

**Two of the rivers—the Brahmaputra and the Śoṇa—are called nadas, or main rivers. These are other great rivers that are very prominent: Candravasā, Tāmraparṇī, Avaṭodā, Kṛtamālā, Vaihāyasī, Kāverī, Veṇī, Payasvinī, Śarkarāvartā, Tuṅgabhadrā, Kṛṣṇāveṇyā, Bhīmarathī, Godāvarī, Nirvindhyā, Payoṣṇī, Tāpī, Revā, Surasā, Narmadā, Carmaṇvatī, Mahānadī, Vedasmṛti, Ṛṣikulyā, Trisāmā, Kauśikī, Mandākinī, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Dṛṣadvatī, Gomatī, Sarayū, Rodhasvatī, Saptavatī, Suṣomā, Śatadrū, Candrabhāgā, Marudvṛdhā, Vitastā, Asiknī and Viśvā. The inhabitants of Bhārata-varṣa are purified because they always remember these rivers. Sometimes they chant the names of these rivers as mantras, and sometimes they go directly to the rivers to touch them and bathe in them. Thus the inhabitants of Bhārata-varṣa become purified.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

As in Ilavrta, here also are rivers and mountains. *Nitambaprabhava* means, “Originating from the edge.” *Atmana* means, “By their bodies also*—*they touch.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The people in Bhārata use the waters of these rivers which sanctify even by the mention of their names. The smriti says, “One who mentions the name of Gaṅgā even though he is at a distance of hundred *yojanas* from the river is washed off of all his sins and goes to Brahmaloka.” The rivers are listed from Chandramasa to Vishwa, since Kāverī is mentioned separately. Marudvrdha should be taken as another river. Since Gaṅgā has been described in detail earlier, it is omitted here. Sindhu and Shona are male rivers.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*ātmānā* = by their bodies. *Upasprshanti* = touch by sipping and bathing.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*ātmānā* means with the body. *Andha* is Brahmā’s son.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

They \[rivers\] sanctify us even by the mention of their names. The names of a few are stated. Charmanvati is the adjective used to qualify Narmada, so there is no repetition. *Andha* means the Brahmaputra.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By sipping and bathing they touch the rivers whose names themselves are sanctifying

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

What can be said about physical contact with the rivers since the very names of the rivers purify? The male and female rivers are listed*—*Chandravasa and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The people use the waters of these rivers which sanctify even by the uttering of their names. The rivers are listed. Vishwa is called Unmattaganga sometimes. The greatness of this river is described in the work *Harileela Kalpa Taru.*

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Even in Bhārata, not merely in Ilavrta, there are rivers and mountains. The people of Bhārata come into physical contact also with the waters of the rivers, the very names of which sanctify one who utters them.

### Text 19

*अस्मिन्नेव वर्षे पुरुषैर्लब्धजन्मभिः शुक्ललोहितकृष्णवर्णेन स्वारब्धेन कर्मणा*  
*दिव्यमानुषनारकगतयो बह्व्य आत्मन आनुपूर्व्येण सर्वा ह्येव सर्वेषां विधीयन्ते*  
*यथावर्णविधानमपवर्गश्चापि भवति ॥१९॥*

*asminn eva varṣe puruṣair labdha-janmabhiḥ śukla-lohita-kṛṣṇa-varṇena svārabdhena karmaṇā divya-mānuṣa-nāraka-gatayo bahvya ātmana ānupūrvyeṇa sarvā hy eva sarveṣāṁ vidhīyante yathā-varṇa-vidhānam apavargaś cāpi bhavati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*asmin eva varṣe—*in this tract of land (Bhārata-varṣa); *puruṣaiḥ—*by the people; *labdha-janmabhiḥ—*who have taken birth; *śukla—*of the mode of goodness; *lohita—*of the mode of passion; *kṛṣṇa—*of the mode of ignorance; *varṇena—*according to the division; *sva—*by himself; *ārabdhena—*begun; *karmaṇā—*by activities; *divya—*divine; *mānuṣa—*human; *nāraka—*hellish; *gatayaḥ—*goals; *bahvyaḥ—*many; *ātmanaḥ—*of his own; *ānupūrvyeṇa—*according to acts performed previously; *sarvāḥ—*all; *hi—*certainly; *eva—*indeed; *sarveṣām—*of all of them; *vidhīyante—*are allotted; *yathā-varṇa-vidhānam—*in terms of different castes; *apavargaḥ—*the path of liberation; *ca—*and; *api—*also; *bhavati—*is possible.

**Перевод:**

**The people who take birth in this tract of land are divided according to the qualities of material nature—the modes of goodness \[sattva-guṇa\], passion \[rajo-guṇa\], and ignorance \[tamo-guṇa\]. Some of them are born as exalted personalities, some are ordinary human beings, and some are extremely abominable, for in Bhārata—varṣa one takes birth exactly according to one's past karma. If one's position is ascertained by a bona fide spiritual master and one is properly trained to engage in the service of Lord Viṣṇu according to the four social divisions \[brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra\] and the four spiritual divisions \[brahmacārī, gṛhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa\], one's life becomes perfect.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Those who take birth here earn a place in heaven, etc. by their pious (sattvic) deeds. Because corresponding results befall all, those who observe the rules and regulations of *varṇa* and *āśrama*, especially those of the sannyasa and vanaprastha order, attain *mokṣa*. This is possible where all paraphernalia is present. It is not, however, that there is no *mokṣa* \[liberation\] elsewhere. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Bhārata’s greatness is stated here. The people born here observe their *dharmas* and attain many results. The sattvic people \[*brāhmaṇa* or those in goodness\] observe all the *dharmas* and obtain heaven. The rajas people \[those in passion\] stay here even in their subsequent births. The tamas people \[those in ignorance\] go down to hell by their acts. It is said in the *Gītā*: “Those situated in the mode of goodness gradually go upward to the higher planets; those in the mode of passion live on the earthly planets; and those in the abominable mode of ignorance go down to the hellish worlds.” Not merely that*—*some worship God and attain *mokṣa* having renounced everything else. It means there is the possibility of observing many pracitices here which lead to *mokṣa* \[liberation\]. This does not however prelude the sadhana \[practice\] leading to *mokṣa* in other varshas \[lands\]. For Badarayana has himself stated the same in his *Brahma-sutras*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Living entities perform pious and sinful acts under the influence of Sattva \[goodness\] and other modes of nature and as a result they attain heaven and other destinations. The “white, red and black color” signify the sattva, rajas and tamas *guṇa*s. *Swarnabhdhena* means an action which has begun to yield its fruit. *ātmānāh* means, “By the will of God.” Attainment of heaven and other destinations come to all in accordance with their acts through Varna and *āśrama*. Do only three results come to people in Bhārata*—*what about *mokṣa* \[liberation\]? The question is answered: not merely the above three, liberation from the bondage of *saṁsāra* \[birth and death\] is also achieved here.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Instead of “kola” there are two readings: “konna” and “konnaka.” Govardhana is the famous playground of Kṛṣṇa. Now it appears small because it is shrinking into the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this *varṣa* only and that too in the region of one thousand *yojanas*. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*, “Listen to the nine divisions of Bhārata-varṣa. They are Indradvīpa, Kaśeru, Tāmraparṇa, Gabhastimān, Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gāndharva, Vāruṇa, and the ninth, Navadvīpa, which is situated near the ocean in the midst of the other eight islands. Navadvīpa extends 1,000 *yojanas* from north to south.” Śrī Swami has explained the word “sagara sambrta” as situated in the proximity of the sea. Because no other name has been told for the ninth island, it is implied that its name is “Navadvipa.” The particulars of this island are given there only. “To the east, the Kirata's live and to the west the yavanas. In the east of this island there are the denizens of Kāmarupa. Odhas, Kalingas and Magadhas are all the denizens in the south.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Without violating the codes of *varṇas* and *āśramas*, a *brāhmaṇa* can take all four *āśramas*. A *kṣatriya* can take three*—*except sannyasa. A vaisya can take two*—*except vanaprastha and sannyasa. A sudra has only one asrama*—*that of the householder. This has been made clear in my commentary of the first hundred verses here.

Apavarga or *mokṣa* \[liberation\] is also attainable here*—*it is not that it is not attainable elsewhere. Badarayana himself states in the *Brahmasutras* that *mokṣa* is attainiable by demigods in heaven. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

This is my opinion. Viswanatha maintains that *mokṣa* is attainable only here and no where else*—*and that too within the 1,000 *yojana* stretch between the sea and the Himalayas. He has quoted from the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* to support this. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

“By white, red and black acts,” means sattvic, rajas and tamas activities. They earn many future results. As everyone receives reactions for actions performed (*karma*) as enjoined in the *Vedas* either *dharma* (pious) or adharma (impious), so *mokṣa* \[liberation\] is also possible. The conjunction “cha” indicates very few people attain *mokṣa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The people who are born here perform three kinds of actions, sattvic, rajas and tamas and attain heaven, this world (the earth), and hell respectively. Not merely that, they also perform sadhana \[spiritual practice\] and earn *mokṣa* \[liberation\].

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Shukla \[white\] action is sattvic action which leads to heaven. Lohita \[red\] action is rajas action and it leads to a human birth again. Kṛṣṇa \[black\] action is tamas action and leads to hell. Not merely these three, but by non attachment and worship of God, liberation is also achieved.

### Text 20

*योऽसौ भगवति सर्वभूतात्मन्यनात्म्येऽनिरुक्तेऽनिलयने परमात्मनि वासुदेवे*  
*ऽनन्यनिमित्तभक्तियोगलक्षणो नानागतिनिमित्ताविद्याग्रन्थिरन्धनद्वारेण*  
*यदा हि महापुरुषपुरुषप्रसङ्गः ॥२०॥*

*yo 'sau bhagavati sarva-bhūtātmany anātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane paramātmani vāsudeve 'nanya-nimitta-bhakti-yoga-lakṣaṇo nānā-gati-nimittāvidyā-granthi-randhana-dvāreṇa yadā hi mahā-puruṣa-puruṣa-prasaṅgaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ—*anyone who; *asau—*that; *bhagavati—*unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *sarva-bhūta-ātmani—*the Supersoul of all living entities; *anātmye—*having no attachment; *anirukte—*who is beyond the mind and speech; *anilayane—*not dependent on anything else; *parama-ātmani—*unto the Supreme Soul; *vāsudeve—*Lord Vāsudeva, the son of Vasudeva; *ananya—*without any other; *nimitta—*cause; *bhakti-yoga-lakṣaṇaḥ—*having symptoms of pure devotional service; *nānā-gati—*of varied destinations; *nimitta—*the cause; *avidyā-granthi—*the bondage of ignorance; *randhana—*of cutting; *dvāreṇa—*by means; *yadā—*when; *hi—*indeed; *mahā-puruṣa—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *puruṣa—*with the devotee; *prasaṅgaḥ—*an intimate relationship.

**Перевод:**

**After many, many births, when the results of one's pious activities mature, one gets an opportunity to associate with pure devotees. Then one is able to cut the knot of bondage to ignorance, which bound him because of varied fruitive activities. As a result of associating with devotees, one gradually renders service to Lord Vāsudeva, who is transcendental, free from attachment to the material world, beyond the mind and words, and independent of everything else. That bhakti-yoga, devotional service to Lord Vāsudeva, is the real path of liberation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The nature of liberation is described. *Anatmya* means “devoid of desire and other things that orginate in a body.” *Anirukta* means “beyond words.” *Anilayana* means “having no support.” One who has cut the shackles of *avidyā* \[ignorance\] that cause repeated births, attains liberation through *bhakti-yoga* \[devotional service\] by contact with great Vaiṣṇavas. Such devotion should be free of other desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

When will one attain liberation? What are the religious duties prescribed for this? Who is the one who bestows liberation and what is the nature of his blessing? All these questions are answered here. Previous *puṇya* \[pious activity\] and *pāpa* \[sinful activity\] are obstacles to *bhakti-yoga* \[devotional service\]. When these obstacles are removed by the grace of God, *bhakti-yoga* leads to liberation. Thus, observance of one’s prescribed duties \[*dharma*\], removal of sins, *bhakti-yoga* and liberation (*mokṣa*) is the order of events. *Dharma* is prescribed to one according to his *varṇa* and *āśrama*. *Bhakti* in Mahapuruṣa (i.e. Viṣṇu) is a different mode of mind. Here *avidyā* means “*puṇya* and *pāpa* (sins).” They are the actions, work. It should be noted that *avidyā* sometimes means the acts prescribed for one (because *puṇya* is also stated as *avidyā* and this leads to *puṇya*).

Sometimes the acts that bind the *jīva* to *saṁsāra* are called *avidyā* (because *avidyā* also means sins, which cause this bondage). Devotional service to Viṣṇu cuts the knot of *avidyā* which is responsible for taking one to heaven, hell, etc. It results from niṣkāmakarma, i.e. prescribed acts performed with the intention of pleasing God and not with any selfish interest. The object of *Bhakti-yoga* is next mentioned. The object is is Vāsudeva which is explained by the word “Sarva-ātma,” all-pervading. *ātmā* is the body, *atmya* is the nature of the body and *anatmya* means “he is different from the body.” *Anirukta* means he cannot be classified as a man or a demigod, etc.*—*which means he is different from all of them. He is different from the liberated *jīva* soul also, because he is *Anilayana*, i.e. has no support. The liberated soul has the support of God, the word “Paramātmā” implies that He is different from the eternally liberated (nitya-siddha) *jīvas* also. *Bhakti* should be performed for God without expecting anything in return and this type leads to liberation.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The word “api” suggests that the *jīvas* will acquire unswerving devotion to the Lord when they come in contact with great persons. *Bhakti-yoga* should not be used for other purposes. Then only it will generate liberation. How? By burning the knot of *avidyā* which is responsible for all these destinations. *Bhakti-yoga* should be earned by placing one's mind in Vāsudeva, who is devoid of the defects of a physical body (Anatmya), who is not fully described even by the *Vedas* (Anirukte), who has no other support as he is the supporter of everything (Anilagahe), who gives bliss even to the liberated souls (Paramātmāni). To indicate that even incarnations are capable of giving liberation, the word Vāsudeva is used. The word “hi” signifies that association with good people is the only way of getting *bhakti-yoga*, because that is what the learned say. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The most important cause of liberation is association with saintly persons as explained in relationship with Nārada from the first canto \[of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*\] itself. Although following one’s prescribed *dharma* is also a secondary cause. If one achieves even liberation in the form of *bhakti-yoga*, what is to be said about getting other things?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What is the nature of liberation and when will it happen? Here this question is answered. *Bhagavān* means endowed with many auspicious virtues which attract the minds of all persons. *Anatmya* means he is to be served by the other *ātmās*  and is not identified with other *ātmās* . *Anirukta* means his greatness cannot be described by the worldly. *Anilayana* means he is not destroyed even during the maha pralaya \[great flood devastation\]. These are the things that make him most worthy of being worshipped. He is Vasudeva’s son. Sincere devotion to Him is the means of salvation. Even *bhakti-yoga* itself is called *mokṣa* \[liberation\]*—*and this will take place when one comes into contact with great personalities.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

If a question be asked as to what the nature of liberation is and how it is obtained*—*the reply is given here. Bhagavān means endowed with very auspicious attributes like handsomeness and so on. That is why He attracts the minds of everyone. He is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Apavarga \[liberation\] is of many types; such as sayujya \[merging into the Supreme\] and others. What type of apavarga is intended here? The reply is given: the liberation intended here is *bhakti-yoga* which is the form of a flow of love towards Vasudeva’s son Kṛṣṇa, without expecting anything in return.”

Such love, everyone experiences towards his own self (*ātmā* ), so why does that make Him God? It is God who is the *ātmā* of everyone.

If He is the *ātmā* of everyone, then everyone becomes equal. Whence this worship?

No, He is Paramātmā and the *jīva* soul is His part and parcel. The part should be subservient to the whole and hence the devotional service.

If He is at one place, then He is limited. If He is all pervasive then He has contact with all material bodies and hence He is equal to the *jīva* souls. Then, why this devotional service?

The reply is: “No, He is not equal to the living entities. He is not affected by the properties of this body, although He is inside it. He has no false ego as the *jīva* soul has.”

Let there be worship when the world is manifest. During the pralaya \[unmanifest dissolution\], He will also be dissolved, then why this devotional service?

“No, he is *Anilayana*. He is not destroyed during the devastation (Pralaya). He is *Anirukta* because His greatness cannot be defined. So His devotional service is justified. His devotional service will cut the knots of *avidyā* \[ignorance\], responsible for reactions and miseries.

When will such *bhakti-yoga* come?

When the living entities come into contact with great souls.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The nature of apavarga is stated. Apavarga is *bhakti-yoga* to Vāsudeva, who is devoid of the properties of a material body, who has no other support as He is self-supporting and He who cannot be described by words completely. Devotional service should not be guided by any ulterior motive. This liberated state is obtained when one comes in contact with great souls, great devotees of Viṣṇu.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The means of apavarga is narrated. When one gets the association of great Haribhaktas \[devotees of the Lord\], then the ignorance which causes births and deaths is burnt up and liberation in one’s original blissful form is obtained.

Is it possible only by observing *dharma*?

No, it is only attained through unswerving devotion to God.

What is the nature of God? He is *anatmya*, different from the *jīva* souls; *Anirukta* indescribable by mundane words; *Anilayana,* has no other support; *Paramātmā*, the Supreme Soul. He is Vāsudeva, the form that gives liberation (*mokṣa*).

### Text 21

*एतदेव हि देवा गायन्ति*  
*अहो अमीषां किमकारि शोभनं*  
*प्रसन्न एषां स्विदुत स्वयं हरिः ।*  
*यैर्जन्म लब्धं नृषु भारताजिरे*  
*मुकुन्दसेवौपयिकं स्पृहा हि नः ॥२१॥*

*etad eva hi devā gāyanti—*  
*aho amīṣāṁ kim akāri śobhanaṁ*  
*prasanna eṣāṁ svid uta svayaṁ hariḥ*  
*yair janma labdhaṁ nṛṣu bhāratājire*  
*mukunda-sevaupayikaṁ spṛhā hi naḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*etat—*this; *eva—*indeed; *hi—*certainly; *devāḥ—*all the demigods; *gāyanti—*chant; *aho—*oh; *amīṣām—*of these inhabitants of Bhāratavarṣa; *kim—*what; *akāri—*was done; *śobhanam—*pious, beautiful activities; *prasannaḥ—*pleased; *eṣām—*upon them; *svit—*or; *uta—*it is said; *svayam—*personally; *hariḥ—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *yaiḥ—*by whom; *janma—*birth; *labdham—*obtained; *nṛṣu—*in human society; *bhārata-ajire—*in the courtyard of Bhārata-varṣa; *mukunda—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who can offer liberation; *sevā-aupayikam—*which is the means of serving; *spṛhā—*desire; *hi—*indeed; *naḥ—*our.

**Перевод:**

**Since the human form of life is the sublime position for spiritual realization, all the demigods in heaven speak in this way: How wonderful it is for these human beings to have been born in the land of Bhārata-varṣa. They must have executed pious acts of austerity in the past, or the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself must have been pleased with them. Otherwise, how could they engage in devotional service in so many ways? We demigods can only aspire to achieve human births in Bhārata-varṣa to execute devotional service, but these human beings are already engaged there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here praise is sung for human birth which brings all four *puruṣārthas* \[goals of life\]. Hari was gracious enough to grant those persons birth in Bhārata-bhūmi, without no effort on their part. We can only covet a birth there. Those who have taken birth there and are engaged in the service of Mukunda, are really blessed.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Because this *varṣa* \[Bhārata-varṣa\] is the place where one can execute practices leading to heaven or liberation, its glory is sung by demigods.

What are the good acts that these people have performed to get a birth in Bhārata-bhūmi, that God is pleased with them and bestows all His grace on them? Is it their holy acts that are responsible for this excellence, or is it only God’s kindness? In this way, the greatness of Bhārata and the greatness of being a human being there are expressed. In the human form the individual soul is capable of serving God which cannot be done when he is born as an animal or some other creature.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Because this birth is very appropriate to serve Mukunda \[Kṛṣṇa\], the question arises, “What good acts did they do to warrant a birth in Bhārata-bhūmi?” *Sprhatmabhih* means, “those who had this desire in their minds.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Did they do some extraordinary good deed or was Hari \[God\] simply pleased with them without any effort on their part? Such fortune cannot be merely the outcome of piety (*puṇya*). Wicked people are also present in Bhārata, however only those who have taken births conducive to His service are truly blessed**.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The birth one takes should be conducive to *dharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Those who live in Bhārata-bhūmi have their ambitions fulfilled. The genitive case in the word “ameeshami” is used in the instrumental sense.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Even demigods praise and sing about a human birth in Bhārata, which is conducive to Bhagavat seva \[service to the Supreme Lord\]. Their song is given in the next eight verses. What holy act did these people who are born in Bhārata perform to have received a birth here? Or did God on His own grant them this birth? Wicked people are also here, so what is the greatness of a birth here? No, what is meant is that a birth here, conducive to the seva of the Lord, is praiseworthy.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Although it has been said that this place is conducive to achieve heaven and liberation, still more praise is given. “Oh! What great act was done by these people who have taken birth in Bhārata. That too they have a birth which is useful in the service of God. Or is it that God himself was pleased with them and gave this opportunity to them, because we do not see any great deed done by these people in the past? This means birth in Bhārata is very rare and being born as a human being is still more so and the rarest and most fortunate is to be able to serve God here.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Those who are born in Bhārata and devoutly perform the acts prescribed to them will get this devotion. What good things did these people do, or did Hari \[God\] bless them on His own so that they have gotten a birth in Bhārata suitable for devotional service?

### Text 22

*किं दुष्करैर्नः क्रतुभिस्तपोव्रतै*  
*र्दानादिभिर्वा द्युजयेन फल्गुना ।*  
*न यत्र नारायणपादपङ्कज*  
*स्मृतिः प्रमुष्टातिशयेन्द्रियोत्सवात् ॥२२॥*

*kiṁ duṣkarair naḥ kratubhis tapo-vratair*  
*dānādibhir vā dyujayena phalgunā*  
*na yatra nārāyaṇa-pāda-paṅkaja-*  
*smṛtiḥ pramuṣṭātiśayendriyotsavāt*

**Пословный перевод:**

*kim—*what is the value; *duṣkaraiḥ—*very difficult to perform; *naḥ—*our; *kratubhiḥ—*with performances of sacrifice; *tapaḥ—*with austerities; *vrataiḥ—*vows; *dāna-ādibhiḥ—*with executing charitable activities and so on; *vā—*or; *dyujayena—*with achieving the heavenly kingdom; *phalgunā—*which is insignificant; *na—*no; *yatra—*where; *nārāyaṇa-pāda-paṅkaja—*of the lotus feet of Lord Nārāyaṇa; *smṛtiḥ—*the remembrance; *pramuṣṭa—*lost; *atiśaya—*excessive; *indriya-utsavāt—*due to material sense gratification.

**Перевод:**

**The demigods continue: After performing the very difficult tasks of executing Vedic ritualistic sacrifices, undergoing austerities, observing vows and giving charity, we have achieved this position as inhabitants of the heavenly planets. But what is the value of this achievement? Here we are certainly very engaged in material sense gratification, and therefore we can hardly remember the lotus feet of Lord Nārāyaṇa. Indeed, because of our excessive sense gratification, we have almost forgotten His lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Their desire is expressed in seven verses. What is the use of our attaining heaven through strenuous sacrifices? There, the memory of Nārāyaṇa’s Lotus feet is erased by excessive sense enjoyment. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In the next three stanzas it is stated that for those who live in other *varṣas*, the opportunity for service to God is unavailable and so it is useless. What is the use of attaining heaven by means of sacrifices, charities and other things? Heaven is, after all, trivial and furthermore dangerous because excessive sense enjoyment there wipes out the memory of Śrī Nārāyaṇa \[the Supreme Lord\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is the use of reaching heaven, where the memory of the Lord is erased? This is spoken in reference to those who have reached heaven through their good actions. It does not apply to the demigods themselves, since Nārāyaṇa is never erased from their minds. This is what the scriptures testify to.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

An anology of people with umbrellas is used. Though born here, many people do evil deeds and are thereby not subject to His compassion. The same idea is expressed by them in the next stanza also. His devotees naturally following the footsteps of their master.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

If the demigods were asked, “You have also come here with great *puṇya* \[pious activities\], etc. and are enjoying your stay in heaven, why do you want to be born in Bhārata-bhūmi?” They reply, “Fie on heaven, its enjoyments and the good deeds that lead to it. There is no use in staying in heaven because the memory of Mukunda is erased by excessive sense enjoyment. Instead, even a short life in Bhārata endowed with the memory of the Lord is great and it is to be coveted.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

You were also born in Bhāratavarsha and by your good deeds here, have attained heaven and are enjoying there now. Why then do you crave a birth in Bhārata again? If a question be asked like this, the demigods say: “Fie on heaven and the other material enjoyments there.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Phalgu* means trivial. By excessive sense enjoyment the memory of Nārāyaṇa is erased and so it is not here.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The demigods opine that those who live in different varshas and in places like heaven are not so fortunate and wise and thus are reproachable. What is the use of heaven which is attained by many hard practices and charity, etc. when there is no service of God here. There is excessive sense enjoyment which has erased even the memory of God.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Having praised those who aspire for liberation in Bhārata, others who perform pious acts aspiring to attain heaven are reproached.

What is the use of sacrifices intended to propitiate us? Attainment of heaven is by itself the goal.

“No, it is very trivial and it is dangerous also, for the memory of Hari is erased here amidst excessive enjoyments. So Bhārata-bhūmi with Harismarana \[rememberance of God\] is better than a stay in Swarga \[heaven\] without rememberance of the Lord.”

### Text 23

*कल्पायुषां स्थानजयात्पुनर्भवात्*  
*क्षणायुषां भारतभूजयो वरम् ।*  
*क्षणेन मर्त्येन कृतं मनस्विनः*  
*सन्न्यस्य संयान्त्यभयं पदं हरेः ॥२३॥*

*kalpāyuṣāṁ sthānajayāt punar-bhavāt*  
*kṣaṇāyuṣāṁ bhārata-bhūjayo varam*  
*kṣaṇena martyena kṛtaṁ manasvinaḥ*  
*sannyasya saṁyānty abhayaṁ padaṁ hareḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*kalpa-āyuṣām—*of those who have a life duration of many millions of years, like Lord Brahmā; *sthāna-jayāt—*than achievement of the place or planetary systems; *punaḥ-bhavāt—*which is liable to birth, death and old age; *kṣaṇa-āyuṣām—*of persons who have only one hundred years of life; *bhārata-bhū-jayaḥ—*a birth in the land of Bhārata-varṣa; *varam—*more valuable; *kṣaṇena—*for such a short life; *martyena—*by the body; *kṛtam—*the work executed; *manasvinaḥ—*those actually understanding the value of life*; sannyasya—*surrendering unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; *saṁyānti—*they achieve; *abhayam—*where there is no anxiety; *padam—*the abode; *hareḥ—*of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**A short life in the land of Bharata-varṣa is preferable to a life achieved in Brahmaloka for millions and billions of years because even if one is elevated to Brahmaloka, he must return to repeated birth and death. Although life in Bhārata-varṣa, in a lower planetary system, is very short, one who lives there can elevate himself to full Kṛṣṇa consciousness and achieve the highest perfection, even in this short life, by fully surrendering unto the lotus feet of the Lord. Thus one attains Vaikuṇṭhaloka, where there is neither anxiety nor repeated birth in a material body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Those who have even a short life are great because they attain the lotus feet of Nārāyaṇa in spite of their mortal frames.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In the higher worlds, living entities live for a Brahmā-kalpa amidst excessive comforts. The demigods say that getting a birth in Bhārata is to be preferred to spending a *kalpa*-long life in the upper worlds. Even a short life in Bhārata is desirable, for in such a short time people discard everything, set their minds on God, meditate upon him and attain liberation \[*mokṣa*\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Why do you praise the Bhārata-bhūmi because even people here are reborn? If an objection be raised like this, the reply is given. “A small life here is better than a *kalpa*-long life in Maharloka and other places. The daring ones disregard everything, concentrate their minds only on God, and reach the fearless highest place of Viṣṇu. This is the reason for the praise.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Sannyasya* means having offered to Hari \[God\].

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is amazing that a stay in Bhārata is superior to a stay in Brahmaloka is what is stated here. Even a long stay in Brahmaloka does not guarantee liberation, whereas even a short span of life in Bhārata, properly used by discarding all attachments and meditating only on Hari, will beget liberation.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is stated here that Bhārata-varṣa is even better than Brahmaloka. Those who have lifespans extending for a *kalpa* \[a day of Brahmā equaling more than four billion earth years\] live in Brahmaloka. But even a short life in Bhārata is better than the *kalpa* life of Brahmaloka, for that stay in Brahmaloka does not guarantee liberation \[*mokṣa*\]. Whereas, even a minute’s stay in Bhārata brings liberation for those who fully surrender to Vāsudeva, discarding all else.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Let alone Swarga, even Brahmaloka does not deserve to be respected if there is no memory of the Lord. The life of few minutes in Bhārata is superior to the *kalpa*-long life in Satyaloka, because in that short span, brave people discard all their attachments, meditate on God, and attain His lotus feet which is free from all fears.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

A life of a small span in Bhārata is better than the *kalpa*-long life in the upper worlds. For those who live in the upper worlds are reborn at the end of the Kalpa. But those in Bhārata discard all attachments, offer everything to Hari and attain His feet which is a fearless place of permanent bliss. Here Maharloka is indicated by the words, “where people live for a *kalpa*.” It is said in the Bhāgavata \[Śrīmad Bhāgavatam\] that in Maharloka people live for a *kalpa* and that there is no return to earth from Satyaloka, the loka of Brahmā.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Why is the stay in Maharloka and others not desirable? There life is very long stretching over a *kalpa*.

No, a stay in Maharloka does not guarantee freedom from Saṁsāra. But even a short stay in Bhārata is capable of assuring no return to Saṁsāra \[the cycle of repeated birth and death\] if properly used*—*the proper use is fixing one’s mind in Hari and discarding all attachments.

### Text 24

*न यत्र वैकुण्ठकथासुधापगा*  
*न साधवो भागवतास्तदाश्रयाः ।*  
*न यत्र यज्ञेशमखा महोत्सवाः*  
*सुरेशलोकोऽपि न वै स सेव्यताम् ॥२४॥*

*na yatra vaikuṇṭha-kathā-sudhāpagā*  
*na sādhavo bhāgavatās tadāśrayāḥ*  
*na yatra yajñeśa-makhā mahotsavāḥ*  
*sureśa-loko 'pi na vai sa sevyatām*

**Пословный перевод:**

*na—*not; *yatra—*where; *vaikuṇṭha-kathā-sudhā-āpagāḥ—*the nectarean rivers of discussions about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is called Vaikuṇṭha, or one who drives away all anxiety; *na—*nor; *sādhavaḥ—*devotees; *bhāgavatāḥ—*always engaged in the service of the Lord; *tat-āśrayāḥ—*who are sheltered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *na—*nor; *yatra—*where; *yajña-īśa-makhāḥ—*the performance of devotional service to the Lord of sacrifices; *mahā-utsavāḥ—*which are actual festivals; *sureśa-lokaḥ—*a place inhabited by the denizens of heaven; *api—*although; *na—*not; *vai—*certainly; *saḥ—*that; *sevyatām—*be frequented.

**Перевод:**

**An intelligent person does not take interest in a place, even in the topmost planetary system, if the pure Ganges of topics concerning the Supreme Lord's activities does not flow there, if there are not devotees engaged in service on the banks of such a river of piety, or if there are no festivals of saṅkīrtana-yajña to satisfy the Lord \[especially since saṅkīrtana-yajña is recommended in this age\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Where the nectar rivers of Mukundakatha \[topics of the Lord\] do not flow and where there are no great festivals glorifying the Lord, even if it be Brahmā’s Satyaloka, it does not deserve respect.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Where there are no rivers of Bhagavat Katha flowing, where there are no people rejoicing in those rivers, where there are no periodic festivals glorifing God, the place is not desirable to be reached even though it may be Brahmaloka itself.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

When Maharloka \[one of the higher planetary systems\], etc. are giving so much happiness, why are they regarded as inferior to Bhārata? The reply is, “there, Nārāyaṇa-*katha* \[discussions of Nārāyaṇa\] is not to be found because the great Bhāgavatas are rare there. They have reached that place only through their pious activities (satkarma) and they remain mostly silent and enjoy what is offered to them. This is told in the *śrutis*. So the attainment of those lokas is not to be desired.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A place where there are no rivers of the stories of Mukunda flowing and where there are no periodic festivals of the Lord does not deserve to be respected even if it is Brahmaloka itself.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The swami \[Śrīdhara Svāmi\] explains that nectar itself is sweet but topics about the Lord discussed by pure devotees is sweeter still. Bhajan \[chanting the glories of the Lord\] is one of the best sacrifices, as is stated in Bhāgavata \[ Śrīmad Bhāgavatam\]. This is the greatest festival*—*without which even Brahmaloka does not command respect.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Kshanayasham* means short lived. *Abhaya* = *mokṣa*. They live for a while and discarding everything, they perform devotional service to the Lord Hari and go back to Godhead.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Where there are no nectar rivers of talks about the Lord, where there are no devotees who preach for the benefit of themselves and others, where there are no great periodic festivals to extol the glory of the Lord, then even if it be Brahmaloka, it need not be respected or coveted.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Why do you deride Maharloka in favor of Bhārata-varṣa? In Maharloka there is so much joy. To this question reply is given here. “Even Satyaloka, let alone Maharloka, does not become respectable if there are no rivers of talks about the Lord flowing there, no great devotees, and no periodical festivals glorifying God.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

According to Kaimutya nyaya in the absence of the above, even a stay in Bhārata does not become desirable. *Suresha* means Indra whose loka \[planet\] is heaven. Apart from the regions of Bhārata, even Indra’s loka is not desirable if there are no talks about the Lord and great festivals glorifying Him.

### Text 25

*प्राप्ता नृजातिं त्विह ये च जन्तवो*  
*ज्ञानक्रियाद्रव्यकलापसम्भृताम् ।*  
*न वै यतेरन्नपुनर्भवाय ते*  
*भूयो वनौका इव यान्ति बन्धनम् ॥२५॥*

*prāptā nṛ-jātiṁ tv iha ye ca jantavo*  
*jñāna-kriyā-dravya-kalāpa-sambhṛtām*  
*na vai yaterann apunar-bhavāya te*
