*bhūyo vanaukā iva yānti bandhanam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*prāptāḥ—*who have obtained; *nṛ-jātim—*a birth in human society; *tu—*certainly; *iha—*in this land of Bhārata-varṣa; *ye—*those who; *ca—*also; *jantavaḥ—*the living beings; *jñāna—*with knowledge; *kriyā—*with activities; *dravya—*of ingredients; *kalāpa—*with a collection; *sambhṛtām—*full; *na—*not; *vai—*certainly; *yateran—*endeavor; *apunaḥ-bhavāya—*for the position of immortality; *te—*such persons; *bhūyaḥ—*again; *vanaukāḥ—*birds; *iva—*like; *yānti—*go; *bandhanam—*to bondage*.*

**Перевод:**

**Bhārata-varṣa offers the proper land and circumstances in which to execute devotional service, which can free one from the results of jñāna and karma. If one obtains a human body in the land of Bhārata-varṣa, with clear sensory organs with which to execute the saṅkīrtana-yajña, but in spite of this opportunity he does not take to devotional service, he is certainly like liberated forest animals and birds that are careless and are therefore again bound by a hunter.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Persons replete with knowledge, good deeds, etc. are to be censured if they have no desire for spiritual liberation. *Apunarbhava* is liberation. *Vanokasa* means birds. Just as birds released by a hunter which remain in that vicinity again get caught in a net, so does a *jīva* soul taking a human birth. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having decried those living in other varshas, now those born here as human beings are also decried if they do not have a desire for liberation. What type of human body? One equipped with: *Dravya* = the five elements, *Kriya* = motor organs, *Jñāna* = the sensory organs and other things by which a person can worship and meditate upon God. In spite of all this, if they do not strive for liberation, they will get caught again in Saṁsāra like forest birds. If forest birds set free by a hunter remain there enjoying where the hunter has spread his net, they will get caught again and such will be the plight of those who do not strive for salvation here.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Those who are born here and do not strive for liberation are destined to hell only. The dictionary gives two other meanings for the word *vana*: *naraka* (hell) and *bhajana* (praising and worshipping).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is not that everyone in Bhārata-bhumi is devoted to God*—*there are a some devotees here for which the praise is meant.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pitied are those who get a birth in Bhārataequipped with all motor and sensory organs and all other objects useful to the worship of the Lord, but do not strive for *bhakti-yoga*. They will be caught again like the birds let free from a hunter, lingering in the same forest where the hunter has spread his net.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Such people are pitiable in spite of reaching Bhārata, as is a farmer who continues to be a farmer even after getting a chintamani gem \[a gem which turns iron into gold\]. Knowledge is *Adhidaivam* (related to demigods). Actions and *Adhyātma* are related to the body, Dravyam is *Adhibhuta—*the external objects. Pity on a person with all bodily excellences and the capability of chanting and hearing of harinama kirtan \[chanting of the glories of God\] but does not strive for *Apunarbhava* \[*bhakti-yoga*\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Those who are always bound are reproached here, in spite of their having everything useful for the service of the Lord. *Vanauka* means forest dwellers.

### Text 26

*यैः श्रद्धया बर्हिषि भागशो हवि*  
*र्निरुप्तमिष्टं विधिमन्त्रवस्तुतः ।*  
*एकः पृथङ्नामभिराहुतो मुदा*  
*गृह्णाति पूर्णः स्वयमाशिषां प्रभुः ॥२६॥*

*yaiḥ śraddhayā barhiṣi bhāgaśo havir*  
*niruptam iṣṭaṁ vidhi-mantra-vastutaḥ*  
*ekaḥ pṛthaṅ-nāmabhir āhuto mudā*  
*gṛhṇāti pūrṇaḥ svayam āśiṣāṁ prabhuḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaiḥ—*by whom (the inhabitants of Bhārata-varṣa); *śraddhayā—*faith and confidence; *barhiṣi—*in the performance of Vedic ritualistic sacrifices; *bhāgaśaḥ—*by division; *haviḥ—*oblations; *niruptam—*offered; *iṣṭam—*to the desired deity; *vidhi—*by the proper method; *mantra—*by reciting mantras; *vastutaḥ—*with the proper ingredients; *ekaḥ—*that one Supreme Personality of Godhead; *pṛthak—*separate; *nāmabhiḥ—*by names; *āhutaḥ—*called; *mudā—*with great happiness; *gṛhṇāti—*He accepts; *pūrṇaḥ—*the Supreme Lord. who is full in Himself; *svayam—*personally; *āśiṣām—*of all benedictions; *prabhuḥ—*the bestower.

**Перевод:**

**In India \[Bhārata-varṣa\], there are many worshipers of the demigods, the various officials appointed by the Supreme Lord, such as Indra, Candra and Sūrya, all of whom are worshiped differently. The worshipers offer the demigods their oblations, considering the demigods part and parcel of the whole, the Supreme Lord. Therefore the Supreme Personality of Godhead accepts these offerings and gradually raises the worshipers to the real standard of devotional service by fulfilling their desires and aspirations. Because the Lord is complete, He offers the worshipers the benedictions they desire even if they worship only part of His transcendental body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The good luck of those who live in Bhārata-bhūmi where Hari Himself receives the oblations offered in the name of Indra, Agni and others is exclaimed.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Oh! The fortune of those that are born here! The oblations offered in the name of Indra, Agni and others, are acceptd by Lord Vāsudeva because He is the real bearer of the names Agni, Indra, etc. and He is supersoul residing in their hearts. He is *Aptasamastakama*, i.e. all of His desires are always fulfilled and there remains nothing to be fulfilled. Such being the case, why does He receive the oblations? It is to bestow His grace upon the sacrificer. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Śuka \[Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the reciter of the *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*\] explains that good actions performed in *Bhārata-varṣa* are more pleasing to the Lord than those done in other *khaṇḍas* \[countries\]*—*thus the praise. Hari himself comes and receives the oblations offered in the name of Indra and other gods, for He is their inner-dweller and the real Indra. He does not come there for His benefit, like demigods, for He is *purna*, always full of virtues, there is no dearth of anything in him. He is competent to fulfill all the desires of His devotees.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It is stated here that those who perform devotional service to the Lord in His many forms are really blessed. Though infinite and devoid of any mundane desire, Lord Hari Himself receives the oblations offered in the name of Agni, Indra and other gods.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is stated here that those who perform worship of the Viswarupa \[universal form of the Lord\] as enjoined in the *Gītā* are indeed blessed. It is with this intention only that Hari accepts the oblations that are offered to the demigs bearing the name of Indra, Agni and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

It is exclaimed here that even sakāma bhaktas \[devotees whose devotion is mixed with material aspirations\] here are great because Hari Himself, in spite of not wanting anything, accepts the oblations in the name of Indra, Agni and other gods.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Devotees are of two kinds: sakāmas (endowed with desire) and the niṣkāmas (bereft of any desire). What they are going to achieve is stated here: the oblations offered in accordance with the scriptures by eligible persons of Bhārata-bhūmi, in the name of Indra, Agni and other demigods, are received by Lord Hari, because the demigods are His own forms.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

For this reason also Bhārata-varṣa is great, they say. Hari Himself, in spite of not wanting anything, comes and accepts the oblations in the sacrifices which are performed according to the scriptures, by those who live here. It is Hari only who accepts the oblations offered in the names of Indra, Agni and others, because they are His names actually. The demigods are the secondary meanings of those words.

### Text 27

*सत्यं दिशत्यर्थितमर्थितो नृणां*  
*नैवार्थदो यत्पुनरर्थिता यतः ।*  
*स्वयं विधत्ते भजतामनिच्छता*  
*मिच्छापिधानं निजपादपल्लवम् ॥२७॥*

*satyaṁ diśaty arthitam arthito nṛṇāṁ*  
*naivārthado yat punar arthitā yataḥ*  
*svayaṁ vidhatte bhajatām anicchatām*  
*icchāpidhānaṁ nija-pāda-pallavam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*satyam—*certainly; *diśati—*He offers; *arthitam—*the object prayed for; *arthitaḥ—*being prayed to; *nṛṇām—*by the human beings; *na—*not; *eva—*indeed; *artha-daḥ—*the bestower of benedictions; *yat—*which; *punaḥ—*again; *arthitā—*a demand for a benediction; *yataḥ—*from which; *svayam—*personally; *vidhatte—*He gives; *bhajatām—*unto those engaged in His service; *anicchatām—*although not desiring it; *icchā-pidhānam—*which covers all desirable things; *nija-pāda-pallavam—*His own lotus feet.

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead fulfills the material desires of a devotee who approaches Him with such motives, but He does not bestow benedictions upon the devotee that will cause him to demand more benedictions again. However, the Lord willingly gives the devotee shelter at His own lotus feet, even though such a person does not aspire for it, and that shelter satisfies all his desires. That is the Supreme Personality's special mercy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They say that those devoid of material desires living there are indeed blessed. It is true that He gives what one asks for, but that is not the highest *puruṣārtha* \[goal of life\], because desire creeps up again in different ways after one desire is fulfilled. For those who do not desire anything material, He gives His own lotus feet which award whatever one asks for and also puts an end to all further material desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The word “ashisham prabhuh” suggests that only God should be approached to obtain any of the four *puruṣārthas* \[goals of life\]. There also, only those who strive for *mokṣa* are praiseworthy. It is true that God supplies whatever one asks for, yet He also does not give. The idea is that generally one asks for material comforts and God supplies these, but in reality these are not true rewards. God’s real gift is liberation which frees one from all misery and bestows eternal bliss. Even if He gives, that is why it is said, He does not give. Even after getting what one desired the tendency to beg does not vanish from the *jīva* soul*—*he begs for some other thing. But for those who worship God without any desire, He gives His own feet which will put an end to all material desires. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Hari does not just receive oblations and keep quiet*—*rather He gives commensurate rewards. It is true that Hari gives them heaven for their good, but if they ask for something else in heaven, He does not reward it. It should not be thought that swarga \[the heavenly planets\] is the limit of what He can award. For those who perform niṣkāma *karma* \[service without material desire\], He gives his own tender feet which fulfill all desires \[Note from the translator: here the word *icchavidhanam* is rendered, “the fulfiller of all desires.”\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Those who have pure devotion, even though they have desires, are equal to Niṣkāmabhaktas, in a sense. It is true that Hari gives whatever one asks for, yet He gives in such a way that at the end of the enjoyment of the object given, they will not desire it again, as seen in the case of Dhruva. He gives His own feet which remove all other desires just as a father gives his son sugar candy curtailing the son’s mud-eating. Although both the sakāma and niṣkāma bhaktas ultimately attain His feet they should not be regarded as equal. The naturally pure and the purified do not become equal. \[Note: This paragraph is repeated by Śrī Vaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

It is true that the Lord gives whatever the suppliants ask for, yet He does not give the highest gift to them because even after getting what they desired for, another desire creeps up in their minds. But for niṣkāma bhaktas \[pure devotees\] He gives His own lotus feet which fulfills all desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Among the two types of devotees, Hari gives whatever the devotees with material desires request, yet He does not award them the highest benediction because, even after getting what they desire, more desires creep up in their minds. For the pure devotees, Lord Hari awards His own lotus feet fulfilling all desires and thus no further desires creep up in their minds. In this way, they always enjoy the bliss of God's grace and do not lament or hanker as do motivated devotees.

### Text 28

*यद्यत्र नः स्वर्गसुखावशेषितं*  
*स्विष्टस्य सूक्तस्य कृतस्य शोभनम् ।*  
*तेनाजनाभे स्मृतिमज्जन्म नः स्याद्*  
*वर्षे हरिर्यद्भजतां शं तनोति ॥२८॥*

*yady atra naḥ svarga-sukhāvaśeṣitaṁ*  
*sviṣṭasya sūktasya kṛtasya śobhanam*  
*tenājanābhe smṛtimaj janma naḥ syād*  
*varṣe harir yad-bhajatāṁ śaṁ tanoti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yadi—*if; *atra—*in this heavenly planet; *naḥ—*of us; *svarga-sukha-avaśeṣitam—*whatever remains after the enjoyment of heavenly happiness; *su-iṣṭasya—*of a perfect sacrifice; *su-uktasya—*of diligently studying the Vedic literature; *kṛtasya—*of having performed a kind act; *śobhanam—*the resultant actions; *tena—*by such a resultant action; *ajanābhe—*in the land of Bhārata-varṣa; *smṛti-mat janma—*a birth enabling one to remember the lotus feet of the Lord; *naḥ—*of us; *syāt—*let there be; *varṣe—*in the land; *hariḥ—*the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *yat—*wherein; *bhajatām—*of the devotees; *śam tanoti—*expands the auspiciousness.

**Перевод:**

**We are now living in the heavenly planets, undoubtedly as a result of our having performed ritualistic ceremonies, pious activities and yajñas and having studied the Vedas. However, our lives here will one day be finished. We pray that at that time, if any merit remains from our pious activities, we may again take birth in Bhārata-varṣa as human beings able to remember the lotus feet of the Lord. The Lord is so kind that He personally comes to the land of Bhārata-varṣa and expands the good fortune of its people.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

That is why they pray. *Shobhana* means happiness.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having praised those who strive for liberation here, the demigods express their wish thereby praising Bhārata-bhūmi. “We have attained heaven by performing many sacrifices, giving many gifts and so on. If there is any residual *puṇya* after enjoying in heaven, we want to use it for gaining a birth in Bhārata-bhūmi wherein God is always remembered. A birth without mental communion with God is of no use. What is the value of this mental communion? Hari bestows all His mercy to those who do so. \[Note: This paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Śuka says, “They reveal their intention: Because Hari does good to those who worship Him in Bhārata, we also desire to be born there, using our residual *puṇya* \[pious credits\], so that we will also worship Him and receive His grace. We want such a birth which will be useful to His worship.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“If there is any *puṇya* remaining for the worship, chanting, charity and discourses we have offered, may we get a birth in Bhārata-bhūmi, where Hari gives a lot of comfort and happiness to His suppliants ?

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Having praised the birth of devotees in Bhārata-bhūmi, the demigods also pray for the same. “If there is any *puṇya* \[pious credit\] remaining for the good deeds we performed and which brought us here, may we get a birth in Bhārata, useful for the service of God. He blesses those who perform His devotional service whereas in heaven there are many obstacles to such service.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Praising birth in Bhārata-varṣa, they also pray for the same. If there is any residual *puṇya* for the pious activities we have performed, (which have brought us here), we would like to have a birth in Bhārata, where we will always have his memory and serve him better. There are two types of persons in heaven*—*those in power like Indra, etc. and the second type is those who have gone to heaven by their good deeds only and they are not entitled to any power there. The second type of people pray for a birth in Bhārata so that they can perform their sadhana \[practice\] for liberation. For the first type *mokṣa* is assured although they do not do anything particular to gain *mokṣa*. Whatever they do, only causes the exuberance of bliss in *mokṣa*. So they also pray for a birth in Bhārata so that they will have the exuberance of bliss in *mokṣa*. Both of them are called devas, demigods. When it is said that demigods pray, both these types should be taken into consideration.

### Text 29-30

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*जम्बूद्वीपस्य च राजन्नुपद्वीपानष्टौ हैक उपदिशन्ति सगरात्मजैर*  
*श्वान्वेषण इमां महीं परितो निखनद्भिरुपकल्पितान् ॥२९॥ तद्यथा स्वर्णप्रस्थ*  
*श्चन्द्रशुक्ल आवर्तनो रमणको मन्दरहरिणः पाञ्चजन्यः सिंहलो लङ्केति ॥३०॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*jambūdvīpasya ca rājann upadvīpān aṣṭau haika upadiśanti sagarātmajair aśvānveṣaṇa imāṁ mahīṁ parito nikhanadbhir upakalpitān; tad yathā svarṇaprasthaś candraśukla āvartano ramaṇako mandarahariṇaḥ pāñcajanyaḥ siṁhalo laṅketi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—*Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued to speak; *jambūdvīpasya—*of the island known as Jambūdvīpa; *ca—*also; *rājan—*O King; *upadvīpān aṣṭau—*eight subordinate islands; *ha—*certainly; *eke—*some; *upadiśanti—*learned scholars describe; *sagara-ātma-jaiḥ—*by the sons of Mahārāja Sagara; *aśva-anveṣaṇe—*while trying to find their lost horse; *imām—*this; *mahīm—*tract of land; *paritaḥ—*all around; *nikhanadbhiḥ—*digging; *upakalpitān—*created; *tat—*that; *yathā—*as follows; *svarṇa-prasthaḥ—*Svarṇaprastha; *candra-śuklaḥ—*Candraśukla; *āvartanaḥ—*Āvartana; *ramaṇakaḥ—*Ramaṇaka; *mandara-hariṇaḥ—*Mandara-hariṇa; *pāñcajanyaḥ—*Pāñcajanya; *siṁhalaḥ—*Siṁhala;  *laṅkā—*Laṅkā; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, in the opinion of some learned scholars, eight smaller islands surround Jambūdvīpa. When the sons of Mahārāja Sagara were searching all over the world for their lost horse, they dug up the earth, and in this way eight adjoining islands came into existence. The names of these islands are Svarṇaprastha, Candraśukla, Āvartana, Ramaṇaka, Mandara-hariṇa, Pāñcajanya, Siṁhala and Laṅkā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Ashwanveshane* means as they went in search of the sacrificial horse. The islands are mentioned by their names.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the Jambūdvīpa with its nine divisions and their mountains and rivers and having praised the human birth in Bhārata-bhūmi, now the islands of Jambūdvīpa are described. The learned people say that Jambūdvīpa has other eight ancillary islands. They were not created by Priyavrata but by Sagara’s sons, as they dug the earth in search of the sacrificial horse.

They are named Swarnaprastha and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The ancillary islands of the Jambūdvīpa are stated.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The ancillary islands to Jambūdvīpa are mentioned. They were not created by the chariot wheel of Priyavrta. They were created when Sagara’s children dug the earth in search of the sacrificial horse. The eight islands are individually named. They are eight as mentioned here. But in the Shakuntala episode of *Mahābhārata*, thirteen islands are mentioned by number in the text and the commentator has given the names of three among the remaining five islands. He has said they are Romakapattana, Siddhapana and Yamakoti. He has not mentioned the other two names.

### Text 31

*एवं तव भारतोत्तम जम्बूद्वीपवर्षविभागो यथोपदेशमुपवर्णित इति ॥३१॥*

*evaṁ tava bhāratottama jambūdvīpa-varṣa-vibhāgo yathopadeśam upavarṇita iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*evam—*thus; *tava—*unto you; *bhārata-uttama—*O best of the descendents of Bharata; *jambūdvīpa-varṣa-vibhāgaḥ—*the divisions of the island of Jambūdvīpa; *yathā-upadeśam—*as much as I am instructed by the authorities; *upavarṇitaḥ—*explained; *iti—*thus.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King Parīkṣit, O best of the descendants of Bharata Mahārāja, I have thus described to you, as I myself have been instructed, the island of Bhārata-varṣa and its adjoining islands. These are the islands that constitute Jambūdvīpa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Svishta* = good sacrifice. *Sukta* = discourse. If there is any residual *puṇya* of some good deed we have done, may we get a birth in Bhārata-varṣa? Of what kind? Where one knows for certain that Lord Hari only is to be served, because Hari bestows happiness on those who serve Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Śuka concludes the description of Jambūdvīpa. “O best among the Bhāratas, I have described the divisions of Jambūdvīpa as per the teachings of my gurus and in the same order.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Some people say that there are eight ancillary islands to Jambūdvīpa. But more learned say they are parts of the ocean only and need not be regarded as separate islands.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

That is why they pray. If there is any remaining *puṇya* that has brought us here to heaven, we would like to be born in Bhārata-bhūmi, get the association of good people and praise and worship Lord Hari.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

You are the best among those born in that dynasty because you have the great fortune of hearing the greatness of Lord Hari.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By saying “as they dug the earth,” the author conveys that Bhārata-khaṇḍa, though 9,000 *yojanas* broad, appears smaller, because of their digging.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

By addressing Parīkṣit as Bharatottama, Śuka implies that he is the most worthy candidate for *śravaṇa* (i.e., hearing the glory of God). Śuka concludes the description of Jambūdvīpa.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Śuka concludes the description of Jambū Island: “Dear emperor, as I have heard from my teachers, I have narrated to you the details of Jambūdvīpa with all its divisions, in the proper order. This concludes the topic.”

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Nineteenth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “A Description of the Island of Jambūdvīpa.”

## Chapter 20 - Studying the Structure of the Universe

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*अतः परं प्लक्षादीनां प्रमाणलक्षणसंस्थानतो वर्षविभाग उपवर्ण्यते*  
*॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṁ plakṣādīnāṁ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa-saṁsthānato varṣa-vibhāga upavarṇyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; ataḥ param—after this; plakṣa-ādīnām—of the island named Plakṣa and others; pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa-saṁsthānataḥ—from the angle of dimensions, particular characteristics and form; varṣa-vibhāgaḥ—the division of the island; upavarṇyate—is described.

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hereafter I shall describe the dimensions, characteristics and forms of the six islands beginning with the island of Plakṣa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Twentieth Chapter describes the inner and outer dimensions of the six islands starting from Plakṣa, the oceans and the Lokāloka Mountain.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Sthiti* = limit. *Atah =* from Jambū Island.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The Jambū Island has been described in detail. Hereafter Śuka describes Plakṣa and other islands by their divisions, magnitudes, features and the disposition of its inhabitants whose virtues are always on the ascent.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The glory of Nārāyaṇa is extolled here by explaining His creation of Plakṣa and other islands. *Pramana* = magnitude. *Lakshana* = the uniqueness of rivers and mountains. *Samsthana* = shape; squarish, circular and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

After describing the Jambū Island, Śrī Śuka describes the Plakṣa and other islands surrounding it.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Śuka described in detail the Jambū Island in four chapters indicative of attaining the four *puruṣārthas* \[goals of life\]. He now sets out to describe the other islands. Hereafter, the divisions, salient features and other aspects of the islands starting from Plakṣa, will be narrated.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Śuka begins describing Plakṣa and the other islands. *Pramana* = magnititude. *Lakshana* = shape. *Samsthana* = the situation of mountains and rivers.

### Text 2

*जम्बूद्वीपोऽयं यावत्प्रमाणविस्तारस्तावता क्षारोदधिना परिवेष्टितो यथा*  
*मेरुर्जम्ब्वाख्येन लवणोदधिरपि ततो द्विगुणविशालेन प्लक्षाख्येन परिक्षिप्तो*  
*यथा परिखा बाह्योपवनेन । प्लक्षो जम्बूप्रमाणो द्वीपाख्याकरो हिरण्मय*  
*उत्थितो यत्राग्निरुपास्ते सप्तजिह्वस्तस्याधिपतिः प्रियव्रतात्मज इध्मजिह्वः स्वं*  
*द्वीपं सप्तवर्षाणि विभज्य सप्तवर्षनामभ्य आत्मजेभ्य आकलय्य स्वयमात्मयोगेनो*  
*परराम ॥२॥*

*jambūdvīpo 'yaṁ yāvat-pramāṇa-vistāras tāvatā kṣārodadhinā pariveṣṭito yathā merur jambv-ākhyena lavaṇodadhir api tato dvi-guṇa-viśālena plakṣākhyena parikṣipto yathā parikhā bāhyopavanena; plakṣo jambū-pramāṇo dvīpākhyākaro hiraṇmaya utthito yatrāgnir upāste sapta-jihvas tasyādhipatiḥ priyavratātmaja idhmajihvaḥ svaṁ dvīpaṁ sapta-varṣāṇi vibhajya sapta-varṣa-nāmabhya ātmajebhya ākalayya svayam ātma-yogenopararāma.*

**Пословный перевод:**

jambū-dvīpaḥ—Jambūdvīpa, the island named Jambū; ayam—this; yāvat-pramāṇa-vistāraḥ—as much as the measure of its width, namely 100,000 yojanas (one yojana equals eight miles); tāvatā—so much; kṣāra-udadhinā—by the ocean of salt water; pariveṣṭitaḥ—surrounded; yathā—just as; meruḥ—Sumeru Mountain; jambū-ākhyena—by the island named Jambū; lavaṇa-udadhiḥ—the ocean of salt water; api—certainly; tataḥ—thereafter; dvi-guṇa-viśālena—which is twice as wide; plakṣa-ākhyena—by the island named Plakṣa; parikṣiptaḥ—surrounded; yathā—like; parikhā—a moat; bāhya—external; upavanena—by a gardenlike forest; plakṣaḥ—a plakṣa tree; jambū-pramāṇaḥ—having the height of the jambū tree; dvīpa-ākhyā-karaḥ—causing the name of the island; hiraṇmayaḥ—magnificently splendorous; utthitaḥ—rising; yatra—where; agniḥ—a fire; upāste—is situated; sapta-jihvaḥ—having seven flames; tasya—of that island; adhipatiḥ—the king or master; priyavrata-ātmajaḥ—the son of King Priyavrata; idhma-jihvaḥ—named Idhmajihva; svam—own; dvīpam—island; sapta—seven; varṣāṇi—tracts of land; vibhajya—dividing into; sapta-varṣa-nāmabhyaḥ—for whom the seven tracts of land were named; ātmajebhyaḥ—to his own sons; ākalayya—offering; svayam—personally; ātma-yogena—by the devotional service of the Lord; upararāma—he retired from all material activities.

**Перевод:**

**As Sumeru Mountain is surrounded by Jambūdvīpa, Jambūdvīpa is also surrounded by an ocean of salt water. The breadth of Jambūdvīpa is 100,000 yojanas \[800,000 miles\], and the breadth of the saltwater ocean is the same. As a moat around a fort is sometimes surrounded by gardenlike forest, the saltwater ocean surrounding Jambūdvīpa is itself surrounded by Plakṣadvīpa. The breadth of Plakṣadvīpa is twice that of the saltwater ocean—in other words 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\]. On Plakṣadvīpa there is a tree shining like gold and as tall as the jambū tree on Jambūdvīpa. At its root is a fire with seven flames. It is because this tree is a plakṣa tree that the island is called Plakṣadvīpa. Plakṣadvīpa was governed by Idhmajihva, one of the sons of Mahārāja Priyavrata. He endowed the seven islands with the names of his seven sons, divided the islands among the sons, and then retired from active life to engage in the devotional service of the Lord.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Tāvatā* means the same breadth of 100,000. Parikṣiptaḥ means surrounded by. *Upāste* means stands. Ākalayya means having offered.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

First he describes Plakṣa Island. As an example, just as Jambū is 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] wide surrounded by the salt ocean of identical width, even so the salt ocean is encircled by Plakṣa Island which is twice as broad, i.e. 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] similar to a trench by one’s outer garden. The Plakṣa tree is as high as the Jambū tree and it lends its name to the island. Agni resides at the bottom of the lustrous tree and he was the ruler of the island for a long time. Priyavrata’s son named Idhmajihva, divided the island into seven parts bearing the names of his sons and gave it to them. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Tavata Vistarena* = one 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. The Plakṣa has the same magnitude of Jambū. *Aakalayya* = having given.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Parikshipta* = surrounded by. *Upa* = in excess. *Akalayya* = having given.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tataḥ = from Jambū Island. *Dvigunavishalena* = having a breadth of 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\]. *Parikha* = a funnel-shaped trench filled with water to prevent enemy access. *Upa* = in excess. *Tatsya* = of Plakṣa Island. The names of the seven sons \[of King Sagara\] are the names of seven divisions.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

This is surrounded by the salt ocean 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] wide. The Plakṣa tree is responsible for the name of the island and is as high as the Jambū tree. *Saptajihva* = Agni. *Upaste* = stands.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This Jambū island is surrounded by the salt ocean of equal magnitude (100,000 *yojanas*) \[800,000 miles\] just as Meru is surrounded by Jambū Island. The example is not regarding the magnitude. Because all the undesirable things of Jambū Island entered into the ocean making it salty and of passionate (rajas) character.

*Tasya* = of the island. *Aakalaya* = having given. *Aatmayogena* = by meditation on God. Because of being Priyavrata’s sons, their rule extended to tens of thousands of years.

*Parikshipta* = encircled. Here what should be noted is this: the chariot designed by Priyavrata gained in speed day by day thus it did not move only in a particular trench. The wheels of his chariot were either reinforced or replaced each time so that they became bigger than the previous ones. In this way, the islands and oceans formed by the chariot’s wheels went on increasing in width twofold.

The height is that of the Jambū 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\]. The spread of the tree is also 1,100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\]. It is 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] thick at the bottom. Plakṣa lends its name to the island.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

After Idhmajihva gave the land to his sons, he absorbed himself in meditation and attained liberation.

### Text 3-4

*शिवं यवसं सुभद्रं शान्तं क्षेमममृतमभयमिति वर्षाणि तेषु गिरयो नद्यश्च*  
*सप्तैवाभिज्ञाताः ॥३॥ मणिकूटो वज्रकूट इन्द्रसेनो ज्योतिष्मान् सुपर्णो*  
*हिरण्यष्ठीवो मेघमाल इति सेतुशैलाः । अरुणा नृम्णाङ्गिरसी सावित्री सुप्तभाता*  
*ऋतम्भरा सत्यम्भरा इति महानद्यः । यासां जलोपस्पर्शनविधूतरजस्तमसो*  
*हंसपतङ्गोर्ध्वायनसत्याङ्गसंज्ञाश्चत्वारो वर्णाः सहस्रायुषो विबुधोपमसन्दर्शन*  
*प्रजननाः स्वर्गद्वारं त्रय्या विद्यया भगवन्तं त्रयीमयं सूर्यमात्मानं यजन्ते॥४॥*

*śivaṁ yavasaṁ subhadraṁ śāntaṁ kṣemam amṛtam abhayam iti varṣāṇi teṣu girayo nadyaś ca saptaivābhijñātāḥ; maṇikūṭo vajrakūṭa indraseno jyotiṣmān suparṇo hiraṇyaṣṭhīvo meghamāla iti setu-śailāḥ aruṇā nṛmṇāṅgirasī sāvitrī suptabhātā ṛtambharā satyambharā iti mahā-nadyaḥ; yāsāṁ jalopasparśana-vidhūta-rajas-tamaso haṁsa-pataṅgordhvāyana-satyāṅga-saṁjñāś catvāro varṇāḥ sahasrāyuṣo vibudhopama-sandarśana-prajananāḥ svarga-dvāraṁ trayyā vidyayā bhagavantaṁ trayīmayaṁ sūryam ātmānaṁ yajante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śivam—Śiva; yavasam—Yavasa; subhadram—Subhadra; śāntam—Śānta; kṣemam—Kṣema; amṛtam—Amṛta; abhayam—Abhaya; iti—thus; varṣāṇi—the tracts of land according to the names of the seven sons; teṣu—in them; girayaḥ—mountains; nadyaḥ ca—and rivers; sapta—seven; eva—indeed; abhijñātāḥ—are known; maṇi-kūṭaḥ—Maṇikūṭa; vajra-kūṭaḥ—Vajrakūṭa; indra-senaḥ—Indrasena; jyotiṣmān—Jyotiṣmān; suparṇaḥ—Suparṇa; hiraṇya-ṣṭhīvaḥ—Hiraṇyaṣṭhīva; megha-mālaḥ—Meghamāla; iti—thus; setu-śailāḥ—the ranges of mountains marking the borders of the varṣas; aruṇā—Aruṇā; nṛmṇā—Nṛmṇā; āṅgirasī—Āṅgirasī; sāvitrī—Sāvitrī; supta-bhātā—Suptabhātā; ṛtambharā—Ṛtambharā; satyambharā—Satyambharā; iti—thus; mahā-nadyaḥ—very large rivers; yāsām—of which; jala-upasparśana—simply by touching the water; vidhūta—washed off; rajaḥ-tamasaḥ—whose modes of passion and ignorance; haṁsa—Haṁsa; pataṅga—Pataṅga; ūrdhvāyana—Ūrdhvāyana; satyāṅga—Satyāṅga; saṁjñāḥ—named; catvāraḥ—four; varṇāḥ—castes or divisions of men; sahasra-āyuṣaḥ—living for one thousand years; vibudha-upama—similar to the demigods; sandarśana—in having very beautiful forms; prajananāḥ—and in producing children; svarga-dvāram—the gateway to the heavenly planets; trayyā vidyayā—by performing ritualistic ceremonies according to Vedic principles; bhagavantam—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; trayī-mayam—established in the Vedas; sūryam ātmānam—the Supersoul, represented by the sun-god; yajante—they worship.

**Перевод:**

**The seven islands \[varṣas\] are named according to the names of those seven sons—Śiva, Yavasa, Subhadra, Śānta, Kṣema, Amṛta and Abhaya. In those seven tracts of land, there are seven mountains and seven rivers. The mountains are named Maṇikūṭa, Vajrakūṭa, Indrasena, Jyotiṣmān, Suparṇa, Hiraṇyaṣṭhīva and Meghamāla, and the rivers are named Aruṇā, Nṛmṇā, Āṅgirasī, Sāvitrī, Suptabhātā, Ṛtambharā and Satyambharā. One can immediately be free from material contamination by touching or bathing in those rivers, and the four castes of people who live in Plakṣadvīpa—the Haṁsas, Pataṅgas, Ūrdhvāyanas and Satyāṅgas—purify themselves in that way. The inhabitants of Plakṣadvīpa live for one thousand years. They are beautiful like the demigods, and they also beget children like the demigods. By completely performing the ritualistic ceremonies mentioned in the Vedas and by worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead as represented by the sun-god, they attain the sun, which is a heavenly planet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Abhijnata* means famous. They \[the chief mountains\] are only seven in number—others are there in the thousands. Since it is stated that Mānasottara is circular these mountains in Plakṣa and the other five islands must be horizontal, touching the oceans on both sides. Otherwise, there cannot be seven divisions due to these mountains. In *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* it is said that these mountains are starting from the east.

Rajas \[the influence of the mode of passion\] and tamas \[the influence of the mode of ignorance\] are warded off by their \[the rivers’\] waters. There, the Hamsas, as *brāhmaṇa*, are good-looking, devoid of fatigue, without perspiration and endowed with the power to procreate. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

His sons names are Śiva, etc. There, the famous rivers and mountains are only seven in number. The frontier mountains are Manikuta and others while the rivers are Aruna and others. Śuka again praises the rivers.

The four divisions of people are purified by bathing in the rivers. The *brāhmaṇa*, known as Hamsas, are handsome like demigods and have good offspring. They worship Sūrya \[the sungod\], who constitutes the body of Paramātmā \[supersoul\], by performing rituals of the three *Vedas*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Abhijnatah =* famous or important. *Setashaila* = frontier mountains. Appearing like demigods and having good procreating power. *Suryatmanam* = of the form of Sūrya.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The mountains act as demarcating lines touching the oceans on both sides.

The Hamsas, etc. stand in the place of the Brahmana and others \[ksatriyas, vaisyas and śūdras\]. Their appearance is like that of demigods, and they possess the power to procreate.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Yavasa* should be read as *Yashasya* = famous. Only the important ones, like the sun, are counted, whereas the unimportant ones, such as stars, are not counted. Otherwise, if they were seven circular mountains not touching the ocean, they would have created eight divisions. The directions of “east and so on” stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* would then also not hold good.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The famous \[ones\] are seven only whereas the other less famous ones are many.

The Hamsas, etc. stand in the place of the Brahmana and others \[ksatriyas, vaisyas and śūdras\]. Their appearance is like that of demigods, and they possess the power to procreate. They live for a thousand years and, by means of the three *Vedas*, worship Sūrya, who grants heaven.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Manikuta, etc. are the mountains and Aruna, etc. are the rivers.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Śiva and others are the names of the varshas (divisions) and the frontier mountains and rivers are only seven in number. The not-so-famous ones are many. In *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* these divisions are stated to be in the order starting from the east and going clockwise.

The seven mountains are Manikuta, etc. and the the rivers are Aruna, etc.

### Text 5

*प्रत्नस्य विष्णो रूपं यत्सत्यस्यर्तस्य ब्रह्मणः ।*  
*अमृतस्य च मृत्योश्च सूर्यमात्मानमीमहीति ॥५॥*

*pratnasya viṣṇo rūpaṁ yat*  
*satyasyartasya brahmaṇaḥ*  
*amṛtasya ca mṛtyoś ca*  
*sūryam ātmānam īmahīti*

**Пословный перевод:**

pratnasya—of the oldest person; viṣṇoḥ—Lord Viṣṇu; rūpam—the form; yat—which; satyasya—of the Absolute Truth; ṛtasya—of dharma; brahmaṇaḥ—of the Supreme Brahman; amṛtasya—of the auspicious result; ca—and; mṛtyoḥ—of death (the inauspicious result); ca—and; sūryam—the demigod Sūrya; ātmānam—the Supersoul or origin of all souls; īmahi—we approach for shelter; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**\[This is the mantra by which the inhabitants of Plakṣadvīpa worship the Supreme Lord.\] Let us take shelter of the sun-god, who is a reflection of Lord Viṣṇu, the all-expanding Supreme Personality of Godhead, the oldest of all persons. Viṣṇu is the only worshipable Lord. He is the Vedas, He is religion, and He is the origin of all auspicious and inauspicious results.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The *mantras* referred to are also commented upon. “Pratnasya” means “of Viṣṇu, the most ancient one.” Sūrya is the form of Viṣṇu, We take refuge in him. How is he? He is the presiding deity of right conduct and other virtues. Satya means right conduct. Rta means right knowledge. Brahmanah means of knowledge of *Vedas*. Amrtasya means of good fruits. Mrtyoh means of bad fruits. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Rupam* = a deity form. *Tatra* = in Satyaloka etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

They chant a *mantra*. *Pratnasya* = of the beginnignless. *Satyasya* = of him who does not become transformed. *Rta* = holy deeds and their results. This worship has been explained in detail in the Upanishads in the *pratardana vidya* context.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Pratnasya* = of the ancient one who is responsible for the creation of the world. “We take refuge in that form of His because Viṣṇu is the *ātmā*  of all.” *Satyasya* = of he who has no bias. *Rtasya* = of he who has a soothing voice.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The *mantra* they chant is stated here. *Pratnasya* = of the beginningless; because He is the creator of the world. *Rtsya* - of the form of fructification of good deeds. *Amrtasya* = of *mokṣa* \[liberation\]. Mrtasya = of bondage. We take refuge in Sūrya who happens to be the Sharira (body) of Viṣṇu.

### Text 6

*प्लक्षादिषु पञ्चसु पुरुषाणामायुरिन्द्रियमोजः सहो बलं बुद्धिर्विक्रम इति च*  
*सर्वेषामौत्पत्तिकी सिद्धिरविशेषेण वर्तते ॥६॥*

*plakṣādiṣu pañcasu puruṣāṇām āyur indriyam ojaḥ saho balaṁ buddhir vikrama iti ca sarveṣām autpattikī siddhir aviśeṣeṇa vartate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

plakṣa-ādiṣu—in the islands headed by Plakṣa; pañcasu—five; puruṣāṇām—of the inhabitants; āyuḥ—long duration of life; indriyam—soundness of the senses; ojaḥ—bodily strength; sahaḥ—mental strength; balam—physical strength; buddhiḥ—intelligence; vikramaḥ—bravery; iti—thus; ca—also; sarveṣām—of all of them; autpattikī—inborn; siddhiḥ—perfection; aviśeṣeṇa—without distinction; vartate—exists.

**Перевод:**

**O King, longevity, sensory prowess, physical and mental strength, intelligence and bravery are naturally and equally manifested in all the inhabitants of the five islands headed by Plakṣadvīpa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

For people who live there, the siddhis \[mystic perfections\] are natural and in abundance.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Generally, for the people who live in Plakṣa and the other five islands, the mystic perfections are natural. These mountains are straight touching the ocean on both sides, otherwise there cannot be seven divisions. The divisions have been stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* as starting from the east, hence they must be straight.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“We take refuge in Sūrya, the ancient one who is the stimulating power of vocal and physical austerities.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The names of his sons and the divisions are Śiva, etc. The consistency of dynasties, places, rivers and mountains should be attributed to Priyavrata’s will as well as the presence of Bhagavan \[the Supreme Lord\] manifested within him.

The famous rivers and mountains are only seven in number although other rivers and mountains are also there.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Strength, valor, resistance, intellect, etc. are natual for those who live in Plakṣa and the other islands. All of them have the same age.

### Text 7

*प्लक्षः स्वसमानेनेक्षुरसोदेनावृतो यथा तथा द्वीपोऽपि*  
*शाल्मलो द्विगुणविशालः समानेन सुरोदेनावृतः परिवृङ्क्ते ॥७॥*

*plakṣaḥ sva-samānenekṣu-rasodenāvṛto yathā tathā dvīpo 'pi śālmalo dvi-guṇa-viśālaḥ samānena surodenāvṛtaḥ parivṛṅkte.*

**Пословный перевод:**

plakṣaḥ—the land known as Plakṣadvīpa; sva-samānena—equal in width; ikṣu-rasa—of sugarcane juice; udena—by an ocean; āvṛtaḥ—surrounded; yathā—just as; tathā—similarly; dvīpaḥ—another island; api—also; śālmalaḥ—known as Śālmala; dvi-guṇa-viśālaḥ—twice as big; samānena—equal in width; surā-udena—by an ocean of liquor; āvṛtaḥ—surrounded; parivṛṅkte—exists.

**Перевод:**

**Plakṣadvīpa is surrounded by an ocean of sugarcane juice, equal in breadth to the island itself. Similarly, there is then another island—Sālmalīdvīpa—twice as broad as Plakṣadvīpa \[400,000 yojanas, or 3,200,000 miles\] and surrounded by an equally broad body of water called Surāsāgara, the ocean that tastes like liquor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Dwigunavishala* = 400,000 *yojanas* \[3,200,000 miles\] broad. *Parivrntkte* = exists separately.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Thus, Plaksa Island has been described in detail. Now, by that example, Śuka describes the Shalmali Island. Just as Plakṣa is surrounded by Sugarcane Juice Ocean, which has an identical width of 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\], the Shalmali Island, which is 400,000 *yojanas* \[3,200,000 miles\] wide, is surrounded by Liquor \[Suroda\] Ocean of the same width.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Parivrttena* = circular. This should be borne in mind in all the islands.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Autpattiki* = natural, coming along with the birth.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Just as Plakṣa Island is encircled by the *sattvic* \[goodness\] Sugarcane Juice Ocean of 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] width, so Shalmala Island which is 400,000 *yojanas* \[93,200,000 miles\] wide is encircled by a tamasa \[ignorance\] wine-like water ocean. *Parivrnkta* = shines in all directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Just as Plaksa Island is surrounded by Sugarcane Juice Ocean, so the Shalmala Island, which is 400,000 *yojanas* \[3,200,000 miles\] wide, is surrounded by Suroda of an identical width.

### Text 8

*यत्र ह वै शाल्मली प्लक्षायामा यस्यां वाव किल निलयमाहुर्भगवतश्छन्दः*  
*स्तुतः पतत्त्रिराजस्य सा द्वीपहूतये उपलक्ष्यते ॥८॥*

*yatra ha vai śālmalī plakṣāyāmā yasyāṁ vāva kila nilayam āhur bhagavataś chandaḥ-stutaḥ patattri-rājasya sā dvīpa-hūtaye upalakṣyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatra—where; ha vai—certainly; śālmalī—a śālmalī tree; plakṣa-āyāmā—as big as the plakṣa tree (one hundred yojanas broad and eleven hundred yojanas high); yasyām—in which; vāva kila—indeed; nilayam—rest or living place; āhuḥ—they say; bhagavataḥ—of the most powerful; chandaḥ-stutaḥ—who worships the Lord by Vedic prayers; patattri-rājasya—of Garuḍa, the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu; sā—that tree; dvīpa-hūtaye—for the name of the island; upalakṣyate—is distinguished.\]

**Перевод:**

**On Sālmalīdvīpa there is a śālmalī tree, from which the island takes its name. That tree is as broad and tall as the plakṣa tree—in other words 100 yojanas \[800 miles\] broad and 1,100 yojanas \[8,800 miles\] tall. Learned scholars say that this gigantic tree is the residence of Garuḍa, the king of all birds and carrier of Lord Viṣṇu. In that tree, Garuḍa offers Lord Viṣṇu his Vedic prayers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Yatra* = in which Island. *Shalmali* = silkcotton tree. The *Vedas* enjoin that the parts of the *Veda* are the limbs of Garuḍa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now the tree is described. The silk cotton tree is as large as the island and at the bottom of the tree is the abode of Garuḍa, king of birds. He is called chandahstut because his limbs are the meters of the *Vedas*. That Shalmali tree accounts for the name of the island.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Where the Shalmali tree grew—that island is called Shalmala. It is one and a half times higher than the Plakṣa tree. Garuḍa is called *chandahshtut* because he is praised by *Vedas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Pratnasya* = of the *purāṇa puruṣa* \[oldest person\]. We take refuge in the sun who resides in Satya \[goodness\] and other virtues. Brahma = *Vedas*. *Amrtasya* = of good result. *Mrtyoh* = of bad results. Garuḍa is known as Chandrashut as he is praised by the *Vedas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The famous silk cotton tree, 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] thick, 1100 *yojanas* \[8,800 miles\] high (like the Plakṣa Tree) lends its name to the island. It is the abode of Garuḍa, praised by the *Vedas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

There is a silk cotton tree in that island which has the same width as that of the Plakṣa tree. It is said to be the abode of Garuḍa, who is praised by the *Vedas*.

### Text 9

*तद्द्वीपाधिपतिः प्रियव्रतात्मजो यज्ञबाहुः स्वसुतेभ्यः सप्तभ्यस्तन्नामानि*  
*सप्तवर्षाणि व्यभजत्सुरोचनं सौमनस्यं रमणकं देववर्षं पारिभद्रमाप्यायनम*  
*विज्ञातमिति ॥९॥*

*tad-dvīpādhipatiḥ priyavratātmajo yajñabāhuḥ sva-sutebhyaḥ saptabhyas tan-nāmāni sapta-varṣāṇi vyabhajat surocanaṁ saumanasyaṁ ramaṇakaṁ deva-varṣaṁ pāribhadram āpyāyanam avijñātam iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-dvīpa-adhipatiḥ—the master of that island; priyavrata-ātmajaḥ—the son of Mahārāja Priyavrata; yajña-bāhuḥ—named Yajñabāhu; sva-sutebhyaḥ—unto his sons; saptabhyaḥ—seven in number; tat-nāmāni—having names according to their names; sapta-varṣāṇi—seven tracts of land; vyabhajat—divided; surocanam—Surocana; saumanasyam—Saumanasya; ramaṇakam—Ramaṇaka; deva-varṣam—Deva-varṣa; pāribhadram—Pāribhadra; āpyāyanam—Āpyāyana; avijñātam—Avijñāta; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**The son of Mahārāja Priyavrata named Yajñabāhu, the master of Sālmalīdvīpa, divided the island into seven tracts of land, which he gave to his seven sons. The names of those divisions, which correspond to the names of the sons, are Surocana, Saumanasya, Ramaṇaka, Deva-varṣa, Pāribhadra, Āpyāyana and Avijñāta.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tannamani* = names of the sons.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The ruler of Island, Yajnabahu, divided the Island into seven parts and gave it to his sons bearing the same names. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The islands’ names are Surochana, etc.

### Text 10

*तेषु वर्षाद्रयो नद्यश्च सप्तैवाभिज्ञाताः स्वरसः शतशृङ्गो वामदेवः कुन्दो*  
*मुकुन्दः पुष्पवर्षः सहस्रश्रुतिरिति । अनुमतिः सिनीवाली सरस्वती कुहू रजनी*  
*नन्दा राकेति ॥१०॥*

*teṣu varṣādrayo nadyaś ca saptaivābhijñātāḥ svarasaḥ śataśṛṅgo vāmadevaḥ kundo mukundaḥ puṣpa-varṣaḥ sahasra-śrutir iti; anumatiḥ sinīvālī sarasvatī kuhū rajanī nandā rāketi*  
*.*

**Пословный перевод:**

teṣu—in those tracts of land; varṣa-adrayaḥ—mountains; nadyaḥ ca—as well as rivers; sapta eva—seven in number; abhijñātāḥ—understood; svarasaḥ—Svarasa; śata-śṛṅgaḥ—Śataśṛṅga; vāma-devaḥ—Vāmadeva; kundaḥ—Kunda; mukundaḥ—Mukunda; puṣpa-varṣaḥ—Puṣpa-varṣa; sahasra-śrutiḥ—Sahasra-śruti; iti—thus; anumatiḥ—Anumati; sinīvālī—Sinīvālī; sarasvatī—Sarasvatī; kuhū—Kuhū; rajanī—Rajanī; nandā—Nandā; rākā—Rākā; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**In those tracts of land there are seven mountains—Svarasa, Śataśṛṅga, Vāmadeva, Kunda, Mukunda, Puṣpa-varṣa and Sahasra-śruti. There are also seven rivers—Anumati, Sinīvālī, Sarasvatī, Kuhū, Rajanī, Nandā and Rākā. They are still existing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Teshu* = in those divisions.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Their names are Surochana and so on. Although other not-so-famous rivers and mountains exist, there are seven famous rivers and mountains here headed by Svarasa and Anumati respectively.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The *upāsanā mantra* is stated. We take refuge in Sūrya. The reason is we get everything from him. Satyasya =of him who has no bias. Rtasya= who speaks consisely and pleasingly. He is the promulgator of the *Vedas* from which all disciplines and austerities emerge. Actually Viṣṇu is the propounder of the *Vedas*. But surya is Viṣṇu’s own self. So surya is said to be the promulgator of *Vedas*.

*Svarasa*, etc. are the mountains. Anumati etc., the rivers.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

There are seven frontier mountains and seven great rivers. The mountains are Swarsa etc. the rivers are Anumati etc.

### Text 11

*तद्वर्षपुरुषाः श्रुतधरवीर्यधरवसुन्धरेषन्धरसंज्ञा भगवन्तं वेदमयं सोममात्मानं*  
*वेदेन यजन्ते ॥११॥*

*tad-varṣa-puruṣāḥ śrutadhara-vīryadhara-vasundhareṣandhara-saṁjñā bhagavantaṁ vedamayaṁ somam ātmānaṁ vedena yajante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-varṣa-puruṣāḥ—the residents of those tracts of land; śrutadhara—Śrutadhara; vīryadhara—Vīryadhara; vasundhara—Vasundhara; iṣandhara—Iṣandhara; saṁjñāḥ—known as; bhagavantam—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; veda-mayam—fully conversant with the Vedic knowledge; somam ātmānam—represented by the living entity known as Soma; vedena—by following the Vedic rules and regulations; yajante—they worship.

**Перевод:**

**Strictly following the cult of varṇāśrama-dharma, the inhabitants of those islands, who are known as Śrutidharas, Vīryadharas, Vasundharas and Iṣandharas, all worship the expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead named Soma, the moon-god.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Because Garuḍa praises Viṣṇu by various Chandas (Vedic *mantras*), he is called Chandahstut. *Nilayanam* means the abode of Garuḍa. The pronoun *sa* means Shalmali. *Hutaye* means for ordinary usage.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The four divisions there are shrutadhara and so on. They worship Soma who is extolled in the *Vedas* and happens to be the sharira \[body\] of the supersoul \[Paramātmā\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The people in the divisions of Shalmali island. Vedamayam = propounded by the *Vedas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Plakshyama* means having the width of the Plakṣa Island. Because of the vastness, ancient people say that there is the abode of Garuḍa, the king of birds. Of him (Garuḍa), who is praised by the *Vedas* and who also praises Viṣṇu with Vedic hymns.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

*Autpattiki* = natural. *Avisheshena* = equal.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The people of that island, who use social divisions such as Shrutadhara, etc., indicating *brāhmaṇa*, ksatriya, etc. They worship soma as taught in the *Vedas*. By his rays, he gives food to the demigods and Pitra \[forefathers\] in the bright half and dark half of the month. May he be bountiful to us.

### Text 12

*स्वगोभिः पितृदेवेभ्यो विभजन् कृष्णशुक्लयोः ।*  
*प्रजानां सर्वासां राजान्धः सोमो न आस्त्विति ॥१२॥*

*sva-gobhiḥ pitṛ-devebhyo*  
*vibhajan kṛṣṇa-śuklayoḥ*  
*prajānāṁ sarvāsāṁ rājā-*  
*ndhaḥ somo na āstv iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

sva-gobhiḥ—by expansion of his own illuminating rays; pitṛ-devebhyaḥ—unto the pitās and the demigods; vibhajan—dividing; kṛṣṇa-śuklayoḥ—into the two fortnights, dark and light; prajānām—of the citizens; sarvāsām—of all; rājā—the king; andhaḥ—food grains; somaḥ—the moon-god; naḥ—toward us; āstu—let him remain favorable; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**\[The inhabitants of Śālmalīdvīpa worship the demigod of the moon in the following words.\] By his own rays, the moon-god has divided the month into two fortnights, known as śukla and kṛṣṇa, for the distribution of food grains to the pitās and the demigods. The demigod of the moon is he who divides time, and he is the king of all the residents of the universe. We therefore pray that he may remain our king and guide, and we offer him our respectful obeisances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sva-gobhiḥ means by his rays. *Andah* means food. “Let the king Soma be be bountiful towards us. The Sandhi in Astu (taken for Aastu) is not intended.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

By his rays the moon gives food to the demigods in the bright half and the pitrs in the dark half. Therefore, let Soma be the king of us all, and may he be bountiful to us.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Soma is the food given to the demigods and pitrs in *suklapaksha* \[bright fortnight\] and Kṛṣṇa paksha \[dark fortnight\] respectively through his rays. May he be bountiful to us.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sva-gobhiḥ = by his rays. *Andhah* = food. May Soma be our king and be inclined towards us.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

If there had been *sandhi*, the reading “*no*” would have spoiled the meter.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Andhah* = food. May he, the king, be bountiful towards us.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The people of four castes who live there are absorbed in the worship of Chandra. Their *mantra* is Svagobhih and so on. During Shuklapaksha he gives food to the gods and during Kṛṣṇa Paksha to pitrs. He gives food to all other creatures also. Because the plants scorched by sun’s rays get rejuvinated by the moon’s rays and produce food grains and other things which is food for many creatures. “May he be our protector.”

### Text 13

*एवं सुरोदाद्बहिस्तद्द्विगुणः समानेनावृतो घृतोदेन यथापूर्वः कुशद्वीपो यस्मिन्*  
*कुशस्तम्बो देवकृतस्तद्द्वीपाख्याकरो ज्वलन इवापरः स्वशष्परोचिषा दिशो*  
*विराजयति ॥१३॥*

*evaṁ surodād bahis tad-dvi-guṇaḥ samānenāvṛto ghṛtodena yathā-pūrvaḥ kuśa-dvīpo yasmin kuśa-stambo deva-kṛtas tad-dvīpākhyākaro jvalana ivāparaḥ sva-śaṣpa-rociṣā diśo virājayati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; surodāt—from the ocean of liquor; bahiḥ—outside; tat-dvi-guṇaḥ—twice that; samānena—equal in width; āvṛtaḥ—surrounded; ghṛta-udena—an ocean of clarified butter; yathā-pūrvaḥ—as previously with Sālmalīdvīpa; kuśa-dvīpa—the island called Kuśadvīpa; yasmin—in which; kuśa-stambaḥ—kuśa grass; deva-kṛtaḥ—created by the supreme will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tat-dvīpa-ākhyā-karaḥ—giving the island its name; jvalanaḥ—fire; iva—like; aparaḥ—another; sva-śaṣpa-rociṣā—by the effulgence of the young sprouting grass; diśaḥ—all directions; virājayati—illuminates.

**Перевод:**

**Outside the ocean of liquor is another island, known as Kuśadvīpa, which is 800,000 yojanas \[6,400,000 miles\] wide, twice as wide as the ocean of liquor. As Śālmalīdvīpa is surrounded by a liquor ocean, Kuśadvīpa is surrounded by an ocean of liquid ghee as broad as the island itself. On Kuśadvīpa there are clumps of kuśa grass, from which the island takes its name. This kuśa grass, which was created by the demigods by the will of the Supreme Lord, appears like a second form of fire, but with very mild and pleasing flames. Its young shoots illuminate all directions.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Evam* = like before. *Tasmat* = from Shalmali Island. *Dviguna* = 800,000 *yojanas* \[6,400,000 miles\] broad. *Yasmin* = in which island. *Kusastamba* = a grove of kusa grass. Accounts for the name of the island.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

By the example of Shalmali Island, Śuka describes the Kusa Island. Just like the Salmali Island, the Kusa Island is surrounded by the ocean of ghee, 800,000 *yojanas* \[6,400,000 miles\] wide. A grove of kusha grass shining like the flames of fire lends its name to the island. It illumines all directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Like previous, i.e. as Shalmala Island surrounded by Suroda, beyond that Kusha Island 800,000 *yojanas* \[6,400,000 miles\] wide is encircled by a sattvic ocean of ghee equally wide.

A kusa grove, created by God, shining like fire and illuminating all directions by lustre of its tender sprouts, lends its name to the island.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Beyond Shalmali island, there is Kusa Island, 800,000 *yojanas* \[6,400,000 miles\] wide and surrounded by the ocean of Ghee of equal width. There is a grove of Kusa grass, which shines like fire and lends its name to the island. The tender sprouts of the grove resemble flames of fire as they shine.

### Text 14

*तद्द्वीपपतिः प्रैयव्रतो राजन् हिरण्यरेता नाम स्वं द्वीपं सप्तभ्यः स्वपुत्रेभ्यो यथाभागं*  
*विभज्य स्वयं तप आतिष्ठत वसुवसुदानदृढरुचिनाभिगुप्तस्तुत्यव्रतविविक्तवाम*  
*देवनामभ्यः ॥१४॥*

*tad-dvīpa-patiḥ praiyavrato rājan hiraṇyaretā nāma svaṁ dvīpaṁ saptabhyaḥ sva-putrebhyo yathā-bhāgaṁ vibhajya svayaṁ tapa ātiṣṭhata vasu-vasudāna-dṛḍharuci-nābhigupta-stutyavrata-vivikta-vāmadeva-nāmabhyaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-dvīpa-patiḥ—the master of that island; praiyavrataḥ—the son of Mahārāja Priyavrata; rājan—O King; hiraṇyaretā—Hiraṇyaretā; nāma—named; svam—his own; dvīpam—island; saptabhyaḥ—unto seven; sva-putrebhyaḥ—his own sons; yathā-bhāgam—according to division; vibhajya—dividing; svayam—himself; tapaḥ ātiṣṭhata—engaged in austerities; vasu—unto Vasu; vasudāna—Vasudāna; dṛḍharuci—Dṛḍharuci; nābhi-gupta—Nābhigupta; stutya-vrata—Stutyavrata; vivikta—Vivikta; vāma-deva—Vāmadeva; nāmabhyaḥ—named.

**Перевод:**

**O King, another son of Mahārāja Priyavrata, Hiraṇyaretā, was the king of this island. He divided it into seven parts, which he delivered to his seven sons according to the rights of inheritance. The King then retired from family life to engage in austerities. The names of those sons are Vasu, Vasudāna, Dṛḍharuci, Stutyavrata, Nābhigupta, Vivikta and Vāmadeva.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tatdvipapati* = the lord of Kusa Island. *Rajanniti* = this is the course of the kings.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Its ruler, Hiranyareta, divided the island into seven parts and gave it to his sons of the same name as in the previous Islands. Then Hiranyareta engaged himself in penance.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Vasu, etc. are the names of his sons for whom he divided his kingdom. Then he observed penances.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Hiranyareta, the ruler of that island, divided and gave the island to his seven sons and then engaged himself in penance.

### Text 15

*तेषां वर्षेषु सीमागिरयो नद्यश्चाभिज्ञाताः सप्त सप्तैव चक्रश्चतुःशृङ्गः कपि*  
*लश्चित्रकूटो देवानीक ऊर्ध्वरोमा द्रविण इति रसकुल्या मधुकुल्या मित्रविन्दा*  
*श्रुतविन्दा देवगर्भा घृतच्युता मन्त्रमालेति ॥१५॥*

*teṣāṁ varṣeṣu sīmā-girayo nadyaś cābhijñātāḥ sapta saptaiva cakraś catuḥśṛṅgaḥ kapilaś citrakūṭo devānīka ūrdhvaromā draviṇa iti rasakulyā madhukulyā mitravindā śrutavindā devagarbhā ghṛtacyutā mantramāleti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

teṣām—all those sons; varṣeṣu—in the tracts of land; sīmā-girayaḥ—border mountains; nadyaḥ ca—as well as rivers; abhijñātāḥ—known; sapta—seven; sapta—seven; eva—certainly; cakraḥ—Cakra; catuḥ-śṛṅgaḥ—Catuḥ-śṛṅga; kapilaḥ—Kapila; citra-kūṭaḥ—Citrakūṭa; devānīkaḥ—Devānīka; ūrdhva-romā—Ūrdhvaromā; draviṇaḥ—Draviṇa; iti—thus; rasa-kulyā—Ramakulyā; madhu-kulyā—Madhukulyā; mitra-vindā—Mitravindā; śruta-vindā—Śrutavindā; deva-garbhā—Devagarbhā; ghṛta-cyutā—Ghṛtacyutā; mantra-mālā—Mantramālā; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**In those seven islands there are seven boundary mountains, known as Cakra, Catuḥśṛṅga, Kapila, Citrakūṭa, Devānīka, Ūrdhvaromā and Draviṇa. There are also seven rivers, known as Ramakulyā, Madhukulyā, Mitravindā, Śrutavindā, Devagarbhā, Ghṛtacyutā and Mantramālā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Teṣām = of Vasu and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Vasu, etc. are his sons. *Cakra*, etc. are the seven mountains.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Yathapurva* = like Shalmala surrounded by Suroda. *Sashpa* = tender grass. By their luster.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The names of the divisions are Surochana and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The names of his sons are *Punarvasu*, etc. Seven mountains and seven rivers are famous there—i.e. *Cakra*, etc. and Rasakulya, etc. respectively.

### Text 16

*यासां पयोभिः कुशद्वीपौकसः कुशलकोविदाभियुक्तकुलकसंज्ञा भगवन्तं*  
*जातवेदसरूपिणं कर्मकौशलेन यजन्ते ॥१६॥*

*yāsāṁ payobhiḥ kuśadvīpaukasaḥ kuśala-kovidābhiyukta-kulaka-saṁjñā bhagavantaṁ jātaveda-sarūpiṇaṁ karma-kauśalena yajante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāsām—of which; payobhiḥ—by the water; kuśa-dvīpa-okasaḥ—the inhabitants of the island known as Kuśadvīpa; kuśala—Kuśala; kovida—Kovida; abhiyukta—Abhiyukta; kulaka—Kulaka; saṁjñāḥ—named; bhagavantam—unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; jātaveda—the demigod of fire; sa-rūpiṇam—manifesting the form; karma-kauśalena—by expertise in ritualistic ceremonies; yajante—they worship.

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of the island of Kuśadvīpa are celebrated as the Kuśalas, Kovidas, Abhiyuktas and Kulakas. They are like the brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras respectively. By bathing in the waters of those rivers, they all become purified. They are expert in performing ritualistic ceremonies according to the orders of the Vedic scriptures. Thus they worship the Lord in His aspect as the demigod of fire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In this manner, Kusa Island is encircled by the ghee ocean which is beyond Sauroda Ocean. *Shashpani* means tender sprouts.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Rasakulya, etc. are the great rivers. The people who live there are sanctified by these rivers. Their divisions are *kushala*, etc. They worship God in the form of Agni by their excellent deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Shashpa* = tender sprouts.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Yasam* = of Rasakulya and others. *Jatavedasvarupinam* = firegod, worshiped by exquisite deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Svashasparochisha = by the lustre of the tender grass contained in it.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

It should be appended that they get purified by the waters of these rivers. Kushala, Kovida, etc. stand in place of the four castes *brāhmaṇa*, etc. *Jataveda* = Agni. They worship and please him by the exquisiteness of their sacrifices.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The people who lived there are of four divisions, i.e. *kushala*, in place of *brāhmaṇa* and other castes. The rivers purify them as they bathe in the waters. By their excellent deeds, they worship Agni, who is the body of Viṣṇu.

### Text 17

*परस्य ब्रह्मणः साक्षाज्जातवेदोऽसि हव्यवाट् ।*  
*देवानां पुरुषाङ्गानां यज्ञेन पुरुषं यजेति ॥१७॥*

*parasya brahmaṇaḥ sākṣāj*  
*jāta-vedo 'si havyavāṭ*  
*devānāṁ puruṣāṅgānāṁ*  
*yajñena puruṣaṁ yajeti*

**Пословный перевод:**

parasya—of the Supreme; brahmaṇaḥ—Brahman; sākṣāt—directly; jāta-vedaḥ—O fire-god; asi—you are; havyavāṭ—the carrier of Vedic offerings of grains and ghee; devānām—of all the demigods; puruṣa-aṅgānām—who are limbs of the Supreme Person; yajñena—by performing the ritualistic sacrifices; puruṣam—to the Supreme person; yaja—please carry oblations; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**\[This is the mantra by which the inhabitants of Kuśadvīpa worship the fire-god.\] O fire-god, you are a part of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, and you carry to Him all the offerings of sacrifices. Therefore we request you to offer to the Supreme Personality of Godhead the yajñic ingredients we are offering the demigods, for the Lord is the real enjoyer.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Dear Agni, you are the carrier of Havis \[offerings of ghee\] to Lord Hari.” Thus, by means of sacrifices to the demigods, worship Hari only. The purport is, “I offer to the whole what is offered to the limbs.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Havyavat* = the carrier of oblations. “Because you carry oblations to even Hari.” *Yajña*= sacrifice, i.e. that which is placed in thy hand is given to Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The hymn is stated: “You are the carrier of oblations to God. So worship Hari only through the sacrifices offered to other demigods.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Dear Agni, you are the carrier of oblations to Nārāyaṇa and other gods. Be present in us and by our good deeds worship Viṣṇu who bears the name Yajña.”

### Text 18

*तथा घृतोदाद्बहिः क्रौञ्चद्वीपो द्विगुणः स्वमानेन क्षीरोदेन परित उपकॢप्तो वृतो*  
*यथा कुशद्वीपो घृतोदेन यस्मिन् क्रौञ्चो नाम पर्वतराजो द्वीपनामनिर्वर्तक*  
*आस्ते ॥१८॥*

*tathā ghṛtodād bahiḥ krauñcadvīpo dvi-guṇaḥ sva-mānena kṣīrodena parita upakḷpto vṛto yathā kuśadvīpo ghṛtodena yasmin krauñco nāma parvata-rājo dvīpa-nāma-nirvartaka āste.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tathā—so also; ghṛta-udāt—from the ocean of clarified butter; bahiḥ—outside; krauñca-dvīpaḥ—another island, known as Krauñcadvīpa; dvi-guṇaḥ—twice as big; sva-mānena—as the same measurement; kṣīra-udena—by an ocean of milk; paritaḥ—all around; upakḷptaḥ—surrounded; vṛtaḥ—surrounded; yathā—like; kuśa-dvīpaḥ—the island known as Kuśadvīpa; ghṛta-udena—by an ocean of clarified butter; yasmin—in which; krauñcaḥ nāma—named Krauñca; parvata-rājaḥ—a king of mountains; dvīpa-nāma—the name of the island; nirvartakaḥ—bringing about; āste—exists.

**Перевод:**

**Outside the ocean of clarified butter is another island, known as Krauñcadvīpa, which has a width of 1,600,000 yojanas \[12,800,000 miles\], twice the width of the ocean of clarified butter. As Kuśadvīpa is surrounded by an ocean of clarified butter, Krauñcadvīpa is surrounded by an ocean of milk as broad as the island itself. On Krauñcadvīpa there is a great mountain known as Krauñca, from which the island takes its name.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Upaklpta* means “surrounded by—just as Kusa Island is surrounded by the ocean of ghee.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Krauncha Island is described by the previous example. Krauncha Island is 1,600,000 *yojanas* \[12,800,000 miles\] wide and surrounded by the ocean of milk of equal magnitude. The mountain Krauncha lends its name to the island.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Kshirodena = by the ocean of milk. This should be interpreted as per the references given by the Acharya.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Upaklpta* = surrounded. *Vrata* is construed with the next words.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It means beyond the ocean of ghee and twice as broad as Kusa Island (1,600,000 *yojanas* \[12,800,000 miles\] broad). Accounts for the name of the island.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Avaklpta* = surrounded by.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Beyond the Ghee Ocean lies Krauncha Island 1,600,000 *yojanas* \[12,800,000 miles\] wide encircled by the Milk Ocean which is equally wide. Milk means milk-like water and not actual milk. The famous mountain Krauncha which is situated in the island lends its name to the island.

### Text 19

*योऽसौ गुहप्रहरणोन्मथितनितम्बकुञ्जोऽपि क्षीरोदेनासिच्यमानो भगवता*  
*वरुणेनाभिगुप्तो विभयो बभूव ॥१९॥*

*yo 'sau guha-praharaṇonmathita-nitamba-kuñjo 'pi kṣīrodenā-sicyamāno bhagavatā varuṇenābhigupto vibhayo babhūva.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yaḥ—which; asau—that (mountain); guha-praharaṇa—by the weapons of Kārttikeya, the son of Lord Śiva; unmathita—shaken; nitamba-kuñjaḥ—whose trees and vegetables along the slopes; api—although; kṣīra-udena—by the ocean of milk; āsicyamānaḥ—being always bathed; bhagavatā—by the greatly powerful; varuṇena—the demigod known as Varuṇa; abhiguptaḥ—protected; vibhayaḥ babhūva—has become fearless.

**Перевод:**

**Although the vegetables living on the slopes of Mount Krauñca were attacked and devastated by the weapons of Kārttikeya, the mountain has become fearless because it is always bathed on all sides by the ocean of milk and protected by Varuṇadeva.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Whose lower regions are inflicted by the weapons of Guha, brought up by Kārttikeya.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

This Krauncha Mountain was afflicted in the lower regions by the weapons of Guha. The yogurt’s soothing effect added to Varuna’s blessing has made the mountain fearless.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The lower regions and groves of which are bombarded by the weapons of Shanmukha. Being splashed by the ocean of milk.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Parivrnkte* = exists separately; the root belongs to *Rudh* group; the *atmanepada* is Vedic.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Guha = Kārttikeya. Vibhaya = devoid of fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

This Krauncha. *Ayudhena* = by the weapons operated to kill Tarakasura. *Nitamba* = lower regions. *Kunja* = inner places covered with leaves from outside. *Vibhaya* = devoid of fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Whose lower regions and groves are attacked by the weapons of Shanmukha.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The Krauncha mountain was afflicted in its lower region and groves by Guha’s weapons. It then became immersed in the milk ocean and Varuna offered protection. Now, the mountain stands fearless.

### Text 20

*तस्मिन्नपि प्रैयव्रतो घृतपृष्ठो नामाधिपतिः स्वे द्वीपे वर्षाणि सप्त विभज्य*  
*तेषु पुत्रनामसु सप्त रिक्थादान्वर्षपान्निवेश्य स्वयं भगवान्भगवतः परमकल्याण*  
*यशस आत्मभूतस्य हरेश्चरणारविन्दमुपजगाम ॥२०॥*

*tasminn api praiyavrato ghṛtapṛṣṭho nāmādhipatiḥ sve dvīpe varṣāṇi sapta vibhajya teṣu putra-nāmasu sapta rikthādān varṣapān niveśya svayaṁ bhagavān bhagavataḥ parama-kalyāṇa-yaśasa ātma-bhūtasya hareś caraṇāravindam upajagāma.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasmin—in that island; api—also; praiyavrataḥ—the son of Mahārāja Priyavrata; ghṛta-pṛṣṭhaḥ—Ghṛtapṛṣṭha; nāma—named; adhipatiḥ—the king of that island; sve—his own; dvīpe—in the island; varṣāṇi—tracts of land; sapta—seven; vibhajya—dividing; teṣu—in each of them; putra-nāmasu—possessing the names of his sons; sapta—seven; rikthā-dān—sons; varṣa-pān—the masters of the varṣas; niveśya—appointing; svayam—himself; bhagavān—very powerful; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; parama-kalyāṇa-yaśasaḥ—whose glories are so auspicious; ātma-bhūtasya—the soul of all souls; hareḥ caraṇa-aravindam—the lotus feet of the Lord; upajagāma—took shelter at.

**Перевод:**

**The ruler of this island was another son of Mahārāja Priyavrata. His name was Ghṛtapṛṣṭha, and he was a very learned scholar. He also divided his own island among his seven sons. After dividing the island into seven parts, named according to the names of his sons, Ghṛtapṛṣṭha Mahārāja completely retired from family life and took shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord, the soul of all souls, who has all auspicious qualities. Thus he attained perfection.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Even in that Island Grihitaprshta divided it into seven parts and gave it to his seven sons as in the previous islands. Then, he performed penance with great devotion and attained the feet of God.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Ghritaprsta is ruler of that island. He also divided and distributed his kingdom to his seven sons and himself went to a penance grove to perform meditation on Lord Hari. For what effect? Because Hari is the remover of all miseries of bondage. Even listening to the fame of Hari removes all the distress of bondage thus of what is Hari Himself incapable? Kala, karma and swabhava which are the causes of distress, do not trouble the souls as they are all his own forms. How did he get such a sublime knowledge? By the grace of Hari only did he get the knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Even in that island Ghrta Prista, Priyavrata’s son, divided it into seven parts and gave it to his sons bearing the same names as that of the parts. For himself, he performed meditation and attained the beautiful feet of Hari

### Text 21

*आमो मधुरुहो मेघपृष्ठः सुधामा भ्राजिष्ठो लोहितार्णो वनस्पतिरिति घृतपृष्ठसु*  
*तास्तेषां वर्षगिरयः सप्त सप्तैव नद्यश्चाभिख्याताः शुक्लो वर्धमानो भोजन*  
*उपबर्हिणो नन्दो नन्दनः सर्वतोभद्र इति अभया अमृतौघा आर्यका तीर्थवती*  
*रूपवती पवित्रवती शुक्लेति ॥२१॥*

*āmo madhuruho meghapṛṣṭhaḥ sudhāmā bhrājiṣṭho lohitārṇo vanaspatir iti ghṛtapṛṣṭha-sutās teṣāṁ varṣa-girayaḥ sapta saptaiva nadyaś cābhikhyātāḥ śuklo vardhamāno bhojana upabarhiṇo nando nandanaḥ sarvatobhadra iti abhayā amṛtaughā āryakā tīrthavatī rūpavatī pavitravatī śukleti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

āmaḥ—Āma; madhu-ruhaḥ—Madhuruha; megha-pṛṣṭhaḥ—Meghapṛṣṭha; sudhāmā—Sudhāmā; bhrājiṣṭhaḥ—Bhrājiṣṭha; lohitārṇaḥ—Lohitārṇa; vanaspatiḥ—Vanaspati; iti—thus; ghṛtapṛṣṭha-sutāḥ—the sons of Ghṛtapṛṣṭha; teṣām—of those sons; varṣa-girayaḥ—boundary hills of the tracts of land; sapta—seven; sapta—seven; eva—also; nadyaḥ—rivers; ca—and; abhikhyātāḥ—celebrated; śuklaḥ vardhamānaḥ—Śukla and Vardhamāna; bhojanaḥ—Bhojana; upabarhiṇaḥ—Upabarhiṇa; nandaḥ—Nanda; nandanaḥ—Nandana; sarvataḥ-bhadraḥ—Sarvatobhadra; iti—thus; abhayā—Abhayā; amṛtaughā—Amṛtaughā; āryakā—Āryakā; tīrthavatī—Tīrthavatī; rūpavatī—Rūpavatī; pavitravatī—Pavitravatī; śuklā—Śuklā; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**The sons of Mahārāja Ghṛtapṛṣṭha were named Āma, Madhuruha, Meghapṛṣṭha, Sudhāmā, Bhrājiṣṭha, Lohitārṇa and Vanaspati. In their island there are seven mountains, which indicate the boundaries of the seven tracts of land, and there are also seven rivers. The mountains are named Śukla, Vardhamāna, Bhojana, Upabarhiṇa, Nanda, Nandana and Sarvatobhadra. The rivers are named Abhayā, Amṛtaughā, Āryakā, Tīrthavatī, Rūpavatī, Pavitravatī and Śuklā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Lord knows on His own. Whose fame is very sacred.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The names of his sons are Amogha and so on. There are seven famous mountains and rivers—Sukla, etc. are the mountains and Abhaya, etc are the rivers.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Rikthadan* = sons.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Bhagavan* = one who has knowledge of creation, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Bhagavan* means one who has the knowledge of creation and so on. Bhagavan also means endowed with the six virtues of Aishwarya \[wealth\], *dharma* \[steadfast\], fame, lustre, knowledge and the absence of desire. He took refuge in the lotus feet of Hari, the remover of bondage.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Ama, etc. are the names of his sons. The frontier mountains there are seven. Other mountains are also there but not so famous. The names of the seven famous mountains are Sukla, etc.

### Text 22

*यासामम्भः पवित्रममलमुपयुञ्जानाः पुरुषऋषभद्रविणदेवकसंज्ञा वर्षपुरुषा*  
*आपोमयं देवमपां पूर्णेनाञ्जलिना यजन्ते ॥२२॥*

*yāsām ambhaḥ pavitram amalam upayuñjānāḥ puruṣa-ṛṣabha-draviṇa-devaka-saṁjñā varṣa-puruṣā āpomayaṁ devam apāṁ pūrṇenāñjalinā yajante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāsām—of all the rivers; ambhaḥ—the water; pavitram—very sanctified; amalam—very clean; upayuñjānāḥ—using; puruṣa—Puruṣa; ṛṣabha—Ṛṣabha; draviṇa—Draviṇa; devaka—Devaka; saṁjñāḥ—endowed with the names; varṣa-puruṣāḥ—the inhabitants of those varṣas; āpaḥ-mayam—Varuṇa, the lord of water; devam—as the worshipable deity; apām—of water; pūrṇena—with full; añjalinā—folded palms; yajante—do worship.

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of Krauñcadvīpa are divided into four castes, called the Puruṣas, Ṛṣabhas, Draviṇas and Devakas. Using the waters of those sanctified rivers, they worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead by offering a palmful of water at the lotus feet of Varuṇa, the demigod who has a form of water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Apomayam* means made of water.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Guru*, etc are the four castes there. They are sanctified by the waters of the above rivers. They worship God by offering both hands full of water to Him who has water as His sharira (body).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Ammayam* = the god of water, endowed with many virtues.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Apomayane* = made of water.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Even in that Krauncha island. *Bhagavan* = a seer.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Using the pure water of these rivers the four castes, i.e. puruṣa and so on which stand in place of the terms *brāhmaṇa*, etc. worship Lord Hari in the form of water by offering palmfuls of water.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The rivers are Abhaya, etc. The people of that island are of four divisions, Rshabha, etc. which stand in place of *brāhmaṇa*, etc. They are purified by the rivers as they use the waters.
