They worship Viṣṇu in the form of water by offering palmfuls of water. Water happens to be the Sharira of Hari, whom they worship.

### Text 23

*आपः पुरुषवीर्याः स्थ पुनन्तीर्भूर्भुवःसुवः ।*  
*ता नः पुनीतामीवघ्नीः स्पृशतामात्मना भुव इति ॥२३॥*

*āpaḥ puruṣa-vīryāḥ stha*  
*punantīr bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ*  
*tā naḥ punītāmīva-ghnīḥ*  
*spṛśatām ātmanā bhuva iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

āpaḥ—O water; puruṣa-vīryāḥ—endowed with the energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; stha—you are; punantīḥ—sanctifying; bhūḥ—of the planetary system known as Bhūḥ; bhuvaḥ—of the Bhuvaḥ planetary system; suvaḥ—of the Svaḥ planetary system; tāḥ—that water; naḥ—of us; punīta—purify; amīva-ghnīḥ—who destroys sin; spṛśatām—of those touching; ātmanā—by your constitutional position; bhuvaḥ—the bodies; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**\[The inhabitants of Krauñcadvīpa worship with this mantra.\] O water of the rivers, you have obtained energy from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore you purify the three planetary systems, known as Bhūloka, Bhuvarloka and Svarloka. By your constitutional nature, you take away sins, and that is why we are touching you. Kindly continue to purify us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Dear waters, you have your powers by the grace of Īśvara, that is why you touch the three worlds. For the same reason, sanctify us as we touch you who are naturally the dispeller of sins.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Dear waters, you are the non-different powers of God. You sanctify the three worlds and are the dispellers of sins. Please purify us as we touch you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The water which is the sperm of Nārāyaṇa purifies the three worlds. May those waters purify us also as we come in contact with them.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Even there he went on his own. Bhagavan means one who has the knowledge of creation and destruction.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Dear waters, your powers are bestowed by the Lord. So purify us as we touch you. You, by nature dispel sins.”

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Ataeva* = by the powers bestowed by īśvara.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Apomayam* = made of water. Worship the Lord Hari with palmfuls of water. You have your powers bestowed by Hari. Purify our bodies as we bathe in you and drink (your waters).

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

“Dear waters, you are the sharira of puruṣa, Hari. You sanctify the three worlds, so purify us also as we bathe in you. You by nature dispel distress and sins.”

### Text 24

*एवं पुरस्तात्क्षीरोदात्परित उपवेशितः शाकद्वीपो द्वात्रिंशल्लक्षयोजनायामः*  
*समानेन च दधिमण्डोदेन परीतो यस्मिन् शाको नाम महीरुहः स्वक्षेत्रव्यप*

*evaṁ purastāt kṣīrodāt parita upaveśitaḥ śākadvīpo dvātriṁśal-lakṣa-yojanāyāmaḥ samānena ca dadhi-maṇḍodena parīto yasmin śāko nāma mahīruhaḥ sva-kṣetra-vyapadeśako yasya ha mahā-surabhi-gandhas taṁ dvīpam anuvāsayati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; purastāt—beyond; kṣīra-udāt—from the ocean of milk; paritaḥ—all around; upaveśitaḥ—situated; śāka-dvīpaḥ—another island, known as Śākadvīpa; dvā-triṁśat—thirty-two; lakṣa—100,000; yojana—yojanas; āyāmaḥ—whose measure; samānena—of equal length; ca—and; dadhi-maṇḍa-udena—by an ocean containing water resembling churned yogurt; parītaḥ—surrounded; yasmin—in which land; śākaḥ—śāka; nāma—named; mahīruhaḥ—a fig tree; sva-kṣetra-vyapadeśakaḥ—giving the island its name; yasya—of which; ha—indeed; mahā-surabhi—a greatly fragrant; gandhaḥ—aroma; tam dvīpam—that island; anuvāsayati—makes fragrant.

**Перевод:**

**Outside the ocean of milk is another island, Śākadvīpa, which has a width of 3,200,000 yojanas \[25,600,000 miles\]. As Krauñcadvīpa is surrounded by its own ocean of milk, Śākadvīpa is surrounded by an ocean of churned yogurt as broad as the island itself. In Śākadvīpa there is a big śāka tree, from which the island takes its name. This tree is very fragrant. Indeed, it lends its scent to the entire island.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Dadhimanda means the juice of curds. That itself is water of which. Saka is a tree whose leaves are soft outside and rough inside.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Anuvasayati* = spreads fragrance.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Saka Island is described by the previous example: it is 3,200,000 *yojanas* \[25,600,000 miles\] wide and is encircled by the milk ocean of equal width. Saka is a mighty tree which lends its name to the island and whose fragrance spreads over the entire island.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Beyond the milk ocean there is Shaka island 3,200,000 *yojanas* \[25,600,000 miles\] wide surrounded by the ocean of curds juice of an equal width.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Beyond the milk ocean the Shaka island is situated (3,200,000 *yojanas* \[25,600,000 miles\] wide) and surrounded by the ocean of curds of equal width. *Dadhimanda* means churned curds. The water of that ocean resembles churned curds. There is a Shaka tree in that island and it lends its name to the island and its extraordinary fragrance spreads throughout the island.

*पुत्रनामानि तेषु स्वात्मजान् पुरोजवमनोजवपवमानधूम्रानीकचित्ररेफबहुरूप*  
*विश्वधारसंज्ञान्निधाप्याधिपतीन् स्वयं भगवत्यनन्त आवेशितमतिस्तपोवनं*  
*प्रविवेश ॥२५॥*

*tasyāpi praiyavrata evādhipatir nāmnā medhātithiḥ so 'pi vibhajya sapta varṣāṇi putra-nāmāni teṣu svātmajān purojava-manojava-pavamāna-dhūmrānīka-citrarepha-bahurūpa-viśvadhāra-saṁjñān nidhāpyādhipatīn svayaṁ bhagavaty ananta ā-veśita-matis tapovanaṁ praviveśa.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasya api—of that island also; praiyavrataḥ—a son of Mahārāja Priyavrata; eva—certainly; adhipatiḥ—the ruler; nāmnā—by the name; medhā-tithiḥ—Medhātithi; saḥ api—he also; vibhajya—dividing; sapta varṣāṇi—seven divisions of the island; putra-nāmāni—possessing the names of his sons; teṣu—in them; sva-ātmajān—his own sons; purojava—Purojava; manojava—Manojava; pavamāna—Pavamāna; dhūmrānīka—Dhūmrānīka; citra-repha—Citrarepha; bahu-rūpa—Bahurūpa; viśvadhāra—Viśvadhāra; saṁjñān—having as names; nidhāpya—establishing as; adhipatīn—the rulers; svayam—himself; bhagavati—in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anante—in the unlimited; āveśita-matiḥ—whose mind was fully absorbed; tapaḥ-vanam—in the forest where meditation is performed; praviveśa—he entered.

**Перевод:**

**The master of this island, also one of the sons of Priyavrata, was known as Medhātithi. He also divided his island into seven sections, named according to the names of his own sons, whom he made the kings of that island. The names of those sons are Purojava, Manojava, Pavamāna, Dhūmrānīka, Citrarepha, Bahurūpa and Viśvadhāra. After dividing the island and situating his sons as its rulers, Medhātithi personally retired, and to fix his mind completely upon the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he entered a forest suitable for meditation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Medhatithi is the lord of the island. He also divided the island into seven parts and gave it to his sons. He then went to a penance grove and attained siddhis \[mystic perfections\].

The names of the mountains are *Cakra*, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Priyavrata’s son, Medhatithi, was the ruler of that island. He also divided the island into seven parts and gave it to his sons bearing the same names of the parts. Their names are Purojava, etc. He then went to a penance grove and attained the lotus feet of Hari by his meditation and penance. In *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* the position of the milk ocean and curds ocean is interchanged. It should be interpreted as the position of a different Brahmā-kalpa \[day of Brahmā\].

Ṛtavrata and others who stand in place of Brahmā, perform *prāṇāyama* in that island. Getting purified by shaking off *rajas* \[passion\] and *tamas* \[ignorance\] aspects they worship Lord Hari in the from of Vāyu.

### Text 29

*एवमेव दधिमण्डोदात्परतः पुष्करद्वीपस्ततो द्विगुणायामः समन्तत*  
*उपकल्पितः समानेन स्वादूदकेन समुद्रेण बहिरावृतो यस्मिन् बृहत्पुष्करं*  
*ज्वलनशिखामलकनकपत्रायुतायुतं भगवतः कमलासनस्याध्यासनं परिकल्पितम्*

*evam eva dadhi-maṇḍodāt parataḥ puṣkaradvīpas tato dvi-guṇāyāmaḥ samantata upakalpitaḥ samānena svādūdakena samudreṇa bahir āvṛto yasmin bṛhat-puṣkaraṁ jvalana-śikhāmala-kanaka-patrāyutāyutaṁ bhagavataḥ kamalāsanasyādhyāsanaṁ parikalpitam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam eva—thus; dadhi-maṇḍa-udāt—the ocean of yogurt; parataḥ—beyond; puṣkara-dvīpaḥ—another island, named Puṣkaradvīpa; tataḥ—than that (Śākadvīpa); dvi-guṇa-āyāmaḥ—whose measurement is twice as great; samantataḥ—on all sides; upakalpitaḥ—surrounded; samānena—equal in width; svādu-udakena—possessing sweet water; samudreṇa—by an ocean; bahiḥ—outside; āvṛtaḥ—surrounded; yasmin—in which; bṛhat—very big; puṣkaram—lotus flower; jvalana-śikhā—like the flames of a blazing fire; amala—pure; kanaka—gold; patra—leaves; ayuta-ayutam—possessing 100,000,000; bhagavataḥ—greatly powerful; kamala āsanasya—of Lord Brahmā, whose sitting place is on the lotus flower; adhyāsanam—sitting place; parikalpitam—considered.

**Перевод:**

**Outside the ocean of yogurt is another island, known as Puṣkaradvīpa, which is 6,400,000 yojanas \[51,200,000 miles\] wide, twice as wide as the ocean of yogurt. It is surrounded by an ocean of very tasteful water as broad as the island itself. On Puṣkaradvīpa there is a great lotus flower with 100,000,000 pure golden petals, as effulgent as the flames of fire. That lotus flower is considered the sitting place of Lord Brahmā, who is the most powerful living being and who is therefore sometimes called bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Which has tens of thousands of golden leaves which are pure like flames.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now Puṣkara Island is described. It is 6,400,000 *yojanas* \[51,200,000 miles\] wide and is surrounded by the pure water ocean of the same width. There is a very big lotus in that island whose golden petals shine like flames of fire. The lotus flower is endowed with tens of thousands of such petals and the pericarp of the flower is the seat of four faced Brahmā, whom the people of that island worship.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Dadimondodat* = from the ocean of milk. Endowed with golden petals pure like the flames of the fire. Of the region lying inside and outside Mānasottara Mountain.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The flower which has tens of thousands of golden-colored petals, shining like the flames of fire.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tatah* = from Krauncha Island. *Dviguna* = 6,400,000 *yojanas* \[51,200,000 miles\] broad.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Jwalana* = fire. Having hundreds of thousands of golden-colored petals shining like the flames of a burning fire.

### Text 30

*तद्द्वीपमध्ये मानसोत्तरनामैक एवार्वाचीनपराचीनवर्षयोर्मर्यादाचलोऽयुतयोजनो*  
*च्छ्रायायामो यत्र तु चतसृषु दिक्षु चत्वारि पुराणि लोकपालानामिन्द्रादीनां*  
*यदुपरिष्टात्सूर्यरथस्य मेरुं परिभ्रमतः संवत्सरात्मकं चक्रं देवानामहोरात्राभ्यां*  
*परिभ्रमति ॥३०॥*

*tad-dvīpa-madhye mānasottara-nāmaika evārvācīna-parācīna-varṣayor maryādācalo 'yuta-yojanocchrāyāyāmo yatra tu catasṛṣu dikṣu catvāri purāṇi loka-pālānām indrādīnāṁ yad-upariṣṭāt sūrya-rathasya meruṁ paribhramataḥ saṁvatsarātmakaṁ cakraṁ devānām aho-rātrābhyāṁ paribhramati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-dvīpa-madhye—within that island; mānasottara—Mānasottara; nāma—named; ekaḥ—one; eva—indeed; arvācīna—on this side; parācīna—and beyond, or outside; varṣayoḥ—of tracts of land; maryādā—indicating the boundary; acalaḥ—a great mountain; ayuta—ten thousand; yojana—eight miles; ucchrāya-āyāmaḥ—whose height and width; yatra—where; tu—but; catasṛṣu—in the four; dikṣu—directions; catvāri—four; purāṇi—cities; loka-pālānām—of the directors of planetary systems; indra-ādīnām—headed by Indra; yat—of which; upariṣṭāt—on the top; sūrya-rathasya—of the chariot of the sun-god; merum—Meru Mountain; paribhramataḥ—while circumambulating; saṁvatsara-ātmakam—consisting of one saṁvatsara; cakram—wheel or orbit; devānām—of the demigods; ahaḥ-rātrābhyām—by the day and night; paribhramati—moves around.

**Перевод:**

**In the middle of that island is a great mountain named Mānasottara, which forms the boundary between the inner side and the outer side of the island. Its breadth and height are 10,000 yojanas \[80,000 miles\]. On that mountain, in the four directions, are the residential quarters of demigods such as Indra. In the chariot of the sun-god, the sun travels on the top of the mountain in an orbit called the Saṁvatsara, encircling Mount Meru. The sun's path on the northern side is called Uttarāyaṇa, and its path on the southern side is called Dakṣiṇāyana. One side represents a day for the demigods, and the other represents their night.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In this island, the only demarcating mountain is Mānasottara which runs circularly in the middle of the island. It is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high and equally broad. On top of the mountain, there are the four cities in the four directions of Indra, Agni, Varuna and Kuvera. The wheel of the sun’s chariot moves over these four cities and is called Saṁvatsara by name. It causes day and night to the demigods and pitrs \[forefathers\] by Uttarāyaṇa \[northern motion\] and Dakṣiṇāyana \[southern motion\]. It resembles an ordinary wheel.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

*Dviguna* = 1,600,000 *yojanas* \[12,800,000 miles\] wide encircled by the rajas \[passionate\] milk ocean of an identical dimension as in the previous islands.

### Text 31

*तद्द्वीपस्याप्यधिपतिः प्रैयव्रतो वीतिहोत्रो नामैतस्यात्मजौ रमणकधातकि*  
*नामानौ वर्षपती नियुज्य स स्वयं पूर्वजवद्भगवत्कर्मशील एवास्ते ॥३१॥*

*tad-dvīpasyāpy adhipatiḥ praiyavrato vītihotro nāmaitasyātmajau ramaṇaka-dhātaki-nāmānau varṣa-patī niyujya sa svayaṁ pūrvajavad-bhagavat-karma-śīla evāste.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-dvīpasya—of that island; api—also; adhipatiḥ—the ruler; praiyavrataḥ—a son of Mahārāja Priyavrata; vītihotraḥ nāma—named Vītihotra; etasya—of him; ātma-jau—unto the two sons; ramaṇaka—Ramaṇaka; dhātaki—and Dhātaki; nāmānau—having the names; varṣa-patī—the rulers of the two tracts of land; niyujya—appointing; saḥ svayam—himself; pūrvaja-vat—like his other brothers; bhagavat-karma-śīlaḥ—being absorbed in activities to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva—indeed; āste—remains.

**The ruler of this island, the son of Mahārāja Priyavrata named Vītihotra, had two sons named Ramaṇaka and Dhātaki. He granted the two sides of the island to these two sons and then personally engaged himself in activities for the sake of the Supreme Personality of Godhead like his elder brother Medhātithi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Devanamahoratribhyam* means by Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Vitihotra’s sons Ramanaka and Dhataki are the rulers of the two divisions given to them by their father like his previous brothers. Vitihotra also was absorbed in penance before leaving this world.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The wheel of saṁvatsara contains the five spokes of which are the six seasons. This is supported by the Matsya Purāṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because only those who reside to the south of Jambūdvīpa can know the upper regions. The word “paravishya” is obvious, i.e. “the manifested thing in the world.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The two divisions caused by circular Mānasottara Mountain are also circular. “The day and night of demigods” means Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In Puṣkara Island, the two divisions caused by circular Mānasottara Mountain are also circular.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Ahoratrabhyam* = by Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“You are the one whose lower regions and groves are attacked by Guha’s weapons, Shakti by name.”

He made his sons rulers of the divisions and went for penance.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The Puṣkara Island is situated beyond the curds ocean, is 6,400,000 *yojanas* \[51,200,000 miles\] wide and is surrounded by the pure water ocean of equal width. The island derives its name by a Puṣkara—(lotus flower) with millions of petals resembling gold in color, which grows there. This lotus is the seat of Brahmā, the creator. There is only one frontier mountain in that island, Mānasottara which is also circular and situated in the middle of the island. Mānasottara Mountain divides the island into two equal circular parts. Vitihotra, the ruler of the island placed his sons Ramanaka and Dhataki in charge of the two parts bearing the same names. The wheel of the sun’s chariot moves on Mānasottara as the sun moves around Meru. This wheel, although extraordinary in character, rolls like any other ordinary wheel on top of the mountain.

### Text 32

*तद्वर्षपुरुषा भगवन्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणं सकर्मकेण कर्मणाराधयन्तीदं चोदाहरन्ति*  
*॥३२॥*

*tad-varṣa-puruṣā bhagavantaṁ brahma-rūpiṇaṁ sakarmakeṇa karmaṇārādhayantīdaṁ codāharanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-varṣa-puruṣāḥ—the inhabitants of that island; bhagavantam—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; brahma-rūpiṇam—exhibited as Lord Brahmā being seated on the lotus; sa-karmakeṇa—for fulfillment of material desires; karmaṇā—by performing ritualistic activities according to the Vedas; ārādhayanti—worship; idam—this; ca—and; udāharanti—they chant.

**Перевод:**

**For the fulfillment of material desires, the inhabitants of this tract of land worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead as represented by Lord Brahmā. They offer prayers to the Lord as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Brahmarupinam* means having the form of the lotus-seated Brahmā.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The people who reside there worship God in the form of Brahmā. The worship mainly consists of mental thought processes. Manu has called these thought processes also *karma*. When the reading is taken as *akarmana* it means for the sake of liberation from *karma*. The other usage of the word *karma* means “what the *Vedas* allot to be enjoyed by each individual.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Akarmakena* = by meditation. Because meditation is possible only after arresting the flow of mind in various directions. It may also mean “not desiring any reward.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Sakarmaka” means “actions which earn for the performer the same loka as that of Brahmā.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

By that action which breeds another action—namely *sakāmakarma* \[actions motivated by a desire to enjoy the results\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Sakarmakena* = by such *karma* \[actions\] which produce more *karma* \[reactions\] i.e., sakāma *karma* \[actions motivated by a desire to enjoy the results\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

They worship Lord Vāsudeva in the form of Brahmā by *karma-yoga* which includes prayers and obeisances. This means they do not know Vāsudeva directly.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The people who live there worship Brahmā who happens to be the sharira \[body\] of Lord Hari. They worship him by *karma-yoga* which is of the nature of mental worship. They chant the following *mantra*:

The caste of the people living in other islands was described, but here the caste is not mentioned. We get information about this in the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* which describes that this island is verily a heaven on earth, and as such, there is no distinction of castes there. All the people are alike and perform Vedic worship in the same manner.

### Text 33

*यत्तत्कर्ममयं लिङ्गं ब्रह्मलिङ्गं जनोऽर्चयेत् ।*  
*एकान्तमद्वयं शान्तं तस्मै भगवते नम इति ॥३३॥*

*yat tat karmamayaṁ liṅgaṁ*  
*brahma-liṅgaṁ jano 'rcayet*  
*ekāntam advayaṁ śāntaṁ*  
*tasmai bhagavate nama iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—which; tat—that; karma-mayam—obtainable by the Vedic ritualistic system; liṅgam—the form; brahma-liṅgam—which makes known the Supreme Brahman; janaḥ—a person; arcayet—must worship; ekāntam—who has full faith in the one Supreme; advayam—nondifferent; śāntam—peaceful; tasmai—unto him; bhagavate—the most powerful; namaḥ—our respects; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**Lord Brahmā is known as karma-maya, the form of ritualistic ceremonies, because by performing ritualistic ceremonies one may attain his position and because the Vedic ritualistic hymns become manifest from him. He is devoted to the Supreme Personality of Godhead without deviation, and therefore in one sense he is not different from the Lord. Nevertheless, he should be worshiped not as the monists worship him, but in duality. One should always remain a servitor of the Supreme Lord, the supreme worshipable Deity. We therefore offer our respectful obeisances unto Lord Brahmā, the form of manifest Vedic knowledge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Karmamayam* means the result of *karma*. *Brahmalingam* means by which Brahmā is known. *Ekantam* means owing loyalty to one parameswara \[supreme controller, God\]. In fact it is *advaita* \[without duality\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

They perform their *upāsanā* in Brahmā. He is the body of God, who is known only through the *Vedas*. *Karmamayam* means who is endowed with the operations of the creation, destruction, protection, etc. of the world. The word *advaita* should be taken as an adverb. They perform their worship in such a way that they realize the oneness of Brahman as he is qualified by both the subtle and gross forms of matter and souls. Our obeisances to you , Hiraṇyagarbha.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Dear Lord, people worship your form endowed with all auspicious virtues.” *Karmamayam* = attainable through sacrifices or the important purport of *Vedas*. Brahmā’s body and mind are always in consonance with God’s mind. That is why it is called *advaita*—not changing either here or after liberation. *Advaita* does not mean the oneness of souls, for the word *bhedana* \[with difference\] is used. They worship Viṣṇu as different from Brahman.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Karmamayam* = attainable through *karma*. *Lingam* = deity form. By which *brahma* is known. *Bhedena* = the worship of him thinking he is master and we are the servants. *Ekantam* = having allegiance only to him. *Advaita* is non different from him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Karmamyam* = attainable by *karma*. *Lingam* = by which *brahma* is known. In fact the advaita is real and non-different from Parameswara.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Karmamayam* = attainable through *karma*. *Lingam* = the fruit. *Brahmalingam* = known through the *Vedas*. *Advayam* = without a second—it is so called in the *Vedas* because we do not have a second person who can be worshiped like Vāsudeva.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The names of his sons are Ama and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Here the hymn that is chanted by the people is told. *Brahma* = whose knowledge is produced by the *Vedas*. *Karmamayam* = full of actions like creation and so on. *Lingam* = body of God—having allegiance only to Him they worship. *Advayam* = unparalleled. *Shantam* = of a quiet nature in spite of the *rajo guṇa* \[mode of passion\]. They chant, “Our obeisances to You, Bhagavan whose virtues are manifest.”

### Text 34

*ऋषिरुवाच*  
*ततः परस्ताल्लोकालोकनामाचलो लोकालोकयोरन्तराले परित उपक्षिप्तः*  
*॥३४॥*

*tataḥ parastāl lokāloka-nāmācalo lokālokayor antarāle parita upakṣiptaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—from that ocean of sweet drinking water; parastāt—beyond; lokāloka-nāma—named Lokāloka; acalaḥ—a mountain; loka-alokayoḥ antarāle—between the countries full of sunlight and those without sunlight; paritaḥ—all around; upakṣiptaḥ—exists.

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, beyond the ocean of sweet water and fully surrounding it, is a mountain named Lokāloka, which divides the countries that are full of sunlight from those not lit by the sun.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Tatah* means beyond the pure water ocean. *Loka* means where there is sunlight. *Aloka* means the place of no sunlight. What is beyond them is the mountain Lokāloka. It is so called because it stands between the regions of loka, sunlight and aloka, darkness. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the seven islands, Śrī Śuka narrates what is beyond the islands. What is beyond them is the mountain Lokāloka. It is so called because it stands between the regions of loka, sunlight and aloka, darkness.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Beyond that, outside.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Loka = having sunlight. Aloka = devoid of sunlight. In between them, to separate them, the mountain is circular.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is situated circularly in all the eight directions, otherwise, there could not be divisions.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Tatah* = after the pure water ocean. *Loka* = the region having sunlight. *Aloka* = region engulfed in darkness.

### Text 35

*यावन्मानसोत्तरमेर्वोरन्तरं तावती भूमिः काञ्चन्यन्यादर्शतलोपमा यस्यां प्रहितः*  
*पदार्थो न कथञ्चित्पुनः प्रत्युपलभ्यते तस्मात्सर्वसत्त्वपरिहृतासीत् ॥३५॥*

*yāvan mānasottara-mervor antaraṁ tāvatī bhūmiḥ kāñcany anyādarśa-talopamā yasyāṁ prahitaḥ padārtho na kathañcit punaḥ pratyupalabhyate tasmāt sarva-sattva-parihṛtāsīt.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvat—as much as; mānasottara-mervoḥ antaram—the land between Mānasottara and Meru (beginning from the middle of Mount Sumeru); tāvatī—that much; bhūmiḥ—land; kāñcanī—made of gold; anyā—another; ādarśa-tala-upamā—whose surface is just like the surface of a mirror; yasyām—on which; prahitaḥ—dropped; padārthaḥ—a thing; na—not; kathañcit—in any way; punaḥ—again; pratyupalabhyate—is found; tasmāt—therefore; sarva-sattva—by all living entities; parihṛtā—abandoned; āsīt—was.

**Перевод:**

**Beyond the ocean of sweet water is a tract of land as broad as the area between the middle of Mount Sumeru and the boundary of Mānasottara Mountain. In that tract of land there are many living beings. Beyond it, extending to Lokāloka Mountain, is another land, which is made of gold. Because of its golden surface, it reflects light like the surface of a mirror, and any physical article that falls on that land can never be perceived again. All living entities, therefore, have abandoned that golden land.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The distance between Mount Sumeru and Mānasottara is 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]; some say so much of earth lies between Suddhoda and Lokāloka. This area is known as the golden land which resembles the surface of a mirror, where anything which comes in contact with it disappears. This does not apply to demigods however. All other creatures avoid it.

Sometimes it is said that the golden land is twice that of the inner part. Here “twice” does not mean the linear dimension—it only means that the demigods derive a happiness which is twice of what they derived inside.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The dimension between Meru’s center and Mānasottara is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. The same dimension is attributed to the golden land beyond the pure water ocean. Beyond that is Lokāloka avoided by all creatures.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tatra* = in that earth. *Anya* = different. *Prahita* = fallen.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The region of loka and pure water ocean is divided into two halves as described. The distance between Meru and Mānasottara is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. That much of earth is generally inhabited by people and creatures. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “The settlements of people and creatures are around the pure water ocean.” Thus it will become 31,000,000 *yojanas* \[248,000,000 miles\]. The width of Puṣkara Island and the pure water ocean is 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]. The total becomes 41,100,000 *yojanas* \[328,800,000 miles\]. Beyond that is golden land. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*; “The two-fold golden land is avoided by all creatures.” So it will be 123,300,000 *yojanas* \[986,400,000 miles\]. Lokāloka is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] wide beyond the above. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*; “The Lokāloka Mountain is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] broad.” Here the dimension of the golden land is not mentioned, but by the above calculation we get 10,000 short of 1,700,000. So the 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1,000,000,000 miles\] between Meru’s center and the end of Lokāloka should be understood in this manner. Then, there is another 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1,000,000,000 miles\] wide region of darkness all around. Anything which falls on the golden earth becomes gold and so it is not seen again. It has been placed by God at the end of the three worlds. It’s height is such that it does not allow any light from the celestial bodies to go beyond it. It has got a proportionate thickness.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The mountains are Shukla, etc. and the rivers are Abhaya, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

What distance of land is there between Mountains Meru and Mānasottara, the same is the extent of golden earth \[or golden land\]. Thus, excluding the oceans, the land of the islands will be 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]. This is the extent of golden land. If we take the oceans also into account, then the golden land would be 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\], which would be contrary to Śrī Madhvacharya’s statement in *Mahābhārata Tatparya Nirnaya*. There it is said,

*antyadhyardha sthalam hai mam*

One and half times the previous one is the extent of the golden land which will come to 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]. But even then we fall short of 150,000 *yojanas* \[1,200,000 miles\]. The objection which can be raised is that subtracting the width of the oceans, the land comes to 9,450,000 *yojanas* \[75,600,000 miles\]. But since it is said there: “bahyato vajralepakam,” (has a diamond border at the end), the diamond border is 150,000 *yojanas* \[1,200,000 miles\] and hence it will be 96.

### Text 36

*लोकालोक इति समाख्या यदनेनाचलेन लोकालोकस्यान्तर्वर्तिनावस्थाप्यते*  
*॥३६॥*

*lokāloka iti samākhyā yad anenācalena lokālokasyāntarvar-tināvasthāpyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

loka—with light (or with inhabitants); alokaḥ—without light (or without inhabitants); iti—in this way; samākhyā—designation; yat—which; anena—by this; acalena—mountain; loka—of the land inhabited by living entities; alokasya—and of the land not inhabited by living entities; antarvartinā—which is in the middle; avasthāpyate—is established.

**Перевод:**

**Between the lands inhabited by living entities and those that are uninhabited stands the great mountain which separates the two and which is therefore celebrated as Lokāloka.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here the distance between the pure water ocean and Lokāloka is stated. What extent of earth lies between Meru and Mānasottara is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]—the same extent of earth is beyond the pure water ocean also. There are creatures there beyond that and before Lokāloka there is different region of earth. It is the golden land. It is 83,900,000 *yojanas* \[671,200,000 miles\] wide. It has not been inhabited by people. Then only the distance of 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1,000,000,000 miles\] between Meru and Lokāloka stated earlier holds good. Any object which falls there disappears, hence it is desolate. This does not apply to demigods because it is said that the golden land is created for the rejoicing of demigods. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava\]

Even in the *Shaiva Tantra* it is stated thus: “The seven islands and oceans account for 25,350,000 of *yojanas* \[202,800,000 miles\]. Beyond that is golden land for 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\], where demigods rejoice. Lokāloka Mountain lies beyond that 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\]. This is inclusive of the earth’s expanse stated above.” \[Note: these two paragraphs are repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is justly named Lokāloka as it stands as a frontier mountain between loka and aloka.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The etymology of Lokāloka is that it divides Loka and Aloka into two equal parts

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Samakhya* = name or etymology—that which is at the center divides into two equal parts.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The mountain is named Lokāloka because it divides the earth into two parts Loka and Aloka and stands in between.

### Text 37

*स लोकत्रयान्ते परित ईश्वरेण विहितो यस्मात्सूर्यादीनां ध्रुवापवर्गाणां*  
*ज्योतिर्गणानां गभस्तयोऽर्वाचीनांस्त्रीँ ललोकानावितन्वाना न कदाचित्पराचीना*  
*भवितुमुत्सहन्ते तावदुन्नहनायामः ॥३७॥*

*sa loka-trayānte parita īśvareṇa vihito yasmāt sūryādīnāṁ dhruvāpavargāṇāṁ jyotir-gaṇānāṁ gabhastayo 'rvācīnāṁs trīḹ lokān āvitanvānā na kadācit parācīnā bhavitum utsahante tāvad un-nahanāyāmaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

saḥ—that mountain; loka-traya-ante—at the end of the three lokas (Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka and Svarloka); paritaḥ—all around; īśvareṇa—by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; vihitaḥ—created; yasmāt—from which; sūrya-ādīnām—of the sun planet; dhruva-apavargāṇām—up to Dhruvaloka and other, inferior luminaries; jyotiḥ-gaṇānām—of all the luminaries; gabhastayaḥ—the rays; arvācīnān—on this side; trīn—the three; lokān—planetary systems; āvitanvānāḥ—spreading throughout; na—not; kadācit—at any time; parācīnāḥ—beyond the jurisdiction of that mountain; bhavitum—to be; utsahante—are able; tāvat—that much; unnahana-āyāmaḥ—the measure of the height of the mountain.

**Перевод:**

**By the supreme will of Kṛṣṇa, the mountain known as Lokāloka has been installed as the outer border of the three worlds—Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka and Svarloka—to control the rays of the sun throughout the universe. All the luminaries, from the sun up to Dhruvaloka, distribute their rays throughout the three worlds, but only within the boundary formed by this mountain. Because it is extremely high, extending even higher than Dhruvaloka, it blocks the rays of the luminaries, which therefore can never extend beyond it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is situated like a frontier mountain at the end of the three lokas. *Yasmat* means from which impedes first the sun and Dhruva at the end. *Aavitanvanah* means illuminating in all directions. They cannot go beyond it. Such is the height and breadth of the mountain. Because it is higher than Dhruva. It is said to be situated beyond the three worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

This mountain is also circular and contains the three worlds within its belly. The mountain is as high and wide as to block the rays of the celestial bodies starting from the sun and ending in Dhruva. The rays illuminate the three worlds which are below from above. The rays can never cross and go beyond the mountain.

To facilitate the knowledge of the height and width of the mountain, the dimension of the earth is first mentioned here. The learned say that the earth is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4,000,000,000 miles\]. Earth is to be taken here as *brahmāṇḍa*. The height of Lokāloka is a fourth of this dimension, i.e. 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1,000,000,000 miles\]. It has a proportionate width.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

This mountain was created by God after the creation of the three worlds or at the end of the three worlds. It is as high as the three worlds i.e. 5,700,000 *yojanas* \[45,600,000 miles\]. The thickness is 5,050,000 *yojanas* \[40,40,000 miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Lokatraya* = the three worlds—at the end of it. In all directions, the Lokāloka is so high and broad as to block the rays of the celestial bodies which cast their shine only inside but not outside Lokāloka. It is higher than Dhruva and that is why it is said to be situated at the end of the three worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It means that this Lokāloka Mountain extends as far as the three lokas. *Satu =* Lokāloka Mountain. *Bhugolasya* = of the *brahmāṇḍa* sphere which is related to the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The Lokāloka is created and placed as a frontier mountain by Īśvara \[God\] such that the three worlds fall inside the mountain which is also circular. The rays of the sun, Dhruva \[Dhruvaloka, the polestar\], etc. illuminate the worlds which are vertically downwards. They can never go beyond the Lokāloka Mountain since the mountain has such height and thickness as to block the rays.

### Text 38

*एतावाँललोकविन्यासो मानलक्षणसंस्थाभिर्विचिन्तितः कविभिः स*  
*तु पञ्चाशत्कोटिगणितस्य भू गोलस्य तुरीयभागोऽयं लोकालोकाचलः ॥३८॥*

*etāvāḹ loka-vinyāso māna-lakṣaṇa-saṁsthābhir vicintitaḥ kavibhiḥ sa tu pañcāśat-koṭi-gaṇitasya bhū-golasya turīya-bhāgo 'yaṁ lokālokācalaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etāvān—this much; loka-vinyāsaḥ—the placing of the different planets; māna—with measurements; lakṣaṇa—symptoms; saṁsthābhiḥ—as well as with their different situations; vicintitaḥ—established by scientific calculations; kavibhiḥ—by learned scholars; saḥ—that; tu—but; pañcāśat-koṭi—500,000,000 yojanas; gaṇitasya—which is measured at; bhū-golasya—of the planetary system known as Bhūgolaka; turīya-bhāgaḥ—one fourth; ayam—this; lokāloka-acalaḥ—the mountain known as Lokāloka.

**Перевод:**

**Learned scholars who are free from mistakes, illusions and propensities to cheat have thus described the planetary systems and their particular symptoms, measurements and locations. With great deliberation, they have established the truth that the distance between Sumeru and the mountain known as Lokāloka is one fourth of the diameter of the universe—or, in other words, 125,000,000 yojanas \[1 billion miles\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The distance between Meru and Lokāloka should be taken as 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\] on either side.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

To facilitate the knowledge of the height and width of the mountain, the dimension of the earth is first mentioned here. The learned say that the earth is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\]. Earth is to be taken here as *brahmāṇḍa* \[the universe\]. The height of Lokāloka is a fourth of this dimension, i.e. 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. It has a proportionate width.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The celestial sphere and the terrestrial sphere \[vertical and horizontal spheres\] are both 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] in width. A fourth of it will be 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. That is the height of the Lokāloka. The diameter of the earth is 3,400,000 *yojanas* 27,200,000 miles\] short of 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\]. It is like this. From the center of the Meru to the center of Mānasottara, it is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. From the center of Mānasottara to the end of the pure water ocean is 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]. There after the golden land is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. Thus, measuring on one side of Meru, the total will be 41,100,000 *yojanas* \[328,800,000 miles\]. It is the same on the other side of Meru also. So the inner diameter of Lokāloka will be 82,200,000 *yojanas* \[657,600,000 miles\]. Beyond Lokāloka, the aloka region is also 82,200,000 *yojanas* \[657,600,000 miles\] on either side. So the total comes 246,600,000 *yojanas* \[1,972,800,000 miles\], which is 3,400,000 *yojanas* \[27,200,000 miles\] short of 250,000,000 *yojanas* \[2 billion miles\]. There is a cavity of 1,700,000 *yojanas* \[13,600,000 miles\] all around the earth \[Bhū-maṇḍala\] including the bottom also. This facilitates the serpent Śeṣa to hold the earth aloft and the elephants to hold the earth in position. If we interpret otherwise it will be irrelevant. Also the immersion of the *aṇḍa* \[universal egg\] at the end of Chaksusa Manvantara would also become difficult to defend.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Because the earth, like the sun, is at the center of the egg-like celestial sphere, the terrestrial sphere is also 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4,000,000,000 miles\] wide. One fourth of it is 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\], which is the height. The earth is 53,400,000 *yojanas* \[427,200,000 miles\] wide. From the center of Meru to the center of Mānasottara it is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. From there until Sweetwater Ocean it is 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]. So from Meru to Lokāloka is 41,100,000 *yojanas* \[328,800,000 miles\] on either side. Thus, the inner diameter of Lokāloka is 82,200,000 *yojanas* \[657,600,000 miles\]. Beyond Lokāloka there is the same distance on either side. The thickness of Lokāloka is 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\], on either side, so the width of the earth \[Bhū-maṇḍala\] is 3,400,000 *yojanas* \[27,200,000 miles\] short of 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\]. Another 1,700,000 *yojanas* \[13,600,000 miles\] are on either side between earth \[Bhū-maṇḍala\] and the coverings of the universe, where the serpant Śeṣa and the elephants hold aloft the earth. The immersing of the earth after the Cākṣuṣa Manvantra can thus be explained and not otherwise.

Nilakanta has discussed this in his commentary on *Mahābhārata*, *Bhishma Parva*: Each side of a square measuring a hasta is 24 inches. The total length of four sides (*paridhi*) will be 96 inches. The diagonals will be a bit shorter. The measurements of Jambū is said to be 18,600 *yojanas* \[148,800,000 miles\]. This should be taken as the total length of four sides, 4,650 *yojanas* \[37,200 miles\] will be each side. The diagonal will be 6,576 *yojanas* \[52,608 miles\]. Earth \[Jambūdvīpa\] is a square. The four vertices of earth’s \[Jambūdvīpa’s\] square touch the ocean. The astronomers say each side of earth’s square is 4,967 *yojanas* \[32,536 miles\]. But we disagree with that and take it as 4,650 *yojanas* \[37,200 miles\]. The difference between these two is 367 *yojanas* \[2,936 miles\]. But it is said 317 *yojanas* \[2,536 miles\]. This difference is because of the variation in the unit of measurement. Earth \[Jambūdvīpa\] is a square, but the sun’s path around Meru is circular. We do not accept the two sun’s theory of the Bauddhas \[Jains\]. All the other aspects should be taken as enjoined in the books on astronomy. The *Purāṇas* say that earth’s \[Bhū-maṇḍala’s\] expanse is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\].

These are things which we should not try to understand by logic. The *anirvachaniya* theory is to be accepted which vouches for the inexplicability of things or whatever dimensions have been stated in *Purāṇas*. We should take only a twentieth part of that. A reduction factor of 1/20 is to be applied everywhere—so 500,000,000 means 25,000,000. The width of Jambūdvīpa is 5,000 and not 100,000. The width of Bhārata-khaṇḍa is 450 *yojanas* \[3,600 miles\] in place of 9,000 *yojanas* 72,000 miles\]. Bhārata-varṣa is triangular. The dimensions are given quite differently because the basic units of *angula* \[finger\] and *hasta* \[hand\] differ from person to person. Thus, the contradictions should be resolved on this basis. It is said in the *Purāṇas* that Vyāsa is Nārāyaṇa incarnate, then how did he state contradictorily to astronomy? Vyāsa has transgressed astronomy and it could be according to a different *angula* and *hasta* units—so the contradiction is only apparent and not absolute. Then how can there be a contradiction between *Bhāgavata* and astronomy? This question has been raised in *Goladarsha*, a book on astronomy and also answered there. The essence of the reply is this: the earth has two dimensions—one is very big and the other is the small spherical dimension mentioned in the works on astronomy. Parīkṣit has questioned about the Bhū-gola (the earth’s sphere) and Śuka has replied. This confirms with the spherical shape of astronomy.

There is another word in that context—it is vishesha which means the golden *aṇḍa* \[egg, universe\]. It is said that earth rests like a mustard seed on hood of Ananta. The analogy implies the spherical shape. In the Kardama story the word, “bhuva golam” is used, which confirms the above fact. This is the small earth, but where is another big earth? We reply it is above the star belt. It is like a reflection. Its circumference is 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\] as told in the *Bhāgavata*. There is sphere of fire in between the two earths. There is also a sphere of water in between the two. This has been stated in the *Sūrya-siddhānta* and other works. All the sentences of *Bhāgavata* should be interpreted against the background of all these things. The contradictions should be resolved as I have suggested earlier and the *Bhāgavata* should be deemed to be valid.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

It was said “such height,”—here the actual height is given as 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The height and width of the mountain is to be stated. However, to know them we should know the magnitude of the earth which is reminded here. The extent of the entire earth is known to be 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] by great people. A fourth of it will be 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. This is the height of Lokāloka Mountain \[distance from Meru to Lokāloka Mountain\]. The thickness \[distance from Lokāloka Mountain to the coverings of the universe\] is also the same.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

“Bhūlokasya turiya bhage yavan lokaloka chalak:”

It is said here that the entire extent of the loka is just a part of the width of the Brahmāṇḍa sphere, in the sentence starting with sa ta. Bhū-golasya turiya bhaga = the locative case use is in the sense of determining a part from a whole or a single one from a group. In the midst of the fourth part of 125,000,000 yojanas \[1 billion miles\] dimension.

Whatever the distance between Meru and Lokāloka, all that is within the fourth part of the diameter of *brahmāṇḍa*, is what it means.

### Text 41

*आकल्पमेवं वेषं गत एष भगवानात्मयोगमायया विरचितविविधलोक*  
*यात्रागोपीयायेत्यर्थः ॥४१॥*

*ākalpam evaṁ veṣaṁ gata eṣa bhagavān ātma-yogamāyayā viracita-vividha-loka-yātrā-gopīyāyety arthaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ā-kalpam—for the duration of the time of creation; evam—thus; veṣam—appearance; gataḥ—has accepted; eṣaḥ—this; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ātma-yoga-māyayā—by His own spiritual potency; viracita—perfected; vividha-loka-yātrā—the livelihood of the various planetary systems; gopīyāya—just to maintain; iti—thus; arthaḥ—the purpose.

**Перевод:**

**The various forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, such as Nārāyaṇa and Viṣṇu, are beautifully decorated with different weapons. The Lord exhibits those forms to maintain all the varied planets created by His personal potency, yogamāyā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

If a question arises that God can do everything as the inner-dweller only, why should He be situated all around, the author himself explains. For protecting the various worldly affairs designed by his yogic powers, God takes this external form by His own pastime and stays till the end of the *kalpa* \[day of Brahmā\]. This is what it means.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

On the top of the mountain, God resides until the end of the *kalpa* controlling and supervising all the activities in the three worlds. He is in his infinite glory endowed with *dharma*, *jñāna* and all excellences. He has chosen to reside there as His own pastime.

Thus from the center of the Meru (at the bottom) until the ocean of pure water the distance is 25,350,000 *yojanas* \[202,800,000 miles\]. It is said like this elsewhere also: “Dear one, the seven islands and seven oceans together measure 25,350,000 *yojanas* \[202,800,000 miles. Beyond that is the golden land for 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\]. It is where the demigods rejoice. Beyond that, lies the mountain Lokāloka.”

In the same way, the distance between the pure water ocean until the golden land is also stated as 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. The width of the golden land is not expressly stated, but since we know that the inner diameter of the *brahmāṇḍa* is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] and we also know the width of the seven islands and oceans as also the dimensions of the darkness which is said to be equal to the magnitude of the Loka, we arrive at 83,900,000 *yojanas* \[671,200,000 miles\] which is the extent of the golden land. In the sentence quoted above it is said to be 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\]—this is an approximation since 839+157.5=996.50 *lakh* \[times 10,000\] *yojanas* which is only 350,000 *yojanas* \[2,800,000 miles\] short of 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\].

Aakalpam—until the pralaya \[devastation\]. Like this he has reached there. The same is what I expressed earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

A doubt is raised by the word *nanu*. Until the end of the *kalpa*, He will be at Lokāloka. If He who has created the world does not protect it, who else will?

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The previous sentence is explained here. With all His extraordinary powers, God is stationed there for the protection and welfare of the world till the end of the *kalpa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

God could have managed everything by being the *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\]. Thus the question could be raised as to the necessity for Him to be present in the mountain in another form. The reply is it is His own will, a pastime. He is there to conduct the affairs of the worlds and also for the welfare of the worlds. He is not bound to be there but He is there on his own free will.
