**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The magnitude of Aloka is 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\] on one side of Meru. *Tatah* means from Lokāloka or Aloka beyond that—the path shown to Arjuna by Kṛṣṇa while retrieving the *brāhmaṇa* sons.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now the magnitude of Aloka is being stated. “Dear King, by stating the dimension of the inner part of Lokāloka, the dimension of the outer part is also stated as it were. The inner part measuring 125,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\], the outer part also measures the same. This is what is to be understood here. Meru occupies the center of *brahmāṇḍa*, 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] wide from the center of Meru on earth \[Bhū-maṇḍala\] it will be 250,000,000 *yojanas* \[2 billion miles\] to the *brahmāṇḍa* in all directions. If we start from Meru and move horizontally towards the wall of the universe, Jambū island measures 50,000 *yojanas* \[400,000 miles\], Thereafter the salt ocean, Plakṣa and other islands are of the magnitude stated above. The dimension of the seven islands and oceans is 25,050,000 *yojanas* \[200,400,000 miles\]. The dimension of the earth from this point till the golden land is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\]. The golden earth is 83,900,000 *yojanas* \[671,200,000 miles\]. Adding these three (250.5+157.5+839=1247) We get 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\].

Beyond Lokāloka the region Aloka measures 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. Ordinary people cannot go there, only yogiswaras \[masters of *yoga*\] can go. Actually beyond the pure water ocean there is directly golden land and nothing in between. Thus, the dimension stated should necessarily become the dimension of the golden land. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*, “beyond the pure water ocean the Loka part still exists. It is twice the dimension of its inner part and is avoided by all people.” The statement that golden land is 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\] wide also holds good. Then, the text should be interpreted like this, “the dimension of the inner part (diameter) of Lokāloka has been stated. By this, the dimension of the outer region beyond Lokāloka is also stated as it were. If the inner diameter is subtracted from 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] which is the diameter of the *Aṇḍa* \[universe\], we get the dimension of the remaining outer region.”

This should be understood: here we should divide the Bhū-maṇḍala into four parts with Meru as the center. These four divisions resemble a triangle, small at the beginning and getting wider as we go towards the wall. The axes are the radii of the sphere measuring 250,000,000 *yojanas* \[2 billion miles\]. The region beyond Lokāloka being 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\], the inner region also becomes 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. Of this, from the center of the Meru to pure water ocean it is 25,350,000 *yojanas* \[202,800,000 miles\]. From this ocean until Lokāloka to the wall of the universe, it is 83,900,000 *yojanas* \[671,200,000 miles\]. Adding it will be 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\] on each side. The golden land is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\] wide. The statement of *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* that the golden land is twice as wide should be interpreted as twice of (Meru to Suddhoda dimension, i.e. 9,600,000 *yojanas* \[76,800,000 miles\]). The other statement that the golden land is 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\] should be interpreted as the distance between Meru and the end point of golden earth is 100,000,000 *yojanas* \[800,000,000 miles\]. Actually, it will be 101,400,000 *yojanas* \[811,200,000 miles\]. Hence this is an approximation.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

This much is the expanse of the three worlds where demigods and men live. It stands as a fourth part of the magnitude of the *brahmāṇḍa* which is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\]. This should be further clarified. Solid water is one part. Darkness is the second part. Lokāloka is the third part. Inside Lokāloka is the fourth part. It only means that the Loka falls in this fourth part. It does not mean 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. The magnitude of loka is 35,000,000 *yojanas* \[280,000,000 miles\]. By this the magnitude of Aloka is also explained. *Yogeshwaranam* = of those endowed with eight siddhis anima and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The width of Aloka is 8,200,000 *yojanas* \[65,600,000 miles\] where only yogeswaras can go and none else.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Viswanatha says it is 82,200,000 *yojanas* \[657,600,000 miles\] outside, all around. Beyond Lokāloka it is said that there is darkness only. It means that the yogis enter darkness. Thus, it is said “alokad va” or light—or of Nārada and others who divest themselves of their eight enclosures \[bodily coverings\] and try to attain *mokṣa* \[liberation\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The inner width is 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\] on one side of Meru. By this the dimension of Aloka is stated as it were. It lies beyond Lokāloka.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The inner extent of Lokāloka on one side of Meru has been stated. It is 1,250,000,000 *yojanas* \[1 billion miles\]. By stating this, the magnitude of Aloka beyond Lokāloka is also stated, as it were. It is only accessible to yogiswaras as was demonstrated by Śrī Kṛṣṇa while retrieving the *brāhmaṇa*’s son.

### Text 43

*अण्डमध्यगतः सूर्यो द्यावाभूम्योर्यदन्तरम् ।*  
*सूर्याण्डगोलयोर्मध्ये कोट्यः स्युः पञ्चविंशतिः ॥४३॥*

*aṇḍa-madhya-gataḥ sūryo*  
*dyāv-ābhūmyor yad antaram*  
*sūryāṇḍa-golayor madhye*  
*koṭyaḥ syuḥ pañca-viṁśatiḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍa-madhya-gataḥ—situated in the center of the universe; sūryaḥ—the sun globe; dyāv-ābhūmyoḥ—the two planetary systems Bhūrloka and Bhuvarloka; yat—which; antaram—in between; sūrya—of the sun; aṇḍa-golayoḥ—and the globe of the universe; madhye—in the middle; koṭyaḥ—groups of ten million; syuḥ—are; pañca-viṁśatiḥ—twenty-five.

**Перевод:**

**The sun is situated \[vertically\] in the middle of the universe, in the area between Bhūrloka and Bhuvarloka, which is called antarikṣa, outer space. The distance between the sun and the circumference of the universe is twenty-five koṭi yojanas \[two billion miles\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The dimension of the *brahmāṇḍa* \[universe\], which has been narrated in detail is expressed from all directions now. The earth and the sky from the lower and upper halves of the *brahmāṇḍa*. *Andamadhyagatah* means occupying the central position between these two halves—twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\] in all directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It is stated that for all measurements in earth, the point of reference is the center of Meru. Now for all other celestial measurements it is said that the point of reference is the sun. From the sun the wall of the universe is twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\] on all sides. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Which is the central part of the 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] *brahmāṇḍa*? The answer is given here: the path where the sun moves between earth and heaven is the center of *brahmāṇḍa*. From there it measures twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\] in all directions.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Lokāloka occupies Loka by one half and Aloka by the other half, thus it occupies the region beyond the golden land. In *Shivatantra* it is said, “Lokāloka lies beyond.” Otherwise 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\] will not hold good because it is responsible for a sublime voyage, it is said “Vishuddhantargatam.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The dimension of the universal sphere has until now been described vertically. Vertically also from the midpoint the sun (Sūrya) it is twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Dyavabhumyoh*—of the earth and the sky. From the sun it is twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\] to *aṇḍa* upwards and downwards.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

What dimensions have been stated in detail are concisely stated here. The sun occupies the mid point of the *brahmāṇḍa* \[universe\]. From that point, the distance to the wall of the *brahmāṇḍa* is twenty-five koṭi *yojanas* \[two billion miles\] on all sides. The width of Lokāloka should also be included here, as stated above.

### Text 44

*मृतेऽण्ड एष एतस्मिन् यदभूत्ततो मार्तण्ड इति व्यपदेशः ।*  
*हिरण्यगर्भ इति यद्धिरण्याण्डसमुद्भवः ॥४४॥*

*mṛte 'ṇḍa eṣa etasmin yad abhūt tato mārtaṇḍa iti vyapadeśaḥ; hiraṇyagarbha iti yad dhiraṇyāṇḍa-samudbhavaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

mṛte—dead; aṇḍe—in the globe; eṣaḥ—this; etasmin—in this; yat—which; abhūt—entered personally at the time of creation; tataḥ—from that; mārtaṇḍa—Mārtaṇḍa; iti—thus; vyapadeśaḥ—the designation; hiraṇya-garbhaḥ—known as Hiraṇyagarbha; iti—thus; yat—because; hiraṇya-aṇḍa-samudbhavaḥ—his material body was created from Hiraṇyagarbha.

**Перевод:**

**The sun-god is also known as Vairāja, the total material body for all living entities. Because he entered this dull egg of the universe at the time of creation, he is also called Mārtaṇḍa. He is also known as Hiraṇyagarbha because he received his material body from Hiraṇyagarbha \[Lord Brahmā\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The reason for staying in the middle of the *brahmāṇḍa* is stated by giving the etymology of his name—because the sun entered in the form of Vairāja into the mrta, which means insentient.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Sūrya derives his name Martanda because of his association with *brahmāṇḍa*. Because he entered into the mrta = insentient *aṇḍa*. Similarly, Brahmā also derives his name Hiranyagharbha, because of his birth in the golden *aṇḍa*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The sun is called Martanda as he is the middle of the insentient *aṇḍa*, just like Brahmā is called because of his birth in the *aṇḍa* \[universe\].

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The sun is called the Martanda because he is placed in the insentient *aṇḍa*. Hiranyagharba is the subtle adjacent of the group of all *jīvas*, thus he is stationed in *aṇḍa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is said, “he is the sun” with reference to *antaryāmī* \[the supersoul\]. He is like an adjunct to the subtle forms of all *jīvas*. Another feature is the emergence of the golden *aṇḍa* (universe), his gross form.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Incidentally the sun’s other names are told. Because he entered *Aṇḍa* which was Mrta—bereft of light, He is called Martanda. Because Brahmā accupies the central portion, womblike position, of the golden *aṇḍa*, he is called Hiraṇyagarbha.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The mountains are Isana and others, the rivers Anagha etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

It should be noted that sometimes Sūrya himself is referred to Hiranyagharba.

### Text 45

*सूर्येण हि विभज्यन्ते दिशः खं द्यौर्मही भिदा ।*  
*स्वर्गापवर्गौ नरका रसौकांसि च सर्वशः ॥४५॥*

*sūryeṇa hi vibhajyante*  
*diśaḥ khaṁ dyaur mahī bhidā*  
*svargāpavargau narakā*  
*rasaukāṁsi ca sarvaśaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūryeṇa—by the sun-god within the sun planet; hi—indeed; vibhajyante—are divided; diśaḥ—the directions; kham—the sky; dyauḥ—the heavenly planets; mahī—the earthly planets; bhidā—other divisions; svarga—the heavenly planets; apavargau—and the places for liberation; narakāḥ—the hellish planets; rasaukāṁsi—such as Atala; ca—also; sarvaśaḥ—all.

**Перевод:**

**O King, the sun-god and the sun planet divide all the directions of the universe. It is only because of the presence of the sun that we can understand what the sky, the higher planets, this world and the lower planets are. It is also only because of the sun that we can understand which places are for material enjoyment, which are for liberation, which are hellish and subterranean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

And also the directions are divided by the sun only. *Kham* means the sky. Bhida means other divisions also. Swarga is the place of rejoicing. *Apavarga* means the region of *mokṣa*. Rasaukāṁsi means the netherworlds—Atala, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The sun is not merely the reference point while measuring celestial events, but he is also responsible for the reckoning of directions. He is also responsible for the knowledge of the divisions of the fourteen worlds. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bhida—another division. Svargapavarga—heaven and *mokṣa*. Rasaukāṁsi —the nether worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The classification of the directions is where he \[the sun\] rises—it is east. It is west where he sets, it is south where he is at midday and it is north where he is at the middle of the night. It is through Sūrya-maṇḍala \[the solar planetary system\] only that the *jīvas* \[living entities\] go to heaven or *mokṣa* \[liberation\], situated as he is in the middle of the earth and heaven. There is sunlight in all the islands. The nether worlds are devoid of sunlight. Sarvathain—all respects.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Kham—sky. Mahibhida—another region of earth. Swargapavarga—places and *mokṣa*. Rasaukāṁsi—the nether worlds, Atala and others.

### Text 46

*देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्याणां सरीसृपसवीरुधाम् ।*  
*सर्वजीवनिकायानां सूर्य आत्मा दृगीश्वरः ॥४६॥*

*deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣyāṇāṁ*  
*sarīsṛpa-savīrudhām*  
*sarva-jīva-nikāyānāṁ*  
*sūrya ātmā dṛg-īśvaraḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

deva—of the demigods; tiryak—the lower animals; manuṣyāṇām—and the human beings; sarīsṛpa—the insects and the serpents; sa-vīrudhām—and the plants and trees; sarva-jīva-nikāyānām—of all groups of living entities; sūryaḥ—the sun-god; ātmā—the life and soul; dṛk—of the eyes; īśvaraḥ—the Personality of Godhead.

**Перевод:**

**All living entities, including demigods, human beings, animals, birds, insects, reptiles, creepers and trees, depend upon the heat and light given by the sun-god from the sun planet. Furthermore, it is because of the sun's presence that all living entities can see, and therefore he is called dṛg-īśvara, the Personality of Godhead presiding over sight.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

For the sake of worship it is said that Sūrya is the soul of demigods and others. Drgiswara means he is stationed in the eye. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The sun is not merely associated with the above functions—he is also the presiding deity of the eye. He is a *sarira* \[body\] of Viṣṇu.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Nārāyaṇa is called Sūrya as he is attainable by suris. He only divides the sky into ten directions. He is also the one who gives knowledge to all.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sūrya is to be thought of as one’s own self.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Because it is said in the *Vedas* he is described as the soul of the groups of all *jīvas* and he is also the observer. The *Medini Lexicon* gives the meaning of *nikaya* as “the group.”

Sūrya is to be thought of as one’s own self.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

God is called *ātmā*  because of the help he renders to the devas (demigods). He is also the *Ashraya*—supporting base. He is also stationed in the eye.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The hymn is told: “May he protect us who is known as the controller of the entire worlds (īśvara). He enters the moving and non-mobile creatures and sustains and nourishes them by the operation of prana, apana and so on.”

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twentieth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “Studying the Structure of the Universe.”

## Chapter 21 - The Movements of the Sun

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*एतावानेव भूवलयस्य संन्निवेशः प्रमाणलक्षणतो व्याख्यातः ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*etāvān eva bhū-valayasya sanniveśaḥ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇato vyākhyātaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; etāvān—so much; eva—certainly; bhū-valayasya sanniveśaḥ—the arrangement of the whole universe; pramāṇa-lakṣaṇataḥ—according to measurement (fifty crores of yojanas, or four billion miles in width and length) and characteristics; vyākhyātaḥ—estimated.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, I have thus far described the diameter of the universe \[fifty crores of yojanas, or four billion miles\] and its general characteristics, according to the estimations of learned scholars.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Etavan—universe fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\] by width, 25 \[twenty-five *crores* of *yojanas*, or two billion miles\] by height.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Atah* = after describing the dimensions of the earth \[greater earth\] along with *kāla-cakra* and Śiśumāra. The regions situated around should be taken by the word bhuvalayasya.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

This chapter explains how Lord Hari controls the sun and other celestial bodies. The earthen sphere which constitutes the Loka \[planetary system\] has been described above.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Bhuvalayasya means all the different regions around (Meru).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The Bhūloka is described in the previous chapter. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “Whatever is attainable by feet is called Bhūloka. The region between earth and the sun is called Bhuvarloka where there are siddhas and sages.” From the sun’s disc until Dhruvaloka, it is Swarga loka. Maharloka stretches to 10,000,000 *yojanas* \[80,000,000 miles\] above Swarga. Janaloka is of the extent of 20,000,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000,000 miles\] above Maharloka. Tapoloka extends to 80,000,000 *yojanas* \[640,000,000 miles\]. Above Tapoloka, Satyaloka stretches up to 120,000,000 *yojanas* \[960,000,000 miles\]. After that, there is darkness, Garbhodhaka and the wall of the *brahmāṇḍa* \[universe\]. Darkness and such waters should be cognized as occupying every direction. The magnitude of darkness has been stated earlier. The width of Garbhodaka is equal to the sum of the width of all oceans. The thickness of the wall is 10,000,000 *yojanas* \[80,000,000 miles\]. Beyond that, there are envelopes of water and so on, each ten times thicker than the previous one. This, in brief, is the state of things. Now the situation of Bhuvarloka and Swarga is stated.

Etavaneva = fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\] only.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

In the previous chapter, the worship on earth was stated, now in three chapters, the glory of the Lord is described by narrating the arrangement of the sun and his motion. The dimension of Bhū-maṇḍala should also be taken as same in the case of heaven (*dyumaṇḍala*).

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

By stating the magnitude of Bhū-maṇḍala, the magnitude of Dyu-maṇḍala is also stated. From Meru to Lokāloka on either side is Bhū-maṇḍala. From sun in the middle to Lokāloka is the Dyu-maṇḍala. Both are fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\] wide.

21.1: Etavan-50 crore by width, 25 by height.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now the dimensions of Antarikṣa and swarga are stated. *Sannivesha* = width. The width of heaven is also fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\].

### Text 2

*एतेन हि दिवो मण्डलमानं तद्विद उपदिशन्ति यथा द्विदलयोर्निष्पावादीनां*  
*ते अन्तरेणान्तरिक्षं तदुभयसन्धितम् ॥२॥*

*etena hi divo maṇḍala-mānaṁ tad-vida upadiśanti yathā dvi-dalayor niṣpāvādīnāṁ te antareṇāntarikṣaṁ tad-ubhaya-sandhitam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etena—by this estimation; hi—indeed; divaḥ—of the upper planetary system; maṇḍala-mānam—the measurement of the globe; tat-vidaḥ—the experts who know about it; upadiśanti—instruct; yathā—just as; dvi-dalayoḥ—in the two halves; niṣpāva-ādīnām—of grain such as wheat; te—of the two divisions; antareṇa—in the intervening space; antarikṣam—the sky or outer space; tat—by the two; ubhaya—on both sides; sandhitam—where the two parts join.

**Перевод:**

**As a grain of wheat is divided into two parts and one can estimate the size of the upper part by knowing that of the lower, so, expert geographers instruct, one can understand the measurements of the upper part of the universe by knowing those of the lower part. The sky between the earthly sphere and heavenly sphere is called antarikṣa, or outer space. It adjoins the top of the sphere of earth and the bottom of that of heaven.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Just as in a dicot when the dimension of the one half is told the dimension of the other half is also known. *Te antarena* = between them. *Ubhayasandhitam*—both touching.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Etena = by the dimension of the earth. Tadvidas = the astronomers. Nishpava = a dichotic cereal \[grain\]; other cereals can also be taken. Antarikṣa has an extent of 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] is the opinion of Cakravartī \[Viśvanātha Cakravartī\], occupies the middle of Antarikṣa.

The two halves of the dicots like *nishpava* and others are identical in their magnitude. Like that, the magnitude of the upper heaven is identical to that of the lower earth \[Bhū-maṇḍala\]—the dimension of Antarikṣa between them is the same.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Nishpava is a food (grain), a dicot. By knowing the dimension of one half, that of the other half is also known. Between them is Antarikṣa touching both.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The width of heaven is also fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\] is the opinion of great people. The example given is that of the dichotic cereal *nishpava*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Because they are like two halves of a dichotic grain—by knowing the dimension of one half, the dimension of the other half is also known, as they are identical. Between them is Antarikṣa Loka, touching both of them on either side.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The same is stated by means of an example—a dicotic cereal is the example. By giving this example, the width of Antarikṣa (or Bhuvah) is also stated. It is also fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\].

### Text 3

*यन्मध्यगतो भगवांस्तपतामपतिस्तपन आतपेन त्रिलोकीं प्रतपत्यवभासयत्यात्म*  
*भासा स एष उदगयनदक्षिणायनवैषुवतसंज्ञाभिर्मान्द्यशैघ्र्यसमानाभिर्गतिभिरारोहण*  
*वारोहणसमानस्थानेषु यथासवनमभिपद्यमानो मकरादिषु राशिष्वहोरात्राणि*  
*दीर्घह्रस्वसमानानि विधत्ते ॥३॥*

*yan-madhya-gato bhagavāṁs tapatāṁ patis tapana ātapena tri-lokīṁ pratapaty avabhāsayaty ātma-bhāsā sa eṣa udagayana-dakṣiṇāyana-vaiṣuvata-saṁjñābhir māndya-śaighrya-samānābhir gatibhir ārohaṇāvarohaṇa-samāna-sthāneṣu yathā-savanam abhipadyamāno makarādiṣu rāśiṣv aho-rātrāṇi dīrgha-hrasva-samānāni vidhatte.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—of which (the intermediate space); madhya-gataḥ—being situated in the middle; bhagavān—the most powerful; tapatām patiḥ—the master of those that heat the whole universe; tapanaḥ—the sun; ātapena—by heat; tri-lokīm—the three worlds; pratapati—heats; avabhāsayati—lights; ātma-bhāsā—by its own illuminating rays; saḥ—that; eṣaḥ—the sun globe; udagayana—of passing to the northern side of the equator; dakṣiṇa-ayana—of passing to the southern side of the equator; vaiṣuvata—or of passing through the equator; saṁjñābhiḥ—by different names; māndya—characterized by slowness; śaighrya—swiftness; samānābhiḥ—and by equality; gatibhiḥ—by movement; ārohaṇa—of rising; avarohaṇa—of going down; samāna—or of staying in the middle; sthāneṣu—in positions; yathā-savanam—according to the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; abhipadyamānaḥ—moving; makara-ādiṣu—headed by the sign Makara (Capricorn); rāśiṣu—in different signs; ahaḥ-rātrāṇi—the days and nights; dīrgha—long; hrasva—short; samānāni—equal; vidhatte—makes.

**Перевод:**

**In the midst of that region of outer space \[antarikṣa\] is the most opulent sun, the king of all the planets that emanate heat, such as the moon. By the influence of its radiation, the sun heats the universe and maintains its proper order. It also gives light to help all living entities see. While passing toward the north, toward the south or through the equator, in accordance with the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, it is said to move slowly, swiftly or moderately. According to its movements in rising above, going beneath or passing through the equator—and correspondingly coming in touch with various signs of the zodiac, headed by Makara \[Capricorn\]—days and nights are short, long or equal to one another.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The sun’s slow, fast, and average motion is named Uttarāyaṇa and so on. During that time, the sun takes different courses some elevated and some not. He makes day and night long, short and equal in Capricorn and other constellations. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The position of the earth's surface has been described earlier. As an appendage for correct apprehension, the dimensions of the upper worlds must be described in three more chapters. The width of earth’s surface is fifty *crores* of *yojanas* \[four billion miles\]. By this, the width of heaven can also be known—it is also the same. Just as in a native flour mill made of two stones, if the width of the lower stone is known, that the upper stone is also known because both of them have the same dimension. It is like that here also.

The sky or Antrakisha loka has also the same division; it lies between the above two, touching them on both sides. The sun is at the center of the sky and by his movement causes the activities of the people living under his shine. He illuminates the three worlds—earth, sky and heaven. His gait \[speed of motion\] is not uniform; sometimes slow, fast and normal. These speeds are called Uttarāyaṇa, Dakṣiṇāyana and Vaishuva respectively. They are the elevated, inclined and normal tracks respectively. The days and nights get longer and shorter as he \[the sungod\] moves in Makara and five other constellations. As said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*, there is a circular track on Śiśumāra \[the mystical form of the dolphin\]. It is 8,000 *yojanas* \[64,000 miles\] in circumference. The sun and all the other planets and stars move along this path. Makara and other constellations are figures formed on Śiśumāra’s body. These three tracks are the elevated, inclined and normal tracks.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Etena = by the dimension of the Bhū-sphere. Nishpava = a dicot. Just as the dimension of one half is equal to that of the other, even so the upper world is of the same dimension as that of the lower. Between them Antarikṣa is situated, touching both of them. Antarikṣa's dimension is 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\]. The sun occupies the middle of the Antarikṣa by his slow, fast and medium speeds during Uttarāyaṇa, etc., which cause days and nights to become longer, shorter and equal. They are the elevated, inclined and the middle tracks respectively.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Uttarāyaṇa is the name of the slow motion—in the elevated track. Yathasavana = as per the time. In Makara (Capricorn) and five constellations, he \[the sungod\] makes the days gradually longer and the nights gradually shorter. Dakṣiṇāyana is the name of the fast motion by which he makes the nights gradually longer and the days gradually shorter in Cancer and five other constellations. By the vaishuvata gait he makes the days and nights equal.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Between them is situated the sky (Antarikṣa). It touches both the lower and upper worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Occupying the center of Dyuloka, Bhagavān Sūrya, the head of celestial bodies, illuminates the three worlds by his luster. He has three gaits, going through which he renders the days and nights longer, shorter or equal.

The stanza of *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* quoted earlier is also stated here, however a different meaning is given. The distance between the edges of the northern and southern speeds of elevation and depression is 180 *yojanas*. \[Note from the translator: perhaps the word *lakh*s \[10,000’s\] is missing here. In other words 18,000,000 *yojanas* or 144,000,000 miles\]. The circumference of the tracks is as stated earlier. While moving in a year through Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana, the lateral movement of the sun on Mānasottara is 180 (*lakh*) *yojanas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Antarikṣa has the same width as the earth and heaven and is placed by God between them. There is a statement of Madhwacharya that: “Antarikṣa and Swarga are one *crore yojanas* \[80,000,000 miles\] wide.” This does not refer to the entire loka \[planetary system\] but a part of both the worlds where demigods rejoice. So there is no contradiction.

### Text 4

*यदा मेषतुलयोर्वर्तते तदाहोरात्राणि समानानि भवन्ति यदा वृषभादिषु*  
*पञ्चसु च राशिषु चरति तदाहान्येव वर्धन्ते ह्रसति च मासि मास्येकैका घटिका*  
*रात्रिषु ॥४॥*

*yadā meṣa-tulayor vartate tadāho-rātrāṇi samānāni bhavanti yadā vṛṣabhādiṣu pañcasu ca rāśiṣu carati tadāhāny eva vardhante hrasati ca māsi māsy ekaikā ghaṭikā rātriṣu.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yadā—when; meṣa-tulayoḥ—in Meṣa (Aries) and Tulā (Libra); vartate—the sun exists; tadā—at that time; ahaḥ-rātrāṇi—the days and nights; samānāni—equal in duration; bhavanti—are; yadā—when; vṛṣabha-ādiṣu—headed by Vṛṣabha (Taurus) and Mithuna (Gemini); pañcasu—in the five; ca—also; rāśiṣu—signs; carati—moves; tadā—at that time; ahāni—the days; eva—certainly; vardhante—increase; hrasati—is diminished; ca—and; māsi māsi—in every month; eka-ekā—one; ghaṭikā—half hour; rātriṣu—in the nights.

**Перевод:**

**When the sun passes through Meṣa \[Aries\] and Tulā \[Libra\], the durations of day and night are equal. When it passes through the five signs headed by Vṛṣabha \[Taurus\], the duration of the days increases \[until Cancer\], and then it gradually decreases by half an hour each month, until day and night again become equal \[in Libra\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is said “equal” because there is not much of variation. Only one day and night will be exactly equal. Although the days get longer even in Taurus and Gemini, and shorter from Cancer and so on, it is said that days become longer when compared to the night. Even when nights get longer with respect to the day, it is said they become shorter. “By one ghatika \[a unit of time equaling 24 minutes\]” is an approximation since it actually always differs every month. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It is explained here that it is not to that the days always become longer and nights shorter. Rather, only when the sun moves from Taurus to Virgo do the days become longer—not otherwise.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

By the effulgence of Nārāyaṇa, the sun shines. He \[the sungod\] moves along with stars like any other planet. During Uttarāyaṇa, when he occupies Makara to Mithuna his movement is slow on the elevated inner track. During the Dakṣiṇāyana when he occupies the other six constellations, his movement is fast in the outside inclined track. When in Mesha and Tula, he moves with his normal speed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The same is now described with detail: because there is not much of variation, it is said they \[the duration of day and night\] are equal. Absolute equality will only occur on one particular day. Although in Karkataka, Simha and Kanya \[constellations\], the length of the days diminish, they are said to be longer because they are longer than the corresponding nights. “By one ghatika every month” is an approximation since it actually differs from month to month.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tat = mentioned above. Ekasya = of the northen of southern hemispheres.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The sun is situated in the middle of the sky. He is the lord of all celestial bodies as he nourishes the moon and other celestial bodies by his rays. He gives heat and light to the three worlds. Actually it is *antaryāmī* \[supersoul situated within the heart of the sungod\] who gives heat and light to the three worlds—that is why the word “Bhagavān” is used.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The features of Antarikṣa, and also the details of the three tracks, ascent, descent and normal are all stated. Here, “days become longer” means longer than 12 hours. Similarly, “nights become shorter” means less than 12 hours. Thus, there is no confusion.

### Text 5

*यदा वृश्चिकादिषु पञ्चसु वर्तते तदाहोरात्राणि विपर्ययाणि भवन्ति ॥५॥*

*yadā vṛścikādiṣu pañcasu vartate tadāho-rātrāṇi viparyayāṇi bhavanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yadā—when; vṛścika-ādiṣu—headed by Vṛścika (Scorpio); pañcasu—five; vartate—remains; tadā—at that time; ahaḥ-rātrāṇi—the days and nights; viparyayāṇi—the opposite (the duration of the day decreases, and that of night increases); bhavanti—are.

**Перевод:**

**When the sun passes through the five signs beginning with Vṛścika \[Scorpio\], the duration of the days decreases \[until Capricorn\], and then gradually it increases month after month, until day and night become equal \[in Aries\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Viparyayani—the days become shorter and nights longer.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Viparyayani means that the days become shorter and nights longer.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In the five constellations starting from Vrshabha it becomes the reverse of what is said earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The sun’s travel on elevated and lower tracks through the constellations of Makara, etc. cause changes in the duration of days and nights.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The days and nights become longer in Vrshabha and five constellations and shorter in Scorpio and five constellations respectively. That the days increase by “one ghatika a month” is an approximation—it is sometimes more and sometimes less than that.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The same idea is described in detail. Even though the days (period of sunlight) and nights go on changing the composite day (i.e. day + night) does not change—it is always 60 ghatikas (24 hours). If the day grows longer by a certain amount, the corresponding night becomes less by the same amount. This process starts from the day of equinox when the day and night are equal. The longest day will have the shortest night and vice-versa, thus, the total duration of a day remains unchanged.

### Text 6

*यावद्दक्षिणायनमहानि वर्धन्ते यावदुदगयनं रात्रयः ॥६॥*

*yāvad dakṣiṇāyanam ahāni vardhante yāvad udagayanaṁ rātrayaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvat—until; dakṣiṇa-ayanam—the sun passes to the southern side; ahāni—the days; vardhante—increase; yāvat—until; udagayanam—the sun passes to the northern side; rātrayaḥ—the nights.

**Перевод:**

**Until the sun travels to the south the days grow longer, and until it travels to the north the nights grow longer.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here the time of their increase and decrease is told.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What has been stated above is further narrated in detail. The seven winds: Aavaha, *pravāha*, Udvaha, Samvaha, Vivaha, Paravaha and Parivaha propel the Jyotis*cakra* of which Sūrya is the lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Yavad Dakṣiṇāyanam* = starting from Uttarāyaṇa until Dakṣiṇāyana.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Yavad dakshinayanam = starting from Uttarāyaṇa until Dakṣiṇāyana—this is how it should be interpreted in the ensuing passages also.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Viparyayani* means the nights get longer and the days reduce in length. The increase every month is as stated earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The actual increase is stated here. During Uttarāyaṇa, days go on getting longer than the previous night.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The tightening and loosening of ropes and all such things are again stated here.

### Text 7

*एवं नव कोटय एकपञ्चाशल्लक्षाणि योजनानां मानसोत्तर*  
*गिरिपरिवर्तनस्योपदिशन्ति तस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं पुरीं पूर्वस्मान्मेरोर्देवधानीं*  
*नाम दक्षिणतो याम्यां संयमनीं नाम पश्चाद्वारुणीं निम्लोचनीं नाम उत्तरतः*  
*सौम्यां विभावरीं नाम तासूदयमध्याह्नास्तमयनिशीथानीति भूतानां प्रवृत्तिनि*  
*वृत्तिनिमित्तानि समयविशेषेण मेरोश्चतुर्दिशम् ॥७॥*

*evaṁ nava koṭaya eka-pañcāśal-lakṣāṇi yojanānāṁ mānasottara-giri-parivartanasyopadiśanti tasminn aindrīṁ purīṁ pūrvasmān meror devadhānīṁ nāma dakṣiṇato yāmyāṁ saṁyamanīṁ nāma paścād vāruṇīṁ nimlocanīṁ nāma uttarataḥ saumyāṁ vibhāvarīṁ nāma tāsūdaya-madhyāhnāstamaya-niśīthānīti bhūtānāṁ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-nimittāni samaya-viśeṣeṇa meroś catur-diśam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; nava—nine; koṭayaḥ—ten millions; eka-pañcāśat—fifty-one; lakṣāṇi—hundred thousands; yojanānām—of the yojanas; mānasottara-giri—of the mountain known as Mānasottara; parivartanasya—of the circumambulation; upadiśanti—they (learned scholars) teach; tasmin—on that (Mānasottara Mountain); aindrīm—of King Indra; purīm—the city; pūrvasmāt—on the eastern side; meroḥ—of Sumeru Mountain; devadhānīm—Devadhānī; nāma—of the name; dakṣiṇataḥ—on the southern side; yāmyām—of Yamarāja; saṁyamanīm—Saṁyamanī; nāma—named; paścāt—on the western side; vāruṇīm—of Varuṇa; nimlocanīm—Nimlocanī; nāma—named; uttarataḥ—on the northern side; saumyām—of the moon; vibhāvarīm—Vibhāvarī; nāma—named; tāsu—in all of them; udaya—rising; madhyāhna—midday; astamaya—sunset; niśīthāni—midnight; iti—thus; bhūtānām—of the living entities; pravṛtti—of activity; nivṛtti—and cessation of activity; nimittāni—the causes; samaya-viśeṣeṇa—by the particular times; meroḥ—of Sumeru Mountain; catuḥ-diśam—the four sides.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued; My dear King, as stated before, the learned say that the sun travels over all sides of Mānasottara Mountain in a circle whose length is 95,100,000** ***yojanas*** **\[760,800,000 miles\]. On Mānasottara Mountain, due east of Mount Sumeru, is a place known as Devadhānī, possessed by King Indra. Similarly, in the south is a place known as Saṁyamanī, possessed by Yamarāja, in the west is a place known as Nimlocanī, possessed by Varuṇa, and in the north is a place named Vibhāvarī, possessed by the moon-god. Sunrise, midday, sunset and midnight occur in all those places according to specific times, thus engaging all living entities in their various occupational duties and also making them cease such duties.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By such slow and other motions: 95,100,000 \[*yojanas* or 760,800,000 miles\] circumference should be calculated from the diameter of 31,500,000 \[*yojanas* or 252,000,000 miles\]. So the distance traveled in fifteen ghatikas should be calculated by trinomials on this basis. The details that are required here are to be obtained from other Purāṇas. It is stated in the *Vāyu Purāṇa*:

*“For all planets there are only three tracks. The central one is called JARADGAVA, the northern one is called AIRAVATA, and the southern is called VAISHVANARA. These are the three tracks. Each one of these tracks is divided into three parts. Three stars constitute each such part. The northern track has three parts: NAGAVITHI, GAJAVITHI and AIRAVATI. ARSHABHI, GOVITHI and JARADGAVI are the parts of the middle track which is also called VAISHUVATA. AJAVITHI, MRGAVITHI and VAISHVANARI are the parts of the southern track. The details of the stars which form these parts are also explained:*

- Nagavithi—Aswini, Bharani, Krittika.
- Gajavithi—Rohini, Mrigashira, Ardra.
- Airavathi—Punarvasu, Pushvya, Ashlesha.
- Arshabi—Makha, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni.
- Govithi—Hasta, Chitra, Swathi.
- Jaradgavi—Vishaka, Anuradha, Jyesta.
- Ajavithi—Moola, Purvashada, Uttarashada.
- Mrgavithi—Śravaṇa, Dhanista, Satabhisha.
- Vaishvanari—Purvabhadra, Uttarabhadra, Revathi.

*Such being the situation, during Uttarāyaṇa, the two ropes tied to the yoke of the chariot are pulled up. The chariot enters the inner elevated track. The gait (motion) becomes slow and the days grow longer, and nights shorter. During Dakṣiṇāyana the two ropes are loosened, the chariot slips into the outer track. There, the gait is faster*—*days become shorter and nights longer. During VAISHAVATA the ropes are normal*—*the chariot moves on the central track*—*days and nights become equal. This is what is said in Viṣṇu Purāṇa.”* \[Note: the above two paragraphs are repeated by Vīrarāghava, Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

This is stated in this verse: “Yada neshatulayoh …” The points of sunrise and sunset on Mānasottara are stated. The city “Aindri” is situated in the east of that mountain. The sunrise and sunset in those cities differ in the four directions surrounding Meru. For those living in the south, “Aindri” is in the east. For those living in the west of Meru, Yamya becomes the point of sunrise and hence the east. For those living in the north, “Varuni” becomes east in the same manner. For those living in the east, “*saumya*” becomes the east and so on. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

The distance between Meru and Mānasottara is 31,500,000 *yojanas* \[252,000,000 miles\]. The width of the sun’s track is 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\]. The total 317 multiplied by 3 is 951 which is the circumference of the sun’s track. This is the distance covered in a single day. For fractions thereof we should calculate by three. The sunrise and midday sun are responsible for stirring up the people toward work—sunset and midnight are responsible for withdrawal from work. The terms “sunrise” and “sunset” are only by notation since in actuality there cannot be any rise or setting for one \[the sun\] who always moves. During Uttarāyaṇa, the chariot is dragged to the inner track which is smaller in width. Just like the movement of an ox very near to the thrashing pole becomes slow, so does the movement of the chariot in the inner track. In the outer track, the movement becomes faster like that of the ox at the farthest end from the thrashing pole. The sun will be visible for only a part of the period then and so the days become shorter.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Here the distance covered by the sun in a single day and night is stated—it is 95,100,000 \[*yojanas* or 760,800,000 miles\] as the seers say. The rising and setting of the sun in Devadhani and Nimlochani and so on are just a notation since there cannot be any rising or setting for one who is always moving. By his \[the sungod’s\] different positions on the mountain \[Mānasottara\] he causes different activities to people residing around Meru. Nishitha means midnight.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The inner diameter of Mānasottara is 31,500,000 *yojanas* \[252,000,000 miles\]. The width of the sun’s track is 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\]. The total 317 multiplied by 3 is 951 which is the circumference of the sun’s track. Indra’s city is situated in the east of the hill. Rising and setting are associated with these cities, they say. For those living in the south, sunrise will be at Indra’s city, for those living in the west, sunrise will be at Samyamani, for those living in the north, sunrise will be at Varunas’s city, and so on. Sunset, midday and midnight also should be construed in this manner.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The sun goes around the Mānasottara in his three gaits. The circumference of his track is 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\]. The sunrise, sunset and so on around Meru are only by notation—*Viṣṇu Purāṇa* explains that the relative visibility is called sunrise, midday and sunset.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

In this prose the distance covered by the sun in a single day is stated. It is 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\]. There are four cities situated atop Mānasottara, namely those of Indra, Yama, Varuna and Soma.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The path covered by the sun on Mānasottara is 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\]. The phenomenon of sunrise and sunset in the four directions around Meru is described as in other commentaries. The rising and mid-day are responsible for the activities of people. Sunset and midnight are responsible for withdrawal and rest.

### Text 8-9

*तत्रत्यानां दिवसमध्यङ्गत एव सदादित्यस्तपति सव्येनाचलं दक्षिणेन करोति*  
*॥८॥ यत्रोदेति तस्य ह समानसूत्रनिपाते निम्लोचति यत्र क्वचन*  
*स्यन्देनाभितपति तस्य हैष समानसूत्रनिपाते प्रस्वापयति तत्र गतं न पश्यन्ति*  
*ये तं समनुपश्येरन् ॥९॥*

*tatratyānāṁ divasa-madhyaṅgata eva sadādityas tapati savyenācalaṁ dakṣiṇena karoti; yatrodeti tasya ha samāna-sūtra-nipāte nimlocati yatra kvacana syandenābhitapati tasya haiṣa samāna-sūtra-nipāte prasvāpayati tatra gataṁ na paśyanti ye taṁ samanupaśyeran.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatratyānām—for the living entities residing on Mount Meru; divasa-madhyaṅgataḥ—being positioned as at midday; eva—indeed; sadā—always; ādityaḥ—the sun; tapati—heats; savyena—to the left side; acalam—Sumeru Mountain; dakṣiṇena—to the right (being forced by wind blowing to the right, the sun moves to the right); karoti—moves; yatra—the point where; udeti—it rises; tasya—of that position; ha—certainly; samāna-sūtra-nipāte—at the diametrically opposite point; nimlocati—the sun sets; yatra—where; kvacana—somewhere; syandena—with perspiration; abhitapati—heats (at midday); tasya—of that; ha—certainly; eṣaḥ—this (the sun); samāna-sūtra-nipāte—at the diametrically opposite point; prasvāpayati—the sun causes to sleep (as at midnight); tatra—there; gatam—gone; na paśyanti—do not see; ye—who; tam—the sunset; samanupaśyeran—seeing.

**Перевод:**

**The living entities residing on Sumeru Mountain are always very warm, as at midday, because for them the sun is always overhead. Although the sun moves counterclockwise, facing the constellations, with Sumeru Mountain on its left, it also moves clockwise and appears to have the mountain on its right because it is influenced by the dakṣiṇāvarta wind. People living in countries at points diametrically opposite to where the sun is first seen rising will see the sun setting, and if a straight line were drawn from a point where the sun is at midday, the people in countries at the opposite end of the line would be experiencing midnight. Similarly, if people residing where the sun is setting were to go to countries diametrically opposite, they would not see the sun in the same condition.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Tatratyanam* = for people residing in Meru. Although by his \[the sun’s\] motion, which is against the stars, he keeps Meru to his Left, he keeps Meru to the right as he is attached to the clockwise moving *jyotisa* wheel \[*kāla-cakra*, the wheel of time, indicating the movement of the constellations\] or the moved by the agency of *pravāha* Vāyu \[ropes of air\]. Because of the movement of the wheel, the sun appears to be attached to the earth at the time of sunrise, at a very long distance during midday and apparently entering the earth at sunset. When he \[the sun\] goes even further it will be midnight. All this is also with respect to those who live on the seashore, thus the Vedic sentence, “the sun rises from the waters and sets in the waters,” is not literal. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

It is told in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “During the sunrise, sunset and all other times and in all directions, the sun appears in front of them. It is sunrise when the sun becomes visible and sunset when he becomes invisible. Actually the sun neither rises nor rests. The visibility and otherwise is considered as similarly when he is in the intermediate directions of northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest he touches three other corner points and two cities. The directions northeast, etc. are corner points. It is said there only: “therefore in the north direction it as always day and night. Meru is situated to the north of all islands.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śrīvaṁśīdhara and Śukadeva\]

This verse clarifies the absence of the sun’s rising and setting. Syandena—by causing perspiration. Praswapayati—makes it midnight. Ye tam Samanupasyeran—the point diametrically opposite to the “praswapa” point.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Samanasutranipate = diametrically opposite point. Nimlochati = sets. Rising, setting, midday and midnight differ from *varṣa* to *varṣa* is what is stated here. Thus, around Meru, when there is sunrise at a place (*varṣa*) then it is midday in the previous *varṣa* and midnight in the next *varṣa* and sunset in the next *varṣa*, people living in every *varṣa* feel that they are to the south of Meru and experience sunrise and so on in the above manner.

Ata eva = because the sunrise and sunset are not fixed points.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

This has been stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*:

*“At the beginning of Uttarāyaṇa, the sun enters Makara. Then he goes to Khumbha (Aquarius) and Meena (Pisces). After covering these three constellations, he enters into Vaishuvati motion where he makes the days and nights equal. Then every day the nights decrease and the days become longer. At the end of Mithuna, the day is the longest. Entering Karkataka (cancer), the sun takes the Dakṣiṇāyana motion. Driven by the force of Vāyu, the sun moves faster and covers the region of earth in a short time just as the edge of a potter's wheel moves faster. He takes just twelve Muhurthas to cover the region of earth in the day and covers the night of 13 ½ stars in 18 muhurthas. Just as the center of a potter's wheel moves slowly, even the* sun *assumes a slow motion in Uttarāyaṇa. To cover the same region of earth he takes 18 Muhurthas during the day and covers the 13 ½ star belt during night in 12 Muhurthas. The sun is visible for a longer period and that is the reason for the days to go longer. Just as the navel of the potter's wheel also revolves in circular but stays where it is, so Dhruva executes the circular motion, but stays at the same place.”*

That the days and nights are equal both in Aries and Libra is stated in the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* also. As the sun completes a rotation on Mānasottara, he covers 95,100,000 \[*yojanas* or 760,800,000 miles\]. To bring home the idea of sunrise and sunset, the position of the four cities on Mānasottara is stated. In the east there is Devadhani, in the south—Samyamani, in the west—Nimlochani and in the north—Vibhavaro, respectively ruled by Indra, Yama, Varuna and Soma. The sunrise stirs people into activity and sunset makes them retire from work. For people to the south of Meru, it is sunrise in Devadhani and sunset in Nimlochani. For people living to the west of Meru, it is sunrise at Samyamani and sunset at Vibhavari. Like this, it should be understood for all other places. For people living in Meru, There is neither sunrise nor sunset—they always see the sun as occupying the position at midday. Also Meru is to the north of people living any where in any island including Plakṣa Island and others. All these are stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*.

Here the details of sunrise and sunset are stated. At what point the sun rises on the Mānasottara mountain, he sets exactly at the diametrically opposite point. If he causes sweat and fatigue at some point on the mountain, at the diametrically opposite point he sends them to sleep. So if it is midday at Samyamani, it has to be midnight at Vibhavari. It should be understood like this in all the four directions. \[Note: these paragraphs are repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

In Ilavrta-varṣa the sun moves in the left direction of Meru, keeping Meru always to his right. The motion will be substantiated later.

Where he \[the sun\] rises on the Meru, he sets in the exactly diametrically opposite point. During Dakṣiṇāyana, every day the rise will be a bit more towards the south than in the previous day. The setting also will be more towards the south than in the previous day. During Uttarāyaṇa both of them inch towards the north daily. If he rises in Devadhani, he moves people into daily activities, while setting at Nimlochani, he causes people to withdraw. When he is at Vibhavari, it is midnight and he causes them to sleep.

Tatraiva = In Vishnu Purana only.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is stated 5,100,000 (in excess of 90,000,000). This should be examined. It should be 945, i.e., 3 x 315 *yojanas*. Or it may be taken as 315+2 *lakh* excess in Mānasottara according to Bhāgavatam. In the commentary, the *vittis* are described according to *Vāyu Purāṇa* and not according to stars as they are found in different places. It is not according to the intercepts of the sun. For then Revathi and Aswini (one pair) and Aswini and Chitra (another pair) should be placed in the same Vithi according to the ascent and descent. So the relationship between the vithis and the stars should be explained otherwise: as the stars are the superintending deities of the *vithis*. The lines in the commentary \[Note from the translator: apparently Śrīdhara’s\] suggest this.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

There is no sunrise or sunset for the people residing in Meru. Even *Parasara Smrti* says that there is no rising or setting for the sun who is always moving.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“They are reversed” means nights become longer and days decrease.

Here the time of the increase and decrease is stated. From Uttarāyaṇa’s starting until Dakṣiṇāyana, the sun moves with a slow gait. Then each day becomes longer than the previous day and each night becomes shorter than the previous night. Beginning from Dakṣiṇāyana until Uttarāyaṇa the case is reversed—nights grow longer and days shorter than in the previous days.

A pertinent question could be: “When the sun’s track is the same, how can there be changes in day and night?” The reply is even though the track is the same, the width of the constellations are not the same and so as the sun moves in those constellations, he takes a longer or shorter time, causing the changes in the dimension of day and night.

Of the constellations, Pisces and Aries are short, Taurus and Aquarius are slightly longer than that. Capricorn and Gemini are still longer. Leo and Scorpio are even longer than the above two. Cancer and Sagittarius are the longest. Virgo and Libra are neither long nor short. Thus, because of the disproportion of the constellations, the duration changes. This is also stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*. \[Note: these paragraphs are repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

For those living in Meru, there is no sunrise or sunset.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The sun rises and sets exactly at diametrically opposite points on the Mānasottara Mountain. It should be noted that this situation occurs only on equinoxes. From the next day onwards during Uttarāyaṇa, both the rising and setting points are to the north of the points of the previous day, whereas during Dakṣiṇāyana they are to the south.

### Text 10

*यदा चैन्द्र्याः पुर्याः प्रचलते पञ्चदशघटिकाभिर्याम्यां सपादकोटिद्वयं*  
*योजनानां सार्धद्वादशलक्षाणि साधिकानि चोपयाति ॥१०॥*

*yadā caindryāḥ puryāḥ pracalate pañcadaśa-ghaṭikābhir yāmyāṁ sapāda-koṭi-dvayaṁ yojanānāṁ sārdha-dvādaśa-lakṣāṇi sādhikāni copayāti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yadā—when; ca—and; aindryāḥ—of Indra; puryāḥ—from the residence; pracalate—it moves; pañcadaśa—by fifteen; ghaṭikābhiḥ—half hours (actually twenty-four minutes); yāmyām—to the residence of Yamarāja; sapāda-koṭi-dvayam—two and a quarter crores (22,500,000); yojanānām—of yojanas; sārdha—and one half; dvādaśa-lakṣāṇi—twelve hundred thousand; sādhikāni—twenty-five thousand more; ca—and; upayāti—he passes over.

**Перевод:**

**When the sun travels from Devadhānī, the residence of Indra, to Saṁyamanī, the residence of Yamarāja, it travels 23,775,000 yojanas \[190,200,000 miles\] in fifteen ghaṭikās \[six hours\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sadhikani = in excess by 25,000.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Here the time taken to travel from one city to another on the mountain is stated. When he \[the sun\] starts from Indra’s city, he covers 23,775,000 *yojanas* \[190,200,000 miles\] in 15 ghatikas and reaches Samyamani in the south.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Sadhikani* = exceeding by 25000.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The length of the track is stated here. Because the circumference of the circle is slightly more than three times its diameter, the length is stated as 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\]. The sunrise and sunset on all the four sides of Meru are only by notation. It is not the same for all places. When there is sunrise at a particular place, it is midnight at another place, sunset at a second place and midday at a third place. Similarly the case with sunset and so on. This holds good on all sides of Meru.

### Text 11

*एवं ततो वारुणीं सौम्यामैन्द्रीं च पुनस्तथान्ये च ग्रहाः सोमादयो*  
*नक्षत्रैः सह ज्योतिश्चक्रे समभ्युद्यन्ति सह वा निम्लोचन्ति ॥११॥*

*evaṁ tato vāruṇīṁ saumyām aindrīṁ ca punas tathānye ca grahāḥ somādayo nakṣatraiḥ saha jyotiś-cakre samabhyudyanti saha vā nimlo-canti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this way; tataḥ—from there; vāruṇīm—to the quarters where Varuṇa lives; saumyām—to the quarters where the moon lives; aindrīṁ ca—and to the quarters where Indra lives; punaḥ—again; tathā—so also; anye—the others; ca—also; grahāḥ—planets; soma-ādayaḥ—headed by the moon; nakṣatraiḥ—all the stars; saha—with; jyotiḥ-cakre—in the celestial sphere; samabhyudyanti—rise; saha—along with; vā—or; nimlocanti—set.

**From the residence of Yamarāja the sun travels to Nimlocanī, the residence of Varuṇa, from there to Vibhāvarī, the residence of the moon-god, and from there again to the residence of Indra. **Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Although the sun rises and sets along with other stars, they are not visible during sunlight, thus their association is stated in relationship with the moon and other planets.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It should be understood the same of way: as he \[the sun\] leaves Samyamani and reaches Nimlochani and Vibhavari. Even the moon and other planets accompanied by stars rise and set like the sun in Devadhani and other cities. The planets set along with the stars. Even the sun rises with the stars and sets with the stars, yet because the stars are not visible during day light, the sun’s association with the stars is not mentioned.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Sardhadwadasa = 1,275,000.

Yatra = in the region below the *vithi*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Saha va = along with.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Sadhikani = 23,775,000 *yojanas* \[190,200,000 miles\]. This multiplied by 4 gives 95,100,000 *yojanas* \[760,800,000 miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Adhikara = exceeding by 25,000.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Although the sun rises and sets along with stars like other planets, it is not mentioned, as stars are not visible in daylight.

The other planets like the moon and others also have their rising and setting on Mānasottara along with the stars. But in case of the sun, the association of stars is not mentioned as they are not visible during sunlight.

Sadhikani = 25,000 is the exceeding part.

### Text 12

*एवं मुहूर्तेन चतुस्त्रिंशल्लक्षयोजनान्यष्टशताधिकानि सौरो रथस्त्रयीमयोऽसौ चतसृषु*

evam—thus; muhūrtena—in a muhūrta (forty-eight minutes); catuḥ-triṁśat—thirty-four; lakṣa—hundred thousands; yojanāni—yojanas; aṣṭa-śatādhikāni—increased by eight hundred; sauraḥ rathaḥ—the chariot of the sun-god; trayī-mayaḥ—which is worshiped by the Gāyatrī mantra (oṁ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ tat savitur, etc.); asau—that; catasṛṣu—to the four; parivartate—he moves; purīṣu—through different residential quarters.

**Thus the chariot of the sun-god, which is trayīmaya, or worshiped by the words oṁ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, travels through the four residences mentioned above at a speed of 3,400,800 yojanas \[27,206,400 miles\] in a muhūrta.**

Trayimaya and all is for the sake of worship.

The distance covered in a *muhūrta* is on the Mānasottara—not any where else. In other works on astronomy the orbit of the sun is stated lesser than this.

“Trayimaya” is stated for the sake of worship.

The distance covered in a single *Muhūrta* is stated here. Trayimaya is stated for worship.

12: The distance from one city to another on Manasottara is one fourth of its circumference. In 15 Ghatikas he covers the distance of 237.7

The sun’s chariot covers 3,400,800 *yojanas* \[27,206,400 miles\] in a *muhūrta* and 2,000 *yojanas* \[16,000 miles\] and a *gavyuh* in a *kshana* \[a unit of time, 1.6 seconds\]. The numbers do not tally here and we get a doubt whether this is the motion of the sun’s chariot or of *jyotis-cakra*.

### Text 13

*यस्यैकं चक्रं द्वादशारं षण्नेमि त्रिणाभि संवत्सरात्मकं*  
*समामनन्ति तस्याक्षो मेरोर्मूर्धनि कृतो मानसोत्तरे कृतेतरभागो यत्र*  
*प्रोतं रविरथचक्रं तैलयन्त्रचक्रवद्भ्रमन्मानसोत्तरगिरौ परिभ्रमति ॥१३॥*

*yasyaikaṁ cakraṁ dvādaśāraṁ ṣaṇ-nemi tri-ṇābhi saṁvatsarātmakaṁ samāmananti tasyākṣo meror mūrdhani kṛto mānasottare kṛtetara-bhāgo yatra protaṁ ravi-ratha-cakraṁ taila-yantra-cakravad bhraman mānasottara-girau paribhramati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of which; ekam—one; cakram—wheel; dvādaśa—twelve; aram—spokes; ṣaṭ—six; nemi—the segments of the rim; tri-ṇābhi—the three pieces of the hub; saṁvatsara-ātmakam—whose nature is a saṁvatsara; samāmananti—they fully describe; tasya—the chariot of the sun-god; akṣaḥ—the axle; meroḥ—of Sumeru Mountain; mūrdhani—on the top; kṛtaḥ—fixed; mānasottare—on the mountain known as Mānasottara; kṛta—fixed; itara-bhāgaḥ—the other end; yatra—where; protam—fixed on; ravi-ratha-cakram—the wheel of the chariot of the sun-god; taila-yantra-cakra-vat—like the wheel of an oil-pressing machine; bhramat—moving; mānasottara-girau—on Mānasottara Mountain; paribhramati—turns.

**Перевод:**

**The chariot of the sun-god has only one wheel, which is known as Saṁvatsara. The twelve months are calculated to be its twelve spokes, the six seasons are the sections of its rim, and the three cātur-māsya periods are its three-sectioned hub. One side of the axle carrying the wheel rests upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, and the other rests upon Mānasottara Mountain. Affixed to the outer end of the axle, the wheel continuously rotates on Mānasottara Mountain like the wheel of an oil-pressing machine.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The twelve months are the spokes; the six seasons—the rim and the three chaturmasyas—the navel of the wheel. 50,000 *yojanas* \[400,000 miles\] above the Mānasottara Mountain, on a track supported by Vāyu or it should be assumed that the wheel itself has that height. Otherwise since Mānasottara is only 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high and Meru is 84,000 *yojanas* \[762,000 miles\] high, the axle cannot be horizontal. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava and Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The sun’s chariot has only one wheel. There are twelve spokes controlled by the deities of the twelve months. The six pieces of the rim are controlled by the deities of the six seasons. The navel of the wheel is called saṁvatsara by name. The length of the axle that stretches from Meru to Mānasottara is 25,700,000 *yojanas* \[205,600,000 miles\] is stated in the Purāṇa. "The axle to the chariot that stretches from Meru to Mānasottara is 250 *lakh* + seven *lakh*s.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In the commentary it is stated as a second alternative that the wheel of the chariot could be that high. In that case there cannot be two movements at the same time. The pulling in opposite directions may stop the chariot. Even though the horses are strong, the wheel of wind only may move forward detached from the chariot. The chariot cannot move. The chariot may be seen in the constellation of other stars. But it cannot occupy different places by itself. For the moon and other planets, different positions are possible and are seen according to the analogy of the ant on the potter’s wheel. So the first alternative of an elevated track supported by wind should be adhered to. This elevated track should be 90,000 *yojanas* \[720,000 miles\] above Mānasottara and 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] above Meru. \[Note from the translator: so that the axle becomes horizontal\].

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The twelve months are the spokes; the six seasons form the rim and three chaturmasas the navel of the wheel. One end of the axle, to which the wheel is fixed, is fixed slightly below the top of Meru. The opinion of His Holiness Śhridhara Svami is that the other end of the axle, near the wheel, moves on a track which is 50,000 *yojanas* above Mānasottara and is supported by wind. The length of the axle which is 60,000 *yojanas* above the earth is slightly less than 15,700,000.

What is the distance that the sun covers in a single *Muhūrta*?

The wheel of the chariot fixed at the other end on Mānasottara revolves like the wheel of a native oil mill.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Although the sun rises and sets along with stars like other planets, it is not mentioned because stars are not visible in the daylight.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The spokes, rim and the hub of the wheel are described. The statement that the sun’s chariot and the Jyotis*cakra* are equal is only for the sake of worship.

### Text 14

*तस्मिन्नक्षे कृतमूलो द्वितीयोऽक्षस्तुर्यमानेन सम्मितस्तैलयन्त्राक्षवद् ध्रुवे*  
*कृतोपरिभागः ॥१४॥*

*tasminn akṣe kṛtamūlo dvitīyo 'kṣas turyamānena sammitas taila-yantrākṣavad dhruve kṛtopari-bhāgaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasmin akṣe—in that axle; kṛta-mūlaḥ—whose base is fixed; dvitīyaḥ—a second; akṣaḥ—axle; turyamānena—by one fourth; sammitaḥ—measured; taila-yantra-akṣa-vat—like the axle of an oil-pressing machine; dhruve—to Dhruvaloka; kṛta—fixed; upari-bhāgaḥ—upper portion.

**Перевод:**

**As in an oil-pressing machine, this first axle is attached to a second axle, which is one-fourth as long \[3,937,500 yojanas, or 31,500,000 miles\]. The upper end of this second axle is attached to Dhruvaloka by a rope of wind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

One end of (the shaft) is fixed to the axle near the wheel; the other end is at Dhruva. The length of the shaft is a fourth of the distance between Meru and Mānasottara which is 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\], thus 157.5 divided by 4 = 3,937,500 *yojanas* \[31,500,000 miles\]. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The second axle is one fourth in length to that of the first is what it means.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There is another axle fixed to the first axle near the wheel. Its length is one fourth of the first one, i.e., 3,937,500 *yojanas* \[31,500,000 miles\]. It is situated in the region of the salt ocean diametrically opposite to the first axle. The second axle is shorter than the first, so it is tied by the ropes of the wind at Dhruvaloka.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Aksha = axle.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

This is what should be noted here. According to Parasara Smriti, the sun is at a height of 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] from the earth and Dhruva is 3,800,000 *yojanas* \[30,400,000 miles\] above the sun. Thus, the second axle should be slightly long and it should be fixed up or down in Viṣṇupada, where Dhruva is.

Here the length of the downward Dakṣiṇāyana track is stated. This is where the sun moves fast. A day has 30 *muhūrtas* and the total circumference is 951 *lakh*, thus in one *muhūrta* the distance covered should be 951/30 = 3,170,000 *yojanas* \[25,360,000 miles\]. However, here it is stated as 3,400,800 *yojanas* \[27,206,400 miles\]. It is so because this is the Dakṣiṇāyana track where the sun’s movement is faster. In his faster movement, the sun covers 3,400,800 *yojanas* \[27,206,400 miles\] per *muhūrta*. This is not the average speed and so there is no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The second axle is one fourth the length of the first one. The first one being 15,750,000 *yojanas* \[126,000,000 miles\], the second one is 3,937,500 *yojanas* \[31,500,000 miles\] long.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The second axle (shaft) is fixed to the first near the wheel and the other end of the second is at Dhruva. The length of the second is a fourth part of the first one.

### Text 15

*रथनीडस्तु षट्त्रिंशल्लक्षयोजनायतस्तत्तुरीयभागविशालस्तावान् रविरथयुगो*  
*यत्र हयाश्छन्दोनामानः सप्तारुणयोजिता वहन्ति देवमादित्यम् ॥१५॥*

*ratha-nīḍas tu ṣaṭ-triṁśal-lakṣa-yojanāyatas tat-turīya-bhāga-viśālas tāvān ravi-ratha-yugo yatra hayāś chando-nāmānaḥ saptāruṇa-yojitā vahanti devam ādityam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ratha-nīḍaḥ—the interior of the chariot; tu—but; ṣaṭ-triṁśat-lakṣa-yojana-āyataḥ—3,600,000 yojanas long; tat-turīya-bhāga—one quarter of that measure (900,000 yojanas); viśālaḥ—having a width; tāvān—so much also; ravi-ratha-yugaḥ—the yoke for the horses; yatra—where; hayāḥ—horses; chandaḥ-nāmānaḥ—having the different names of Vedic meters; sapta—seven; aruṇa-yojitāḥ—hooked up by Aruṇadeva; vahanti—carry; devam—the demigod; ādityam—the sun-god.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, the carriage of the sun-god's chariot is estimated to be 3,600,000 yojanas \[28,800,000 miles\] long and one-fourth as wide \[900,000 yojanas, or 7,200,000 miles\]. The chariot's horses, which are named after Gāyatrī and other Vedic meters, are harnessed by Aruṇadeva to a yoke that is also 900,000 yojanas wide. This chariot continuously carries the sun-god.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Nida = seat yoked by Aruna.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The seat of the chariot is 3,600,000 *yojanas* \[28,800,000 miles\] x 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\]. The yoke of the chariot is also 3,600,000 *yojanas* \[28,800,000 miles\] long and 900,000 *yojanas* broad. The goddesses of the seven meters, Gāyatrī and others, are yoked to the chariot by Aruna. They draw the chariot.

There is another axle attached to the former long axle, to which the wheel is fixed. One end of the second axle is fixed to the former near the wheel. The other end of the second axle is in Dhruva loka. The length of the second axle (shaft) is a fourth part of the former’s length. The seat of the sun in the chariot is 3,600,000 *yojanas* \[28,800,000 miles\] wide and 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\] deep. The yoke has the same length as that of the width of long axle mentioned earlier. The horses are tied to the yoke to the left of the wheel. Some say that it is 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\]—only Aruna knows the truth. The length of the central beam which stretches in the middle from between the yoke to behind the chariot should also be calculated accordingly.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Rathanida is not the sun’s seat—but rather the region of wind that moves along with the chariot. The chariot is very small. The width of the sun’s disc should also be constructed accordingly.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nida = inner chamber of the chariot. The sun sits in the chamber which is 40,000 *yojanas* \[320,000 miles\] above the wheel. The horses Gāyatrī and others are yoked by Aruna.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Here “ratha nida” should be understood as the aerial region in contact with the moving chariot. It does not mean the central seat where the sun-god sits, because the chariot has a very small dimension. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “The sun’s chariot is nine thousand *yojanas*.” This is how the width 10,000. *yojanas* of the sun’s disc is also to be understood.

As per the Matsya Purāṇa, the seven meters take the form of horses and pull the chariot along.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The horses bear the names of Gāyatrī and other meters.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The axle is situated above the Mānasottara Mountain. Otherwise Mānasottara, being 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high and Meru being 84,000 *yojanas* \[672,000 miles\] high, the axle cannot be horizontal.

The sun’s seat in the chariot is 3,600,000 yojanas \[28,800,000 miles\] by 900,000 yojanas \[7,200,000 miles\]. Even the yoke is 900,000 yojanas \[7,200,000 miles\] long. Aruna is Garuda's brother and due to their association with Garuda, the horses are Gayatri, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The seat of the sun’s chariot is 3,600,000 *yojanas* \[28,800,000 miles\] wide and 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\] deep. The horses, the seven meters, are yoked by Aruna, the driver.

purastāt—in front; savituḥ—of the sun-god; aruṇaḥ—the demigod named Aruṇa; paścāt—looking backward; ca—and; niyuktaḥ—engaged; sautye—of a charioteer; karmaṇi—in the work; kila—certainly; āste—remains.

**Although Aruṇadeva sits in front of the sun-god and is engaged in driving the chariot and controlling the horses, he looks backward toward the sun-god.**

He is seated in front of the sun, facing the sun.

Aruna is seated both the front and on another side of the sun. This situation occurs because of the multiplicity of bodies.

Although sitting in front of the sun, he is facing west—it is stated in the *Vāyu Purāṇa* that the position of the horses is to the left of the wheel.

Aruna sits in front of the sun facing him and drives the chariot with his back turned towards the track that lies ahead. It is also explained that he faces the east and drives the chariot towards the west. Anyone who faces the sun faces the east.

Aruna sits in front of the sun facing him and drives the chariot with his back turned towards the track that lies ahead. It is also explained that he faces the east and drives the chariot towards the west. Anyone who faces the sun faces the east.

Aruna is appointed as the driver of the chariot and even though he sits in front of the sun, he faces the sun.

Aruna sits in the place assigned for the driver in front of the sun. He is slightly to the back of the seat. If we do not interpret the sentence this way, the phenomenon of Arunodaya before sunrise cannot be explained.

Now on the basis of the Purāṇa, Vijaya Dhwaja says the axle is 25,700,000 *yojanas* \[205,600,000 miles\] long—then certainly this is not the perpendicular distance. Therefore Vijaya Dhwaja does not subscribe to the idea that the track is either 50,000 *yojanas* \[400,000 miles\] or 90,000 *yojanas* \[720,000 miles\] above Mānasottara and is supported by Vāyu.\]

The passage starting with the word *laksha* and ending with the word *bhuvalayasya* is a verse. “He” means the sun.

## Chapter 22 - The Orbits of the Planets

### Text 1

*राजोवाच*  
*यदेतद्भगवत आदित्यस्य मेरुं ध्रुवं च प्रदक्षिणेन परिक्रामतो*  
*राशीनामभिमुखं प्रचलितं चाप्रदक्षिणं भगवतोपवर्णितममुष्य वयं कथमनु*  
*मिमीमहीति ॥१॥*

*rājovāca*  
*yad etad bhagavata ādityasya meruṁ dhruvaṁ ca pradakṣiṇena parikrāmato rāśīnām abhimukhaṁ pracalitaṁ cāpradakṣiṇaṁ bhagavatopavarṇitam amuṣya vayaṁ katham anumimīmahīti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

rājā uvāca—the King (Mahārāja Parīkṣit) inquired; yat—which; etat—this; bhagavataḥ—of the most powerful; ādityasya—of the sun (Sūrya Nārāyaṇa); merum—the mountain known as Sumeru; dhruvam ca—as well as the planet known as Dhruvaloka; pradakṣiṇena—by placing on the right; parikrāmataḥ—which is going around; rāśīnām—the different signs of the zodiac; abhimukham—facing toward; pracalitam—moving; ca—and; apradakṣiṇam—placing on the left; bhagavatā—by Your Lordship; upavarṇitam—described; amuṣya—of that; vayam—we (the hearer); katham—how; anumimīmahi—can accept it by argument and inference; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī: My dear lord, you have already affirmed the truth that the supremely powerful sun-god travels around Dhruvaloka with both Dhruvaloka and Mount Sumeru on his right. Yet at the same time the sun-god faces the signs of the zodiac and keeps Sumeru and Dhruvaloka on his left. How can we reasonably accept that the sun-god proceeds with Sumeru and Dhruvaloka on both his left and right simultaneously?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The anticlockwise movement against the constellations is discussed. “As you stated, he \[the sun\] moves on the left side of Meru, always keeping Meru to his right. You have also stated a clockwise motion. How do we understand this?

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The relevance of this chapter is as told in the previous chapter. The *rāśis* also move in the anticlockwise direction. Then how do we correctly understand the movement of the sun in the anticlockwise direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A doubt arises as it is said, “going to the left and keeping to the right.” Clockwise motion is what is observed everyday. The movement against the *rāśis* is anticlockwise. They are opposite to each other and hence the doubt.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The idea behind the question is that a single object cannot have two different motions (in opposite directions) simultaneously.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“You have said that the sun goes around Meru along with the other nakshatras (stars) in the clockwise direction and you have also said that the sun moves against the direction of stars in the anticlockwise direction. Since the two movements are opposite to each other, how do we understand this?”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Abhimukha means clockwise.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The position of the moon and other planets is stated in this chapter. The king asks about the two different motions of the sun referred to in the previous chapter, namely clockwise and anticlockwise.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

“In the previous chapter, you have said the sun moves both in the clockwise and anticlockwise directions. It is contradictory, yet your words cannot be dismissed. How do we understand this?”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**
