“You have described two motions for the sun—one along with the constellations in the clockwise direction and the other against the *rāśis* in the anticlockwise direction. How to reconcile this is our question.”

### Text 2

*स होवाच*  
*यथा कुलालचक्रेण भ्रमता सह भ्रमतां तदाश्रयाणां पिपीलिकादीनां*  
*गतिरन्यैव प्रदेशान्तरेष्वप्युपलभ्यमानत्वादेवं नक्षत्रराशिभिरुपलक्षितेन*  
*कालचक्रेण ध्रुवं मेरुं च प्रदक्षिणेन परिधावता सह परिधावमानानां*  
*तदाश्रयाणां सूर्यादीनां ग्रहाणां गतिरन्यैव नक्षत्रान्तरे राश्यन्तरे*  
*चोपलभ्यमानत्वात् ॥२॥*

*sa hovāca*  
*yathā kulāla-cakreṇa bhramatā saha bhramatāṁ tad-āśrayāṇāṁ pipīlikādīnāṁ gatir anyaiva pradeśāntareṣv apy upalabhyamānatvād evaṁ nakṣatra-rāśibhir upalakṣitena kāla-cakreṇa dhruvaṁ meruṁ ca pradakṣiṇena paridhāvatā saha paridhāvamānānāṁ tad-āśrayāṇāṁ sūryādīnāṁ grahāṇāṁ gatir anyaiva nakṣatrāntare rāśy-antare copalabhyamānatvāt.*

**Пословный перевод:**

saḥ—Śukadeva Gosvāmī; ha—very clearly; uvāca—answered; yathā—just as; kulāla-cakreṇa—a potter's wheel; bhramatā—turning around; saha—with; bhramatām—of those turning around; tat-āśrayāṇām—being located on that (wheel); pipīlika-ādīnām—of small ants; gatiḥ—the motion; anyā—other; eva—certainly; pradeśa-antareṣu—in different locations; api—also; upalabhyamānatvāt—due to being experienced; evam—similarly; nakṣatra-rāśibhiḥ—by the stars and signs; upalakṣitena—being seen; kāla-cakreṇa—with the great wheel of time; dhruvam—the star known as Dhruvaloka; merum—the mountain known as Sumeru; ca—and; pradakṣiṇena—on the right; paridhāvatā—going around; saha—with; paridhāvamānānām—of those going around; tat-āśrayāṇām—whose shelter is that wheel of time; sūrya-ādīnām—headed by the sun; grahāṇām—of the planets; gatiḥ—the motion; anyā—other; eva—certainly; nakṣatra-antare—in different stars; rāśi-antare—in different signs; ca—and; upalabhyamānatvāt—due to being observed.

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī clearly answered: When a potter's wheel is moving and small ants located on that big wheel are moving with it, one can see that their motion is different from that of the wheel because they appear sometimes on one part of the wheel and sometimes on another. Similarly, the signs and constellations, with Sumeru and Dhruvaloka on their right, move with the wheel of time, and the antlike sun and other planets move with them. The sun and planets, however, are seen in different signs and constellations at different times. This indicates that their motion is different from that of the zodiac and the wheel of time itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The essence of the reply is that both these movements are not contradictory because one is due to the movement of the sun and the other to that of the *chakra* (*jyotis-cakra*).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The reply given is adducing an analogy of an ant and a potter’s wheel. The ant on the potter’s wheel moves when the potter’s wheel moves; however, the ant is not fixed to the wheel. Thus, when the wheel starts moving, if the ant also starts moving, it will be found in a different place on the wheel when the wheel completes a full rotation. If the speed of the ant is less than that of the wheel, then the place on the wheel where the ant is found after the completion of each rotation will be in the opposite direction of the movement of the wheel.

Here also the sun and the stars move in the clockwise direction, although they cannot be moved without a support. It should be inferred that the very support is *kāla-cakra*. Actually *kāla-cakra* is Śiśumāra himself. The sun is found in different places on the *kāla-cakra* each day. This anticlockwise motion is the apparent motion, while the actual movement is in the clockwise direction. Hence there should be no difficulty in understanding this.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Just as an ant which moves in the clockwise direction on a potter's wheel, also moving in the clockwise direction, is found at different places on the wheel at different times because of the difference in their speeds, even the sun who moves in the clockwise direction along with the stars around Dhruva and Meru is found in different places because of the difference of his speed and that of the stars. This causes his anticlockwise motion which is only an apparent motion. The absolute motion is in the clockwise direction only.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Śuka clearly replied: as they move along with the *chakra*, there are two movements—one induced by the wheel and the other of their own. So there is no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

As they move under the influence of *kāla-cakra*—the motion caused by their individual effort is different because they are found in different constellations.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The crux of the reply is this: just as for the ant on the potter's wheel, there are two motions, one due to the wheel and the other due to the ant itself, even so, here, one movement of the sun is due to *kāla-cakra* and the other is due to himself. Hence there is no contradiction.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Because of the two different speeds of the potter's wheel and the ant, the ant has a different motion. Similarly, the sun has two motions—one is of the *kāla-cakra* and the other his \[the sun’s\] own.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The movement of the ant on the potter’s wheel is different only because it is found in different places on the wheel. Had the speed of the ant been the same as that of the wheel, it would be found in exactly the same place on the wheel. By this example the two-fold motion of the sun and other planets is justifiable since they are found in different parts of the *kāla-cakra* which is their support.

### Text 3

*स एष भगवानादिपुरुष एव साक्षान्नारायणो लोकानां स्वस्तय आत्मानं त्रयीमयं*  
*कर्मविशुद्धिनिमित्तं कविभिरपि च वेदेन विजिज्ञास्यमानो द्वादशधा*  
*विभज्य षट्सु वसन्तादिष्वृतुषु यथोपजोषमृतुगुणान् विदधाति ॥३॥*

*sa eṣa bhagavān ādi-puruṣa eva sākṣān nārāyaṇo lokānāṁ svastaya ātmānaṁ trayīmayaṁ karma-viśuddhi-nimittaṁ kavibhir api ca vedena vijijñāsyamāno dvādaśadhā vibhajya ṣaṭsu vasantādiṣv ṛtuṣu yathopa-joṣam ṛtu-guṇān vidadhāti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

saḥ—that; eṣaḥ—this; bhagavān—the supremely powerful; ādi-puruṣaḥ—the original person; eva—certainly; sākṣāt—directly; nārāyaṇaḥ—the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa; lokānām—of all the planets; svastaye—for the benefit; ātmānam—Himself; trayī-mayam—consisting of the three Vedas (Sāma, Yajur and Ṛg); karma-viśuddhi—of purification of fruitive activities; nimittam—the cause; kavibhiḥ—by great saintly persons; api—also; ca—and; vedena—by Vedic knowledge; vijijñāsyamānaḥ—being inquired about; dvādaśa-dhā—in twelve divisions; vibhajya—dividing; ṣaṭsu—in six; vasanta-ādiṣu—headed by spring; ṛtuṣu—seasons; yathā-upajoṣam—according to the enjoyment of their past activities; ṛtu-guṇān—the qualities of the different seasons; vidadhāti—he arranges.

**Перевод:**

**The original cause of the cosmic manifestation is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa. When great saintly persons, fully aware of the Vedic knowledge, offered prayers to the Supreme Person, He descended to this material world in the form of the sun to benefit all the planets and purify fruitive activities. He divided Himself into twelve parts and created seasonal forms, beginning with spring. In this way He created the seasonal qualities, such as heat, cold and so on.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

For the full fructification of the deeds done in the appropriate time only, He is responsible. He divides Himself and takes many forms.

Vijijnasyamana = being discussed. Yathopajasham = according to the results of *karma*.

Rtagunan = heat and cold.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

For the accuracy of the rites observed in Vasantha and other seasons. The learned means those who know the past, present and future.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

God divides Himself into twelve forms (for months) and six forms (for seasons, *ṛtus*) and brings about the sanctity of deeds performed in the particular period.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Sa eva = the famous kalarupa \[form of time\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The worship of God through Sūrya takes place because both difference and non-difference occur between the part and the whole. Thus, it is said that Nārāyaṇa Himself manages everything for the sanctity of the particular rites done in the appropriate time.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Even this is a pastime of God to manage the affairs of the world. He takes many forms and rules over the seasons Vasantha and others. He is Kala \[time\] and is propounded by the *Vedas*.

### Text 4

*तमेतमिह पुरुषास्त्रय्या विद्यया वर्णाश्रमाचारानुपथा उच्चावचैः कर्मभिराम्नातै*  
*र्योगवितानैश्च श्रद्धया यजन्तोऽञ्जसा श्रेयः समधिगच्छन्ति ॥४॥*

*tam etam iha puruṣās trayyā vidyayā varṇāśramācārānupathā uccāvacaiḥ karmabhir āmnātair yoga-vitānaiś ca śraddhayā yajanto 'ñjasā śreyaḥ samadhigacchanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam—Him (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); etam—this; iha—in this world of mortality; puruṣāḥ—all people; trayyā—having three divisions; vidyayā—by the Vedic knowledge; varṇa-āśrama-ācāra—the practices of the varṇāśrama system; anupathāḥ—following; ucca-avacaiḥ—higher or lower according to the different positions in the varṇāśrama-dharma (brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra); karmabhiḥ—by their respective activities; āmnātaiḥ—handed down; yoga-vitānaiḥ—by meditation and other yogic processes; ca—and; śraddhayā—with great faith; yajantaḥ—worshiping; añjasā—without difficulty; śreyaḥ—the ultimate benefit of life; samadhigacchanti—they attain.

**Перевод:**

**According to the system of four varṇas and four āśramas, people generally worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa, who is situated as the sun-god. With great faith they worship the Supreme Personality as the Supersoul according to ritualistic ceremonies handed down in the three Vedas, such as agnihotra and similar higher and lower fruitive acts, and according to the process of mystic yoga. In this way they very easily attain the ultimate goal of life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

People endowed with *varṇas* and *āśramas* worship Him by sacrifices in the form of Indra. They worship Him by meditation and so on in his *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\] form.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Lord Nārāyaṇa Himself controls everything—Sūrya happens to be His body. Nārāyaṇa functions as the soul of that body dividing the year into twelve months, the seasons into six, day and night and so on. It is Nārāyaṇa who gives heat, rain or cold at appropriate times. He is extolled in the *Vedas* as residing in Sūrya and having a golden hue.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

He takes twelve forms—the reason: for those who follow the code and conduct of *varṇas* and *āśramas*. *Yoga-vitana* means by the method of offering everything to God.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They worship the *antaryāmī* of Indra and others by following the method of *aṣṭāṅga-yoga*

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Those who have *varṇas* and *āśramas*, worship the sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The living entities (*jīvas*) worship God by so many good deeds and attain heaven. Gradually they perform worship and by the strength of knowledge and devotion they get liberation.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

People who have *varṇas* and *āśrama* offer their worship to Nārāyaṇa through sandhyavandana, agnihotra and other rituals and thus attain fulfillment of all their desires. It is said in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*: “Demons (rakshasas) named Mandehas attack Sūrya both in the mornings and the evenings and a battle ensues. The water offered by sages and other people in the form of arghya acts as a weapon and kills the Rākṣasas, however, they are born again and torment Sūrya. Therefore the water is to be offered along with Vedic hymns every morning and evening.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

It is God only in the form of Sūrya. He divides time into various divisions of months, seasons and so on. He is worshipped by people with castes and *āśramas* in the appropriate time. He controls the months and seasons so that they exhibit their natural phenomena during that time. He is mainly known through the *Vedas*. Those who worship attain fulfillment of their desires and ultimately even liberation.

### Text 5

*अथ स एष आत्मा लोकानां द्यावापृथिव्योरन्तरेण नभोवलयस्य काल*  
*चक्रगतो द्वादश मासान् भुङ्क्ते राशिसंज्ञान् संवत्सरावयवान्मासः पक्षद्वयं दिवा*  
*नक्तं चेति सपादर्क्षद्वयमुपदिशन्ति यावता षष्ठमंशं भुञ्जीत स वै*  
*ऋतुरित्युपदिश्यते संवत्सरावयवः ॥५॥*

*atha sa eṣa ātmā lokānāṁ dyāv-āpṛthivyor antareṇa nabho-valayasya kālacakra-gato dvādaśa māsān bhuṅkte rāśi-saṁjñān saṁvatsarāvayavān māsaḥ pakṣa-dvayaṁ divā naktaṁ ceti sapādarkṣa-dvayam upadiśanti yāvatā ṣaṣṭham aṁśaṁ bhuñjīta sa vai ṛtur ity upadiśyate saṁvatsarāvayavaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—therefore; saḥ—He; eṣaḥ—this; ātmā—the living force; lokānām—of all the three worlds; dyāv-ā-pṛthivyoḥ antareṇa—between the upper and lower portions of the universe; nabhaḥ-valayasya—of outer space; kāla-cakra-gataḥ—positioned in the wheel of time; dvādaśa māsān—twelve months; bhuṅkte—passes; rāśi-saṁjñān—named after the zodiac signs; saṁvatsara-avayavān—the parts of the whole year; māsaḥ—one month; pakṣa-dvayam—two fortnights; divā—a day; naktam ca—and a night; iti—thus; sapāda-ṛkṣa-dvayam—by stellar calculations, two and a quarter constellations; upadiśanti—they instruct; yāvatā—by as much time; ṣaṣṭham aṁśam—one sixth of his orbit; bhuñjīta—pass; saḥ—that portion; vai—indeed; ṛtuḥ—a season; iti—thus; upadiśyate—is instructed; saṁvatsara-avayavaḥ—a part of a year.

**Перевод:**

**The sun-god, who is Nārāyaṇa, or Viṣṇu, the soul of all the worlds, is situated in outer space between the upper and lower portions of the universe. Passing through twelve months on the wheel of time, the sun comes in touch with twelve different signs of the zodiac and assumes twelve different names according to those signs. The aggregate of those twelve months is called a saṁvatsara, or an entire year. According to lunar calculations, two fortnights—one of the waxing moon and the other of the waning—form one month. That same period is one day and night for the planet Pitṛloka. According to stellar calculations, a month equals two and one quarter constellations. When the sun travels for two months, a season passes, and therefore the seasonal changes are considered parts of the body of the year.**

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Sūrya is in the *kāla-cakra* situated between earth and heaven in the sky. He is responsible for months, the division of the year. Chaitra and so on are lunar months.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Sūrya is the soul of the world. He is stationed in the *kāla-cakra* which is in the sky between the heaven and earth. He moves and covers the *rāśis*, mesha and others. The solar month is counted from one sankramana to another. Sankramana means transition from one *rāśi* to another. Thus, from the day the sun enters the Mesha constellation until the day he enters the Vrishabha constellation, it is the Mesha month in the solar calendar. From that day until he enters the Mithuna constellation, it is the Vrshabha month. Caitra and so on, are lunar months. They are counted from the first day of the bright half to the immediate new moon day. The first day of the bright half will be the day next to the full moon. The months are named so because of their association with the particular star on the day of the full moon. Thus the month in which the moon will be in conjunction with the star Chitra on the day of the full moon is called Chaitra. The month he will be in conjunction with Vishaka on the day of the full moon is called Vaishakha and so on. The time taken by the sun to cover a sixth part of his track is called a *ṛtu* and the time taken to cover half the track is called an ayana. Rtu is a two month period and ayana a six month one.

### Text 6

*अथ च यावतार्धेन नभोवीथ्यां प्रचरति तं कालमयनमाचक्षते ॥६॥*

*atha ca yāvatārdhena nabho-vīthyāṁ pracarati taṁ kālam ayanam ācakṣate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—now; ca—also; yāvatā—by as long as; ardhena—half; nabhaḥ-vīthyām—in outer space; pracarati—the sun moves; tam—that; kālam—time; ayanam—ayana; ācakṣate—is said.

**Перевод:**

**Thus the time the sun takes to rotate through half of outer space is called an ayana, or its period of movement \[in the north or in the south\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is stated here that by His motion, He is responsible for the usages of various months. He is the soul of all people and enters into the *kāla-cakra* situated in the middle of the sky. The names of the constellations are Mesha and so on. The names Chaitra and so on are by lunar reckoning. With respect to the movement of the moon, the two halves (bright and dark) constitute a month. With respect to the sun, the time taken by him to move through 2 ¼ stars is a month. For pitrs, a day and a night constitute a month. A six part means two constellations.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\] Nārāyaṇa of Sūrya is to be understood by the pronoun *sa* (He). He covers the twelve months Mesha, Vrshabha and others bearing the same name of the constellations, in the correct order. The duration of a month is indicated by the word Pakha-dvaya (two halves). 2¼ stars is the duration of a month with respect to the constellations. Both of them hold good as they are different ways of stating the same thing. A sixth part of the track he covers in two months is a Rtu \[season\]. Half the track he covers in six months is an ayana. The slow, fast and normal motions in Uttarāyaṇa, Dakṣiṇāyana and Vaishuvata should also be borne in mind here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The division of months and so on is based on Solar motion only is what is stated here. The Nabho-maṇḍala is between the earth’s and heaven's maṇḍalas. Fixed to the *kāla-cakra* means fixed to the *Jyotis-cakra* which is related to the *kāla-cakra*. The month is defined in different ways i.e., with respect to the motion of the sun, with respect to Gods and Pitrs and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Atha” is used as an embellishment of the sentence. Ardhena= in six months.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The sun himself is responsible for the division of the year into months by his movement occupying different *rāśis*. Chaitra and so on, are the lunar months. There are other methods also of reckoning the month with respect to demigods, Pitrs \[ancestors\] and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The month is reckoned with respect to the sun and with respect to the moon. A bright half and a dark half (15 days) make a lunar month. The time taken by the sun to cover 2¼ stars is a solar month. Mesha, Vrshaba etc., are solar months.

### Text 7

*अथ च यावन्नभोमण्डलं सह द्यावापृथिव्योर्मण्डलाभ्यां कार्त्स्न्येन*  
*स ह भुञ्जीत तं कालं संवत्सरं परिवत्सरमिडावत्सरमनुवत्सरं*  
*वत्सरमिति भानोर्मान्द्यशैघ्र्यसमगतिभिः समामनन्ति ॥७॥*

*atha ca yāvan nabho-maṇḍalaṁ saha dyāv-āpṛthivyor maṇḍalābhyāṁ kārtsnyena sa ha bhuñjīta taṁ kālaṁ saṁvatsaraṁ parivatsaram iḍāvatsaram anuvatsaraṁ vatsaram iti bhānor māndya-śaighrya-sama-gatibhiḥ samāmananti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—now; ca—also; yāvat—as long as; nabhaḥ-maṇḍalam—outer space, between the upper and lower world; saha—along with; dyau—of the upper world; āpṛthivyoḥ—of the lower world; maṇḍalābhyām—the spheres; kārtsnyena—entirely; saḥ—he; ha—indeed; bhuñjīta—may pass through; tam—that; kālam—time; saṁvatsaram—Saṁvatsara; parivatsaram—Parivatsara; iḍāvatsaram—Iḍāvatsara; anuvatsaram—Anuvatsara; vatsaram—Vatsara; iti—thus; bhānoḥ—of the sun; māndya—slow; śaighrya—speedy; sama—and equal; gatibhiḥ—by the speeds; samāmananti—the experienced scholars describe.

**Перевод:**

**The sun-god has three speeds—slow, fast and moderate. The time he takes to travel entirely around the spheres of heaven, earth and space at these three speeds is referred to, by learned scholars, by the five names Saṁvatsara, Parivatsara, Iḍāvatsara, Anuvatsara and Vatsara.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

When there is a transition (samkranti) on the first day of the bright half, both solar and lunar months start simultaneously. “Sah” means a year. According to the solar months, the days in a year increase by six. According to lunar months, they decrease by six. Thus, there is a difference of twelve days in a year in that the lunar year is completed first and then the solar year. At the end of five years, the difference will be 60 days causing two extra months (malamasa) according to the lunar calendar. Then the sixth year starts. The five years should be understood with this perspective. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Sūrya moves in the anticlockwise direction, as stated above in Mesha and other constellations which are supported by *kāla-cakra*. A twelfth part of the *kāla-cakra* is called a *rāśi* (constellation). The sun takes a month to cover a constellation. Twelve months make a year. According to lunar reckoning the two halves, bright and dark, together make a month. With respect to the sun, the time taken to cover 2 ¼ stars in the *kāla-cakra*, is a month. From the point of view of pitrs \[ancestors\], their day and night is a month for us. The time taken by the sun to cover a sixth part of the *kāla-cakra* is called a *ṛtu* \[season\]. Half of the *kāla-cakra* is called an ayana.

When lunar and solar months start together on the first day of the bright half, then at the end of the year, the solar calculation for the year will be six days more and the lunar year will be six days less—the total difference being twelve days. At the end of five years, the total difference will be 60 days and for that reason there will be two Mala masas (excess months) in the lunar calendar. From the sixth year onwards, it will be as it was at the beginning of the sixth previous year. Because of the difference in days between these two reckonings the year is classified as Idavatsara, Parivatsara and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

He covers the orbit in the sky along with the orbits of earth and heaven in his different motions (gaits). That is why the year is named and reckoned in five different ways.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

With respect to the moon, two halves make a month. With respect to Pitrs \[ancestors\], their day and night is a month here. With respect to the sun, the time taken by him to cover 2 ¼ stars is a month.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nabho-maṇḍala \[the orbit of the sky\] is of the same magnitude as the other two maṇḍalas mentioned above—it is not more than that. The nomenclature of Saṁvatsara, Vatsara and so on, have been narrated in the third Canto of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The time taken by Sūrya to complete a full revolution of Nabho-maṇḍala is called saṁvatsara, vatsara and so on, because of the variation in the speed of the sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

A sixth part of the saṁvatsara is two *rāśis*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

When the sun covers the entire track, it is a year. The year is named in five different ways as Vatsara, Saṁvatsara and so on because of the slow, fast and normal gaits of the sun.

### Text 8

*एवं चन्द्रमा अर्कगभस्तिभ्य उपरिष्टाल्लक्षयोजनत उपलभ्यमानोऽर्कस्य*  
*संवत्सरभुक्तिं पक्षाभ्यां मासभुक्तिं सपादर्क्षाभ्यां दिनेनैव पक्षभुक्तिमग्रचारी*  
*द्रुततरगमनो भुङ्क्ते ॥८॥*

*evaṁ candramā arka-gabhastibhya upariṣṭāl lakṣa-yojanata upalabhyamāno 'rkasya saṁvatsara-bhuktiṁ pakṣābhyāṁ māsa-bhuktiṁ sapādarkṣābhyāṁ dinenaiva pakṣa-bhuktim agracārī drutatara-gamano bhuṅkte.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—thus; candramā—the moon; arka-gabhastibhyaḥ—from the rays of the sunshine; upariṣṭāt—above; lakṣa-yojanataḥ—by a measurement of 100,000 yojanas; upalabhyamānaḥ—being situated; arkasya—of the sun globe; saṁvatsara-bhuktim—the passage of one year of enjoyment; pakṣābhyām—by two fortnights; māsa-bhuktim—the passage of one month; sapāda-ṛkṣābhyām—by two and a quarter days; dinena—by a day; eva—only; pakṣa-bhuktim—the passage of a fortnight; agracārī—moving impetuously; druta-tara-gamanaḥ—passing more speedily; bhuṅkte—passes through.

**Перевод:**

**Above the rays of the sunshine by a distance of 100,000 yojanas \[800,000 miles\] is the moon, which travels at a speed faster than that of the sun. In two lunar fortnights the moon travels through the equivalent of a saṁvatsara of the sun, in two and a quarter days it passes through a month of the sun, and in one day it passes through a fortnight of the sun.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the status of the sun, now in this chapter, the position, movement, functions, etc. of the other planets is described.

The moon is 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] above the sun’s disc. He is faster than the sun. The distance of *kāla-cakra* the sun covers in a year, the moon covers in a month. What the sun covers in a fortnight, the moon covers in a day, and so on. What the sun covers in a month, the moon covers within 2¼ stars \[constellations\], i.e within 67 ½ *muhūrtas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The moon covers in a month the distance covered by the sun in a year. “The sun’s monthly movement in a single day,” i.e. because he is faster than the sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The position and function of the moon and other planets are also stated hereafter. The moon is situated 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] above the sun and 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] above the earth. By 2 ¼ stars means in 2 ¼ days. He is faster than the sun and covers the distance covered by the sun in a short time.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Arkagabhasti means the sun’s disc. 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] above means 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] above the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“From the rays of the sun” means the sun’s disc. 2¼ stars means 2¼ days.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He covers half of it in six months.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The moon is situated 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] above the sun. He is faster than the sun. The distance the sun covers in a year, the moon covers in a month. The distance the sun covers in a month, the moon covers in 2 ¼ days or 135 ghatikas (which means 60 hours).

### Text 9

*अथ चापूर्यमाणाभिश्च कलाभिरमराणां क्षीयमाणाभिश्च कलाभिः*  
*पित्णामहोरात्राणि पूर्वपक्षापरपक्षाभ्यां वितन्वानः सर्वजीवनिवहप्राणो*  
*जीवश्चैकमेकं नक्षत्रं त्रिंशता मुहूर्तैर्भुङ्क्ते ॥९॥*

*atha cāpūryamāṇābhiś ca kalābhir amarāṇāṁ kṣīyamāṇābhiś ca kalābhiḥ pitṝṇām aho-rātrāṇi pūrva-pakṣāpara-pakṣābhyāṁ vitanvānaḥ sarva-jīva-nivaha-prāṇo jīvaś caikam ekaṁ nakṣatraṁ triṁśatā muhūrtair bhuṅkte.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—thus; ca—also; āpūryamāṇābhiḥ—gradually increasing; ca—and; kalābhiḥ—by the parts of the moon; amarāṇām—of the demigods; kṣīyamāṇābhiḥ—by gradually decreasing; ca—and; kalābhiḥ—by parts of the moon; pitṝṇām—of those on the planet known as Pitṛloka; ahaḥ-rātrāṇi—the days and nights; pūrva-pakṣa-apara-pakṣābhyām—by the period of waxing and waning; vitanvānaḥ—distributing; sarva-jīva-nivaha—of the total living entities; prāṇaḥ—the life; jīvaḥ—the chief living being; ca—also; ekam ekam—one after another; nakṣatram—a constellation of stars; triṁśatā—by thirty; muhūrtaiḥ—muhūrtas; bhuṅkte—passes through.

**Перевод:**

**When the moon is waxing, the illuminating portions of it increase daily, thus creating day for the demigods and night for the pitās. When the moon is waning, however, it causes night for the demigods and day for the pitās. In this way the moon passes through each constellation of stars in thirty muhūrtas \[an entire day\]. The moon is the source of nectarean coolness that influences the growth of food grains, and therefore the moon-god is considered the life of all living entities. He is consequently called Jīva, the chief living being within the universe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The position and function of the moon and other planets are stated. Arkagabhastibhyah = above the sun’s disc. Sapadarkshabhyam = by 2¼ days. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

He is responsible for all actions of creations as well as for their life breath. A day means 30 *muhūrtas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The two halves designed for the worship of Pitrs. He is Prana because he is the lord of herbs.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Bright half and dark half” (of a month) are day and night to the demigods and for the pitrs \[ancestors\]. This information is for their worship at the proper time, but actually the Uttarāyaṇa and the Dakṣiṇāyana are day and night to the demigods, as is enjoined in various smritis \[corollary Vedic scriptures\].

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

When he covers the entire Nabho-maṇḍala (track) with his three types of motions, it is a year and is called saṁvatsara, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The moon has sixteen faculties. He is the god of the mind. He is the ruler of all plants and thus is called annamaya. He is responsible for sustaining the lives of all creations and thus he is called amrtamaya. In short, he is the lord of everything.

### Text 10

*य एष षोडशकलः पुरुषो भगवान्मनोमयोऽन्नमयोऽमृतमयो देवपितृ*  
*मनुष्यभूतपशुपक्षिसरीसृपवीरुधां प्राणाप्यायनशीलत्वात्सर्वमय इति*  
*वर्णयन्ति ॥१०॥*

*ya eṣa ṣoḍaśa-kalaḥ puruṣo bhagavān manomayo 'nnamayo 'mṛtamayo deva-pitṛ-manuṣya-bhūta-paśu-pakṣi-sarīsṛpa-vīrudhāṁ prāṇāpy āyana-śīlatvāt sarvamaya iti varṇayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yaḥ—that; eṣaḥ—this; ṣoḍaśa-kalaḥ—having all sixteen parts (the full moon); puruṣaḥ—the person; bhagavān—having great power received from the Supreme Personality of Godhead; manaḥ-mayaḥ—the predominating deity of the mind; anna-mayaḥ—the source of potency for food grains; amṛta-mayaḥ—the source of the substance of life; deva—of all the demigods; pitṛ—of all the inhabitants of Pitṛloka; manuṣya—all human beings; bhūta—all living entities; paśu—of the animals; pakṣi—of the birds; sarīsṛpa—of the reptiles; vīrudhām—of all kinds of herbs and plants; prāṇa—life air; api—certainly; āyana-śīlatvāt—due to refreshing; sarva-mayaḥ—all-pervading; iti—thus; varṇayanti—the learned scholars describe.

**Перевод:**

**Because the moon is full of all potentialities, it represents the influence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The moon is the predominating deity of everyone's mind, and therefore the moon-god is called Manomaya. He is also called Annamaya because he gives potency to all herbs and plants, and he is called Amṛtamaya because he is the source of life for all living entities. The moon pleases the demigods, pitās, human beings, animals, birds, reptiles, trees, plants and all other living entities. Everyone is satisfied by the presence of the moon. Therefore the moon is also called Sarvamaya \[all-pervading\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The same is said vividly in this prose.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Causing day and night for the pitrs with the bright half and dark half of the month, he covers a single star in 30 *muhūrtas*. He is the one who sustains and nourishes the life breath of all creatures and hence is called Jīva himself. Chandra is Lord Viṣṇu’s body and called Manomāyā because he is the lord of the mind for all creatures. He is called Annamaya because he is the lord of herbs; sarvamaya because he is the lord of everything. This is what those who know him say.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is said in the previous prose is supported here. Because everything depends upon him, he is called Sarvamaya.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because he is responsible for life, he is called Jīva. He is also called Amrtamaya as he is full of nectar.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Puruṣa means the front runner of everything. The root *pura* means running in the front. God has a handsome form. He is “manomaya” as he is stationed in the mind. He nourishes the creatures by his rays. He is the lord of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He causes day and night for the demigods and Pitrs by the bright half and dark half of the month. He is the soul of all lives, so he is called Jīva and Prana. He is the deity of foods and nectar.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Now the position of the moon and other planets and their functions are described. Above the sun’s rays means the sun’s disc. He is faster than the sun. He covers in a month what the sun covers in a year. What distance the sun covers in a month, the moon covers in 2¼ days.

The elders say that the moon is endowed with 16 faculties—the five sensory organs, five motor organs, five great elements and mind. He is the mind of Lord Nārāyaṇa, and is hence endowed with such extraordinary powers.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He causes day for the demigods by his bright half when the demigods are worshipped. He causes the dark half for the pitrs which is the proper time for their worship.

### Text 11

*तत उपरिष्टाद्द्विलक्षयोजनतो नक्षत्राणि मेरुं दक्षिणेनैव*  
*कालायन ईश्वरयोजितानि सहाभिजिताष्टाविंशतिः ॥११॥*

*tata upariṣṭād dvi-lakṣa-yojanato nakṣatrāṇi meruṁ dakṣiṇenaiva kālāyana īśvara-yojitāni sahābhijitāṣṭā-viṁśatiḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—from that region of the moon; upariṣṭāt—above; dvi-lakṣa-yojanataḥ—200,000 yojanas; nakṣatrāṇi—many stars; merum—Sumeru Mountain; dakṣiṇena eva—to the right side; kāla-ayane—in the wheel of time; īśvara-yojitāni—attached by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; saha—with; abhijitā—the star known as Abhijit; aṣṭā-viṁśatiḥ—twenty-eight.

**Перевод:**

**There are many stars located 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above the moon. By the supreme will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, they are fixed to the wheel of time, and thus they rotate with Mount Sumeru on their right, their motion being different from that of the sun. There are twenty-eight important stars, headed by Abhijit.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

So that Meru is to the right—they do not have a movement of their own. In the *kāla-cakra*, the star Abhijit is situated at the junction of Śravaṇa and Uttarashada.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

300,000 *yojanas* \[2,400,000 miles\] above the moon, the stars are situated and they also move around Meru. The stars are fixed to *kāla-cakra*, i.e they have only one type of motion and no anticlockwise motion like the sun. Abhijit is a star between Uttarashada and Śravaṇa. The star belt consists of 28 stars including Abhijit.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Kalanayane” means to apprise the correct time or it may be taken to mean *kāla-cakra*. Abhijit is between Uttarashada and Śravaṇa. Some say it is between Revathi and Ashwini.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

300,000 *yojanas* \[2,400,000 miles\] means it is 500,000 *yojanas* \[4,000,000 miles\] from the earth. They do not have a separate motion of their own. *Kalayana* means *kāla-cakra*. They are 28 including Abhijit.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“From the moon it is 300,000 *yojanas* \[2,400,000 miles\]” means it is 500,000 *yojanas* \[4,000,000 miles\] from the earth. \[Note: according to the commentaries, the distance of 300,000 *yojanas* above the moon is correct rather than 200,000 as given in the verse quoted above.\] Even the stars are studded in the *kāla-cakra*. As the *kāla-cakra* goes around Meru, the stars also do likewise. The fourth quarter of Uttarashada and the first four ghatikas of Śravaṇa are said to constitute the Abhijit star, according to astronomers.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Kalayana means the *kāla-cakra*. The stars are 28 in number including Abhijit which, as per the Vedic passages, is a very auspicious star situated between Uttaraashada and Śravaṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He causes the bright half and the dark half of the month. The bright half is the time for the worship of the Pitrs (manes, ancestors). He is the controller of food, life and nectar, thus he is called Annamaya, Jīva and Amrtamaya.

The stars move in the clockwise direction only, unlike the sun and other planets, they do not have the anticlockwise motion. They are situated within the *kāla-cakra*. They are 28 in number including Abhijit which is situated between Uttarashada and Śravaṇa.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

300,000 *yojanas* \[2,400,000 miles\] above the moon the stars are placed by God in the *kāla-cakra*. They move in the clockwise direction only, not having two kinds of motion like the planets. The stars are 28 in number including Abhijit.

### Text 12

*तत उपरिष्टादुशना द्विलक्षयोजनत उपलभ्यते पुरतः पश्चात्सहैव वार्कस्य*  
*शैघ्र्यमान्द्यसाम्याभिर्गतिभिरर्कवच्चरति लोकानां नित्यदानुकूल एव*  
*प्रायेण वर्षयंश्चारेणानुमीयते स वृष्टिविष्टम्भग्रहोपशमनः ॥१२॥*

*tata upariṣṭād uśanā dvi-lakṣa-yojanata upalabhyate purataḥ paścāt sahaiva vārkasya śaighrya-māndya-sāmyābhir gatibhir arkavac carati lokānāṁ nityadānukūla eva prāyeṇa varṣayaṁś cāreṇānumīyate sa vṛṣṭi-viṣṭambha-grahopaśamanaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—from that bunch of stars; upariṣṭāt—above; uśanā—Venus; dvi-lakṣa-yojanataḥ—200,000 yojanas (1,600,000 miles); upalabhyate—is experienced; purataḥ—in front; paścāt—behind; saha—along with; eva—indeed; vā—and; arkasya—of the sun; śaighrya—speedy; māndya—slow; sāmyābhiḥ—equal; gatibhiḥ—the movements; arkavat—exactly like the sun; carati—rotates; lokānām—of all the planets within the universe; nityadā—constantly; anukūlaḥ—offering favorable conditions; eva—indeed; prāyeṇa—almost always; varṣayan—causing rainfall; cāreṇa—by infusing the clouds; anumīyate—is perceived; saḥ—he (Venus); vṛṣṭi-viṣṭambha—obstacles to rainfall; graha-upaśamanaḥ—nullifying planets.

**Перевод:**

**Some 1,600,000 miles above this group of stars is the planet Venus, which moves at almost exactly the same pace as the sun according to swift, slow and moderate movements. Sometimes Venus moves behind the sun, sometimes in front of the sun and sometimes along with it. Venus nullifies the influence of planets that are obstacles to rainfall. Consequently its presence causes rainfall, and it is therefore considered very favorable for all living beings within this universe. This has been accepted by learned scholars.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

When the sun enters a constellation first, Venus follows him \[the sun\]. When they enter a constellation simultaneously, then Venus goes into retrograde motion. The impediment to rain is removed by this planet.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The function of Mars is influenced by the position of Venus.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

700,000 *yojanas* \[5,600,000 miles\] from earth. Removes the impediments to rain.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“By his movement” means when he skips over the normal stars. Mostly he gives rain and nullifies the effect of Mars who obstructs rain.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Venus is situated 200,000 yojanas (1,600,000 miles) above the stars. He has three types of motion—in his normal motion, he moves along with the sun at the same speed, whereas sometimes he overtakes the sun and sometimes he lags behind the sun. He is normally a benefic planet and causes rains. Mercury is similar to Venus.

### Text 13

*उशनसा बुधो व्याख्यातस्तत उपरिष्टाद् द्विलक्षयोजनतो बुधः ।*  
*सोमसुत उपलभ्यमानः प्रायेण शुभकृद्यदार्काद् व्यतिरिच्येत तदातिवाता*  
*भ्रप्रायानावृष्ट्यादिभयमाशंसते ॥१३॥*

*uśanasā budho vyākhyātas tata upariṣṭād dvi-lakṣa-yojanato budhaḥ soma-suta upalabhyamānaḥ prāyeṇa śubha-kṛd yadārkād vyatiricyeta tadātivātābhra-prāyānāvṛṣṭy-ādi-bhayam āśaṁsate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

uśanasā—with Venus; budhaḥ—Mercury; vyākhyātaḥ—explained; tataḥ—from that (Venus); upariṣṭāt—above; dvi-lakṣa-yojanataḥ—1,600,000 miles; budhaḥ—Mercury; soma-sutaḥ—the son of the moon; upalabhyamānaḥ—is situated; prāyeṇa—almost always; śubha-kṛt—very auspicious to the inhabitants of the universe; yadā—when; arkāt—from the sun; vyatiricyeta—is separated; tadā—at that time; ativāta—of cyclones and other bad effects; abhra—clouds; prāya—almost always; anāvṛṣṭi-ādi—such as scarcity of rain; bhayam—fearful conditions; āśaṁsate—expands.

**Перевод:**

**Mercury is described to be similar to Venus, in that it moves sometimes behind the sun, sometimes in front of the sun and sometimes along with it. It is 1,600,000 miles above Venus, or 7,200,000 miles above earth. Mercury, which is the son of the moon, is almost always very auspicious for the inhabitants of the universe, but when it does not move along with the sun, it forbodes cyclones, dust, irregular rainfall, and waterless clouds. In this way it creates fearful conditions due to inadequate or excessive rainfall.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By explaining the movement of Venus, Budha is also explained in that he moves just behind or in front of the sun. Aashamsate = indicates.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Venus is situated 200,000 yojanas (1,600,000 miles) above the star belt. Sometimes he \[Venus\] follows the sun and covers the same star after the sun has covered it by his movement. Sometimes he goes along with the sun and both of them will be in the same star \[constellation\]. He is always beneficial to the world. When he transgresses the order of the stars in his movement, he indicates rain. By stating the position of Venus, Mercury (budha)’s movement is also described since he also moves either in front of the sun, just behind the sun, or along with the sun, like Venus.Mercury is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Venus. When he does not move with the sun, he causes hurricane and drought.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Like Venus, Mercury also moves in front of or just behind or along with the sun. He is 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\] above the earth and 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Venus.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Venus is situated 700,000 *yojanas* \[5,600,000 miles\] above the earth. Tatah means from the stars. Transgression means skipping a star in the middle. It is like going from Ashwini to Krittika directly without touching Bharani in between. He causes rain.

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] from Venus means 900,000 *yojanas* \[7,200,000 miles\] above the earth. “Normally a benefic” means sometimes he is a malefic also. That is when he gets separated from the sun. Fear of hurricanes, overcast sky and absence of rain.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

By stating the movement of Venus, Mercury’s movement is also stated because he is similar to Venus in his movement going in front of, along with or behind the sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Budha resembles Venus in his motions. His chariot is described like this, “The chariot is made of materials of wind and fire. It has eight saffron colored horses which have the speed of the wind.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Mercury is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Venus. He is generally beneficial to the world. When he does not move with the sun, he causes hurricanes and droughts.

### Text 14

*अत ऊर्ध्वमङ्गारकोऽपि योजनलक्षद्वितय उपलभ्यमानस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः*  
*पक्षैरेकैकशो राशीन्द्वादशानुभुङ्क्ते यदि न वक्रेणाभिवर्तते प्रायेणाशुभग्रहो*  
*ऽघशंसः ॥१४॥*

*ata ūrdhvam aṅgārako 'pi yojana-lakṣa-dvitaya upalabhyamānas tribhis tribhiḥ pakṣair ekaikaśo rāśīn dvādaśānubhuṅkte yadi na vakreṇābhivartate prāyeṇāśubha-graho 'gha-śaṁsaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ataḥ—from this; ūrdhvam—above; aṅgārakaḥ—Mars; api—also; yojana-lakṣa-dvitaye—at a distance of 1,600,000 miles; upalabhyamānaḥ—is situated; tribhiḥ tribhiḥ—with each three and three; pakṣaiḥ—fortnights; eka-ekaśaḥ—one after another; rāśīn—the signs; dvādaśa—twelve; anubhuṅkte—passes through; yadi—if; na—not; vakreṇa—with a curve; abhivartate—approaches; prāyeṇa—almost always; aśubha-grahaḥ—an unfavorable, inauspicious planet; agha-śaṁsaḥ—creating trouble.

**Перевод:**

**Situated 1,600,000 miles above Mercury, or 8,800,000 miles above earth, is the planet Mars. If this planet does not travel in a crooked way, it crosses through each sign of the zodiac in three fortnights and in this way travels through all twelve, one after another. It almost always creates unfavorable conditions in respect to rainfall and other influences.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Aghashamsa = forebodes distress. By three halves if he is not retrograde.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Mars is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Mercury. In his normal gait, he takes 1½ month to cover a *rāśi*. He is normally a malefic, or when he is in the direct motion he is beneficial. In his retrograde motion, he becomes inimical.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

In conjunction with good planets, he gives good things and in conjunction with bad planets, he gives bad things. That is why the word “mostly” is used.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

1,100,000 *yojanas* \[8,800,000 miles\] above the earth. “If he is not retrograde” is construed with the previous words. He indicates bad things.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above mercury means 1,100,000 *yojanas* \[8,800,000 miles\] above the earth. Aghashamsa means forebodes distress. If he is in the 10th house, he is very beneficial. That is why the word “mostly” is used. If he is in retrogression, he stays in a constellation for many months.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He indicates misery. If he is not retrograde he takes 1 ½ months to cover a *rāśi*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He moves like the sun—either in front of him, along with him or just behind him. His normal motion is equal to that of the sun—only in his abnormal motion is he either in front of or behind the sun. He removes the impediments to rain. Sukra’s chariot is described in the *Purāṇas*: “Sukra’s chariot is equipped with all weapons; it has a retinue which follows him, and the horses of the chariot are born on earth.”

If he \[Mars\] is retrograde, then he takes one and a half months to cover a *rāśi*. Generally he indicates misery. “The chariot of Mars is eight cornered and made of gold. The hue of the horses is like that of *padmaraga* (crimson).”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Mars is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Mercury. Normally he is a malefic. He takes 1½ months to cover a *rāśi* in his normal motion. While in retrogression, he takes more than that. Some opine that Mars is benefic in retrogression and malefic in direct motion.

### Text 15

*तत उपरिष्टाद् द्विलक्षयोजनान्तरगता भगवान् बृहस्पतिरेकैकस्मिन्राशौ*  
*परिवत्सरं परिवत्सरं चरति यदि न वक्रः स्यात्प्रायेणानुकूलो ब्राह्मणकुलस्य*  
*॥१५॥*

*tata upariṣṭād dvi-lakṣa-yojanāntara-gatā bhagavān bṛhaspatir ekaikasmin rāśau parivatsaraṁ parivatsaraṁ carati yadi na vakraḥ syāt prāyeṇānukūlo brāhmaṇa-kulasya.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—that (Mars); upariṣṭāt—above; dvi-lakṣa-yojana-antara-gatāḥ—situated at a distance of 1,600,000 miles; bhagavān—the most powerful planet; bṛhaspatiḥ—Jupiter; eka-ekasmin—in one after another; rāśau—sign; parivatsaram parivatsaram—for the period of Parivatsara; carati—moves; yadi—if; na—not; vakraḥ—curved; syāt—becomes; prāyeṇa—almost always; anukūlaḥ—very favorable; brāhmaṇa-kulasya—to the brāhmaṇas of the universe.

**Перевод:**

**Situated 1,600,000 miles above Mars, or 10,400,000 miles above earth, is the planet Jupiter, which travels through one sign of the zodiac within the period of a Parivatsara. If its movement is not curved, the planet Jupiter is very favorable to the brāhmaṇas of the universe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

If he \[Jupiter\] is not curved, then it is parivatsaram.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Jupiter is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Mars. If he is not retrograde, he is beneficial to the *brāhmaṇa*. He covers each *rāśi* in a Parivatsara.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“By that much” means 30 anuvastsaras. He moves slowly in the constellations and covers the entire orbit in 30 *anuvatsaras*. That is why he is called “Shanischara” i.e. “one who moves slowly.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] from the earth. “If he is not retrograde” should be construed with the previous words.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Mars means 1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] above the earth. If he is retrograde he takes more than a *parivatsara* to go from one constellation to another. It is said “mostly” because when stationed in inimical places, he gives misery also.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

If he \[Jupiter\] does not travel in a curved way, then the time taken is a Parivatsara.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

If he \[Jupiter\] does not travel in a curved way, he takes a parivatsara to cover the entire track. His chariot is also described: “The golden chariot of Jupiter is drawn by eight horses whose color is snow white. He Stays in each *rāśi* \[sign of the zodiac\] for a year.”

Saturn’s chariot is also described, “Shani moves slowly in his chariot drawn by horses born from the akasha \[the sky\] of variegated color.”

*Paramam padam* means the abode of Dhruva.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above him is the celebrated Jupiter, beneficial to the world in general and *brāhmaṇas* in particular. If he is not retrograde, he takes one year to cover a *rāśi* by his movement.

### Text 16

*तत उपरिष्टाद्योजनलक्षद्वयात्प्रतीयमानः शनैश्चर एकैकस्मिन्*  
*राशौ त्रिंशन्मासान् विलम्बमानः सर्वानेवानुपर्येति तावद्भिरनुवत्सरैः प्रायेण*  
*हि सर्वेषामशान्तिकरः ॥१६॥*

*tata upariṣṭād yojana-lakṣa-dvayāt pratīyamānaḥ śanaiścara ekaikasmin rāśau triṁśan māsān vilambamānaḥ sarvān evānuparyeti tāvadbhir anuvatsaraiḥ prāyeṇa hi sarveṣām aśāntikaraḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—that (Jupiter); upariṣṭāt—above; yojana-lakṣa-dvayāt—by a distance of 1,600,000 miles; pratīyamānaḥ—is situated; śanaiścaraḥ—the planet Saturn; eka-ekasmin—in one after another; rāśau—zodiac signs; triṁśat māsān—for a period of thirty months in each; vilam-bamānaḥ—lingering; sarvān—all twelve signs of the zodiac; eva—certainly; anuparyeti—passes through; tāvadbhiḥ—by so many; anuvatsaraiḥ—Anuvatsaras; prāyeṇa—almost always; hi—indeed; sarveṣām—to all the inhabitants; aśāntikaraḥ—very troublesome.

**Перевод:**

**Situated 1,600,000 miles above Jupiter, or 12,000,000 miles above earth, is the planet Saturn, which passes through one sign of the zodiac in thirty months and covers the entire zodiac circle in thirty Anuvatsaras. This planet is always very inauspicious for the universal situation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Saturn is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Jupiter. He takes 2 ½ years to cover a *rāśi*—in the same way he covers all the *rāśis*. He is normally malefic.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] from there means 1,500,000 *yojanas* \[12,000,000 miles\] from the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Jupiter means 1,500,000 *yojanas* \[12,000,000 miles\] above the earth. *Tavadbhih* means by thirty. Mostly he is a malefic, however in the 3rd, 6thand 11thplaces he is a benefic.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Saturn is situated 200,000 yojanas \[1,600,000 miles\] above Jupiter. He stays in each *rāśi* for 30 months; thus, due to his slow movement, he is called “Shanischara.” Normally he is considered malefic.

### Text 17

*तत उत्तरस्मादृषय एकादशलक्षयोजनान्तर उपलभ्यन्ते य एव लोकानां*  
*शमनुभावयन्तो भगवतो विष्णोर्यत्परमं पदं प्रदक्षिणं प्रक्रमन्ति ॥१७॥*

*tata uttarasmād ṛṣaya ekādaśa-lakṣa-yojanāntara upalabhyante ya eva lokānāṁ śam anubhāvayanto bhagavato viṣṇor yat paramaṁ padaṁ pradakṣiṇaṁ prakramanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—the planet Saturn; uttarasmāt—above; ṛṣayaḥ—great saintly sages; ekādaśa-lakṣa-yojana-antare—at a distance of 1,100,000 yojanas; upalabhyante—are situated; ye—all of them; eva—indeed; lokānām—for all the inhabitants of the universe; śam—the good fortune; anubhāvayantaḥ—always thinking of; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; viṣṇoḥ—Lord Viṣṇu; yat—which; paramam padam—the supreme abode; pradakṣiṇam—placing on the right; prakramanti—circumambulate.

**Перевод:**

**Situated 8,800,000 miles above Saturn, or 20,800,000 miles above earth, are the seven saintly sages, who are always thinking of the well-being of the inhabitants of the universe. They circumambulate the supreme abode of Lord Viṣṇu, known as Dhruvaloka, the polestar.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

1,100,000 yojanas \[8,800,000 miles\] above Saturn, the seven sages \[Note by the translator: (the Great Bear)\] are situated. They are there for the welfare of the world and also move in a clockwise direction around Dhruva-maṇḍala, an abode of Viṣṇu.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

As he has the tendency to go in front of others, he has a very fast motion.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

1,100,000 yojanas \[8,800,000 miles\] means 2,600,000 *yojanas* \[20,800,000 miles\] from the earth. Param Padam means the world of Dhruva.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

1,100,000 yojanas \[8,800,000 miles\] above Saturn means 2,600,000 *yojanas* \[20,800,000 miles\] above earth. They are stationed in the north. *Paramam padam* means Dhruva loka.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The seven sages are situated 1,100,000 yojanas \[8,800,000 miles\] above Saturn. They are absorbed in penance for the welfare of the world. They go around Dhruvaloka, the abode of Viṣṇu, in the clockwise direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In the 8thtext, where the moon's motion is described, there is a word “agrachari” which means running in the front. This is the correct reading—rather than “ugrachari”or fierce motion.

For Mars and Saturn it is said in the text that they are mostly malefic in nature. Although they are malefic they give good things if they are stationed in a good house like the eleventh. So it is not that they are always malefic.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twenty-second Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The Orbits of the Planets.”

## Chapter 23 - The Śiśumāra Planetary Systems

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*अथ तस्मात्परतस्त्रयोदशलक्षयोजनान्तरतो यत्तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम*  
*भिवदन्ति यत्र ह महाभागवतो ध्रुव औत्तानपादिरग्निनेन्द्रेण प्रजापतिना*  
*कश्यपेन धर्मेण च समकालयुग्भिः सबहुमानं दक्षिणतः क्रियमाण*  
*इदानीमपि कल्पजीविनामाजीव्य उपास्ते तस्येहानुभाव उपवर्णितः ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*atha tasmāt paratas trayodaśa-lakṣa-yojanāntarato yat tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padam abhivadanti yatra ha mahā-bhāgavato dhruva auttānapādir agninendreṇa prajāpatinā kaśyapena dharmeṇa ca samakāla-yugbhiḥ sabahu-mānaṁ dakṣiṇataḥ kriyamāṇa idānīm api kalpa-jīvinām ājīvya upāste tasyehānubhāva upavarṇitaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; atha—thereupon; tasmāt—the sphere of the seven stars; parataḥ—beyond that; trayodaśa-lakṣa-yojana-antarataḥ—another 1,300,000 yojanas; yat—which; tat—that; viṣṇoḥ paramam padam—the supreme abode of Lord Viṣṇu, or the lotus feet of Lord Viṣṇu; abhivadanti—the Ṛg Veda mantras praise; yatra—on which; ha—indeed; mahā-bhāgavataḥ—the great devotee; dhruvaḥ—Mahārāja Dhruva; auttānapādiḥ—the son of Mahārāja Uttānapāda; agninā—by the fire-god; indreṇa—by the heavenly King, Indra; prajāpatinā—by the Prajāpati; kaśyapena—by Kaśyapa; dharmeṇa—by Dharmarāja; ca—also; samakāla-yugbhiḥ—who are engaged at the time; sa-bahu-mānam—always respectfully; dakṣiṇataḥ—on the right side; kriyamāṇaḥ—being circumambulated; idānīm—now; api—even; kalpa-jīvinām—of the living entities who exist at the end of the creation; ājīvyaḥ—the source of life; upāste—remains; tasya—his; iha—here; anubhāvaḥ—greatness in discharging devotional service; upavarṇitaḥ—already described (in the Fourth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam).

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: My dear King, 1,300,000 yojanas \[10,400,000 miles\] above the planets of the seven sages is the place that learned scholars describe as the abode of Lord Viṣṇu. There the son of Mahārāja Uttānapāda, the great devotee Mahārāja Dhruva, still resides as the life source of all the living entities who live until the end of the creation. Agni, Indra, Prajāpati, Kaśyapa and Dharma all assemble there to offer him honor and respectful obeisances. They circumambulate him with their right sides toward him. I have already described the glorious activities of Mahārāja Dhruva \[in the Fourth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

After stating the details of the sun’s movement, Dhruva’s position and function is stated here. 1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] above the seven sages is the place called Parama Padam of Viṣṇu or Dhruvaloka, where Dhruva worships Viṣṇu along with his contemporaries.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Dhruva meditates and worships Viṣṇu along with Kashyapa and others, who will attain Sayujya ( liberation ) along with Dhruva.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] above the earth. Agni and others are stars living in the same time period.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Atha* means after mentioning the place of Dhruva. Śiśumāra is an aquatic creature. 1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] above the sages means 3,900,000 *yojanas* \[312,000,000 miles\] above the earth. Kashyapa and others stay as long as Dhruvaloka exists, thus they are called contemporaries. Aajivya means support. Lord Hari is indicated by the word “worships.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Dhruva resides in what is called the highest abode of Viṣṇu. He is there with his contemporaries Agni and others, in the form of stars. People living in Bhū and Antarikṣa depend upon Dhruva. Those living in Maharloka and upwards and the netherworlds do not depend upon him. His greatness has been described earlier in the Fourth Canto \[of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam\].

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

After stating the position and function of the sun and other planets in the previous chapter, the place and functions of Dhruva are stated here. He is situated 1,300,000 *yojanas* \[10,400,000 miles\] beyond the sun. The place is called the abode of Viṣṇu, as He manifests there. There, Dhruva is engaged in the worship Hari along with Agni, Yama, Kashyapa and others who are his contemporaries and are in the form of stars.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Agni and others also have the forms of stars. They are his \[Dhruva’s\] contemporaries. Dhruva preaches to those who reside in Maharloka and other lokas, where people live for an entire *kalpa*. He is thus the support of all those people.

### Text 2

*स हि सर्वेषां ज्योतिर्गणानां ग्रहनक्षत्रादीनामनिमिषेणाव्यक्तरंहसा भगवता*  
*कालेन भ्राम्यमाणानां स्थाणुरिवावष्टम्भ ईश्वरेण विहितः शश्वदवभासते ॥२॥*

*sa hi sarveṣāṁ jyotir-gaṇānāṁ graha-nakṣatrādīnām animiṣeṇāvyakta-raṁhasā bhagavatā kālena bhrāmyamāṇānāṁ sthāṇur ivāvaṣṭambha īśvareṇa vihitaḥ śaśvad avabhāsate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

saḥ—that planet of Dhruva Mahārāja; hi—indeed; sarveṣām—of all; jyotiḥ-gaṇānām—the luminaries; graha-nakṣatra-ādīnām—such as the planets and stars; animiṣeṇa—who does not rest; avyakta—inconceivable; raṁhasā—whose force; bhagavatā—the most powerful; kālena—by the time factor; bhrāmyamāṇānām—being caused to revolve; sthāṇuḥ iva—like a post; avaṣṭambhaḥ—the pivot; īśvareṇa—by the will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vihitaḥ—established; śaśvat—constantly; avabhāsate—shines.

**Перевод:**

**Established by the supreme will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the polestar, which is the planet of Mahārāja Dhruva, constantly shines as the central pivot for all the stars and planets. The unsleeping, invisible, most powerful time factor causes these luminaries to revolve around the polestar without cessation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The famous abode of Viṣṇu, where Dhruva worships him. Samakalayugbhih means with his contemporaries.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He is placed as the support of celestial bodies and stays in a single place. He appears there only.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sthanu, by pun means, Dhruva cannot be shaken by *kāla-cakra*. On the other hand, he is the support of *kāla-cakra*, which is under his control. This excellence is bestowed on him by Īśvara, who is capable of doing and undoing things.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Sthanu means a firm pole or a trunk of a tree. It also means Rudra. So by pun it means Dhruva is unshakeable like Rudra. This greatness he achieved by the grace of Hari, who is capable of doing, and undoing things.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In this chapter, the position of Dhruva and the Śiśumāra *Chakra* are described. It is called the highest abode of Viṣṇu. Agni and other stars respectfully go around Dhruva, who is then absorbed in the worship of Viṣṇu.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

His greatness on earth was earlier described, yet here his importance and greatness while residing in heaven is described. Animisha means incessant, not stopping—that is Kala (Time) a form of God. God has placed Dhruva there to exemplify the greatness of His devotee.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

He has been placed by God like the immovable central pole in a thrashing field. He appears like that always.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The greatness of Dhruva is stated. Animisha is Lord Viṣṇu himself, because He never closes his eyes. This form of His is called Kala. Avashtamba means the support. As the oxen move around the pole without violating their positions, so do the stars and planets move in their assigned positions only. Like the oxen, some are tied from inside and some others from outside of the *kāla-cakra*. God has fixed them to the *kāla-cakra*. Avaha and the others are the Vāyus \[winds\] that propel them.

### Text 3

*यथा मेढीस्तम्भ आक्रमणपशवः संयोजितास्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः सवनैर्यथास्थानं*  
*मण्डलानि चरन्त्येवं भगणा ग्रहादय एतस्मिन्नन्तर्बहिर्योगेन कालचक्र*  
*आयोजिता ध्रुवमेवावलम्ब्य वायुनोदीर्यमाणा आकल्पान्तं परिचङ्क्रमन्ति*  
*नभसि यथा मेघाः श्येनादयो वायुवशाः कर्मसारथयः परिवर्तन्ते एवं*  
*ज्योतिर्गणाः प्रकृतिपुरुषसंयोगानुगृहीताः कर्मनिर्मितगतयो भुवि न*  
*पतन्ति ॥३॥*

*yathā meḍhīstambha ākramaṇa-paśavaḥ saṁyojitās tribhis tribhiḥ savanair yathā-sthānaṁ maṇḍalāni caranty evaṁ bhagaṇā grahādaya etasminn antar-bahir-yogena kāla-cakra āyojitā dhruvam evāvalambya vāyunodīryamāṇā ākalpāntaṁ paricaṅ kramanti nabhasi yathā meghāḥ śyenādayo vāyu-vaśāḥ karma-sārathayaḥ parivartante evaṁ jyotirgaṇāḥ prakṛti-puruṣa-saṁyogānugṛhītāḥ karma-nirmita-gatayo bhuvi na patanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yathā—exactly like; meḍhīstambhe—to the pivot post; ākramaṇa-paśavaḥ—bulls for threshing rice; saṁyojitāḥ—being yoked; tribhiḥ tribhiḥ—by three; savanaiḥ—movements; yathā-sthānam—in their proper places; maṇḍalāni—orbits; caranti—traverse; evam—in the same way; bha-gaṇāḥ—the luminaries, like the sun, the moon, Venus, Mercury, Mars and Jupiter; graha-ādayaḥ—the different planets; etasmin—in this; antaḥ-bahiḥ-yogena—by connection with the inner or outer circles; kāla-cakre—in the wheel of eternal time; āyojitāḥ—fixed; dhruvam—Dhruvaloka; eva—certainly; avalambya—taking support of; vāyunā—by the wind; udīryamāṇāḥ—being propelled; ā-kalpa-antam—until the end of the creation; paricaṅ kramanti—revolve all around; nabhasi—in the sky; yathā—exactly like; meghāḥ—heavy clouds; śyena-ādayaḥ—birds such as the big eagle; vāyu-vaśāḥ—controlled by the air; karma-sārathayaḥ—whose chariot drivers are the results of their own past activities; parivartante—move around; evam—in this way; jyotiḥ-gaṇāḥ—the luminaries, the planets and stars in the sky; prakṛti—of material nature; puruṣa—and of the Supreme Personality, Kṛṣṇa; saṁyoga-anugṛhītāḥ—supported by the combined efforts; karma-nirmita—caused by their own past fruitive activities; gatayaḥ—whose movements; bhuvi—on the ground; na—not; patanti—fall down.

**Перевод:**

**When bulls are yoked together and tied to a central post to thresh rice, they tread around that pivot without deviating from their proper positions—one bull being closest to the post, another in the middle, and a third on the outside. Similarly, all the planets and all the hundreds and thousands of stars revolve around the polestar, the planet of Mahārāja Dhruva, in their respective orbits, some higher and some lower. Fastened by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to the machine of material nature according to the results of their fruitive acts, they are driven around the polestar by the wind and will continue to be so until the end of creation. These planets float in the air within the vast sky, just as clouds with hundreds of tons of water float in the air or as the great śyena eagles, due to the results of past activities, fly high in the sky and have no chance of falling to the ground.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Like oxen tied at the thrashing pole. They are assisted by their *karma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Oxen tied to a thrashing pole with a three stringed rope, move in circles around the central pole—some of them tied from inside and others tied from outside. In the same manner, the celestial bodies which are tied to the *kāla-cakra* from inside and outside move in circles around Dhruva, propelled by their *karma* and the force of *pravāha* Vāyu. They resemble the birds that fly in the sky and do not fall. The *karma* of *jīvas* and the properties of matter such as wind are manifold and wonderful and are responsible for holding these bodies in the sky.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

As oxen tied to a thrashing pole move around the poles with their eyes open, so do all the celestial bodies go around Dhruva in their assigned path and with their assigned speed. They never move otherwise. “Three savanna” in the present context means the three different gaits of the sun and other planets. Some stars are attached from inside to Dhruva and others from outside. As stated earlier, they are propelled by the winds, Avaha, etc.; and are endowed with speed and other natural powers by which they do not fall.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Tribhih Savanaih” means in the morning, midday and evening. By the changes brought about by the farmers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Just as the oxen tied to the central pole of the threshing floor move in their respective positions, so do the stars and planets, fixed by Īśvara \[the controller\] in the proper positions within the *kāla-cakra* move by their own *karma* \[the results of previous activities\] and propelled by Vāyu \[wind or the demigod of wind, Vāyu\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tied by the farmers to the central pole of the thrashing floor. “The three *savana*” means the nearer, central and farther position from the pole at the center. In the present context, it means the three gaits \[speeds\] of the sun. These celestial bodies have been situated lower and lower from Saturn and higher and higher by God and are propelled by the force of *pravāha* Vāyu, and all of them are under the influence of *māyā* \[the energy of the Lord\].

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“For them their *karma* is *sarathi*” means, “renders assistance.” Prkrti is the primordial matter in the form of cause and effect. *Puruṣa* is the *jīva* \[individual living entity\]. Their association with each other is beginningless. These planets are assisted by this association also. Endowed with corporeal bodies which are the categories of that matter, the *jīvas* in the form of stars and planets do not fall.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Just as the oxen tied to the thrashing pole move in circles in their respective places in all the three parts of the day, so do the planets placed higher and lower in the *kāla-cakra* by īśvara, move around Dhruva, until the end of the *kalpa* \[time period of a day of Brahmā equaling 4.3 billion years\] driven by Vāyu.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The same idea is further clarified. As oxen tied to a pole do not violate their path and position, so do the stars and planets move around Dhruva, driven by Vāyu and assisted by their own *karma*. They are attached to the *kāla-cakra* by ropes of wind from inside and outside and they do not fall because of these reasons. The same thing is further elaborated. The association of *prakṛti* (matter) and *puruṣa* (the living entity) is so complex that it produces wonderful events. This is one of the reasons for their not falling. The planets move like birds or even clouds in the sky.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

They do not fall like us because they have done excellent good deeds in the form of the worship of Viṣṇu. As a result of these, they are endowed with extraordinary powers.

### Text 4

*केचनैतज्ज्योतिरनीकं शिशुमारसंस्थानेन भगवतो वासुदेवस्य*  
*योगधारणायामनुवर्णयन्ति ॥४॥*

*kecanaitaj jyotir-anīkaṁ śiśumāra-saṁsthānena bhagavato vāsudevasya yoga-dhāraṇāyām anuvarṇayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

kecana—some yogīs or learned scholars of astronomy; etat—this; jyotiḥ-anīkam—great wheel of planets and stars; śiśumāra-saṁsthānena—imagine this wheel to be a śiśumāra (dolphin); bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vāsudevasya—Lord Vāsudeva (the son of Vasudeva), Kṛṣṇa; yoga-dhāraṇāyām—in absorption in worship; anuvarṇayanti—describe.

**Перевод:**

**This great machine, consisting of the stars and planets, resembles the form of a śiśumāra \[dolphin\] in the water. It is sometimes considered an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva. Great yogīs meditate upon Vāsudeva in this form because it is actually visible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is to be understood that because God is there as the support, there is no chance of falling. This prose is an introduction to that. Jyotiranikam = *jyotis-cakra* situated in his yogic body.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Added to the above two things, there is the third and most important thing, which causes these bodies not to fall—namely, the super power of Lord Śiśumāra, who is Viṣṇu Himself. The people who know the *Vedas* say that the entire Jyotis*cakra* is in the yogic force of Lord Śiśumāra. They do their meditation in the same manner.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

More than anything else, Lord Śiśumāra has held them by His yogic power—thus they do not fall.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

For the sake of yogic meditation, it could be imagined as one pleases in the form of Śiśumāra. That is why it is said, “moon in the mind" and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Jyotiranikam means *jyotiscakra*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is not that they have no support which may cause them to fall—they are supported by the yogic powers of Śiśumāra. They are said to be the yogic form of Śiśumāra for the sake of worship. That is how the statements “moon in the mind,” etc. hold good.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

There is no room to suspect a fall because they are held by God’s form Śiśumāra.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

With the assistance of *karma*, they do not fall down from the sky.

Because they are borne by īśvara, there is no chance of their falling.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The most important reason for their not falling down is that they are borne by Lord Śiśumāra. The learned say that all the stars and planets are positioned in and borne by the yogic form of Lord Vāsudeva.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Actually there is support, and so no chance of falling. They are held by Śiśumāra, so that they do not fall but move in their proper orbits. The seers say that the yogic powers of the Lord are what prevents these bodies from falling.

### Text 5

*यस्य पुच्छाग्रेऽवाक्षिरसः कुण्डलीभूतदेहस्य ध्रुव उपकल्पितस्तस्य लाङ्गूले*  
*प्रजापतिरग्निरिन्द्रो धर्म इति पुच्छमूले धाता विधाता च कट्यां सप्तर्षयः ।*  
*तस्य दक्षिणावर्तकुण्डलीभूतशरीरस्य यान्युदगयनानि दक्षिणपार्श्वे तु*  
*नक्षत्राण्युपकल्पयन्ति दक्षिणायनानि तु सव्ये । यथा शिशुमारस्य कुण्डला*  
*भोगसन्निवेशस्य पार्श्वयोरुभयोरप्यवयवाः समसंङ्ख्या भवन्ति । पृष्ठे त्वजवीथी*  
*आकाशगङ्गा चोदरतः ॥५॥*

*yasya pucchāgre 'vākśirasaḥ kuṇḍalī-bhūta-dehasya dhruva upakalpitas tasya lāṅgūle prajāpatir agnir indro dharma iti puccha-mūle dhātā vidhātā ca kaṭyāṁ saptarṣayaḥ; tasya dakṣiṇāvarta-kuṇḍalī-bhūta-śarīrasya yāny udagayanāni dakṣiṇa-pārśve tu nakṣatrāṇy upakalpayanti dakṣiṇāyanāni tu savye; yathā śiśumārasya kuṇḍalā-bhoga-sanniveśasya pārśvayor ubhayor apy avayavāḥ samasaṅkhyā bhavanti; pṛṣṭhe tv ajavīthī ākāśa-gaṅgā codarataḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of which; puccha-agre—at the end of the tail; avākśirasaḥ—whose head is downward; kuṇḍalī-bhūta-dehasya—whose body, which is coiled; dhruvaḥ—Mahārāja Dhruva on his planet, the polestar; upakalpitaḥ—is situated; tasya—of that; lāṅgūle—on the tail; prajāpatiḥ—of the name Prajāpati; agniḥ—Agni; indraḥ—Indra; dharmaḥ—Dharma; iti—thus; puccha-mūle—at the base of the tail; dhātā vidhātā—the demigods known as Dhātā and Vidhātā; ca—also; kaṭyām—on the hip; sapta-ṛṣayaḥ—the seven saintly sages; tasya—of that; dakṣiṇa-āvarta-kuṇḍalī-bhūta-śarīrasya—whose body is like a coil turning toward the right side; yāni—which; udagayanāni—marking the northern courses; dakṣiṇa-pārśve—on the right side; tu—but; nakṣatrāṇi—constellations; upakalpayanti—are situated; dakṣiṇa-āyanāni—the fourteen stars, from Puṣyā to Uttarāṣāḍhā, marking the northern course; tu—but; savye—on the left side; yathā—just like; śiśumārasya—of the dolphin; kuṇḍalā-bhoga-sanniveśasya—whose body appears like a coil; pārśvayoḥ—on the sides; ubhayoḥ—both; api—certainly; avayavāḥ—the limbs; samasaṅkhyāḥ—of equal number (fourteen); bhavanti—are; pṛṣṭhe—on the back; tu—of course; ajavīthī—the first three stars marking the southern route (Mūlā, Pūrvaṣāḍhā and Uttarāṣāḍhā); ākāśa-gaṅgā—the Ganges in the sky (the Milky Way); ca—also; udarataḥ—on the abdomen.

**Перевод:**

**This form of the śiśumāra has its head downward and its body coiled. On the end of its tail is the planet of Dhruva, on the body of its tail are the planets of the demigods Prajāpati, Agni, Indra and Dharma, and at the base of its tail are the planets of the demigods Dhātā and Vidhātā. Where the hips might be on the śiśumāra are the seven saintly sages like Vasiṣṭha and Aṅgirā. The coiled body of the Śiśumāra-chakra turns toward its right side, on which the fourteen constellations from Abhijit to Punarvasu are located. On its left side are the fourteen stars from Puṣyā to Uttarāṣāḍhā. Thus its body is balanced because its sides are occupied by an equal number of stars. On the back of the śiśumāra is the group of stars known as Ajavīthī, and on its abdomen is the Ganges that flows in the sky \[the Milky Way\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“In the tail” means, “lower part of the front.: The fourteen Uttarāyaṇa stars ending from Punarvasu are on the right. The fourteen Dakṣiṇāyana stars starting from Pushya are to the left.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The same is elaborated. The body of Śiśumāra is coiled in the middle only and head down, tail up. At the tip of the tail are Dhata and Vidhata, the seven sages in the waist, Prajāpati in the tail, Agni slightly below Prajāpati, Indra below Agni, Dharma further down, Uttarāyaṇa stars on the right side, Dakṣiṇāyana stars on the left side. On the back is Ajavithi, the Dakṣiṇāyana course of Sūrya, the milky way in the stomach and so on. It should be meditated in the same way. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The fourteen Uttarāyaṇa stars from Abhijit to Punarvasu are on the right side and the fourteen Dakṣiṇāyana stars from Pushya to Uttarashada are on the left side. Ajavithi is the first part of the southern course.

### Text 6

*पुनर्वसुपुष्यौ दक्षिणवामयोः श्रोण्योरार्द्राश्लेषे च दक्षिणवामयोः पश्चिमयोः*  
*पादयोरभिजिदुत्तराषाढे दक्षिणवामयोर्नासिकयोर्यथासङ्ख्यं श्रवणपूर्वाषाढे*  
*दक्षिणवामयोर्लोचनयोर्धनिष्ठा मूलं च दक्षिणवामयोः कर्णयोर्मघादीन्यष्ट*  
*नक्षत्राणि दक्षिणायनानि वामपार्श्ववङ्क्रिषु युञ्जीत तथैव मृगशीर्षादीन्युदगय*  
*नानि दक्षिणपार्श्ववङ्क्रिषु प्रातिलोम्येन प्रयुञ्जीत शतभिषाज्येष्ठे*  
*स्कन्धयोर्दक्षिणवामयोर्न्यसेत् ॥६॥*

*punarvasu-puṣyau dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ śroṇyor ārdrāśleṣe ca dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ paścimayoḥ pādayor abhijid-uttarāṣāḍhe dakṣiṇa-vāmayor nāsikayor yathā-saṅkhyaṁ śravaṇa-pūrvāṣāḍhe dakṣiṇa-vāmayor locanayor dhaniṣṭhā mūlaṁ ca dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ karṇayor maghādīny aṣṭa nakṣatrāṇi dakṣiṇāyanāni vāma-pārśva-vaṅkriṣu yuñjīta tathaiva mṛga-śīrṣādīny udagayanāni dakṣiṇa-pārśva-vaṅkriṣu prātilomyena prayuñjīta śatabhiṣā-jyeṣṭhe skandhayor dakṣiṇa-vāmayor nyaset.*

**Пословный перевод:**

punarvasu—the star named Punarvasu; puṣyau—and the star named Puṣyā; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—on the right and left; śroṇyoḥ—loins; ārdrā—the star named Ārdrā; aśleṣe—the star named Aśleṣā; ca—also; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—at the right and left; paścimayoḥ—behind; pādayoḥ—feet; abhijit-uttarāṣāḍhe—the stars named Abhijit and Uttarāṣāḍhā; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—on the right and left; nāsikayoḥ—nostrils; yathā-saṅkhyam—according to numerical order; śravaṇa-pūrvāṣāḍhe—the stars named Śravaṇā and Pūrvāṣāḍhā; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—at the right and left; locanayoḥ—eyes; dhaniṣṭhā mūlam ca—and the stars named Dhaniṣṭhā and Mūlā; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—at the right and left; karṇayoḥ—ears; maghā-ādīni—the stars such as Maghā; aṣṭa nakṣatrāṇi—eight stars; dakṣiṇa-āyanāni—which mark the southern course; vāma-pārśva—of the left side; vaṅkriṣu—at the ribs; yuñjīta—may place; tathā eva—similarly; mṛga-śīrṣā-ādīni—such as Mṛgaśīrṣā; udagayanāni—marking the northern course; dakṣiṇa-pārśva-vaṅkriṣu—on the right side; prātilomyena—in the reverse order; prayuñjīta—may place; śatabhiṣā—Śatabhiṣā; jyeṣṭhe—Jyeṣṭhā; skandhayoḥ—on the two shoulders; dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ—right and left; nyaset—should place.

**Перевод:**
