**On the right and left sides of where the loins might be on the Śiśumāra-chakra are the stars named Punarvasu and Puṣyā. Ārdrā and Aśleṣā are on its right and left feet, Abhijit and Uttarāṣāḍhā are on its right and left nostrils, Śravaṇā and Pūrvāṣāḍhā are at its right and left eyes, and Dhaniṣṭhā and Mūlā are on its right and left ears. The eight stars from Maghā to Anurādhā, which mark the southern course, are on the ribs of the left of its body, and the eight stars from Mṛgaśīrṣā to Pūrvabhādra, which mark the northern course, are on the ribs on the right side. Śatabhiṣā and Jyeṣṭhā are on the right and left shoulders.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The break up of the same thing is stated here. Punarvasu is the last star of Uttarāyaṇa. Pushya is the first star of Dakṣiṇāyana. Ardra and Ashlesha are their adjacent stars. Abhijit is the first star of Uttarāyaṇa. Uttarashada is the last star of Dakṣiṇāyana. Śravaṇa and Purvashada are their next and prior stars respectively. Dhanista and Moola are the next and prior stars of the above pair. The eight Dakṣiṇāyana stars starting from Magha to Anuradha are in the left bones. The eight Uttarāyaṇa stars from Mrgashirsha to Purvabhadra are situated on the right side bones. Shatabhisha (an Uttarāyaṇa star) and Jyesta (a Dakṣiṇāyana star), are located on the shoulders.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here in the form of a circle only means the middle part, neither the tail nor the head. That is why the Uttarāyaṇa stars are on the right side. Even though it is coiled in the middle, sideways and upwards and downwards, it is uneven and the discrepancies observed here should be attributed to that. The position of Nārāyaṇa in the heart should be explained thus. Ajavithi is the first part of the southern path. Mula, Purvashadha and Uttarashadha constitute the Ajavithi. Where the position of stars is stated in the ear and so on, they should be taken as the raised part of those organs. Akashaganga is also on a high because it comes there. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Shronyoh* means hips. *Vadhri* means bones. “In the reverse order” means, in the order of Mrgashira, Rohini, Krittika, Bharani and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The reading “vankri” means a rib. \[Note by the translator: here the word *vankri* is taken instead of the reading *vadhri*.\]

### Text 7

*उत्तराहनावगस्तिरधराहनौ यमो मुखेषु चाङ्गारकः शनैश्चर उपस्थे बृहस्पतिः*  
*ककुदि वक्षस्यादित्यो हृदये नारायणो मनसि चन्द्रो नाभ्यामुशना स्तनयोरश्विनौ*  
*बुधः प्राणापानयो राहुर्गले केतवः सर्वाङ्गेषु रोमसु सर्वे तारागणाः*  
*॥७॥*

*uttarā-hanāv agastir adharā-hanau yamo mukheṣu cāṅgārakaḥ śanaiścara upasthe bṛhaspatiḥ kakudi vakṣasy ādityo hṛdaye nārāyaṇo manasi candro nābhyām uśanā stanayor aśvinau budhaḥ prāṇāpānayo rāhur gale ketavaḥ sarvāṅgeṣu romasu sarve tārā-gaṇāḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

uttarā-hanau—on the upper jaw; agastiḥ—the star named Agasti; adharā-hanau—on the lower jaw; yamaḥ—Yamarāja; mukheṣu—on the mouth; ca—also; aṅgārakaḥ—Mars; śanaiścaraḥ—Saturn; upasthe—on the genitals; bṛhaspatiḥ—Jupiter; kakudi—on the back of the neck; vakṣasi—on the chest; ādityaḥ—the sun; hṛdaye—within the heart; nārāyaṇaḥ—Lord Nārāyaṇa; manasi—in the mind; candraḥ—the moon; nābhyām—on the navel; uśanā—Venus; stanayoḥ—on the two breasts; aśvinau—the two stars named Aśvin; budhaḥ—Mercury; prāṇāpānayoḥ—in the inner airs known as prāṇa and apāna; rāhuḥ—the planet Rāhu; gale—on the neck; ketavaḥ—comets; sarva-aṅgeṣu—all over the body; romasu—in the pores of the body; sarve—all; tārā-gaṇāḥ—the numerous stars.

**Перевод:**

**On the upper chin of the śiśumāra is Agasti; on its lower chin, Yamarāja; on its mouth, Mars; on its genitals, Saturn; on the back of its neck, Jupiter; on its chest, the sun; and within the core of its heart, Nārāyaṇa. Within its mind is the moon; on its navel, Venus; and on its breasts, the Aśvinī-kumāras. Within its life air, which is known as prāṇāpāna, is Mercury, on its neck is Rāhu, all over its body are comets, and in its pores are the numerous stars.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Yama, Nārāyaṇa and Ashwins are stars. Kakud means the raised part on the back of the neck.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Uttarahanu is the upper jaw. Adharahanu means the lower jaw. Though Mars and others are stationed in the respective limbs, their motion is due to the motion of the particular limb of Śiśumāra.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana stars are on either side of the coiled middle body. The Uttarāyaṇa stars starting from Abhijit to Punarvasu are placed respectively in the right hip, foot, nose, eye, ear and nose respectively. The Dakṣiṇāyana stars, i.e. the eight stars from Mrgashira to Revathi should be placed on the right side. Shatabhisha is in the right shoulder. Of the Dakṣiṇāyana stars starting from Pushya to Uttarashada, the five stars from Pushya to Moola should be placed in the feet, nose, eye and ear. The stars from Magha to Anuradha should be placed on the left in the same order. Jyesta is in the left shoulder. Both Agastya and Yama are in the form of stars. Ketus are situated on the back of the neck. The plural is used as they are endowed with accessory stars. The rest is clear.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Dhruva is situated at the tip of the tail of the coiled Śiśumāra. Langula means the middle of the tail here. The Uttarāyaṇa stars’ positions have been elaborated. Pratilomya means reverse order, i.e. from Purvabhadra to Mrgashira.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Yama is a star. Jupiter is on the raised part of the back of the neck.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Yama, Nārāyaṇa and Ashwins are in the form of stars. Jupiter is on the raised point, behind the neck.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Agasthya is in the upper jaw; Yama is in the lower jaw; Mars is in the mouth; Saturn is in the reproductive organ; Brhaspati is in the shoulder; Venus is in the navel; the Ashwins are in the breasts; Budha is in the breath; Rāhu is in the neck, the Ketus are all over the body and the stars are in the hairs on the body. This is how the meditation should be done.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Prajāpati and others are in the form of stars and are located in the middle of the tail and so on as elaborated. The Dakṣiṇāyana stars are fourteen in number from Pushya to Uttarashada. The Uttarāyaṇa stars are fourteen from Abhijit to Punarvasu.

### Text 8

*एतदु हैव भगवतो विष्णोः सर्वदेवतामयं रूपमहरहः सन्ध्यायां*  
*प्रयतो वाग्यतो निरीक्षमाण उपतिष्ठेत नमो ज्योतिर्लोकाय कालायनाया*  
*निमिषां पतये महापुरुषायाभिधीमहीति ॥८॥*

*etad u haiva bhagavato viṣṇoḥ sarva-devatāmayaṁ rūpam aharahaḥ sandhyāyāṁ prayato vāgyato nirīkṣamāṇa upatiṣṭheta namo jyotir-lokāya kālāyanāyānimiṣāṁ pataye mahā-puruṣāyābhidhīmahīti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etat—this; u ha—indeed; eva—certainly; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; viṣṇoḥ—of Lord Viṣṇu; sarva-devatā-mayam—consisting of all the demigods; rūpam—form; ahaḥ-ahaḥ—always; sandhyāyām—in the morning, noon and evening; prayataḥ—meditating upon; vāgyataḥ—controlling the words; nirīkṣamāṇaḥ—observing; upatiṣṭheta—one should worship; namaḥ—respectful obeisances; jyotiḥ-lokāya—unto the resting place of all the planetary systems; kālāyanāya—in the form of supreme time; animiṣām—of the demigods; pataye—unto the master; mahā-puruṣāya—unto the Supreme person; abhidhīmahi—let us meditate; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, the body of the śiśumāra, as thus described, should be considered the external form of Lord Viṣṇu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Morning, noon and evening, one should silently observe the form of the Lord as the Śiśumāra-chakra and worship Him with this mantra: "O Lord who has assumed the form of time! O resting place of all the planets moving in different orbits! O master of all demigods, O Supreme Person, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You and meditate upon You."**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Loka here means support. We pray to him through hymns.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Meditation should be done every day, picturing the Śiśumāra, the stars and planets in the above mentioned way. The meditation should be done in the morning and evening with silence and utmost attention. The Vedic hymn should also be chanted. It means “Obeisances to You, who are of the nature of the *kāla-cakra*, Lord of all demigods and the greatest person. We meditate on this form of Yours.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Animisha means demigods. “To the Lord of the demigods” means they offer their obeisances and prayers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The above mentioned positions of stars are elaborated. On the left side it is in the reverse order like Mrgashira, Rohini, Krittika and so on. The eight stars ending in Purvabhadra are on the right side bones.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Animisha means demigods, because they do not wink.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

This Śiśumāra form must be worshipped and prayed to by the *mantra* cited below.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This form of Viṣṇu should be praised by the following *mantra*. *Jyotisham lokaya* means the dwelling place of all luminaries. We offer our obeisances.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

This form should be meditated upon every day during mornings and evenings with silence and utmost care. The *mantra* is stated. We offer our obeisances to Hari, the Lord of Brahmā and all other deities.

### Text 9

*ग्रहर्क्षतारामयमाधिदैविकं*  
*पापापहं मन्त्रकृतां त्रिकालम् ।*  
*नमस्यतः स्मरतो वा त्रिकालं*  
*नश्येत तत्कालजमाशु पापम् ॥९॥*

*graharkṣatārāmayam ādhidaivikaṁ*  
*pāpāpahaṁ mantra-kṛtāṁ tri-kālam*  
*namasyataḥ smarato vā tri-kālaṁ*  
*naśyeta tat-kālajam āśu pāpam*

**Пословный перевод:**

graha-ṛkṣa-tārā-mayam—consisting of all the planets and stars; ādhidaivikam—the leader of all the demigods; pāpa-apaham—the killer of sinful reactions; mantra-kṛtām—of those who chant the mantra mentioned above; tri-kālam—three times; namasyataḥ—offering obeisances; smarataḥ—meditating; vā—or; tri-kālam—three times; naśyeta—destroys; tat-kāla-jam—born at that time; āśu—very quickly; pāpam—all sinful reactions.

**Перевод:**

**The body of the Supreme Lord, Viṣṇu, which forms the Śiśumāra-chakra, is the resting place of all the demigods and all the stars and planets. One who chants this mantra to worship that Supreme Person three times a day—morning, noon and evening—will surely be freed from all sinful reactions. If one simply offers his obeisances to this form or remembers this form three times a day, all his recent sinful activities will be destroyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Mantrakrtam means for those who chant the *mantra* cited above.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

For those who meditate and pray in the above manner, the sins committed in the past, present and future will be dispelled.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

For those who meditate upon and pray to Śiśumāra in the above mentioned way, all their sins are washed off by the Lord. The word indicates that this is famous in the stanza, “Nārāyaṇa is a famous thief, etc.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Mars and other planets move from one *rāśi* to another because of the movement of the limb on which they are situated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He is the remover of sins of those who chant the above mentioned *mantra*.

What should be understood here is this: Dhruva is 3,800,000 *yojanas* \[30,400,000 miles\] above the sun. 10,000,000 *yojanas* \[80,000,000 miles\] from Dhruva is Maharloka. 20,000,000 *yojanas* \[160,000,000 miles\] from there is Janaloka. 80,000,000 *yojanas* \[640,000,000 miles\] from there is Satyaloka. 120,000,000 *yojanas* \[960,000,000 miles\] from there is Satyaloka. So from the sun it is 23.38 *crore yojanas* until Satyaloka, and Vaikuṇṭha is situated in the 1.62 *crore yojanas* above Satyaloka. Thereafter it is *brahmāṇḍa* shell. This is how it is stated in *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*. Like this, the earth is 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] below the sun. In the next 70,000 *yojanas* \[560,000 miles\] downwards, the seven underworlds are situated. Śeṣa is situated further 30,000 *yojanas* \[240,000 miles\] downwards. So the Garbhodaka (water inside the *brahmāṇḍa*) is 200,000 *yojanas* \[1,600,000 miles\] below the sun. The thickness of that water is 249,800,000 *yojanas* \[1,998,400,000 miles\]. Like this the vertical height of *brahmāṇḍa* is 500,000,000 *yojanas* \[4 billion miles\]. It is the diameter measuring from any point within the *brahmāṇḍa* to the diametrically opposite point. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

They offer their worship with the Vedic hymns that dispel all the sins.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

All sins vanish for he who offers his *pranamas* chanting this *mantra* to Śiśumāra, the controller of all the demigods in the form of planets.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The description of lakes based on *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* is also the same. Only *Brahma Vaivartha Purāṇa* is quoted to support the distance between Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

For those who offer their prayers and obeisances to Śiśumāra Hari, three times a day, the sins committed in the particular time get washed away.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

To the left of the back there is Ajavithi. This Ajavithi is not the same as mentioned in the *Vāyu Purāṇa* quoted earlier. This is a different Ajavithi according to Puranic texts. The exact places of the Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana stars are stated here. One should meditate in the same way.

Yama is another star. Viṣṇu is called Sarvadevatamaya, not because He is identical with all other demigods, but because He is superior to all other demigods. Jyotirloka means the support of the celestial bodies. Kalayana means he who appraises us of time. By this *mantra*, they conduct the worship.

For one who chants the *mantra* and offers obeisances, the three problems Adhidaivika, Adhibhautika, and Adhyatmika vanish.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twenty-third Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The Śiśumāra Planetary Systems.”

## Chapter 24 - The Subterranean Heavenly Planets

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*अधस्तात्सवितुर्योजनायुते स्वर्भानुर्नक्षत्रवच्चरतीत्येके योऽसावमरत्वं*  
*ग्रहत्वं चालभत भगवदनुकम्पया स्वयमसुरापसदः सैंहिकेयो ह्यतदर्हस्तस्य*  
*तात जन्म कर्माणि चोपरिष्टाद्वक्ष्यामः ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*adhastāt savitur yojanāyute svarbhānur nakṣatravac caratīty eke yo 'sāv amaratvaṁ grahatvaṁ cālabhata bhagavad-anukampayā svayam asurāpasadaḥ saiṁhikeyo hy atad-arhas tasya tāta janma karmāṇi copariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; adhastāt—below; savituḥ—the sun globe; yojana—a measurement equal to eight miles; ayute—ten thousand; svarbhānuḥ—the planet known as Rāhu; nakṣatra-vat—like one of the stars; carati—is rotating; iti—thus; eke—some who are learned in the Purāṇas; yaḥ—which; asau—that; amaratvam—a lifetime like those of the demigods; grahatvam—a position as one of the chief planets; ca—and; alabhata—obtained; bhagavat-anukampayā—by the compassion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svayam—personally; asura-apasadaḥ—the lowest of the asuras; saiṁhikeyaḥ—being the son of Siṁhikā; hi—indeed; a-tat-arhaḥ—not qualified for that position; tasya—his; tāta—O my dear King; janma—birth; karmāṇi—activities; ca—also; upariṣṭāt—later; vakṣyāmaḥ—I shall explain.

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, some historians, the speakers of the Purāṇas, say that 10,000** ***yojanas*** **\[80,000 miles\] below the sun is the planet known as Rāhu, which moves like one of the stars. The presiding deity of that planet, who is the son of Siṁhikā, is the most abominable of all asuras, but although he is completely unfit to assume the position of a demigod or planetary deity, he has achieved that position by the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Later I shall speak further about him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Having described the situation obtaining from Sūrya \[the sun\] to Dhruva \[the polestar\], the situation below the sun is being described hereafter. Swarbhanu means Rāhu, the son of Simhika.

Rāhu did not deserve to become a planet or immortal because he was a wretched demon (asura), the son of Simhika.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the status of celestial bodies from Sūrya to Dhruva upwards, henceforeward the downward status is described. Some say Rāhu moves like the stars 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] below the sun. He was awarded the status of planethood and that of immortality by the grace of God although he did not deserve it, as he was a demon born of Simhika. His birth and deeds will be narrated later in the Eight Canto of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The luxurious netherworlds are described here as the glory of Nārāyaṇa. After describing the planets, including Saturn, in the previous chapter, now the position of Rāhu is described first. The disc widths of the sun, moon and Rāhu are also described. Some pauranikas \[scholars of the Puraṇas\] say that Rāhu goes around Meru in the clockwise direction like other stars, while some astrologers say that he rises from the earth beyond Mānasottara and sets in the earth on the western direction. Others say that he reaches the east through the middle part of Patala, then reaches the earth in the east beyond Mānasottara and sets in the earth in the west. Still others say that he moves in the sky around Meru in the anticlockwise direction. Atadarha means not fit to become immortal. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It is said “some,” because in the opinion of the author, there is no *pravāha* Vāyu there, and Rāhu moves on his own.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The idea here is that he does not deserve to be either immortal nor to have the status of a planet.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The pauranikas \[scholars of the Purāṇas\] say that Rāhu moves like the stars around Meru, propelled by the *pravāha* Vāyu \[wind\], however, the personal opinion of the author is that Rāhu moves on his own, because Rāhu’s orbit is outside the purview of the *pravāha* Vāyu.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Here, the positions of Rāhu, Atala, etc. situated below the sun are described. Parashara has said, “The sun is 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] above the earth.” 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] below the sun, Rāhu gained the position of a planet and immortality by God’s compassion, although unworthy.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Having described the situation above the sun, here, the situation below the sun is described. The pauranikas say like this, however astronomers have a different view.

Addressing as, “Dear Tata (father),” indicates affection. “Later” means in the sixth and eighth cantos of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam.

They say the sun’s disc is 10,000 *yojanas* wide, the moon’s 12,000 and Rāhu’s 13,000.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

After describing the position above Sūrya \[the sun\], the position below him is described here.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Having described the situation above the sun’s disc, the situation below is described, starting from Rāhu. Some opine that Rāhu goes around Meru like other stars in the clockwise direction. The word “some” is used to record the difference of opinion, since others, astronomers, feel that Rāhu rises from the earth in the east and sets in the west. Aalabhata = received. Saimhikeya = son of Simhika. Atadarshah = not fit to become immortal.

### Text 2

*यददस्तरणेर्मण्डलं प्रतपतस्तद्विस्तरतो योजनायुतमाचक्षते द्वादशसहस्रं*  
*सोमस्य त्रयोदशसहस्रं राहोर्यः पर्वणि तद्व्यवधानकृद्वैरानुबन्धः सूर्या*  
*चन्द्रमसावभिधावति ॥२॥*

*yad adas taraṇer maṇḍalaṁ pratapatas tad vistarato yojanāyutam ācakṣate dvādaśa-sahasraṁ somasya trayodaśa-sahasraṁ rāhor yaḥ parvaṇi tad-vyavadhāna-kṛd vairānubandhaḥ sūryā-candramasāv abhidhāvati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—which; adaḥ—that; taraṇeḥ—of the sun; maṇḍalam—globe; pratapataḥ—which is always distributing heat; tat—that; vistarataḥ—in terms of width; yojana—a distance of eight miles; ayutam—ten thousand; ācakṣate—they estimate; dvādaśa-sahasram—20,000 yojanas (160,000 miles); somasya—of the moon; trayodaśa—thirty; sahasram—one thousand; rāhoḥ—of the planet Rāhu; yaḥ—which; parvaṇi—on occasion; tat-vyavadhāna-kṛt—who created an obstruction to the sun and moon at the time of the distribution of nectar; vaira-anubandhaḥ—whose intentions are inimical; sūryā—the sun; candramasau—and the moon; abhidhāvati—runs after them on the full-moon night and the dark-moon day.

**Перевод:**

**The sun globe, which is a source of heat, extends for 10,000 yojanas \[80,000 miles\]. The moon extends for 20,000 yojanas \[160,000 miles\], and Rāhu extends for 30,000 yojanas \[240,000 miles\]. Formerly, when nectar was being distributed, Rāhu tried to create dissension between the sun and moon by interposing himself between them. Rāhu is inimical toward both the sun and the moon, and therefore he always tries to cover the sunshine and moonshine on the dark-moon day and full-moon night.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The eclipse is narrated here. While nectar was being distributed to the demigods, Rāhu sat between the sun-god and the moon-god. Since they exposed him, a hatred arose between himself and them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Because of the context, the eclipse is explained here. The sun’s disc is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] broad, the moon’s disc is 12,000 *yojanas* \[96,000 miles\] and that of Rāhu is 13,000 *yojanas* \[104,000 miles\]. Because of his greater size, he is able to cover both the sun and the moon sometimes. He sat between them in the situation of consuming nectar. He rushed towards them for fighting. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The sun’s disc is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] broad. The moon’s disc is 20,000 *yojanas* \[160,000 miles\] broad. Dvidasa means twice ten. Rāhu’s disc is 40,000 *yojanas* \[320,000 miles\] broad. Trayodasa means three tens plus ten. This is not imagination—it is according to the words of Śrī Madhwacharya, “Except the breadths of the discs of Ravi, Chandra and Rāhu (and also the interchange of milk ocean and curds ocean), all other things (narrated here) have to be accepted here as perfectly correct.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Taranermandalam = the sun’s disc seated in the middle part (seat) of the chariot.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The eclipse is described. Parva = new moon and full moon. He sat between them and was exposed by them during the nectar-drinking (*amrtapana*) ceremony. He engenders that hatred even now.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Ado maṇḍalam* means the sun’s disc positioned on the seat of the chariot. *Parva* means new moon and full moon. In order to obstruct the vision of the sun and moon for those on earth, Rāhu seated himself between the sun and moon while the nectar was being drunk.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The sun’s disc is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] wide. During *amrtapana*, he entered between the sun and the moon. Having been exposed, even now he has hatred and runs towards them.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Keeping in mind the earlier incident and engendering hatred, Rāhu rushes towards the sun and the moon to attack them on the new moon and full moon days.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Now the width of sun’s and others discs are described. Dvadashasahasra means Dvidasasahasram, that is two times ten thousand, meaning thereby twenty thousand *yojanas*, thus it is twice as broad as the sun’s disc. Trayodasa should be interpreted as *tridasa* and *dasa* i.e. three tens and ten meaning forty in all. Thus, Rāhu’s disc is 40,000 *yojanas* \[320,000 miles\] broad—twice that of the moon. That is why it is said by Madhvacarya, “Everything should be interpreted without contradiction to Bhāgavata. The only exception being the position of the milk and curds ocean and the width of Rāhu, the moon and the sun. The words should be interpreted differently so that they do not contradict other *pramanas*.”

Because he was exposed by the sun and the moon while he sat between them during the nectar-drinking (*amrtapana*), his neck was cut. Thus, he still nourishes that hatred and rushes to attack them on the new moon and full moon days.

### Text 3

*तन्निशम्योभयत्रापि भगवता रक्षणाय प्रयुक्तं सुदर्शनं नाम भागवतं*  
*दयितमस्त्रं तत्तेजसा दुर्विषहं मुहुः परिवर्तमानमभ्यवस्थितो मुहूर्तमुद्वि*  
*जमानश्चकितहृदय आरादेव निवर्तते तदुपरागमिति वदन्ति लोकाः ॥३॥*

*tan niśamyobhayatrāpi bhagavatā rakṣaṇāya prayuktaṁ sudarśanaṁ nāma bhāgavataṁ dayitam astraṁ tat tejasā durviṣahaṁ muhuḥ parivartamānam abhyavasthito muhūrtam udvijamānaś cakita-hṛdaya ārād eva nivartate tad uparāgam iti vadanti lokāḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat—that situation; niśamya—hearing; ubhayatra—around both the sun and moon; api—indeed; bhagavatā—by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; rakṣaṇāya—for their protection; prayuktam—engaged; sudarśanam—the wheel of Kṛṣṇa; nāma—named; bhāgavatam—the most confidential devotee; dayitam—the most favorite; astram—weapon; tat—that; tejasā—by its effulgence; durviṣaham—unbearable heat; muhuḥ—repeatedly; parivartamānam—moving around the sun and moon; abhyavasthitaḥ—situated; muhūrtam—for a muhūrta (forty-eight minutes); udvijamānaḥ—whose mind was full of anxieties; cakita—frightened; hṛdayaḥ—the core of whose heart; ārāt—to a distant place; eva—certainly; nivartate—flees; tat—that situation; uparāgam—an eclipse; iti—thus; vadanti—they say; lokāḥ—the people.

**Перевод:**

**After hearing from the sun and moon demigods about Rāhu's attack, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, engages His disc, known as the Sudarśana chakra, to protect them. The Sudarśana chakra is the Lord's most beloved devotee and is favored by the Lord. The intense heat of its effulgence, meant for killing non-Vaiṣṇavas, is unbearable to Rāhu, and he therefore flees in fear of it. During the time Rāhu disturbs the sun or moon, there occurs what people commonly know as an eclipse.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The revolving Sudarśana *chakra* stays there and Rāhu faces it for some time but is unable to bear it, thus he withdraws. This position is called an eclipse. The sun and the moon are wholly or partly covered according to the different positions of Rāhu. Rāhu does not devour either of them, as they are in different orbits.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Seing this, Lord Viṣṇu has placed his irresistible, revolving Sudarśana *chakra* at both places. Rāhu stands for some time in front of the *chakra* and unable to bear it, withdraws. He covers a part or whole of the sun or moon before withdrawing, and people call it an eclipse. The partial or total eclipse depends upon the position of Rāhu, upright or slanted. He does not actually touch either of them as he is very far away from them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Bhāgavata means dear to the Lord. Staying in front of the revolving wheel, he \[Rāhu\] trembles and withdraws quickly to a distance.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sudarśana is placed at both places, i.e. in front of the sun and the moon. Rāhu stays in front of the sun and moon for some time, but, unable to bear the Sudarśana, withdraws. While he stays there, he covers the sun or moon partly or wholly. This is what people call an eclipse. The partial or full coverage depends upon the position of Rāhu. He does not come into physical contact with them, as he is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] away. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tam = the hatred. Ubhayatrapi = at both places—meaning both near the sun and the moon. Arat = from a distance; antara = in the middle—because he is at a distance of 10,000 *yojanas* from the sun.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The eclipse is either partial or full depending upon the position of Rāhu. Rāhu does not touch either of them as he is 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] away.

People say that an eclipse occurs when the sun or moon are invisible because Rahu obscures them.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Rāhu covers the sun’s or moon’s disc as he rushes to fight with them. This phenomenon is called an eclipse. Rāhu’s position is far off; thus, he will never touch either of them.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Bhāgavatam = dear to Bhagavān. Parivartamanam = revolving around. Uparaga = eclipse.

### Text 4

*ततोऽधस्तात्सिद्धचारणविद्याधराणां सदनानि तावन्मात्र एव ॥४॥*

*tato 'dhastāt siddha-cāraṇa-vidyādharāṇāṁ sadanāni tāvan mātra eva.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—the planet Rāhu; adhastāt—below; siddha-cāraṇa—of the planets known as Siddhaloka and Cāraṇaloka; vidyādharāṇām—and the planets of the Vidyādharas; sadanāni—the residential places; tāvat mātra—only that much distance (eighty thousand miles); eva—indeed.

**Перевод:**

**Below Rāhu by 10,000 yojanas \[80,000 miles\] are the planets known as Siddhaloka, Cāraṇaloka and Vidyādhara-loka.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Tavanmatra means 10,000 *yojanas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tatah = below Rāhu.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Tatah = from Rāhu. Tavanmatre = at 10,000 *yojanas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The abodes of the Siddhas and Charanas are situated 10,000 *yojanas* below Rāhu’s orbit.

### Text 5

*ततोऽधस्ताद्यक्षरक्षः पिशाचप्रेतभूतगणानां विहाराजिरमन्तरिक्षं यावद्वायुः प्रवाति*  
*यावन्मेघा उपलभ्यन्ते ॥५॥*

*tato 'dhastād yakṣa-rakṣaḥ-piśāca-preta-bhūta-gaṇānāṁ vihārājiram antarikṣaṁ yāvad vāyuḥ pravāti yāvan meghā upalabhyante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ adhastāt—beneath the planets occupied by the Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Vidyādharas; yakṣa-rakṣaḥ-piśāca-preta-bhūta-gaṇānām—of Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas, ghosts and so on; vihāra-ajiram—the place of sense gratification; antarikṣam—in the sky or outer space; yāvat—as far as; vāyuḥ—the wind; pravāti—blows; yāvat—as far as; meghāḥ—the clouds; upalabhyante—are seen.

**Перевод:**

**Beneath Vidyādhara-loka, Cāraṇaloka and Siddhaloka, in the sky called antarikṣa, are the places of enjoyment for the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas, ghosts and so on. Antarikṣa extends as far as the wind blows and the clouds float in the sky. Above this there is no more air.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Antarikṣa is the place where there are no planets—it extends to where wind blows and birds fly.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tāvanamātre = At 10,000 *yojanas*

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tataḥ = below the region of Siddhas. No special proof is adduced here. We have to guess, as on the previous occasion.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The limit of Antarikṣa is described as including where winds blow strongly, yet because the wind is invisible, another indicator is stated as “until where clouds are perceived.”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

10,000 *yojanas* below is Antarikṣa, the place where Rākṣasas, Pisacas (ghosts) and bhutas (the servants of Śiva) move in groups. It is 9,900 *yojanas* in its depth, where wind blows strongly and cloulds are observed.

### Text 6

*ततोऽधस्ताच्छतयोजनान्तर इयं पृथिवी यावद्धंसभासश्येन सुपर्णादयः*  
*पतत्त्रिप्रवरा उत्पतन्तीति ॥६॥*

*tato 'dhastāc chata-yojanāntara iyaṁ pṛthivī yāvad dhaṁsa-bhāsa-śyena-suparṇādayaḥ patattri-pravarā utpatantīti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ adhastāt—beneath that; śata-yojana—of one hundred yojanas; antare—by an interval; iyam—this; pṛthivī—planet earth; yāvat—as high as; haṁsa—swans; bhāsa—vultures; śyena—eagles; suparṇa-ādayaḥ—and other birds; patattri-pravarāḥ—the chief among birds; utpatanti—can fly; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**Below the abodes of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by a distance of 100 yojanas \[800 miles\] is the planet earth. Its upper limits extend as high as swans, hawks, eagles and similar large birds can fly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Bhūloka extends over the earth to where the birds like swans and others fly.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] below Rāhu are the abodes of the Siddhas, and 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] further below, is the Antarikṣa—a rejoicing place for Yakshas. There are no houses there. It extends to where wind blows strongly and clouds are perceived. The earth (Bhūloka) is situated one hundred *yojanas* \[800 miles\] below the Antarikṣa and it extends to as high as the best of birds can fly.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Tāvanmātre = at a distance of 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\].

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The extent of Bhūloka above the earth is described as up until where the hamsa \[swan\] and other birds fly.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tataḥ = from the place of yajña\[sacrifice\]. The best of birds such as the vulture and others. The body of these birds is made of earth, thus they can move in the earthly realm only.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Antarikṣa, the rejoicing place of the yakshas, is situated below the abodes of the Siddhas. The 100,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] distance between earth and the sun includes all these.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The limit of Bhūloka, (over the earth) is described as being as high as birds like swans and others fly. The bodies of the birds are derivatives of the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Below the clouds is *prithvi* \[earth\], stretching to 100 *yojanas* \[800 miles\] above its surface. It extends up to where swans and other birds can fly.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Tavanmatre = at the same distance of 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\]. Like a playground for rejoicing—the place where earthly birds fly, is also part of the earth, is the idea.

### Text 7

*उपवर्णितं भूमेर्यथासन्निवेशावस्थानमवनेरप्यधस्तात् सप्त भूविवरा एकैकशो*  
*योजनायुतान्तरेणायामविस्तारेणोपकॢप्ता अतलं वितलं सुतलं तलातलं*  
*महातलं रसातलं पातालमिति ॥७॥*

*upavarṇitaṁ bhūmer yathā-sanniveśāvasthānam avaner apy adhastāt sapta bhū-vivarā ekaikaśo yojanāyutāntareṇāyāma-vistāreṇopakḷptā atalaṁ vitalaṁ sutalaṁ talātalaṁ mahātalaṁ rasātalaṁ pātālam iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

upavarṇitam—stated previously; bhūmeḥ—of the planet earth; yathā-sanniveśa-avasthānam—according to the arrangement of the different places; avaneḥ—the earth; api—certainly; adhastāt—beneath; sapta—seven; bhū-vivarāḥ—other planets; eka-ekaśaḥ—in succession, up to the outer limit of the universe; yojana-ayuta-antareṇa—with an interval of ten thousand yojanas (eighty thousand miles); āyāma-vistāreṇa—by width and length; upakḷptāḥ—situated; atalam—named Atala; vitalam—Vitala; sutalam—Sutala; talātalam—Talātala; mahātalam—Mahātala; rasātalam—Rasātala; pātālam—Pātāla; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, beneath this earth are seven other planets, known as Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talātala, Mahātala, Rasātala and Pātāla. I have already explained the situation of the planetary systems of earth. The width and length of the seven lower planetary systems are calculated to be exactly the same as those of earth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Each one is 10,000 *yojanas* 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and wide—that is the expanse of the netherworlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The earth (entire Bhū-maṇḍala) has been described above very elaborately. Now the author proceeds to explain the status of the lokas \[planetary systems\] below the earth. Below the earth, there are seven holes. Each of the seven planetary systems is 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and equally broad and are placed one below the other. The comforts and happiness vary from one system to another and all of them are more comfortable than earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The netherworlds are placed one above the other according to the comforts they provide.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Adhastat = lower and lower. Atala and others are holes only and are 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and wide, placed one below the other.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Adhastat means in the lower and lower regions. Atala, etc. are holes only. 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] below the earth is Atala, 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] below Atala is Vitala and so on. Each of them is 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and equally wide.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Each of them is 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and wide.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The description of Bhūloka is concluded here.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The bottom of Meru Mountain has sunk 16,000 *yojanas* \[128,000 miles\] into the earth. 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] below earth means 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] below the 16,000 yojana level. Actually it will be 26,000 *yojanas* from the surface of the earth. Each of them is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] high and wide. They form part of Bhūloka as it is said in the First Canto of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam, i.e. that Bhūloka along with the netherworlds are the feet of the Virat Puruṣa \[universal form of the Lord\].

They are named Atala and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Bhūloka has been described. Even below this earth, there are seven planetary systems, each 10,000 *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] high and wide. They are seven holes in the earth known as Atala, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The seven worlds are placed according to the comfort they provide—or they are placed one above the other.

### Text 8

*एतेषु हि बिलस्वर्गेषु स्वर्गादप्यधिककामभोगैश्वर्यानन्दभूतिविभूतिभिः*  
*सुसमृद्धभवनोद्यानाक्रीडविहारेषु दैत्यदानवकाद्रवेया नित्यप्रमुदितानुरक्त*  
*कलत्रापत्यबन्धुसुहृद्अनुचरा गृहपतय ईश्वरादप्यप्रतिहतकामा मायाविनोदा*  
*निवसन्ति ॥८॥*

*eteṣu hi bila-svargeṣu svargād apy adhika-kāma-bhogaiśvaryānanda-bhūti-vibhūtibhiḥ susamṛddha-bhavanodyānākrīḍa-vihāreṣu daitya-dānava-kādraveyā nitya-pramuditānurakta-kalatrāpatya-bandhu-suhṛd-anucarā gṛha-pataya īśvarād apy apratihata-kāmā māyā-vinodā nivasanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

eteṣu—in these; hi—certainly; bila-svargeṣu—known as the heavenly subterranean worlds; svargāt—than the heavenly planets; api—even; adhika—a greater quantity; kāma-bhoga—enjoyment of sense gratification; aiśvarya-ānanda—bliss due to opulence; bhūti—influence; vibhūtibhiḥ—by those things and wealth; su-samṛddha—improved; bhavana—houses; udyāna—gardens; ākrīḍa-vihāreṣu—in places for different types of sense gratification; daitya—the demons; dānava—ghosts; kādraveyāḥ—snakes; nitya—who are always; pramudita—overjoyed; anurakta—because of attachment; kalatra—to wife; apatya—children; bandhu—family relations; suhṛt—friends; anucarāḥ—followers; gṛha-patayaḥ—the heads of the households; īśvarāt—than those more capable, like the demigods; api—even; apratihata-kāmāḥ—whose fulfillment of lusty desires is unimpeded; māyā—illusory; vinodāḥ—who feel happiness; nivasanti—live.

**Перевод:**

**In these seven planetary systems, which are also known as the subterranean heavens \[bila-svarga\], there are very beautiful houses, gardens and places of sense enjoyment, which are even more opulent than those in the higher planets because the demons have a very high standard of sensual pleasure, wealth and influence. Most of the residents of these planets, who are known as Daityas, Dānavas and Nāgas, live as householders. Their wives, children, friends and society are all fully engaged in illusory, material happiness. The sense enjoyment of the demigods is sometimes disturbed, but the residents of these planets enjoy life without disturbances. Thus they are understood to be very attached to illusory happiness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The netherworlds are generally described here. The Daityas (sons of Diti and their descendants) live there. The houses there are very prosperous and endowed with all sorts of joyous comforts. The wives love their husbands always. There is no desire not fulfilled. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The variation in comforts in these worlds is expressly stated hereafter. The demons and others live in these netherworlds whose luxury and comforts excel those in heaven. The rejoicing is also great. There are well equipped houses, parks, playgrounds, meeting places and all. The women folk are always in love with their husbands.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Samrddhi = exuberance. Vibhuti = the series of progeny. Aakrida = playing grounds. Aavihara = places where couples rejoice.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The netherworlds are generally described. Bhuti = the influence. Vibhuti = riches. Iswarat = even from Indra.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In these Bilasvargas (subterranean heavens) there are play grounds and tracks for traveling.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The general features of the netherworlds are stated. The houses are full of all sorts of desirable objects. The residents’ desires are never thwarted by universal directors (Loka-pālas) such as Indra and others. The residents are amused by their own māyā, which means the expertise of knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Tavanmatre = at a distance of 10,000 *yojanas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Bhavana = houses of common people. Prakara = compounds. Gopuram = city entrances. Sabha = a place where the king can sit. Chaitya = temple. Chataspatha = square. Aayatani = tourist abodes.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The sons of Diti, Danu and Kadri are all Kashyapa’s children.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The undergrounds are described in general in the next few verses until the verse starting from “Atalam.” Here the sons of Diti and others live, is the main construction. What sort of cities? Where houses are endowed with many comforts and luxury. Aakrida and Vihara mean places of play. There wives are always joyous. Iswarat means Śiva. There, fearlessness is due to the boon they have obtained.

### Text 9

*येषु महाराज मयेन मायाविना विनिर्मिताः पुरो नानामणिप्रवर*  
*प्रवेकविरचितविचित्रभवनप्राकारगोपुरसभाचैत्यचत्वरायतनादिभिर्नागासुरमि*  
*थुनपारावतशुकसारिकाकीर्णकृत्रिमभूमिभिर्विवरेश्वरगृहोत्तमैः समलङ्कृताश्चका*  
*सति ॥९॥*

*yeṣu mahārāja mayena māyāvinā vinirmitāḥ puro nānā-maṇi-pravara-praveka-viracita-vicitra-bhavana-prākāra-gopura-sabhā-caitya-catvarāyatanādibhir nāgāsura-mithuna-pārāvata-śuka-sārikākīrṇa-kṛtrima-bhūmibhir vivareśvara-gṛhottamaiḥ samalaṅkṛtāś cakāsati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yeṣu—in those lower planetary systems; mahā-rāja—O my dear King; mayena—by the demon named Maya; māyā-vinā—possessing advanced knowledge in the construction of material comforts; vinirmitāḥ—constructed; puraḥ—cities; nānā-maṇi-pravara—of valuable gems; praveka—with excellent; viracita—constructed; vicitra—wonderful; bhavana—houses; prākāra—walls; gopura—gates; sabhā—legislative meeting rooms; caitya—temples; catvara—schools; āyatana-ādibhiḥ—with hotels or recreation halls and so on; nāga—of living entities with snakelike bodies; asura—of demons, or godless persons; mithuna—by couples; pārāvata—pigeons; śuka—parrots; sārikā—mynas; ākīrṇa—crowded; kṛtrima—artificial; bhūmibhiḥ—possessing areas; vivara-īśvara—of the leaders of the planets; gṛha-uttamaiḥ—with first-class houses; samalaṅkṛtāḥ—decorated; cakāsati—shine magnificently.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, in the imitation heavens known as bila-svarga there is a great demon named Maya Dānava, who is an expert artist and architect. He has constructed many brilliantly decorated cities. There are many wonderful houses, walls, gates, assembly houses, temples, yards and temple compounds, as well as many hotels serving as residential quarters for foreigners. The houses for the leaders of these planets are constructed with the most valuable jewels, and they are always crowded with living entities known as Nāgas and Asuras, as well as many pigeons, parrots and similar birds. All in all, these imitation heavenly cities are most beautifully situated and attractively decorated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“And dear king, there are beautiful cities built by Maya.”

“Of what sort?”

“The houses of the serpents and Asuras have walls and floors built with the best of gems and there are many birds also. Outside, there are artificial floors and trees with bottom platforms built of stones.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

“Dear king, you need not be amused by all this, because your opulence is similar. Chaitya = temple. Ayatana = the stone (squares) construction at the bottom of a tree.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Dear king, in those worlds, the cities built by head magician Maya, shine brightly.”

“How are they?”

“Endowed with good houses of their lords, the houses are studded with precious stones of all kinds. Those places abound in parks and water spots where many birds sweetly coo.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

There are beautiful cities in those holes. *Māyā* here means capable of producing things and not illusion. The cities abound in houses built of precious stones as well as temples and trees with bottom platforms built of stones. Around the houses are artificial floors.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There, the cities are shining. What sort of cities? Built with the best among the best gems. The serpents and *asuras* \[demons\] move in pairs. Artificial floors are thronged by pairs of *paravata* and other birds. The reading “filled with various voices of birds,” nanasvara is better.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In these Bilasvargas (subterranean heavens) there are play grounds and tracks for traveling.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Dear king, there are many houses built by Māyā, who has wonderful demonic powers.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

These underground cities built by Māyā are full in splendor with houses built of the best gems and thronged by pairs of sweet singing birds.

*नीलोत्पल लोहितशतपत्रादिवनेषु कृतनिकेतनानामेकविहाराकुलमधुरविविध*  
*स्वनादिभिरिन्द्रियोत्सवैरमरलोकश्रियमतिशयितानि ॥१०॥*

*udyānāni cātitarāṁ mana-indriyānandibhiḥ kusuma-phala-stabaka-subhaga-kisalayāvanata-rucira-viṭapa-viṭapināṁ latāṅgāliṅgitānāṁ śrībhiḥ samithuna-vividha-vihaṅgama-jalāśayānām amala-jala-pūrṇānāṁ jhaṣakulollaṅghana-kṣubhita-nīra-nīraja-kumuda-kuva-laya-kahlāra-nīlotpala-lohita-śatapatrādi-vaneṣu kṛta-niketanānām eka-vihārākula-madhura-vividha-svanādibhir indriyotsavair amara-loka-śriyam atiśayitāni.*

**Пословный перевод:**

udyānāni—the gardens and parks; ca—also; atitarām—greatly; manaḥ—to the mind; indriya—and to the senses; ānandibhiḥ—which cause pleasure; kusuma—by flowers; phala—of fruits; stabaka—bunches; subhaga—very beautiful; kisalaya—new twigs; avanata—bent low; rucira—attractive; viṭapa—possessing branches; viṭapinām—of trees; latā-aṅga-āliṅgitānām—which are embraced by the limbs of creepers; śrībhiḥ—by the beauty; sa-mithuna—in pairs; vividha—varieties; vihaṅgama—frequented by birds; jala-āśayānām—of reservoirs of water; amala-jala-pūrṇānām—full of clear and transparent water; jhaṣa-kula-ullaṅghana—by the jumping of different fish; kṣubhita—agitated; nīra—in the water; nīraja—of lotus flowers; kumuda—lilies; kuvalaya—flowers named kuvalaya; kahlāra-kahlāra flowers; nīla-utpala—blue lotus flowers; lohita—red; śata-patra-ādi—lotus flowers with a hundred petals and so on; vaneṣu—in forests; kṛta-niketanānām—of birds that have made their nests; eka-vihāra-ākula—full of uninterrupted enjoyment; madhura—very sweet; vividha—varieties; svana-ādibhiḥ—by vibrations; indriya-utsavaiḥ—invoking sense enjoyment; amara-loka-śriyam—the beauty of the residential places of the demigods; atiśayitāni—surpassing.

**Перевод:**

**The parks and gardens in the artificial heavens surpass in beauty those of the upper heavenly planets. The trees in those gardens, embraced by creepers, bend with a heavy burden of twigs with fruits and flowers, and therefore they appear extraordinarily beautiful. That beauty could attract anyone and make his mind fully blossom in the pleasure of sense gratification. There are many lakes and reservoirs with clear, transparent water, agitated by jumping fish and decorated with many flowers such as lilies, kuvalayas, kahlāras and blue and red lotuses. Pairs of cakravākas and many other water birds nest in the lakes and always enjoy in a happy mood, making sweet, pleasing vibrations that are very satisfying and conducive to enjoyment of the senses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

There are parks which excel the parks of the demigods in heaven. With what luster? With the luster of flowers, sprouts and fruits. The branches of trees, embraced by creepers, are bent downwards by the weight of the fruits and flowers. The water spots are full of pairs of sweetly-cooing water birds like the cakravaka and others. The ponds are full of crystal clear waters and lotuses. Due to all these excellences, they excel the parks of the demigods. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The lakes are full of flowers, like the lotus and the like, that sway in the gentle air, when their pollen falls into the waters, making them fragrant.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The ponds are full of the purest of waters. Of what sort? Where there are water birds and fish in pairs. There are delightful flowers of various colors such as blue lotuses, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The branches of trees, are embraced by creepers, are bent downwards by the weight of the fruits and flowers. They cause delight to the eyes of those who behold them, like the womenfolk of the leaders living there. The beauty of such parks surpasses the beauty of the parks of heaven. The cities shine with such things.

*न वा एतेषु वसतां दिव्यौषधिरसरसायनान्नपानस्नानादिभिराधयो व्याधयो*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; vā—either; eteṣu—in these planets; vasatām—of those residing; divya—wonderful; auṣadhi—of herbs; rasa—the juices; rasāyana—and elixirs; anna—by eating; pāna—drinking; snāna-ādibhiḥ—by bathing in and so on; ādhayaḥ—mental troubles; vyādhayaḥ—diseases; valī—wrinkles; palita—grey hair; jarā—old age; ādayaḥ—and so on; ca—and; deha-vaivarṇya—the fading of bodily luster; daurgandhya—bad odor; sveda—perspiration; klama—fatigue; glāniḥ—lack of energy; iti—thus; vayaḥ avasthāḥ—miserable conditions due to increasing age; ca—and; bhavanti—are.

By the drinking of rasayana and bathing. Aadhi = mental diseases. Glani = lack of courage. Vayovastha = childhood, old age and so on.

Those who live there are not afflicted with physical diseases and mental illness since they consume the juice of divine herbs and the preparations made from them. Adhayah = illness (mental). Vali = wrinkles. Palitham = greying of hair. Glani = cheerlessness.

### Text 16

*अथातले मयपुत्रोऽसुरो बलो निवसति येन ह वा इह*  
*सृष्टाः षण्णवतिर्मायाः काश्चनाद्यापि मायाविनो धारयन्ति यस्य च जृम्भ*

*या वै बिलायनं प्रविष्टं पुरुषं रसेन हाटकाख्येन साधयित्वा स्वविलासा*  
*वलोकनानुरागस्मितसंलापोपगूहनादिभिः स्वैरं किल रमयन्ति*  
*यस्मिन्नुपयुक्ते पुरुष ईश्वरोऽहं सिद्धोऽहमित्ययुतमहागजबलमात्मानम*  
*भिमन्यमानः कत्थते मदान्ध इव ॥१६॥*

*athātale maya-putro 'suro balo nivasati yena ha vā iha sṛṣṭāḥ ṣaṇ-ṇavatir māyāḥ kāścanādyāpi māyāvino dhārayanti yasya ca jṛmbhamāṇasya mukhatas trayaḥ strī-gaṇā udapadyanta svairiṇyaḥ kāminyaḥ puṁścalya iti yā vai bilāyanaṁ praviṣṭaṁ puruṣaṁ rasena hāṭakākhyena sādhayitvā sva-vilāsāvalokanānurāga-smita-saṁlāpopagūhanādibhiḥ svairaṁ kila ramayanti yasminn upayukte puruṣa īśvaro 'haṁ siddho 'ham ity ayuta-mahā-gaja-balam ātmānam abhimanyamānaḥ katthate madāndha iva.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—now; atale—on the planet named Atala; maya-putraḥ asuraḥ—the demon son of Maya; balaḥ—Bala; nivasati—resides; yena—by whom; ha vā—indeed; iha—in this; sṛṣṭāḥ—propagated; ṣaṭ-ṇavatiḥ—ninety-six; māyāḥ—varieties of illusion; kāścana—some; adya api—even today; māyā-vinaḥ—those who know the art of magical feats (like manufacturing gold); dhārayanti—utilize; yasya—of whom; ca—also; jṛmbhamāṇasya—while yawning; mukhataḥ—from the mouth; trayaḥ—three; strī-gaṇāḥ—varieties of women; udapadyanta—were generated; svairiṇyaḥ—svairiṇī (one who only marries in her same class); kāminyaḥ—kāmiṇī (one who, being lusty, marries men from any group); puṁścalyaḥ—puṁścalī (one who wants to go from one husband to another); iti—thus; yāḥ—who; vai—certainly; bila-ayanam—the subterranean planets; praviṣṭam—entering; puruṣam—a male; rasena—by a juice; hāṭaka-ākhyena—made from an intoxicating herb known as hāṭaka; sādhayitvā—making sexually fit; sva-vilāsa—for their personal sense gratification; avalokana—by glances; anurāga—lustful; smita—by smiling; saṁlāpa—by talking; upagūhana-ādibhiḥ—and by embracing; svairam—according to their own desire; kila—indeed; ramayanti—enjoy sex pleasure; yasmin—which; upayukte—when used; puruṣaḥ—a man; īśvaraḥ aham—I am the most powerful person; siddhaḥ aham—I am the greatest and most elevated person; iti—thus; ayuta—ten thousand; mahā-gaja—of big elephants; balam—the strength; ātmānam—himself; abhimanyamānaḥ—being full of pride; katthate—they say; mada-andhaḥ—blinded by false prestige; iva—like.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, now I shall describe to you the lower planetary systems, one by one, beginning from Atala. In Atala there is a demon, the son of Maya Dānava named Bala, who created ninety-six kinds of mystic power. Some so-called yogīs and svāmīs take advantage of this mystic power to cheat people even today. Simply by yawning, the demon Bala created three kinds of women, known as svairiṇī, kāmiṇī and puṁścalī. The svairiṇīs like to marry men from their own group, the kāmiṇīs marry men from any group, and the puṁścalīs change husbands one after another. If a man enters the planet of Atala, these women immediately capture him and induce him to drink an intoxicating beverage made with a drug known as hāṭaka \[cannabis indica\]. This intoxicant endows the man with great sexual prowess, of which the women take advantage for enjoyment. A woman will enchant him with attractive glances, intimate words, smiles of love and then embraces. In this way she induces him to enjoy sex with her to her full satisfaction. Because of his increased sexual power, the man thinks himself stronger than ten thousand elephants and considers himself most perfect. Indeed, illusioned and intoxicated by false pride, he thinks himself God, ignoring impending death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Svairinis are those who engage with those partners of their own castes. Kaminis are those engaged with other castes also. Pumschali are women who move very quickly from man to man. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

Bilayana means the abode in the form of holes. Sadhayitva means making them capable of sex. They seduce them with all their guile, when the drink *hāṭaka* is consumed.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Having stated the general features of the holes, the particulars are being stated. Shannavati means ninety six. Those women who lose control at the very sight of a man are called Pumschali. They are absorbed in hugging and kissing.

Mahagaja is the leader of a herd of elephants. Kathate = boasts.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described all the netherworlds in general, the author sets out to describe each one vividly. He starts with Atala loka. Maya’s son, Bala, by name, lives in Atala. His attributes are stated: he is the promulgator of the 96 kinds of magic, some of which, even the present day magicians employ. When he yawned, three types of women came out from his mouth—the Svarinis, Kaminis, and Pumschalis.

The drink *hāṭaka* is described. When a person consumes it, he feels he has the strength of ten thousand direction elephants and he prattles, “I am God; I am great."

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Having described the general features of the netherworlds, from hereon the particular features of each of them is described. Bala by name. Kaschana means some of his illusions. None of them \[women\] are under the rule of a husband. They seduce men by hugging and kissing them.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Svairiṇyaḥ* = acting according to their own will. *Kāminyaḥ* = lusty always. *Puṁścalyaḥ* = moving from man to man, shameless.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The classification of the three types of women is given.

When they consume the juice called *hāṭaka*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Now the holes are described individually, starting with Atala. Of the ninety six tricks of magic he promulgated, some are used by the present day magicians. As Bala yawned, three types of women came out of his mouth.

The women make the men who enter there drink the *hāṭaka* juice. When a person consumes it, he feels he has the strength of ten thousand direction elephants and he prattles, “I am God; I am great."

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

These three types of women do not show loyalty to any one man—they seduce all men who enter there.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Having described generally, now they are described individually. As Bala yawns, three types of bad women come out of his mouth.

### Text 17

*ततोऽधस्ताद्वितले हरो भगवान्हाटकेश्वरः स्वपार्षदभूतगणावृतः*  
*प्रजापतिसर्गोपबृंहणाय भवो भवान्या सह मिथुनीभूत आस्ते यतः*  
*प्रवृत्ता सरित्प्रवरा हाटकी नाम भवयोर्वीर्येण यत्र*  
*चित्रभानुर्मातरिश्वना समिध्यमान ओजसा पिबति तन्निष्ठ्यूतं*  
*हाटकाख्यं सुवर्णं भूषणेनासुरेन्द्रावरोधेषु पुरुषाः सह पुरुषीभिर्धारयन्ति*  
*॥१७॥*

*tato 'dhastād vitale haro bhagavān hāṭakeśvaraḥ sva-pārṣada-bhūta-gaṇāvṛtaḥ prajāpati-sargopabṛṁhaṇāya bhavo bhavānyā saha mithunī-bhūta āste yataḥ pravṛttā sarit-pravarā hāṭakī nāma bhavayor vīryeṇa yatra citrabhānur mātariśvanā samidhyamāna ojasā pibati tan niṣṭhyūtaṁ hāṭakākhyaṁ suvarṇaṁ bhūṣaṇenāsurendrāvarodheṣu puruṣāḥ saha puruṣībhir dhārayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—the planet Atala; adhastāt—beneath; vitale—on the planet; haraḥ—Lord Śiva; bhagavān—the most powerful personality; hāṭakeśvaraḥ—the master of gold; sva-pārṣada—by his own associates; bhūta-gaṇa—who are ghostly living beings; āvṛtaḥ—surrounded; prajāpati-sarga—of the creation of Lord Brahmā; upabṛṁhaṇāya—to increase the population; bhavaḥ—Lord Śiva; bhavānyā saha—with his wife, Bhavānī; mithunī-bhūtaḥ—being united in sex; āste—remains; yataḥ—from that planet (Vitala); pravṛttā—being emanated; sarit-pravarā—the great river; hāṭakī—Hāṭakī; nāma—named; bhavayoḥ vīryeṇa—due to the semina and ovum of Lord Śiva and Bhavānī; yatra—where; citra-bhānuḥ—the fire-god; mātariśvanā—by the wind; samidhyamānaḥ—being brightly inflamed; ojasā—with great strength; pibati—drinks; tat—that; niṣṭhyūtam—spit out with a hissing sound; hāṭaka-ākhyam—named Hāṭaka; suvarṇam—gold; bhūṣaṇena—by different types of ornaments; asura-indra—of the great asuras; avarodheṣu—in the homes; puruṣāḥ—the males; saha—with; puruṣībhiḥ—their wives and women; dhārayanti—wear.

**Перевод:**

**The next planet below Atala is Vitala, wherein Lord Śiva, who is known as the master of gold mines, lives with his personal associates, the ghosts and similar living entities. Lord Śiva, as the progenitor, engages in sex with Bhavānī, the progenitress, to produce living entities, and from the mixture of their vital fluid the river named Hāṭakī is generated. When fire, being made to blaze by the wind, drinks of this river and then sizzles and spits it out, it produces gold called Hāṭaka. The demons who live on that planet with their wives decorate themselves with various ornaments made from that gold, and thus they live there very happily.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Bhavayoḥ* means of Śiva and Parvatī. *Citrabhānu* means Agni—blown and discarded by Agni. *Avarodha* means harem. *Puruṣī* means women.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

After Atala, Vitala is described as below Atala. Śiva lives with his divine consort Parvatī. They are engaged in sex for the furtherance of Brahmā’s creation. He is called Hatakeswara, because he is the producer of *hāṭaka*, a type of gold. The vital fluids of the celestial pair flow in the form of the river *hāṭaka*. With the help of Vāyu, Agni burns and blows the waters of this river producing the gold *hāṭaka*. The men and women who live in Atala make ornaments with this gold and wear it on their person.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Yasmin* = the juice. *Bavayoḥ* = of Śiva and Parvatī. *Edhyamāno* = becomes increased. *Avarodha* = the harem, women’s apartment. *Puruṣī* = women having the strength of men.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pumsavana means fetus. Agni makes it hard so that it can be converted into an ornament studded with gems. People wear it with utmost pleasure.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Śiva and Parvatī are engaged in union for furthering the creation of Brahmā. Pibathi means makes it hard. Heated and blown by Agni.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Bhavayoh = of Śiva and Pārvatī. Kindled by the wind blown by Agni. Wear in the form of ornaments.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

In Vitala, below Atala, Śiva Hatakeswara, by name, lives with his attendants. He is engages in union with Parvatī for furthering the creation of Brahmā. He is called Hatakeswara, because he is responsible for the genesis of a particular type of gold called *hāṭaka*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Chitrabhanu is fire. Getting kindled with the assistance of Vāyu, he converts it into gold which both men and women wear on their person.

### Text 18

*ततोऽधस्तात्सुतले उदारश्रवाः पुण्यश्लोको विरोचनात्मजो*  
*बलिर्भगवता महेन्द्रस्य प्रियं चिकीर्षमाणेनादितेर्लब्धकायो भूत्वा*  
*वटुवामनरूपेण पराक्षिप्तलोकत्रयो भगवदनुकम्पयैव पुनः प्रवेशित*  
*इन्द्रादिष्वविद्यमानया सुसमृद्धया श्रियाभिजुष्टः स्वधर्मेणाराधयंस्तमेव*  
*भगवन्तमाराधनीयमपगतसाध्वस आस्तेऽधुनापि ॥१८॥*

*tato 'dhastāt sutale udāra-śravāḥ puṇya-śloko virocanātmajo balir bhagavatā mahendrasya priyaṁ cikīrṣamāṇenāditer labdha-kāyo bhūtvā vaṭu-vāmana-rūpeṇa parākṣipta-loka-trayo bhagavad-anukampayaiva punaḥ praveśita indrādiṣv avidyamānayā susamṛddhayā śriyābhijuṣṭaḥ sva-dharmeṇārādhayaṁs tam eva bhagavantam ārādhanīyam apagata-sādhvasa āste 'dhunāpi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ adhastāt—beneath the planet known as Vitala; sutale—on the planet known as Sutala; udāra-śravāḥ—very greatly celebrated; puṇya-ślokaḥ—very pious and advanced in spiritual consciousness; virocana-ātmajaḥ—the son of Virocana; baliḥ—Bali Mahārāja; bhagavatā—by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; mahā-indrasya—of the King of heaven, Indra; priyam—the welfare; cikīrṣamāṇena—desiring to perform; āditeḥ—from Aditi; labdha-kāyaḥ—having obtained His body; bhūtvā—appearing; vaṭu—brahmacāri; vāmana-rūpeṇa—in the form of a dwarf; parākṣipta—wrested away; loka-trayaḥ—the three worlds; bhagavat-anukampayā—by the causeless mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva—certainly; punaḥ—again; praveśitaḥ—caused to enter; indra-ādiṣu—even among the demigods like the King of heaven; avidyamānayā—not existing; susamṛddhayā—much enriched by such exalted opulence; śriyā—by good fortune; abhijuṣṭaḥ—being blessed; sva-dharmeṇa—by discharging devotional service; ārādhayan—worshiping; tam—Him; eva—certainly; bhagavantam—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ārādhanīyam—who is most worshipable; apagata-sādhvasaḥ—without fear; āste—remains; adhunā api—even today.

**Перевод:**

**Below the planet Vitala is another planet, known as Sutala, where the great son of Mahārāja Virocana, Bali Mahārāja, who is celebrated as the most pious king, resides even now. For the welfare of Indra, the King of heaven, Lord Viṣṇu appeared in the form of a dwarf brahmacārī as the son of Aditi and tricked Bali Mahārāja by begging for only three paces of land but taking all the three worlds. Being very pleased with Bali Mahārāja for giving all his possessions, the Lord returned his kingdom and made him richer than the opulent King Indra. Even now, Bali Mahārāja engages in devotional service by worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead in the planet of Sutala.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Even now Bali is in Sutala. How? He formerly lost his three planetary systems because Lord Hari was desirous of doing good to Indra. Then, Bali was made to enter Sutala by the compassion of God, who was born of Aditi and took a small form.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Now Sutala is described. Tatah means in Sutala, which is below Vitala. Urushrava = famous. puṇya shloka = whose fame brings auspiciousness to those who remember him.

Living there is Virochana’s son Bali who one of the greatest devotees. How is he? Fearlessly worshipping the same Viṣṇu, born of Adithi in the form of a small *brāhmaṇa* boy, by whose compassion, Bali was made to enter Sutala, where the luxury and joys exceed those in Indra loka. This boy robbed him of his kingdom and threw him in a corner. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*Īśvarat* = from the competent also.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Śrava* means fame. Whose fame deserves to be sung in songs. He was made to enter Sutala, is what is understood.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tataḥ* = from Vitala. *Śrava* = fame. Puṇya śloka means whose praise is auspicious. Apagata Sadhvasa means devoid of fear.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Their ability is described. Bilayanam = the place of the hole. When the juice is consumed. The vital fluids of Śiva and Parvatī.

### Text 19

*नो एवैतत्साक्षात्कारो भूमिदानस्य यत्तद्भगवत्यशेषजीवनिकायानां जीव*  
*भूतात्मभूते परमात्मनि वासुदेवे तीर्थतमे पात्र उपपन्ने परया श्रद्धया*  
*परमादरसमाहितमनसा सम्प्रतिपादितस्य साक्षादपवर्गद्वारस्य*  
*यद्बिलनिलयैश्वर्यम् ॥१९॥*

*no evaitat sākṣātkāro bhūmi-dānasya yat tad bhagavaty aśeṣa-jīva-nikāyānāṁ jīva-bhūtātma-bhūte paramātmani vāsudeve tīrthatame pātra upapanne parayā śraddhayā paramādara-samāhita-manasā sampratipāditasya sākṣād apavarga-dvārasya yad bila-nilayaiśvaryam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

no—not; eva—indeed; etat—this; sākṣātkāraḥ—the direct result; bhūmi-dānasya—of contribution of land; yat—which; tat—that; bhagavati—unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; aśeṣa-jīva-nikāyānām—of unlimited numbers of living entities; jīva-bhūta-ātma-bhūte—who is the life and the Supersoul; parama-ātmani—the supreme regulator; vāsudeve—Lord Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa); tīrtha-tame—who is the best of all places of pilgrimage; pātre—the most worthy recipient; upapanne—having approached; parayā—by the topmost; śraddhayā—faith; parama-ādara—with great respect; samāhita-manasā—with an attentive mind; sampratipāditasya—which was given; sākṣāt—directly; apavarga-dvārasya—the gate of liberation; yat—which; bila-nilaya—of bila-svarga, the imitation heavenly planets; aiśvaryam—the opulence.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, Bali Mahārāja donated all his possessions to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāmanadeva, but one should certainly not conclude that he achieved his great worldly opulence in bila-svarga as a result of his charitable disposition. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the source of life for all living entities, lives within everyone as the friendly Supersoul, and under His direction a living entity enjoys or suffers in the material world. Greatly appreciating the transcendental qualities of the Lord, Bali Mahārāja offered everything at His lotus feet. His purpose, however, was not to gain anything material, but to become a pure devotee. For a pure devotee, the door of liberation is automatically opened. One should not think that Bali Mahārāja was given so much material opulence merely because of his charity. When one becomes a pure devotee in love, he may also be blessed with a good material position by the will of the Supreme Lord. However, one should not mistakenly think that the material opulence of a devotee is the result of his devotional service. The real result of devotional service is the awakening of pure love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, which continues under all circumstances.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Some think that his reign over Sutala is the result of his gifting away the earth to Vamana. It is refuted here. The rule of Sutala is not the fruit of the gift. That gift was capable of awarding liberation to its giver because it was given to the best possible candidate, i.e. God, who is the soul of all living entities. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya, and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The *Vedas* say that even a piece of land given to a Vedic scholar is said to bring infinite piety.

The best of eligible candidates, *saksat* Vāsudeva.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Here the word “*bhūmi*” indicates the “three worlds.” The reign of Sutala does not match the gift he has made. Only liberation would be the proper reward. The incidental lordship of Sutala is endowed with comforts excelling heaven. Paramātmā is the antaryāmī of the *jīva*. The gift is given to him. When even the offering of flowers \[to God\] is capable of granting liberation, what should be said if one devoutly offers the three worlds?

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Considering the stature of Vamana, how could this trifle \[receiving Sutala\] be a reward to the gift offered with utmost devotion and humbleness?

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

“Why not accept the rulership of the three worlds that is going to be offered in the next Manvantara, as the main reward of this gift?” The reply is: “Ruling for a period of a Manvantara is trivial compared to the infiniteness of time.” God gives him a reward that is not consumed by time and that is the excessive bliss in liberation.

### Text 20

*यस्य ह वाव क्षुतपतनप्रस्खलनादिषु विवशः सकृन्नामाभिगृणन् पुरुषः*  
*कर्मबन्धनमञ्जसा विधुनोति यस्य हैव प्रतिबाधनं मुमुक्षवोऽन्यथैवोपलभन्ते*  
*॥२०॥*

*yasya ha vāva kṣuta-patana-praskhalanādiṣu vivaśaḥ sakṛn nāmābhigṛṇan puruṣaḥ karma-bandhanam añjasā vidhunoti yasya haiva pratibādhanaṁ mumukṣavo 'nyathaivopalabhante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom; ha vāva—indeed; kṣuta—when in hunger; patana—falling down; praskhalana-ādiṣu—stumbling and so on; vivaśaḥ—being helpless; sakṛt—once; nāma abhigṛṇan—chanting the holy name of the Lord; puruṣaḥ—a person; karma-bandhanam—the bondage of fruitive activity; añjasā—completely; vidhunoti—washes away; yasya—of which; ha—certainly; eva—in this way; pratibādhanam—the repulsion; mumukṣavaḥ—persons desiring liberation; anyathā—otherwise; eva—certainly; upalabhante—are trying to realize.

**Перевод:**

**If one who is embarrassed by hunger or who falls down or stumbles chants the holy name of the Lord even once, willingly or unwillingly, he is immediately freed from the reactions of his past deeds. Karmīs entangled in material activities face many difficulties in the practice of mystic yoga and other endeavors to achieve that same freedom.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By accidentally uttering the holy name while sneezing or yawning, etc., one gets freedom from the bondage of material reactions. The people aspiring for salvation, normally take a different course of *yoga*, sankhya, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*No eva eta* = it is not only this much.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What to speak of gifting the three worlds or offering flowers—it is said here that even repeating the name will suffice to remove all the bondage for His devotees. Those who chant His name, cast off their bondage effortlessly. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

Not merely the people who give in charity, also those aspiring for liberation take to the *aṣṭāṅga-yoga* \[eight-fold mystic path\] of yama, niyama and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Even the chanting of His name during illness and other things will suffice to bring one liberation. Such being the case, discarding the effortless course, the Mimamsakas and Patanjalas follow a difficult course of knowledge and practices. Truly they are befooled. It is said in Gītā, “wicked people, devoid of knowledge, do not attain Me. However, we are the servants of the Lord who has preached to us, “Engage your mind always in thinking of Me, become My devotee, offer obeisances to Me and worship Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

If God’s name is so great, why do all people not attain liberation? The reply is, “God did not bless the humans so much in so far as they only crave for the riches and not for His grace.” This is a general statement and there are exceptions. God’s grace is the only means to salvation and all humans are not after it.

### Text 21

*तद्भक्तानामात्मवतां सर्वेषामात्मन्यात्मद आत्मतयैव ॥२१॥*

*tad bhaktānām ātmavatāṁ sarveṣām ātmany ātmada ātmatayaiva.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat—that; bhaktānām—of great devotees; ātma-vatām—of self-realized persons like Sanaka and Sanātana; sarveṣām—of all; ātmani—to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the soul; ātma-de—who gives Himself without hesitation; ātmatayā—who is the Supreme Soul, Paramātmā; eva—indeed.

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in everyone's heart as the Supersoul, sells Himself to His devotees such as Nārada Muni. In other words, the Lord gives pure love to such devotees and gives Himself to those who love Him purely. Great, self-realized mystic yogīs such as the four Kumāras also derive great transcendental bliss from realizing the Supersoul within themselves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The gift was given to God, who gives knowledge to his devotees, as one’s own *ātmā*. So the rule of Sutala is not its fruit. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

*Karma-yoga* produces devotion to God and removes the reactions to past and future sins which are obstacles to obtaining His grace.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Urushrava means that he had listened to many scriptures glorifying God. The kingdom of Sutala is not a reward to the gift of three worlds. It has come to him as an effect of his former good deeds. The gift he made to God, the Lord of all living entities, is responsible to bring blissful liberation. There could not have been a more holy and deserving candidate for the gift. The gift was given with utmost humbleness and not haughtiness. Even the chanting of god’s name removes one’s sins. Good deeds are responsible for the cleansing of the mind and ultimately the meeting of God. Even the chanting of his name is like that. He is the giver of liberation to His devotees.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

So, it is not the reward. What sort of candidate? One who gives Himself to His devotees such as Nārada and others thereby increasing their transcendental bliss. Thus a gift of sensuous objects was not His intention which was proved by His choosing to become the door keeper of Bali.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is not the reward of the gift. This construction should thus be taken backwards. Gifted to him, who gives himself to his devotees, and is of the nature of god-experience to yogis like Sanaka and others. By these two epithets the bliss of love and the bliss of experience are stated. For him who gives these two, how can the pleasure derived from external objects be worthy? He gave the bliss of love to Bali by becoming his door keeper.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

This is a continuation of the previous verse. The kingdom of Sutala is not the reward for such a gift from one endowed with devotion, renunciation and other virtues such as knowing everything about creation, destruction, etc.

### Text 22

*न वै भगवान्नूनममुष्यानुजग्राह यदुत पुनरात्मानुस्मृतिमोषणं मायामय*  
*भोगैश्वर्यमेवातनुतेति ॥२२॥*

*na vai bhagavān nūnam amuṣyānujagrāha yad uta punar ātmānusmṛti-moṣaṇaṁ māyāmaya-bhogaiśvaryam evātanuteti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; vai—indeed; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; nūnam—certainly; amuṣya—unto Bali Mahārāja; anujagrāha—showed His favor; yat—because; uta—certainly; punaḥ—again; ātma-anusmṛti—of remembrance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; moṣaṇam—which robs one; māyā-maya—an attribute of Māyā; bhoga-aiśvaryam—the material opulence; eva—certainly; ātanuta—extended; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead did not award His mercy to Bali Mahārāja by giving him material happiness and opulence, for these make one forget loving service to the Lord. The result of material opulence is that one can no longer absorb his mind in the Supreme Personality of Godhead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is stated here that rather than being a reward of compassion, instead such a gift is an impediment to spiritual progress because it robs one of the memory of God. It is said, “for he whose mind is fixed in Vāsudeva during chanting (*japa*), offering sacrifice (*homa*) and worship, the reign of heaven, etc. are just impediments.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

If the gift given by Bali was capable of bringing liberation, or if Bali was a very great devotee, or if God was highly pleased, why did He not give salvation to Bali? The answer to this question is that *prarabdha karma* \[effects of sinful activities already committed\] cannot be washed off—one has to either enjoy or suffer them. The lordship of Sutala was a result of Bali’s previous actions. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

It is Bali’s devotion only which is responsible for the luxury he is in. When everything was snatched away from him and he was put in a prison-like cave, Bali did not begrudge Hari.
