This verse explains that such devotion cannot be seen in human beings. Begging was just a pretext to take away all of Bali’s belongings thus leaving him with only his body. When Bali was not allowed to go out of the cave without fulfilling his promise, Bali said the following words, “Even at the cost of life, I will not forsake my devotion to God.” Thus it is said that Hari did not bless humans as much as he did Bali.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

His gift was not with the intention of any other reward. He is the soul of all living entities. The *jñānīs* \[impersonalists seeking knowledge\] think about identity more than the common people. He gives Himself to His devotees. This trifle cannot be a reward to what Bali did. God did not bless Indra, but rather blessed Bali—not by riches but by His presence.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Actually, luxury is an impediment to devotion, thus luxury is not a reward of God’s grace. Indra did not have that devotion, because of his association with luxury, so God did not bless Indra, but blessed only Bali.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Indra is not as great a devotee as Bali. To Indra, God gave the three worlds, but to Bali He gave Himself. The comforts of heaven are impediments to God’s grace.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Although obtained by God’s compassion, the luxury of Sutala is just an impediment to Bali’s devotion. Hari did not bless him well because He gave comforts which allure the person who enjoys them and which spoil the memory of the Lord. This is stated in the *Parasara Smrti*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Only God realization is responsible for liberation. How can chanting of his name beget liberation? The reply is, chanting leads to God realization, which in turn leads to liberation. Liberation has two aspects—becoming free from reactions to *karma* and attaining bliss. Chanting of God’s name is responsible for both, although gradually.

### Text 23

*यत्तद्भगवतानधिगतान्योपायेन याच्ञाच्छलेनापहृतस्वशरीरावशेषितलोकत्रयो*  
*वरुणपाशैश्च सम्प्रतिमुक्तो गिरिदर्यां चापविद्ध इति होवाच ॥२३॥*

*yat tad bhagavatānadhigatānyopāyena yācñā-cchalenāpahṛta-sva-śarīrāvaśeṣita-loka-trayo varuṇa-pāśaiś ca sampratimukto giri-daryāṁ cāpaviddha iti hovāca.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—which; tat—that; bhagavatā—by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anadhigata-anya-upāyena—who is not perceived by other means; yācñā-chalena—by a trick of begging; apahṛta—taken away; sva-śarīra-avaśeṣita—with only his own body remaining; loka-trayaḥ—the three worlds; varuṇa-pāśaiḥ—by the ropes of Varuṇa; ca—and; sampratimuktaḥ—completely bound; giri-daryām—in a cave in a mountain; ca—and; apaviddhaḥ—being detained; iti—thus; ha—indeed; uvāca—said.

**Перевод:**

**When the Supreme Personality of Godhead could see no other means of taking everything away from Bali Mahārāja, He adopted the trick of begging from him and took away all the three worlds. Thus only his body was left, but the Lord was still not satisfied. He arrested Bali Mahārāja, bound him with the ropes of Varuṇa and threw him in a cave in a mountain. Nevertheless, although all his property was taken and he was thrown into a cave, Bali Mahārāja was such a great devotee that he spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Bali’s undivided devotion is stated in detail here. In what condition? Having no other recourse, God resorted to begging thus leaving Bali only with his body as a possession. Bali was tied by ropes and tossed in a corner. Bali spoke the following words: \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara, Vīrarāghava, Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It was said he was a *mahābhāgavata*, meaning he did not want anything except the service of God.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Bali’s own words are stated in the next five verses.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bali’s devotion and God’s grace can be known through Bali’s words. Having no other recourse, Vamana had to beg Bali. Pratimuktha = bounded. Apavidha = tossed aside.

### Text 24

*नूनं बतायं भगवानर्थेषु न निष्णातो योऽसाविन्द्रो यस्य सचिवो*  
*मन्त्राय वृत एकान्ततो बृहस्पतिस्तमतिहाय स्वयमुपेन्द्रेणात्मानमयाच*  
*तात्मनश्चाशिषो नो एव तद्दास्यमतिगम्भीरवयसः कालस्य मन्वन्तर*  
*परिवृत्तं कियल्लोकत्रयमिदम् ॥२४॥*

*nūnaṁ batāyaṁ bhagavān artheṣu na niṣṇāto yo 'sāv indro yasya sacivo mantrāya vṛta ekāntato bṛhaspatis tam atihāya svayam upendreṇātmānam ayācatātmanaś cāśiṣo no eva tad-dāsyam ati-gambhīra-vayasaḥ kālasya manvantara-parivṛttaṁ kiyal loka-trayam idam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

nūnam—certainly; bata—alas; ayam—this; bhagavān—very learned; artheṣu—in self-interest; na—not; niṣṇātaḥ—very experienced; yaḥ—who; asau—the King of heaven; indraḥ—Indra; yasya—of whom; sacivaḥ—the prime minister; mantrāya—for giving instructions; vṛtaḥ—chosen; ekāntataḥ—alone; bṛhaspatiḥ—named Bṛhaspati; tam—him; atihāya—ignoring; svayam—personally; upendreṇa—by means of Upendra (Lord Vāmanadeva); ātmānam—myself; ayācata—requested; ātmanaḥ—for himself; ca—and; āśiṣaḥ—blessings (the three worlds); no—not; eva—certainly; tat-dāsyam—the loving service of the Lord; ati—very; gambhīra-vayasaḥ—having an insurmountable duration; kālasya—of time; manvantara-parivṛttam—changed by the end of a life of a Manu; kiyat—what is the value of; loka-trayam—three worlds; idam—these.

**Перевод:**

**Alas, how pitiable it is for Indra, the King of heaven, that although he is very learned and powerful and although he chose Bṛhaspati as his prime minister to instruct him, he is completely ignorant concerning spiritual advancement. Bṛhaspati is also unintelligent because he did not properly instruct his disciple Indra. Lord Vāmanadeva was standing at Indra's door, but King Indra, instead of begging Him for an opportunity to render transcendental loving service, engaged Him in asking me for alms to gain the three worlds for his sense gratification. Sovereignty over the three worlds is very insignificant because whatever material opulence one may possess lasts only for an age of Manu, which is but a tiny fraction of endless time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“The venerable Brhaspati whom the knowledgeable Indra has chosen as his advisor, is not really an expert in so far as Indra had to leave him and beg Me through Upendra \[the incarnation of Vamanadeva\].” Having pleased God, one should only choose God and not the three worlds, because the latter is a trifle. What are the three worlds, which vanish at the end of a Manu in comparison to infinite time, which moves on forever? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya, and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Brhaspati was not really intelligent. Had he been so, he would have told Indra the right thing to do. Why did Indra not beg himself? Why did he make his master beg on his behalf? Even then, he begged the comforts of the three worlds only and not the service of God. Indra is really infatuated. Why did he not send Brhaspati to beg on his behalf? Even then, I \[Bali\] would have given the three worlds to him. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Indra discarded Vamana who was Himself the highest goal and made Him his messenger and asked me \[Bali\] for the three worlds, which is a trifle compared to the invaluable Vamana.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Even as Indra was conferring with his intelligent minister Brhaspati about entering into a compromise with me, God, astute as He is and desirous of blessing me with servitude, came to me in the form of a *brāhmaṇa* boy. Thus I was begged by Him although I am myself the beggar and He is the master. This is the idea contained in Bali’s words. “What are these three worlds compared to the fourteen worlds which are also very transitory? He blessed me by snatching away my kingdom, lest I should grow haughty and forsake His service. God snatches away the riches from any one whom He wants to bless.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He discarded Upendra \[God, Vamana\] and begged a tiny creature like me for the three worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Bata means it is a pity. Although Indra knows many things, he is not wise because, seeing no other recourse, he made Vamana beg the three worlds from me. Indra should have begged Vamana for nothing but His servitude. However, since he did not do that, he is not wise. These three worlds, transient as they are, lasting till the end of a Manvantara, are only a trifle compared to infinite time.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The word *bata* is used in the sense of relishing—i.e. the words of Bali are highly relishable to any devotee of Hari.

### Text 25

*यस्यानुदास्यमेवास्मत्पितामहः किल वव्रे न तु स्वपित्र्यं यदुताकुतोभयं*  
*पदं दीयमानं भगवतः परमिति भगवतोपरते खलु स्वपितरि ॥२५॥*

*yasyānudāsyam evāsmat-pitāmahaḥ kila vavre na tu sva-pitryaṁ yad utākutobhayaṁ padaṁ dīyamānaṁ bhagavataḥ param iti bhagavatoparate khalu sva-pitari.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); anudāsyam—the service; eva—certainly; asmat—our; pitā-mahaḥ—grandfather; kila—indeed; vavre—accepted; na—not; tu—but; sva—own; pitryam—paternal property; yat—which; uta—certainly; akutaḥ-bhayam—fearlessness; padam—position; dīyamānam—being offered; bhagavataḥ—than the Supreme Personality of Godhead; param—other; iti—thus; bhagavatā—by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; uparate—when killed; khalu—indeed; sva-pitari—his own father.

**Перевод:**

**Bali Mahārāja said: My grandfather Prahlāda Mahārāja is the only person who understood his own self-interest. Upon the death of Prahlāda's father, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva wanted to offer Prahlāda his father's kingdom and even wanted to grant him liberation from material bondage, but Prahlāda accepted neither. Liberation and material opulence, he thought, are obstacles to devotional service, and therefore such gifts from the Supreme Personality of Godhead are not His actual mercy. Consequently, instead of accepting the results of karma and jñāna, Prahlāda Mahārāja simply begged the Lord for engagement in the service of His servant.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Prahlāda is the only intelligent person, Bali says. After the death of his father, when God offered him the kingdom, he did not accept it because the kingdom was no good. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

My grandfather Prahlāda is the only intelligent one. The reason—he desired only the servitude of the servants of God. When his father was killed by Nṛsiṁha, he did not long for his father’s kingdom, but wanted only the service of the Lord. The reason for that is told—the kingdom is small and bound by time, whereas God is infinite and assures fearlessness for His servants. He wanted liberation at the end of life. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Prahlāda did not choose the kingdom, nor did he choose fearless liberation. He chose only the servitude of God’s servants.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In the entire world, Prahlāda is the most intelligent, says Bali here.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Prahlāda only begged for the servitude of God’s servants because attachment to a kingdom spoils love of God.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Indra had engaged Brhaspati to enter into a compromise with me. But Vamana set him aside and himself begged me, an unworthy person, for the sake of Indra. Why for the sake of Indra and not for Himself? Because He is Aptakama \[in need of nothing\].

### Text 26

*तस्य महानुभावस्यानुपथममृजितकषायः को वास्मद्विधः परिहीणभगवदनुग्रह*  
*उपजिगमिषतीति ॥२६॥*

*tasya mahānubhāvasyānupatham amṛjita-kaṣāyaḥ ko vāsmad-vidhaḥ parihīṇa-bhagavad-anugraha upajigamiṣatīti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasya—of Prahlāda Mahārāja; mahā-anubhāvasya—who was an exalted devotee; anupatham—the path; amṛjita-kaṣāyaḥ—a person who is materially contaminated; kaḥ—what; vā—or; asmat-vidhaḥ—like us; parihīṇa-bhagavat-anugrahaḥ—being without the favor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; upajigamiṣati—desires to follow; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**Bali Mahārāja said: Persons like us, who are still attached to material enjoyment, who are contaminated by the modes of material nature and who lack the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, cannot follow the supreme path of Prahlāda Mahārāja, the exalted devotee of the Lord.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Someone may ask, “You are a great hero yourself. Why do you respect him \[Prahlāda Mahārāja\] so much?” Bali gives the reply, “How can anyone whose dirty material desires are not washed off, and who has not received the grace of God, ever expect to tread the path of Prahlāda?” Tasyanupatha means following his path.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It is said here, “Who can attain his \[Prahlāda’s\] path. How can a fly follow the path of Garuḍa \[the giant eagle carrier of Viṣṇu\]? Anyone whose shackles of *karma* are not shattered and who is not subject to the grace of God, like myself, can never even dream to follow the footsteps of that great soul, my grandfather.” \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Only Prahlāda, my grandfather, reads Hari’s mind correctly. After his father was slain, when he was offered a carefree kingdom, he refused and chose only God’s servitude. There is a vast difference between Prahlāda and people like us. One who is not free from desires and is not blessed by God, can even dream of treading the path chosen by Prahlāda.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

If it be suggested that, “You are also like Prahlāda,” Bali refutes very humbly and shyly. Anupatha means a similar path.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

An objection is raised and replied. No such things for Prahlāda.

### Text 27

*तस्यानुचरित मुपरिष्टाद्विस्तरिष्यते यस्य भगवान्स्वयमखिलजगद्गुरुर्नारायणो*  
*द्वारि गदापाणिरवतिष्ठते निजजनानुकम्पितहृदयो येनाङ्गुष्ठेन पदा दशकन्धरो*  
*योजनायुतायुतं दिग्विजय उच्चाटितः ॥२७॥*

*tasyānucaritam upariṣṭād vistariṣyate yasya bhagavān svayam akhila-jagad-gurur nārāyaṇo dvāri gadā-pāṇir avatiṣṭhate nija-janānukampita-hṛdayo yenāṅguṣṭhena padā daśa-kandharo yojanāyutāyutaṁ dig-vijaya uccāṭitaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasya—of Bali Mahārāja; anucaritam—the narration; upariṣṭāt—later (in the Eighth Canto); vistariṣyate—will be explained; yasya—of whom; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svayam—personally; akhila-jagat-guruḥ—the master of all the three worlds; nārāyaṇaḥ—the Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa Himself; dvāri—at the gate; gadā-pāṇiḥ—bearing the club in His hand; avatiṣṭhate—stands; nija-jana-anukampita-hṛdayaḥ—whose heart is always filled with mercy for His devotees; yena—by whom; aṅguṣṭhena—by the big toe; padā—of His foot; daśa-kandharaḥ—Rāvaṇa, who had ten heads; yojana-ayuta-ayutam—a distance of eighty thousand miles; dik-vijaye—for the purpose of gaining victory over Bali Mahārāja; uccāṭitaḥ—driven away.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: My dear King, how shall I glorify the character of Bali Mahārāja? The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the master of the three worlds, who is most compassionate to His own devotee, stands with club in hand at Bali Mahārāja's door. When Rāvaṇa, the powerful demon, came to gain victory over Bali Mahārāja, Vāmanadeva kicked him a distance of eighty thousand miles with His big toe. I shall explain the character and activities of Bali Mahārāja later \[in the Eighth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

If it were asked, “Then why not narrate the story of Bali now?” The reply is, “We will narrate it later.” At whose door Viṣṇu stays out of compassion for His devotees. After all, Viṣṇu kicked Rāvaṇa a long distance. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha, Śukadeva and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

If it were asked, “Then why not narrate the story of Bali now?” The reply is, “It will be done in the eighth canto of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*.” Bali’s greatness cannot be completely told in a few words. Because the master of the worlds, who does not deserve to become the servant of anyone, became Bali’s doorkeeper holding a mace in His hand. Once, when Rāvaṇa went there during his conquest, Vamana kicked him a very long distance. This story is famous in *Rāmayana* and other *Purāṇas*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

26-27 Parihina = extremely bereft of. And he who is not a receptacle of God’s grace.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tasya = of Bali.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The story told in *Vālmīki Rāmayana* is slightly different. It belongs to another *kalpa* and hence the difference.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Bali lives in Sutala even now. How? Initially his three worlds were snatched away by Hari. Later, he was permitted entry into Sutala by God, who was born of Aditi in the form of a *brāhmaṇa* boy.

### Text 28

*ततोऽधस्तात्तलातले मयो नाम दानवेन्द्रस्त्रिपुराधिपतिर्भगवता*  
*पुरारिणा त्रिलोकीशं चिकीर्षुणा निर्दग्धस्वपुरत्रयस्तत्प्रसादाल्लब्धपदो*  
*मायाविनामाचार्यो महादेवेन परिरक्षितो विगतसुदर्शनभयो महीयते ॥२८॥*

*tato 'dhastāt talātale mayo nāma dānavendras tri-purādhipatir bhagavatā purāriṇā tri-lokī-śaṁ cikīrṣuṇā nirdagdha-sva-pura-trayas tat-prasādāl labdha-pado māyāvinām ācāryo mahādevena parirakṣito vigata-sudarśana-bhayo mahīyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—the planet known as Sutala; adhastāt—below; talātale—in the planet known as Talātala; mayaḥ—Maya; nāma—named; dānava-indraḥ—the king of the Dānava demons; tri-pura-adhipatiḥ—the Lord of the three cities; bhagavatā—by the most powerful; purāriṇā—Lord Śiva, who is known as Tripurāri; tri-lokī—of the three worlds; śam—the good fortune; cikīrṣuṇā—who was desiring; nirdagdha—burned; sva-pura-trayaḥ—whose three cities; tat-prasādāt—by Lord Śiva's mercy; labdha—obtained; padaḥ—a kingdom; māyā-vinām ācāryaḥ—who is the ācārya, or master, of all the conjurers; mahā-devena—by Lord Śiva; parirakṣitaḥ—protected; vigata-sudarśana-bhayaḥ—who is not afraid of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His Sudarśana cakra; mahīyate—is worshiped.

**Перевод:**

**Beneath the planet known as Sutala is another planet, called Talātala, which is ruled by the Dānava demon named Maya. Maya is known as the ācārya \[master\] of all the māyāvīs, who can invoke the powers of sorcery. For the benefit of the three worlds, Lord Śiva, who is known as Tripurāri, once set fire to the three kingdoms of Maya, but later, being pleased with him, he returned his kingdom. Since that time, Maya Dānava has been protected by Lord Śiva, and therefore he falsely thinks that he need not fear the Sudarśana cakra of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is stated here that Bali lives happily in Sutala by the grace of Hari and similarly does Maya live happily in Talatala by the grace of Śiva (by whose grace he received that place). Mahiyate means “is worshipped.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

After Sutala, Talatala is described here. In that hole, Maya, a leader of Dānavas lives. How? Formerly he was the lord of the three cities which were burnt down by Śiva whose intention was to do good to the three worlds. Then by Śiva’s grace, Māyā was granted entry to Talatala. He lives there without the fear of Sudarśana, because Śiva, a great devotee of Sudarśana himself, has blessed him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Śam* = happiness. *Mahīyate* = is worshipped.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Māyā is a magician who has the blessings of Śiva by which he lives amidst luxury, yet he can never be compared to Bali.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mahīyate = is worshipped.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tataḥ = from Sutala.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Labdhapadaḥ* = one who has got the position. *Mahīyate* = is worshipped.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Below Sutala, Talatala is situated. This is where Māyā lives. With an intention to do good to the three worlds, Śiva burnt down the three cities of Māyā. Then Māyā worshipped him and got his grace. By the grace of Śiva only, he was given shelter in Talatala, where he lives as the guru of magicians without the fear of Sudarśana.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

By the grace of Śiva, Māyā obtained the place of Talatala and is worshipped there.

### Text 29

*ततोऽधस्तान्महातले काद्रवेयाणां सर्पाणां नैकशिरसां क्रोधवशो नाम*  
*गणः कुहकतक्षककालियसुषेणादिप्रधाना महाभोगवन्तः पतत्त्रिराजाधिपतेः*  
*पुरुषवाहादनवरतमुद्विजमानाः स्वकलत्रापत्यसुहृत्कुटुम्बसङ्गेन क्वचित्प्रमत्ता*  
*विहरन्ति ॥३९॥*

*tato 'dhastān mahātale kādraveyāṇāṁ sarpāṇāṁ naika-śirasāṁ krodhavaśo nāma gaṇaḥ kuhaka-takṣaka-kāliya-suṣeṇādi-pradhānā mahā-bhogavantaḥ patattri-rājādhipateḥ puruṣa-vāhād anavaratam udvijamānāḥ sva-kalatrāpatya-suhṛt-kuṭumba-saṅgena kvacit pramattā viharanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ—the planet Talātala; adhastāt—beneath; mahātale—in the planet known as Mahātala; kādraveyāṇām—of the descendants of Kadrū; sarpāṇām—who are big snakes; na eka-śirasām—who have many hoods; krodha-vaśaḥ—always subject to anger; nāma—named; gaṇaḥ—the group; kuhaka—Kuhaka; takṣaka—Takṣaka; kāliya—Kāliya; suṣeṇa—Suṣeṇa; ādi—and so on; pradhānāḥ—who are the prominent ones; mahā-bhogavantaḥ—addicted to all kinds of material enjoyment; patattri-rāja-adhipateḥ—from the king of all birds, Garuḍa; puruṣa-vāhāt—who carries the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anavaratam—constantly; udvijamānāḥ—afraid; sva—of their own; kalatra-apatya—wives and children; suhṛt—friends; kuṭumba—relatives; saṅgena—in the association; kvacit—sometimes; pramattāḥ—infuriated; viharanti—they sport.

**Перевод:**

**The planetary system below Talātala is known as Mahātala. It is the abode of many-hooded snakes, descendants of Kadrū, who are always very angry. The great snakes who are prominent are Kuhaka, Takṣaka, Kāliya and Suṣeṇa. The snakes in Mahātala are always disturbed by fear of Garuḍa, the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu, but although they are full of anxiety, some of them nevertheless sport with their wives, children, friends and relatives.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

There is the group of serpents endowed with many hoods. Kuhaka and others are chief amonst them. Mahabhogavantah means having a gigantic form. Purushavaha = Garuḍa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Then Mahatala planetary system is described here. In Mahatala, situated below Talatala, there is a group of serpents with many heads, Kadru’s children, called Krodhavashas. Kuhaka and others are the important among them. They have gigantic bodies and sometimes make merry with their wives and children, although they are always afraid of Garuḍa. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Mahābhogavantaḥ* = having big bodies. *Vāha* means vehicle, Garuḍa—from him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Naikaśirasām* = having many hoods. This is only elaborated further by the words Kuhaka, etc. *Puruṣavāha* = Garuḍa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tataḥ* = from Talatala. They are always afraid of Garuḍa, the king of birds. *Kvacit* means in some places of Mahatala.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Mahābhogavantaḥ* = having huge bodies.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Below Talatala is the fifth hole, Mahatala, where serpents Kuhaka and others live.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

They have many hoods. That is elaborated—Kuhaka and so on. They are afraid of Garuḍa always. Sometimes they forget him and make merry with their families, although not always.

### Text 30

*ततोऽधस्ताद्रसातले दैतेया दानवाः पणयो नाम निवातकवचाः*  
*कालेया हिरण्यपुरवासिन इति विबुधप्रत्यनीका उत्पत्त्या महौजसो*  
*महासाहसिनो भगवतः सकललोकानुभावस्य हरेरेव तेजसा*  
*प्रतिहतबलावलेपा बिलेशया इव वसन्ति ये वै सरमयेन्द्रदूत्या वाग्भि*  
*र्मन्त्रवर्णाभिरिन्द्राद्बिभ्यति ॥३०॥*

*tato 'dhastād rasātale daiteyā dānavāḥ paṇayo nāma nivāta-kavacāḥ kāleyā hiraṇya-puravāsina iti vibudha-pratyanīkā utpattyā mahaujaso mahā-sāhasino bhagavataḥ sakala-lokānubhāvasya harer eva tejasā pratihata-balāvalepā bileśayā iva vasanti ye vai saramayendra-dūtyā vāgbhir mantra-varṇābhir indrād bibhyati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ adhastāt—below the planetary system Mahātala; rasātale—on the planet called Rasātala; daiteyāḥ—the sons of Diti; dānavāḥ—the sons of Danu; paṇayaḥ nāma—named Paṇis; nivāta-kavacāḥ—Nivāta-kavacas; kāleyāḥ—Kāleyas; hiraṇya-puravāsinaḥ—Hiraṇya-puravāsīs; iti—thus; vibudha-pratyanīkāḥ—enemies of the demigods; utpattyāḥ—from birth; mahā-ojasaḥ—very powerful; mahā-sāhasinaḥ—very cruel; bhagavataḥ—of the Personality of Godhead; sakala-loka-anubhāvasya—who is auspicious for all planetary systems; hareḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; eva—certainly; tejasā—by the Sudarśana cakra; pratihata—defeated; bala—strength; avalepāḥ—and pride (because of bodily strength); bila-īśayāḥ—the snakes; iva—like; vasanti—they live; ye—who; vai—indeed; saramayā—by Saramā; indra-dūtyā—the messenger of Indra; vāgbhiḥ—by the words; mantra-varṇābhiḥ—in the form of a mantra; indrāt—from King Indra; bibhyati—are afraid.

**Перевод:**

**Beneath Mahātala is the planetary system known as Rasātala, which is the abode of the demoniac sons of Diti and Danu. They are called Paṇis, Nivāta-kavacas, Kāleyas and Hiraṇya-puravāsīs \[those living in Hiraṇya-pura\]. They are all enemies of the demigods, and they reside in holes like snakes. From birth they are extremely powerful and cruel, and although they are proud of their strength, they are always defeated by the Sudarśana cakra of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who rules all the planetary systems. When a female messenger from Indra named Saramā chants a particular curse, the serpentine demons of Mahātala become very afraid of Indra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Vibudhapratyahika = foes of demigods. Their pride is dented by Sudarśana, whose power is found everywhere. The story is that once demons stole Indra’s cow and hid it. Indra’s messenger named Sarama came in search of the cow. The demons wanted a treaty but Sarama refused and said, “Be killed by Indra and lie flat.” They were afraid on hearing that. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Rasātala is described here. It is situated below Talatala. The sons of Diti and Danu called Panis live there. They are three-fold: Nivatakavachas, Kalakeyas and Hiranyapuravasins (dwellers of the golden city). They are the foes of the demigods and are very strong and haughty by nature. Their haughtiness, however, is dented by the Sudarśana *cakra* of the Lord. They live like serpents in a hole. How? Always afraid of Indra, because of the words of Sarama, the dog of demigods. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Daityas are the foes of the demigods. Indra’s message delivered by Sarama frightens them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tataḥ* = from Mahatala. Panis are a section of Daityas. *Nigūḍhā* = concealed. “Oh Panis, be killed and fall on the earth,” is the meaning of the Vedic text. *Bibhyati* = are afraid.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Their pride was dented by Sudarśana *cakra* as the Panis live frightened by Surama’s words.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Demons named Panis live in Rasātala.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Vibudhapratyahika = foes of the demigods. Their pride is laid low by Sudarśana, which enters there, often. They are called Panis.

### Text 31

*ततोऽधस्तात्पाताले नागलोकपतयो वासुकिप्रमुखाः शङ्खकुलिकमहाशङ्ख*  
*श्वेतधनञ्जयधृतराष्ट्रशङ्खचूडकम्बलाश्वतरदेवदत्तादयो महाभोगिनो*  
*महामर्षा निवसन्ति येषामु ह वै पञ्चसप्तदशशतसहस्रशीर्षाणां फणासु*  
*विरचिता महामणयो रोचिष्णवः पातालविवरतिमिरनिकरं स्वरोचिषा*  
*विधमन्ति ॥३१॥*

*tato 'dhastāt pātāle nāga-loka-patayo vāsuki-pramukhāḥ śaṅkha-kulika-mahāśaṅkha-śveta-dhanañjaya-dhṛtarāṣṭra-śaṅkhacūḍa-kambalāśvatara-devadattādayo mahā-bhogino mahāmarṣā nivasanti yeṣām u ha vai pañca-sapta-daśa-śata-sahasra-śīrṣāṇāṁ phaṇāsu viracitā mahā-maṇayo rociṣṇavaḥ pātāla-vivara-timira-nikaraṁ sva-rociṣā vidhamanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tataḥ adhastāt—beneath that planet Rasātala; pātāle—on the planet known as Pātāla; nāga-loka-patayaḥ—the masters of the Nāgalokas; vāsuki—by Vāsuki; pramukhāḥ—headed; śaṅkha—Śaṅkha; kulika—Kulika; mahā-śaṅkha—Mahāśaṅkha; śveta—Śveta; dhanañjaya—Dhanañjaya; dhṛtarāṣṭra—Dhṛtarāṣṭra; śaṅkha-cūḍa—Śaṅkhacūḍa; kambala—Kambala; aśvatara—Aśvatara; deva-datta—Devadatta; ādayaḥ—and so on; mahā-bhoginaḥ—very addicted to material happiness; mahā-amarṣāḥ—greatly envious by nature; nivasanti—live; yeṣām—of all of them; u ha—certainly; vai—indeed; pañca—five; sapta—seven; daśa—ten; śata—one hundred; sahasra—one thousand; śīrṣāṇām—of those possessing hoods; phaṇāsu—on those hoods; viracitāḥ—fixed; mahā-maṇayaḥ—very valuable gems; rociṣṇavaḥ—full of effulgence; pātāla-vivara—the caves of the Pātāla planetary system; timira-nikaram—the mass of darkness; sva-rociṣā—by the effulgence of their hoods; vidhamanti—disperse.

**Перевод:**

**Beneath Rasātala is another planetary system, known as Pātāla or Nāgaloka, where there are many demoniac serpents, the masters of Nāgaloka, such as Śaṅkha, Kulika, Mahāśaṅkha, Śveta, Dhanañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Śaṅkhacūḍa, Kambala, Aśvatara and Devadatta. The chief among them is Vāsuki. They are all extremely angry, and they have many, many hoods—some snakes five hoods, some seven, some ten, others a hundred and others a thousand. These hoods are bedecked with valuable gems, and the light emanating from the gems illuminates the entire planetary system of bila-svarga.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

With great anger and having five or more very big hoods.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

After Rasātala, Patala is described. In Patala, the leaders of the serpent world, Vasuki and others live. They have great bodies, broad hoods and great rage. The serpents are further described as having five, seven and many, many hoods upon which gems dispel the darkness of Patala. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Mahabhoginah = having big bodies or extremely enjoying sensuous pleasures. Virachita = natural. Vidhamanti = destroy.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Shirsha is normally a hunter, but here it is used as a masculine gendered word by Panini’s sanction. This change is possible only in the *Vedas* yet since the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is equal to the *Vedas*, hence this change is permissible.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mahabhoginah = having large hoods.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Tatah = from Rasātala. Shirsha is masculine in gender, according to the sanction of Panini.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

They have gigantic bodies and are always furious. The gems on their hoods dispel the darkness there. The usage of the masculine Shirsha in place of neuter indicates that *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam* is as sacred as the *Vedas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Bhavayoh = of Śiva and Pārvatī. Assisted by Vāyu, Agni consumes the vital fluid and converts it into gold, which is worn in the form of ornaments by the wives of these asuras.

Even when an uncontrolled uttering of his name will suffice to beget liberation from bondage, what shall we say about the gift of three worlds?

Liberation is not easy. The yogis take recourse in sankhya and *yoga* to achieve it. This is very famous in the śāstras.

The topic is concluded. The sway of Sutala is not a reward for the gift he made to the most worthy of all. This sentence is understood in connection with the previous one.

Attaining God is the only worthy reward of God’s grace. Hari did not bless Indra as His great devotee.

God’s ways and pastimes are strange in so far as He took this incarnation of Vamana for the sake of Indra, and yet did not bless him, as he blessed Bali. The luxury of Indra causes him to forget God, who gave the luxury to him.

Since Bali was a great devotee, God thought that riches would be an impediment to his sadhana and thus took it away from him. This is evident from Bali’s own words.

My grandfather Prahlāda is the only wise one in this world, as he refused his paternal kingdom, and chose the servitude of Hari only. So even for us the path tread by Bali is the one that is worthy to be followed. But it is difficult, says Bali. One who has not gotten free from material desires and who is not a receptacle of divine grace, can never aspire to follow the path of Bali.

Then if it were to be asked why not narrate Bali’s story in detail, the answer is, it will be narrated in the 8thCanto in a different context depicting noble characters. Here the context is that of sthana (referred to in 2.10)

As the king is still inquisitive to hear the story of Bali, in spite of Śuka’s above words, the story is very briefly narrated. Vamana stands with a mace in his hand at the door of Bali and when Rāvaṇa came there during his conquest, Vamana kicked him very far away by his toe.

As Bali lives happily in Sutala by the grace of Hari, so does Māyā in Talatala by the grace of Śiva. Maya attained the place and remained fearless of Sudarśana.

There is a group of serpents with many hoods, such as Kuhaka and others. They are always afraid of Garuḍa, the vehicle of Hari. Sometimes they make merry with their families.

The different sects of asuras, their pride thwarted by Sudarśana, live in Rasātala, like serpents in a hole. They are frightened by the words of Sarama. Mahabhogin = having big bodies. Amarsha = rage. Having hoods which are five and more in number.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Patala is the seventh hole where serpents with more than five hoods live angrily.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

They have more than five hoods. They are endowed with big bodies and are fierce by nature. The gems on their hoods dispel the darkness around them.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twenty-fourth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The Subterranean Heavenly Planets.”

## Chapter 25 - The Glories of Lord Ananta

### Text 1

*श्रीशुक उवाच*  
*तस्य मूलदेशे त्रिंशद्योजनसहस्रान्तर आस्ते या वै कला*  
*भगवतस्तामसी समाख्यातानन्त इति सात्वतीया द्रष्टृदृश्ययोः*  
*सङ्कर्षणमहमित्यभिमानलक्षणं यं सङ्कर्षणमित्याचक्षते ॥१॥*

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*tasya mūla-deśe triṁśad-yojana-sahasrāntara āste yā vai kalā bhagavatas tāmasī samākhyātānanta iti sātvatīyā draṣṭṛ-dṛśyayoḥ saṅkarṣaṇam aham ity abhimāna-lakṣaṇaṁ yaṁ saṅkarṣaṇam ity ācakṣate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

śrī-śukaḥ uvāca—Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said; tasya—of the planet Pātāla; mūla-deśe—in the region beneath the base; triṁśat—thirty; yojana—eight-mile units of measurement; sahasra-antare—at an interval of one thousand; āste—remains; yā—which; vai—indeed; kalā—an expansion of an expansion; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tāmasī—related to darkness; samākhyātā—called; anantaḥ—Ananta; iti—thus; sātvatīyāḥ—the devotees; draṣṭṛ-dṛśyayoḥ—of matter and spirit; saṅkarṣaṇam—the drawing together; aham—I; iti—thus; abhimāna—by self-conception; lakṣaṇam—symptomized; yam—whom; saṅkarṣaṇam—Saṅkarṣaṇa; iti—thus; ācakṣate—learned scholars describe.

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said to Mahārāja Parīkṣit: My dear King, approximately 240,000 miles beneath the planet Pātāla lives another incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is the expansion of Lord Viṣṇu known as Lord Ananta or Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa. He is always in the transcendental position, but because He is worshiped by Lord Śiva, the deity of tamo-guṇa or darkness, He is sometimes called tāmasī. Lord Ananta is the predominating Deity of the material mode of ignorance as well as the false ego of all conditioned souls. When a conditioned living being thinks, "I am the enjoyer, and this world is meant to be enjoyed by me," this conception of life is dictated to him by Saṅkarṣaṇa. Thus the mundane conditioned soul thinks himself the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Tasya = of Pātāla. Who is Ananta? Those who worship the quartet of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha according to sattvata practice think He is one of these—namely, Saṅkarṣaṇa. What is the reason for calling Him by that name? Because he brings together the perceiver and the perceived.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having described the situation under the Bhūloka until Pātālaloka, Śuka now describes Ananta, who bears the entire earth from below it. Śeṣa is stationed 30,000 *yojanas* \[240,000 miles\] below Pātāla. He has another famous name, Ananta. He is a part of the form of God which is presented in *tāmasa ahaṅkāra*. Śeṣa is the propounder of the *pañcarātra*. Those who know *pañcarātra* call Him Saṅkarṣaṇa. He brings the knower and the known together. He has the knowledge of objects which are beyond the scope of sensory organs and He bestows it to His devotees. He is responsible for the cognizance of the “I-element” \[false ego, ahamkara\] in the living entities. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Tasya = of Pātāla. This form of Ananta guides the *tamoguṇa*. Ananta brings together the perceiver (jiva), and the perceived (the body), together and makes the soul feel an identity with the body. Is the identity real then? No, it is an illusion. It is called *abhimāna* and Ananta is the one who is the cause of such an illusion. He is called Saṅkarṣaṇa for bringing the soul and body together.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In this chapter, the glory of Saṅkarṣaṇa is extolled. *Tāmasi* means controlling Rudra and others who are responsible for the destruction. “Sattvatas” means Nārada and others who follow the *Sattvata Samhita* spoken by God in accordance with the *Vedas*. He is called Saṅkarṣaṇa because He brings together the perceiver and the perceived and produces the “I” \[false ego, ahamkara\] perception.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Thirty thousand *yojanas* \[240,000 miles\] below Pātāla, Śeṣa stays. He is the same *tāmasi* form of *bhagavān*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Moola pradesha* means below Pātāla. The word *tāmasi* is used because this form is the executor of destruction, an aspect of *tamoguṇa*. He is called Śeṣa and Ananta. Those who know *pañcarātra* call him Saṅkarṣaṇa also, because He brings the seer (living entity) and the seen (body), house and other things, together. From that results the misconception of “I-ness” and “my-ness” in what is not me or mine \[false ego, ahamkara\].

### Text 2

*यस्येदं क्षितिमण्डलं भगवतोऽनन्तमूर्तेः सहस्रशिरस एकस्मिन्नेव*  
*शीर्षणि ध्रियमाणं सिद्धार्थ इव लक्ष्यते ॥२॥*

*yasyedaṁ kṣiti-maṇḍalaṁ bhagavato 'nanta-mūrteḥ sahasra-śirasa ekasminn eva śīrṣaṇi dhriyamāṇaṁ siddhārtha iva lakṣyate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom; idam—this; kṣiti-maṇḍalam—universe; bhagavataḥ—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; ananta-mūrteḥ—in the form of Anantadeva; sahasra-śirasaḥ—who has thousands of hoods; ekasmin—on one; eva—only; śīrṣaṇi—hood; dhriyamāṇam—is being sustained; siddhārthaḥ iva—and like a white mustard seed; lakṣyate—is seen.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: This great universe, situated on one of Lord Anantadeva's thousands of hoods, appears just like a white mustard seed. It is infinitesimal compared to the hood of Lord Ananta.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

His infiniteness is narrated. The pronouns are construed with the next sentence.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The entire earth rests on one of His thousand hoods like a mustard seed. Thus, because of His infinite strength, He is called Ananta.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The name Ananta (meaning “infinite”) is justified in Him because He bears the entire earth effortlessly on His head. *Siddartha* = mustard.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The form “*tāmasi”* is used because it is the inner dweller of Rudra, the manager of *tamoguṇa*. Otherwise, the sentence, “You have taken the form of sattva” would be the meaning, however, that would be contradictory.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Tāmasi* means the promulgator of destruction, an aspect of tamas—not that His form itself is *tamasi* since verse ten states that the form is pure sattva. Those following the path of *Sattvata Samhita* call him Saṅkarṣaṇa for He brings the enjoyer and the enjoyed together and creates the perception of “I am the enjoyer and this is the object of my enjoyment.” Saṅkarṣaṇa is stationed in the perception yet He is to be meditated upon for purification from this misconception.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Tatah* = from Pātāla. *Tāmasi* = the propagator of destruction, a function of *tamoguṇa*. *Drstr drshyayoh* means the enjoyer and the object of enjoyment. Unification means the perception that I am the enjoyer and this is the object of enjoyment. To get rid of the “I-ness” and “my-ness” in such perceptions, they meditate upon Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The pronouns here are construed with the word *bhagavān*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He is called Saṅkarṣaṇa because He brings the soul and body together, the result of which is the “I-perception” in the body. His devotees worship to get rid of this illusion.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Even the name of Ananta is fully justified in Him because of His infinite strength. Ananta means boundless which is evident since He bears the entire earth effortlessly on His head like a mustard seed.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

How is the name Ananta justified in Him? He exhibits infinite strength by holding the earth like a mustard seed on His head.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

He is called Ananta because of His infinite strength indicated by His bearing the earth on His head like a  small seed.

### Text 3

*यस्य ह वा इदं कालेनोपसञ्जिहीर्षतोऽमर्षविरचितरुचिर*  
*भ्रमद्भ्रुवोरन्तरेण साङ्कर्षणो नाम रुद्र एकादशव्यूहस्त्र्यक्षस्त्रिशिखं*  
*शूलमुत्तम्भयन्नुदतिष्ठत् ॥३॥*

*yasya ha vā idaṁ kālenopasañjihīrṣato 'marṣa-viracita-rucira-bhramad-bhruvor antareṇa sāṅkarṣaṇo nāma rudra ekādaśa-vyūhas try-akṣas tri-śikhaṁ śūlam uttambhayann udatiṣṭhat.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom; ha vā—indeed; idam—this (material world); kālena—in due course of time; upasañjihīrṣataḥ—desiring to destroy; amarṣa—by anger; viracita—formed; rucira—very beautiful; bhramat—moving; bhruvoḥ—the two eyebrows; antareṇa—from between; sāṅkarṣaṇaḥ nāma—named Sāṅkarṣaṇa; rudraḥ—an incarnation of Lord Śiva; ekādaśa-vyūhaḥ—who has eleven expansions; tri-akṣaḥ—three eyes; tri-śikham—having three points; śūlam—a trident; uttambhayan—raising; udatiṣṭhat—arose.

**Перевод:**

**At the time of devastation, when Lord Anantadeva desires to destroy the entire creation, He becomes slightly angry. Then from between His two eyebrows appears three-eyed Rudra, carrying a trident. This Rudra, who is known as Saṅkarṣaṇa, is the embodiment of the eleven Rudras, or incarnations of Lord Śiva. He appears in order to devastate the entire creation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

His *tāmasa* nature is narrated. He raises His eyebrows in rage to destroy the universe yet those eyebrows appear charming. He also expands from between the moving eyebrows.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It was said that the form of Ananta is a *tāmasi* form. Ananta is the supervising deity of *tāmasahankara*. When He desires to destroy the world at the end of the two *parārdhas*, He knits His eyebrows and from the middle of these brows emanate a group of eleven Rudras who destroy the world. The Rudras wield tridents in their hands and have three eyes. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

When He desires to destroy, He knits His brows in anger (an aspect of *tamas* \[the mode of ignorance\]) and thus Rudra is born, just as when He wishes to create, the lotus of the nature of *rajas* \[passion\] comes out of His navel.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Because *māyā* is under His control, angry Rudra took birth from between His eyebrows when He desired to destroy. Rudra divided Himself into eleven forms just as the *puruṣa* \[Supreme Lord who has no equal\] bore the lotus flower from His navel when He desired to create.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Rudra and His eleven forms came out of the knitted brows of Śeṣa as the latter assumed rage for the destruction of the world.

### Text 4

*यस्याङ्घ्रिकमलयुगलारुणविशदनखमणिषण्डमण्डलेष्वहिपतयः सह सात्वत*  
*र्षभैरेकान्तभक्तियोगेनावनमन्तः स्ववदनानि परिस्फुरत्कुण्डलप्रभामण्डित*  
*गण्डस्थलान्यतिमनोहराणि प्रमुदितमनसः खलु विलोकयन्ति ॥४॥*

*yasyāṅghri-kamala-yugalāruṇa-viśada-nakha-maṇi-ṣaṇḍa-maṇḍaleṣv ahi-patayaḥ saha sātvatarṣabhair ekānta-bhakti-yogenāvanamantaḥ sva-vadanāni parisphurat-kuṇḍala-prabhā-maṇḍita-gaṇḍa-sthalāny ati-manoharāṇi pramudita-manasaḥ khalu vilokayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom; aṅghri-kamala—of lotus feet; yugala—of the pair; aruṇa-viśada—brilliant pink; nakha—of the nails; maṇi-ṣaṇḍa—like gems; maṇḍaleṣu—on the round surfaces; ahi-patayaḥ—the leaders of the snakes; saha—with; sātvata-ṛṣabhaiḥ—the best devotees; ekānta-bhakti-yogena—with unalloyed devotional service; avanamantaḥ—offering obeisances; sva-vadanāni—their own faces; parisphurat—glittering; kuṇḍala—of the earrings; prabhā—by the effulgence; maṇḍita—decorated; gaṇḍa-sthalāni—whose cheeks; ati-manoharāṇi—very beautiful; pramudita-manasaḥ—their minds refreshed; khalu—indeed; vilokayanti—they see.

**Перевод:**

**The pink, transparent toenails on the Lord's lotus feet are exactly like valuable gems polished to a mirror finish. When the unalloyed devotees and the leaders of the snakes offer their obeisances to Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa with great devotion, they become very joyful upon seeing their own beautiful faces reflected in His toenails. Their cheeks are decorated with glittering earrings, and the beauty of their faces is extremely pleasing to see.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

His handsomeness is stated. Their faces are reflected in the shining, gem-like nails of His lotus-like feet. They see their faces reflected with cheeks illuminated by the luster of their earrings.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

His handsomeness is explained here. As His devotees, the followers of Sattvata Samhita, offer their obeisances to Him by prostrating at His feet, they see the reflection of their own faces illumined by their dangling ear-ornaments in the host of bright nails of Ananta’s feet.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Ekadasavyuhah = His form divided into eleven individual forms—the group of those forms. Uttambhayam = wielding.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

His handsomeness is described. The host of his nails acts like a mirror.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Śeṣa is handsome. Subhagatvam = handsomeness.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The sattvata \[transcendental\] leaders and other serpents look at their own faces reflected in the bright and pure nails of Saṅkarṣaṇa's feet as they bow their head to offer *praṇāms* \[respects\].

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Though fierce at the time of destruction by accepting *tamoguṇa*, now He assumes *sattva guṇa* \[the mode of goodness\] and appears handsome to His devotees during this time of protection. The leaders of the serpents see their own reflection in the bright and pure nails of Śeṣa as they offer their obeisances to him.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

His Godly nature is stated here. All the pronouns stand for Ananta.

They look at the reflection of their faces illumined by dangling ear ornaments in the pure reddish nails of Ananta.

### Text 5

*यस्यैव हि नागराजकुमार्य आशिष आशासानाश्चार्वङ्गवलयविलसित*  
*विशद विपुलधवलसुभगरुचिरभुजरजतस्तम्भेष्वगुरुचन्दनकुङ्कुमपङ्कानुलेपे*  
*नावलिम्पमानास्तद्अभिमर्शनोन्मथितहृदयमकरध्वजावेशरुचिरललितस्मितास्तद*  
*नुरागमदमुदितमद विघूर्णितारुणकरुणावलोकनयनवदनारविन्दं सव्रीडं किल*  
*विलोकयन्ति ॥५॥*

*yasyaiva hi nāga-rāja-kumārya āśiṣa āśāsānāś cārv-aṅga-valaya-vilasita-viśada-vipula-dhavala-subhaga-rucira-bhuja-rajata-stambheṣv aguru-candana-kuṅkuma-paṅkānulepenāvalimpamānās tad-abhimarśanonmathita-hṛdaya-makara-dhvajāveśa-rucira-lalita-smitās tad-anurāgamada-mudita-mada-vighūrṇitāruṇa-karuṇāvaloka-nayana-vadanāravindaṁ savrīḍaṁ kila vilokayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—of whom; eva—certainly; hi—indeed; nāga-rāja-kumāryaḥ—the unmarried princesses of the serpent kings; āśiṣaḥ—blessings; āśāsānāḥ—hoping for; cāru—beautiful; aṅga-valaya—on the sphere of His body; vilasita—gleaming; viśada—spotless; vipula—long; dhavala—white; subhaga—indicating good fortune; rucira—beautiful; bhuja—on His arms; rajata-stambheṣu—like columns of silver; aguru—of aloe; candana—of sandalwood; kuṅkuma—of saffron; paṅka—from the pulp; anulepena—with an ointment; avalimpamānāḥ—smearing; tat-abhimarśana—by contact with His limbs; unmathita—agitated; hṛdaya—in their hearts; makara-dhvaja—of Cupid; āveśa—due to the entrance; rucira—very beautiful; lalita—delicate; smitāḥ—whose smiling; tat—of Him; anurāga—of attachment; mada—by the intoxication; mudita—delighted; mada—due to intoxication with kindness; vighūrṇita—rolling; aruṇa—pink; karuṇa-avaloka—glancing with kindness; nayana—eyes; vadana—and face; aravindam—like lotus flowers; sa-vrīḍam—with bashfulness; kila—indeed; vilokayanti—they see.

**Перевод:**

**Lord Ananta's arms are attractively long, beautifully decorated with bangles and completely spiritual. They are white, and so they appear like silver columns. When the beautiful princesses of the serpent kings, hoping for the Lord's auspicious blessing, smear His arms with aguru pulp, sandalwood pulp and kuṅkuma, the touch of His limbs awakens lusty desires within them. Understanding their minds, the Lord looks at the princesses with a merciful smile, and they become bashful, realizing that He knows their desires. Then they smile beautifully and look upon the Lord's lotus face, which is beautified by reddish eyes rolling slightly from intoxication and delighted by love for His devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The girls get smitten with love as they anoint perfumes to His lovely arms which resemble pillars of silver. They behold His face with eyes broadened on account of love, slightly reddish as they are.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

To fulfill their desires, the Nāga girls worship Him by anointing the beautiful silver-like arms of Ananta with sandal paste and perfumes. While doing so, they are smitten by love at the very touch of His arms and look at His face shyly with smiles on their faces. Ananta’s face is lit with bright eyes, broadened in His bliss and benevolence toward His devotees. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Tadabhimarshanena* = by touching His shoulders shyly is an adverb.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

As the Nāga girls anoint His shoulders (resembling silver pillars) with perfumes, they are smitten with love and look bashfully at the sweet face of Ananta. He very compassionately casts His glance at the girls who become startled and more bashful, thinking that the Lord has read their inner minds. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Angavalaya = the group of His organs. Vishoda = pure. Vipula = large. Dhavala = white. Subhaga = beautiful. Ruchira = indicative of intentions. Lalita = auspicious. Anuragena = love for His devotees. Mada = happiness.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The Nāga girls, smitten with love, look bashfully at His face as they anoint His arms in worship. His eyes are broad out of His own bliss and also out of grace upon His devotees. \[Note from the translator: The word *mada* is derived from the root *mad* which means happiness\].

### Text 6

*स एव भगवाननन्तो ऽनन्तगुणार्णव आदिदेव उपसंहृतामर्षरोषवेगो*  
*लोकानां स्वस्तय आस्ते ॥६॥*

*sa eva bhagavān ananto 'nanta-guṇārṇava ādi-deva upasaṁhṛtāmarṣa-roṣa-vego lokānāṁ svastaya āste.*

**Пословный перевод:**

saḥ—that; eva—certainly; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anantaḥ—Anantadeva; ananta-guṇa-arṇavaḥ—the reservoir of unlimited transcendental qualities; ādi-devaḥ—the original Lord, or nondifferent from the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; upasaṁhṛta—who has restrained; amarṣa—of His intolerance; roṣa—and wrath; vegaḥ—the force; lokānām—of all people on all planets; svastaye—for the welfare; āste—remains.

**Перевод:**

**Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is the ocean of unlimited spiritual qualities, and thus He is known as Anantadeva. He is nondifferent from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. For the welfare of all living entities within this material world, He resides in His abode, restraining His anger and intolerance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The force of anger and intolerance has been controlled by Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Ananta is devoid of any limitation of time and space. He is endowed with infinite attributes and having withdrawn His anger, stays there for the welfare of the world.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

An ocean of infinite attributes such as handsomeness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Rage is withdrawn as it is irrelevant at the time of sustenance. Amarsha is intolerance and anger is an off-shoot.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Now at the time of sustenance, the anger is not relevant, thus it has been withdrawn.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Intolerance of a mistake is *amarsha*. The act of punishing the culprit is rage.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is an ocean of infinite virtues and devoid of the three limitations of time, space and matter. He has no anger now and remains there for the welfare of the good people.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

He who has withdrawn the force of both intolerance and anger.

### Text 7

*ध्यायमानः सुरासुरोरगसिद्धगन्धर्वविद्याधरमुनिगणैरनवरतमदमुदितविकृत*  
*विह्वललोचनः सुललितमुखरिकामृतेनाप्यायमानः स्वपार्षदविबुधयूथपती*  
*नपरिम्लानरागनवतुलसिकामोदमध्वासवेन माद्यन्मधुकरव्रातमधुरगीतश्रियं*  
*वैजयन्तीं स्वां वनमालां नीलवासा एककुण्डलो हलककुदि*  
*कृतसुभगसुन्दरभुजो भगवान्महेन्द्रो वारणेन्द्र इव काञ्चनीं*  
*कक्षामुदारलीलो बिभर्ति ॥७॥*

*dhyāyamānaḥ surāsuroraga-siddha-gandharva-vidyādhara-muni-gaṇair anavarata-mada-mudita-vikṛta-vihvala-locanaḥ sulalita-mukharikāmṛtenāpyāyamānaḥ sva-pārṣada-vibudha-yūtha-patīn aparimlāna-rāga-nava-tulasikāmoda-madhv-āsavena mādyan madhukara-vrāta-madhura-gīta-śriyaṁ vaijayantīṁ svāṁ vanamālāṁ nīla-vāsā eka-kuṇḍalo hala-kakudi kṛta-subhaga-sundara-bhujo bhagavān mahendro vāraṇendra iva kāñcanīṁ kakṣām udāra-līlo bibharti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhyāyamānaḥ—being meditated upon; sura—of demigods; asura—demons; uraga—snakes; siddha—inhabitants of Siddhaloka; gandharva—inhabitants of Gandharvaloka; vidyādhara—Vidyādharas; muni—and of great sages; gaṇaiḥ—by groups; anavarata—constantly; mada-mudita—delighted by intoxication; vikṛta—moving to and fro; vihvala—rolling; locanaḥ—whose eyes; su-lalita—excellently composed; mukharika—of speech; amṛtena—by the nectar; āpyāyamānaḥ—pleasing; sva-pārṣada—His own associates; vibudha-yūtha-patīn—the heads of the different groups of demigods; aparimlāna—never faded; rāga—whose luster; nava—ever fresh; tulasikā—of the tulasī blossoms; āmoda—by the fragrance; madhu-āsavena—and the honey; mādyan—being intoxicated; madhukara-vrāta—of the bees; madhura-gīta—by the sweet singing; śrīyam—which is made more beautiful; vaijayantīm—the garland named vaijayantī; svām—His own; vanamālām—garland; nīla-vāsāḥ—covered with blue garments; eka-kuṇḍalaḥ—wearing only one earring; hala-kakudi—on the handle of a plow; kṛta—placed; subhaga—auspicious; sundara—beautiful; bhujaḥ—hands; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; mahā-indraḥ—the King of heaven; vāraṇa-indraḥ—the elephant; iva—like; kāñcanīm—golden; kakṣām—belt; udāra-līlaḥ—engaged in transcendental pastimes; bibharti—wears.

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: The demigods, the demons, the Uragas \[serpentine demigods\], the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Vidyādharas and many highly elevated sages constantly offer prayers to the Lord. Because He is intoxicated, the Lord looks bewildered, and His eyes, appearing like flowers in full bloom, move to and fro. He pleases His personal associates, the heads of the demigods, by the sweet vibrations emanating from His mouth. Dressed in bluish garments and wearing a single earring, He holds a plow on His back with His two beautiful and well-constructed hands. Appearing as white as the heavenly King Indra, He wears a golden belt around His waist and a vaijayantī garland of ever-fresh tulasī blossoms around His neck. Bees intoxicated by the honeylike fragrance of the tulasī flowers hum very sweetly around the garland, which thus becomes more and more beautiful. In this way, the Lord enjoys His very magnanimous pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

For the sake of His worship it is stated: He is meditated upon by demigods and others. While consuming drinks, His eyes are large. He addresses His devotees with sweet words. He wears a blue garment. He has only one earring. He has a plough placed on His beautiful shoulder. He wears a vanamālā \[garland\] made of flowers, which is thronged by bees seeing honey. Kakshya = a strap (normally put on elements), here a golden one. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Again Ananta is described here. The demigods meditate upon Him. He is always blissful in Himself. He has slightly reddish eyes with slow moving eye-balls. He addresses His devotees with nectarine words. He wears a garland made of Kṛṣṇa Tulasi thronged with maddened bees. He wears a black garment. He has an earring in only one ear and sports a plough on His handsome shoulder and a golden chain around His waist. This is how He should be meditated upon. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Whose luster does not fade. Amodamadhvasavena = fragrant juice of honey wearing the plough on his shoulder. Kakshya = A belt around the stomach.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Graceful words resembling elixir. Kaksha is a belt around the waist—here it is golden.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Kaksha = a chain tied around the stomach. The elephant of Indra is *Airāvata*.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He has now withdrawn the force of his anger because it is the time of protection of the world.  
It was said He is present for the welfare of the world. How is the welfare achieved? It is only by meditation. For this purpose His form is described in great detail.

### Text 8

*य एष एवमनुश्रुतो ध्यायमानो मुमुक्षूणामनादिकालकर्मवासनाग्रथितम*  
*विद्यामयं हृदयग्रन्थिं सत्त्वरजस्तमोमयमन्तर्हृदयं गत आशु निर्भिनत्ति*  
*तस्यानुभावान् भगवान् स्वायम्भुवो नारदः सह तुम्बुरुणा सभायां*  
*ब्रह्मणः संश्लोकयामास ॥८॥*

*ya eṣa evam anuśruto dhyāyamāno mumukṣūṇām anādi-kāla-karma-vāsanā-grathitam avidyāmayaṁ hṛdaya-granthiṁ sattva-rajas-tamomayam antar-hṛdayaṁ gata āśu nirbhinatti tasyānubhāvān bhagavān svāyambhuvo nāradaḥ saha tumburuṇā sabhāyāṁ brahmaṇaḥ saṁślokayām āsa.*

**Пословный перевод:**

yaḥ—who; eṣaḥ—this one; evam—thus; anuśrutaḥ—being heard from a bona fide spiritual master; dhyāyamānaḥ—being meditated upon; mumukṣūṇām—of persons desiring liberation from conditioned life; anādi—from immemorial; kāla—time; karma-vāsanā—by the desire for fruitive activities; grathitam—tied tightly; avidyā-mayam—consisting of the illusory energy; hṛdaya-granthim—the knot within the heart; sattva-rajaḥ-tamaḥ-mayam—made of the three modes of material nature; antaḥ-hṛdayam—in the core of the heart; gataḥ—situated; āśu—very soon; nirbhinatti—cuts; tasya—of Saṅkarṣaṇa; anubhāvān—the glories; bhagavān—the greatly powerful; svāyambhuvaḥ—the son of Lord Brahmā; nāradaḥ—the sage Nārada; saha—along with; tumburuṇā—the stringed instrument called a Tumburu; sabhāyām—in the assembly; brahmaṇaḥ—of Lord Brahmā; saṁślokayām āsa—described in verses.

**Перевод:**

**If persons who are very serious about being liberated from material life hear the glories of Anantadeva from the mouth of a spiritual master in the chain of disciplic succession, and if they always meditate upon Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Lord enters the cores of their hearts, vanquishes all the dirty contamination of the material modes of nature, and cuts to pieces the hard knot within the heart, which has been tied tightly since time immemorial by the desire to dominate material nature through fruitive activities. Nārada Muni, the son of Lord Brahmā, always glorifies Anantadeva in his father's assembly. There he sings blissful verses of his own composition, accompanied by his stringed instrument \[or a celestial singer\] known as Tumburu.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Saṁślokayāmāsa = described.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He manifests in the heart of those who meditate upon Him and removes the bondage of *karma* \[material fruitive reactions\]. This *karma* bondage has come with the living entity since time immemorial and it is due to the three qualities of material nature, *sattva* \[goodness\], *rajas* \[passion\] and *tamas* \[ignorance\]. One should first hear of His greatness from a teacher, ponder it well and then meditate. In Brahmās assembly amidst demigods and sages, Tumburu and Nārada sing of Ananta’s greatness.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Samshlokayamasa = described in verses.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Saṁślokayāmāsa means praised in verses as an incarnation of Puruṣa.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Anubhava = prowess—because He is an incarnation of the Puruṣa \[Supreme Lord\], He is praised in verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He, along with the Gandharva \[celestial singer\] Tumburu, sang the Lord’s praise.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Sang along with the Gandharva Tumburu.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Having been meditated upon as stated above, He enters the minds of His devoteess and cuts the knot of ignorance that has been there since time immemorial. The venerable Nārada and Tambura sing of His valor and other virtues.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The description of Saṅkarṣaṇa’s form is given for the sake of meditation.

### Text 9

*उत्पत्तिस्थितिलयहेतवोऽस्य कल्पाः*  
*सत्त्वाद्याः प्रकृतिगुणा यदीक्षयासन् ।*  
*यद्रूपं ध्रुवमकृतं यदेकमात्मन्*  
*नानाधात्कथमु ह वेद तस्य वर्त्म ॥९॥*

*utpatti-sthiti-laya-hetavo 'sya kalpāḥ*  
*sattvādyāḥ prakṛti-guṇā yad-īkṣayāsan*  
*yad-rūpaṁ dhruvam akṛtaṁ yad ekam ātman*  
*nānādhāt katham u ha veda tasya vartma*

**Пословный перевод:**

utpatti—of creation; sthiti—maintenance; laya—and dissolution; hetavaḥ—the original causes; asya—of this material world; kalpāḥ—capable of acting; sattva-ādyāḥ—headed by the sattva-guṇa; prakṛti-guṇāḥ—the modes of material nature; yat—of whom; īkṣayā—by the glance; āsan—became; yat-rūpam—the form of whom; dhruvam—unlimited; akṛtam—uncreated; yat—who; ekam—one; ātman—in Himself; nānā—variously; adhāt—has manifested; katham—how; u ha—certainly; veda—can understand; tasya—His; vartma—path.

**Перевод:**

**By His glance, the Supreme Personality of Godhead enables the modes of material nature to act as the causes of universal creation, maintenance and destruction. The Supreme Soul is unlimited and beginningless, and although He is one, He has manifested Himself in many forms. How can human society understand the ways of the Supreme?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The mode of goodness and other modes of nature responsible for the creation, etc., of the universe, become operative by His benevolent glance. That form of His is without beginning or end. The reason is that although He is one, He bears within Himself the entire world. How can ordinary people know His nature, which is verily Brahman \[spiritual\]. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Viśvanātha Cakravartī and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

As long as material nature (*prakṛti*) was not seen by the Lord (Puruṣa), it was not capable of producing the Mahātattva \[total material substance\] etc. Whose form is eternal and natural because it is of the nature of chit (knowledge) alone bore the entire world in the pores of His hair and nourished it. "*Tasya vartma*” means the path leading to Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The purport is that He is the efficient cause of the universe like a potter. He is not the material cause like clay as some others feel. His desire to create the universe makes Him cast his glance at *prakṛti* \[material nature\], after which He bears the multifarious universe within His body. Not knowing His real nature and greatness, how can a person like me attempt to praise Him?

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Hari’s quartet consists of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha of which the second form is present in Śeṣa. Thus, with the qualities of the in-dwelling supersoul Saṅkarṣaṇa, the expansion Śeṣa is described.

The qualities of goodness (*sattva*) and others became surcharged to produce the universe by His graceful glance over them. An insentient thing cannot act by itself as it requires the presence of a sentient being, either inside or outside. Thus, will not Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is present within the modes of nature, be also subject to transformation, when the *guṇas* get transformed? To this objection, Śuka replies. No. God does not become transformed because His form is natural and unchanged having never been produced. He is not like the living entity (*jīva*), who, though unborn, is subject to transformation due to association with the material body. Nor is He like matter, which although eternal, becomes transformed from cause into effect. God is not like that. On no account does He become transformed. He bears the entire universe within Himself, thus who can understand the nature and functioning of Saṅkarṣaṇa, the inner controller of Śeṣa?

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The reason for Śeṣa’s rage is the tendency of the universe to be averse to God.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Only by His glance did sattva \[goodness\] and other modes of nature become capable to produce. His form is eternal, He is Brahman. He bears the entire universe in His person. How can anyone know Him without His grace?

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He enters the mind of those who meditate upon Him and cuts the knot of ignorance present there.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

An efficient cause like the potter is one who stirs the other causes which are his own forms into action so that they will transform themselves into the respective effects.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Saṁślokayāmāsa means narrated in verses.

### Text 10

*मूर्तिं नः पुरुकृपया बभार सत्त्वं*  
*संशुद्धं सदसदिदं विभाति तत्र ।*  
*यल्लीलां मृगपतिराददेऽनवद्या*  
*मादातुं स्वजनमनांस्युदारवीर्यः ॥१०॥*

*mūrtiṁ naḥ puru-kṛpayā babhāra sattvaṁ*  
*saṁśuddhaṁ sad-asad idaṁ vibhāti tatra*  
*yal-līlāṁ mṛga-patir ādade 'navadyām*  
*ādātuṁ svajana-manāṁsy udāra-vīryaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūrtim—different forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; naḥ—unto us; puru-kṛpayā—because of great mercy; babhāra—exhibited; sattvam—existence; saṁśuddham—completely transcendental; sat-asat idam—this material manifestation of cause and effect; vibhāti—shines; tatra—in whom; yat-līlām—the pastimes of whom; mṛga-patiḥ—the master of all living beings, who is exactly like a lion (the master of all other animals); ādade—taught; anavadyām—without material contamination; ādātum—to conquer; sva-jana-manāṁsi—the minds of His devotees; udāra-vīryaḥ—who is most liberal and powerful.

**Перевод:**

**This manifestation of subtle and gross matter exists within the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Out of causeless mercy toward His devotees, He exhibits various forms, which are all transcendental. The Supreme Lord is most liberal, and He possesses all mystic power. To conquer the minds of His devotees and give pleasure to their hearts, He appears in different incarnations and manifests many pastimes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Then how can aspirants serve Him? The reply is given. Out of compassion for His devotees, He took a sattvic form from which the entire world of cause and effect appears. The pastime He exhibited to conquer the minds of His devotees is emulated by the lion, whose valor is very noble. “How can an aspirant worship anyone else?” This is explained in the next verse. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Although His nature is incomprehensible, He has taken this Saṅkarṣaṇa form with a view to bless His devotees. This form is a lila vigraha (accepted as His pastime). It is pure sattva \[goodness\] and contains no element of rajas \[passion\] or tamas \[ignorance\]. The lion emulated His gait and valor. Only to bless His devotees, He accepts the worship of the Nāga girls \[daughters of the snakes\], bears the earth on His hood and promulgates *Sattvata Samhita*. This is attested in *Mahābhārata*: “Manu will teach us the *Sattavata Samhita* which Saṅkarṣaṇa, in the form of Śeṣa, composed.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

His bearing the universe in Himself is briefly stated. He is an embodiment of all virtues like knowledge, strength and so on, yet He manifests a form which appears limited in the eyes of common people. There can never be equality between the substratum and what is present in it. The lion emulated Him in valor. Although the world He bears is different from Him, He also bears His own forms of Matsya and so on, which are non-different from Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He bore the incarnation of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa and so on. Are they material forms? No, they are pure bliss and knowledge. That is what *sattva* means. Even Yashoda saw the entire universe in His form. Like a lion, he showed many lilas to attract the minds of His devotees. His valor is noble as was shown in the lifting of Govardhana.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Murtim” = the forms of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa and so on. In whose form this world of chit \[knowledge\] and achit \[ignorance\] appears as was witnessed by Yashoda. By which form he emulated a lion to attract the minds of devotees and for the same reason He held aloft Govardhana. His intention was, “By seeing My form, they will increase devotion for Me.” Even the lion emulates Śeṣa’s valor, or the simile may be understood this way; just as a lion kills an elephant instantly, so does the Lord kill enemies.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

For what benefit does Brahman hold the universe like this? He has no personal benefit—it is His pastime. It is to bless His devotees and attract their minds so that they obtain the concentration needed to meditate upon Him. He is the Lord of all mrgas, which means living entities. So whom do we take refuge in other than Śeṣa?

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Although His nature is difficult to know, He can be described in brief as He has taken the Saṅkarṣaṇa form. He, in whose body this universe of cause and effects appear, has taken this form out of compassion towards us, His devotees—the form of pure goodness and nothing else. He is the Lord of Brahmā and other demigods. Mrga is taken in a passive sense and means *brahma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

In these verses, Śeṣa is praised, but creation of the world and other such attributes are narrated. These are the exclusive characteristics of Hari. Thus, these prayers are to be classified as *misra* (mixed) prayers wherein both Śeṣa and His *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\] Hari are praised. Whatever attributes are applicable to Śeṣa should be applied to His *antaryāmī* Hari. *Prakṛti* is incapable of producing its byproducts unless looked at by the *antaryāmī* of Śeṣa and so on.

### Text 11

*मूर्धन्यर्पितमणुवत्सहस्रमूर्ध्नो*  
*भूगोलं सगिरिसरित्समुद्रसत्त्वम् ।*  
*आनन्त्यादनिमितविक्रमस्य भूम्नः*  
*को वीर्याण्यधिगणयेत्सहस्रजिह्वः ॥११॥*

*yan-nāma śrutam anukīrtayed akasmād*  
*ārto vā yadi patitaḥ pralambhanād vā*  
*hanty aṁhaḥ sapadi nṛṇām aśeṣam anyaṁ*  
*kaṁ śeṣād bhagavata āśrayen mumukṣuḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

yat—of whom; nāma—the holy name; śrutam—heard; anukīrtayet—may chant or repeat; akasmāt—by accident; ārtaḥ—a distressed person; vā—or; yadi—if; patitaḥ—a fallen person; pralambhanāt—out of joking; vā—or; hanti—destroys; aṁhaḥ—sinful; sapadi—that instant; nṛṇām—of human society; aśeṣam—unlimited; anyam—of other; kam—what; śeṣāt—than Lord Śeṣa; bhagavataḥ—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; āśrayet—should take shelter of; mumukṣuḥ—anyone desiring liberation.

**Перевод:**

**Even if he be distressed or degraded, any person who chants the holy name of the Lord, having heard it from a bona fide spiritual master, is immediately purified. Even if he chants the Lord's name jokingly or by chance, he and anyone who hears him are freed from all sins. Therefore how can anyone seeking disentanglement from the material clutches avoid chanting the name of Lord Śeṣa? Of whom else should one take shelter?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

And let alone His form, even His name is so noble that by chanting it a terrible sinner gets purified. His name destroys all sins? If so, chanted how? In distress or in joking, even if the name is heard it purifies one. Whom else can we worship other than Śeṣa? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

His greatness was described above. Here the greatness of His name is described. A person with a deadly disease gets relief by uttering His name. A terrible sinner gets purified by the same act. Not only that—having become purified, the sinner and suffering persons are themselves capable of purifying others. Thus, whom else, other than Śeṣa, shall we worship? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Even remembering His name will suffice to get rid of sins. Then what does chanting of the name not achieve? None else has this greatness, thus Śeṣa’s *antaryāmī* Hari only is to be praised. This greatness has been seen in the case of Ajamila.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Mrgapati = Varaha, the incarnation of Viṣṇu. It is said in that context, “Vanagocharo mrgah” —these are Hiraṇyākṣa’s words. The *līlā* \[pastime\] of Varaha is bearing the earth, which Śeṣa has emulated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

One becomes pure when one chants His name in distress, or for joking or even for deceit. What will not happen if His name is uttered with great devotion?

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The extraordinary thing is that even His name purifies those who have fallen from grace. Saying this, Śeṣa is praised in two verses. The holy name instantly destroys sins as it was found in the case of Ajamila.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The subject matter of his song is stated in the next five stanzas. Sattva and other *guṇas* are incapable of producing the Mahattattva, etc. without being gracefully glanced at by Him. He is both the efficient and material cause of the universe. Without His grace, who can know Him?

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

He has taken this form only to bless His devotees. His form is pure goodness, which means a blend of strength, knowledge and other virtues. It does not mean *sattva guṇa* \[the mode of mundane goodness\] contaminated with rajas \[passion\] or tamas \[ignorance\]. He executed many heroic deeds for His devotees to meditate upon and become emancipated.

### Text 12

*मूर्धन्यर्पितमणुवत्सहस्रमूर्ध्नो*  
*भूगोलं सगिरिसरित्समुद्रसत्त्वम् ।*  
*आनन्त्यादनिमितविक्रमस्य भूम्नः*  
*को वीर्याण्यधि गणयेत्सहस्रजिह्वः ॥१२॥*

*mūrdhany arpitam aṇuvat sahasra-mūrdhno*  
*bhū-golaṁ sagiri-sarit-samudra-sattvam*  
*ānantyād animita-vikramasya bhūmnaḥ*  
*ko vīryāṇy adhi gaṇayet sahasra-jihvaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūrdhani—on a hood or head; arpitam—fixed; aṇu-vat—just like an atom; sahasra-mūrdhnaḥ—of Ananta, who has thousands of hoods; bhū-golam—this universe; sa-giri-sarit-samudra-sattvam—with many mountains, trees, oceans and living entities; ānantyāt—due to being unlimited; animita-vikramasya—whose power is immeasurable; bhūmnaḥ—the Supreme Lord; kaḥ—who; vīryāṇi—potencies; adhi—indeed; gaṇayet—can count; sahasra-jihvaḥ—although having thousands of tongues.

**Перевод:**

**Because the Lord is unlimited, no one can estimate His power. This entire universe, filled with its many great mountains, rivers, oceans, trees and living entities, is resting just like an atom on one of His many thousands of hoods. Is there anyone, even with thousands of tongues, who can describe His glories?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The earthen sphere along with mountains. *Sattvāni* = beings. Only a thousand tongued person can count.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Even a man endowed with a thousand faces cannot describe the greatness of Śeṣa who bears on His head the earth like a mustard seed. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Even Śeṣa’s bearing of the earth on His hood is due to Hari’s \[the Lord’s\] presence in Him. Will even the thousand-tongued Śeṣa be able to praise Him? This clearly indicates Śeṣa’s *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\] and not Śeṣa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The earth rests like an atom on only one head. Sattvani = the creatures. Even with a thousand tongues, who can count His virtues?

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The fact that God’s form is infinite, in spite of appearing to have a small stature, is brought out here by comparing the earth to an atom. None can count His virtues.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**
