Even His name heard from the elders or teachers, or uttered in distress or in a jovial mood will instantly remove all the sins of those persons. How can an aspirant approach anyone else? When the worship of Śeṣa who is an “part” (amsa) of God is capable of producing such results, what is the worship of God Himself incapable of achieving?

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

For that reason, He takes various forms of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc. His form is pure goodness without a trace of passion and ignorance.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Even a thousand-tongued person cannot count His virtues, thus who else can? It is said, “They return because their arrows are exhausted, not because of the earth or the sky, similarly they withdraw from praising because their intellect is exhausted, not because the virtues of Nārāyaṇa are exhausted.”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

His extraordinary and noble strength is to benefit others. He bears the earth on His head like an atom. Even the thousand-tongued Śeṣa cannot count His virtues. This evidently cannot be a praise addressed to Śeṣa.

### Text 13

*एवम्प्रभावो भगवाननन्तो*  
*दुरन्तवीर्योरुगुणानुभावः ।*  
*मूले रसायाः स्थित आत्मतन्त्रो*  
*यो लीलया क्ष्मां स्थितये बिभर्ति ॥१३॥*

*evam-prabhāvo bhagavān ananto*  
*duranta-vīryoru-guṇānubhāvaḥ*  
*mūle rasāyāḥ sthita ātma-tantro*  
*yo līlayā kṣmāṁ sthitaye bibharti*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam-prabhāvaḥ—who is so powerful; bhagavān—the Supreme Personality of Godhead; anantaḥ—Ananta; duranta-vīrya—insurmountable prowess; uru—great; guṇa-anubhāvaḥ—possessing transcendental qualities and glories; mūle—at the base; rasāyāḥ—of the lower planetary systems; sthitaḥ—existing; ātma-tantraḥ—completely self-sufficient; yaḥ—who; līlayā—easily; kṣmām—the universe; sthitaye—for its maintenance; bibharti—sustains.

**Перевод:**

**There is no end to the great and glorious qualities of that powerful Lord Anantadeva. Indeed, His prowess is unlimited. Though self-sufficient, He Himself is the support of everything. He resides beneath the lower planetary systems and easily sustains the entire universe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He who has infinite strength, whose virtues and capabilities are many, is supported by Himself and stays at the bottom of the earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Does He bear this earth being subject to His *karma* \[reactions to past activities\]? “No,” is the reply. His strength is infinite, His virtues endless, thus, it is only a pastime. He is not subject to any *karma*, rather He bears out of kindness only. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Śuka concludes this prayer stating extraordinary qualities which are found in Śeṣa. He has infinite prowess like this. Thus, the word Ananta is used who has many, many virtues. He is independent and not subjected to the influence of *karma*, thus He bears the universe only for *līlā* (pastime) and for the welfare of the world.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Although the Lord's form appears to have a small finite size, it is infinite. So the Bhū-maṇḍala is just an atom.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The preposition *dus* is in the privative sense. \[Note from the translator: There are many instances in *Bhāgavatam* when the word *duranta* is used to state God’s attributes meaning “infinite” and not “tragic” as sometimes construed\].

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Evaṁ prabhāvaḥ* = has the qualities as mentioned above.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

*Duranta* means having no end; infinite. His virtues and prowess are many. He is not dependent on anyone else. He holds the earth aloft.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Now stating that He is the cause of the sustenance, how He bears the earth on his head is described. He is infinite in spite of His small appearance, so, in whom else shall we take refuge?

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

His valor is infinite. Śeṣa’s *antaryāmī* \[supersoul\] only lifted the earth from Rasātala, not Śeṣa. Obviously the character of a mixed praise is evident here.

### Text 14

*एता ह्येवेह नृभिरुपगन्तव्या गतयो यथाकर्मविनिर्मिता यथोपदेशमनु*  
*वर्णिताः कामान्कामयमानैः ॥१४॥*

*etā hy eveha nṛbhir upagantavyā gatayo yathā-karma-vinirmitā yathopadeśam anuvarṇitāḥ kāmān kāmayamānaiḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etāḥ—all these; hi—indeed; eva—certainly; iha—in this universe; nṛbhiḥ—by all living entities; upagantavyāḥ—achievable; gatayaḥ—destinations; yathā-karma—according to one's past activities; vinirmitāḥ—created; yathā-upadeśam—as instructed; anuvarṇitāḥ—described accordingly; kāmān—material enjoyment; kāmayamānaiḥ—by those who are desiring.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, as I heard of it from my spiritual master, I have fully described to you the creation of this material world according to the fruitive activities and desires of the conditioned souls. Those conditioned souls, who are full of material desires, achieve various situations in different planetary systems, and in this way they live within this material creation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The courses of those who covet so many things are these only. All these are attainable through *karma*. They have been described as taught to me.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Yathopadeśam* = as per the scriptures.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Śuka concludes the present topic. These are the worlds which persons attain when they perform *karma* \[actions\] with some desire or the other. They have been related to you as per the scriptures and per the tradition.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Śuka concludes. “I have narrated the different worlds attainable through fruitive activities “*Sakāmakarma*,” according to how I have heard them from my teachers. They are different and do not resemble each other.

### Text 15

*एतावतीर्हि राजन्पुंसः प्रवृत्तिलक्षणस्य धर्मस्य विपाकगतय उच्चावचा*  
*विसदृशा यथाप्रश्नं व्याचख्ये किमन्यत्कथयाम इति ॥१९॥*

*etāvatīr hi rājan puṁsaḥ pravṛtti-lakṣaṇasya dharmasya vipāka-gataya uccāvacā visadṛśā yathā-praśnaṁ vyācakhye kim anyat kathayāma iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etāvatīḥ—of such a kind; hi—certainly; rājan—O King; puṁsaḥ—of the human being; pravṛtti-lakṣaṇasya—symptomized by inclinations; dharmasya—of the execution of duties; vipāka-gatayaḥ—the resultant destinations; ucca-avacāḥ—high and low; visadṛśāḥ—different; yathā-praśnam—as you inquired; vyācakhye—I have described; kim anyat—what else; kathayāma—shall I speak; iti—thus.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, I have thus described how people generally act according to their different desires and, as a result, get different types of bodies in higher or lower planets. You inquired of these things from me, and I have explained to you whatever I have heard from authorities. What shall I speak of now?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Dear king, these are the places attainable by men who follow pravrtti *dharma* \[eligious activities performed by persons seeking elevation to higher planets or for economic prosperity, the final aim of which is sense gratification\]. I have answered according to your question. What else shall I narrate? \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The courses of the results of actions performed with desire are multifarious. They have been described to you. What else shall I relate? This is said to give an opportunity to the king to raise a fresh question which Śuka will answer subsequently.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

These are the courses of places which are attainable through sakāma*karma*. The place attainable by *niṣkāmakarma* is a different one which has not been stated. The place attainable by forbidden acts (*nishiddha karma*) is also not stated yet—it means these courses are high and low, not resembling one another.

By stating this is what has been described, Śuka implies that there are many other things to be known which have not been stated. “So tell me what I should narrate further,” is the question put to Parīkṣit.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

By those who have so many desires.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

As the high and low cannot be of a single nature, it is said visadisa = not resembling each other. Because there are many things that may be told, he asks, what else shall I narrate?

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The division of the world that I have narrated is according to the sastras \[scriptures\] and tradition. These are the places in the *brahmāṇḍa* which one can attain through fruitive work (sakāmakarma). Nothing has been stated by my own imagination. What more would you like to hear? These are the words you like to hear?

These are the words of Śuka addressed to Parīkṣit.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

This is possible for Him because He is endowed with wonderful powers that defy imagination and logic. His strength is boundless, His virtues numerous and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Ananta bears the earth, not out of reactions to past work, but as a pastime. Everything has been explained as per scriptures. What more shall I narrate?

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

What more would you like me to narrate?

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twenty-fifth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “The Glories of Lord Ananta.”

## Chapter 26 - A Description of the Hellish Planets

### Text 1

*राजोवाच*  
*महर्ष एतद्वैचित्र्यं लोकस्य कथमिति ॥१॥*

*rājovāca*  
*maharṣa etad vaicitryaṁ lokasya katham iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*rājā uvāca*—the King said; *maharṣe*—O great saint (Śukadeva Gosvāmī); *etat*—this; *vaicitryam*—variegatedness; *lokasya*—of the living entities; *katham*—how; *iti*—thus.

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī: My dear sir, why are the living entities put into different material situations? Kindly explain this to me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It was suggested that the joys and sorrows of the living entities are different by saying that they attain places which are graded. Parīkṣit asks the reason for the this statement.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In the last chapter, it was said that these are the resultant courses of *pravrtti dharma*, meaning that these are courses as a result of nishiddha i.e. forbidden deeds. Even in these *lokas* \[places or planets\] attainable through *Pravrtti karma*, there is gradation in the joys and sorrows of those who live here. What is it due to?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The reason for the differences in the courses of the living entities is asked.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Below the earth, in those holes, according to their sins. Śuka is addressed as maharṣi. Even a *ṛṣi* will be able to narrate these things, yet you are not merely a ṛṣi but a great *ṛṣi* \[maharṣi\]. Thus, there should be no difficulty for you in answering my question. This is implied in the address. The joys and sorrows of different persons are different. What is this due to?

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In this chapter, the hells are described. After hearing the differences in the high and low courses, the king asked the reason for the difference in the enjoyment there.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Recognizing Śuka’s grace on him for giving him an opportunity to question, Parīkṣit asks Śuka about the reason for the variety in enjoyments. By addressing him as a great sage he implies the doubt he wishes to be cleared.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

When Śuka said these are the courses of *pravrtti dharma*, it is implied that the courses of *adharma* are different. As in the case of *pravrtti dharma* \[fruitive action performed according to scripture\], the results of *adharma* \[irreligious action\] will also produce varied results. The king asks for the reason.

### Text 2

*ऋषिरुवाच*  
*त्रिगुणत्वात्कर्तुः श्रद्धया कर्मगतयः पृथग्विधाः सर्वा एव सर्वस्य*  
*तारतम्येन भवन्ति ॥२॥*

*ṛṣir uvāca*  
*tri-guṇatvāt kartuḥ śraddhayā karma-gatayaḥ pṛthag-vidhāḥ sarvā eva sarvasya tāratamyena bhavanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ṛṣiḥ uvāca*—the great saint (Śukadeva Gosvāmī) said; *tri-guṇatvāt*—because of the three modes of material nature; *kartuḥ*—of the worker; *śraddhayā*—because of the attitudes; *karma-gatayaḥ*—destinations resulting from activity; *pṛthak*—different; *vidhāḥ*—varieties; *sarvāḥ*—all; *eva*—thus; *sarvasya*—of all of them; *tāratamyena*—in different degrees; *bhavanti*—become possible.

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, in this material world there are three kinds of activities—those in the mode of goodness, the mode of passion and the mode of ignorance. Because all people are influenced by the three modes of material nature, the results of their activities are also divided into three. One who acts in the mode of goodness is religious and happy, one who acts in passion achieves mixed misery and happiness, and one who acts under the influence of ignorance is always unhappy and lives like an animal. Because of the varying degrees to which the living entities are influenced by the different modes of nature, their destinations are also of different varieties.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The answer is given saying that even though the action done by different people is the same, because of the difference in the attitude of the persons, the fruits reaped are different. A *sattvic* \[goodness\] faith gives happiness. A *rajas* \[passionate\] faith gives a mixture of joy and sorrow. The *tamas* \[ignorant\] faith gives misery and ignorance. There is gradation even in these faiths and hence the gradation in joys and sorrows.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

It is said, “the sage replied,” implying that Śuka has the knowledge of whatever Parīkṣit has asked. Faiths are of three kinds, *sattvic*, *rajas* and *tamas*. *Sattvic* \[in goodness\] faith begets *dharma* \[religion\] only. *Rajas* \[in passion\] faith begets both *dharma* and *adharma* \[irreligion\]. *Tamas* \[in ignorance\] faith begets *adharma* and infatuation. No living entity is either *sattvic*, *rajasic*, or *tamasic* always, rather they change from time to time, hence the variety found here.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The crux of the reply is that although the *dharma* that makes one attain *Bhūloka* is the same, gradation is found here due to the dissimilarity of faith in the performers, i.e association with the three modes of nature and past deeds. The agents, their perceptions, their faiths, and the resulting *karma* are threefold, the *sattvica*, the *rajasa* and the *tamasa*. It is said in *Bhagavad-gītā*, “a *sattvic* person is one who is devoid of attachment, who is not boastful, who is endowed with courage and cheer and who is unaffected by the accomplishment or non-accomplishment of his acts. A *rajasic* person is one who is attached to many things, who wants to enjoy the fruit of his *karma*, who is greedy, fond of violence, impure, joyous at times and depressed at other times. A *tamasic person* is one who is unjust, very naughty, arrogant, lazy, thinking of cheating others, always discontented and who never forgets the past mistakes of others.

Their understanding is also three-fold: that understanding by which one knows what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, what is to be feared and what is not to be feared, what is binding and what is liberating, is in the mode of goodness. That understanding which cannot distinguish between religion and irreligion, between action that should be done and action that should not be done, is in the mode of passion. That understanding which considers irreligion to be religion and religion to be irreligion, under the spell of illusion and darkness, and strives always in the wrong direction, is in the mode of ignorance.

Faith is also of three kinds: Men in the mode of goodness worship the demigods; those in the mode of passion worship the demons; and those in the mode of ignorance worship ghosts and spirits.

Actions are also of three types: That action which is regulated and which is performed without attachment, without love or hatred, and without desire for fruitive results is said to be in the mode of goodness. But action performed with great effort by one seeking to gratify his desires, and enacted from a sense of false ego, is called action in the mode of passion. That action performed in illusion, in disregard of scriptural injunctions, and without concern for future bondage or for violence or distress caused to others is said to be in the mode of ignorance.

This being the case, a *sattvic* performer endowed with *sattvic* perception and *sattvic* faith performs actions in goodness and attains infinite bliss. The *rajasic* performer will be endowed with the same *rajasa* perception and faith and will perform passionate actions as a result of which he obtains *Bhūloka,* etc. and enjoys limited happiness. A *tamasic* performer, endowed with ignorant perception and faith performs the same actions as the *rajasic* performer does, reaches *Bhūloka* and obtains more grief or sometimes only grief. \[Note: this commentary is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

To encourage real renunciation, the disgusting nature of hell is narrated. As hell is a place of utmost agony, good people will try to ward off the desire and actions which lead to hell, thereby obtaining detachment from the material world. “Dear great sage, how is it that one is happy and another miserable? Also how is it that there is a gradation in the happiness and misery of the people?” The question is answered by Śuka: it is due to different faiths of performers of good or bad deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The fruits are different when there is inequality. Even when there is equality of the three *guṇas* also, the effect is different for other reasons.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The living entity is bound by three *guṇas*—*sattva*, *rajas* and *tamas*. The faiths of the living entities depend upon these *guṇas* which are not uniform in all. The difference in enjoyment is due to the difference in their faiths in spite of doing the same deed. *Gītā* also says, “Those situated in the mode of goodness gradually go upward to the higher planets; those in the mode of passion live on the earthly planets; and those in the abominable mode of ignorance go down to the hellish worlds.”

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

If the same actions executed with different faiths cause a variety of results, then what to speak of when even the actions are different? This is the idea of the reply.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Śuka has said that there is gradation in the enjoyment of people as they attain different courses. The king asks the reason for this. Śuka replies saying that even if actions (*karma*) are the same, the faiths are varying and this begets varying results. Not merely that—the demigods worshiped are also different and each one bestows happiness on his worshippers according to his own nature and capacity. This has been elaborated in the *Gītā*. “I am in everyone’s heart as the Supersoul. As soon as one desires to worship some demigod, I make his faith steady so that he can devote himself to that particular deity. Endowed with such a faith, he endeavors to worship a particular demigod and obtains his desires. But in actuality these benefits are bestowed by Me alone. Those in goodness worship demigods, those in passion worship yakshas and demigods, and even rakshasas, whereas those in ignorance, worship the ghosts and spirits.”

### Text 3

*अथेदानीं प्रतिषिद्धलक्षणस्याधर्मस्य तथैव कर्तुः श्रद्धाया वैसादृश्यात्कर्मफलं*  
*विसदृशं भवति या ह्यनाद्यविद्यया कृतकामानां तत्परिणामलक्षणाः*  
*सृतयः सहस्रशः प्रवृत्तास्तासां प्राचुर्येणानुवर्णयिष्यामः ॥३॥*

*athedānīṁ pratiṣiddha-lakṣaṇasyādharmasya tathaiva kartuḥ śraddhāyā vaisādṛśyāt karma-phalaṁ visadṛśaṁ bhavati yā hy anādy-avidyayā kṛta-kāmānāṁ tat-pariṇāma-lakṣaṇāḥ sṛtayaḥ sahasraśaḥ pravṛttās tāsāṁ prācuryeṇānuvarṇayiṣyāmaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*atha*—thus; *idānīm*—now; *pratiṣiddha*—by what is forbidden; *lakṣaṇasya*—symptomized; *adharmasya*—of impious activities; *tathā*—so also; *eva*—certainly; *kartuḥ*—of the performer; *śraddhāyāḥ*—of faith; *vaisādṛśyāt*—by the difference; *karma-phalam*—the reaction of fruitive activities; *visadṛśam*—different; *bhavati*—is; *yā*—which; *hi*—indeed; *anādi*—from time immemorial; *avidyayā*—by ignorance; *kṛta*—performed; *kāmānām*—of persons possessing many lusty desires; *tat-pariṇāma-lakṣaṇāḥ*—the symptoms of the results of such impious desires; *sṛtayaḥ*—hellish conditions of life; *sahasraśaḥ*—by thousands upon thousands; *pravṛttāḥ*—resulted; *tāsām*—them; *prācuryeṇa*—very widely; *anuvarṇayiṣyāmaḥ*—I shall explain.

**Перевод:**

**Just as by executing various pious activities one achieves different positions in heavenly life, by acting impiously one achieves different positions in hellish life. Those who are activated by the material mode of ignorance engage in impious activities, and according to the extent of their ignorance, they are placed in different grades of hellish life. If one acts in the mode of ignorance because of madness, his resulting misery is the least severe. One who acts impiously but knows the distinction between pious and impious activities is placed in a hell of intermediate severity. And for one who acts impiously and ignorantly because of atheism, the resultant hellish life is the worst. Because of ignorance, every living entity has been carried by various desires into thousands of different hellish planets since time immemorial. I shall try to describe them as far as possible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Faith in ignorance makes one do prohibited acts—and there is gradation in that also due to desires obtained from association with ignorance (*avidyā*) from a long, long time. This leads to various types of hells which I will presently describe.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The earth, heaven and Patala *lokas* are places attainable by faith in goodness and pious activities. The place that will be attained by *adharma* is hell, which will presently be narrated. One who does forbidden acts like the killing of a *brāhmaṇa* will be a sinner. As there is variety in *dharma*, there is variety in *adharma* also. When a misdeed is done accidentally, the punishment is small. When it is done intentionally, the punishment is great. Even there, when a non believer does it, it will bring greater punishment. The reason for evil deeds is the living entities’ association with *avidyā* \[ignorance\] from beginingless time. How *avidyā* contacts the *jīva* is difficult to explain. The *jīva* performs actions according to the desires induced by this *avidyā* and the resultant reactions to such deeds are numerous, but I will narrate only the prominent among them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Just as there is gradation in the result of happiness for those who observe *pravrtti karma* \[prescribed activities\] with faith in goodness, there is gradation in the results of misdeeds also which are done with faith in the mode of ignorance, hence, the ensuing miseries vary from person to person. *Avidyākāma* means the desire to obtain the fruit, result \[*phala*\]. *Karma* means the subtle impression of such desires. Even sacrifices can be taken as *avidyā* with a desire to obtain the fruits of such sacrifices. Whatever misdeeds performed exist in the living entity in a subtle form. Because of the dissimilarity of these, the miseries suffered are also dissimilar. The results attained through such misdeeds number in the thousands. Actually, they cannot be numbered—thus, it is impossible to narrate all of them in detail. Therefore, I will narrate only a few important among them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is forbidden by the scriptures is evil. People do it with different levels of faith. The *jīvas* are under the influence of a beginingless avidyā which breeds desires according to which they act and as a result of which they get into these places called hell. They are thousands in number but I will describe to you the important among them. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Viśvanātha Cakravartī and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Because the ignorance is different in different *jīvas*, their acts lead to different miseries. The sins which are a result of the beginingless *avidyā* of each *jīva* lead them to different hells which I will presently describe.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Having replied to the king’s question, Śuka sets out to describe the hells which are attained as a result of *adharma*. Just as there is variety in the faith of those who observe *dharma*, there is variety in the faith of those who perform *adharma* also. This is responsible for the variety in the misery that results. For this purpose only God has designed thousands of hells. But I will narrate to you only a few of them which are prominent, since it is not possible to describe them all.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The results of *adharma* meaning that which is forbidden by the *Vedas*, are graded according to the faith of the performers just like in prvrtti *dharma* \[performance of pious activities in accord with the *Vedas*\]. The results are different because of the influence of ignorance, desires and actions, all of which have no beginning. The result of *adharma* is that one is sent to hells, which are thousands in number. I cannot narrate all of them because they are countless. I will narrate to you only a few important among them.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

So it is not the same for all people. The *jīvas* are under the influence of *avidyā* (ignorance), desires and actions from a beginingless time and perform misdeeds accordingly. The results of such misdeeds shall be narrated to you briefly.

### Text 4

*राजोवाच*  
*नरका नाम भगवन् किं देशविशेषा अथवा बहिस्त्रिलोक्या*  
*आहोस्विदन्तराल इति ॥४॥*

*rājovāca*  
*narakā nāma bhagavan kiṁ deśa-viśeṣā athavā bahis tri-lokyā āhosvid antarāla iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*rājā uvāca*—the King said; *narakāḥ*—the hellish regions; *nāma*—named; *bhagavan*—O my Lord; *kim*—whether; *deśa-viśeṣāḥ*—a particular country; *athavā*—or; *bahiḥ*—outside; *tri-lokyāḥ*—the three worlds (the universe); *āhosvit*—or; *antarāle*—in the intermediate spaces within the universe; *iti*—thus.

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī: My dear lord, are the hellish regions outside the universe, within the covering of the universe, or in different places on this planet?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Are the regions in the three worlds only, or beyond the *brahmāṇḍa* or between the enclosures of *brahmāṇḍa*?

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The king then asks about these places of punishment—”Are they regions of the earth or do they exist between the other *lokas* already narrated?” “Outside the three worlds” means in the outer enclosures of the *brahmāṇḍa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Because nothing is said to a person who does not ask, Parīkṣit questions. “Are they different regions? Or are they names given to intense misery? If they are different regions, in what direction are they situated, at what depth or height?”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He who does what is forbidden will get the fruit of his misdeed which is different from person to person due to a difference in their faiths. He who does an evil deed by accident gets a small punishment, he who does it knowingly, out of infatuation, is in the middle and receives greater punishment than the former. He who decries the authority of the *Vedas*, argues that what he has done is right and performs the misdeed, receives the greatest punishment. “Although they \[hells\] exist in the thousands, I will narrate to you only the important ones.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The fruits of *dharma*, i.e. enjoyment on the earth, within the subterranean lokas and in the heavenly planets, have been described. The fruits of *adharma* also remain to be described—they are the miseries experienced in the hells. Whether one performs *dharma* or *adharma*, the difference in the faiths of the performers accounts for the differences of the results obtained.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Śuka is addressed as *bhagavān* which means a person who has knowledge. The implication is, “Since you are omniscient, kindly narrate to me all I have asked for.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The King asks the sage where the hells are situated; whether on the earth itself, outside the *brahmāṇḍa* \[universe\]*,* inside the *brahmāṇḍa* or somewhere else.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The king asks where the hells are situated. “Is it here only or some where else?”

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Are they regions on earth or do they fall between the *lokas* or are they situated outside the *brahmāṇḍa*?

### Text 5

*ऋषिरुवाच*  
*अन्तराल एव त्रिजगत्यास्तु दिशि दक्षिणस्यामधस्ताद्भूमेरुपरिष्टाच्च*  
*जलाद्यस्यामग्निष्वात्तादयः पितृगणा दिशि स्वानां गोत्राणां परमेण*  
*समाधिना सत्या एवाशिष आशासाना निवसन्ति ॥५॥*

*ṛṣir uvāca*  
*antarāla eva tri-jagatyās tu diśi dakṣiṇasyām adhastād bhūmer upariṣṭāc ca jalād yasyām agniṣvāttādayaḥ pitṛ-gaṇā diśi svānāṁ gotrāṇāṁ parameṇa samādhinā satyā evāśiṣa āśāsānā nivasanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ṛṣiḥ uvāca*—the great sage replied; *antarāle*—in the intermediate space; *eva*—certainly; *tri-jagatyāḥ*—of the three worlds; *tu*—but; *diśi*—in the direction; *dakṣiṇasyām*—southern; *adhastāt*—beneath; *bhūmeḥ*—on the earth; *upariṣṭāt*—a little above; *ca*—and; *jalāt*—the Garbhodaka Ocean; *yasyām*—in which; *agniṣvāttā-ādayaḥ*—headed by Agniṣvāttā; *pitṛ-gaṇāḥ*—the persons known as *pitās; diśi*—direction; *svānām*—their own; *gotrāṇām*—of the families; *parameṇa*—with great; *samādhinā*—absorption in thoughts of the Lord; *satyāḥ*—in truth; *eva*—certainly; *āśiṣaḥ*—blessings; *āśāsānāḥ*—desiring; *nivasanti*—they live.

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Śukadeva Gosvāmī answered: All the hellish planets are situated in the intermediate space between the three worlds and the Garbhodaka Ocean. They lie on the southern side of the universe, beneath Bhū-maṇḍala, and slightly above the water of the Garbhodaka Ocean. Pitṛloka is also located in this region between the Garbhodaka Ocean and the lower planetary systems. All the residents of Pitṛloka, headed by Agniṣvāttā, meditate in great samādhi on the Supreme Personality of Godhead and always wish their families well.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Śuka replies, “They \[hells\] are situated inside the *brahmāṇḍa*, to the south, below the earth and above the inside waters of *brahmāṇḍa*.” In these areas to the south, groups of forefathers like the Agnishvattas and others live wishing welfare for their descendents. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Śuka replies. “They are regions where there is so much of misery. They are within the *brahmāṇḍa*, to the south of Bhārata-khaṇḍa, below the earth and above the fetal waters of *brahmāṇḍa*.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because they \[the Pitrs\] wish the welfare of their clans, these people get some relief.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Below the Patala and above the waters.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

To the south of the Bhārata-khaṇḍa, below the seven netherworld *lokas* and above the water inside the *brahmāṇḍa* is situated the water called Garbhodaka. The word “others” indicates Agnishvatta and others forming the Pitṛ group. Who should be included in the group of pitrs is stated by Manu. These Pitṛs are different for different people. The sons of *Virāt* (Somasadas) are the Pitṛs for the Sādhyas. The sons of Kashayapa known as the Agnishvattas are Pitṛs for the demigods. For the Daityas, Danāvas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Serpents, Rakshasas, birds and Kinnaras, the sons of Atri known as Barhishadas are the Pitṛs. For the *brāhmaṇa*, the Somapas are the Pitrs; for *kṣatriyas* it is the Havirbhujas, for vaiśyas it is Aajyapas, for Śūdras, the Śukalins are the Pitṛs. The Somapas are Sukra’s sons, the Havirbhujas are Angirasa’s sons. The Aajyapas are Pulastya’s sons, the Śukalins are Vasista’s sons.” Wishing welfare for those who come into their respective clans, the Pitrs bestow all prosperity and progeny upon the descendents who worship them.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Inside the *brahmāṇḍa*, below the earth and above the waters. The netherworlds are seven, below them is hell, below hell is darkness and below that is water. The learned say that thereafter is the shell of *brahmāṇḍa*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Śuka replies that they are within the *brahmāṇḍa*, below the earth and above the fetal waters.

### Text 6

*यत्र ह वाव भगवान् पितृराजो वैवस्वतः स्वविषयं प्रापितेषु स्वपुरुषैर्जन्तुषु*  
*सम्परेतेषु यथाकर्मावद्यं दोषमेवानुल्लङ्घितभगवच्छासनः सगणो दमं*  
*धारयति ॥६॥*

*yatra ha vāva bhagavān pitṛ-rājo vaivasvataḥ sva-viṣayaṁ prāpiteṣu sva-puruṣair jantuṣu sampareteṣu yathā-karmāvadyaṁ doṣam evānullaṅghita-bhagavac-chāsanaḥ sagaṇo damaṁ dhārayati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yatra*—where; *ha vāva*—indeed; *bhagavān*—the most powerful; *pitṛ-rājaḥ*—Yamarāja, the king of the *pitās; vaivasvataḥ*—the son of the sun-god; *sva-viṣayam*—his own kingdom; *prāpiteṣu*—when caused to reach; *sva-puruṣaiḥ*—by his own messengers; *jantuṣu*—the human beings; *sampareteṣu*—dead; *yathā-karma-avadyam*—according to how much they have violated the rules and regulations of conditional life; *doṣam*—the fault; *eva*—certainly; *anullaṅghita-bhagavat-śāsanaḥ*—who never oversteps the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s order; *sagaṇaḥ*—along with his followers; *damam*—punishment; *dhārayati*—executes.

**Перевод:**

**The King of the pitās is Yamarāja, the very powerful son of the sun-god. He resides in Pitṛloka with his personal assistants and, while abiding by the rules and regulations set down by the Supreme Lord, has his agents, the Yamadūtas, bring all the sinful men to him immediately upon their death. After bringing them within his jurisdiction, he properly judges them according to their specific sinful activities and sends them to one of the many hellish planets for suitable punishments.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

According to the crime committed, the crime itself affords the punishment to those who have transgressed the rules established by God.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Yama lives there. When his servants bring the dead to his Loka \[planet\] and present them before him, he, assisted by his servants, punishes them strictly according to their evils. It is Nārāyaṇa’s ruling that he should look after this job, which he does with obedience.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

According to their sins. Never transgressing the orders of Hari.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Svavishaya means his kingdom. This process is meant to punish according to the evils they have done to turn them towards God.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Yatra = in those hells. Svavishaya = his land according to the wrong deeds done by them. He frightens the souls desiring to turn their mentality towards God. He transforms the wrong doings into punishments because he will never transgress the commands of Brahmā, the creator and Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He punishes according to the severity of the misdeeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

There, Yama, Sūrya’s son, who was appointed by Lord Hari for this purpose, punishes the sinners according to their sins. Yama is capable of the duty assigned.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Yama gives punishment to those that are brought to his kingdom by his servants, at the behest of Nārāyaṇa. His punishment is in accordance with the evil of the persons.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Yama punishes according to the severity of the misdeeds they have committed.

### Text 7

*तत्र हैके नरकानेकविंशतिं गणयन्ति अथ तांस्ते राजन्नामरूपलक्षणतो*  
*ऽनुक्रमिष्यामस्तामिस्रोऽन्धतामिस्रो रौरवो महारौरवः कुम्भीपाकः कालसूत्रमसि*  
*पत्रवनं सूकरमुखमन्धकूपः कृमिभोजनः सन्दंशस्तप्तसूर्मिर्वज्रकण्टकशाल्मली*  
*वैतरणी पूयोदः प्राणरोधो विशसनं लालाभक्षः सारमेयादनमवीचिरयःपा*  
*नमिति । किञ्च क्षारकर्दमो रक्षोगणभोजनः शूलप्रोतो दन्दशूकोऽवटनि*  
*रोधनः पर्यावर्तनः सूचीमुखमित्यष्टाविंशतिर्नरका विविधयातनाभूमयः ॥७॥*

*tatra haike narakān eka-viṁśatiṁ gaṇayanti atha tāṁs te rājan nāma-rūpa-lakṣaṇato ‘nukramiṣyāmas tāmisro ‘ndhatāmisro rauravo mahārauravaḥ kumbhīpākaḥ kālasūtram asipatravanaṁ sūkaramukham andhakūpaḥ kṛmibhojanaḥ sandaṁśas taptasūrmir vajrakaṇṭaka-śālmalī vaitaraṇī pūyodaḥ prāṇarodho viśasanaṁ lālābhakṣaḥ sārameyādanam avīcir ayaḥpānam iti; kiñca kṣārakardamo rakṣogaṇa-bhojanaḥ śūlaproto dandaśūko ‘vaṭa-nirodhanaḥ paryāvartanaḥ sūcīmukham ity aṣṭā-viṁśatir narakā vividha-yātanā-bhūmayaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatra*—there; *ha*—certainly; *eke*—some; *narakān*—the hellish planets; *eka-viṁśatim*—twenty-one; *gaṇayanti*—count; *atha*—therefore; *tān*—them; *te*—unto you; *rājan*—O King; *nāma-rūpa-lakṣaṇataḥ*—according to their names, forms and symptoms; *anukramiṣyāmaḥ*—we shall outline one after another; *tāmisraḥ*—Tāmisra; *andha-tāmisraḥ*—Andhatāmisra; *rauravaḥ*—Raurava; *mahā-rauravaḥ*—Mahāraurava; *kumbhī-pākaḥ*—Kumbhīpāka; *kāla-sūtram*—Kālasūtra; *asi-patravanam*—Asi-patravana; *sūkara-mukham*—Sūkaramukha; *andha-kūpaḥ*—Andhakūpa; *kṛmi-bhojanaḥ*—Kṛmibhojana; *sandaṁśaḥ*—Sandaṁśa; *tapta-sūrmiḥ*—Taptasūrmi; *vajra-kaṇṭaka-śālmalī*—Vajrakaṇṭaka-śālmalī; *vaitaraṇī*—Vaitaraṇī; *pūyodaḥ*—Pūyoda; *prāṇa-rodhaḥ*—Prāṇarodha; *viśasanam*—Viśasana; *lālā-bhakṣaḥ*—Lālābhakṣa; *sārameyādanam*—Sārameyādana; *avīciḥ*—Avīci; *ayaḥ-pānam*—Ayaḥpāna; *iti*—thus; *kiñca*—some more; *kṣāra-kardamaḥ*—Kṣārakardama; *rakṣaḥ-gaṇa-bhojanaḥ*—Rakṣogaṇa-bhojana; *śūla-protaḥ*—Śūlaprota; *danda-śūkaḥ*—Dandaśūka; *avaṭa-nirodhanaḥ*—Avaṭa-nirodhana; *paryāvartanaḥ*—Paryāvartana; *sūcī-mukham*—Sūcīmukha; *iti*—in this way; *aṣṭā-viṁśatiḥ*—twenty-eight; *narakāḥ*—hellish planets; *vividha*—various; *yātanā-bhūmayaḥ*—lands of suffering in hellish conditions.

**Перевод:**

**Some authorities say that there is a total of twenty-one hellish planets, and some say twenty-eight. My dear King, I shall outline all of them according to their names, forms and symptoms. The names of the different hells are as follows: Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Raurava, Mahāraurava, Kumbhīpāka, Kālasūtra, Asi-patravana, Sūkaramukha, Andhakūpa, Kṛmibhojana, Sandaṁśa, Taptasūrmi, Vajrakaṇṭaka-śālmalī, Vaitaraṇī, Pūyoda, Prāṇarodha, Viśasana, Lālābhakṣa, Sārameyādana, Avīci, Ayaḥpāna, Kṣārakardama, Rakṣogaṇa-bhojana, Śūlaprota, Dandaśūka, Avaṭa-nirodhana, Paryāvartana and Sūcīmukha. All these planets are meant for punishing the living entities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is said according to another reckoning that there are twenty-eight in number.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The learned say that the important ones among them are twenty-one in number. I will describe them to you, one after the other, by their names, characteristics and the type of punishment that is dispensed there. They are named Tamisra to Ayahpana. Vajrakantaka-Shalmali is the name of one, and Avichi is another (if we split like this it will be exactly 21). They are further described in the next verse starting with the word “Suchimukha” and so on. This list consists of seven which taken together with the first twenty-one make twenty-eight in all.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The hells are twenty-one in number, seven are main. Some say there are many others. Here the grief is very high.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Tamisra and others are twenty-one in number, and with the seven enumerated earlier they become twenty-eight.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The main ones are seven in number. Even then the Pauranikas think otherwise. I will narrate that to you because as a king you have to follow the right path and guide your subjects also in the right path.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Another view is that the hells are twenty-eight in number where *jīvas* are subjected to great pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The important among them are.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Some great sages say that the hells are twenty-one in number—they are the main ones. I will narrate to you those hells by their names, features and the mode of punishment given there. They are twenty-one counting from Tamisra to Ayahpana; Ksharakardama to Paryavartanah are another seven—thus the total becomes twenty-eight. These are the places of utmost pain for evil-doers.

### Text 8

*तत्र यस्तु परवित्तापत्यकलत्राण्यपहरति स हि कालपाशबद्धो*  
*यमपुरुषैरतिभयानकैस्तामिस्रे नरके बलान्निपात्यते अनशना*  
*नुदपानदण्डताडनसन्तर्जनादिभिर्यातनाभिर्यात्यमानो जन्तुर्यत्र कश्मल*  
*मासादित एकदैव मूर्च्छामुपयाति तामिस्रप्राये ॥८॥*

*tatra yas tu para-vittāpatya-kalatrāṇy apaharati sa hi kāla-pāśa-baddho yama-puruṣair ati-bhayānakais tāmisre narake balān nipātyate anaśanānudapāna-daṇḍa-tāḍana-santarjanādibhir yātanābhir yātyamāno jantur yatra kaśmalam āsādita ekadaiva mūrcchām upayāti tāmisra-prāye.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatra*—in those hellish planets; *yaḥ*—a person who; *tu*—but; *para-vitta-apatya-kalatrāṇi*—the money, wife and children of another; *apaharati*—takes away; *saḥ*—that person; *hi*—certainly; *kāla-pāśa-baddhaḥ*—being bound by the ropes of time or Yamarāja; *yama-puruṣaiḥ*—by the assistants of Yamarāja; *ati-bhayānakaiḥ*—who are very fearful; *tāmisre narake*—into the hell known as Tāmisra; *balāt*—by force; *nipātyate*—is thrown; *anaśana*—starvation; *anudapāna*—without water; *daṇḍa-tāḍana*—beaten with rods; *santarjana-ādibhiḥ*—by scolding and so on; *yātanābhiḥ*—by severe punishments; *yātyamānaḥ*—being punished; *jantuḥ*—the living entity; *yatra*—where; *kaśmalam*—misery; *āsāditaḥ*—obtained; *ekadā*—sometimes; *eva*—certainly; *mūrcchām*—fainting; *upayāti*—obtains; *tāmisra-prāye*—in that condition, which is almost entirely dark.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, a person who appropriates another’s legitimate wife, children or money is arrested at the time of death by the fierce Yamadūtas, who bind him with the rope of time and forcibly throw him into the hellish planet known as Tāmisra. On this very dark planet, the sinful man is chastised by the Yamadūtas, who beat and rebuke him. He is starved, and he is given no water to drink. Thus the wrathful assistants of Yamarāja cause him severe suffering, and sometimes he faints from their chastisement.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The grief in the hells differs from person to person because of the difference in the evil acts they have committed.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

From here on, each of them is separately described. He who snatches others’ money and belongings are brought here by Yama’s servants and bound with “Yama’s ropes” and then thrown into a hell called Tamisra. There, he has no food or water—only darkness abounds. He is beaten and threatened by Yama’s servants and until he faints.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The individual hells and the mode of punishment in each are described. They are subjected to acute pain by Yama’s servants—sometimes they faint also.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The misdeed itself transforms into punishment. *Bhagavān* means Brahmā here—by his order. The intention of punishment is to turn the *jīvas* mentally towards God. Or “Bhagavatshasana” means the *Vedas* only.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Yatyamana = being subjected to great pain. Tamisrapraye = abounding in darkness.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Yatyamana = being subjected to pain. Ekadaiva = instantly.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He described in detail the variety of pain experienced due to the variety in the evil deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The different hells that are attained by different evils are elaborately described from here on. A person who snatches others’ wives and belongings ends up in Tamisra, where there is darkness. He is beaten and threatened by Yama’s servants. Being subjected to pain, he immediately becomes unconscious. The names Tamisra and others have both etymology and usage.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Yatyamana = being tormented. By saying “sometimes,” Śuka opines that at some other times, the sinner does not faint.

### Text 9

*एवमेवान्धतामिस्रे यस्तु वञ्चयित्वा पुरुषं दारादीनुपयुङ्क्ते यत्र शरीरी*  
*निपात्यमानो यातनास्थो वेदनया नष्टमतिर्नष्टदृष्टिश्च भवति यथा*  
*वनस्पतिर्वृश्च्यमानमूलस्तस्मादन्धतामिस्रं तमुपदिशन्ति ॥९॥*

*evam evāndhatāmisre yas tu vañcayitvā puruṣaṁ dārādīn upayuṅkte yatra śarīrī nipātyamāno yātanā-stho vedanayā naṣṭa-matir naṣṭa-dṛṣṭiś ca bhavati yathā vanaspatir vṛścyamāna-mūlas tasmād andhatāmisraṁ tam upadiśanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*evam*—in this way; *eva*—certainly; *andhatāmisre*—in the hellish planet known as Andhatāmisra; *yaḥ*—the person who; *tu*—but; *vañcayitvā*—cheating; *puruṣam*—another person; *dāra-ādīn*—the wife and children; *upayuṅkte*—enjoys; *yatra*—where; *śarīrī*—the embodied person; *nipātyamānaḥ*—being forcibly thrown; *yātanā-sthaḥ*—always situated in extremely miserable conditions; *vedanayā*—by such suffering; *naṣṭa*—lost; *matiḥ*—whose consciousness; *naṣṭa*—lost; *dṛṣṭiḥ*—whose sight; *ca*—also; *bhavati*—becomes; *yathā*—as much as; *vanaspatiḥ*—the trees; *vṛścyamāna*—being cut; *mūlaḥ*—whose root; *tasmāt*—because of this; *andhatāmisram*—Andhatāmisra; *tam*—that; *upadiśanti*—they call.

**Перевод:**

**The destination of a person who slyly cheats another man and enjoys his wife and children is the hell known as Andhatāmisra. There his condition is exactly like that of a tree being chopped at its roots. Even before reaching Andhatāmisra, the sinful living being is subjected to various extreme miseries. These afflictions are so severe that he loses his intelligence and sight. It is for this reason that learned sages call this hell Andhatāmisra.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Puruṣa* means husband. For having deceived him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

In Andhatamisra the punishment is like in Tamisra. He who snatches others’ belongings or women and enjoys them is put in Andatamisra. He will be subjected to so much of punishment here that he becomes unconscious very often. Unconsciousness is what distinguishes Andhatamisra from Tamisra.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Vrshchyamana mulah means cut at the bottom. There is no vision because of the blinding darkness. In Tamisra there is no consciousness due to fainting. In Andha Tamisra the eyes are inoperative because of the darkness.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Puruṣa* means the master.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

He who cheats others by saying, “she is my sister,” “she is my disciple” and so on falls in the blinding hell where he becomes unconscious. That is why it is called darkness.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Puruṣa* = the owner of wives and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Andahatamisra is described. A person who cheats others and enjoys their women and property falls into this hell where he is tormented in the same way as in Tamisra. The difference is that he loses his sight, loses his mind and falls like a tree cut at the bottom of its trunk.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Where in Tamisra the evil doer is subjected to pain and instantly becomes unconscious. It is just darkness there.

He who cheats the owner and snatches his wife and other belongings is pushed into this hell.

He loses his consciousness like a tree cut at the bottom of its trunk.

### Text 10

*यस्त्विह वा एतदहमिति ममेदमिति भूतद्रोहेण केवलं*  
*स्वकुटुम्बमेवानुदिनं प्रपुष्णाति स तदिह विहाय स्वयमेव तदशुभेन रौरवे*  
*निपतति ॥१०॥*

*yas tv iha vā etad aham iti mamedam iti bhūta-droheṇa kevalaṁ sva-kuṭumbam evānudinaṁ prapuṣṇāti sa tad iha vihāya svayam eva tad-aśubhena raurave nipatati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—one who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *etat*—this body; *aham*—I; *iti*—thus; *mama*—mine; *idam*—this; *iti*—thus; *bhūta-droheṇa*—by envy of other living entities; *kevalam*—alone; *sva-kuṭumbam*—his family members; *eva*—only; *anudinam*—day to day; *prapuṣṇāti*—supports; *saḥ*—such a person; *tat*—that; *iha*—here; *vihāya*—giving up; *svayam*—personally; *eva*—certainly; *tat*—of that; *aśubhena*—by the sin; *raurave*—in Raurava; *nipatati*—he falls down.

**Перевод:**

**A person who accepts his body as his self works very hard day and night for money to maintain his own body and the bodies of his wife and children. While working to maintain himself and his family, he may commit violence against other living entities. Such a person is forced to give up his body and his family at the time of death, when he suffers the reaction for his envy of other creatures by being thrown into the hell called Raurava.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He who considers the body as himself and wealth as his and in this consciousness raises his family. Because of this bad act.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“This body is myself. This earth is mine.” These are the misconceptions which lead to Raurava hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It means for him, the same thing happens.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He who feels the body is himself, the money is his, and oppresses all others, falls into Raurava. If he does not torment others, he does not come here.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Tat* means the family.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He who lives with the mentality of “I am,” this body and “it is mine,” in relationship to his family, nourishing only them, discards both the body and family here and enters hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Raurava is described. The animals killed by him do not become Rurus, for they do not have such a *karma* to be born as Rurus. But the misdeeds themselves take the form of Rurus and inflict misery on the evil-doers.

### Text 11

*ये त्विह यथैवामुना विहिंसिता जन्तवः परत्र यमयातनामुपगतं त एव*  
*रुरवो भूत्वा तथा तमेव विहिंसन्ति तस्माद्रौरवमित्याहू रुरुरिति*  
*सर्पादतिक्रूरसत्त्वस्यापदेशः ॥११॥*

*ye tv iha yathaivāmunā vihiṁsitā jantavaḥ paratra yama-yātanām upagataṁ ta eva ruravo bhūtvā tathā tam eva vihiṁsanti tasmād rauravam ity āhū rurur iti sarpād ati-krūra-sattvasyāpadeśaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—those who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *yathā*—as much as; *eva*—certainly; *amunā*—by him; *vihiṁsitāḥ*—who were hurt; *jantavaḥ*—the living entities; *paratra*—in the next life; *yama-yātanām upagatam*—being subjected to miserable conditions by Yamarāja; *te*—those living entities; *eva*—indeed; *ruravaḥ*—*rurus* (a kind of envious animal); *bhūtvā*—becoming; *tathā*—that much; *tam*—him; *eva*—certainly; *vihiṁsanti*—they hurt; *tasmāt*—because of this; *rauravam*—Raurava; *iti*—thus; *āhuḥ*—learned scholars say; *ruruḥ*—the animal known as *ruru; iti*—thus; *sarpāt*—than the snake; *ati-krūra*—much more cruel and envious; *sattvasya*—of the entity; *apadeśaḥ*—the name.

**Перевод:**

**In this life, an envious person commits violent acts against many living entities. Therefore after his death, when he is taken to hell by Yamarāja, those living entities who were hurt by him appear as animals called rurus to inflict very severe pain upon him. Learned scholars call this hell Raurava. Not generally seen in this world, the ruru is more envious than a snake.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The sinful acts themselves take the form of Rurus, very cruel animals with sharp, heavy horns.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He who is very much attached to his own body thinking it to be himself and to his family thinking it to be his—and who nourishes his family members by exploiting others, will go to the Raurava hell. The same sins he has committed take the form of Rurus and inflict misery on him. Ruru is the name of an animal having many horns and which is more cruel than serpents. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Raurava is alternatively described. Ruru is the name of a poisonous animal.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ta eva means the very act of violence. Śuka himself explains the word *ruru* as, “an animal not known here.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The very misdeeds take the form of Rurus, a very cruel animal, as described by Śuka himself.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The very deeds of violence take the form of Rurus. Rurus are creatures unknown in the world here, thus the sage explains the word.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

They become Rurus which are creatures more cruel than serpents and which cause great pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Ruru is the name of a cruel animal. Apadeśa = name.

### Text 12

*एवमेव महारौरवो यत्र निपतितं पुरुषं क्रव्यादा नाम रुरवस्तं क्रव्येण*  
*घातयन्ति यः केवलं देहम्भरः ॥१२॥*

*evam eva mahārauravo yatra nipatitaṁ puruṣaṁ kravyādā nāma ruravas taṁ kravyeṇa ghātayanti yaḥ kevalaṁ dehambharaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*evam*—thus; *eva*—certainly; *mahā-rauravaḥ*—the hell known as Mahāraurava; *yatra*—where; *nipatitam*—being thrown; *puruṣam*—a person; *kravyādāḥ nāma*—named *kravyāda; ruravaḥ*—the *ruru* animals; *tam*—him (the condemned person); *kravyeṇa*—for eating his flesh; *ghātayanti*—kill; *yaḥ*—who; *kevalam*—only; *dehambharaḥ*—intent upon maintaining his own body.

**Перевод:**

**Punishment in the hell called Mahāraurava is compulsory for a person who maintains his own body by hurting others. In this hell, ruru animals known as kravyāda torment him and eat his flesh.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It means “for the sake of flesh.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The distinction of this hell from the previous Raurava is stated to be that one who nourishes his own body falls here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

For the sake of flesh at the cost of harming others.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

By inflicting misery and agony on creatures.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In Maharaurava—for the sake of flesh.

*Svadharmaḥ* = one who forsakes his own *dharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Maharaurava is described. It is like Raurava except that here the Rurus attack the person for the sake of his flesh. One who is intent only on nourishing his own body comes to this hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

He who feels that he has built the house and other things and that they are his.

### Text 13

*यस्त्विह वा उग्रः पशून् पक्षिणो वा प्राणत उपरन्धयति*  
*तमपकरुणं पुरुषादैरपि विगर्हितममुत्र यमानुचराः कुम्भीपाके तप्ततैले*  
*उपरन्धयन्ति ॥१३॥*

*yas tv iha vā ugraḥ paśūn pakṣiṇo vā prāṇata uparandhayati tam apakaruṇaṁ puruṣādair api vigarhitam amutra yamānucarāḥ kumbhīpāke tapta-taile uparandhayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—a person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *ugraḥ*—very cruel; *paśūn*—animals; *pakṣiṇaḥ*—birds; *vā*—or; *prāṇataḥ*—in a live condition; *uparandhayati*—cooks; *tam*—him; *apakaruṇam*—very cruel-hearted; *puruṣa-ādaiḥ*—by those who eat human flesh; *api*—even; *vigarhitam*—condemned; *amutra*—in the next life; *yama-anucarāḥ*—the servants of Yamarāja; *kumbhīpāke*—in the hell known as Kumbhīpāka; *tapta-taile*—in boiling oil; *uparandhayanti*—cook.

**Перевод:**

**For the maintenance of their bodies and the satisfaction of their tongues, cruel persons cook poor animals and birds alive. Such persons are condemned even by man-eaters. In their next lives they are carried by the Yamadūtas to the hell known as Kumbhīpāka, where they are cooked in boiling oil.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Pranatah = living. Uparundhayanti = cook. Apakarunam = mercilessly.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Maharaurava is another hell where the punishment is more than in Raurava. The difference being that here, the Rurus tear away the person fallen there for the sake of flesh. Kumbhipaka is another hell where a person who torments other creatures and animals and cooks them alive is put in a big pot of oil and cooked as he did to the animals. Kumbhi means a big pot. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Uparundhayanti means suffocate.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pranata Uparunahayanti = cook them alive.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Kumbhi means a vessel. Kumbhipaka means being cooked in a vessel.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Ugra= cruel natured. Cooks them alive. Apakarunam = mercilessly.

### Text 14

*यस्त्विह ब्रह्मध्रुक् स कालसूत्रसंज्ञके नरके अयुतयोजनपरिमण्डले*  
*ताम्रमये तप्तखले उपर्यधस्तादग्न्यर्काभ्यामतितप्यमानेऽभिनिवेशितः*  
*क्षुत्पिपासाभ्यां च दह्यमानान्तर्बहिःशरीर आस्ते शेते चेष्टतेऽवतिष्ठति*  
*परिधावति च यावन्ति पशुरोमाणि तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि ॥१४॥*

*yas tv iha brahma-dhruk sa kālasūtra-saṁjñake narake ayuta-yojana-parimaṇḍale tāmramaye tapta-khale upary-adhastād agny-arkābhyām ati-tapyamāne ‘bhiniveśitaḥ kṣut-pipāsābhyāṁ ca dahyamānāntar-bahiḥ-śarīra āste śete ceṣṭate ‘vatiṣṭhati paridhāvati ca yāvanti paśu-romāṇi tāvad varṣa-sahasrāṇi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *brahma-dhruk*—the killer of a *brāhmaṇa; saḥ*—such a person; *kālasūtra-saṁjñake*—named Kālasūtra; *narake*—in the hell; *ayuta-yojana-parimaṇḍale*—having a circumference of eighty thousand miles; *tāmra-maye*—made of copper; *tapta*—heated; *khale*—in a level place; *upari-adhastāt*—above and beneath; *agni*—by fire; *arkābhyām*—and by the sun; *ati-tapyamāne*—which is being heated; *abhiniveśitaḥ*—being made to enter; *kṣut-pipāsābhyām*—by hunger and thirst; *ca*—and; *dahyamāna*—being burned; *antaḥ*—internally; *bahiḥ*—externally; *śarīraḥ*—whose body; *āste*—remains; *śete*—sometimes lies; *ceṣṭate*—sometimes moves his limbs; *avatiṣṭhati*—sometimes stands; *paridhāvati*—sometimes runs here and there; *ca*—also; *yāvanti*—as many; *paśu-romāṇi*—hairs on the body of an animal; *tāvat*—that long; *varṣa-sahasrāṇi*—thousands of years.

**Перевод:**

**The killer of a brāhmaṇa is put into the hell known as Kālasūtra, which has a circumference of eighty thousand miles and which is made entirely of copper. Heated from below by fire and from above by the scorching sun, the copper surface of this planet is extremely hot. Thus the murderer of a brāhmaṇa suffers from being burned both internally and externally. Internally he is burning with hunger and thirst, and externally he is burning from the scorching heat of the sun and the fire beneath the copper surface. Therefore he sometimes lies down, sometimes sits, sometimes stands up and sometimes runs here and there. He must suffer in this way for as many thousands of years as there are hairs on the body of an animal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Khala means a plain.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Brahma* means *Vedas*. Khala means a heated pit. Fire from below and sun from above. Our sun is not there, but for the sake of punishing sinners, God has placed another sun there.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

A person who kills his own father or *brāhmaṇa* is put in the Kalasutra hell. It is a copper, circular plain, 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] in diameter. It is heated by the sun from above and from fire below so that it is red hot. The person is put there where he cries, begs, rolls and does many such things. He must stay there for the number of years equaling the number of hairs on the animals he killed. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Khala is a floor where grains are dried—the sun from above and fire from below heat it. Not merely the person who offends his father and so on, but also those who torment quadrupeds and other animals must fall here.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Khala is a plain.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Khala is a plain ground.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Kalasutra and the evil responsible for attaining it are described. A person who kills his father, *brāhmaṇa* and the *Vedas* reaches this hell. Here, there is a plain ground heated from above and below by the sun and fire. Unable to bear the heat, the evil doer falls on the ground and tries to run, sit and lie down, but cannot do anything. He stays there for the number of years corresponding to the number of hairs on an animal.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The place where grains are dried is called *khala*. In such a place, heated by fire from below and by the sun from above, sinners are placed.

### Text 15

*यस्त्विह वै निजवेदपथादनापद्यपगतः पाखण्डं चोपग*  
*तस्तमसिपत्रवनं प्रवेश्य कशया प्रहरन्ति तत्र हासावितस्ततो*  
*धावमान उभयतो धारैस्तालवनासिपत्रैश्छिद्यमानसर्वाङ्गो हा हतोऽस्मीति*  
*परमया वेदनया मूर्च्छितः पदे पदे निपतति स्वधर्महा पाखण्डानुगतं*  
*फलं भुङ्क्ते ॥१५॥*

*yas tv iha vai nija-veda-pathād anāpady apagataḥ pākhaṇḍaṁ copagatas tam asi-patravanaṁ praveśya kaśayā praharanti tatra hāsāv itas tato dhāvamāna ubhayato dhārais tāla-vanāsi-patraiś chidyamāna-sarvāṅgo hā hato ‘smīti paramayā vedanayā mūrcchitaḥ pade pade nipatati sva-dharmahā pākhaṇḍānugataṁ phalaṁ bhuṅkte.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *nija-veda-pathāt*—from his own path, recommended by the *Vedas; anāpadi*—even without an emergency; *apagataḥ*—deviated; *pākhaṇḍam*—a concocted, atheistic system; *ca*—and; *upagataḥ*—gone to; *tam*—him; *asi-patravanam*—the hell known as Asi-patravana; *praveśya*—making enter; *kaśayā*—with a whip; *praharanti*—they beat; *tatra*—there; *ha*—certainly; *asau*—that; *itaḥ tataḥ*—here and there; *dhāvamānaḥ*—running; *ubhayataḥ*—on both sides; *dhāraiḥ*—by the edges; *tāla-vana-asi-patraiḥ*—by the swordlike leaves of palm trees; *chidyamāna*—being cut; *sarva-aṅgaḥ*—whose entire body; *hā*—alas; *hataḥ*—killed; *asmi*—I am; *iti*—thus; *paramayā*—with severe; *vedanayā*—pain; *mūrcchitaḥ*—fainted; *pade pade*—at every step; *nipatati*—falls down; *sva-dharma-hā*—the killer of his own principles of religion; *pākhaṇḍa-anugatam phalam*—the result of accepting an atheistic path; *bhuṅkte*—he suffers.

**Перевод:**

**If a person deviates from the path of the Vedas in the absence of an emergency, the servants of Yamarāja put him into the hell called Asi-patravana, where they beat him with whips. When he runs hither and thither, fleeing from the extreme pain, on all sides he runs into palm trees with leaves like sharpened swords. Thus injured all over his body and fainting at every step, he cries out, “Oh, what shall I do now! How shall I be saved!” This is how one suffers who deviates from the accepted religious principles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Sva-dharma-hā* means a person who has forsaken his *dharma*, duty.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He who deviates from his path of *dharma* when there is no crisis—for during the period of crisis, some generosity is shown. Pakhaṇḍa means that is which is opposed to the *Vedas* including manufactured worship claimed to be in accordance with the *Vedas*. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrīvaṁśīdhara\]

Following a pakhaṇḍa *dharma* is always evil. He is lashed with whips by the servants of Yama. When he runs to avoid the beating, he comes into contact with the branches of the trees whose leaves are like double-edged swords. He is cut all over and he shouts and cries in pain. \[Note: this commentary is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Because it is said, “when there is no crisis,” it implies that there is some concession during a crisis. Dhara means sharp edge. In the Talavana, the leaves are like double edged swords. Those who forsake their assigned *dharma*s fall here.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*Kasha* is a whip. “In asipatravana” = where every leaf of the trees is like a knife. The follower of a pakhaṇḍa is punished by double-edged swords.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Though very cruel, Rurus torment only the evildoer and none else because they originate from the evil doings of the same performer.

In the forest of Tala trees whose leaves resemble swords. He cries, “Alas, I am dead.” This is the result of forsaking one’s own *dharma* and accepting another *dharma* opposed to him.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

*Ta eva* means the servants of Yama, who torment one who was engaged in evil thoughts only for his personal comforts. Uparandhayanti means suffocate him.

### Text 16

*यस्त्विह वै राजा राजपुरुषो वा अदण्ड्ये दण्डं प्रणयति ब्राह्मणे वा*  
*शरीरदण्डं स पापीयान्नरकेऽमुत्र सूकरमुखे निपतति तत्रातिबलैर्वि*  
*निष्पिष्यमाणावयवो यथैवेहेक्षुखण्ड आर्तस्वरेण स्वनयन् क्वचिन्मूर्च्छितः*  
*कश्मलमुपगतो यथैवेहादृष्टदोषा उपरुद्धाः ॥१६॥*

*yas tv iha vai rājā rāja-puruṣo vā adaṇḍye daṇḍaṁ praṇayati brāhmaṇe vā śarīra-daṇḍaṁ sa pāpīyān narake ‘mutra sūkaramukhe nipatati tatrātibalair viniṣpiṣyamāṇāvayavo yathaivehekṣukhaṇḍa ārta-svareṇa svanayan kvacin mūrcchitaḥ kaśmalam upagato yathaivehā-dṛṣṭa-doṣā uparuddhāḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *rājā*—a king; *rāja-puruṣaḥ*—a king’s man; *vā*—or; *adaṇḍye*—unto one not punishable; *daṇḍam*—punishment; *praṇayati*—inflicts; *brāhmaṇe*—unto a *brāhmaṇa; vā*—or; *śarīra-daṇḍam*—corporal punishment; *saḥ*—that person, king or government officer; *pāpīyān*—the most sinful; *narake*—in the hell; *amutra*—in the next life; *sūkaramukhe*—named Sūkaramukha; *nipatati*—falls down; *tatra*—there; *ati-balaiḥ*—by very strong assistants of Yamarāja; *viniṣpiṣyamāṇa*—being crushed; *avayavaḥ*—the different parts of whose body; *yathā*—like; *eva*—certainly; *iha*—here; *ikṣu-khaṇḍaḥ*—sugarcane; *ārta-svareṇa*—with a pitiable sound; *svanayan*—crying; *kvacit*—sometimes; *mūrcchitaḥ*—fainted; *kaśmalam upagataḥ*—becoming illusioned; *yathā*—just like; *eva*—indeed; *iha*—here; *adṛṣṭa-doṣāḥ*—who is not at fault; *uparuddhāḥ*—arrested for punishment.

**Перевод:**

**In his next life, a sinful king or governmental representative who punishes an innocent person, or who inflicts corporal punishment upon a brāhmaṇa, is taken by the Yamadūtas to the hell named Sūkaramukha, where the most powerful assistants of Yamarāja crush him exactly as one crushes sugarcane to squeeze out the juice. The sinful living entity cries very pitiably and faints, just like an innocent man undergoing punishments. This is the result of punishing a faultless person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Svanayan = weeping. Kashmalam upagatah = the person faints, just like the animals he captured.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Śukaramukha is described. A person or king who punishes an innocent person or gives capital punishment to a *brāhmaṇa* falls in the Śukaramukha hell where animals called Sukra tear him apart. He is also squeezed like a sugarcane stick and he becomes unconscious time and again. If a *brāhmaṇa* commits a crime, he can be punished by confiscating his money, shaving his head or face etc., or banishing him from the city or kingdom, however, he should not be physically punished.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Who punishes one who does not deserve it. Capital punishment means beating or cutting the limbs. One imprisoned here will be treated as if a thief.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Svanayan = crying—because he has held innocent creatures captive and punished them.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Punishes one who does not deserve it. Capital punishment means beating or cutting off of the limbs. He will be powdered by the strong servants of Yama. He will be crushed in a machine as sugarcane is crushed in a crusher.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Svanayam = crying, like the animals he trapped.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Śukaramukha and the evil which leads one there are described. If a king or a prince or a minister, etc. punishes an innocent person or punishes a *brāhmaṇa* physically, he enters this hell. There, fierce animals, resembling a boar, bite him in all his limbs. He is squeezed like a sugarcane stick. He suffers great pain, cries aloud and sometimes becomes unconscious just like innocent animals being tortured.

### Text 17

*यस्त्विह वै भूतानामीश्वरोपकल्पितवृत्तीनामविविक्तपरव्यथानां स्वयं*  
*पुरुषोपकल्पितवृत्तिर्विविक्तपरव्यथो व्यथामाचरति स परत्रान्धकूपे तदभिद्रोहेण*  
*निपतति तत्र हासौ तैर्जन्तुभिः पशुमृगपक्षिसरीसृपैर्मशकयूकामत्कुण*  
*मक्षिकादिभिर्ये के चाभिद्रुग्धास्तैः सर्वतोऽभिद्रुह्यमाणस्तमसि विहतनिद्रा*  
*निर्वृतिरलब्धावस्थानः परिक्रामति यथा कुशरीरे जीवः ॥१७॥*

*yas tv iha vai bhūtānām īśvaropakalpita-vṛttīnām avivikta-para-vyathānāṁ svayaṁ puruṣopakalpita-vṛttir vivikta-para-vyatho vyathām ācarati sa paratrāndhakūpe tad-abhidroheṇa nipatati tatra hāsau tair jantubhiḥ paśu-mṛga-pakṣi-sarīsṛpair maśaka-yūkā-matkuṇa-makṣikādibhir ye ke cābhidrugdhās taiḥ sarvato ‘bhidruhyamāṇas tamaśi vihata-nidrā-nirvṛtir alabdhāvasthānaḥ parikrāmati yathā kuśarīre jīvaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—any person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *bhūtānām*—to some living entities; *īśvara*—by the supreme controller; *upakalpita*—designed; *vṛttīnām*—whose means of livelihood; *avivikta*—not understanding; *para-vyathānām*—the pain of others; *svayam*—himself; *puruṣa-upakalpita*—designed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *vṛttiḥ*—whose livelihood; *vivikta*—understanding; *para-vyathaḥ*—the painful conditions of others; *vyathām ācarati*—but still causes pain; *saḥ*—such a person; *paratra*—in his next life; *andhakūpe*—to the hell named Andhakūpa; *tat*—to them; *abhidroheṇa*—by the sin of malice; *nipatati*—falls down; *tatra*—there; *ha*—indeed; *asau*—that person; *taiḥ jantubhiḥ*—by those respective living entities; *paśu*—animals; *mṛga*—wild beasts; *pakṣi*—birds; *sarīsṛpaiḥ*—snakes; *maśaka*—mosquitoes; *yūkā*—lice; *matkuṇa*—worms; *makṣika-ādibhiḥ*—flies and so on; *ye ke*—whoever else; *ca*—and; *abhidrugdhāḥ*—persecuted; *taiḥ*—by them; *sarvataḥ*—everywhere; *abhidruhyamāṇaḥ*—being injured; *tamaśi*—in the darkness; *vihata*—disturbed; *nidrā-nirvṛtiḥ*—whose resting place; *alabdha*—not being able to obtain; *avasthānaḥ*—a resting place; *parikrāmati*—wanders; *yathā*—just as; *ku-śarīre*—in a low-grade body; *jīvaḥ*—a living entity.

**Перевод:**

**By the arrangement of the Supreme Lord, low-grade living beings like bugs and mosquitoes suck the blood of human beings and other animals. Such insignificant creatures are unaware that their bites are painful to the human being. However, first-class human beings—brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas—are developed in consciousness, and therefore they know how painful it is to be killed. A human being endowed with knowledge certainly commits sin if he kills or torments insignificant creatures, who have no discrimination. The Supreme Lord punishes such a man by putting him into the hell known as Andhakūpa, where he is attacked by all the birds and beasts, reptiles, mosquitoes, lice, worms, flies, and any other creatures he tormented during his life. They attack him from all sides, robbing him of the pleasure of sleep. Unable to rest, he constantly wanders about in the darkness. Thus in Andhakūpa his suffering is just like that of a creature in the lower species.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The bugs and other such creatures are destined to live on human blood yet they do not know other’s agony. However, for those who can appreciate the agony of others, the *Vedas* prescribe rules and regulations. Abhidrughdhah means tormented without sleep and without staying at a single place, he rolls in darkness.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Andhakupa and how it is attained is also described. Creatures such as bugs, mosquitoes and other such insects are destined to live on human and animal blood. These creatures are unaware of the misery they cause to others. A person, unmindful about others’ livelihood, who kills such creatures, enters the hell Andhakupa where the same insects that were formerly killed by him, now sting him again and again. He cannot sleep nor stay in a particular place or position. He spends a long time without sleeping and running in all directions. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Śrī Giridhara Lāla\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Not caring for other’s grief, those who kill insects and creatures which have no other means of subsistence other than the bodies of humans and animals (as per God’s design), fall here. Kusharira means a leper’s body.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bugs and other insects are unaware of the misery they cause to others since they subsist on others’ bodies. But human beings endowed with knowledge ought to know the pain caused to others.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The word “etc.” indicates flies and mosquitoes. *Puruṣa* means Hari \[the Supreme Lord\]. By inflicting pain on bugs and others. The perpetuator, along with these insects. Being a leper.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Inflicting misery on those creatures which cannot know others’ miseries, they now lose the comfort of sleep.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He who offends others and nourishes his own body without worshipping God, falls into this hell where he is killed for his flesh.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The bugs and mosquitoes are destined to subsist on human blood by God, however are unaware of the pain they inflict on others. Human beings know the rules and regulations, however, and are aware of the pains of others, thus they cannot be pardoned.

### Text 18

*यस्त्विह वा असंविभज्याश्नाति यत्किञ्चनोपनतमनिर्मितपञ्चयज्ञो*  
*वायससंस्तुतः स परत्र कृमिभोजने नरकाधमे निपतति तत्र शतसहस्रयोजने*  
*कृमिकुण्डे कृमिभूतः स्वयं कृमिभिरेव भक्ष्यमाणः कृमिभोजनो यावत्तदप्रत्ताप्रहूतादो*  
*ऽनिर्वेशमात्मानं यातयते ॥१८॥*

*yas tv iha vā asaṁvibhajyāśnāti yat kiñcanopanatam anirmita-pañca-yajño vāyasa-saṁstutaḥ sa paratra kṛmibhojane narakādhame nipatati tatra śata-sahasra-yojane kṛmi-kuṇḍe kṛmi-bhūtaḥ svayaṁ kṛmibhir eva bhakṣyamāṇaḥ kṛmi-bhojano yāvat tad aprattāprahūtādo ‘nirveśam ātmānaṁ yātayate.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—any person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *asaṁ-vibhajya*—without dividing; *aśnāti*—eats; *yat kiñcana*—whatever; *upanatam*—obtained by Kṛṣṇa’s grace; *anirmita*—not performing; *pañca-yajñaḥ*—the five kinds of sacrifice; *vāyasa*—with the crows; *saṁstutaḥ*—who is described as equal; *saḥ*—such a person; *paratra*—in the next life; *kṛmibhojane*—named Kṛmibhojana; *naraka-adhame*—into the most abominable of all hells; *nipatati*—falls down; *tatra*—there; *śata-sahasra-yojane*—measuring 100,000 *yojanas* (800,000 miles); *kṛmi-kuṇḍe*—in a lake of worms; *kṛmi-bhūtaḥ*—becoming one of the worms; *svayam*—he himself; *kṛmibhiḥ*—by the other worms; *eva*—certainly; *bhakṣyamāṇaḥ*—being eaten; *kṛmi-bhojanaḥ*—eating worms; *yāvat*—as long as; *tat*—that lake is wide; *apratta-aprahūta*—unshared and unoffered food; *adaḥ*—one who eats; *anirveśam*—who has not performed atonement; *ātmānam*—to himself; *yātayate*—gives pain.

**Перевод:**

**A person is considered no better than a crow if after receiving some food, he does not divide it among guests, old men and children, but simply eats it himself, or if he eats it without performing the five kinds of sacrifice. After death he is put into the most abominable hell, known as Kṛmibhojana. In that hell is a lake 100,000 yojanas \[800,000 miles\] wide and filled with worms. He becomes a worm in that lake and feeds on the other worms there, who also feed on him. Unless he atones for his actions before his death, such a sinful man remains in the hellish lake of Kṛmibhojana for as many years as there are yojanas in the width of the lake.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Without distributing any food to others. Without performing the five prescribed sacrifices. That is why he is regarded as equal to a crow. He stays in a pit eating only worms for a long time. Unless atoned for, eating stolen food, not distributing food to others, and not offering food to the demigods brings this misery.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Krimibhojana is described and also its cause. He who does not share his food with others like guests and others, and who does not perform the stipulated five sacrifices for the purification of the food, falls in this hell. It is a pit which is one *lakh* \[100,000\] *yojanas* \[800,000 miles\] wide and is filled with insects of all sorts. The person also becomes an insect there where he is bitten and must live by eating those insects. He must stay there for as many years as there are miles in the width of the pit. This hell is a result of not sharing and not offering one’s food. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Without sharing the food with others and without offering it to demigods, one is equal to a crow. Such a person falls in this pit and eats only insects. Anirvesha means for not having atoned for his sins while on earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Without distributing any food to others. Without performing the five prescribed sacrifices. That is why he is regarded as equal to a crow. Without giving food to the children and the aged. Apratta means not come in the proper way. Here *vetana* means atonement. Yatayati means subjected to pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Upanatam = what is gotten. He is regarded as equal to a crow. Stays in the pit of worms until the completion of his sin.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He becomes an insect and eats insects while remaining in the pit for as long as his evil lasts.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Krimibhojana and the evil which begets the same are described. A person who does not share his food with guests and others and does not perform the sacrifices prescribed for the purification of the food, lands here. It is a large pit filled with insects.
