The evil doer also becomes an insect, he eats the insects only, bitten by others and spends a long time equal to the width of the pit here. This is the result of not sharing and not offering one’s food.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Just as a thief is confined to a cell, here, the sinner is also confined to the small place where he suffers greatly.

Without sharing the God-given food with others and without offering the food to demigods in the prescribed process and not atoning for their lapses, they fall in this hell.

### Text 19

*यस्त्विह वै स्तेयेन बलाद्वा हिरण्यरत्नादीनि ब्राह्मणस्य वापहरत्यन्यस्य*  
*वानापदि पुरुषस्तममुत्र राजन् यमपुरुषा अयस्मयैरग्निपिण्डैः सन्दंशैस्त्वचि*  
*निष्कुषन्ति ॥१९॥*

*yas tv iha vai steyena balād vā hiraṇya-ratnādīni brāhmaṇasya vāpaharaty anyasya vānāpadi puruṣas tam amutra rājan yama-puruṣā ayasmayair agni-piṇḍaiḥ sandaṁśais tvaci niṣkuṣanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—any person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *steyena*—by thievery; *balāt*—by force; *vā*—or; *hiraṇya*—gold; *ratna*—gems; *ādīni*—and so on; *brāhmaṇasya*—of a *brāhmaṇa; vā*—or; *apaharati*—steals; *anyasya*—of others; *vā*—or; *anāpadi*—not in a calamity; *puruṣaḥ*—a person; *tam*—him; *amutra*—in the next life; *rājan*—O King; *yama-puruṣāḥ*—the agents of Yamarāja; *ayaḥ-mayaiḥ*—made of iron; *agni-piṇḍaiḥ*—balls heated in fire; *sandaṁśaiḥ*—with tongs; *tvaci*—on the skin; *niṣkuṣanti*—tear to pieces.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, a person who in the absence of an emergency robs a brāhmaṇa—or, indeed, anyone else—of his gems and gold is put into a hell known as Sandaṁśa. There his skin is torn and separated by red-hot iron balls and tongs. In this way, his entire body is cut to pieces.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Niṣkuṣanti means the verb “cut.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Sandamsha is described, as also its cause. He who steals others’ or a *brāhmaṇa*’s valuable properties, lands in this hell, where Yama’s servants hold him by red hot tongs and drag him about.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

They remove parts of the skin and flesh by tongs.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Niṣkuṣanti = cut (verb).

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Another’s belonging when there is no crisis. A *brāhmaṇa*’s belonging even when there is crisis. Sandamsha means tongs. Nishkushanti means touch him.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Niṣkuṣanti = cut.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

In a plain ground, he suffers from this pain for a long time.

Nishkushanti = cut using tongs. Śuka implies that everyone is free to do his duty, which the servants of Yama do and so they are not at fault.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Sandamsha and the evil which brings one here are described. One who steals a *brāhmaṇa*’s or other’s property, when there is no crisis, comes to this hell. Here Yama’s servants pluck his skin and flesh with red hot tongs.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

They pluck the sinner with tongs.

### Text 20

*यस्त्विह वा अगम्यां स्त्रियमगम्यं वा पुरुषं योषिदभिगच्छति तावमुत्र*  
*कशया ताडयन्तस्तिग्मया सूर्म्या लोहमय्या पुरुषमालिङ्गयन्ति स्त्रियं च*  
*पुरुषरूपया सूर्म्या ॥२०॥*

*yas tv iha vā agamyāṁ striyam agamyaṁ vā puruṣaṁ yoṣid abhigacchati tāv amutra kaśayā tāḍayantas tigmayā sūrmyā lohamayyā puruṣam āliṅgayanti striyaṁ ca puruṣa-rūpayā sūrmyā.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—any person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *agamyām*—unsuitable; *striyam*—a woman; *agamyam*—unsuitable; *vā*—or; *puruṣam*—a man; *yoṣit*—a woman; *abhigacchati*—approaches for sexual intercourse; *tau*—both of them; *amutra*—in the next life; *kaśayā*—by whips; *tāḍayantaḥ*—beating; *tigmayā*—very hot; *sūrmyā*—by an image; *loha-mayyā*—made of iron; *puruṣam*—the man; *āliṅgayanti*—they embrace; *striyam*—the woman; *ca*—also; *puruṣa-rūpayā*—in the form of a man; *sūrmyā*—by an image.

**Перевод:**

**A man or woman who indulges in sexual intercourse with an unworthy member of the opposite sex is punished after death by the assistants of Yamarāja in the hell known as Taptasūrmi. There such men and women are beaten with whips. The man is forced to embrace a red-hot iron form of a woman, and the woman is forced to embrace a similar form of a man. Such is the punishment for illicit sex.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Tigma means red hot. Surmya means a statue.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Taptasurmi and its cause are described. A man who has sex with a woman who he is not supposed to have sex with or a woman who has sex with a man she is not supposed to have sex with, both land in this hell. There, they are made to embrace a red hot statue of a woman or a man respectively and are whipped by Yama’s servants.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Surmya means a statue made of some metal.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Agamya is a woman not married to a person or a woman having contact with a person other than her husband. A red hot statue. Surmya means such a statue as per the lexicon “chintamani.”

Make them embrace a red hot statue.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Surmya = by a statue.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

He who follows the paths which are opposed to those enjoined in the *Vedas*. Kasha = whip. During a crisis there is concession in punishment.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The women one should avoid are listed: a *brāhmaṇa* woman, a widow, a woman belonging to his own clan, a queen, any respectable lady, a highly placed lady and a niggard. They are made to embrace a red hot statue or effigy.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Tatpatasurmi and the cause for coming there is described. If a man or woman has sex with a person whom he or she is not supposed to have sex with, they come to this hell. Here, one is beaten with whips by Yama’s servants and made to embrace a red hot metallic statue of a man or a woman, as the case may be.

### Text 21

*यस्त्विह वै सर्वाभिगमस्तममुत्र निरये वर्तमानं वज्रकण्टकशाल्मलीमारोप्य*  
*निष्कर्षन्ति ॥२१॥*

*विण्मूत्रपूयशोणितकेशनखास्थिमेदोमांसवसावाहिन्यामुपतप्यन्ते॥२२॥*

*ye tv iha vai rājanyā rāja-puruṣā vā apākhaṇḍā dharma-setūn bhindanti te samparetya vaitaraṇyāṁ nipatanti bhinna-maryādās tasyāṁ niraya-parikhā-bhūtāyāṁ nadyāṁ yādo-gaṇair itas tato bhakṣyamāṇā ātmanā na viyujyamānāś cāsubhir uhyamānāḥ svāghena karma-pākam anusmaranto viṇ-mūtra-pūya-śoṇita-keśa-nakhāsthi-medo-māṁsa-vasā-vāhinyām upatapyante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—persons who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *rājanyāḥ*—members of the royal family, or *kṣatriyas; rāja-puruṣāḥ*—government servants; *vā*—or; *apākhaṇḍāḥ*—although born in responsible families; *dharma-setūn*—the bounds of prescribed religious principles; *bhindanti*—transgress; *te*—they; *samparetya*—after dying; *vaitaraṇyām*—named Vaitaraṇī; *nipatanti*—fall down; *bhinna-maryādāḥ*—who have broken the regulative principles; *tasyām*—in that; *niraya-parikhā-bhūtāyām*—the moat surrounding hell; *nadyām*—in the river; *yādaḥ-gaṇaiḥ*—by ferocious aquatic animals; *itaḥ tataḥ*—here and there; *bhakṣyamāṇāḥ*—being eaten; *ātmanā*—with the body; *na*—not; *viyujyamānāḥ*—being separated; *ca*—and; *asubhiḥ*—the life airs; *uhyamānāḥ*—being carried; *sva-aghena*—by his own sinful activities; *karma-pākam*—the result of his impious activities; *anusmarantaḥ*—remembering; *viṭ*—of stool; *mūtra*—urine; *pūya*—pus; *śoṇita*—blood; *keśa*—hair; *nakha*—nails; *asthi*—bones; *medaḥ*—marrow; *māṁsa*—flesh; *vasā*—fat; *vāhinyām*—in the river; *upatapyante*—are afflicted with pain.

**Перевод:**

**A person who is born into a responsible family—such as a kṣatriya, a member of royalty or a government servant—but who neglects to execute his prescribed duties according to religious principles, and who thus becomes degraded, falls down at the time of death into the river of hell known as Vaitaraṇī. This river, which is a moat surrounding hell, is full of ferocious aquatic animals. When a sinful man is thrown into the River Vaitaraṇī, the aquatic animals there immediately begin to eat him, but because of his extremely sinful life, he does not leave his body. He constantly remembers his sinful activities and suffers terribly in that river, which is full of stool, urine, pus, blood, hair, nails, bones, marrow, flesh and fat.**

It is filled with all nasty things one can think of. They do not die, but float in the river by the help of their own breath. *ātmā* means his body.

He who destroys the livelihood of *brāhmaṇa* or other innocent people engaged in the worshipping of demigods. It is suggested that if it belongs to non-believers, there is no harm. Vitarana i.e. dana or charity—the river which can be crossed if charity is given to the worthy is called Vaitarini.

They are carried by the winds and waves. They do not die. The river is of blood, fat and other such things.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Pasucharya = acting according to one’s own will, like an animal.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

They float in the river without dying and recollecting the evil deeds they did.

It is like a trench around the hells and is filled with all nasty matter.

Vaitarini is described. If a king or a royal person transgresses the Vedic orders, he falls into this hell. Vaitarini is a trench-like river around the hells which is full of all nasty material such as secretion, nails, hair, fat, bones, etc. The evil-doer falls in this river, spends a long time here and recollects his past deeds.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Surmya is an effigy or idol.

### Text 24

*ये त्विह वै श्वगर्दभपतयो ब्राह्मणादयो मृगयाविहारा अतीर्थे च*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—those who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—or; *śva*—of dogs; *gardabha*—and asses; *patayaḥ*—maintainers; *brāhmaṇa-ādayaḥ*—*brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas* and *vaiśyas; mṛgayā vihārāḥ*—taking pleasure in hunting animals in the forest; *atīrthe*—other than prescribed; *ca*—also; *mṛgān*—animals; *nighnanti*—kill; *tān*—them; *api*—indeed; *samparetān*—having died; *lakṣya-bhūtān*—becoming the targets; *yama-puruṣāḥ*—the assistants of Yamarāja; *iṣubhiḥ*—by arrows; *vidhyanti*—pierce.

They kill animals when there is no guest or necessity.

Certain non-prohibited animals may be killed for the sake of a guest or sacrifice. A cruel or poisonous animal may be killed for the welfare of the people, but other than that, it is an evil act. Yama’s servants shoot them with arrows when the person almost loses his breath and life. For this reason it is called Prananirodha.

Atirtha means during a time when there is no shraddha or such festival.

The owners of dogs and asses.

Killing, however, of such animals in other places, such as the forest, is evil. When they come here, Yama’s servants shoot arrows at the persons who formerly shot animals.

Not separated from their bodies or breath, they are carried by currents of the river and suffer greatly.

The dogs, also servants of Yama, attack violently and devour him.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Sarameyadana is described. Those who commit burglary, set other’s houses on fire, poison others, and political persons who loot villages and towns, come here. In this hell, a pack of hounds attacks them violently, tearing them into pieces and devouring them.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The “lords of hell” means Yama’s servants.

### Text 28

*यस्त्विह वा अनृतं वदति साक्ष्ये द्रव्यविनिमये दाने वा कथञ्चित्स*  
*वै प्रेत्य नरके ऽवीचिमत्यधःशिरा निरवकाशे योजनशतोच्छ्रायाद् गिरिमूर्ध्नः*  
*सम्पात्यते यत्र जलमिव स्थलमश्मपृष्ठमवभासते तदवीचिमत्तिलशो विशीर्य*  
*माणशरीरो न म्रियमाणः पुनरारोपितो निपतति ॥२८॥*

*yas tv iha vā anṛtaṁ vadati sākṣye dravya-vinimaye dāne vā kathañcit sa vai pretya narake ‘vīcimaty adhaḥ-śirā niravakāśe yojana-śatocchrāyād giri-mūrdhnaḥ sampātyate yatra jalam iva sthalam aśma-pṛṣṭham avabhāsate tad avīcimat tilaśo viśīryamāṇa-śarīro na mriyamāṇaḥ punar āropito nipatati.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *anṛtam*—a lie; *vadati*—speaks; *sākṣye*—giving witness; *dravya-vinimaye*—in exchange for goods; *dāne*—in giving charity; *vā*—or; *kathañcit*—somehow; *saḥ*—that person; *vai*—indeed; *pretya*—after dying; *narake*—in the hell; *avīcimati*—named Avīcimat (having no water); *adhaḥ-śirāḥ*—with his head downward; *niravakāśe*—without support; *yojana-śata*—of eight hundred miles; *ucchrāyāt*—having a height; *giri*—of a mountain; *mūrdhnaḥ*—from the top; *sampātyate*—is thrown; *yatra*—where; *jalam iva*—like water; *sthalam*—land; *aśma-pṛṣṭham*—having a surface of stone; *avabhāsate*—appears; *tat*—that; *avīcimat*—having no water or waves; *tilaśaḥ*—in pieces as small as seeds; *viśīryamāṇa*—being broken; *śarīraḥ*—the body; *na mriyamāṇaḥ*—not dying; *punaḥ*—again; *āropitaḥ*—raised to the top; *nipatati*—falls down.

**Перевод:**

**A person who in this life bears false witness or lies while transacting business or giving charity is severely punished after death by the agents of Yamarāja. Such a sinful man is taken to the top of a mountain eight hundred miles high and thrown headfirst into the hell known as Avīcimat. This hell has no shelter and is made of strong stone resembling the waves of water. There is no water there, however, and thus it is called Avīcimat \[waterless\]. Although the sinful man is repeatedly thrown from the mountain and his body broken to tiny pieces, he still does not die but continuously suffers chastisement.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Dravya vinimaya* means trading. Niravakasha means without support. The meaning of the word Avichi is told—vichi is a wave (of air or water). The place where there is no such wave is Avichi.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Avichi is described. A person who gives a false statement as a witness regarding transactions, lands in this hell. It is a stone surface where there is no water. The person is dropped from a height on the stone breaking him to pieces.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

When he has to give a statement as witness to a business deal. It appears like water from a distance but actually it is a stone. This is Avichi. Niravakasha means without any protection.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Niravakashe = where there is no protection. Avichi = where there are no ripples of water.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

During attesting as a witness.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Vitchi is a wave. A place where there are no waves either of wind or water is Avichi. This is the name of a hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

Dravyavinimaya = trade. Niravakasha = without any support.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Avichimat is described. A person who gives a false statement as a witness to trade or some other business comes to this hell. It is a very stony surface without water. He is thrown from the cliff of a mountain to this ground, when his body is blown into pieces. Even then he does not die, but suffers great pain.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Sartha means business people.

The meaning of Avichimat is explained. It means a stone surface where there is no water.

### Text 29

*यस्त्विह वै विप्रो राजन्यो वैश्यो वा सोमपीथस्तत्कलत्रं वा*  
*सुरां व्रतस्थोऽपि वा पिबति प्रमादतस्तेषां निरयं नीतानामुरसि*  
*पदाक्रम्यास्ये वह्निना द्रवमाणं कार्ष्णायसं निषिञ्चन्ति ॥२९॥*

*yas tv iha vai vipro rājanyo vaiśyo vā soma-pīthas tat-kalatraṁ vā surāṁ vrata-stho ‘pi vā pibati pramādatas teṣāṁ nirayaṁ nītānām urasi padākramyāsye vahninā dravamāṇaṁ kārṣṇāyasaṁ niṣiñcanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *vipraḥ*—a learned *brāhmaṇa; rājanyaḥ*—a *kṣatriya; vaiśyaḥ*—a *vaiśya; vā*—or; *soma-pīthaḥ*—drink *soma-rasa; tat*—his; *kalatram*—wife; *vā*—or; *surām*—liquor; *vrata-sthaḥ*—being situated in a vow; *api*—certainly; *vā*—or; *pibati*—drinks; *pramādataḥ*—out of illusion; *teṣām*—of all of them; *nirayam*—to hell; *nītānām*—being brought; *urasi*—on the chest; *padā*—with the foot; *ākramya*—stepping; *asye*—in the mouth; *vahninā*—by fire; *dravamāṇam*—melted; *kārṣṇāyasam*—iron; *niṣiñcanti*—they pour into.

**Перевод:**

**Any brāhmaṇa or brāhmaṇa’s wife who drinks liquor is taken by the agents of Yamarāja to the hell known as Ayaḥpāna. This hell also awaits any kṣatriya, vaiśya, or person under a vow who in illusion drinks soma-rasa. In Ayaḥpāna the agents of Yamarāja stand on their chests and pour hot melted iron into their mouths.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

If any of the following drink wine, they are subjected to this hell: a *brāhmaṇa*, the wife of a *brāhmaṇa*, a person observing an austerity, a king and a ksatriya who has performed a sacrifice. A warrior or a merchant who consumes soma, tabooed for him, will also have the same hell.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Ayahpana is described here. If a *brāhmaṇa* or his wife drinks wine or if a *kṣatriya* or a vaishya drinks soma which is forbidden to them they come to this hell. They are made to drink molten iron by Yama’s servants here. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva, Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya and Yādavārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

For *brāhmaṇa*, wine is always forbidden. For warriors and merchants it is forbidden sometimes.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Somapīthaḥ* = one who has consumed soma. Molten iron.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The hell Ayahpana is described. The ksatriyas and vaishyas are forbidden from drinking soma, although a substitute is prescribed for them. Sura means wine which is of three kinds. Tatkalatram means the wife of a *brāhmaṇa*, *kṣatriya* or *vaiśya*. Even if a person other than the three above castes consumes wine while performing a vrata. Karshnayasam means molten iron. Pramada means not knowing or accidentally doing things. This hell is for those who consume wine.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Standing as a witness in a trade. Niravakasha means without support. If a merchant (*vaiśya*) or his wife drinks wine while observing a vow or a *vrata* dedicated to his forefathers, then they are sinners and liable to be punished.

### Text 30

*अथ च यस्त्विह वा आत्मसम्भावनेन स्वयमधमो जन्मतपोविद्याचार*  
*वर्णाश्रमवतो वरीयसो न बहु मन्येत स मृतक एव मृत्वा क्षारकर्दमे*  
*निरयेऽवाक् षिरा निपातितो दुरन्ता यातना ह्यश्नुते ॥३०॥*

*atha ca yas tv iha vā ātma-sambhāvanena svayam adhamo janma-tapo-vidyācāra-varṇāśramavato varīyaso na bahu manyeta sa mṛtaka eva mṛtvā kṣārakardame niraye ‘vāk-śirā nipātito durantā yātanā hy aśnute.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*atha*—furthermore; *ca*—also; *yaḥ*—anyone who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *ātma-sambhāvanena*—by false prestige; *svayam*—himself; *adhamaḥ*—very degraded; *janma*—good birth; *tapaḥ*—austerities; *vidyā*—knowledge; *ācāra*—good behavior; *varṇa-āśrama-vataḥ*—in terms of strictly following the principles of *varṇāśrama; varīyasaḥ*—of one who is more honorable; *na*—not; *bahu*—much; *manyeta*—respects; *saḥ*—he; *mṛtakaḥ*—a dead body; *eva*—only; *mṛtvā*—after dying; *kṣārakardame*—named Kṣārakardama; *niraye*—in the hell; *avāk-śirā*—with his head downward; *nipātitaḥ*—thrown; *durantāḥ yātanāḥ*—severe painful conditions; *hi*—indeed; *aśnute*—suffers.

**Перевод:**

**A lowborn and abominable person who in this life becomes falsely proud, thinking “I am great,” and who thus fails to show proper respect to one more elevated than he by birth, austerity, education, behavior, caste or spiritual order, is like a dead man even in this lifetime, and after death he is thrown headfirst into the hell known as Kṣārakardama. There he must suffer great tribulation at the hands of the agents of Yamarāja.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He is dead while living—then he dies for a second time.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

He who is of an inferior status but feels that he is superior to the great people who are pious and perform austerities is dead even while he lives. Dying for a second time, he reaches Kharakardama—a pit filled with salt juice.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Ksharakardama is described. If a person of low learning and habits insults one more virtuous, then he comes to this hell after his second death, for he is dead, even while he lives. Here in a pit with saltish and burning fluids he is suspended by Yama’s servants upside down.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

One who insults persons who are to be honored, falls in the pit of salt paste and endures endless misery.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Having explained the twenty hells, Śuka starts to narrate the other seven hells.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Ksharakardama is described. A lowly person, by his habits and knowledge, who does not respect holy persons and on the other hand insults them, comes to this hell. It is a pit filled with a paste of salt and other burning material. Here Yama’s servants immerse them upside down.  
He endures great pain.

### Text 31

*ये त्विह वै पुरुषाः पुरुषमेधेन यजन्ते याश्च स्त्रियो नृपशून् खादन्ति तांश्च ते*  
*पशव इव निहता यमसदने यातयन्तो रक्षोगणाः सौनिका इव स्वधितिनाव*  
*दायासृक् पिबन्ति नृत्यन्ति च गायन्ति च हृष्यमाणा यथेह पुरुषादाः*  
*॥३१॥*

*ye tv iha vai puruṣāḥ puruṣa-medhena yajante yāś ca striyo nṛ-paśūn khādanti tāṁś ca te paśava iva nihatā yama-sadane yātayanto rakṣo-gaṇāḥ saunikā iva svadhitināvadāyāsṛk pibanti nṛtyanti ca gāyanti ca hṛṣyamāṇā yatheha puruṣādāḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—persons who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *puruṣāḥ*—men; *puruṣa-medhena*—by sacrifice of a man; *yajante*—worship (the goddess Kālī or Bhadra Kālī); *yāḥ*—those who; *ca*—and; *striyaḥ*—women; *nṛ-paśūn*—the men used as sacrifice; *khādanti*—eat; *tān*—them; *ca*—and; *te*—they; *paśavaḥ iva*—like the animals; *nihatāḥ*—being slain; *yama-sadane*—in the abode of Yamarāja; *yātayantaḥ*—punishing; *rakṣaḥ-gaṇāḥ*—being Rākṣasas; *saunikāḥ*—the killers; *iva*—like; *svadhitinā*—by a sword; *avadāya*—cutting to pieces; *asṛk*—the blood; *pibanti*—drink; *nṛtyanti*—dance; *ca*—and; *gāyanti*—sing; *ca*—also; *hṛṣyamāṇāḥ*—being delighted; *yathā*—just like; *iha*—in this world; *puruṣa-adāḥ*—the man-eaters.

**Перевод:**

**There are men and women in this world who sacrifice human beings to Bhairava or Bhadra Kālī and then eat their victims’ flesh. Those who perform such sacrifices are taken after death to the abode of Yamarāja, where their victims, having taken the form of Rākṣasas, cut them to pieces with sharpened swords. Just as in this world the man-eaters drank their victims’ blood, dancing and singing in jubilation, their victims now enjoy drinking the blood of the sacrificers and celebrating in the same way.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Those who worship Bhairava, etc. with human flesh or women who eat human flesh. A host of Rakshasas having the form of their desire. Here, they dance as cannibals dance.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Here the hell *Rakṣaḥ-gaṇāḥ bhojana* is described. Those men who perform human sacrifices, even women who kill men to propitiate some demigod end up in this hell. Here, the same persons they killed earlier slit them by sharp weapons like butchers, drink their blood and dance in joy as cannibals do.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Puruṣa medha* is a human sacrifice. Yama’s servants slit him with a knife like butchers.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Ātmasambhāvana* = false pride.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Svadhiti is a knife. They slit him. This hell is called *Rakṣaḥ-gaṇāḥ bhojana* (to be eaten by a host of Rakshasas).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The hell *Rakṣaḥ-gaṇāḥ bhojana* is described here. Just as cannibals worship Bhairava and other such demigods, drink and dance, so the group of Rakshasas slit these evil doers and drink their blood and dance.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

*Rakṣaḥ-gaṇāḥ bhojana* is described. Those men who worship Bhadrakali and others by a human sacrifice and those women who eat flesh are brought here after their death. The same persons killed earlier are a group of rakshasas here who slit the evil doer with a sharp knife, drink his blood and dance as cannibals do.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Those who worship Bhairava and others by a puruṣamedha, that is, by killing a human being. Saunika means butchers. They slit their bodies with a knife and dance as cannibals dance here or as they danced earlier.

### Text 32

*ये त्विह वा अनागसोऽरण्ये ग्रामे वा वैश्रम्भकैरुपसृतानुपविश्रम्भय्य*  
*जिजीविषून्शूलसूत्रादिषूपप्रोतान् क्रीडनकतया यातयन्ति तेऽपि च*  
*प्रेत्य यमयातनासु शूलादिषु प्रोतात्मानः क्षुत्तृड्भ्यां चाभिहताः कङ्क*  
*वटादिभिश्चेतस्ततस्तिग्मतुण्डैराहन्यमाना आत्मशमलं स्मरन्ति ॥३२॥*

*ye tv iha vā anāgaso ‘raṇye grāme vā vaiśrambhakair upasṛtān upaviśrambhayya jijīviṣūn śūla-sūtrādiṣūpaprotān krīḍanakatayā yātayanti te ‘pi ca pretya yama-yātanāsu śūlādiṣu protātmānaḥ kṣut-tṛḍbhyāṁ cābhihatāḥ kaṅka-vaṭādibhiś cetas tatas tigma-tuṇḍair āhanyamānā ātma-śamalaṁ smaranti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—persons who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *anāgasaḥ*—who are faultless; *araṇye*—in the forest; *grāme*—in the village; *vā*—or; *vaiśrambhakaiḥ*—by means of good faith; *upasṛtān*—brought near; *upaviśrambhayya*—inspiring with confidence; *jijīviṣūn*—who want to be protected; *śūla-sūtra-ādiṣu*—on a lance, thread, and so on; *upaprotān*—fixed; *krīḍanakatayā*—like a plaything; *yātayanti*—cause pain; *te*—those persons; *api*—certainly; *ca*—and; *pretya*—after dying; *yama-yātanāsu*—the persecutions of Yamarāja; *śūla-ādiṣu*—on lances and so on; *prota-ātmānaḥ*—whose bodies are fixed; *kṣut-tṛḍbhyām*—by hunger and thirst; *ca*—also; *abhihatāḥ*—overwhelmed; *kaṅka-vaṭa-ādibhiḥ*—by birds such as herons and vultures; *ca*—and; *itaḥ tataḥ*—here and there; *tigma-tuṇḍaiḥ*—having pointed beaks; *āhanyamānāḥ*—being tortured; *ātma-śamalam*—own sinful activities; *smaranti*—they remember.

**Перевод:**

**In this life some people give shelter to animals and birds that come to them for protection in the village or forest, and after making them believe that they will be protected, such people pierce them with lances or threads and play with them like toys, giving them great pain. After death such people are brought by the assistants of Yamarāja to the hell known as Śūlaprota, where their bodies are pierced with sharp, needlelike lances. They suffer from hunger and thirst, and sharp-beaked birds such as vultures and herons come at them from all sides to tear at their bodies. Tortured and suffering, they can then remember the sinful activities they committed in the past.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Those who cause a false sense of protection by means of traps.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Shulaprota is described. Those who cheat innocent animals living in the village or forest by placing traps and other devices with food strewn inside and inflict violence on them, enter this hell. Here they are tied or woven to a pillar where cruel birds with beaks as sharp as diamonds, cause them great pain by attacking them.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Vaisrambhaka* = cheating with traps etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Cheating the animals by spreading food and grains or making them fall from a height. The word “etc.” used here means vultures. This hell is called Shulaprota.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Viśrabhaka* = deceitful traps and the like.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Shulaprota is described. Those who cheat innocent animals by laying traps with baits, who take them captive and play with them by piercing ropes into their body for controlling them, are treated in the same way here. In addition to that, fierce birds with sharp beaks peck at them as they remain immovable, being tied or sewed to a pole.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

The hefty person is dead here itself, and so dies for a second time.

Those who cheat animals with traps spreading bait.

### Text 33

*ये त्विह वै भूतान्युद्वेजयन्ति नरा उल्बणस्वभावा यथा*  
*दन्दशूकास्तेऽपि प्रेत्य नरके दन्दशूकाख्ये निपतन्ति यत्र नृप*  
*दन्दशूकाः पञ्चमुखाः सप्तमुखा उपसृत्य ग्रसन्ति यथा बिलेशयान् ॥३३॥*

*ye tv iha vai bhūtāny udvejayanti narā ulbaṇa-svabhāvā yathā dandaśūkās te ‘pi pretya narake dandaśūkākhye nipatanti yatra nṛpa dandaśūkāḥ pañca-mukhāḥ sapta-mukhā upasṛtya grasanti yathā bileśayān.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—persons who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vai*—indeed; *bhūtāni*—to living entities; *udvejayanti*—cause unnecessary pain; *narāḥ*—men; *ulbaṇa-svabhāvāḥ*—angry by nature; *yathā*—just like; *dandaśūkāḥ*—snakes; *te*—they; *api*—also; *pretya*—after dying; *narake*—in the hell; *dandaśūka-ākhye*—named Dandaśūka; *nipatanti*—fall down; *yatra*—where; *nṛpa*—O King; *dandaśūkāḥ*—serpents; *pañca-mukhāḥ*—having five hoods; *sapta-mukhāḥ*—having seven hoods; *upasṛtya*—reaching up; *grasanti*—eat; *yathā*—just like; *bileśayān*—mice.

**Перевод:**

**Those who in this life are like envious serpents, always angry and giving pain to other living entities, fall after death into the hell known as Dandaśūka. My dear King, in this hell there are serpents with five or seven hoods. These serpents eat such sinful persons just as snakes eat mice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Bileśaya = rat.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Here bileshaya means a rat, not a serpent. Dandaśūka is a serpent who always bites.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Dandaśūka is described. Those who are very cruel-natured like serpents, who frighten and torment others, enter this hell. Here five-hooded and seven-hooded serpents devour them like rats.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Those who cheat animals by making them falsely believe them. Balakas (vultures with long beaks) and dandashukas (snakes always prone to biting) frighten and bite these persons.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Dandaśūka is described. Those cruel-natured persons who frighten innocent people, come here. In this hell, big serpents with five or seven hoods devour them like rats.

### Text 34

*ये त्विह वा अन्धावटकुसूलगुहादिषु भूतानि निरुन्धन्ति तथामुत्र*  
*तेष्वेवोपवेश्य सगरेण वह्निना धूमेन निरुन्धन्ति ॥३४॥*

*ye tv iha vā andhāvaṭa-kusūla-guhādiṣu bhūtāni nirundhanti tathāmutra teṣv evopaveśya sagareṇa vahninā dhūmena nirundhanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*ye*—persons who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *andha-avaṭa*—a blind well; *kusūla*—granaries; *guha-ādiṣu*—and in caves; *bhūtāni*—the living entities; *nirundhanti*—confine; *tathā*—similarly; *amutra*—in the next life; *teṣu*—in those same places; *eva*—certainly; *upaveśya*—causing to enter; *sagareṇa*—with poisonous fumes; *vahninā*—with fire; *dhūmena*—with smoke; *nirundhanti*—confine.

**Перевод:**

**Those who in this life confine other living entities in dark wells, granaries or mountain caves are put after death into the hell known as Avaṭa-nirodhana. There they themselves are pushed into dark wells, where poisonous fumes and smoke suffocate them and they suffer very severely.**

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*Sagareṇa* = Along with poison.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Avata is described. Those who tease blind, deaf and other disabled children placing them in a pit and torment them, enter this hell. Here, they are also placed in pits where poisonous smoke and fire are injected.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Avata is a suffocating hole. Kusula is a dark room where grains are stored or a wooden vessel. Sagarena means with fire mixed with poison.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Bileśaya = rat.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The hell called “Avata Nirodha” is described. In pitch darkness. Avata is a pit. Kusula is a cupboard where food is kept which is built with grass and clay. Guha is a cave.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Bileśayan = rats.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Avata nirodha is described. Those who torment blind, deaf and other physically disabled children by placing them in pits or caves come here. Here they are also treated in the same way. They are also placed in a pit where hot and poisonous gases are injected. They stay there, immovable as they are, suffering great pain.

### Text 35

*यस्त्विह वा अतिथीनभ्यागतान् वा गृहपतिरसकृदुपगतमन्युर्दिधक्षुरिव पापेन*  
*चक्षुषा निरीक्षते तस्य चापि निरये पापदृष्टेरक्षिणी वज्रतुण्डा गृध्राः*  
*कङ्ककाकवटादयः प्रसह्योरुबलादुत्पाटयन्ति ॥३५॥*

*yas tv iha vā atithīn abhyāgatān vā gṛha-patir asakṛd upagata-manyur didhakṣur iva pāpena cakṣuṣā nirīkṣate tasya cāpi niraye pāpa-dṛṣṭer akṣiṇī vajra-tuṇḍā gṛdhrāḥ kaṅka-kāka-vaṭādayaḥ prasahyoru-balād utpāṭayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—a person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this life; *vā*—or; *atithīn*—guests; *abhyāgatān*—visitors; *vā*—or; *gṛha-patiḥ*—a householder; *asakṛt*—many times; *upagata*—obtaining; *manyuḥ*—anger; *didhakṣuḥ*—one desiring to burn; *iva*—like; *pāpena*—sinful; *cakṣuṣā*—with eyes; *nirīkṣate*—looks at; *tasya*—of him; *ca*—and; *api*—certainly; *niraye*—in hell; *pāpa-dṛṣṭeḥ*—of he whose vision has become sinful; *akṣiṇī*—the eyes; *vajra-tuṇḍāḥ*—those who have powerful beaks; *gṛdhrāḥ*—vultures; *kaṅka*—herons; *kāka*—crows; *vaṭa-ādayaḥ*—and other birds; *prasahya*—violently; *uru-balāt*—with great force; *utpāṭayanti*—pluck out.

**Перевод:**

**A householder who receives guests or visitors with cruel glances, as if to burn them to ashes, is put into the hell called Paryāvartana, where he is gazed at by hard-eyed vultures, herons, crows and similar birds, which suddenly swoop down and pluck out his eyes with great force.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

A guest is one who is not known earlier. Abhyagata is one who is known earlier and invited.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The hell Akshiparyavarta is described. Those who cast a disregardful and sideways glance at guests and invited people, enter this hell. Here, fierce crows and other birds pluck out their eyes.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Apacakṣuṣā* means looking sideways.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*Atīthi* = not known before. Abhyagata = known.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The difference between a guest and an invitee is as stated earlier (by Śrīdhara). Kankas are birds who live on the carcasses of dead animals. Tunda is a beak. This hell is called “Paryavartana.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The hell paryavarthana is described here.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The hell Paryavartana is described. Those who stare at guests, invited people or beggars repeatedly with fierce anger, come to this hell. Here, fierce birds like vultures, etc. attack them and instantly remove their eyes.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Dandaśuka is a serpent always prone to biting. Like big snakes here.

### Text 36

*यस्त्विह वा आढ्याभिमतिरहङ्कृतिस्तिर्यक्प्रेक्षणः सर्वतोऽभिविशङ्की*  
*अर्थव्ययनाशचिन्तया परिशुष्यमाणहृदयवदनो निर्वृतिमनवगतो ग्रह*  
*इवार्थमभिरक्षति स चापि प्रेत्य तद्उत्पादनोत्कर्षणसंरक्षणशमलग्रहः सूचीमुखे*  
*नरके निपतति यत्र ह वित्तग्रहं पापपुरुषं धर्मराजपुरुषा वायका इव*  
*सर्वतोऽङ्गेषु सूत्रैः परिवयन्ति ॥३६॥*

*yas tv iha vā āḍhyābhimatir ahaṅkṛtis tiryak-prekṣaṇaḥ sarvato ‘bhiviśaṅkī artha-vyaya-nāśa-cintayā pariśuṣyamāṇa-hṛdaya-vadano nirvṛtim anavagato graha ivārtham abhirakṣati sa cāpi pretya tad-utpādanotkarṣaṇa-saṁrakṣaṇa-śamala-grahaḥ sūcīmukhe narake nipatati yatra ha vitta-grahaṁ pāpa-puruṣaṁ dharmarāja-puruṣā vāyakā iva sarvato ‘ṅgeṣu sūtraiḥ parivayanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yaḥ*—any person who; *tu*—but; *iha*—in this world; *vā*—or; *āḍhya-abhimatiḥ*—proud because of wealth; *ahaṅkṛtiḥ*—egotistic; *tiryak-prekṣaṇaḥ*—whose vision is crooked; *sarvataḥ abhiviśaṅkī*—always fearful of being cheated by others, even by superiors; *artha-vyaya-nāśa-cintayā*—by the thought of expenditure and loss; *pariśuṣyamāṇa*—dried up; *hṛdaya-vadanaḥ*—his heart and face; *nirvṛtim*—happiness; *anavagataḥ*—not obtaining; *grahaḥ*—a ghost; *iva*—like; *artham*—wealth; *abhirakṣati*—protects; *saḥ*—he; *ca*—also; *api*—indeed; *pretya*—after dying; *tat*—of those riches; *utpādana*—of the earning; *utkarṣaṇa*—increasing; *saṁrakṣaṇa*—protecting; *śamala-grahaḥ*—accepting the sinful activities; *sūcīmukhe*—named Sūcīmukha; *narake*—in the hell; *nipatati*—falls down; *yatra*—where; *ha*—indeed; *vitta-graham*—as a money-grabbing ghost; *pāpa-puruṣam*—very sinful man; *dharmarāja-puruṣāḥ*—the commanding men of Yamarāja; *vāyakāḥ iva*—like expert weavers; *sarvataḥ*—all over; *aṅgeṣu*—on the limbs of the body; *sūtraiḥ*—by threads; *parivayanti*—stitch.

**Перевод:**

**One who in this world or this life is very proud of his wealth always thinks, “I am so rich. Who can equal me?” His vision is twisted, and he is always afraid that someone will take his wealth. Indeed, he even suspects his superiors. His face and heart dry up at the thought of losing his wealth, and therefore he always looks like a wretched fiend. He is not in any way able to obtain actual happiness, and he does not know what it is to be free from anxiety. Because of the sinful things he does to earn money, augment his wealth and protect it, he is put into the hell called Sūcīmukha, where the officials of Yamarāja punish him by stitching thread through his entire body like weavers manufacturing cloth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

One who feels very proud because of his wealth and feels that he is great, suspects that everyone will steal his money, even his elders and teachers. Having not enjoyed the money and having toiled for amassing wealth. They knit him with threads. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Vīrarāghava, Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Adyabhimabih = proud on account of wealth—suspects even his teachers. He is stitched. After being in heaven he is born again here with the remnants of *dharma* and *adharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Takes care of the money like ghosts. His miserable task is only to earn, build up, to not spend and to not give to others. Vayaka is a weaver. They weave such a person with sharp threads of silver and gold, or a graha may be taken as a Yaksha.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He is verily a Dhanapisacha.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Only tires himself by earning and building up his wealth.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Avata = suffocating pit. Kusula = a grain pit, a prison. “Immersing in water” should also be taken here. Atithi and Abhyagata, the unknown and known. Papachakshusha = with a crooked sight. Arthabhimatih = attached to his wealth. Ahamkrti = proud and mischievous. He protects the money like a Rākṣasa so that others will not take it. He has only the trouble of earning and the like. Like weavers, Yama’s servants sew his body with sharp strings.

### Text 37

*एवंविधा नरका यमालये सन्ति शतशः सहस्रशस्तेषु सर्वेषु च सर्व*  
*एवाधर्मवर्तिनो ये केचिदिहोदिता अनुदिताश्चावनिपते पर्यायेण विशन्ति*  
*तथैव धर्मानुवर्तिन इतरत्र इह तु पुनर्भवे त उभयशेषाभ्यां निविशन्ति*  
*॥३७॥*

*evaṁ-vidhā narakā yamālaye santi śataśaḥ sahasraśas teṣu sarveṣu ca sarva evādharma-vartino ye kecid ihoditā anuditāś cāvani-pate paryāyeṇa viśanti tathaiva dharmānuvartina itaratra iha tu punar-bhave ta ubhaya-śeṣābhyāṁ niviśanti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*evam-vidhāḥ*—of this sort; *narakāḥ*—the many hells; *yama-ālaye*—in the province of Yamarāja; *santi*—are; *śataśaḥ*—hundreds; *sahasraśaḥ*—thousands; *teṣu*—in those hellish planets; *sarveṣu*—all; *ca*—also; *sarve*—all; *eva*—indeed; *adharma-vartinaḥ*—persons not following the Vedic principles or regulative principles; *ye kecit*—whosoever; *iha*—here; *uditāḥ*—mentioned; *anuditāḥ*—not mentioned; *ca*—and; *avani-pate*—O King; *paryāyeṇa*—according to the degree of different kinds of sinful activity; *viśanti*—they enter; *tathā eva*—similarly; *dharma-anuvartinaḥ*—those who are pious and act according to the regulative principles or Vedic injunctions; *itaratra*—elsewhere; *iha*—on this planet; *tu*—but; *punaḥ-bhave*—into another birth; *te*—all of them; *ubhaya-śeṣābhyām*—by the remainder of the results of piety or vice; *niviśanti*—they enter.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King Parīkṣit, in the province of Yamarāja there are hundreds and thousands of hellish planets. The impious people I have mentioned—and also those I have not mentioned—must all enter these various planets according to the degree of their impiety. Those who are pious, however, enter other planetary systems, namely the planets of the demigods. Nevertheless, both the pious and impious are again brought to earth after the results of their pious or impious acts are exhausted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Itaratra = in heaven. Iha = in this world. Punarbhava = next birth. With residual *dharma* and *adharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

What has been described is just an indicator—there are many other hells where those who do various kinds of evil deeds enter. There are hundreds and thousands in number. As there is gradation in the happiness of those who observe *dharma*, so there is gradation in the misery of those who do not observe and who instead follow the course of *adharma* \[irreligion\]. After enjoying in heaven or suffering in hell, as the case may be, they again come to the earth with residual *dharma* and *adharma*. These are the results of p*ravrtti dharma* \[performance of religious activities for material enjoyment\]. The result of nivrtti *dharma* \[performance of religious activities for detachment\] was narrated to you earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The hells are not only this much—there are thousands of others. Uttaratra means in heaven. Iha means on the earth. With the remnants of both *dharma* and *adharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“Dear king, as you punish the criminals according to their crimes, the same is the case here.” Paryayena means in the order of the misdeeds done. The locative case in the word Punarbhave means the cause is the opinion of his holiness. Viśvanātha thinks it to mean “here” where *dharma* and *adharma* are again produced.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Like by gradation of *dharma* in heaven, with residual *dharma* and *adharma*.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

Concluding the topic, Śuka says that the description he has made of the various hells is just an indication—actually, there are hundreds and thousands of other types of hells where the evil doers (those mentioned and those not mentioned earlier) fall by rotation. Rotation means another batch of evil doers come to the same hell after one batch or an individual has left it. These individuals also move from hell to hell, after finishing the earlier one. It is similar to the enjoyment in heaven by those who observe *dharma*. With residual *dharma* and *adharma* they are born on the earth again. The course of nivrtti *dharma* has been stated to you in the second skanda \[Canto of *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam*\] itself. This is the position of the Andakosa from inside. According to different viewpoints, it consists of ten *lokas*, fourteen *lokas* or three *lokas* inside the *brahmāṇḍa*. The earth and the nether worlds is one, the Antarikṣa being the second, and heaven with the upper worlds, the third.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

Śuka says that there are other various hells, also.

### Text 38

*निवृत्तिलक्षणमार्ग आदावेव व्याख्यातः ॥ एतावानेवाण्डकोशो*  
*यश्चतुर्दशधा पुराणेषु विकल्पित उपगीयते यत्तद्भगवतो नारायणस्य*  
*साक्षान्महापुरुषस्य स्थविष्ठं रूपमात्ममायागुणमयमनुवर्णितमादृतः पठति*  
*शृणोति श्रावयति स उपगेयं भगवतः परमात्मनोऽग्राह्यमपि*  
*श्रद्धाभक्तिविशुद्धबुद्धिर्वेद ॥३८॥*

*nivṛtti-lakṣaṇa-mārga ādāv eva vyākhyātaḥ; etāvān evāṇḍa-kośo yaś caturdaśadhā purāṇeṣu vikalpita upagīyate yat tad bhagavato nārāyaṇasya sākṣān mahā-puruṣasya sthaviṣṭhaṁ rūpam ātmamāyā-guṇamayam anuvarṇitam ādṛtaḥ paṭhati śṛṇoti śrāvayati sa upageyaṁ bhagavataḥ paramātmano ‘grāhyam api śraddhā-bhakti-viśuddha-buddhir veda.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*nivṛtti-lakṣaṇa-mārgaḥ*—the path symptomized by renunciation, or the path of liberation; *ādau*—in the beginning (the Second and Third Cantos); *eva*—indeed; *vyākhyātaḥ*—described; *etāvān*—this much; *eva*—certainly; *aṇḍa-kośaḥ*—the universe, which resembles a big egg; *yaḥ*—which; *caturdaśa-dhā*—in fourteen parts; *purāṇeṣu*—in the *purāṇas; vikalpitaḥ*—divided; *upagīyate*—is described; *yat*—which; *tat*—that; *bhagavataḥ*—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *nārāyaṇasya*—of Lord Nārāyaṇa; *sākṣāt*—directly; *mahā-puruṣasya*—of the Supreme Person; *sthaviṣṭham*—the gross; *rūpam*—form; *ātma-māyā*—of His own energy; *guṇa*—of the qualities; *mayam*—consisting; *anuvarṇitam*—described; *ādṛtaḥ*—venerating; *paṭhati*—one reads; *śṛṇoti*—or hears; *śrāvayati*—or explains; *saḥ*—that person; *upageyam*—song; *bhagavataḥ*—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *paramātmanaḥ*—of the Supersoul; *agrāhyam*—difficult to understand; *api*—although; *śraddhā*—by faith; *bhakti*—and devotion; *viśuddha*—purified; *buddhiḥ*—whose intelligence; *veda*—understands.

**Перевод:**

**In the beginning \[the Second and Third Cantos of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam\] I have already described how one can progress on the path of liberation. In the Purāṇas the vast universal existence, which is like an egg divided into fourteen parts, is described. This vast form is considered the external body of the Lord, created by His energy and qualities. It is generally called the virāṭ-rūpa. If one reads the description of this external form of the Lord with great faith, or if one hears about it or explains it to others to propagate bhāgavata-*****dharma*****, or Kṛṣṇa consciousness, his faith and devotion in spiritual consciousness, Kṛṣṇa consciousness, will gradually increase. Although developing this consciousness is very difficult, by this process one can purify himself and gradually come to an awareness of the Supreme Absolute Truth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

At the outset only in the second canto it has been stated, “that he enters the world of Agni” and so on. The form \[virāṭ-rūpa\] is worthy of being glorified is stated in the *Vedas*,.

Whose intellect is purified by his faith and devotion.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The *brahmāṇḍa* consists of three *lokas*. Sometimes it is said that there are fourteen *lokas* in *brahmāṇḍa*. If we include the worlds higher than heaven in Swarga loka itself, and the seven holes in Bhūloka, then the three *lokas* are Bhūmi, Antarikṣa and Swarga. If each is counted separately then they are fourteen. This *brahmāṇḍa* is a very large pratima (a deity form) of the Lord. After knowing and meditating upon it, one gets the eligibility to know and meditate upon the subtle form of the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Fourteen divisions considering the lokas. Sthavishta means gross. Anishta means subtle.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kuśarīra is the body of animals.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Adaveva means in the second and third cantos.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Fourteen kinds according to common belief. In Skanda and other Purāṇas. Agrahya means which cannot be known. He who reads this.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

The benefit that accrues to those who listen to these chapters is narrated. He who listens to this with devotion gets purification of his mind and will be able to have the knowledge of God. This is the gross form of God, the knowledge of which leads to that of the subtle form.

### Text 39

*श्रुत्वा स्थूलं तथा सूक्ष्मं रूपं भगवतो यतिः ।*  
*स्थूले निर्जितमात्मानं शनैः सूक्ष्मं धिया नयेदिति ॥३९॥*

*śrutvā sthūlaṁ tathā sūkṣmaṁ*  
*rūpaṁ bhagavato yatiḥ*  
*sthūle nirjitam ātmānaṁ*  
*śanaiḥ sūkṣmaṁ dhiyā nayed iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*śrutvā*—after hearing of (from the disciplic succession); *sthūlam*—gross; *tathā*—as well as; *sūkṣmam*—subtle; *rūpam*—form; *bhagavataḥ*—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *yatiḥ*—a *sannyāsī* or devotee; *sthūle*—the gross form; *nirjitam*—conquered; *ātmānam*—the mind; *śanaiḥ*—gradually; *sūkṣmam*—the subtle. spiritual form of the Lord; *dhiyā*—by intelligence; *nayet*—one should lead it to; *iti*—thus.

**Перевод:**

**One who is interested in liberation, who accepts the path of liberation and is not attracted to the path of conditional life, is called yati, or a devotee. Such a person should first control his mind by thinking of the virāṭ-rūpa, the gigantic universal form of the Lord, and then gradually think of the spiritual form of Kṛṣṇa after hearing of both forms. Thus one’s mind is fixed in samādhi. By devotional service one can then realize the spiritual form of the Lord, which is the destination of devotees. Thus his life becomes successful.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Yatha means listening correctly.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

You should hear of both the gross and subtle forms—practice worship of the gross first and then go to the worship of the subtle form, which is attainable only through devotion.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

It is said that the knowledge of the gross leads to the knowledge of the subtle. The gross form should be heard from a teacher. Since everything in *brahmāṇḍa* is a form of God, whatever you think of will be placing your mind in God. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva and Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Of the two forms, it is the gross that is to be known first is what is stated here. *ātmā* means mind. By the worship of the subtle.

### Text 40

*भूद्वीपवर्षसरिदद्रिनभःसमुद्र*  
*पातालदिङ्नरकभागणलोकसंस्था ।*  
*गीता मया तव नृपाद्भुतमीश्वरस्य*  
*स्थूलं वपुः सकलजीवनिकायधाम ॥४०॥*

*bhū-dvīpa-varṣa-sarid-adri-nabhaḥ-samudra-*  
*pātāla-diṅ-naraka-bhāgaṇa-loka-saṁsthā*  
*gītā mayā tava nṛpādbhutam īśvarasya*  
*sthūlaṁ vapuḥ sakala-jīva-nikāya-dhāma*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhū*—of this planet earth; *dvīpa*—and other different planetary systems; *varṣa*—of tracts of land; *sarit*—rivers; *adri*—mountains; *nabhaḥ*—the sky; *samudra*—oceans; *pātāla*—lower planets; *dik*—directions; *naraka*—the hellish planets; *bhāgaṇa-loka*—the luminaries and higher planets; *saṁsthā*—the situation; *gītā*—described; *mayā*—by me; *tava*—for you; *nṛpa*—O King; *adbhutam*—wonderful; *īśvarasya*—of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; *sthūlam*—gross; *vapuḥ*—body; *sakala-jīva-nikāya*—of all the masses of living entities; *dhāma*—which is the place of repose.

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, I have now described for you this planet earth, other planetary systems, and their lands \[varṣas\], rivers and mountains. I have also described the sky, the oceans, the lower planetary systems, the directions, the hellish planetary systems and the stars. These constitute the virāṭ-rūpa, the gigantic material form of the Lord, on which all living entities repose. Thus I have explained the wonderful expanse of the external body of the Lord.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

What is his position? He is the receptacle of all living entities.

The Lord said: In Kṛta-yuga, there was a king by the name Vimala whose capital was in Kanya Kubja. He had a hundred wives, yet he was childless. With this grief, he set out in a chariot to meet his guru. He went to his guru’s place, praised him and begged for progeny. At the behest of the guru, he performed the putreshti sacrifice and then received ninety-nine sons from all of his wives except the eldest. She felt sad and always thought of killing her co-wives’s sons.

Once, when the king went to bathe in the sea along with his other wives on the occasion of the new moon day, the eldest wife killed all the children. The king Vimala became very morose on hearing the news. In course of time, the eldest wife died and went through 8,400,000 hells on account of this sin. She was again born on the earth as an outcaste chandali \[dog-eating woman\]. She was very ugly to look at. She was moving from forest to forest. Fortunately for her, once she heard the discourse on the Fifth Canto of Bhāgavata, and thus she atoned for her sin by this (although accidentally) and became pure. She discarded her material body and went to Vaikuṇṭha.

Oh! the Greatness of Bhāgavata!

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The description of the gross form is concluded by briefly referring to the constituents of the earth, oceans, mountains, and so on. This is a wonderful pratima \[form\] of the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Concluding the topic, Śuka condenses the contents. This is the form of God which houses all the living entities, or of God who dwells in all living entities. I have sung about this form, of which the islands, oceans and mountains are limbs.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

As you listen to the description of the gross, you should listen to the description of the subtle also. You should set your mind on the gross form and gradually and slowly should move to the worship of the subtle form.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Yatha = exactly. By conquering the mind on the gross form, (here, “conquering” means fixing without swerving), you should strive to meditate upon the subtle form. This is possible by devotion only as was stated in the second canto.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Śuka concludes. Samstha=design. Nikaya=group.

The greatness of listening to the fifth canto is described in the Padma Purāṇa.

Viṣṇu said: Dear Brahmā, the result of listening to the Fifth Canto \[of Śrīmad Bhagavatam\] is that it washes off the sin of child-killing. This is my considered opinion, which is close to my heart.

Brahmā said: Please narrate to me and for the benefit of the world about someone who was engaged in child-killing and who atoned by listening to the Fifth Canto.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

These islands and lands constitute the form of Īśvara.

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

40\. In Avichi he is dropped from a great height and his body breaks into pieces.

41\. The commentary is same in all.

42\. Atmasambhavana is thinking high of oneself. He who insults the elders is already dead. And dying for a second time, he enters the hell Ksharakardama to endure endless pain where there is a paste of salt and other burning things.

43\. The commentary is the same in all.

44\. The hell Shulaprota is described. Those who trap animals and play with their lives and torment them, are made to enter this hell where they are treated likewise.

45\. Ulbanaswabhava means terrible and cruel-natured like serpents.

46\. Bileshaya is a rat. “Dear King, you have no such sin. Even if there is any it is destroyed by your devotion,” is the idea behind the address.

47\. Andhavata is a suffocating pit. Kusula is a pit used to store grains. They confine them there only with poisonous heated gases.

48\. Atithi is an unknown person. Abhyagata is a known one.

49\. He who is proud and mischievous because of his wealth, and who protects his wealth with a dry face like a ghost, without spending his money, and who suspects that even his trustworthy father and teachers are after his wealth, falls in this Suchimukha hell.

50\. There, he is woven by strings like joined pieces of cloth are sewed by a thread.

51\. Having described the main hells, Śuka says there are thousand of other types of hells also where sinners fall and suffer one after the other. By addressing him as dear king, Śuka suggests that if the sinner has been punished by the king prior to his death, he will not fall in these pits of hell. They again come to this world with residual *dharma* and *adharma* or with residual *puṇya* \[pious credit\] and *pāpa* \[sinful credit\] which are the results of *dharma* and *adharma* respectively.

52\. Concluding the topic, Śuka narrates the benefits of listening to this particular topic. He who listens to this with rapt attention and devotion gets the knowledge of God, who is not knowable except through the *Vedas*. Because the greatness of Nārāyaṇa is such that he blesses the listener in this way.

53\. The same thing is clarified. Meditating upon the gross form initially, one should gradually move towards the worship of the subtle form.

54\. The islands and oceans, as I have described to you, are the gross form which houses all the living entities in it. It is very wonderful also. “Dear king, if you want to ask anything else, do not hesitate,” Śuka suggests.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhagavat-prasada Acarya:**

If a question be asked as to what is the gross form of God, the concentration on which is prescribed, Śuka replies concluding the chapter. The islands, their divisions, the oceans, the rivers, the mountains, the sky, the netherworlds, the directions, the hells, the upper worlds, the stars and celestial bodies—all these constitute the gross form of the Lord who is a receptacle of all the *jīvas*.

**Комментарий. Автор Yādavārya:**

40\. Uttaratra = in heaven. Iha = here in this world. Punarbhavah = rebirth.

41\. With the remaining parts of *dharma* and *adharma*. Adaveva means in the second canto only. Chatardashadha = in fourteen ways.

42-43. The *brahmāṇḍa* is his gross form. The subtle form is the one in the heart whose image is *jīva*. Listening to the gross form leads to the knowledge of the subtle form. *ātmā* = the mind.

44\. For easy understanding, Śuka sums up the contents. The *brahmāṇḍa* is the bowl where all living entities are housed. Lord Hari is its supporter. The islands and oceans are the limbs of that form.

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Twenty-six Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “A Description of the Hellish Planets.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Different viewpoints described in the commentaries are to be taken as in different creations.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*In proper directions* = east onwards (respectively). *Of proper forms* = not exceeding (differing from) the colors of Indra etc. *Turīyamāna* = one fourth extent, i.e, 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\]. The names are to be known from other Purāṇas. As is said: There are nine cities in Meru, viz. Manovatī, Amarāvatī, Tejovatī, Saṁyamanī, Kṛṣṇāṅganā, Śraddhāvatī, Gandhavatī, Mahodayā and Yaśovatī are of Brahmā, Indra, Agni etc. respectively. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śukadeva\]

**Комментарий. Автор Giridhara Lala:**

The golden city is named Manovatī and is 10,000 *yojanas* \[80,000 miles\] in extent. Around that city of Brahmā, the cities of other eight world-protectors, from east onwards, respectively, befitting their forms, one-fourth the size of Brahmā's city, i.e, 2,500 *yojanas* \[20,000 miles\] extent, are constructed. These are: in the east, Amaravatī for Indra; in south-east, Tejovatī for Agni; in the south, Samyamanī for Yama; in south-west, Kṛṣṇāṅganā for Nirṛti; in the west, Śraddhāvatī for Varuṇa; in the north-west, Gandhavatī for Vāyu; in the north, Mahodayā for Dhanada; and in the north-east, Yaśovatī for Īśāna. As it is said: There are nine cities in Meru, viz. Manovatī, Amarāvatī, Tejovatī, Saṁyamanī, Kṛṣṇāṅganā, Śraddhāvatī, Gandha-vatī, Mahodayā and Yaśovatī are of Brahmā, Indra, Agni etc. respectively. \[Note: this paragraph is repeated by Śrī Bhagavatprasādācārya\]

Thus end the Vaiṣṇava *ācāryas* commentaries of the Fifth Canto, Sixteenth Chapter of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled, “A Description of Jambūdvīpa.”
